it is clear that restructuring is necessary, it is necessary in order to increase productivity, to promote technological innovation, but always on the assumption that jobs are maintained. but today, throughout europe, the numerous restructuring processes already mentioned have one main objective: redundancy. and these redundancies are mainly due to two things: either the relentless pursuit of profit, or the lack of liquidity in companies due to recessionary policies promoted by the european union and national governments, which cause consumption to contract. this means that redundancies are not inevitable, but rather the result of concrete policies adopted and implemented by concrete politicians, and which in this parliament are expressed by a majority. to assume that restructuring is acceptable in the abstract concept of economic change is to assume that there is no alternative and that redundancies are inevitable, even if minimised. there are many alternatives to layoffs, and today's workers know this better than ever.

in writing. − this document from the committee on regional development, of which i am a member, seeks to explore effective and efficient mechanisms to create synergies between the european funding programmes covered by the future common strategic framework. better integration of the implementation of funding programmes will make it possible to increase the effectiveness of european funding at local and regional level. moreover, following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, territorial cohesion constitutes an objective of the treaty under article 174 tfeu, together with economic and social cohesion. there is thus a growing need for a bottom-up approach to mobilise the potential of local and regional development. to this end, i agree that it is essential to establish common rules and close coordination for all the funds covered by the common strategic framework. for the reasons given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. − this own-initiative report proposes to strengthen the territorial objective of cohesion policy, to further integrate european funds into the 2014-2020 mff and to provide mechanisms for the integration of the structural funds and for the creation of synergies between the 5 european funds (erdf, esf, cohesion fund, eafrd and emff) covered by the common provisions regulation. unfortunately, there are several negative aspects to this report. it is worth noting that, at a time when the majority of parliament says it is defending 'solidarity' more than ever, the report accepts the blackmail of those who want to reduce cohesion funds or, at best, keep them at current levels of poverty, then defies the usual arguments of greater efficiency, synergies, innovative instruments, and finally misses the point: without a substantial increase in the budget, it will not be possible to put into practice the principle of cohesion so much advocated, even more so in a context of deepening capitalist integration (single market, common policies) and its inevitable effects on the increase of inequalities and divergence. we also reject the blackmail of 'macroeconomic conditionality', a principle which is not 'solidarity-based'.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the european solidarity fund is the main instrument of the european union for implementing the principle of solidarity, which is enshrined not only in the treaties for disaster situations, but also, and most importantly, rooted in the fundamental values that created the european union: solidarity among the european peoples. i am in favour of any measure which minimises bureaucracy and prevents the effective and flexible mobilisation of this important fund, particularly in the event of a disaster, so that it is immediately available. the solidarity of the european union with its member states, and above all with its citizens, must never be called into question, and this is the principle and value that must be applied in practice, because without the concrete expression of this value there is no real european union.
in writing. − following the devastating floods in central europe in 2002, the european union (eu) set up the eu solidarity fund which provided financial assistance to deal with the damage caused by 49 disasters, mainly floods and fires. the solidarity fund has proved to be one of the european union's most successful and appreciated instruments, and one of the few at the eu's disposal to demonstrate its solidarity and closeness to citizens. however, after that time, we should simplify procedures and make definitions clearer, more precise and more transparent. the fund is able to respond to major disasters, but not to minor ones. it is therefore necessary to define clearly and precisely the concept of disaster and access to the fund in the case of 'small' disasters. since it is impossible to anticipate how much will be used throughout the year, this instrument should remain outside the eu budget and should continue to be used in exceptional circumstances, even if the catastrophe does not reach the eligibility threshold. i voted in favour of this report because i consider the objectives of the european union solidarity fund to be important.
in writing. − changes in the economic situation of the union and of most of its member states make it imperative to revise the regulation on the european union solidarity fund for the new financial period 2014-2020. this instrument should be adapted to the current reality, with changes that are capable of improving the fund's operational efficiency without generating additional costs. i welcome this new reform proposal which aims to simplify procedures and make definitions clearer, more precise and more transparent.
in writing. − the eu solidarity fund, set up in 2002, is arguably the clearest, most decisive and most important expression of european solidarity towards citizens facing a difficult situation (natural or man-made disaster, terrorist attack, etc.), with some 42 applications approved by the end of 2010, with a total financial support of over eur 2.4 billion. the eusf is widely recognised as one of the most satisfactory instruments at the disposal of the eu. however, it is necessary to amend the current regulation in order to improve the operability and flexibility of the fund, by improving the efficiency and speed of the administrative procedures necessary for its mobilisation, by reducing the time needed for granting aid to the affected regions and by increasing its visibility with a view to improving the eu's credibility with its citizens. understandably, in the current political climate characterised by a difficult budgetary situation in many member states, it is difficult to move forward with a proposal that entails additional costs. however, it seems reasonable to me that an agreement can be reached in good time to adapt this instrument to the present situation and make it more effective, in particular by simplifying procedures and making definitions clearer, more precise and more transparent.
in writing. − the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up in 2002 in the aftermath of the severe floods in central europe and has established itself as the main instrument for assisting european citizens and member states affected by disasters. today, it marks 10 years of success in applying the principle of european solidarity with over €3.2 billion of financial aid provided to 23 member states in 49 disasters. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that in order to continue to provide aid during emergency operations to the populations hit by disasters and to alleviate the financial burden on member states, the effectiveness of the eusf needs to be improved. in particular, by clearly and concretely defining the concept of disaster, and in particular by clarifying the access criteria in cases of 'regional disasters'. but also by reducing the bureaucracy involved in mobilising the fund, thereby reducing the time between the occurrence and the granting of aid.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the european union solidarity fund, implementation and enforcement, as it reiterated the need to review this eusf regulation with a view to improving its operability and flexibility. in view of the trend towards an increase in the number and intensity of natural disasters as a result of climate change, it is urgent to simplify and adapt procedures in order to enhance the effectiveness of the eusf.
in writing. − the european union solidarity fund has embodied the motto that i have often invoked and which i consider essential for the construction of an integration project for the benefit of all the populations of the member states: more than 'united in diversity', we must show that we are 'united in adversity'. my country has already benefited from the fund. i recognise its importance and the need to evaluate how it is working and to improve it wherever necessary and possible. the fact that, as mentioned, the majority of applications to the fund (63%) were submitted under the exceptional category 'regional disaster' of which 66% were rejected after the commission's assessment makes clear the need for this in-depth reflection on its scope and limits. i hope that parliament's recommendations will have the desired effect and that the next evaluation of the fund will look more favourably on it. i would particularly like to see less use of the internet if that means fewer disasters in the union. i would also like to take this opportunity to greet my colleague, rosa estaràs ferragut, and to congratulate her on the excellent work she has done here.
in writing. − the european union solidarity fund (eusf), established in 2002, is a financial instrument for solidarity between all member states (ms) whose objective is to minimise the damage caused by major natural disasters that may occur in the european union or in the states in the process of accession. after 10 years of the fund's application, we have seen that there are some areas for improvement. the time between the day of the disaster and the moment when the affected regions receive the allocated amounts should be shortened. this period, which is on average nine months, can exceed two years. it is therefore necessary to review this mechanism and, if possible, to advance the funds. i voted in favour of the report by mrs rosa estaràs ferragut on the eusf, its implementation and execution, because i agree with the need to change the current methodology in order to simplify procedures so that they are more transparent and the fund more effective. given that 60% of the applications submitted were not considered as major disasters because of a lack of a framework, i call on the commission to ensure that, in the legislative initiative to be presented shortly, smaller disasters can also be included in this fund.
in writing. the report stresses the importance of the european union solidarity fund as an instrument to enable a financial response to major disasters in the member states or in future accession countries. it also makes a set of recommendations to improve the fund's operability and flexibility by simplifying and increasing its visibility and credibility, being critical of the long lead-up to its mobilisation, and advocating the efficiency and speed of administrative procedures, as well as the need to reduce bureaucracy and the time between the occurrence of the disaster and the arrival of support. we have long criticised the delays associated with the mobilisation of the eusf - as was evident in the case of the disaster that affected the island of madeira on 20 february 2010 - and we have long pointed to the need for amendments to its regulation. this report generally accepts most of these amendments and we have therefore supported it. in addition to the above, the following suggestions are also included: the 'possibility of making advance payments as soon as the affected member state has requested aid'; the need to take into account slow-moving disasters such as drought, which particularly affect mediterranean regions; another consideration of disasters with a high regional impact and the revision of the current eligibility thresholds.
in writing. − following the various natural disasters that struck central europe in 2002, and in the absence of an instrument to assist the population and the member states affected by these disasters, the union created a new instrument: the european union solidarity fund. since then, the regulation governing it has not been modified to adapt it to new needs and to correct some of the shortcomings that have been identified during the ten years of application. since its establishment and until september 2012, the fund has provided financial assistance to cope with the damage caused by 49 disasters, mainly floods and fires. it is important that we make some changes to the rules of this fund to make it even more effective. the changes in the economic situation of the union and of most of its member states have led the commission, in a new attempt to adapt the instrument to the current reality, to propose changes to the procedure which are capable of improving the fund's operation without generating additional costs. the aim of this new reform proposal is to simplify procedures and make definitions clearer, more precise and more transparent.
in writing. − following the devastating floods in central europe in 2002, and in the absence of an instrument to assist the population and the member state affected by a disaster, the union created a new instrument: the eu solidarity fund. since then, the regulation governing it has not been modified to adapt it to new needs and to correct some of the shortcomings identified during the ten years of application. the fund has already provided financial assistance to cope with damage caused by 49 disasters, mainly floods and fires. in recent years the commission has been receiving an increasing number of applications, due not only to an increased number of disasters but also to the fact that the existing regulations are not clear as to the possible coverage and eligibility of disasters for which applications are submitted under the derogating scheme of the so-called 'extraordinary regional disasters'. i congratulate the rapporteur on her work and welcome the updating of the solidarity fund legislation, particularly as regards a better definition of disaster, simplification of procedures and, above all, the possibility of classifying a prolonged drought as a disaster. this is a measure that only loses late.
in writing. − the european union solidarity fund has been mobilised over the past 10 years to provide financial assistance in 49 disasters, mostly floods and fires. despite being one of the most successful and appreciated instruments demonstrating the union's solidarity and closeness to european citizens, the eu solidarity fund and its implementation and enforcement have been marked by some shortcomings, mainly due to the ambiguous wording of the regulation and the lengthy process of mobilising the fund. it is therefore necessary to revise the regulation, by simplifying bureaucratic procedures and clarifying the concept of catastrophe, so that the fund can operate more effectively.
in writing. - the autonomous region of madeira, where i come from, has been struck by serious natural disasters in recent years. in fact, the geographical and natural characteristics of this region contribute to a higher risk of disasters. however, its economic and structural conditions also contribute to increasing the severity and duration of its effects. it is therefore necessary that in the near future the solidarity fund can be activated quickly and that at the same time advance payments can be made. it would also be more fair if, in the event of a disaster in an outermost region, the constraints of that region could be taken into account in the weighting of the fund's eligibility criteria. for the reasons i have outlined, i am voting in favour of the document calling for a reform of the solidarity fund.

in writing. − i approve this report, considering that an administrative procedure law can and should strengthen the legitimacy and transparency of the european union, while providing greater legal certainty for citizens and legal persons in their dealings with the administration of the european union. i therefore agree with a set of general principles to be followed in order to achieve good administration and which should lead to more transparent action by the european union. the legitimacy of a european administration is essential, remembering that this is the european year of citizens, and for this reason any act that gives more legitimacy to the institutions of the european union is important.
in writing. − pursuant to article 298 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), this report calls on the european commission to submit a proposal for a regulation on a european law of administrative procedure, with the aim of guaranteeing the right to good administration through an open, efficient and independent administration, based on the european law of administrative procedure. the regulation shall apply to the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies ('the union administration') in their relations with the public, its scope being limited to direct administration. the regulation should therefore codify the fundamental principles of good administration and regulate the procedure to be followed by the union administration. the implementation of an administrative procedure law would help the union to facilitate internal organisation and to promote standards of administration, increasing the legitimacy of this body, and the trust of citizens, who are increasingly confronted with european administration without corresponding procedural rights such as the right to be heard or the right to access their own file. this regulation will help to strengthen good administrative practice, impartiality and legality, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the administrative procedure law is an opportunity to strengthen the legitimacy of the union and, at the same time, to give citizens and legal persons clearer rights and greater legal certainty in their relations with the union administration. it should codify a set of general principles of good administration, which should guide the action of the union administration, and establish a minimum number of basic procedural rules to be followed by the union administration when dealing with individual cases involving a natural or legal person, and other situations where a person has direct or personal contact with the union administration. in particular, these rules should promote transparency and accountability and increase citizens' trust in the eu administration.
in writing. − the eu's powers have been increasing over the years and citizens are increasingly confronted with the eu administration (institutions, bodies, services and agencies). in many cases they do not have procedural rights which they can use if necessary. the eu does not have a coherent and comprehensive set of codified rules of administrative law, which makes it difficult for european citizens to have a clear and comprehensive view of their administrative rights under eu law. in view of the new powers conferred by the lisbon treaty in this area, i support this report which calls for the creation of a regulation which will create minimum guarantees for citizens and businesses, contributing to greater transparency, legitimacy, accountability and to increase citizens' trust in the eu administration. the eu needs to give quick, clear and visible answers to its citizens in an effort to meet their legitimate expectations, which will bring clear benefits not only to citizens but also to the administration in terms of better functioning of services and increased efficiency.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report for urging the commission to submit a proposal for a regulation providing for the introduction of a european law on administrative procedure, with the aim of contributing to a more open, efficient and independent administration, and which applies to the union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
in writing. − an administrative procedure law is an opportunity to strengthen the legitimacy of the union and, at the same time, to give citizens and legal persons clearer rights and greater legal certainty in their relations with the union. the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against fraud and for the commission to be able to take a more active role in the fight against fraud. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances.
in writing. − europeans are well-educated and informed citizens who know their rights and demand that they be respected. relations between citizens and public administrations should be guided by rules and principles which place the public administration at the service of the public. in fact, public services exist to serve citizens who support them with their taxes and not the other way around. the initiative report under review, drawn up by luigi berlinguer, contains a set of recommendations to the commission on a european union (eu) code of administrative procedure. the eu needs an administrative procedure law with clear rules, which defends the rights of citizens. we all know that no rules can bring nothing but trouble. if we want more europe, we need more efficient administration. i voted in favour of this report, which was unanimously approved in the committee on legal affairs, because, like the rapporteur, i am in favour of a more efficient, open and transparent administration. we all know that administrations do not always comply with the law, with significant disadvantages for european citizens. i hope that the new legislation will put an end to the mismanagement which sometimes still occurs in the public administration.
in writing. the report calls on the commission to present a proposal for a regulation on a european administrative procedure law, which the rapporteur believes is an opportunity to strengthen the eu's legitimacy. on the other hand, faced with what it considers to be a pressing problem of the eu today - the lack of citizens' trust, which can affect its legitimacy - the eu needs to give quick, clear and visible answers to citizens in order to respond to their aspirations. this concern about the eu's lack of legitimacy in the eyes of its citizens is significant. the obvious would be to give serious thought to its causes and the subsequent inevitable reversal of policies and guidelines, rather than manoeuvres such as the present one, which are basically a flight forward - also, of course, illegitimate. the problem with this report is not so much its content as the reprehensible motives behind it.
in writing. − an administrative procedure law is an opportunity to strengthen the legitimacy of the union and, at the same time, to give citizens and legal persons clearer rights and greater legal certainty in their dealings with the union's administration. the commission should therefore submit a proposal for a regulation on a european law on administrative procedure. the law should be limited to the direct administration of the eu and be applicable to all the institutions of the union and to all areas of its activity. it is appropriate to codify a set of general principles of good administration, which should guide the action of the union administration, and to lay down a minimum number of basic procedural rules to be followed by the union administration when dealing with individual cases involving a natural or legal person, and other situations where a person has direct or personal contact with the union administration. in particular, these rules should promote transparency and accountability and increase citizens' trust in the eu administration.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation for a law on administrative procedure in the european union for two fundamental reasons: (a) the increase and diversification of the union's administrative tasks, both at the level of the european commission and its departments and at that of the numerous union agencies, require common rules of administrative procedure, which give consistency and predictability to the union's administrative action, by reinforcing the principles of legality, public interest, equality and proportionality, which are essential in the exercise of discretionary powers; (b) citizens and businesses need a common regulatory framework for their relations with the union administration as regards deadlines, right of audience, etc. a law on administrative procedure is today an essential requirement of the rule of law as it was in the member states. a law on administrative procedure is a step forward in the structuring of administrative law in the european union. as european integration progresses and the union becomes self-governing and no longer relies exclusively on the administration of the member states to enforce its laws, administrative law should take its rightful place in the public law of the union.
in writing. − an administrative procedure law is an opportunity to strengthen the legitimacy of the union and, at the same time, to give citizens and legal persons clearer rights and greater legal certainty in their dealings with the union's administration. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this report which proposes that the commission be asked to submit a proposal for a regulation on a european administrative procedure law.
in writing. − this own-initiative report, based on article 298 tfeu, sets out the work of the working party on eu administrative law, chaired by the committee on legal affairs. this work involved a number of professionals in the field, including academics, ngos and people from civil society, who summarised the contributions gathered through conferences, meetings and encounters. the aim is to establish a legislative initiative applicable to all the institutions and fields of activity of the european union. this will create more transparency and legal certainty in the eu's relations with european citizens and businesses, and strengthen citizens' accountability and trust in the european administration.
in writing. the aim of this report is to ask the commission to submit a proposal for a regulation on a european law on administrative procedure. the report also calls for the eu to be able to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action to combat terrorism. we believe that this initiative is part of the growing implementation of the phenomenon of the federalization of administrative law, part of a process of strengthening european capitalist integration which aims to normalize national administrative rights by interfering with the latter. the report opens the door to the creation of a 'communitarianised' administrative law which would be another step towards the construction of a european federation. we do not forget that it is important for administrative regulation to go beyond the application of fundamental rules and principles, always with a view to respecting the principles of transparency, subsidiarity and proportionality. however, it should be ensured that the applicability of such an internal instrument of the european union does not extend to the member states. only in this way will the sovereignty of these states and the national framework of their values be respected, and the values of the state and para-state administration in the broadest sense be taken into account.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that, at a time of widespread financial and economic crisis throughout the european union, there are several processes of restructuring in the labour market. i therefore agree with this report, because european workers involved in restructuring processes must be given guarantees. i would also stress that european legislation is also needed to ensure that restructuring is anticipated and managed in a fair, balanced and competitive manner. it is important to create a european society which requires the involvement of all actors.
in writing. − over the last ten years, european companies have adapted to increasing competitiveness and to an economic and financial crisis which has resulted in the closure or restructuring of many of our companies. there are many differences in legislation in this area in the european union. however, it is important to recognise and protect the parties affected, both the company in terms of its competitiveness and the workers in terms of labour law and safety at work.
in writing. − while restructuring is not a new phenomenon, it has become increasingly common practice, due to the economic changes of recent years and especially the fact that we are going through an economic and financial crisis. a restructuring process can only be successful in an economically and socially responsible way if it is integrated into a strategy that ensures and enhances the long-term sustainability and competitiveness of the company and at the same time protects the interests of its employees, and the dismissal of employees should be considered only as a last resort. each member state is subject to different types of restructuring proceedings and the consequences of those proceedings are also different in each of them. however, this should not affect the rights and obligations arising from eu legislation on the protection of workers or respect for the principle of equal treatment. i believe that the creation of a european framework for restructuring should help to create a climate of mutual trust, and i therefore support the creation of urgent and concrete measures in this area, such as monitoring measures for the activities of companies, in order to prevent any abuse which particularly harms workers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i ask the commission to come forward as soon as possible with legislation on information and consultation of employees in the context of company restructuring. the management of restructuring, which includes company managers, employee representatives and public authorities, will ensure greater respect for the interests of companies and, at the same time, respect for the interests of employees. i understand that companies are going through difficult times, but we need to ensure that firms only use redundancy as a last resort, after all other alternatives have been exhausted.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis has contributed to an increase in the number of closures and restructuring of enterprises and, consequently, to an increase in unemployment in most member states. according to the european restructuring monitor, since 2002 there have been some 14,000 restructuring cases affecting 4 million workers. however, although there are various employment policies in the eu, the fact is that restructuring processes, even if transnational in scope, involving more than one country, do not have a common legal framework. the report therefore calls on the commission to prepare a legislative act on the information and consultation of workers and the anticipation and management of restructuring. this act, rather than a regulation or a directive, which will impose a single regime, should be a set of suggestions from the european commission to the states, which will be able to keep their national rules unchanged in this respect.
in writing. − since the start of the crisis in 2008, the european union (eu) has already lost 1.800.000 jobs. the implications of the crisis during these years led to the adoption of a new form of economic governance in which social and labour issues gained increasing weight. with public deficits under control, all of them have turned to economic growth and employment. due to the relocation of many european companies to other continents and the import of products from emerging economies, business sector restructuring, although not a new phenomenon, has become recurrent in recent times, forcing workers to adapt to the requirements of a greener economy and focused on the efficiency of natural resources. the report by alejandro cercas addresses this issue and contains recommendations to the commission on information and consultation of workers and anticipation and management of restructuring. while i understand that restructuring a company is not always a simple process - even because of the unpredictability - i am aware that companies have to adapt to new social and working conditions. because this report is an essential contribution to helping us to see things more clearly, i voted in favour and i hope that the recommendations adopted will contribute to increasing european industrial gdp.
in writing. - in the abstract, company restructuring may correspond to the alignment of production processes with scientific and technological development, to increase productivity, to improve working conditions, assuming the maintenance of jobs. but restructuring is not done in isolation from the existing social and economic context. today, the numerous restructuring processes throughout europe have essentially one objective: to maintain or increase the profits of companies by laying off workers and intensifying operations. at a time when measures were being called for to stem the rise in unemployment and create jobs, this report accepts dismissals and advocates that, before dismissals, different alternatives be studied, including the renegotiation of 'working conditions'. in other words, it puts workers before the choice of either precariousness or unemployment, which is unacceptable. to assume that restructuring is acceptable in the abstract concept of 'economic change' is to assume that there is no alternative and that redundancies are inevitable, although, as the report says, with minimal impacts. there are alternatives. the productivity gains of labour must be channelled to the wealth creators the workers and not to capital.
in writing. - restructuring is not a new phenomenon but a practice that is becoming more frequent due to economic change and that in recent years has become more prevalent, taking on multiple forms, intensifying in certain sectors and investing in new ones, with unpredictable consequences for the economic and sectoral fabric of the member states. the economic crisis unleashed in 2008 requires companies and workers to make the changes needed to safeguard competitiveness and protect jobs, sharply accelerating the process of change and thus increasing alarmingly for workers, territories and all levels of government the pressures to make structural adjustments. a strong social dialogue, based on mutual trust and shared responsibility, is very important as the best instrument for finding consensual solutions and common approaches to anticipate, prevent and manage restructuring processes.
in writing. − the european parliament resolution calls on the european commission to present as soon as possible, in accordance with article 225 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union and after consulting the social partners, a draft legislative act on information and consultation of workers and anticipation and management of restructuring. indeed, studies carried out at european level have concluded that better anticipation and management of restructuring would help workers and businesses to adapt to the transitions imposed by excess capacity and the need for modernisation and structural adjustment. i voted in favour of this resolution, bearing in mind that information and communication between the parties involved is essential in crisis situations for the management of such situations.
in writing. − the european parliament today called on the commission to present as soon as possible a draft legislative act on information and consultation of workers and anticipation and management of restructuring, in accordance with a set of recommendations respecting fundamental rights, the principle of subsidiarity and the principle of proportionality, freedom of establishment and the right to property. such recommendations on the proposed legislative act shall address the object, definitions and scope of the proposed legislative act, as well as long-term strategic planning, adaptability and employability, anticipation of employment and skills needs, information and consultation on business decisions, minimisation of internal social costs through a social plan, agreements on the management of restructuring processes, minimisation of external economic, social and environmental impact, public and financial support, and the designation of relevant public authorities. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. - restructuring is necessary to increase productivity, to promote technological innovation, and to preserve jobs. today, all over europe, the numerous restructuring processes have only one objective: redundancy. and these redundancies have two main causes: the pursuit of profit and capital accumulation by entrepreneurs or the lack of liquidity in companies due to the recessionary policies promoted by the eu and national governments, which cause the contraction of consumption. the dismissals are the result of concrete policies adopted and implemented by concrete politicians and which are reflected in the majority of the members of this parliament. this report accepts dismissals and advocates that before dismissal different alternatives be studied, among them the renegotiation of 'working conditions'. in other words, it puts workers before the choice of either precariousness or unemployment, which is unacceptable. to assume that restructuring is acceptable in the abstract concept of 'economic change' is to assume that there is no alternative and that redundancies are inevitable, although, as the report says, with minimal impacts. there are alternatives, and today, more than ever, workers are aware of the alternative.

in writing. the territory known as the 'horn of africa' is one of the poorest and most underdeveloped regions in the world, where there is a great deal of insecurity due to all kinds of shortages: food, health, education and, above all, governance. the conditions of insecurity, instability, poverty and bad governance have given rise to criminal activities such as terrorism and piracy that threaten international trade and jeopardise the implementation of the world food programme in the region due to the lack of safe conditions for vessels. the report by mr tannock on the eu strategy for the horn of africa comes at a time when, according to the fao, more than 8 million people are in need of humanitarian aid. i voted in favour because it is urgent that the eu should step up its support for the region, both humanitarian and military, to african countries involved in peacekeeping. i welcome the appointment of a european union special representative for the region and hope that the election of a new somali president and the kenyan elections in 2013 will bring long-term stability that will allow for the functioning of strong and accountable democratic institutions, respect for human rights and enhance economic development in the region.

in writing. − the eu strategy for the horn of africa must address security and stability issues, strengthen the rule of law and ensure fair processes based on effective law enforcement mechanisms and processes, as well as an independent judicial system, while addressing its underlying causes, in particular through development and humanitarian strategies based on clear objectives. the implementation of the eu strategic framework for the horn of africa, which is based on the following points, is of crucial importance: (i) building strong and accountable democratic political structures in all countries; (ii) working with the countries of the region and with regional and international actors and organisations in conflict resolution; (iii) ensuring that the insecurity in the region does not pose a threat to the security of other neighbouring states; (iv) supporting efforts to promote economic growth and poverty reduction; (v) supporting regional political and economic cooperation; (vi) highlighting the importance of promoting sustainable economic growth and poverty reduction in the region, while responding to the basic needs of the population. with the implementation of this strategy, i believe it may be possible to find good solutions for the so-called horn of africa.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, welcoming, both in terms of regional development aid and humanitarian aid, the new plan for the horn of africa proposed by the european commission in 2012, known as share (supporting horn of africa resilience) and designed to become the link between short-term humanitarian aid and long-term development in order to break the vicious circle of crises affecting the region.
in writing. − the horn of africa, which encompasses somalia, ethiopia, djibouti, eritrea, kenya, uganda, sudan and south sudan, is an area that has been ravaged for decades by wars, extreme poverty associated with the problem of food insecurity, terrorism and piracy, lack of health care and very low levels of education. given the particularities of this region and the possible spill-over effects on neighbouring regions, the commission presented a strategy in 2011, followed by the establishment of a special representative for the horn of africa in january 2012, who will be able to coordinate union action with the objectives of the strategy. i would like to focus on three key points: support for the strengthening of regional cooperation by the intergovernmental authority on development, which involves these countries in dialogue and the search for joint solutions; efforts to combat piracy and organised crime; and union support for transition processes, which are crucial moments for countries suffering from great political instability. we must continue to support the development of a region with enormous development potential.

in writing. - i support this report because the preservation of genetic diversity is a key component of the millennium development goals. genetic resources are particularly essential for the sustainability of agriculture and food security. as such, it is imperative to combat the current loss of genetic diversity that occurs through the process of biodiversity erosion, better known as biodiversity piracy. this kind of piracy, which is a challenge to humanity today, is a new challenge for both the owners of this biodiversity and its users, who are generally the rich countries. i therefore believe that the international institutions within the framework of the policy of cohesion for development should support and not contradict the nagoya protocol, considering it to be an effective tool to combat piracy in the field of biodiversity.
in writing. − the protection and preservation of genetic diversity is a key component of the achievement of the millennium development goals. genetic resources (gr) are particularly critical for sustainable agriculture and food security. in this context, biopiracy has emerged as one of the main challenges for developing countries, understood as the situation where biological resources are taken from local communities or indigenous peoples and patented without the profits benefiting the communities where they originate. biopiracy should therefore be one of the major challenges facing the european union, as such practices run counter to the eu's commitments to eradicate poverty and protect europe's biodiversity. the right of farmers to depend on harvested seeds must be safeguarded as an important aspect of the 'right to food'. holders of traditional knowledge should be allowed to maintain, control and protect such knowledge, as it is an important aspect in the fight against biopiracy related to bioprospecting activities. i therefore support this report.

in writing. − genetic resources (gr) are fundamental to sustainable agriculture and food security for all, but are of particular importance for developing countries. moreover, genetic diversity is one of the most important components for the survival of species and the resilience of ecosystems. the loss of genetic diversity resulting from the process of erosion of biodiversity therefore poses a challenge to humanity. despite being vital to human survival, genetic diversity is being lost at an alarming rate. biopiracy - a situation where biological resources are taken from local communities or indigenous peoples and patented, without the resulting profits benefiting the communities where they originate - has emerged as a major concern for developing countries and it is therefore important that the eu takes action to curb and regularize this process.
in writing. the report under review, drawn up by colleague catherine grèze, deals with aspects of the development of intellectual property rights in genetic resources (gr). gmos are essential for sustainable agriculture and enhance food security. however, we have found that ecosystems are experiencing a marked loss of genetic diversity with implications at various levels, including in the achievement of the millennium development goals (mdgs). in view of the scientific advances in this field and the increasing value of these gis, we are witnessing a growing wave of biopiracy which urgently needs to be stopped by clear rules protecting the creators and requiring the inclusion of geographical designations of origin. on the other hand, the large seed companies are trying to change the genetic characteristics of the seeds so that farmers cannot use them on their secondary production cycle farms. this is a situation which needs to be minimised. because this is a matter of great future relevance - we can talk about the survival of several species - i voted in favour of this report and i urge the community authorities to encourage farmers to select and use seeds in accordance with traditional practices.
in writing. the report identifies as a priority the fight against biopiracy, the industrial practice of privatising or patenting the genetic resources or traditional knowledge of indigenous peoples, without the corresponding authorisation or award of compensation to the countries of origin, in most cases developing countries. the rapporteur addresses some of the implications of intellectual property rights in matters of genetic resources, making recommendations that restrict their scope, especially when it comes to ensuring access to food and health in developing countries. these are concerns and recommendations which we share, and the report is generally positive. the eu is called upon, in the context of the implementation of the upov convention, to refrain from supporting the adoption of legislation which could create obstacles to farmers' dependence on harvested seeds, as this would violate the right of access to food in developing countries. it is considered that the eu should not pressure developing countries, particularly ldcs, through bilateral agreements to accept more comprehensive intellectual property standards for seeds and medicines. it is also argued that traditional knowledge should at least enjoy the same level of protection as genetic resources when the nagoya protocol is implemented.

in writing. − the european union's trade policy on intellectual property rights must be consistent with the objective of development policies as enshrined in the eu treaty. biopiracy, that is 'the commercial practice of privatising and patenting traditional knowledge or genetic resources of indigenous peoples without the corresponding authorisation or award of compensation to the countries of origin', is manifested as a practice contrary to the union's commitments in terms of poverty reduction and eradication, protection of biodiversity and the principle of policy coherence in a development perspective, as it criminally prevents the equitable sharing of the benefits resulting from the use of traditional knowledge originating in developing countries. the report therefore calls on the commission to establish mandatory disclosure requirements for the origin of genetic resources during patent applications in order to verify that such patents are legally obtained, in short, to guide the union's development cooperation policies towards poverty eradication and reduction by addressing probity, equity and justice issues in iprs on genetic resources. i voted in favour.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would first of all like to congratulate you on this presidency and, in particular, on the results that ireland has already achieved in its adjustment programme, which are, for a portuguese, a great source of inspiration and hope. i would like to say this: your task is extremely difficult, but it is difficult not only because the challenges are great but especially because the hopes that this parliament and the european citizens place in the irish presidency are perhaps too great. in fact, ireland could not have found a greater historic opportunity for a presidency. at a time when we are experiencing the first symptoms of the crisis coming to an end, when there are interesting results in the euro area, when the situation in greece seems to be calmer, when countries such as portugal and ireland or spain and italy are clearly showing positive signs, at this moment we know that nothing is guaranteed and therefore, having ireland as the presidency is also a source of great inspiration for us, but i think it is something very difficult. the challenge you face is extremely difficult. what did i mean by that? i wanted to say three things basically: we consider the focus on growth to be very positive, we consider the concern for the youth issue to be very important, although i note here that it is often forgotten that in the field of crisis it is the elderly who are suffering the most, particularly because there are pension cuts in virtually all the member states and they also need special attention here. i would like to say one last word just to say this: i had experience working with your minister for european affairs, she was a great advocate of good relations between national parliaments and the european parliament; i hope that she, in her team with the prime minister, can also give the council this example of good cooperation with the european parliament.
it is with great hope that we welcome and welcome the irish presidency. i would like to make three requests to you: firstly, regarding the sovereign debt. we know and hope that ireland will return to the markets to finance itself in the very short term and then we will all benefit from the interventions of the european central bank. my request is that in the two-pack negotiations, when we strengthen economic governance again, we address the question of the euro zone's sovereign debt in such a way as to structure the way it is managed in the future. my second request is about growth and jobs. there is nothing better than the opportunity we have now, when we are discussing the growth prospects for the european union in 2013, to tackle the question of growth and employment and, why not, to review in an objective, clear and calm way what the recommendations and adjustment programmes have been and what in practice has or has not worked or only works when the deadlines are extended and the conditions are reduced. a final note, madam president, and i will end it now, to remind you that in the banking union it is important that we do not end up divided into banks of the first and banks of the second class and that we definitely protect our taxpayers from paying what ireland had to pay for a banking crisis that the citizens ended up having to pay.
stability, jobs, growth is an attractive slogan. unfortunately, the irish presidency's programme replicates the same measures that have been applied in the name of such stability and which are totally contradictory to the objective of promoting employment and growth. reality doesn't lie, the recipe is disastrous. the european semester, which this presidency so dearly cherishes as a solution to stability, means the destruction of public services, privatisation, reduction of wage and pension levels, and therefore more redundancies, more recession, less consumer capacity, more poverty, more vicious circle of social disaster. the question we are asked about the european youth guarantee is this: this instrument should never be a substitute for stable, safe and entitled work. a contract should be given to a job, and all permanent jobs should be given to actual contracts. precariousness must always be combated, because it is the most effective way of perpetuating unemployment, especially among young people. can the irish presidency give us an assurance that it will uphold these principles?
europe is experiencing serious economic and financial difficulties, leading some countries to adopt tough austerity measures to balance public accounts. however, i believe that the european institutions need to adopt more rapidly and effectively some of the measures which are being considered to deepen banking integration. in conjunction with the budgetary balancing measures, i consider it essential that new stimulus measures be adopted to stimulate growth and employment. the eur 10 billion capital increase for the european investment bank, the reindustrialisation of europe and the growing focus on innovation and entrepreneurship are some of the solutions that could lead the european continent to a new phase of economic and social prospecting. i would like to congratulate the irish presidency on setting economic stability, growth and employment as strategic priorities for the next six months. finally, i would point out that the new multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 and the new cohesion policy regulations are due to be adopted in the course of this semester. i hope that there is a broad consensus on the issues in question and i would like to make the council aware of the need to take account of the natural and economic specificities of the eu's outermost regions.

in writing. − the dangerous preparations directive regulates the classification, packaging and labelling of dangerous preparations, i.e. mixtures or solutions of two or more substances. the 1999 directive thus sought to approximate the rules in force in the member states in this field in order to establish a level playing field essential for the proper functioning of the internal market, while seeking to ensure a high level of protection for the general public, consumers and the environment. the proposal aims to update the directive in the light of the lisbon treaty and to take account of new eu legislation adopted in the meantime on this subject, such as the reach regulation. it thus intends to replace provisions which have become obsolete, such as the updating of the legal basis, in order to ensure the clarity and accuracy of the applicable rules. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal, which does not contain any substantive amendments, but merely codifies the existing text without any substantive changes.

in writing. - the mediterranean sea is undergoing a high fishing pressure which may jeopardise the sustainability of its fisheries resources. it is necessary to protect them and at the same time to ensure the survival of the fishing communities and the fishing companies operating there. this balance is obviously delicate but cannot help being permanently tested. the european commission and the european parliament have been following this issue and i am sure they are trying to make sure that it has the best possible legal framework. despite this common position in principle, in practice the institutions differ as to how and to what extent the commission should act. i hope that we can reach an agreement and that the formal question of commission acts does not overlap with the substantive interest which underlies them and that this can be properly defended.
in writing. the mediterranean sea is a unique environment, with a rich diversity of habitats and ecosystems. from an excellent sea route for transporting goods, to marine resources, to tourism potential, all this space powers. if in the past it was a natural barrier, today it is a link between the north (europe) and the south (africa); between the east (middle east and asia) and the west (atlantic). given its high potential, it is important that it is properly protected. one of the potentialities that deserves the most attention is fisheries resources. we all know the biodiversity that this sea contains and the threats to which it is subject. management measures to ensure the sustainable exploitation of fishery resources in the mediterranean sea are therefore urgently needed. because i believe it is essential to adopt a sustainable management plan that will help member states to benefit from this means, i voted in favour of the report drawn up by my colleague anna rosbach on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1967/2006 on the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources in the mediterranean sea.
in writing. - this is another report which seeks to amend the regulation (of 2006) on management measures for the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources in the mediterranean sea in order to bring it into line with article 290 tfeu as regards the delegation of acts to the commission. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a very good one. we have serious reservations about the (unjustified) discretionary power given to the commission, which now has the power to amend member states' management measures and plans. we cannot agree more on the need for sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources. however, we believe that it is mainly through local management - involving the sector and the communities in the definition and implementation of measures - that this sustainable exploitation can be achieved. the harmful effects of overly centralised management are clearly visible in the more than 30 years of the common fisheries policy. that is why we abstained.

in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1967/2006 on management measures for the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources in the mediterranean sea is one of the first fisheries sector documents to be aligned with the new system of delegated and implementing acts, and it is therefore of the utmost importance to find a sound and well-founded legal solution to safeguard the rights conferred by the lisbon treaty on the european parliament. in this context, this report seeks to identify the powers delegated to the commission in regulation (ec) no 1967/2006 and to lay down the procedures for the adoption of those delegated acts. the report proposes the application of delegated acts with a limited duration, so as to allow a regular assessment of their usefulness. the report proposes that the commission should be empowered to adopt delegated acts where member states adopt national measures which are subsequently monitored by the commission, where the member states' measures are considered unsatisfactory. in the event that member states adopt national measures that may affect the fishing fleet of other member states, the report also proposes the adoption of delegated acts. given the relevance of these legislative measures to the sustainable management and exploitation of fishery resources in the mediterranean sea, i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. the convention on biological diversity (cbd) entered into force on 29 december 1993. the cartagena protocol on biosafety was adopted on 29 january 2000 as a complementary agreement to the cbd and entered into force on 11 september 2003. this international treaty provides a framework, based on the precautionary principle, for the safe transfer, handling and use of living modified organisms (lmos) resulting from modern biotechnologies, which may have adverse effects on the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity or involve risks to human health. at the fifth conference of the parties in nagoya, the eu unanimously supported the final compromise reached on the nagoya-kuala lumpur supplementary protocol on civil liability and indemnity, which parliament now approves.
in writing. − the cartagena protocol on biosafety annexed to the convention on biological diversity is an international treaty governing the transboundary movements of living modified organisms (lmos) resulting from modern biotechnologies. in the context of the cartagena protocol, the nagoya-kuala lumpur supplementary protocol on civil liability and indemnity, annexed to the cartagena protocol on biosafety, focuses mainly on the procedures and requirements for the intervention measures that it is required to take in the event of damage caused by lmos that may have adverse effects on the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity or involve risks to human health. i believe that this protocol will make a considerable contribution to the achievement of the objectives of the convention on biological diversity and the cartagena protocol on biosafety. it should be noted that this supplementary protocol has been signed by the majority of the member states and that it is now important for them to ratify it.
in writing. the report welcomes the conclusion of the agreement on behalf of the european union and considers that the nagoya-kuala lumpur supplementary protocol on civil liability and indemnity will make a significant contribution to the achievement of the objectives of the convention on biological diversity and the cartagena protocol on biosafety, which deserves our support. the international rules and procedures in the field of civil liability and compensation for loss and damage resulting from transboundary movements of living modified organisms resulting from modern biotechnologies are at issue. that protocol establishes a procedure for prior informed consent, designed to provide member states with the information necessary to take informed decisions before they allow the importation of those organisms into their territory, which seems to us to be correct. for these reasons, we voted in favour.

in writing. - under article 34 of the convention on biological diversity, any protocol annexed to the convention is subject to ratification by the signatory states. this convention integrated the cartagena protocol on 29 january 2000 as a complementary agreement to the cbd, providing a framework for the safe transfer, handling and use of living modified organisms based on the precautionary principle. however, the parties to the cartagena protocol subsequently met in conference to unanimously support a supplementary protocol, which obliges states to provide in their own domestic law for rules and procedures applicable in the event of damage, and to consider intervention measures to prevent or mitigate damage, or to restore biological diversity in the event of an accident. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's environmental policy is not distorted by the use of chemical weapons, and calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's environmental policy is not distorted by the use of chemical weapons. i voted in favour.

in writing. − the question of public finances in the countries of the economic and monetary union (emu) in the context of the economic and financial crisis is a very delicate one, since unhealthy public finances can jeopardise the economic and social development of countries as well as their political stability. in this respect, it is urgent to ensure a sustainable balance in the finances of the member states, and to ensure less imbalance and greater budgetary and economic integration, accompanied by greater solidarity between member states. although many challenges remain in controlling excessive debt and deficits, some virtuous steps have been taken to ensure further fiscal consolidation and balance and to contain contagion between countries. parliament considered that countries should channel their efforts towards medium- and long-term budgetary balance strategies, taking into account the need to generate growth and development accompanied by fair social protection and improvements in the quality of life of citizens. the countries' focus should be on implementing measures such as pension reform, promotion of public and private investment, assertive public spending cuts and structural reforms. i agree with the content of this report and i vote in favour.

in writing. the economic and financial crisis affecting most member states (ms) has led to an average unemployment rate in the european union of 11%. this situation has forced member states to adopt austerity and budgetary austerity measures which have led to public divestment and, consequently, the bankruptcy of many companies. unfortunately, most of the budgetary restraint measures implemented were not accompanied by strategic reforms. in this context, we need reforms and new policies leading to a genuine monetary union. the fight against fraud and tax evasion, as well as the focus on research, education and programmes to support youth employment, must be at the forefront of eu investment. i voted in favour of the report drawn up by mr alfredo pallone on public finances in emu and i welcome the recommendations to cut non-productive expenditure. as a consequence of the measures taken by the member states, we see that public finances are improving, as is market confidence, which is fundamental to economic recovery. although i am aware that it is not easy to reconcile economic growth with fiscal consolidation, i think that this is the path the eu must take.

in writing. − unfortunately, the economic, financial and banking crisis shows no signs of abating and has exposed public finance issues that negatively affect socioeconomic development and political stability. we are aware that the recent reforms of the economic and budgetary governance framework of the european union cannot, on their own, solve the crisis; comprehensive action is therefore needed to address macro-financial imbalances symmetrically and to increase overall the level of socio-economic convergence and solidarity within the framework of economic and monetary union. credible commitments to growth-friendly austerity measures are needed to find sustainable solutions to the excessive debt and deficit situations in most euro area member states. only with the efforts of each and every one of us will it be possible in the medium term to find our way back to growth.

in writing. - i welcome this report, which is an important step towards the freedom of the member states to rely on credit rating agencies. government debt ratings will have to be subject to specific rules in order to take into account the specificities of sovereign debt ratings. the sovereign debt rating should be considered as a specific rating with specific requirements. we cannot allow national economies to continue to be assessed without clear criteria and methodology. the new rules on sovereign debt ratings could prevent credit rating agencies from interfering with the political agenda. in addition, this is the first time we have a roadmap for the creation of a european rating agency that could be proposed by the commission by the end of 2016. this agency would ensure the ratings of the sovereign debt of the member states.
in writing. − a credit rating agency rates certain financial products or assets (from companies, governments or countries), evaluates, grades and ranks them according to the degree of risk in meeting their debts within the set deadline. these agencies therefore help to set a fair price for the assets concerned. with the outbreak of the financial and sovereign debt crisis, these agencies have been accused of having fuelled the crisis by frivolous or erroneous valuations of some assets, which distorts markets and harms both investors and issuers. the european commission's proposal to regulate the operation of rating agencies thus aims to increase transparency, reduce the over-reliance of markets on ratings, introduce the civil liability of agencies to investors and avoid potential conflicts of interest. the emphasis is on promoting less reliance on external ratings, limiting cross-shareholdings of shareholders in several agencies or between them and their clients, rules on rotation, prohibition of arbitrary publication of ratings, etc. given the importance of these measures for the stability of markets, especially sovereign debt, i give my full support to this report.

in writing. − the activity of credit rating agencies (cras) has a strong impact on the behaviour of economic agents as well as on public institutions. in the recent financial and sovereign debt crisis, these agencies have been accused of having fuelled the crisis by frivolous or erroneous valuations of certain assets, distorting markets and harming both investors and the issuers of these assets. the current sovereign debt crisis has underlined the need to review the procedural, transparency and timeliness requirements for publication, in particular for sovereign ratings, often because of the negative effects that less transparent or less timely publication of ratings has caused in many countries. i support and welcome the new regulation proposed by the commission, which on the one hand will oblige nras to have a specific timetable, a methodology and sources of information for calculating transparent ratings and reduce the excessive reliance on external ratings by investors and bond issuers. i welcome the introduction of the civil liability of agencies for wilful misconduct or gross negligence in their assessments and rules on conflicts of interest between these assessments and a shareholder or member.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support the introduction of new rules relating to the activity of credit rating agencies, which aim to increase transparency, reduce the excessive reliance of markets on credit ratings, introduce the civil liability of agencies towards investors and avoid potential conflicts of interest.
in writing. − there are 23 agencies registered in the eu, but standard & poor's, moody's and fitch have a 96% share of the market (45%, 38% and 13% respectively). the untimely publication of sovereign ratings has contributed to the disruption and destabilisation of markets. therefore, from now on, credit rating agencies should establish an annual rating calendar with a maximum of 3 unsolicited ratings. these ratings shall be published on the friday following the close of trading and at least one hour before the opening of trading. we shall thus have greater transparency. there is now an eu-wide civil liability regime that will protect investors and issuers. the question of conflict of interest is also regulated. the new rules prohibit shareholders of rating agencies (who hold 10% or more of the capital and/or voting rights) from holding 10% or more of the shares in the rated entity. the possibility of owning more than 5% of the capital or voting rights in more than one agency is also blocked, unless they belong to the same group.
in writing. - this report contains positive measures that in some way limit some of the harmful effects of credit rating agencies. examples are challenging the ecb's reliance on agency risk ratings and eliminating some of the automatic effects of ratings that were at the root of the bankruptcies of companies like enron. these measures are part of the commission's stated objective of reducing over-reliance on credit rating agencies. the question is whether, even if reduced, dependence should be maintained or not. with this legislation, it will stand. the european commission itself acknowledges that there may be alternatives to credit ratings, but it is postponing its study until 2015 and its possible implementation until after that date. in other words, the eu and its governments were quick to make people pay for the private debt of the banks, they were quick to put the costs of financial capital's mismanagement on the backs of the workers, but when it comes to challenging the power of this financial capital, the finer things... what is needed is public, democratic control of the entire financial system, freeing it from the clutches of big speculative financial capital.
in writing. − the activity of credit rating agencies has a significant impact on the behaviour of economic and financial actors and on the life of public institutions, and continues to generate considerable public interest and heated political debate. the regulation of these agencies is very important and represents a specific and very sensitive aspect of the more general process of reforming the functioning of financial markets. we must therefore launch a debate which takes account of the different approaches and points of view, but which serves to give the nras an appropriate dimension, which implies that their assessments are treated as information to be taken into account, without the agencies benefiting from a special status and having decisive consequences for the activities of economic and financial operators and public institutions. only then can they be part of a system which is becoming increasingly transparent and in which the information circulating is reliable.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the domenici report on the regulation of credit rating agencies because reality has shown that there is a need to extend and strengthen existing regulation. after having ignored and contested, before the crisis, the factors that caused it, the rating agencies contributed, from the beginning of the crisis, to its aggravation. so the new measures - more conflict of interest control, civil liability to investors, limitations on unsolicited sovereign debt valuations, a ban on national policy recommendations and, above all, less reliance on one's own valuations - are in the right direction. the crisis had its origin in the deregulation of financial markets. at least the crisis will lead to more regulation - and european regulation - to prevent future crises.

in writing. − credit rating agencies provide their opinions and research on credit risk and play a very important role in financial markets, as they provide very useful information to investors, such as undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits) and alternative investment funds (aifs). however, credit rating agencies should not be the sole assessors of credit risk and investors should not blindly or automatically focus on credit rating agencies; instead, they should make their own internal assessments and use the ratings only as a source of advisory information and not in a mechanistic way. in this respect, limiting the influence of the agencies' role in the functioning of the markets as well as their preponderance in some pieces of legislation is essential and their presence should be phased out. investors should also consider the views of more than one agency and highlight the work of smaller agencies, avoiding concentration of market shares and promoting more competition in this sector. the report is a good example of the need to ensure that the european union is able to take action to combat the risks of credit risk.
