in writing. - the present report, by jarosław leszek wałęsa, concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1098/2007 of 18 september 2007 establishing a multiannual plan for the cod stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. since the abovementioned regulation entered into force before the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), certain amendments of a technical nature are necessary. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the basis of article j.3 of the treaty on european union, which provides that the council is to adopt a decision on the basis of article j.3 of the treaty on european union. i voted in favour of this report, as the proposed amendments contribute to a better functioning of the multiannual plan. the fisheries reserves of the baltic sea represent an important food resource which must be urgently preserved on the basis of the co-decision procedure introduced by the treaty of lisbon. the report also allows vessels of less than 12 metres to operate fixed gear within the 10 mile zone and with a submersion time of less than 48 hours, thus contributing to the economic sustainability of small fishing communities.
in writing. − this report follows the commission's proposal for council regulation (ec) no 1098/2007 establishing a multiannual plan for cod stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. as this regulation was adopted before the entry into force of the tfeu, the commission considers it necessary to amend it in accordance with article 290 of the treaty on the delegation of powers. the rapporteur has made some amendments to improve the text. it introduces the need for the commission to consult the baltic sea regional advisory council, relevant stakeholders and the scientific, technical and economic committee for fisheries (stecf) in the evaluation process of the multiannual plan. it adds a new paragraph which allows small-scale fisheries to catch cod during defensive periods without this having a negative impact on pre- and spawning concentrations because they occur far from coastal areas. we voted in favour.
in writing. - the adoption of this report establishes the multiannual plan for cod stocks in the baltic sea, bringing it into line with the decision-making structure introduced by the treaty of lisbon. it is of particular importance that the commission carry out appropriate consultations with the baltic sea regional advisory council and all relevant stakeholders, including at expert level, in order to ensure that the cod stocks in the baltic sea are exploited in a sustainable manner, taking into account economic, social and environmental concerns. it is also important to stress here that, given the increase in cod stocks, the amendment to the report will allow small-scale cod fishing to do so during the fishing season, as this can be economically important for small-scale fishing in view of the prices charged during that period.
in writing. − the main objective of this report is to ensure that the baltic cod stocks are exploited in an environmentally, economically and socially sustainable manner. to achieve that objective, the multiannual plan shall lay down rules for the establishment of annual fishing opportunities in terms of fishing effort and total allowable catches. this proposal introduces amendments to allow the multiannual plan to operate efficiently in the light of the codecision system established by the treaty of lisbon. the report proposes that the management plan should define the maximum fishing mortality rate in this area in accordance with the scientific advice of ices. in addition, the report allows vessels smaller than 12 metres to operate fixed gear within the 10 mile area and with a submersion time of less than 48 hours. this change will allow small-scale fishing vessels to catch cod in coastal areas during the summer, when the species reaches higher prices, with the consequent economic benefits for this segment of the fleet. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it to be an important element in improving the regulation, management and sustainable exploitation of this baltic sea fishery.
in writing. - this report follows the commission's proposal to adapt regulation (ec) no 1098/2007 (establishing a multiannual plan for cod stocks in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks) to the new rules of the lisbon treaty. on the basis of this proposal, the rapporteur has proposed a number of additional amendments which, in general, deserve our agreement. in this respect, the amendment which allows small-scale vessels to catch cod during defensive periods, in particular during the summer months, without having a negative impact on pre-spaw concentrations and spawning concentrations, which occur in deep areas of the baltic sea away from coastal areas, is particularly noteworthy. this is an important measure which will enable this fleet segment to achieve significant economic gains. i voted in favour.

in writing. − regional fisheries management depends to a large extent on technical measures for the conservation of fishery resources and on annual and biennial decisions on catch possibilities. the criteria under which catch is to be made and the extension of the validity of the current technical measures have a considerable impact on the achievement of the objectives of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. − technical measures for the protection of juveniles of marine organisms must be complied with by fishermen in order to ensure the conservation of species and the renewal of their numbers. these must be designed with the purpose in mind and must not be of such a nature as to make fishing unreasonably difficult or unreasonably demanding. the common fisheries policy is aimed at individuals and families - fishermen, businesses and consumers - and must therefore seek to safeguard the interests of all so that they can benefit from fisheries in a satisfactory and environmentally sustainable way. given the transitional nature of technical conservation measures and the need to extend their duration before a more ambitious interinstitutional agreement is reached, i give my consent to this extension.
in writing. − a large part of our food comes from marine environments: fish, molluscs, crustaceans, algae, etc. all depend on the quality of the ecosystems in which they live and, of course, on how they are managed. sustained management of these resources ensures not only the quality but also the quantity of these resources. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. for years, the lack of management measures has led to the extinction of some fish species and in other cases to a sharp reduction in their stocks. in this respect, the preservation of juveniles of marine organisms is essential, as it ensures the renewal of species. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that technical measures for the conservation of fisheries resources, such as 'minimum landing sizes, minimum mesh size, fishing defence zones and periods, limitation of by-catches, the criterion for using more selective fishing gear and measures to protect the marine environment', should be maintained until the new common fisheries policy of the european union comes into force.
in writing. − the european union has exclusive competence to lay down technical measures laying down rules on fishing zones and fishing gear and the fishing effort and/or authorised catches. the eu is also responsible for adopting technical measures to ensure the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources, including measures to protect juveniles of marine organisms. the proposal for a regulation presented by the commission, although updating existing measures concerning the protection of juveniles of marine organisms, following the opinion of the scientific, technical and economic committee for fisheries and the recommendations of the north-east atlantic fisheries commission, remains transitional rather than definitive. the transitional nature creates legal uncertainty for fishermen and their union fishing fleet. i therefore agree with pat the cope gallagher when he says that a permanent solution must be found for the protection of juvenile organisms. i think it is important to stress that, although they are transitional, these measures are of paramount importance given the objective of ensuring sustainable fishing by preserving endangered ecosystems and species. in view of the above, i have voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i approve this report, considering that, in my view, according to the afco's interpretation of rule 13 (1) of the rules of procedure, in a situation of equality between candidates and vacancies, the president may be elected by acclamation or, alternatively, by secret ballot as provided for in rule 169. in the event of a runoff election, the president also decides on the order of precedence of the vice-presidents (article 15 (2), second subparagraph). i note the concern that could be aroused by the fact that such a decision, taken by the president, would not be unanimous. to remedy this situation, i agree that a solution could be to allow a number of members or a political group to challenge the order of precedence proposed by the president or simply to remove the possibility for the president to set the order of precedence, which would automatically lead to a vote.

in writing. - practices and practices, which are sometimes undervalued, are important and sometimes decisive elements of parliamentary life. my experience as a member of the european parliament, as well as as a member and leader of a national parliamentary group, leads me to take these into account and not to disregard their real importance. i therefore believe that the proposed regulation amendment is welcome, although it seems to be a trifle that is indifferent to the actual work of the european parliament and has no direct interest for the citizens, because it is intended to adapt the letter of the law to the practice that has been followed with regard to the order of precedence of the vice-presidents.
in writing. - mr carlo casini drew up a report on the amendment of rule 15 (2) of parliament's rules of procedure (pe) concerning the order of precedence of vice-presidents elected by acclamation. rule 15 (2) of the ep's rules of procedure reads as follows: without prejudice to article 18 (1), the order of precedence of the vice-presidents shall be determined by the order in which they were elected and, in the event of an equal number of votes, by their age. if the election has not been by secret ballot, the order of precedence shall be that in which the president called the election. although not required by the ep's rules of procedure, when the election of a vice-president had not been held by secret ballot, the order of precedence was already established by secret ballot. i voted in favour of this report, which deals with a regulation amendment which is intended to legalise a current practice and thus bring more transparency to the workings of this parliament.
in writing. - in the procedure for electing the vice-presidents of the european parliament, the president has the power, in accordance with the rules of procedure, to determine the order of precedence of the vice-presidents, if the election has not been held by secret ballot, as it corresponds to the order of call made by the president. the report seeks to amend this provision by changing the order of precedence to be established by secret ballot. we believe that transparency should be present in our daily lives and, above all, in all acts relating to public affairs. we believe that the amendment now tabled serves this principle and we have therefore supported it. one of the amendments tabled, concerning the way in which vice-presidents are elected, could possibly favour the election of vice-presidents from smaller groups and, in so doing, contribute to a greater plurality in the composition of parliament's bureau, which would be a positive thing.
in writing. - the adoption of this report is merely to propose an amendment to the rules of procedure in order to bring it into line with the practice of the european parliament as regards the order of precedence of vice-presidents.
in writing. − practice in the european parliament states that when there is agreement between the political groups on the persons to be appointed to the vice-presidencies, these persons (as a rule) are elected by acclamation. however, after that act, the order of precedence shall be determined by voting and by the number of votes cast. this vote is justified because the political groups can agree on persons, but they can never agree on the order of precedence. in this case, the president waives his (legally existing) right to establish the order of precedence. if the political groups cannot agree on the persons to be elected, or if 'independent' candidates have been submitted, a vote shall be taken, the order of precedence being determined by the number of votes obtained at the ballot. as these procedures are not clearly laid down in the rules of procedure of the european parliament, i voted in favour of this draft report which proposes to amend the rules of procedure in order to bring them into line with the practice of the european parliament, thus responding to the concern expressed by the president of the european parliament in 2010.
in writing. - this report aims to clarify and apply the procedure for the order of precedence of vice-presidents elected by acclamation to the practice in force in the european parliament (ep). thus, after a request for interpretation of rules 13 and 15 of the ep's rules of procedure, it was established that in the case of the election of a vice-president by acclamation, precedence should be established by secret ballot and not by choice of the president. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that this amendment will put an end to the concerns and disagreements expressed by several members.

in writing. the number of passengers travelling by air has been increasing by an average of 4.5% per year, making it necessary and urgent to review the existing rules on the protection of air passengers' rights in order to strengthen the existing level of legal certainty and create greater uniformity of application across the eu. the legal framework for the protection of these rights should ensure a minimum level of consumer protection that is resistant to the evolution of commercial practices of air carriers, in particular the introduction of restrictive measures such as the 'one-volume hand baggage' rule, the specification of essential and non-essential items and other restrictions on the admission of cabin baggage. the commission should examine the feasibility and practicability of creating a single legislative instrument that includes all provisions and principles on consumer rights in civil aviation in order to reduce fragmentation, inconsistencies and excessive restrictions. the necessary measures should therefore be introduced to harmonise commercial practice on hand baggage, protecting passengers from excessive restrictions and allowing them to bring on board a reasonable amount of hand baggage, including purchases made in airport shops.
the commission has already submitted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. at the end of 2005, the european commission presented a draft regulation introducing the compulsory origin marking scheme for certain products imported from third countries. the objectives of this proposal were, first, to prevent the use of false or misleading marks of origin, to improve consumer information on the origin of certain products, and to put european products on an equal footing with their trading partners, in particular canada, china, japan and the united states of america, which already require imported products to bear origin labels. the european parliament has always supported the creation of the mandatory origin marking scheme, as indicated in its resolutions adopted in 2006 and 2009. it is therefore not surprising that in october 2010, already under the new legislative powers in trade matters arising from the treaty of lisbon, the european parliament adopted a position at first reading on the draft european commission regulation on the indication of the country of origin on certain products imported from third countries with 529 votes in favour, 49 against and 44 abstentions. subsequently, and despite repeated requests from parliament, the council failed to adopt a common position, effectively blocking the legislative process. recently, in a surprising twist, the commission announced that it would withdraw the regulation currently in force in 2003, claiming that the decision of the world trade organisation panel on the country of origin labelling case for beef and pigmeat had changed the world trade organisation's case law and consequently made the original proposal for a made in regulation incompatible with wto rules. so we ask: firstly, why does the commission choose to withdraw the proposal instead of proposing the necessary amendments to make the regulation compatible with the wto, including, if necessary, a new legal basis to be adopted by the co-legislators under the current procedure during the second reading or in possible trilogues; secondly, does the commission not consider that, in the spirit of good interinstitutional cooperation and respect for the european citizens represented by the adoption of the regulation by a large majority of parliament, it should have consulted parliament and allowed sufficient time for discussion before announcing the withdrawal? does the commission consider that the withdrawal of the regulation is in the general interest of the european union? thirdly, what elements of the original proposal or the text of the proposal adopted by parliament at first reading are no longer compatible with the wto and why? following the wto panel and the appellate body decisions, what is the commission's position on the mandatory origin marking schemes required by many other countries for imported products, such as brazil, canada and the united states? fourthly, and last but not least, what concrete measures does the commission intend to take to ensure the indication of origin and thus the traceability of products imported from third countries in the single market, at least in the sectors already covered by the regulation? what's the timetable? finally, and with that i conclude, does the commission intend to submit a new proposal for this regulation in accordance with the new wto rules and, if so, when?

free trade agreements can make an important contribution to economic dynamism, job creation and wealth generation. unfortunately, however, farming has too often served as a bargaining chip for good deals in services and industry. also in the case of the potential agreement between the european union and mercosur, the 2011 impact study of the european commission showed the damage it would bring to agriculture in europe. this is a situation which must be denounced and rejected, for the sake of european farmers, whose incomes are falling and whose production is threatened, but also for the sake of the whole agri-food industry, which benefits from the production of the internal market, and also for the sake of consumers, who have the guarantee of food quality and hygiene, as well as compliance with environmental and animal welfare rules. these losses are aggravated in vulnerable regions and in relation to sensitive products, such as meat production in the azores. it should also be stressed that the maintenance of a strong european agriculture guarantees the food independence of the european union, which is absolutely fundamental from the point of view of political strategy. these aspects must be taken into account when negotiations are resumed.

in writing. - i am convinced that the approval of this partnership and cooperation agreement between the european union and iraq will contribute to the development of iraq and represents a greater commitment by the eu to the future of that country. it should be noted that for some years the eu was somewhat aloof from iraq; i am therefore pleased to see a new commitment in eu-iraq relations with the approval of this agreement. given its geostrategic importance and the great suffering its people have already suffered, iraq cannot remain outside the european concerns, but must be the subject of joint efforts.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report in the belief that the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european union and the republic of iraq is an important step towards eu collaboration in the transition in iraq, which is properly framed and agreed between the parties. the european union's commitments must be translated into the mobilization of human and financial resources consistent with the political ambitions proclaimed therein.
in writing. − this partnership and cooperation agreement is a historic step towards the opening of relations between the european union and iraq at a time when the country needs the support of the international community for the establishment of a genuine democratic state, where the rule of law must be the basis of national cohesion. the agreement, which is renewable for 10 years, is based on three areas: political, economic and cooperation in the field of social and human development. it is essential that iraq join the international criminal court with the support of the union. on the other hand, the fight against terrorism and the fight against the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction is also a central objective of the eu. the question of human rights and their conditionality is of the utmost importance in an iraq where sectarian wars are a reality. finally, i would like to stress the need for cooperation in social development programmes to improve the quality of life of people in one of the poorest countries in the world. basic access to health, education and employment are the key to the harmonious development of this country.
in writing. - with the signing of this agreement, the eu intends to seize a share of iraq's natural resources, particularly its oil resources. the signing of this agreement is part of the imperialist offensive to re-colonize, which, as in iraq, continues to target regions with a high concentration of natural resources, raw materials and energy routes. the majority of meps are not concerned that iraq remains a country in a state of war and de facto occupation and that its people are denied the right to sovereignty and self-determination in accordance with their aspirations and interests of economic and social development. in iraq, as in the entire middle east region, imperialism has not hesitated to use the worst instruments to achieve its goals, including terrorist attacks, coups d'état, alliances with neo-fascist forces, the promotion of political-religious powers and various counter-revolutionary forces of different ideological backgrounds all in function of imperialist domination, redrawing borders and reorganizing sectoral markets, in particular the energy market with its oil and natural gas resources and its transportation routes.

in writing. - zimbabwe has shown in recent years that it is finally on the road to economic, social and human development. the entry into force of the human rights commission act in zimbabwe is a measure which gives us hope that this country intends to work from now on to mitigate situations of human rights violations. the eu supports and will continue to support the government in harare. however, until the country's path towards sustainable development is consolidated, the suspension of eu development cooperation (under article 96 of the cotonou agreement) should be maintained, although the eu is committed to supporting the zimbabwean people.
in writing. - the proposal concerns the implementation of an economic partnership agreement (epa) between the european community and the states of eastern and southern africa in the light of the current situation in zimbabwe; a provisional epa has been in force since 14 may 2012 between madagascar, mauritius, seychelles and zimbabwe, on the one hand, and the eu, on the other. it is an agreement aimed at 'supporting regional integration through trade development, sustainable growth and poverty reduction, while promoting the gradual integration of acp economies into the world economy'. zimbabwe, a beneficiary country under this agreement despite the entry into force of the human rights commission act which is a step forward in improving the human rights situation still has many violations of fundamental rights and guarantees. the government of national unity of zimbabwe continues to persecute journalists and the civilian population. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because, given that elections are due to be held this year, zimbabwe must be given an opportunity to gain international credibility by respecting human rights and fundamental freedoms.
in writing. − this is the first interim economic partnership agreement (epa) with countries in the african region to enter into force. the epas are part of the eu's push to force african countries to sign the so-called economic partnership agreements (epas), despite their numerous resistance. in this resolution, parliament welcomed the agreement, considering that the epas are a step forward for african countries and for the promotion of fair and open trade, investment and regional integration. anyway, the usual rhetoric. parliament's concern about the signing of this agreement is linked to the lack of democratic transparency and human rights abuses in zimbabwe. but as for the rest, and despite this, the maxim that prevails is the same as always: business as usual. nothing is said about the harmful effects of free trade, the appropriation by multinational companies of natural resources and biodiversity, the increase in unemployment, the weakening of small-scale and family farming and the threats to food sovereignty and security. while rejecting this resolution, we express here our full solidarity with the people of zimbabwe and the other peoples of east and southern africa for their right to development, sovereignty and independence.

in writing. the european parliament resolution on the implementation of the interim economic partnership agreement between the european community and the states of eastern and southern africa, in the light of the current situation in zimbabwe, considers the provisional entry into force of the interim economic partnership agreement to be positive. i voted in favour of this entry into force as an important step towards consolidating the partnership between the eu and the four african countries concerned within a stable legal framework which will allow negotiations to continue with a view to a full-fledged agreement capable of fostering open and fair trade, investment and regional integration.
in writing. the agreement aims to guarantee access to the european single market for the republic of mauritius, the republic of madagascar, the republic of seychelles and the republic of zimbabwe through a system of exemption from quotas and tariffs on exports from these countries. this economic partnership agreement between the eu and the four countries referred to above is an instrument of economic development tailored to their needs and to their economic capacities. however, human rights violations continue to occur in zimbabwe, calling into question the international commitment made by the government of national unity. it should be noted that the human rights violations were carried out by the government itself. i therefore join the rapporteurs in urging the zimbabwean government to comply with its international obligations, or else the eu institutions, with the support of the european parliament, will suspend development cooperation with the country. i also support all the measures taken by the eu to respond to the human rights violations that have occurred in this southern african country. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. - i approve the recommendation, considering that in 2000, the acp states and the eu agreed to establish new trade agreements compatible with the rules of the world trade organisation to replace the unilateral trade preferences regime applied by the eu to imports from the acp countries, which was then in force. under the cotonou agreement, the integration of the acp states into the world economy, the promotion of their sustainable development and the creation of more effective regional markets with predictable and stable standards are the cornerstones of this approach. these new agreements will be based on eu development cooperation, which aims to strengthen the acp states' institutional and production capacities and to support the necessary adaptation processes. since the epas aim to develop and strengthen regional integration processes in the acp states, negotiations were held at regional level with six regional epa groupings defined by the acp states themselves. since then, cariforum has been the only regional group to sign a full epa. i therefore believe that this recommendation should be taken into account when we conclude an economic partnership agreement between the eastern and southern african states and the european community.

in writing. − the interim agreement establishing a framework for an economic partnership agreement (epa) between the states of eastern and southern africa should be seen as a pillar in economic relations between the eu and that region. like my colleague daniel caspary, i believe that the signing of the interim epa is a necessary step towards sustainable growth in the region and highlights the importance of continuing negotiations towards a comprehensive agreement that will promote trade, investment and integration in the region.
in writing. − on 14 may 2012, an interim economic partnership agreement (epa) entered into force between madagascar, mauritius, the seychelles and zimbabwe, on the one hand, and the eu, on the other. it is an agreement aimed at 'supporting regional integration through trade development, sustainable growth and poverty reduction, while promoting the gradual integration of acp economies into the world economy'. the main objective of this apep is to promote the integration of the regional economy into the world economy and to support the development of these countries. in view of the situation in some countries, notably zimbabwe, with regard to the violation of human rights and fundamental guarantees, governments should be alerted to the existence of safeguard clauses providing for the suspension of the agreement in the event of a violation of human rights. i voted in favour of the recommendation drawn up by my colleague daniel caspary, not only because it promotes trade relations between the eu and these four countries in eastern and southern africa, but also because i believe it is a fundamental step towards promoting free trade and the implementation of democratic regimes that function normally, without corruption or fraud and with respect for human rights.
in writing. the report also stresses that the eu's economic partnership agreements (epas) are based on eu development cooperation, which aims to strengthen the acp states' institutional and production capacities and support the necessary adaptation processes. the fact that few acp countries have ratified them to date will be contrary to the good intentions expressed, as well as to the claims that these agreements support regional integration. our position is well known and we reiterate it here, namely that we are opposed to the epas, which are genuine free trade agreements that the eu wants to impose by force, using blackmail if necessary, as it has shown on several occasions. the edf itself is once again being used as a blackmail weapon at a time when its financial volume for 2014-2020 is being discussed. the desired opening up of markets is of course in the interests of the large european economic groups, which want to sell goods and services, exploit raw materials and impose an export-oriented production model in their own interests. this epa will have serious consequences for small farmers and workers in europe and africa and for development objectives in general. obviously, we voted against it.
in writing. − the interim agreement establishing a framework for an economic partnership agreement (epa) between the eastern and southern african states and the ec is an important step towards the further deepening of economic relations between these two regions. it is also the beginning of a path that will lead to more sustainable growth in this region, as well as to a future comprehensive agreement that will foster trade, investment and integration in the region.

in writing. the rapporteur suggests that the provisional agreement be adopted, reinforcing the partnership between the signatory states, bringing it into line with the rules of the world trade organisation and replacing the unilateral system which gave the acp countries preferential access to eu markets on a non-reciprocal basis. the agreement now provides not only for access to exports by the acp countries but also for the gradual opening up of their markets to european exports in the coming years. this interim contractual relationship achieves greater legal certainty, which is essential for improving the trade and investment climate in the eastern and southern african states. in line with the objectives of the cotonou agreement, this interim agreement seeks to promote sustainable development and the creation of more effective regional markets, which can only be achieved by reducing and eventually eradicating poverty through predictable and stable standards.
in writing. − this agreement is of great importance given that it is the first time that the eu has signed a bilateral agreement of a regional nature on the african continent, thus promoting its regional economic integration. the aim of the agreement is to grant access to the european single market to the republic of mauritius, the republic of madagascar, the republic of seychelles and the republic of zimbabwe through a system of exemption from quotas and tariffs on exports from these countries. in contrast, the african countries involved should gradually open their markets to eu exports. this will ensure an investment climate conducive to the development of the secondary sector in these countries. this economic partnership agreement between the eu and the four abovementioned countries is a tailor-made economic development instrument designed to meet their economic requirements and capabilities. in line with the development strategy defined by both parties and in line with the legal framework of the world trade organisation, i believe that this agreement will be a socio-economic asset for all its stakeholders. in view of the above, i have voted in favour of the report.
in writing. the report also stresses that the eu's economic and social cohesion policy is a key element of the eu's economic and social cohesion policy. the fact that only four of the 16 acp countries have ratified the epa contradicts those who advocate the supporting role of these agreements for regional integration. in fact, what the eu wants is the liberalisation of trade, from which its large financial and economic groups seek to secure the opening of markets, sell goods and services, exploit raw materials and impose an export-oriented production model, in accordance with their interests. this epa will have serious consequences for small farmers and workers in the eu and acp countries, as trade barriers are gradually removed.
in writing. - i approve this resolution, starting by stressing that efficient national systems must ensure that state aid measures are exempt from the obligation to notify ex-ante and comply with european union law. furthermore, i would also point out that, to date, only the member states have provided relevant information in relation to state aid control cases. i think the commission should be required to assess whether additional resources will be needed to extend its information gathering tools. however, i express my deep concern at the european court of auditors' conclusion that the commission does not systematically seek to detect unnotified aid measures, nor does it comprehensively assess the ex post facto impact of its state aid control. i would also stress the particular difficulty this poses to new entrants and small and mediumsized enterprises and the distortive effect it has on competition. i therefore believe that the commission, in the context of the modernisation of state aid, should address the issues mentioned above and ensure that any shortcomings in ex ante control of notifications are compensated by effective and rigorous ex post control.
in writing. - this european parliament motion for a resolution stresses the need for greater involvement of the parliament in the preparation and evaluation of state aid proposals, regretting that the parliament does not have a co-decision role in this area. it therefore urges that this situation be changed in the future. it considered that this state aid instrument should ensure a stimulus to economic growth and at the same time prevent an excessive increase in public debt. to this end, state aid must be better targeted, implying less public expenditure and no distortion of competition, while also ensuring the transition to a knowledge-based economy with the development of the necessary services and infrastructure. the role of state aid is to promote a level playing field in the internal market, but its use is also central to achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and the green transformation of the economy. these must therefore be rigorously applied and evaluated in order to reap the full benefits of their positive effects. i am voting in favour of this proposal from the european parliament, as i believe that it contributes to improving the effectiveness of the application of state aid, which is so important in ensuring a level playing field in the internal market.
in writing. the commission has recently put forward two proposals for regulations on the modernisation of state aid, which aim to ensure that economic growth is stimulated without entailing or leading to a further increase in public debt. such a reform aims not only to reduce state aid but also to make it more targeted and non-competitive, by encouraging the development of services, knowledge and infrastructure itself rather than supporting specific enterprises. in addition, this reform aims to focus the commission's intervention on the most relevant cases, exempting a greater number of measures from the notification requirement, which seems to me to be an important measure of procedural economy and rationalisation of resources. i hope, however, that in the course of this process of reviewing the state aid legislation, both the commission and the council will take account of the amendments which will be tabled by this parliament.
in writing. - the proposal for a resolution tabled following a question with oral answer by mrs sharon bowles on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs and industrial policy on the european union's (eu) policy on state aid. the economic and financial crisis forced member states to adopt a new form of governance that cut back on public administration expenditure. state aid has long been criticised as distorting competition and undermining the functioning of the internal market. although this is a very sensitive matter which should be dealt with in a different regulatory framework, namely codecision rather than mere consultation by the european parliament, i nevertheless believe that state aid, if properly modernised, can contribute to economic recovery and job creation. it must therefore be directed towards areas such as research and new technologies.

in writing. the modernisation of state aid proposed in this new regulation may be important in securing a new economic stimulus. however, it must not lead to an increase in public debt, which is already very high in some eu member states. although state aid is scarcer, it should be better targeted, involve less public expenditure and should not distort competition, while supporting the transition to a knowledge-based economy. state aid should be designed to promote the development of services, knowledge and infrastructure itself, rather than supporting specific undertakings. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. − on 24 november 2012, a violent fire broke out in a textile factory in bangladesh, killing 112 people mostly young people and women and injuring many others. as a result, 300 workers lost their jobs. this was not an isolated case and many other fires have occurred in industries which do not meet minimum safety requirements. to reduce production costs and be more competitive in the international market, these companies exploit workers and resort to child labor. first of all, i would like to extend my condolences to all the families of the victims of this and other fires that have occurred in south asia. the demand for high safety standards in european companies has led to the relocation of many of these industries to emerging countries where wages are around one dollar a day and where the recommendations of the international labour organization (ilo) are not met at all. i voted in favour of this joint motion for a resolution because we must demand that all the european union's trading partners respect minimum social, labour and environmental conditions. companies can't just think about profits. you have to think about the workers, too.
in writing. the resolution was adopted following fires in textile factories in south asia, particularly in bangladesh. we support the resolution, but we cannot help expressing some concerns here. there is a general concern, evident throughout the resolution, about the precarious working conditions of these workers and the need for manufacturers to implement legislation on health and safety at work and for greater control by governments through an independent system of labour inspections. bangladesh is now the second largest exporter of clothing to europe, a fact that is inextricably linked to the relocation of european textile production to south asian countries, where labour costs are much lower than in europe. the european retailers who have now contributed to the compensation schemes for the victims and their families are the same ones who condone the subjecting of these workers to inhuman working conditions, which is at the root of this kind of tragedy. the same people who take advantage of unemployment and poverty, as well as of the legislative gaps in these countries in terms of employment, to increase their profits even more.

in writing. − the award of the 2012 nobel peace prize to the european union (eu) was a recognition of the possibility for peoples who once fought each other to feel brotherly in a common project of peace and economic development. this joint motion for a resolution contains a set of recommendations from the conference on the revision of the non-proliferation treaty with regard to the definition of a middle east free of weapons of mass destruction. in the event of a conflict, when one party has a certain type of weapon, this situation generates a race on the other side to find weapons that can balance the war forces. in the war industry, nuclear weapons and weapons of mass destruction have primacy because of the tragic consequences they produce. these weapons, in the hands of dictators, fanatics or extremists, are a matter of great concern to the entire international community, because we never know when they may be used as offensive weapons. because we all want a world free of weapons of mass destruction, i regret that the conference on this subject which was to have been held in helsinki last december did not take place, thus postponing the creation of a corridor free of such weapons in the middle east.
in writing. - we believe that all efforts to achieve the objective of establishing a zone free of nuclear weapons and all other weapons of mass destruction in the middle east should be supported. we are in favour of a programme involving all the nuclear powers with a view to relaunching negotiations on nuclear disarmament, with the ultimate aim of promoting their total dismantling and prohibiting their use and production. with this resolution, the majority of this parliament is showing a certain hypocrisy. they advocate the creation of a nuclear-weapon-free zone in the middle east. but they do not mention, even once, that some of the world's nuclear powers are part of the eu (and nato) and that they themselves should take steps towards the establishment of a nuclear-weapon-free zone in europe. nor do they mention complicity with israel - the only power in the middle east which, illegally and outside international treaties, possesses a vast arsenal of nuclear weapons. nuclear disarmament is inseparable from the need to demilitarise international relations, respect the charter of the united nations, international law, the principles of non-interference and the peaceful settlement of international conflicts. the steps taken by the eu are unfortunately going in the opposite direction.

european union itself is based. posei agriculture is of decisive value in the present and future of the economies of regions heavily dependent on agriculture and under permanent natural constraints, such as the outermost regions. in the azores, agriculture is one of the most important pillars of the regional economy, responsible for the dynamism of most of the secondary sector and a significant part of the tertiary sector, and also determining for the fixation of populations on several islands. in this context, i congratulate the rapporteur and those who have worked with him to present a mr president, commissioner, small and mediumsized enterprises are the backbone of the european economy, the main engine of economic growth in the union and the main creators of jobs. but they are fragile, with few and weak means of surviving the economic or financial crisis we are experiencing, which is weakening them to the point of collapse. this is what is happening throughout the union, and it is getting worse in countries under external assistance such as portugal. under these conditions, banks became more prudent, creating new barriers to access to credit. smes, on the other hand, have been further weakened by the difficulty of access, creating a vicious circle that ruins smes, the middle class and what should be the most solid and stable foundation of a country's economy. this report, for which i congratulate the rapporteur, shows how we can help to reverse this situation and create the conditions to facilitate access by smes to the necessary financing, in particular by combating the disproportionate level of information and bargaining power between smes and banks. we are losing a lot and there is a lot to gain so it is urgent to act.

mr president, the idea of active ageing lends itself to different, sometimes conflicting, approaches. the increase in life expectancy, an achievement of civilization, brings new challenges to which society must find answers. the meaning of that answer will, of course, depend on the kind of society we want. in a society organised around the satisfaction of human needs, new investment is needed in a diverse range of existing and future public services, starting with health. this is the opposite of what is being done in europe and, in particular, in portugal, where these services are being dismantled with dramatic consequences. in a society organized on the basis of profit, the increase in life expectancy serves to fuel the pressure to reduce rights and increase the retirement age, forgetting that labour productivity has increased significantly in recent decades, so this option is not inevitable, contrary to what some would like to believe. it is in the tension and struggle between these opposing views that it will become clear, sooner or later, what active ageing is all about.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, every month citizens spend a substantial portion of their salary or pensions on medicines and wonder about the price they pay, especially in times of crisis and austerity. that is why it is so important that the pricing process and rules are clear and transparent. we all want to know what we're paying for and why. but we come to the house today with a proposal which, despite the improvements in the report, is contrary to the interests of european citizens rather than protecting them, as one would expect, and even prevents member states from reassessing the safety, efficacy and quality of medicines. moreover, by setting deadlines for member states to decide on the price and reimbursement system for each medicinal product, this directive ends up proposing a dictatorship of the pharmaceutical industry because, if countries do not do so within the deadlines, they have to pay the industry, going so far as to enshrine the possibility for the manufacturer to unilaterally impose his price on the member states if the deadlines are not respected. this is unacceptable to us. that is why my group is bringing to the plenary a set of amendments to restore the competence of the member states and to prevent penalties that would affect public health services, already so attacked in times of austerity and with minimal budgets, and also to really guarantee the interests of the citizens.
member states are responsible for the organisation of their health systems and for the allocation of resources allocated to them, including in the area of medicines. that is the way it is, and that is the way it should remain. the action of the troika occupying portugal, forcing the price of medicines to rise and reducing the share of the state, is therefore illegitimate. the result: severe limitations on access to medicines. many users, especially the elderly on lower incomes, have to choose: either the drugs in the pharmacy or the food. some hospitals no longer make medicines available to users in hospital pharmacies. the european commission's concerns about patients' access to medicines are therefore well known. the concern here is something else: the market, always the market, the trade in medicines, the interests of the pharmaceutical companies. finally, a clarification: in portugal we still have a national health service, in accordance with the universal constitution and tending to be free. it would therefore be appropriate to correct the expression used by the european commission, national health insurance scheme. it is that the desires and intentions of some are not yet reality and, as far as we are concerned, never will be.
madam president, commissioner, to meet the challenge of globalisation, europe's growth strategy needs a modern industrial policy based on innovation, resource efficiency and the qualification of human resources. the role of innovation is fundamental and it is important to link industrial policy with the innovation strategy. industrial policy must be based on the efficiency of natural resources, including energy efficiency, making industrial activity compatible with sustainable development, but it is also necessary to develop capacities for innovation through education and training, increasing the number of technological scientists and engineers in europe. in this connection, i would like to mention the proposal for european reindustrialisation, launched by portugal and four other european countries - spain, france, italy, germany - on the eve of the competitiveness council meeting in december. only a global response will unlock the potential of european industry as a driver of growth and job creation. in this regard, we hope that the european budget for 2014-2020 will send an important signal by prioritising the policies that contribute most to growth, i.e. science, innovation, education, support for smes.
the deindustrialization in my country, portugal, the financial strangulation of productive activity and the destruction of thousands of jobs in the industrial sector, which have placed the country in a situation of external dependence that is now more evident than ever, began with portugal's accession to the then eec. employment in this sector fell from 39% of the national total in 1985 to around 16% in 2012, and its value added weight in national gdp from 30% to 13%. and it is not to be assumed that this pace was the same throughout the european union, since the rate of deindustrialization in portugal was several times higher than the average rate of the european union in the same period, i.e. the single market, privatizations, the central role assigned to foreign capital protected by the european union led to the cancellation of the development potential of the most peripheral countries. if it is clear that the market does not work to balance the economy, only public investment in the recovery of core and strategic industries can solve the problem. to do this, the european union should not condition public investment in the member states but rather encourage it and, of course, break with the policies of fiscal consolidation that stifle internal and external markets without which production is meaningless.
the portuguese rulers are euphoric about the pseudo-return to the markets. you celebrate the debt sale, but the country is only going further into debt. the banks are profiting and the happy bankers are telling us that we're all the same and we have to hang in there. the reality is much crueler: a few weeks after the troika's seventh assessment, 72% of portuguese are no longer able to pay their expenses with their salary or pension, due to the reduction in social benefits, the increase in prices and the tax burden. in fact, we're not all the same. the majority is impoverishing to pay the profits of the bank and comes a banker without any shame to demand that you hold and cite the example of greece; he says: the greeks are alive, protesting a little more vehemently than we are, breaking some monuments, but they are there, they are alive. there is no limit to cynicism when you know that greece is on the verge of a humanitarian crisis and suicide rates are rising. we are not all the same but the difference is not between greeks and portuguese. in portugal, as in greece, there are those who pay and are getting poorer and poorer and there are those who profit from this without producing anything. we must turn the page on this nightmare europe. on march 2nd, we will take the streets and squares of the country and run with the troika.
we are discussing a regulation which is fundamental to the future of the fisheries sector. one thing they all seem to agree on the current common fisheries policy is a disaster from a social, environmental and economic point of view. the question is what we will say in ten years' time about the reform we are discussing now. our position is very clear, this is not the reform that was needed. the commission's original proposal has been improved considerably, and i would like to stress the fact that no reference is made to transferable fishing concessions, which is enough for the commission to put to rest the idea of trying to privatise the common good of fisheries resources. but the positive changes introduced are still not enough. a highly centralised policy is still in place, far removed from the complex and diverse reality of european fisheries, which would rather be managed in close proximity, based on knowledge, taking account of the reality and specific features of each country, each fishing zone, each fleet and each resource, and involving fishermen in the solutions and their implementation. let us be clear: the institutional framework created by the treaty of lisbon, which establishes the conservation of marine biological resources as an exclusive competence of the european union, is an obstacle to this proximity management, an obstacle which sooner or later will have to be removed. the necessary setting of environmental objectives must be accompanied by the setting of social and economic objectives, which are essential in any fisheries policy. a fisheries policy is not, and should not be, a mere policy of conservation of resources, although it does not exempt it. it is a fact that without fish there can be no fishing, a fact that many have dangerously ignored for a long time, some still ignore, but it is also a fact that without fishermen there can be no fishing and many also ignore, dangerously, this other dimension that any fisheries policy must have.
mr president, commissioner, mr minister, the vote on the basic regulation, which will shape the future of the common fisheries policy, is the decisive moment in the reform process, and i thank and congratulate the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs for the work they have done so far. i reiterate my commitment to a thorough reform that will solve the long-diagnosed and worsening problems. we need to recover stocks so that there is more fish, but also to value the first sale so that less can be caught and to dignify the profession to develop an entrepreneurship that optimizes resources, that is, we need to accept the challenge of finding a balance between the three pillars of fishing - the environmental, the economic and the social - instead of giving in to the lure of facilitism or the pressure of ngos, to prioritize the environmental and leave the rest for later. the simple equation that today the fishery is closed so that tomorrow there are more fish and the day after tomorrow the fishery is resumed is utopian. fishermen and their families live off their work every day, and you can't just flip the switch on and off like a switch on a switch. this is what only works in the offices of some politicians but not in the real life of fishermen. and we will never achieve success in this reform without the direct involvement and active participation of the sector. that is the case with the proposal on rejections which the ppe is presenting to this house and which must be adopted because it is the only one that is realistic and feasible and that contributes to the preservation of fisheries resources and that has the commitment of the sector. the safeguarding of sensitive biogeographical areas is also essential for the balance of the three pillars of the cfp in the outermost regions. this is also a proposal by the ppe which expects the support of all the groups and in particular of the rapporteur. it would be strange and paradoxical if the environmental concerns of the rapporteur and of the socialists in general were not to extend to the interests of the poorer and more fisheries-dependent regions which want to... the reform of the cfp represents an opportunity for local management that promotes the sustainability of fisheries resources and the viability of coastal communities dependent on fishing. in this respect, the creation of the jrc for the outermost regions such as the azores, which helps to promote an ecosystem approach and takes account of the sensitive nature of our specificities, will be very positive. it is also essential that marine areas identified as sensitive biogeographically in scientific studies are subject to our legislation accordingly to protect them. as such, it is necessary to protect the seamounts and fishing grounds that lie beyond the 100 miles already safeguarded for our regions. in trade with third countries we must also ensure reciprocity of the conditions required in order to guarantee equal treatment and fair competition with our operators, safeguarding public health, as proposed and approved by the committee on fisheries.

in writing. - i approve this report in accordance with the new rules in force under the lisbon treaty. first of all, it should be noted that this report is simpler and more explicit in providing the schemes and their main objectives and in highlighting the role played by the support programme for agricultural products from the smaller aegean islands. i am therefore in favour of adopting this report, stressing once again that the european union, in order to have an effective cohesion policy, must always take account of local and regional specificities so that there is a harmonious implementation of community legislation, which promotes development and growth in all regions and does not hinder their economic development process.
in writing. − although the treaties do not declare them as outermost regions, it is widely recognised that the large number of small aegean islands poses a major challenge to the eu's territorial cohesion policy. this justified the adoption in 1993 of a programme similar to posei to support the development of this 'region'. the large dispersion of small territories and their structural deficiencies are a challenge to cohesion policy and call for support, through specific measures, for the development of the local economy and, in particular, for the production and marketing of agricultural products. the development of the aegean islands should be subject to an assessment of existing needs and shortcomings and accompanied by a clear strategic orientation. it is necessary to stimulate agricultural production geared to promoting synergies between the local agricultural economy and the development of tourism and the conservation of local natural and cultural wealth. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal because i consider that the strategy presented to correct the structural deficiencies in the agricultural sector in the aegean islands is balanced and feasible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'specific measures in the agricultural field for the smaller aegean islands', as it will make it possible to adapt the regulation resulting from the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon and to clarify its objectives, taking into account the importance of the programmes to support agricultural products in this region.
in writing. − the aegean islands have been deserving of special treatment by the european union because of their geographical dispersion and isolation. i believe that this treatment is justified and that it should be maintained, because the outermost regions do not have the same economic alternatives and the same degree of market access as the other european regions. the union is right to focus on the living and working conditions of citizens in these remote areas and to provide them with better conditions for their survival. europe has to gain from its diversity and from the preservation of centuries-old communities with their own cultures and traditions. as with the common agricultural policy as a whole, also with regard to the smaller aegean islands, measures in the agricultural field can and should have social, economic and environmental effects that go far beyond mere food production and intersect with others aimed at promoting the sustainability and development of the populations.
in writing. - the report under consideration, drawn up by mr georgios papastamkos, concerns a set of specific measures to be implemented in the agricultural field in favour of the smaller aegean islands, aimed at promoting 'the production, processing and marketing of certain agricultural products and the supply of raw materials to the islands'. these measures were part of the programme of specific options for coping with remote and insularity (posei), which is itself rooted in the objectives of the european union's (eu) cohesion policy in terms of reducing the regional asymmetries that continue to exist between the communities of central europe and the populations of the peripheral and outermost regions. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to support these regions in order to achieve greater territorial cohesion. we all recognise that the factors of production in the peripheral and outermost regions are more expensive, which increases the final cost of products. so, if these regions are not to be depressed, it is essential that the european union, through its cohesion policy, supports rural infrastructure, traditional products and tourism development, creating conditions for the natural and/or resident populations to settle.
in writing. - this regulation lays down agricultural measures for the smaller aegean islands. recognising the constraints facing these islands and therefore the need for special support to overcome the economic and social constraints that arise from them, specific measures are proposed for these islands - a position which we support. the programme to which this report refers sets out the financing to support local agricultural production and a specific supply scheme to support the supply of essential products and raw materials. unfortunately, the adoption of an amendment proposed by the right wing has weakened the report and the final regulation considerably, since it not only cancelled the proposal to increase the overall allocation of the programme by 30%, but also transferred eur 0.55 million from the programme to support local agricultural production (to ensure the maintenance and development of local production) to the specific supply scheme, which raises serious doubts as this will in practice result in a reduction in the amount of support for local agricultural production. that is why we abstained.
in writing. − in accordance with article 174 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), the strengthening of the union's economic, social and territorial cohesion is an essential factor for its harmonious and balanced development. in this connection, the union will endeavour to reduce the disparity between the levels of development of the various regions and the backwardness of the less-favoured regions and islands, in particular island, cross-border and mountain regions. the large number of small aegean islands is a major challenge for territorial cohesion policy as originally conceived under eu law and as translated into economic and social cohesion policy. this type of programme is important for strengthening the economic, social and territorial cohesion of the union, which is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. the proposal for a regulation submitted to the european parliament constitutes an adaptation of the scheme establishing specific measures in the agricultural field for the smaller aegean islands. these measures, which are covered by the community support programme, are intended to finance the production, processing and marketing of certain agricultural products and the supply of raw materials to the islands. such activities need extraordinary support because the situation of the islands is also extraordinary: either because of the geophysical and climatic conditions (rocky soil, drought, strong winds) or because of the territorial conditions (insularity and grouping into archipelagos). the commission is also proposing to increase the amount of the budget for local production by eur 7.7 million and to increase the annual funding of the specific supply scheme by eur 1.6 million. the rapporteur believes that it is not enough to increase funding: it is necessary to link production aid to a sustainable development strategy and to provide for measures to improve the transport of agricultural products produced or processed on the aegean islands. i voted in favour, in the hope that the aegean islands will be able to correct the permanent and structural deficiencies in their agricultural sector.
in writing. - special schemes have been adopted for the smaller aegean islands under specific regulatory measures, with appropriations from the same posei fund, i.e. the european agricultural guarantee fund/european agricultural fund for rural development, the measures being planned and implemented according to the same basis and under the same framework. the dispersion of the islands and their grouping into archipelagos constitutes an obstacle to their supply and trade, resulting in increased transport costs. the existing transport networks are inadequate and are characterised by structural deficiencies resulting in 'double insularity', as the smaller islands are supplied via other, more central islands. so, although the commission proposal does not bring about any substantive changes to the scheme, i voted in favour of maintaining it, which must take account of the new objective of territorial cohesion under article 174 tfeu.
