in writing. - i welcome this report, starting by pointing out that the issue of the socioeconomic situation of the outermost regions remains very fragile and, in my view, is not properly taken into account in the policies announced by the european commission. i would point out that the amendments introduced must be taken into account in order to respect the particular nature of the milk sector, which is of extreme importance for the outermost region from which i come, the azores, particularly as regards international trade compensation directly affecting these regions, and not to forget the safety licences for imported products. posei, in my view, must be complemented by the common agricultural policy in order not to aggravate the crisis already visible in these regions, which are highly dependent on agriculture and where the levels of socioeconomic development are still far from the european union average.
in writing. − the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down specific measures for agriculture in the outermost regions of the union aims to reform the posei scheme (programme of specific options to deal with remoteness and insularity), set up by regulation (ec) no 247/2006, in order to take account of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. the regulation allows free trade in processed products subject to a specific supply arrangements (sps) between the outermost regions (ors) and increases the annual ceilings for sps for france and portugal. these programmes play an inseparable role in the maintenance and development of agricultural production and the processing industry in the regions concerned. the project also aims to simplify and clarify the reading of the regulation covering all the specific agricultural measures for the nine outermost regions of the european union. at a time of economic crisis such as the present, when these regions are affected by unemployment rates many times higher than the national average, it is important not only to maintain this system but, if possible, to strengthen it. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - specific measures in the field of agriculture for the outermost regions of the union (posei) are intended to compensate for the problems and additional costs caused by the exceptional geographical situation of these regions. they are intended, on the one hand, to ensure the supply of the outermost regions with essential agricultural products and, on the other hand, to support the production and marketing of outermost regions' products abroad by reducing the competitive disadvantages on the internal market to which those products are subject, particularly in view of the great distance separating them from the consumer market. these specific measures have thus made it possible to preserve local production structures and create additional jobs, which would be seriously threatened without the existence of the posei programmes. however, unemployment rates in these regions are twice as high as in the eu and the member states to which they belong. the aim of this initiative is to provide greater legal clarity to the regulation and to reinforce the objectives of the programme. i also support the increase in the funding of measures to allow for better account to be taken of the difficulties created by the specific situation of these regions, aggravated by the economic and financial crisis and the increasing pressure on the sectors concerned.
in writing. - for the nine outermost regions (ors) of the eu, including the azores and madeira, agriculture is a strategic economic sector, not only because it is a major employer and engine of economic development, but also because it ensures food security, an important factor given the insular characteristics of these territories. i believe that increasing food self-sufficiency is fundamental to the ors and their regional development strategies, and i therefore voted in favour of this report. the financial allocation for the programme of specific options on remote and insularity (posei) remained at eur 653.04 million for all nine outermost regions of the eu. the autonomous regions of the azores and madeira receive eur 106.21 million from this envelope. in this posei review, the banana sector was one of the main beneficiaries with additional funding of €40 million. of this, the autonomous regions received eur 1.24 million. the other two sectors important to the azores and madeira, milk and meat, did not benefit from any additional gains from this revision of the programme.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'specific measures in the field of agriculture for the outermost regions of the union', as it contains proposals which will help to simplify and clarify the regulation in the light of the lisbon treaty and to make the support programmes for the outermost regions, in particular the azores and madeira, more effective in order to respond better to the economic difficulties inherent in their geographical situation.
in writing. - the ultraperipheral nature of some regions of the european union naturally affects the movement of people and goods and restricts their access to markets. fortunately, the union has not been insensitive to the special characteristics of these regions and has sought to provide them with aid mechanisms aimed at mitigating the consequences of their extreme peripheral location and promoting the unique characteristics and products of these regions and trade and contacts between similar regions. support for agriculture is particularly important in these cases. i would remind you of the natural apprehension of azorean producers due to the end of milk quotas and the uncertainties about the sustainability of the azorean economy, which is based to a large extent on that production. the economies of the outermost regions need special attention from regional, national and european decision-makers. at present there are serious doubts about the degree of protection afforded to them and creative and reproductive ways of doing so must be considered. i welcome the increase in posei for portugal and hope that this increase will contribute to an effective improvement in the quality of life of the population.
in writing. - the report by mr gabriel mato adrover deals with a set of specific measures in the field of agriculture for the outermost regions of the european union (eu). in 1991, the council adopted the programme of specific options for coping with remote and insularity (posei), which is in turn rooted in the objectives of the european union's (eu) cohesion policy in terms of reducing the regional asymmetries that continue to exist between the communities of central europe and the populations of the peripheral and outermost regions. imported products from third countries produced without respect for the social and environmental requirements imposed on farmers in the european union are destroying the competitiveness of european regional products, which can only be enforced through quality certification and protected designation of origin (pdo), but never through price. however, we know that most european consumers, especially in these times of crisis, are primarily concerned with price. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it is necessary to support sustainable agricultural practices in the outermost regions so that these territories can conserve their populations, protect their cultural values and their historical and geographical heritage.
in writing. the report approves the proposal for a regulation laying down specific measures in the field of agriculture for the eu's outermost regions (ors) - which include madeira and the azores. the specific options programmes on remote and insularity (posei) aim to provide financial assistance for agricultural production and the processing industry, and there is a specific supply scheme for supply to livestock feed, the processing industry and direct consumption, subject to ceilings so as not to interfere with island productions. in addition, some 80% of the funds are used for measures to support local agricultural production, which is essential to maintain the viability of the activity. the report makes positive improvements on the commission proposal: the commission has also adopted a number of proposals to improve the legal basis for the ops and their specific features, and to strengthen the role and the resources of these programmes. we have long advocated these measures to support the ors, which compensate for the constraints and restrictions imposed on these regions. we therefore voted in favour of this report. however, we cannot fail to point out - as we did during the debate in the plenary - the inconsistencies in the eu's agricultural and trade policies which have so harmed these regions.
in writing. - the specific options programmes on remote and insularity (posei) were launched in 1991 to support the french overseas departments, and a year later to cover the outermost regions of portugal and spain. nine regions are currently covered by this measure: guadeloupe, french guiana, martinique, réunion, saint-barthélemy and saint-martin (france), the azores and madeira for portugal, and the canary islands for spain. these programmes play an inseparable role in the maintenance and development of agricultural production and the processing industry in these areas. the viability of the beneficiary sectors would be threatened today without the existence of the posei programmes, due to the economic difficulties faced by these regions as a result of their geographical situation and the limited scope for diversifying their activity. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − this proposal amends regulation (ec) no 247/2006, clarifying the objectives of the scheme and restructuring the text of the legislation to bring it into line with the provisions on delegated and implementing acts provided for in the lisbon treaty. the simplification effort is complemented by the introduction of some legislative changes aimed at correcting the shortcomings identified in recent years in the implementation of posei. the most important amendments are: an increase of 20% in the ceilings for aid granted to france and portugal under the eag for the supply of products for animal feedingstuffs, the processing industry and direct consumption to the outermost regions; making the eag subject to the requirement of avoiding any obstacles to the development of local production; and specifying the procedure for the submission of programmes and their amendments with a view to the approval of support programmes by the commission. given that it is the eu's responsibility to prevent the deterioration of the profitability of these citizens, i voted in favour, in the expectation that this proposal will benefit the azores and madeira.
in writing. − the outermost regions of the european union are regions with special characteristics which have a differentiated status under article 349 of the treaty on the functioning of the eu. this status allows for derogation from the scheme by establishing specific measures to take account of the supply of these regions and to favour local production. under this reform of posei, the outermost regions will have an additional financial allocation to deal with the damage caused to regional banana production, taking into account trade agreements with third countries. in addition, a new method of calculating the quantities to be dispatched or exported is introduced, henceforth based on the average of the three best years between 2005 and 2012, a change to which i contributed. for the reasons i have just given, i voted in favour of the document, aware of the difficulties encountered in the trilogue to arrive at the best possible solution under this regime for the outermost regions.

in writing. the importance of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) for the european economy is indisputable. they are the great engine of the european economy, of economic growth, and they make a huge contribution to job creation in the 27 member states. with the crisis in europe, smes were severely affected by the severe restriction of access to credit, the problems inherent in the contraction of the economy, the non-payment by their debtors, the increase in taxes, the decrease in demand, etc. it is therefore agreed that, if smes are to be able to develop a healthy activity that promotes growth and job creation, it is essential to ensure that they have good access to credit. to that end, it should be ensured that creditors provide clear and transparent information and that the conditions for access to credit are facilitated and do not involve excessive burdens or restrictions. it is emphasised that as smes are very heterogeneous, different and alternative solutions should also be developed as regards their financing arrangements. private savings should also be encouraged. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the importance of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) for the european economy is indisputable. they are the major engine of the european economy and are important drivers of economic growth, making a huge contribution to job creation in the 27 member states. with the onset of the economic crisis in europe, smes were severely affected by the severe restrictions on access to credit, the problems inherent in the contraction of the economy, whether the non-payment of their debtors, the increase in taxes, the decrease in demand, etc. it is therefore common ground that, if smes are to be able to develop a healthy activity that promotes growth and job creation, it is essential that good conditions be established for their access to credit. to that end, it is necessary to ensure that creditors provide clear and transparent information, that the conditions for access to credit are facilitated and do not involve excessive burdens or restrictions. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'small enterprises' in the definition of the term 'small enterprises'. private savings should also be encouraged. i am voting in favour of this report.

in writing. - the importance of smes in the european market and in the european economy is something that cannot be overlooked. it is recalled that they represent more than 98% of european enterprises and provide more than 67% of jobs, and between 2002 and 2010 they were directly responsible for 85% of new jobs in the eu. it is therefore vital that, in these troubled times in the eu, all the necessary efforts be redirected to improve the forms of financing available to this important sector of the economy. i would like to highlight, among others, the importance of capital markets specifically designed for smes in the euro area, such as nyse alternext. this market, which has been operating since 2005, has already enabled several smes to obtain funding of between eur 2,5 million and eur 15 million, demonstrating the impact that these markets can have as a form of financing for these companies. i think it would be essential for the commission to work more on this type of market, making it more accessible and attractive to both companies and investors, and to focus on developing more favourable tax regimes or creating own investment funds in partnership with the eib.
in writing. - it is often said that small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are the 'backbone' of the european economy. in fact, smes account for some 67% of employment in the whole of europe and represent 98% of the business fabric. with the financial crisis we are going through, smes have found themselves in a complicated situation with regard to their liquidity due to the lack of financing from financial institutions. banks have become more prudent and have created credit barriers making life difficult for smes, who thus feel powerless to contribute to economic growth and job creation. it is therefore imperative to make it easier for them to access credit and to reduce bureaucracy. the report by mr de backer focuses on ways of improving and facilitating access to finance for smes. i welcome the creation of the entrepreneurship 2020 and cosme programmes (competitiveness programme for enterprises and smes), which are key to boosting the economy and job creation. i believe that smes are the driving force of the european economy and i voted in favour of this report because, as many of them are young entrepreneurs, it is also a way of giving hope to young people and a step forward in overcoming the crisis.
in writing. - this report is based on a laudable concern and contains proposals that deserve our support: the financing needs of the real economy, especially smes; public guarantees and liquidity support from the ecb; the need to provide more training for small and medium-sized enterprises. but the report does not avoid glaring contradictions and omissions. the conditions under which free competition develops in the single market, favouring the suffocation of smes by monopolies; the so-called austerity policies which crush the wages and purchasing power of workers; the growth of unemployment and the consequent contraction of the internal market - are some examples of trends which have created enormous difficulties for smes and even led many of them to bankruptcy. an effective policy to support smes requires the reduction of high interest rates, the cost of factors of production such as energy, transport, communications, and others - which in turn requires public ownership and management of these key sectors of the economy - as well as the establishment of maximum margins to be applied by large companies to smes. it calls for lower taxes for smes, simplified procedures and reduced capital requirements for access to the structural funds.
in writing. − small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are very important to the european union. they are an important pillar of the european economy and responsible for economic growth in the european union. smes make a major contribution to job creation in its 27 member states. but they are also the most vulnerable, as has become evident in the aftermath of the crisis. with the crisis, some lenders have become more cautious in lending to smes. in addition, new and restrictive rules on, for example, financial institutions and capital requirements implemented by both the eu and national authorities have made it more difficult for smes to access credit. we must therefore find new mechanisms to facilitate access to finance for smes so that they can once again play the important role they have always played in economic growth and job creation.
in writing. the importance of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) for the european economy is undeniable. they are the main engine of the economy and are the drivers of economic growth, making a huge contribution to job creation in the 27 member states. with the onset of the economic crisis in europe, smes were severely affected by the severe restriction on access to credit resulting from the problems inherent in the contraction of the economy: either by the non-payment of their debtors, the increase in taxes, or the decrease in demand, etc. it is therefore common ground that, if smes are to be able to develop a healthy activity that promotes growth and job creation, it is essential that good conditions be established for their access to credit. to do this, we must ensure that creditors provide clear and transparent information and that the conditions for access to credit are easy and do not involve excessive burdens or restrictions. in conclusion, parliament, taking account of the heterogeneity of smes, recommended that different and alternative solutions be developed for the financing of smes. private savings should also be encouraged. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) are the engine of the european economy and the main generators of employment. as such, the socioeconomic success of the union as a whole is largely dependent on the ability of smes to remain competitive in the global market. the support provided by the member states and the union to banking institutions, resulting from the recent and ongoing economic and financial crisis, should therefore be reflected in the provision of credit to smes. we must not forget that smes have also been affected by the crisis and have nevertheless been faced with the difficulty of accessing bank credit to continue developing their activity. the development of initiatives and programmes adapted to the heterogeneous business reality which constitutes the european economic fabric is necessary. the union, within the framework of the eu 2020 strategy, should develop initiatives to facilitate entrepreneurship, development and financing of smes in the area of innovation, while ensuring conditions of competitiveness and financing for all smes in adverse macroeconomic situations. in view of the above, i have voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - this report is based on a laudable concern and includes some proposals which deserve our support, namely: the compulsory transfer of state aids, public guarantees and liquidity support from the ecb to the so-called real economy by private banks, the need to provide more training for small and medium-sized enterprises. there is, however, a huge contradiction that this report does not resolve: improving access to finance, without a policy that puts an end to the eu internal market (which puts monopolies and smes in totally unfair competition), that counters the impoverishment of workers, the growth of unemployment, the contraction of the internal market in many eu countries, will not only not be a solution for smes but will also result in over-indebtedness of companies and individuals, more unemployment and bankruptcies. an effective policy to support smes requires the reduction of high interest rates, the costs of production factors such as energy, transport, communications, etc. (formerly public sectors now in the hands of large national and foreign companies), and the establishment of maximum margins to be applied by large companies to smes. it calls for lower taxes for smes, simplified procedures and equity requirements for access to the structural funds.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioners, i would first like to underline the importance of the report on europe's growth prospects for 2013. we wanted this text to be dealt with by the commission, incorporating our contributions, and we still hope that this will happen because at the spring european council in march the decisions that will be taken in that council will shape the national reform programmes, the stability and convergence programmes and will be a key part of the new statute of the european semester. it is with this document that the semester begins and it is on this process of coordination of economic policies that the national and european parliaments must strengthen democratic control. unfortunately, unlike the other speakers, i have come to the plenary with an extreme position on the economic and monetary committee. the right-wing majority in this committee refused to negotiate on the report and yesterday, against my opinion and against my vote and against the vote of my political group, adopted a text which was cut from the messages we considered essential. we are at a critical moment in european life. the slight recovery in growth in 2010 was wiped out by the austerity agenda. in the spring of 2011, the euro area was forecast to grow by 1.8% in the year ending 2012. we ended up with a recession of -0.4%. for 2013, very weak growth is forecast - 0.1 - but the international monetary fund is probably right when it predicts a recession of -0.2%. the imbalances within europe and in particular in the euro area are reaching unsustainable levels. the six pack procedure on macroeconomic imbalances shows the systematic current account surpluses of three countries - in writing. − i support this recommendation, considering it essential first of all to enable the new member states of the european union to take full advantage of the european union's assistance in their integration process, and at the same time to support these countries to have the right conditions in the context of global trade. i therefore support this recommendation, which aims to adjust the european union's obligations under the world trade organisation rules following the accession of bulgaria and romania. the aim is to agree with the members of the world trade organisation a fair and mutually satisfactory adjustment so as to avoid losses for these new members of the union.
in writing. − with the accession of bulgaria and romania, the union has enlarged its customs union and, in accordance with wto rules, has been called upon to negotiate an agreement on a compensatory adjustment to satisfy all parties, balancing the gains and losses of all concerned. this adjustment should be made if the adoption of the eu external tariff regime results in an increase in duties beyond the level to which the acceding country has committed itself in the wto. the most frequent instrument used to offset higher duties is the opening of the country-specific tariff quota or the addition of the pre-accession tariff quota. on 27 january 2007, the council authorised the commission to enter into negotiations with countries entitled to compensation, resulting in a draft agreement in the form of an exchange of letters with the united states, whereby the united states is compensated for its deteriorated trade position. the commission has chosen the increase in the tariff quotas as a compensatory instrument for products from the usa. i am voting in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report concluding the eu-us agreement in the world trade organisation (wto) on the modification of concessions in the schedules of bulgaria and romania in the context of their accession to the eu. with the accession of the republic of bulgaria and romania, the european union has enlarged its customs union. consequently, in accordance with wto rules, it had to enter into negotiations with the wto members with negotiating powers on the lists of the new member states to agree on a compensatory adjustment that satisfies all parties and counterbalances the increase in the consolidated duties and the consequent significant losses. on 29 january 2007, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with the countries entitled to compensation. the negotiations with the united states have resulted in a draft agreement in the form of an exchange of letters, which was initialled by the eu party on 21 december 2011 and by the us party on 17 february 2012 and is now being finalised.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation to make the necessary amendments to the eu-us agreement, in accordance with gatt 1994, taking into account the enlargement of the customs union when romania and bulgaria joined the eu.
in writing. - i welcome the agreement with the united states, as i believe that the us has a right to have its trade rights restored, which had been slightly degraded by the enlargement of the customs union when romania and bulgaria joined the eu. this compensation agreement is an example of the eu's intention to respect the rules of the multilateral trade regime within the wto. the eu and the united states will notify each other of the completion of their respective internal procedures necessary for the entry into force of the agreement.
in writing. - mr vital moreira presents a recommendation on the draft council decision concluding an agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union (eu) and the united states of america (us) pursuant to article xxiv:6 and article xxviii of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) 1994 relating to the modification of concessions provided for in the schedules of the republic of bulgaria and romania in the context of their accession to the eu. this agreement follows negotiations between the eu and the members of the world trade organisation (wto), with delegated powers to do so, in order to make a compensatory adjustment between the parties. the draft agreement was signed by the eu on 21 december 2011 and by the us on 17 february 2012 and mainly covers poultry and pork meat. the eu's enlargement to include these two states has been beneficial to wto members and taking into account the rapporteur's opinion, i welcome the conclusion of this agreement with the usa and vote in favour of it.

in writing. - the accession of the republic of bulgaria and romania has meant that the european union has had to extend its customs union. therefore, and in accordance with wto rules (article xxvi:6 of gatt 1994), the european union had to enter into negotiations with wto members with negotiating power on the lists of any of the acceding members in order to agree on a compensatory adjustment that would satisfy all parties and counterbalance the increase in the consolidated duties and the consequent significant losses. i therefore welcome the agreement with the united states and i vote in favour of it. the us is thus entitled to have its previous trade rights re-established, which were slightly degraded due to the enlargement of the customs union upon the accession of romania and bulgaria to the eu.
in writing. - the accession of the republic of bulgaria and romania to the european union has had the immediate effect of enlarging their customs union. consequently, in accordance with world trade organisation rules, the european union had to enter into negotiations with wto members with negotiating power on the lists of any of the acceding members to agree on a compensatory adjustment that satisfies all parties and counterbalances the increase in the consolidated duties and the consequent significant losses. eu enlargement has been generally positive for wto members and the necessary adjustments have been duly negotiated and are only dependent on the mutual notification between the parties of the completion of their respective internal procedures necessary for the entry into force of the agreement. in this context, i voted in favour of the proposal to approve the agreement between the european union and the united states of america on the modification of concessions provided for in the schedules of the republic of bulgaria and romania in the context of the accession of these countries to the european union.
in writing. − with the accession of the republic of bulgaria and romania, the union has enlarged its customs union and, in accordance with wto rules, has been called upon to negotiate an agreement on compensatory adjustment. such adjustment is due if the adoption of the eu external tariff regime results in an increase exceeding the level to which the acceding country has committed itself in the wto. the most frequent instrument used to offset higher duties is the opening of the country-specific tariff quota or the increase of the existing ones. on 27 january 2007, the council authorised the commission to enter into negotiations with the countries entitled to compensation, resulting in a draft agreement in the form of an exchange of letters with the united states: the commission has not received any comments from the usa on the allegedly unfair trade practices of the union industry.
in writing. - with the accession of the republic of bulgaria and romania, the european union has enlarged its customs union. consequently, in accordance with wto rules, the european union had to enter into negotiations with wto members to agree on a compensatory adjustment that would satisfy all parties and counterbalance the increase in the consolidated duties and the consequent significant losses. to meet these requirements, two issues were addressed in the agreements: the offsetting of higher duties, for which the most frequently used instrument is the opening of the country-specific tariff quota or the increase of the existing ones; and the addition of the pre-accession tariff quota of bulgaria and romania to the existing union erga omnes quota. the products covered by the eu-us compensation agreement are mainly poultry and pigmeat and food preparations. for the reasons given, i voted in favour of the agreement.

in writing. - i welcome the commission proposal and its main provisions in the context of the current constraints, including financial ones, under which the competent authorities have to decide on the pricing and reimbursement of medicines. i believe that the general objective of this proposal should be to update the existing legislative framework in order to clarify and ensure the proper functioning of the single market and the effectiveness of internal market legislation in decisions on pricing and reimbursement and on obstacles to trade in pharmaceutical products. as a matter of priority, i would like to stress the need to strengthen the provisions relating to the transparency of the decision-making process and the decisions taken, which is a growing demand from society. i therefore suggest a set of additional measures, in particular the obligation for the competent authorities to disclose the names and declarations of interests of experts who are members of the decision-making bodies of the competent authorities. those provisions, as well as increased public access to documents and information, aim to enhance the transparency, integrity and independence of decisions taken and should ultimately strengthen trust in the public authorities responsible at national level.
in writing. − this report provides for a comprehensive update of directive 89/105/eec, with the aim of ensuring the transparency of national measures regulating the pricing of medicinal products for human use and their inclusion in national health insurance systems. the provisions of the directive in question reflect conditions which prevailed on the pharmaceutical market more than 20 years ago and which have since undergone profound changes. examples include the emergence of generic medicines that offer cheaper alternatives to brand-name medicines or the development of increasingly innovative research-based medicines. in this regard, it is necessary to strengthen the provisions relating to the transparency of the decision-making process and of the decisions taken and to oblige the competent authorities to disclose the names and declarations of interests of experts who are members of the decision-making bodies. the appeal procedures in case of failure to meet the deadlines for the inclusion of medicinal products in national health insurance systems should remain administrative and, in case of unjustified delays, be referred to the relevant administrative or judicial body in accordance with national law. i therefore support this report.

in writing. - directive 89/105/eec on the transparency of measures regulating the pricing of medicinal products has never been revised, although market conditions and health policies have changed substantially over the last 20 years. i therefore recognise the relevance of this revision and updating of the existing legislation, which maintains, and does, the principle of the autonomy of the states in regulating the formation of prices and the conditions for reimbursement (participation) of medicines. however, important changes are introduced with regard to (i) adapting the time limits for pricing and reimbursement decisions, (ii) clarifying the relationship between pricing and reimbursement procedures and intellectual property rights and the marketing authorisation procedure, and (iii) establishing certain instruments to facilitate dialogue and the application of the directive and to ensure its effective enforcement.
in writing. - this report generally welcomes the commission proposal and the main provisions, based on a thorough analysis of the current conditions on the pharmaceutical markets and the current context and constraints, including financial constraints, under which the competent authorities have to decide on the pricing and reimbursement of medicinal products. it is therefore foreseen that national decisions on the price and reimbursement of generic medicines can be taken within 60 days. in the case of new medicinal products, the time limit shall be 180 days. the studies carried out have shown that these decisions can currently take up to 250 days for generic medicines and up to 700 days for innovative medicines. this proposal should lead to significant savings for public health budgets and create a more predictable framework for pharmaceutical companies and consequently provide citizens with better access to these products. this report responds to a growing demand from society, particularly when it comes to the pricing and reimbursement of pharmaceutical products.

in writing. − the new reform of the common fisheries policy must ensure genuinely regionalised management, taking into account the diversity of fleets, fishing gear and stocks in each country and fishing zone. it should also respect the rights of regions over their territorial waters, exclusive economic zones (eezs) and adjacent seabed. it is also essential to protect the interests of coastal and small-scale fisheries in a lasting way. as far as the oct are concerned, it is undeniable that the principles and rules of the common fisheries policy are not adapted to the realities of these regions. the commission must bear in mind that these are maritime areas shared with the member states of the union and that, for the outermost regions, maritime areas are shared with the acp states. the reform of the common fisheries policy must also ensure the essential maintenance of the posei-fisheries financial regime and an intelligent link between the emff and posei-fisheries.
in writing. - the common fisheries policy (cfp) has proved ineffective in solving longstanding problems: overfishing, overcapacity, the weak economic situation of many fisheries enterprises, social problems caused by the decline of fisheries in many coastal regions. the new regulation should therefore create an ambitious framework to reverse the persistent negative trend and enable the sustainability and success of the european fisheries sector. the strategy is structured around eight pillars: 1) maximum sustainable yield or msy; 2) obligation to land all catches/no return; 3) a transparent system of individual and collective fishing concessions; 4) reduction of overcapacity; 5) regionalization/consultation of stakeholders; 6) additional stock replenishment measures to oblige member states to close 10 to 20% of their waters to fishing activities within three years; 7) transitional measures for the mediterranean sea; and 8) partnerships with third countries for the purpose of common fisheries management. i voted against this report because it shows that the environmental aspect is still being prioritised, the social and economic pillars are being underestimated, and i do not agree with the requirements imposed under the msy/msy framework and the law banning discarding.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the common fisheries policy, because it includes measures which will contribute to the recovery of stocks, in particular by preventing overfishing and the return of unwanted catches, with a view to improving the environmental, economic and social sustainability of fishing activities.
in writing. − fisheries are essential to the livelihoods of many populations and fish consumption is increasingly necessary for a healthy diet by consumers. the european commission has repeatedly stated that the objectives of the common fisheries policy are to protect stocks against overfishing, to guarantee fishermen an income, to ensure that consumers and the processing industry are regularly supplied at reasonable prices, and to exploit living marine resources in a biologically, environmentally and economically sustainable way. the mere statement of objectives makes it clear how difficult it is to defend all of them in a balanced way. the european union has been divided, broadly speaking, into 'friends of fishermen' and 'friends of fisheries', a dichotomy that must be overcome. i believe that any common fisheries policy which is inflexible and which ignores its main and most direct target groups is bound to fail. the lack of flexibility in the rules, which were too stringent and burdensome for individual fishermen, did not have this concern. this circumstance, which i regret very much, forced me to vote against.
in writing. - the european parliament (ep) has long called for urgent action to revise the common fisheries policy (cfp) of the european union (eu). our concern for the sustainability of fisheries resources, the preservation of biodiversity and the guarantee of minimum living conditions for fishing communities was at the heart of our request. in fact, it is imperative to stop the dumping of thousands and thousands of tonnes of fish into the sea and to restore endangered species. in addition, there are many other opportunities for exploiting marine species, such as aquaculture, which can ensure the supply of markets without endangering stocks. the report under review, drawn up by mrs ulrike rodust, focuses on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the cfp. i hope that this whole process will be completed during the irish presidency and that by the year 2020 we will have more fishing opportunities and more jobs in the sector.
in writing. - this report is a key part of the future common fisheries policy (cfp). this regulation will have profound implications for the future of the sector, starting with portugal - the eu country with the largest eez. despite the improvements made to the commission's initial proposal, such as the abolition of transferable fishing concessions, the document now adopted does not solve the main problems facing national fisheries and may even create new problems. it insists on a centralised management of the cfp, far removed from the complex and diverse reality of eu fisheries. despite the necessary setting of environmental objectives in line with current scientific recommendations, which we have supported, the socioeconomic dimension of fisheries policy is clearly neglected, which will bring obvious damage to small-scale fishing segments and to countries such as portugal where it is very prevalent. small-scale fishing is treated very unsatisfactorily in this regulation. it is significant that any reference to this segment of the fleet has been removed, contrary to the guidelines contained in the ferreira report on small-scale fishing, recently approved by this parliament. for these reasons, and because we understood that the defence of national interests required it, we voted against.

in writing. - i approve this proposal, taking into account that the main objective of the commission proposal for a regulation on the noise level of motor vehicles is to protect public health and the environment by implementing measures to reduce the noise level of motor vehicles. the proposal will introduce a new test method for measuring the noise level of motor vehicles and new limit values for the different categories of vehicles, namely light, medium and heavy vehicles. i also support the general approach of the commission proposal, which represents a major step forward in the fight against the harmful effects of noise emissions from motor vehicles on public health and the environment. however, i believe that the commission proposal would benefit from the introduction of a number of technical additions and adaptations, particularly as regards the creation of incentives for the manufacture and purchase of vehicles with lower noise levels.
in writing. − the main objective of this regulation is to protect public health and the environment by implementing measures to reduce the noise level of motor vehicles. in this connection, a new test method for measuring the noise level of motor vehicles and new limit values for the different categories of vehicles will be introduced. for the purpose of promoting low-noise vehicles and to give consumers an informed choice before purchase, a system of vehicle emission labelling should also be introduced. furthermore, since pavement characteristics have a decisive influence on noise emissions, it is advocated that a road classification system be introduced to enable member states and their national and local authorities to better place and assess the surface quality of their roads with a view to reducing their impact on overall noise levels. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − the proposal for a regulation on the noise level of motor vehicles aims to promote the protection of public health and the environment by implementing measures to reduce the noise level of motor vehicles, by updating the limit values for the different categories of vehicles and by introducing a new test method for measuring the level of noise emission in motor vehicles. the rapporteur proposes a number of technical additions and adaptations to this proposal, with regard to creating incentives for the manufacture and purchase of vehicles with lower noise levels, since excessive noise pollution tends to promote the increase of diseases, disabilities and various disturbances in citizens and should therefore be avoided. a system of labelling vehicle noise emissions is also proposed, with a view to enabling consumers to make an informed choice before buying, as well as a classification of roads more or less prone to noise generation. the report also considers that the setting of limit values should be an element to be determined by co-decision (ordinary legislative procedure) and not by means of delegated acts in the commission. i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted against the report on 'noise from motor vehicles' because the proposals presented clearly reduce the level of ambition and demand of the commission's legislative proposal, thus falling short of the objective of ensuring a high level of protection of health and the environment.
in writing. − the present proposal aims to achieve a high level of protection of public health and the environment through measures to reduce the noise level of motor vehicles, in particular by introducing a new test method for measuring the noise level of motor vehicles and new limit values for the different categories of vehicles, namely light, medium and heavy vehicles.
in writing. the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on the noise level of motor vehicles has as its main objective the protection of public health and the environment through the implementation of measures to reduce the noise level of these vehicles. the proposal provides for a gradual reduction in vehicle noise emissions according to the category of vehicle, applying first to new vehicle models and then to all vehicles entering into service. the commission is also proposing to introduce a system of labelling of vehicle noise emissions so that consumers can make an informed choice, as is already the case with co2 emissions and fuel consumption. it is also important to take into account that noise emitted by motor vehicles emanates from a variety of sources, including the engine, tyres, pavement and aerodynamics. given that prolonged exposure to high levels of noise increases the incidence of cardiovascular disease, cognitive impairment and sleep disorders, i consider it essential to protect the health of citizens and for this reason i voted in favour.
in writing. − noise pollution is the harmful effect on public health and the environment caused by sounds at a certain volume exceeding levels considered normal for humans and other animals. the aim of this proposal for a regulation is to ensure a high level of protection of health and the environment, in particular with regard to the noise level of motor vehicles. however, although the report initially contained important provisions to reduce noise emission by 4 db for light vehicles and 3 db for heavy vehicles, the lead of these provisions during the vote in plenary distorted the content of the report and its positive effects. as regards the verification of conformity of vehicle production, the approved report adds 1db to the limit values set out in the annex to the regulation, falling short of the health protection originally intended. we voted in favour of the amendment which makes the installation of vehicle audible warning systems (avas) compulsory (and not optional), particularly for electric vehicles, which emit a 'continuous sound to indicate a vehicle in operation' for the safety of pedestrians and vulnerable road users.
in writing. - this proposal for a regulation provides for a gradual reduction in the noise emissions of vehicles according to their category, applying first to new vehicle models and then to all vehicles entering into circulation. the proposal would limit the noise level of cars to 68 decibels (db), below the current limit value of 74 db. the aim is thus to protect the health of citizens, taking into account that prolonged exposure to high noise levels increases the incidence of cardiovascular disease, cognitive impairment and sleep disturbances. the introduction of a system of labelling of vehicle noise emissions to enable consumers to make an informed choice before purchase is also envisaged. the labelling already exists for co2 emissions, fuel consumption and tyre noise, and a similar label should now be created for vehicle noise levels. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. the commission proposal for a regulation on the noise level of motor vehicles has as its main objective the protection of public health and the environment through the implementation of measures to reduce that noise level. i voted in favour of the proposal, which is very positive as a whole, but i do so with the reservation that the safety of visually impaired pedestrians must be duly taken into account. in fact, when addressing the issue of audibility of hybrid and electric vehicles, the draft regulation should provide for systems to control these risks, such as equipping quiet vehicles with an acoustic vehicle alerting system (avas) whose sound can easily indicate the state of action of the vehicle (acceleration, braking, reversing, temporary stopping).
in writing. the proposal for a regulation on the noise level of motor vehicles updates the limit values for the different categories of vehicles and introduces a new and sophisticated test method for measuring the level of noise emission in motor vehicles. the proposal for a regulation is based on the need to protect public health and the environment, as motor transport is one of the main sources of noise pollution, the incidence of which tends to increase the number of illnesses, disabilities and various disturbances affecting citizens. the rapporteur supports the proposal, considering that the regulation would benefit from the introduction of a set of technical additions and adaptations to encourage the manufacture and purchase of vehicles with lower noise levels; the committee also notes the interest of a system of labelling of vehicle noise emissions, with a view to enabling consumers to make an informed choice before purchase. i voted in favour of this report, agreeing with the rapporteur's position that the setting of limit values is an element to be determined by co-decision by the co-legislators (in the ordinary legislative procedure) and not by means of delegated acts in the commission.
in writing. - this report aims to ensure the protection of public health and the environment with regard to the noise level of motor vehicles by implementing measures to reduce the noise level of motor vehicles. in addition to timing, both for consumers and for the industry itself, this report aims to introduce new methods for measuring vehicle noise in the light, medium and heavy categories. the proposal is for a reduction of 4 db for light and medium vehicles and 3 db for heavy vehicles, in three phases, covering a period of 8 years, covering the whole car fleet and not just new vehicles. finally, i would like to stress the importance of ensuring that so-called quiet cars are equipped with avas to ensure maximum protection for citizens, in particular blind and partially sighted people.

in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that in some member states the economic and financial crisis has had a severe impact on public finances. while most member states have been forced to take more drastic measures to reduce debt and budget deficits in order to put public finances back on a sustainable path, some countries have been so affected that they have had to resort to eu financial assistance mechanisms. as a result of the enormous financial difficulties, these member states have encountered problems in meeting the co-financing requirements. these difficulties are also evident in the case of the funds under the general programme 'solidarity and management of migration flows'. i therefore support the commission's proposal to allow for the possibility of increasing the co-financing rates for member states benefiting from a financial support mechanism. the proposal is designed to allow an increase of 20 percentage points in the union's co-financing rate and, consequently, to reduce the co-financing needs of the member states concerned.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis has had severe effects on public finances in several eu member states, with some countries having recourse to the eu's financial assistance mechanism. this has led to several member states having problems in meeting the co-financing requirements associated with union funding. in view of this, it is proposed to increase the co-financing rates of the european union and consequently to reduce the co-financing needs of the member states concerned, thus bringing them to 70%. for projects targeting specific priorities and member states covered by the cohesion fund, the rate shall reach a maximum of 95%. it is underlined that the changes in the co-financing rates for member states facing serious financial stability difficulties do not imply an increase in the total amounts of the funds concerned. i supported this report because i agree with the importance of the reduction in the co-financing needs of the member states which have made use of the eu financial assistance mechanism.

in writing. - like the rapporteur, my colleague nils torvalds, i support the european commission's proposals to increase co-financing rates for member states receiving financial assistance. the principle underlying these funds is the creation of a solidarity mechanism between member states in relation to the management of migration flows. this task is not distributed equitably among the member states and a reassessment of the co-financing requirements is justified in the context of the current economic difficulties. i therefore agree with the commission's proposal to increase the cofinancing rates by 20 percentage points for countries benefiting from a financial support mechanism.

in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that technical measures for the conservation of fisheries resources are central elements of a regionalised approach to fisheries management and are added to the annual and biennial decisions taken on catch possibilities. technical measures set out the rules on fishing zones and fishing gear, as opposed to the quantities (fishing effort) and/or catches (tac and quotas) authorised. the commission proposal aims to extend the provisions on technical measures for a further transitional period until a regional framework for technical measures is adopted in accordance with the cfp. as the cfp will not enter into force before 1 january 2013, when the transitional technical measures will expire, the commission is once again proposing an intermediate solution, amending the basic legal act, with an uncertain term. however, i would stress that it is regrettable that another proposal for transitional technical measures is being put before parliament again. it would have been preferable to find a permanent solution in due course. european fishermen need legal certainty and the term 'temporary' should not be used in vain.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it is necessary to ensure the sustainability of fisheries resources and also to ensure that fish stocks are fished sustainably and that the ecosystems in which they live are preserved. poorly designed or inappropriate technical measures can lead to unsustainable fishing practices and, in certain circumstances, can endanger the lives and safety of fishermen.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the conservation of fishery resources, as it will allow the provisions on transitional technical measures to be extended until a regional framework is adopted, in line with the cfp, with a view to ensuring the sustainability of fishing activities.
in writing. - i agree with the rapporteur that it is preferable to give fishermen and businesses in the sector a stable legal framework as regards the technical measures applicable to them. the maintenance of transitional arrangements in matters of this nature does not contribute to the legal certainty of those actors and is therefore a factor of instability. the subject matter of these technical measures is particularly sensitive. the conservation of fisheries resources is essential for the sustainability not only of marine biodiversity but of fisheries as a human activity that generates income and produces societies and individual crops that need to be protected. without the natural resource underlying them, they would necessarily be doomed to disappear. i hope that the conservation of fishery resources will be carried out with sufficient rigor and flexibility to allow timely and attentive responses to the interests of the main actors and their specific circumstances, whenever this is possible without jeopardising the preservation of ecosystems and the renewal of species.
in writing. - we all know that overfishing destroys marine diversity and reduces the prospects for our fishermen by preventing the replenishment of stocks. to prevent this from happening, we must ensure sustainable management of fisheries resources. the report we have just voted on, drawn up by mr pat the cope gallagher, is based on a proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 850/1998 on the conservation of fishery resources through certain technical measures for the protection of juveniles of marine organisms and repealing council regulation (ec) no 1288/2009. because the european union must be an example to the world, i voted in favour of this report and i believe that fisheries have a future only if they are genuinely sustainable. this requires management plans that avoid the capture of juveniles and preserve their growth to adulthood. this regulation will define the mesh sizes of nets to be used and the periods of protection, so as not to affect the normal replenishment of stocks.
in writing. − technical measures lay down rules on the fishing zones and gears used as opposed to the quantities (fishing effort) and/or catches (tac and quotas) authorised. the commission proposal aims to extend the rules on technical measures for the protection of juveniles of marine organisms for a further transitional period until, in a regionalised framework for technical measures, a new framework is adopted in accordance with the future common fisheries policy. the previous regulation included a measure prohibiting fishing with gillnets at depths below 200 metres, which was very burdensome and discriminatory for the portuguese fleet fishing for cod up to approximately 400 metres deep - measures which lacked a scientific basis. we welcome the rapporteur's willingness to accept our amendment on the use of gillnets in ices subarea ix, subject to certain conditions, with a view to putting an end to this discrimination. we voted for the report.
in writing. − the conservation of fishery resources is essential for the maintenance of species and for fishing activity. for my country, portugal, which has a long tradition in the fisheries sector, it is essential to maintain fishing as a viable and sustainable economic activity. maintaining fisheries resources at a good level is important to achieve the numbers needed for consumption and to maintain species with their reproductive capacities and genetic integrity intact. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − technical measures for the conservation of fisheries resources define the rules on fishing zones and fishing gear, and are key elements in a regionalised approach to fisheries management. such measures are designed to ensure the sustainability of fishing activities and are essential to achieving the objectives of the common fisheries policy (cfp). technical conservation measures include the establishment of protection zones and periods, limitation of by-catches, minimum mesh size of nets and minimum landing sizes of species, criteria for the use of more selective fishing gear and environmental protection measures. in this context, this report proposed an update of existing technical measures and the adoption of specific measures aimed at reducing rejections. the report also confirmed an amendment resulting from a portuguese request to allow the national gillnet fleet to resume fishing for redfish between 200 and 600 metres deep. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the importance of these technical measures for the conservation of fishery resources and the safeguarding of the legitimate interests of the national fisheries sector.
in writing. − technical measures for the conservation of fisheries resources are central elements of a regionalised approach to fisheries management. technical measures set out the rules on fishing zones and fishing gear, as opposed to the quantities (fishing effort) and/or catches (tac and quotas) authorised. the commission proposal aims to extend the provisions on technical measures for a further transitional period until a regional framework for technical measures is adopted in line with the common fisheries policy. as it will not enter into force before 1 january 2013, when the transitional technical measures expire, the commission once again proposes an intermediate solution. in addition to the extension of the validity of the current technical measures, the proposed text contains an update of the existing measures, as well as measures to reduce returns in the north-east atlantic, but which have not yet been transposed into union law. for the reasons i have outlined, i voted in favour of the document.

in writing. − violence against women and girls remains one of the most serious human rights violations worldwide, involving victims and perpetrators of all ages and social strata. there can be no tolerance for this kind of situation and the european union is firmly committed to combating any and all forms of violence. women have thus been the main victims of gender-based violence, which constitutes a violation of the fundamental rights to life, safety, liberty, dignity and physical and emotional integrity. special investment in prevention should therefore be made, focusing on areas such as education, knowledge, networking and partnerships, and the exchange of good practice. it is essential to eradicate all forms of violence against women and girls, which requires a coordinated and multi-sectoral approach, including through the creation of a european strategy. it is equally important to strengthen international cooperation and to promote urgent action to eliminate harmful traditional attitudes, practices and customs, including female genital mutilation, early and forced marriage and honour killings.

madam president, commissioner, minister, i think it is useful to start by taking stock of the results of doha. the extension of the kyoto protocol has been positive, but some of the world's largest emitters, such as china and the united states, are still excluded, joined by japan, canada, new zealand and russia. so this agreement covers only about 15% of the world's emissions. this puts into question the objective of limiting the global temperature increase to 2°c. according to a recent united nations study, greenhouse gas emissions levels continue to rise and are 14% above the 2020 targets. if nothing is done, and urgently, there will be a temperature rise of between 3 and 5 degrees celsius this century. another world bank study confirms that global temperatures could rise by 4°c, leading to worsening food crises and extreme weather events, which will particularly affect the poorest. we need to move quickly. no more delays and hesitations. there are also many doubts about funding. in cancun, it was agreed that developed countries would mobilize $100 billion annually to finance climate action in developing countries until 2020. but it is not clear how this funding will be achieved. the eu needs to have a clear and coordinated position on this issue.
madam president, a few days ago the price of a tonne of carbon reached a new low of 2.82 euros. any encouragement to switch to low-carbon technologies was even more distant. according to some analysts, this stimulus would require a carbon price of at least €20 per tonne, seven times higher than the current price. after the frauds it has allowed and after guaranteeing fabulous profits to the polluters, the carbon market reveals once again its essence: to encourage speculation and business as usual in terms of emissions. it's ineffective and it's perverse. now even the "solution" of withdrawing licences from the market - which does not change the essence of the problem - seems to be in jeopardy. it would be good to hear not only from the commission and the council, but also from all those in this parliament who have defended and defend market solutions and the wonderful emissions trading system: from the right to the social democrats, the liberals and even the greens, who are not grey but very grey.
mr president, madam minister, madam commissioner, i welcome the agreement reached in doha to extend the kyoto protocol. although the countries included in the second period of kyoto account for only 15% of global emissions, this is an important decision as the kyoto protocol is the only legally binding agreement to combat climate change. as for the durban platform, progress in doha was limited to discussions on timing and procedural issues and less on content and substance. this is an opportunity for the eu to maintain its leading position by drawing up a solid proposal that takes into account not only environmental concerns but also industrial competitiveness and security of energy supply. i would therefore like to put the following question to the commission: what are the principles, in terms of substance, which the commissioner thinks should be included in the durban platform? is the commission preparing such a proposal? will the commission present its position at the next cop in warsaw on what it wants to see included in the durban platform for a sustainable future, reconciling the environmental side, the competitiveness of the economy and the security of energy supply?
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the wine sector is protected from the risks of fraud and fraudulent practices. as if the dramatic situation in the douro region today were not enough, with thousands of small winegrowers seeing the fruits of their labour without even paying the cost of the harvest, there is now the possibility of usurping traditional names such as vintage, ruby, tawny and others, some of which have been associated with port wine for more than a century. if this were to happen, the laws protecting traditional names, court decisions, industrial property rights and the agreements between the european union and the united states in this field would be used to open the door to the north american wine industry to parasitize the prestige acquired over many years by port wine. it would be yet another intolerable attack on portuguese producers, on consumers, who have been duped, and on the oldest demarcated region in the world, the douro demarcated region. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect.
any authorization of traditional terms, such as the vintage of douro and port wines, by others than the producers themselves constitutes an attack on producers and consumers which deserves our strong reaction and determined fight. it is an attack on consumers because it deliberately and surreptitiously confuses and misleads them into buying cat for a hare. it is an attack on producers because by usurping the legacy of their work and investment, it violently attacks the resources they have built up over time to ensure their competitiveness. the mere possibility of allowing others to use traditional terms runs counter to the european policy of defending consumer rights and the european policies of investing in quality, of promoting designations of origin, of promoting european products. in addition, a previous temporary authorisation in 2006 failed to prevent abuses, which led the commission to notify the united states. it was hoped that this temporary authorization for the use of certain european trade marks by the americans would prevent the use of many other trade marks outside the agreement. the strategy was wrong because not only did it not work, since trademark usurpations persist, but it created a precedent which cannot, under any circumstances, continue to be extended as intended. the problem is not limited to the united states, but threatens to spread to america in general and also to third markets with a great appetite for such designations, in particular the chinese market, which may prefer to import from the united states and thus penalise the european market. i therefore believe that this matter should be closed once and for all and that effective measures should be taken against the usurpation of our trademarks and against the importation of counterfeits.

in writing. − population ageing is one of the most important challenges europe is facing and will face. increased life expectancy and improved health conditions now allow people to live better and longer lives, causing the non-active population to grow, while low birth rates do not allow a replacement of the active population, thus creating difficulties for social security systems. in 2050, the percentage of the population over 60 years old will be 35% compared to only 20% in 2010. that is why, in the knowledge that we are 'aging better' today, it is necessary to find ways of ensuring active, autonomous and healthy ageing, by ensuring that people over 65 remain in the labour market or take on other forms of social intervention, whether in volunteering or in the family, thus freeing up public resources and constituting a real asset for societies.
in writing. − the ageing of the population is now a key challenge for the european union (eu). the number of people aged 65 and over will increase from 85 million in 2008 to 151 million in 2060. moreover, whereas in 2010 20% of the population was 60 years or older, by 2050 this percentage will increase to at least 35%. active and healthy ageing is not just a concept reserved exclusively for our grandparents, but it is also relevant to the younger generations. aging is a process that "technically" begins before birth and ends with death. this report is of great importance because it aims to draw the attention of the european commission to pay particular attention to the multidimensional relationship between older populations and their environment as a precondition for the long-term success of the european innovation partnership for active and healthy ageing.
in writing. the proposal to increase the average number of healthy life years (by 2 years) is the commission's ready response to the increase in average life expectancy, an achievement of civilization, as a result of scientific and technical progress. as we said during the debate, this question lends itself to different and even conflicting approaches. active and healthy ageing creates new social needs and requires investment in a wide range of existing and future public services, starting with health. it also opens up new possibilities for enjoyment and for extending leisure and rest. but the response to the increase in life expectancy in capitalist society seems to be more to increase the pressure on workers, to reduce their rights and to increase the retirement age. this report reflects this tension. the references to the integration of the elderly into the labour market, the flexibility of the labour market, the possibilities of parttime work and providing for different forms of employment contracts suitable for older workers, flexible and partial reforms cannot but raise, even more so in the present political and social context, great concerns.

in writing. - the european union is currently undergoing a demographic transition. its population is ageing rapidly, and the number of people aged 65 and over will increase from 85 million in 2008 to 151 million in 2060. in fact, in 2010, 20% of the population was 60 years or older, and by 2050 that percentage will increase to at least 35%. from a generational point of view, we must therefore question the extent to which the eu and the member states, regions, cities and municipalities are adapted to the needs and (remaining) capacities of their older populations. this implies that we must also ask whether the conditions in these places actually guarantee people an active and healthy ageing. in this context, all policies contributing to active and healthy ageing are welcome and this report, which i am voting for, presents a number of measures, among which i stress the need for a holistic approach to ageing, for comprehensive development and reforms not only in the field of lifelong learning and the labour market, but also in access to them, particularly in terms of transport, infrastructure and buildings.
