in writing. - i approve this report, considering that international trade in wild animals and plants must not constitute a threat to the survival of these species in the wild. whereas it is important to put long-term prosperity above short-term economic interests, and whereas it is, in my view, worrying that the exploitation of wild species, illegal trade in wild fauna and flora, destruction of habitats, climate change and human consumption of natural resources are the main causes of the depletion of biodiversity; i therefore call on the european union and the member states to use the precautionary principle as a basic principle for all their decisions on working papers and proposals for registration, taking particular account of the user-pays principle, an ecosystem-centred approach and traditional conservation principles, while the european union and the member states speak with one voice.
in writing. − the increasing urbanisation and industrialisation of the world has removed some populations from the most immediate contact with many ecosystems and wild species of fauna and flora, and at the same time placed them under greater pressure. news reports often report on the loss of biodiversity, the extinction of species and the unsustainable deterioration of their habitats. the 27 member states of the european union should seek to coordinate their action within the conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora and to ensure that common positions make a serious contribution to raising global awareness and demand for action on these issues.
in writing. − the motion for a resolution follows the questions for oral answer under rule 115 (5) of the rules of procedure on the strategic objectives of the european union (eu) for the 16th meeting of the conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), to be held in bangkok, thailand, from 3 to 14 march 2013. ensuring the conservation of biodiversity is fundamental to the european union's perspective. it is absolutely essential that the european parliament and the council should have a concerted position on this. we must be aware that there is still a lot to be done to preserve vulnerable species, particularly the polar bear. the preservation of biodiversity must often take precedence over economic interests. this thesis is to be defended at the 16th cipes cop in bangkok. there are several stakeholders represented at the cop, but the european union must speak with one voice. only in this way will it be possible to guarantee the essential conditions for the preservation of biodiversity.
in writing. − the conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) regulates international trade in species, i.e. the export, re-export and import of live and dead animals, plants and derivatives. the illegal trade in animals and plants has over the years posed a serious threat to many species and, despite increased control, surveillance and combat in many countries, it remains unfortunately high. we have raised this issue here on several occasions, both in the context of questions to the european commission and in amendments to reports. this resolution addresses a number of concerns, including the transparency of the decision-making process, the financing of cites objectives, the better application of the cites list of marine species caught outside the jurisdiction of any member state, the inclusion of species in annex ii for better control and monitoring, such as certain shark species, and the transfer of annex ii species to annex i (at risk of extinction). this convention has a double benefit, since it protects endangered species and at the same time provides extra protection against invasive species for europe. we voted for the resolution.
in writing. - cites, currently with 177 parties, including the 27 member states of the european union, is the main existing global agreement on wildlife conservation, and aims to prevent the over-exploitation of wild fauna and flora species by international trade. it is essential to ensure that international trade in wild animals and plants does not pose a threat to the survival of those species in the wild. the european union should take a leading role in protecting endangered species by actively participating in the cites convention negotiations and encouraging the removal of gaps that worsen the situation. the eu must be at the forefront of protecting wildlife species. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − this resolution sets out the european parliament's contribution to the eu's strategic objectives for the 16th meeting of the conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites), to be held in bangkok, thailand, from 3 to 14 march 2013. i voted in favour of agreeing with the line taken that it is important to put long-term prosperity above short-term economic interests and to promote effective protection of endangered species.
in writing. the conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) will take place from 3 to 14 march this year. it is the only international conference, to which all 27 member states belong, which aims to take due account of the over-exploitation of wild fauna and flora species by international trade. i believe that we must have a single voice and, given the importance of protecting biodiversity, i am voting in favour of this report.

in writing. − i welcome this report, considering first of all that robust legislation on non-financial transparency will allow investors and citizens to properly assess the true level of corporate social responsibility within companies and businesses operating in the european union. the growing recognition of the role of 'social responsibility' played by business can be interpreted and considered from different perspectives. on the one hand, the process of globalisation and the emergence of 'global' markets favour the development of social and environmental standards by companies; on the other hand, an increasingly attentive and informed society 'demands' that firms behave more responsibly. the dual drive behind the evolution of csr towards an international governance system, defined by some as post-national, reflects the complementarity of interests between business and society at large, which justifies a broader and more forward-looking approach to the subject in order to exploit csr's full potential.

in writing. the commission proposes a new definition of csr as 'the responsibility of enterprises for their impacts on society'. according to this definition, companies should have a set of internal standards that allow them to integrate their social, environmental and ethical concerns into their business operations. the objective of such policies should be to limit any possible negative impacts of business activity by improving and disseminating best practices, to enhance citizens' confidence, and to ensure that high levels of social responsibility are truly recognised and clearly preferred by consumers. such corporate social responsibility rules, however, should always be a form of self-regulation and not an external imposition.
in writing. - the present report, by mr raffaele baldassarre, deals with corporate social responsibility (csr), more specifically with responsible and transparent behaviour by companies in order to achieve sustainable growth. the aim of this initiative is to assess the policies pursued by enterprises in social terms. many companies do not value their social role and are unaware of the benefits - even financial - that can come from being publicly recognised as socially responsible, which will sooner or later lead to increased public confidence. this requires strengthening the links between social responsibility and competitiveness, improving the transparency and effectiveness of social efficiency policies and helping smes not to undervalue their social role but to show them how they can collectively tackle social and environmental problems. i therefore advocate that these programmes should be voluntary and not compulsory, so as not to penalise companies but to make them feel that this is a real improvement in their performance.
in writing. the rapporteur believes that companies can contribute to the development of the so-called social market economy and to the europe 2020 strategy. it considers that csr also and above all means competitiveness and that certain measures can help to create a community of values between the company, its shareholders and society at large. the new definition inherits the concept previously defined by the commission, according to which companies integrate social and environmental concerns into their business activities and interaction with other stakeholders on a voluntary basis. in short, a view that inherits and is subsidiary to the old theories of class conciliation. precarious and low-paid work, flexicurity, relocations for higher profits, the closure of thousands of businesses, millions of unemployed, poverty: this is the reality in europe on which this report is based (even though it tries to ignore it). it is symptomatic that the report, in the present context, does not say a word about the workers and their problems. more than declarations of intent, wish lists and idyllic visions of the world of work, which ignore the sharpening class conflict in it, we need legal instruments that oblige companies to meet their social and environmental responsibilities.
in writing. − the current global economic crisis may have been the result of errors in transparency and accountability, as well as short-term vision. it is the responsibility of all to learn these lessons to avoid a repetition in the future. csr, if properly implemented and practised by all enterprises, makes a major contribution to restoring the lost confidence needed for a sustainable economic recovery and can also mitigate the social consequences of the economic crisis. when companies take responsibility for society, the environment and workers, this creates a win-win situation at all levels, which helps to increase the basis of trust necessary for their economic success. it is therefore important to make csr part of the corporate responsibility strategy and of society as a whole. many companies, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), are setting an excellent example in this respect. hence my vote.
in writing. - since csr is linked to an economic investment whose benefits are not immediately palpable, it is often seen as a burden for companies with limited resources. this fallacy is also justified by the fact that many smes are not usually aware of the positive effects that social responsibility can have on their economic performance and are not informed about good practices that can increase these benefits. this is the importance of this initiative and of promoting the virtues of corporate social responsibility, particularly to smes, which are the engine of the eu economy.

in writing. − on 31 july 2012, the european commission presented a proposal for a rapid response mechanism (rrm) which allows member states to react to vat fraud more quickly and effectively. the european union loses several billion euros a year to this fraud, and the system for combating it is time-consuming and very bureaucratic. the new procedure will allow member states to react to fraud almost immediately, while more permanent measures are being created. it thus becomes a key mechanism in the fight against tax fraud and evasion, while safeguarding public revenues at a time of fiscal constraints and austerity. the commission is also proposing some improvements to the ec proposal, such as the introduction of a prior consultation period, ensuring that the new legislation does not harm compliant businesses or taxpayers, and the involvement of this proposal in a long-term strategy to combat vat fraud. the proposal represents an important step forward in this area and i support it.

in writing. − vat fraud costs national budgets several billion euros annually and in some cases, such as during the period from june 2008 to december 2009, vat fraud in relation to greenhouse gas emission allowances resulted in an estimated loss of five billion euros. in june 2012, the commission put forward a proposal for a rapid response mechanism (rrm) which will allow member states to respond to vat fraud more quickly and effectively. under the mrr, a member state faced with a serious case of sudden and large-scale vat fraud may apply certain emergency measures in a way that is not permitted under current vat legislation. this is all the more relevant at a time when several member states are going through difficult periods in their economies and are undertaking difficult fiscal consolidation and macroeconomic stabilisation measures, and the fight against vat fraud should be an eu priority.
in writing. − the shortage of financial resources at european level, resulting from the economic and financial crisis which has led to a sharp decline in consumption and the bankruptcy of many companies, has led to a significant reduction in public revenue, particularly in value added tax (vat), with direct implications for both national and community budgets. on the other hand, there is an increasing number of tax evasion by crossborder companies issuing bogus invoices or engaging in 'carousel' fraud, which harms not only the public purse but also the companies that are doing the right thing and are faced with this unfair competition. i welcome the commission's initiative to implement a rapid action mechanism against vat fraud - a fraud that costs member states billions of euros every year - which complements other existing anti-fraud instruments. because this is the greatest form of tax fraud, i welcome the adoption of this report by mr david casa and hope that it will be implemented quickly, because this is a fight for the honest citizen, for good business practices and against unfair competition.

in writing. − the european union loses several billion euros annually to vat fraud. the current system for combating vat fraud is time-consuming and very bureaucratic. on 31 july 2012, the commission presented a proposal for a rapid response mechanism (rrm) which allows member states to react to vat fraud more quickly and effectively, acting more quickly and burdening the beneficiaries of the goods/services concerned. with this system, countries will be able to combat complex and linked fraud schemes more effectively. the new procedure will allow the member state to react to fraud almost immediately, while more permanent measures are being created. it thus becomes a key mechanism in the fight against tax fraud and evasion, while safeguarding public revenues at a time of fiscal constraints and austerity. in agreeing with this mechanism and with the proposals put forward by the rapporteur, in particular the inclusion of this proposal in a long-term strategy to combat vat fraud, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − at the end of july 2012, the european commission presented a proposal for a directive on the common system of value added tax as regards the rapid reaction mechanism against fraud. i support this report which aims to contribute to increasing the efficiency of vat in the context of fiscal consolidation, and tax collection and the fight against tax evasion must be improved. i believe that public revenue could increase if there is a continuous fight against carousel fraud which is perpetuated on an international scale due to the rigid reaction of the european authorities. faced with ineffective action at european level, member states may be tempted to take immediate action without an adequate legal basis in eu law and may later be challenged in court for lack of a legal basis. it is essential that there be a reinforcement of the supervision of vat collection systems in the european union and that integrated measures be taken to combat tax fraud and evasion.
in writing. - vat fraud reduces national budgets and the eu's own by several billion euros. the so-called austerity policy, which reduces the purchasing power of workers by reducing wages and raising taxes, also reduces this revenue. the creation of the mrr, enabling member states to react and deal with new forms of fraud, can have positive consequences. currently, if a member state wishes to respond to vat fraud by taking measures not provided for in eu vat legislation, it must submit a formal request for a derogation. the commission draws up a proposal to this effect and submits it to the council for unanimous approval so that the measures can be implemented. this process can be slow and complex, causing delays for the member state in taking the necessary measures to prevent fraud. this possibility should not, however, be an exception but rather an inalienable sovereign right of all member states. if there is a genuine concern about combating tax fraud and tax evasion, then measures should be taken to put an end to the free movement of capital. its maintenance (as a dogma) renders apparently well-intentioned measures ineffective.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering first of all that the commission needs to change its position on the annual growth survey. there is no growth in europe at present and only 0.1% growth is forecast by the european commission. we must ask ourselves how long the european commission and the member states, who are seeing the devastating effects of budgetary and fiscal austerity, will remain in the same position on growth? in my view, that is not acceptable. the commission and the member states themselves present a major contradiction when they say that austerity will 'save' the economic and financial situation of the member states and at the same time they talk about economic growth, while they only take counterproductive measures in relation to economic growth. finally, i would like to stress that if the imf itself has already lowered its growth expectations, i think that is a clear signal for the european union to take alternative measures.
in writing. − this report is part of the european semester process for the coordination of the economic policies of the eu member states. it contributes to the european parliament's opinion on the 2013 annual growth survey (ags) prepared by the european commission. the commission proposal is generally supported. parliament nevertheless considers it important to emphasize a few essential points. it considered it essential that the process of economic and financial adjustment in the member states be accompanied by a growth-friendly strategy adapted to the specific characteristics of each country. it stresses the strategic benefits of using the flexibility of economic adjustment as set out in the stability and growth pact. the recommendation is also left to control public spending so that it does not exceed the level of economic growth, to manage excessive macroeconomic imbalances in the member states (deficits and surpluses) and to promote sustainable, environmentally friendly growth, supported by the promotion of a flexible labour market that helps to combat youth unemployment. i support this report, which recognises the important contribution of the european parliament in the development of the economic governance processes of the european union.
in writing. − the annual growth survey marks the start of the so-called european semester a practice introduced in 2010 and which, in the parlance of the institutions, translates into the method of policy coordination to enable member states to align their economic and budgetary policies with the stability and growth pact and the europe 2020 strategy. the objective of the european semester is not only to ensure the financial stability of the eu, but also to stimulate sustainable growth through reforms, in the framework of the europe 2020 strategy. i therefore vote in favour of this own-initiative report. the commission's recommendations in its growth survey 2013 are based on five fiscal, economic and social priorities for member states. in particular, the promotion of sustainable growth and competitiveness, combined with the fight against unemployment and the social consequences of the crisis, the modernisation of public administration, the reduction of national debts without undermining growth and the restoration of normal lending practices to the economy. i would stress, in view of the situation in my country, that fiscal consolidation which is growth friendly seems to me to be necessary to overcome the crisis, but, and i emphasize this, the measures implemented so far are finally beginning to have positive and encouraging effects.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it was not possible to include in the final proposal measures which would help to readjust the austerity effort by making the time of the budgetary consolidation exercise more flexible. the position of the right-wing political groups in the european parliament, which have rejected proposals to soften the austerity measures that are having a devastating effect on several eurozone economies, is regrettable.
in writing. - although i voted in favour of the report, i believe that it could have gone further in line with the rapporteur's proposals. fiscal consolidation must be smart to allow growth. i voted in favour of amendment no 2 which referred to the possibility that a possible adjustment of the deadline for correcting excessive deficits in specific cases could be justified, in full respect of the spirit and letter of the stability and growth pact, as amended by the six-pack on economic governance, which the member states respect. i also voted in favour of amendment no 3 which called on the council and the commission to monitor and assess the process of fiscal adjustment and its impact on the economic situation of the member states and, on the basis of the principle of differentiated, smart and growth-friendly fiscal consolidation, to monitor intensively the effects of the adjustment deadlines on growth and consolidation, to recognise the strategic benefits that the flexibility of the sgp confers in periods of severe economic recession and to take these elements into account when analysing the medium-term budgetary objective.
in writing. the differences between the right and the social democrats in the process of drawing up and discussing this report, which were also expressed in the final vote, do not hide the essential point: it is the consensus between these two families that has guided the essential process of european capitalist integration, including the lines of response to the crisis in which the eu is immersed. it is not pointless disagreements on incidental aspects that hide the joint support for the budgetary treaty, economic governance and the european semester and what these instruments mean as an attack on democracy and the sovereignty of the peoples. the consensus extends to 'budgetary consolidation', 'structural reforms' and other jargon which means nothing more than a brutal attack on the civilizational achievements of the workers and peoples and, to that extent, represents a civilizational retreat. even on the question of debt mutualization, the consensus between the two is clear in support of the "stability bonds" an instrument of extortion and domination of the centre over the periphery, far from any idea of solidarity sharing the burden of debt. we have voted against this report. not because of any punctual and opportunistic demarcation of the results of these policies, but because we consistently condemn and combat them.

in writing. − this report is a contribution by the european parliament to the european semester process, containing its opinion on the 2013 annual growth survey (ags). the commission proposal is generally supported, but parliament considers it important to emphasize a few essential points. it considered it essential that the process of economic and financial adjustment in the member states be accompanied by a growth-friendly strategy adapted to the specific characteristics of each country. it stresses the strategic benefits of using the flexibility of economic adjustment as set out in the sgp. it also recommends controlling public spending, managing excessive macroeconomic imbalances in the member states and promoting sustainable, environmentally friendly growth, supported by the promotion of a flexible labour market that helps to combat youth unemployment. i think that this is a balanced report, which equates the need for a growth strategy and points to the flexibility of the budgetary adjustment procedures, and i therefore voted in favour. i cannot, however, fail to regret the fact that some of the rapporteur's proposals, which emphasized these aspects and ensured greater adaptation to the realities of the countries under adjustment, were not adopted.
in writing. - i am in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that further fiscal consolidation is necessary to achieve sound public accounts and to reduce public debt, since above 90% of debt there will be no sustainable growth. at the same time, however, member states should introduce the structural reforms needed to avoid future government deficits and to achieve sustainable growth. i am therefore in favour of intelligent differentiation and flexibility, according to the needs of each member state, taking into account the stability and growth pact. i would therefore like to stress the need to make labour markets more flexible so that young people can enter the labour market more easily. the single market, a source of growth and jobs in the european union, where smes play a major role, also needs to be completed. call for political union in the member states to take the necessary structural measures which in the short term may have negative effects on the lives of citizens, but which in the medium and long term will bring sustainable growth, based on eu2020. coordination of the european semester with national fiscal policies is essential for true economic governance.

in writing. - i welcome this report, stressing first and foremost that the european commission must face up to the facts and re-evaluate its economic development models. europe will not be able to achieve the objectives of strategy 2020 if it does not move beyond short-term austerity policies, which are degrading in terms of recent employment and growth figures. what europe needs are investment targets and growth-friendly fiscal consolidation, taking better account of the specific situations of each member state. i also stress the role of parliaments, which must be more involved in order to overcome the lack of democratic accountability of the european semester for the coordination of economic policies.
in writing. − 2012 was a disastrous year for employment in europe. in the 27 member states, almost 26 million european citizens are out of work. unemployment rates have reached historic highs, especially for young people. in my country, portugal, more than one in three young people are looking for a job and have no prospect of finding one. economic growth and job creation must be the european union's top priorities. i therefore supported this report on the annual growth survey for 2013 which sets out what the european union's priorities should be for the next 12 months in terms of reforms and fiscal, economic, social and employment policies. member states should pursue gradual and growth-friendly fiscal consolidation in order to avoid negative short-, medium- and long-term effects on growth and employment.
in writing. − job creation through structural reforms and growth-oriented investment, as well as the fight against poverty and social exclusion, must be central to eu social policies and national agendas. i therefore vote in favour of this own-initiative report. in 2012, the employment situation deteriorated in the eu, bringing the unemployment rate to 10,5%. but this high figure conceals more worrying realities, including a wide discrepancy between the real situation in the various member states and youth unemployment. today, about one in four of our young people is unemployed, but in some member states the proportion rises to one in two. it is urgent to make youth unemployment a priority in the eu and member states. the development of global strategies to combat the problem, including investment in education and training and encouragement of cooperation between education and business, is essential to better meet the needs of a labour market that is also more adaptable, dynamic and inclusive, and that responds with better quality jobs. to this end, fiscal consolidation must be pursued in a differentiated and proportionate manner, in a way that is favourable to growth and ensures economic recovery.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering first of all that a well-functioning single market economically, environmentally and socially is a basic issue for the european semester. i therefore believe that to achieve real improvements, we need clearer and more rigorous governance of the single market. to this end, it is particularly important to establish a transparent and predictable framework that adequately and regularly reflects any positive and negative results achieved by member states in terms of implementation. the single market governance cycle should be considered in the light of the european semester, which already addresses not only economic and budgetary aspects but also employment-related aspects. given the economic importance of the single market, regular assessment of its situation would add value to these assessments and complete the picture. in this sense, in my view, the european semester should serve as a platform and cycle to provide the above-mentioned policy guidance. to this end, it is suggested that a pillar of the single market be created alongside the economic and budgetary aspects.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner oettinger, we are coming to the end of a long legislative process, but i believe it will end well. i would like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs for their involvement and contribution, and i would also like to thank the opinion reports of the other parliamentary committees and the support of the chairman of the itre committee, and especially the support of the commission and the support of the council under the cypriot presidency, as they all contributed to a positive outcome. this regulation implements measures to create a european energy market. it comes at a time when it is no longer feasible for member states to close their energy markets in a logic of self-sufficiency and protectionism. the transformation underway in our energy system requires interdependence at european level as a way of exploiting synergies that create a true european market, allowing the integration of renewables to be accelerated and thus made more sustainable, and generating solidarity and security of supply, avoiding islands and bottlenecks. it is essential to remove physical and interoperability barriers between different countries and to end the geographical isolation or near-isolation of certain european regions in terms of interconnections. this process has been extremely slow and fraught with obstacles. for example, the economic downturn makes infrastructure investment difficult; the positive externalities of infrastructure do not in themselves constitute an incentive for private investment; the construction permit processes have been excessively long, on average 10-12 years. the regulation now agreed proposes a boost to the development of energy infrastructure, a meagre investment of five billion from the mff will leverage some two hundred billion in gas and electricity infrastructure by 2020. a set of geographical corridors and priority areas, smart grids, electricity highways, co2 transportation for infrastructure development have been identified. the selection of projects of common interest shall be made on the basis of criteria in line with the objectives of the european energy policy and shall include a cost-benefit analysis. in the creation of the european energy market, special emphasis is placed on the elimination of the isolation of certain regions. projects of common interest will benefit from simplified and accelerated licensing, including specific spatial planning, allowing for their authorisation within a period of up to four and a half years and subjecting non-compliant member states to infringement procedures by the commission. a mechanism for cross-border cost leasing has been defined based on the benefits of implementing the project with appropriate and risk-proportionate incentives. parliament also proposed a new operational coordination mechanism for the system, which aims to collect and share real-time information on the continuous operation of the network by operators. the central objective will be to ensure security against the possibility of blackouts. the adoption and entry into force of this regulation is therefore urgent. it will promote public and private investment, helping to create the economic growth and jobs that europe so badly needs today.
member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission has already made a number of proposals. if you agree to this legislative proposal, then we will take the following steps: firstly, we will conclude the work with all the parties involved, entso-e and entsog, the transmission system operators, in the coming weeks to present our draft list, our proposal for projects of common european interest. this pci label has several functions. on the one hand, it is a guarantee that the member states concerned will develop their transfrontier networks in exactly the same way. that means one doesn't plan against or without the other. it is a common priority of two or more neighbouring countries, and the route, timetable and capacity issues are coordinated. the bemip process is certainly an example. we are working very closely with the three baltic countries, finland and poland. we also include existing links kaliningrad and russia . we have a consensus on electricity, but the last open question in the gas sector is where the lng terminal will be built, and, in addition, which transmission lines will be needed for gas. this list will then be checked with you. it is then practically the benchmark for us to determine which projects should be implemented as a matter of priority. secondly, the pci label will certainly also create an even better opportunity to get justice in court. this means that we will not fail in court with planning and approval, but - as they have been defined as priorities by the european institutions and by several member states - the building permit will also be confirmed in court. many pcis do not require public funding. we continue to prioritise the financing of energy infrastructure by the market - through network charges, user fees and pragmatic, good regulation, with a decent return and low risk for the investor. the fact that we have developed these plans on a european basis has also aroused great interest, particularly from long-term investors. what do i mean? life insurance companies, in particular, and insurance companies in general, are ideal partners. an insurance company wants to invest the money of its customers, its partners, in the long term, to have a fixed return and the least possible risk. this is precisely what cross-border investments in gas or electricity transmission lines can do. we have no dispute in the commission on the subject of project bonds, but there have been reservations in the council for a long time. the member states have long refused to give us this instrument of indirect indebtedness. it is only a year ago that we first received approval from the member states, in a trial phase of free resources in the current budget, to issue project bonds to test their merits. we will evaluate this experience and i am sure that the whole commission will then accept project bonds in the energy sector as a financing instrument for the next few years and project bonds will be issued on a larger scale because they are ultimately a very efficient form of financing. direct financing is co-financing, i.e. covering 20, 30, 40, 50 or even 60% of the cost of an infrastructure. then the €5 billion or a little more, depending on the outcome of the discussions in connecting europe would be used up very quickly. in many cases, however, interest rate subsidies or even guarantees that never work are sufficient. that is why we want to present a wide range of instruments. for one infrastructure, a particular instrument, for another infrastructure, a very different instrument will be the most efficient form of investment, and then we expect that the 5 or 6 billion euros in implementation will be good for far more than this budget amount. there was a call about nabucco. so what is the general status of the southern corridor? we are confident that 2018 will be the first year that the shah deniz ii gas field will produce gas. the consortium will decide this year who gets those gas supplies. two candidates are in the short list. it is clear that this amounts to 16, 17, 18 billion cubic metres, of which 6 to 7 billion are destined for the turkish market and 10 or 11 billion for the european union market from 2018 onwards. the network in azerbaijan is clear. georgia is clear. in turkey, they are working with tanap, which is a consortium of socar and the turkish gas network operator, and presumably consortium members like bp or total or statoil from the shah deniz ii consortium will go in as co-shareholders. it is clear how the pipelines from the turkish border to the european union will be connected. one concept is called nabucco west, which means bulgaria, romania, hungary, austria and thus the central european market, the other tap, which means greece, albania, italy. the igas have closed, and now it is up to the shah deniz ii consortium to decide who, in their view, has made the more viable, better offer. we expect that decision to be taken in july or september at the latest. we would accept both decisions: both lead to the european internal gas market, both meet our strategic objective of diversification, and the opening of the southern corridor to azerbaijan to supply not only oil but also gas is of high strategic value, so we are anxiously awaiting the direction of the decision this summer. thank you very much for your comments and suggestions. we look forward to continuing our cooperation with you on energy infrastructure.
the rapporteur. - i would like to telegraph a few points. firstly, the president of the commission wrote to the president of parliament about a year ago asking that this report be voted on at first reading. we complied with that request. secondly, we must take account of our main energy requirement: consumers. we know that prices will rise naturally because of the large investment we have to make. the market certainly finances but it is the final consumer who pays and we cannot forget the good use of these resources. third, there's a lot of research to be done, a lot of research on renewables, a lot of research on integrating renewables into smart grids. fourthly, we have to admit that some redundancy of networks will be essential. security of supply requires it. fifthly, we must link these laws and regulations to energy efficiency. these are not separate matters, they are linked and finally i would also like to thank the commission for accepting parliament's recommendation on network coordination. the coordination of networks was once seen as something nebulous, today it is less nebulous, today it is an essential reality and it is thanks to the openness of the commission that it has accepted parliament's recommendation.
the discussion on transeuropean energy infrastructures cannot be dissociated from the context of liberalisation and privatisation of this strategic sector. the commission's proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs intended for human consumption, and the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs intended for human consumption, are both of particular relevance to the present debate. the insistence on the miraculous virtues of market openness and competition does not hide the real consequences of this option. experience shows it clearly: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. monopoly concentration is advancing on a european scale, and workers' and consumers' rights are being eroded. the constraints on the less developed economies are increasing. the other side of the coin of the fabulous profits of the industry's economic groups - to whom publicly funded infrastructure is handed over on a platter - is the heavy energy bill imposed on businesses and households and the increase in energy poverty, which is affecting more and more households in europe.
for the gue/ngl group mr president, i too would like to thank my colleague for her work. it was a very difficult negotiation indeed. mrs tzavela knows that we could not support her proposal, and we do not agree with the commission's proposal. and for very simple reasons. i think this proposal ignores all the priority issues of energy policy in our time. when we have the problem of scarce resources, we abandon binding targets for renewable energy. when we have the central problem in europe of lack of growth and job creation, we abandon energy efficiency, which was fundamental to boosting the economy. when we have the problem of climate change, of sustainable energy, the role of nuclear energy in europe continues to grow, not only to grow, but to grow, even though we are discussing this report two years exactly after the fukushima tragedy. and finally, when we have such severe situations of energy poverty. we are talking about all this, but we are betting on the liberalisation and privatisation of energy, leaving the member states no room to define any action in such strategic sectors as this. and therefore, we cannot support.
mr president, planning is an exercise of freedom. only with freedom can you master the future. having a long-term policy allows us to find our place in the global market of the energy industry and energy efficiency. we must make europe more competitive in this area. all energy policy has a social dimension. it affects our future life. we must ensure fair prices for consumers and find non-discriminatory mechanisms to mitigate the severity of the increases we know are inevitable.
mr president, i would like to stress the importance, also mentioned in this report, of the need to align this long-term strategy with all the regions of europe. the challenges facing energy systems in the most isolated regions, in particular in the outermost islands, where dependence on fuels is exacerbated by distance and geographical isolation, also need to be addressed appropriately. in this connection, i would like to make parliament and the commission aware once again of the need to develop more specific approaches in these cases to find the appropriate answers, not only to solve the particular problems they present but above all to be able to expand the full potential of renewable energies, as in the case of the azores, which are already in full development today, even exceeding the targets set by the union for 2020. however, commissioner, they are still faced with an overly standardised energy policy which does not yet respond adequately to them, and this is something we must also address in this energy road map for 2050.
mr president, we strongly disagree with the market approach taken by the european union in the field of greenhouse gas emissions. the limitations and contradictions of this approach are now clearly visible in the functioning of the carbon market. we therefore reject the idea that measuring and reporting the carbon flow can in any way feed into this market logic underlying the whole approach to the problem of climate change. but we recognize the importance of improving our understanding of carbon flows and the role of soils in these processes. soil is the largest reservoir of organic matter on earth, and this organic matter is essential to its fertility. the preservation of this carbon, as well as the study and monitoring of the mechanisms underlying its fixation and its flows, the anthropogenic impacts, are very important. the efforts to promote an international research and cooperation programme in this field could make an important contribution to filling the knowledge gaps that exist today.
mr president, today marks the 38th anniversary of a major date in portugal's recent history. the project of independent and sovereign progress and development to which the april revolution opened doors required a banking system at the service of the people and the country. this requirement was met on 11 march with the nationalisation of the banking sector. almost four decades later, the banks, although they have been reprivatised, are not only far from fulfilling their social function but have become a veritable drain on the resources of the people and the country. the financial capital raised billions of euros, via the eu/imf programme and speculation on the interest of sovereign debt. money extorted from the pockets of the portuguese workers and people in a process made possible by the treaties and the policies of the european union. it is necessary and possible to stop this robbery. the nationalization of the banks, with public and democratic control of the entire financial system, is an imperative of justice and a necessary step to overcome blockages and put the country back on the path of progress, development and social justice.
mr president, the financing of development cooperation is more than a gesture of solidarity, it is a duty, an imperative of justice. it represents the recognition of the responsibility of the richer countries to correct the asymmetric interdependence which has marked the development of the historical process and which characterizes the dominant economic system on a world scale. it would therefore be intolerable if the next multiannual financial framework were to imply a reduction in the resources available in this field and, in particular, a reduction in the european development fund. we insist, on the contrary, on the need to increase the amount of development aid, to make it more visible, more predictable and to improve democratic control. we also insist that this does not mean that the sectoral policies of the european union must be radically changed, so that they are consistent with the declared but not implemented objectives of development aid.
mr president, commissioner, the establishment of a level playing field for economic and social development in the geographically most remote regions of the union - the outermost regions and the overseas territories - is a merit. i therefore congratulate the rapporteur on the decision to establish an overseas association. in this way, the european union is demonstrating the value of the solidarity on which it is based, while also benefiting from the added value of the specific characteristics of these regions. the objectives of this declaration - increasing competitiveness, strengthening resilience, reducing vulnerability and promoting cooperation with other partners - are essential for our territories as well as for the octs. in this context, i would stress the importance of enhancing the brand image of specific products, especially when these economies are harmed by eu agreements with third countries, and also the need to redefine a differentiated european strategy that strengthens the competitiveness of these regions in the areas of tourism, transport, fisheries and agriculture. all these wishes are, however, met with negative discrimination by the european commission in imposing a 150 km limit for crossborder cooperation, which must be changed urgently.
mr president, i thank you and my colleagues díaz de mera and iacolino for the change in the order of the entries, and i would like to begin by reaffirming that racism and xenophobia are a clear violation of the principles of freedom, democracy, respect for fundamental rights and freedoms and the rule of law. that is a violation of the common values on which the european union is founded. the charter of fundamental rights prohibits all forms of discrimination and obliges member states to actively combat hate crime, i.e. crimes motivated by racism, xenophobia, religious or ethnic intolerance, disability, sexual orientation or gender. unfortunately, discrimination, intolerance and hate crimes continue to be felt daily throughout europe. we need a more active fight at european level against racism, intolerance and xenophobia. this requires that policy-makers in the member states demonstrate greater political will to combat widespread prejudice against certain groups and to redress any harm that may have been caused to victims. as such, i hope the council will not waste any more time and finally adopt the equal treatment directive. i hope that we can also start the process of reviewing the 2008 framework decision soon, hoping that this time it will not take the council six years to reach a political agreement. an effective fight against hate crimes requires that we are able to make these crimes more visible and to hold their perpetrators accountable. we must also break down the wall of silence, encouraging victims and witnesses to report such situations, and ensuring that they have the opportunity to obtain redress.
madam president, as the rapporteur on the situation of fundamental rights, the rule of law and democracy in hungary, i would like to thank all our colleagues. mr verhofstadt has quoted article 7 of the treaty on european union, mr szájer article 4. i would like to quote article 2, which is the first substantive article of the treaties. it says that the union is founded upon democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. not only the member states, but also the union’s institutions, have to respect these values: that means that we too have a direct responsibility to protect these fundamental values of the union. the constitutional amendments do indeed affect some of these fundamental values, from the independence of the judiciary, including the prerogatives of the constitutional court, to freedom of expression. in the context of the report on hungary, we have already produced four working documents, including one co-signed with the epp on the independence of the judiciary. we will also focus, in the upcoming report on hungary, on the fourth amendment, which we will thoroughly assess. meanwhile, we would ask the commission to focus its efforts intensively on the dialogue with hungary on fundamental rights. there is no other issue that merits our attention more than this one.
madam president, very briefly, i promise, and it is a real request for clarification, on what can only be a clerical error or a drafting error. because it says in recital c that, and we are supposed to vote, the credit crisis which is the origin of the current recession was a man-made catastrophe. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. and to say that the international crisis is the fault of men, if it is not a matter of editorial error, would simply be ridiculous and a disrespect for great women like hillary clinton, dilma rousseff, angela merkel, catherine ashton, and so many others who, in their own right, have risen to prominent places in humanity. and that, madam president, is the question of whether it is a mistake or simply ridiculous.
in writing. - i would like to draw attention to the fact that the outermost regions continue to face an overly standardised energy policy which is not yet adequately responsive to their needs. it is not only important to solve the particular problems they have, but above all to enable them to expand their full potential for renewable energy, and the definition of matters relating to european energy infrastructures must take this into account. the plan for this report should take account of the need to integrate peripheral energy markets. regional groups should be set up to propose and re-evaluate projects of common interest with a view to establishing regional lists of projects of common interest. those regional groups shall ensure close cooperation between member states, national regulatory authorities, project promoters and stakeholders. projects of common interest which have been completed or which no longer fulfil the criteria and requirements laid down in this regulation shall not be included in the following union list. existing projects of common interest to be included in the next union list should be subject to the same selection process for the establishment of regional lists and for the establishment of the union list as the proposed projects.
in writing. − sustainable, safe and affordable energy is one of the major challenges that unites europeans, from civil society to policy-makers, industry and environmentalists. the objectives of the european energy policy clearly set targets to be achieved by 2020. these objectives are: (i) 20% reduction in greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions; (ii) 20% of final energy consumption from renewable energy sources; (iii) 20% increase in energy efficiency. this proposal lays down rules for the timely development and interoperability of the trans-european energy networks in order to achieve the energy policy objectives set out in the treaty on the functioning of the european union. it is important to ensure the functioning of the internal energy market, to ensure the security of supply of the union and to promote energy efficiency, the development of new and renewable forms of energy, and the combination of energy networks. the new regulation is a positive and important initiative, as it aims to accelerate the establishment of the internal energy market and deliver concrete results for eu energy policy and climate objectives. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'trans-european energy infrastructures', which presents proposals to strengthen the integration of the internal energy market and to respond to the energy isolation of certain geographical areas, in order to ensure the achievement of the objectives set by the union in terms of competitiveness, security of supply, sustainability and decarbonisation.
in writing. − green growth without undermining competitiveness requires a sustainable and consistent energy policy, the proper functioning of the emission allowance market and the development of national projects that contribute to the community's objectives of reducing emissions and increasing energy independence. it is essential that europe should achieve energy independence, which can only be achieved in two ways: (i) greater diversification of sources which is absolutely necessary in gas; and (ii) increased energy produced in the union. to achieve this, it is necessary to continue to focus on renewable energy, with particular emphasis on wind power, whose offshore potential may be under-exploited, and to redefine european policy for the exploitation of nuclear energy, while ensuring high standards of safety and reliability.
in writing. the report, drawn up by mr antónio fernando correia de campos, concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on guidelines for trans-european energy infrastructures and repealing decision no 1364/2006/ec. the aim of this regulation is to contribute to the creation of a genuine european energy market supplying some 500 million consumers. this requires that member states do not close themselves in on their own interests but instead pool their synergies around a common objective. this regulation will encourage further investment in the improvement of energy transport networks, particularly gas and electricity, thus increasing the safety and quality of the service provided to the european consumer. in addition, the investments made by the jobs generated will contribute to the revival of the european economy. through a partnership between the eu, the ems and industry, an intelligent and integrated pan-european structure can be created, guaranteeing the quality of the service provided and price stability. i voted in favour of this report, which brings a long legislative process to an end, and i hope that it will be implemented quickly, because it is a positive step forward in this area by removing physical and non-operational barriers between member states.
in writing. - this is another step in the definition of the so-called european energy policy, based on the liberalisation of the energy market and the creation of a european energy market. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the energy sector is not left to the private sector. the intention is to establish a european network for the transport of energy between member states and for supply with the outside world. funding will be allocated to so-called projects of common interest, limited to projects aimed at europeanisation networks, proposed by energy transmission system operators, which safeguard the common european and international strategic interest. questions, some of them pertinent, concerning the rationality and security of energy supply are invoked in favour of the implementation of a policy option of liberalization which does not safeguard them. this is yet another example of how public funds are channeled into investments that the energy monopolies will enjoy, reaping fabulous profits. member states have to comply with the rules of the european energy market and the guidelines of the european energy policy in order to receive any funding under the mechanism (thus undermining the possibility of public ownership of this strategic sector). we voted against it, of course.
in writing. − significant efforts are needed to modernise and extend european energy infrastructure and to interconnect networks across borders in order to meet the union's key energy policy objectives of competitiveness, sustainability and security of supply. this regulation aims at: fully integrating the internal energy market, in particular by ensuring that no member state remains isolated from the european grid; contributing to sustainable development and environmental protection, enabling the union to meet its targets of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 20%; increasing energy efficiency by 20% and achieving a 20% share of energy from renewable sources in final energy consumption by 2020, while ensuring security of supply and solidarity between member states. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that sustainable, secure and affordable energy is needed throughout europe, as provided for in the objectives of european energy policy, as enshrined in the treaty of lisbon. at the same time, i believe that the implementation of such a policy has been very slow, and that more rapid, more incisive action is needed where a stronger role for europe in coordinating and integrating national efforts is imperative, without jeopardizing its competitiveness vis-à-vis other producers and other markets. i therefore agree that this process can be improved in the four main areas mentioned: the selection process for projects of common interest shall be directed to europeanisation networks; the proposal must provide effective instruments for the use of infrastructure; the proposal should also promote cooperation and coordination between network operators to deliver the expected benefits; and reinforce investments in this sector.
in writing. − the completion of the single market also requires the creation of a true trans-european energy network through a concerted energy policy at european level that supports security of supply, sustainability and the decarbonisation of energy sources, thus achieving the union's 2020 objective. the problems facing the establishment of the energy market are numerous, including obstacles to the development of crossborder infrastructure, too long licensing procedures and lack of investment. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. as i come from an outermost region, i tabled several amendments which were included in the document, not only on the isolation of the island and remote regions from the single market, but above all on the potential these regions can offer in terms of renewable energy. it is all too important that the more remote regions that are more dependent on fossil fuels receive special attention and support in the search for alternatives.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account the case of the expansion of vienna airport, which according to the investigation started without an environmental impact assessment, and with 27 organisations opposed to this work. i agree with the aim of harmonizing the clear parameters for the independence of expert studies and advocating the adoption of a general regulation on administrative procedures in the union, which strengthens the position of the complainants. i believe that this should serve as an example of the transparency that should be promoted in all administrative procedures, both in the member states and in the european union as a whole.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the commission should reconsider its approach to the handling of the infringement complaint concerning vienna airport. the commission should follow the ombudsman's recommendations for addressing this issue and take into account the obligation of national authorities to ensure that complainants have access to an appeal procedure and that measures are taken to address a conflict of interest in the application of directive 85/337/eec.
in writing. - article 228 tfeu ensures that citizens can complain to the eu ombudsman about issues concerning possible maladministration by the european institutions. it is on this basis that a group of european citizens have lodged a complaint concerning the process of enlargement and improvement of vienna airport in austria, claiming that an environmental impact assessment has not been carried out. in the absence of such an assessment, the commission agreed with the austrian authorities not to pursue its infringement procedure, provided that austria carried out an ex post eia which best simulated an ex ante environmental impact assessment (eia) and allowed the full environmental impact assessment of the projects. i am pleased to see that this report states that neither the european commission nor the austrian authorities have breached any european rules when carrying out the ex post impact assessment. this case, however, shows that clearer rules are needed in relation to infringement proceedings.
in writing. − vienna airport started a set of infrastructure improvements in 1999 without consulting the public, thus violating directive 85/337/ec which required an environmental impact assessment (eia). this special report by the epo follows a complaint lodged with the commission in 2006 in which the complainants complained about the lack of iac. the commission has carried out an infringement investigation. however, considering that the works were in the final stages, it decided to suspend the procedure provided that austria carried out an ex post met assessment. the citizens complained that the commission had not acted correctly and lodged a complaint with the epo. after examining the case, the epo considered that in the circumstances, the commission's decision to ask austria to carry out an ex post eia was in principle not only appropriate but also reasonable. however, the eip found some errors that should have been avoided. i therefore agree with the epp recommendations that the commission should address the shortcomings identified, in particular by ensuring access to an appeal procedure for complainants and by taking measures to avoid conflicts of interest in the application of directive 85/337/ec.
in writing. − the european ombudsman is responsible for receiving complaints concerning maladministration in the activities of eu institutions, bodies, offices or agencies. it also checks the application of the codes of good administrative behaviour and the charter of fundamental rights. this special report deals with the commission's handling of a complaint lodged in 2006 by 27 citizens' initiatives against what they considered to be the negative consequences of the expansion of vienna airport, in particular at the environmental level, as no environmental impact assessment (eia) had been carried out for the said project, in particular with regard to noise pollution. the ombudsman points out that this report corroborates and highlights that the solution found by the commission was not the most appropriate. the commission considers that the measure in question is imputable to the state and that it is imputable to the state. the opinion, like the report, raises some pertinent questions from the point of view of defending the interests of citizens who complain.
in writing. − the role of the european ombudsman is very important in dealing with complaints from union citizens concerning maladministration in the activities of the union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies. in this particular case, it is a complaint by austrian citizens against the way the commission handled the infringement procedure against austria, namely by failing to ensure either that the authority issuing permits for works without a mandatory impact assessment was not responsible for carrying out the ex post eia or that the complainant had access to a judicial remedy against that assessment. the european bodies are there to give answers to the citizens of the eu, and here is another good example of that. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution on the special report of the european ombudsman on the vienna airport case, which concludes that clearer procedures are needed for infringement proceedings, preferably through the adoption of a general regulation on administrative procedures for the eu administration, thus strengthening the position of the complainant. i think this is important, because such a regulation would be an appropriate means of clarifying the obligations of the authorities when communicating with complainants in an infringement procedure, or with bodies representing european citizens, such as the committee on petitions and the ombudsman, for example by introducing an obligation to respond as quickly as possible to the ombudsman's recommendations in order to avoid misinterpretations, such as those which have occurred in this case.
in writing. − the european ombudsman is responsible for receiving complaints from any citizen of the union concerning maladministration in the eu institutions or agencies. the environmental impact study of vienna airport carried out by the austrian authorities, as a result of an agreement with the commission, has two irregularities which the ombudsman considers to be serious, namely: conflict of interest on the part of the body responsible for the expansion of the airport being the same one responsible for the environmental impact study; and lack of access to the procedure for the review of the study by the public. in addition, after the first inquiry carried out by the ombudsman, he found that the commission had not implemented his recommendations. i therefore join the rapporteur in stressing the need to review the environmental impact assessment directive in order to avoid similar situations, especially those relating to the existence of conflicts of interest and the inability of the public concerned to access environmental impact assessments and their compliance with existing european legislation.
in writing. − the european ombudsman is responsible for receiving complaints concerning maladministration in the activities of eu institutions, bodies, offices or agencies. this special report deals with the commission's handling of a complaint lodged in 2006 by 27 citizens' initiatives against what they considered to be the negative consequences of the expansion of vienna airport, in particular at the environmental level, as no environmental impact assessment (eia) had been carried out for the project. the ombudsman considers that this report corroborates and highlights that the solution found by the commission was not the most appropriate. the commission considers that the measure in question is imputable to the state and that it is imputable to the state. we agree with the report's view.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that all sectors contribute to combating climate change, but that, as late as 1997, when the kyoto protocol was signed, there was no scientific capacity to measure and monitor greenhouse gas emissions from land use, soil changes and forest soils. today, with the development and scientific progress achieved, it is possible to measure and monitor emissions in this sector. in this sense, the adoption of these rules, which require monitoring by all member states of soil activities and emissions of greenhouse gases from soil, we can say that the european union's policy package as a world leader in environmental footprint is consolidating its position. if all other sectors have already been identified and measures taken to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, as far as soil is concerned, its change, use, use should not be put aside but considered equally as all other sectors of activity.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'accounting rules and action plans for greenhouse gas emissions and removals from land use and forestry activities' because it is necessary that the climate change dimension be included in all union policies and that all sectors contribute to the union's efforts to combat climate change. it is welcome that technical progress now allows us to include emissions accounting more systematically, but also the removal of emissions linked to land use, land reuse and forestry. agriculture and forestry have a huge potential to contribute to climate change mitigation and adaptation. portugal has been a pioneer in this area and it is important that the union continues to support projects that allow farmers to be compensated for the provision of the environmental carbon sequestration service, which will be counted towards the member states in the kyoto protocol. it seems important to me, however, to stress that emissions from natural disturbances are excluded in certain exceptional circumstances, in particular in the case of forest fires.
in writing. − accounting for land use, land use change and forestry (lulucf) is a key element of energy policy with the potential to, among other things, contribute to mitigation, adaptation, biodiversity conservation and the sustainable use of natural resources. lulucf accounting in the european union should be guided by objectives such as: ensuring policy coherence with existing and planned union legislation on future coordination and integration, including but not limited to the common agricultural policy (cap) and the renewable energy directive; and ensuring that accounting practices and methodologies are in line with the accepted principles of transparency, consistency, comparability, completeness and accuracy not only in member states but among them as members of the european union. i therefore agree with this proposal, which i consider to follow the european commission's proposal and even strengthen it in several respects.
in writing. − accounting for land use, land use change and forestry (lulucf) contributes to mitigation, adaptation, conservation of biodiversity and sustainable use of natural resources. member states (ms) should explore actions to reduce emissions and maintain or increase removals from the categories of activities covered in this report. these activities should, inter alia, identify trends and explore further integration into other european union (eu) policies. the commission should also provide guidance and technical assistance to member states and have the power to issue recommendations for further action. public participation and transparency, as required under eu law, should also be considered. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that the content of the lulucf action plans should be clarified to include recent trends, emission and removal forecasts and measures to integrate the lulucf sectors into other eu policies. in these matters, and in view of the durban convention, i consider it essential that there should be coherence between eu legislation and international regulations. the european union has a key leadership role to play in climate matters and, where harmonisation is preferable or required, it should seek understanding among its member states.
in writing. − this decision establishes accounting rules for anthropogenic greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions and removals resulting from land use, land use change and forestry (lulucf) activities. these rules are intended to be a first step towards the inclusion of these activities in the eu's commitment to reduce emissions as defined in the kyoto protocol and the united nations framework convention on climate change. it also establishes an obligation for member states to provide information on their lulucf actions to limit or reduce emissions and to maintain or increase removals of carbon dioxide, nitrous oxide and methane. member states shall prepare and maintain accounts accurately reflecting all emissions and removals resulting from activities carried out on their territory and falling under the categories of afforestation, reforestation, deforestation, forest management. despite our disagreement in principle on the eu's approach to climate change and in particular to emissions trading, we believe that what is at stake here is the collection and reporting of information useful in supporting public policy making.
in writing. − agriculture and forestry are a vital part of the response to the challenges of today and tomorrow due to their significant contribution to the bio-based economy. the european union should seek to find ways of reducing emissions whilst at the same time allowing highly productive land use to continue. the only way forward for european farmers, cooperatives and foresters is an approach based on the efficient use of natural resources, focussing on the future challenges of increasing demand for food and renewables. farming and forestry are the only economic sectors that naturally sequester carbon in soils and biomass during the production process. the european agricultural model and sustainable forest management take full advantage of the natural capacity for sequestration and storage. to exploit the full mitigation potential of both sectors, scientific knowledge and monitoring methods need to be improved in order to increase confidence in greenhouse gas emissions inventories linked to forestry and agricultural soils. both their accuracy and consistency need to be improved and it is important to examine mitigation options from a holistic point of view using an integrated approach.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider the regulation on a mechanism for monitoring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions (ghg) to be of vital importance, since all this monitoring and control will provide member states with more and better information, giving them tools to see if they are on track to meet the objectives set and allowing the creation of different and technically sound policies to combat climate change.
in writing. - land use accounting, land use change and forestry (lulucf) is a key element of energy policy. the commission proposal, as amended by the rapporteur, aims to include lulucf sectors in efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the eu and to ensure complementarity between union policies by establishing robust accounting rules for emissions and removals from lulucf activities. like the rapporteur, i agree with the european commission's position, as i believe that it is necessary to establish sound and comprehensive accounting rules for the lulucf sector and to enable future policy development with a view to the full inclusion of the lulucf sector in the union's commitments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. i believe that the existence of such a legal framework will contribute to the development of a more sustainable and efficient european energy and environmental policy, and in view of this i voted in favour of the report.
