in writing. - i approve this report, as it aims to improve the monitoring system for greenhouse gas emissions in order to meet the european union's international commitments and obligations and not to jeopardise future international climate change agreements, not to mention the fact that this is required by the requirements of the climate and energy package. i therefore support this report which supports the development of climate change adaptation and mitigation instruments at european union level. in my view, it is important to monitor the evolution of these commitments with transparent and comparable data on greenhouse gas emissions, to know whether the european union and its member states are on track to meet environmental objectives and to develop new and more robust policies against climate change.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the 'mechanism for monitoring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions and other relevant information on climate change' because, if the european union is to meet the greenhouse gas emission reduction targets it has set not only internally but also internationally, under the united nations framework convention on climate change and the kyoto protocol, reliable, accurate and comparable data are needed, which will enable us to assess the way forward and to develop and implement appropriate climate policies.
in writing. − in order to establish harmonised reporting requirements for greenhouse gas emissions monitoring and other information relevant to climate change policy, the power to adopt acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu should be delegated to the european commission. it is therefore of particular importance that the commission carry out appropriate consultations during its preparatory work, including at expert level. the commission, when preparing and drawing up delegated acts, should ensure a simultaneous, timely and appropriate transmission of relevant documents to the european parliament and to the council. the objectives of this regulation, namely the establishment of a mechanism for monitoring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions and for reporting other relevant information at national and union level in relation to climate change, cannot be sufficiently achieved by the member states. however, they can be better achieved at union level. i am glad that the ep has stuck to the text drawn up by the commission for this proposal.
in writing. − the regulation on a mechanism for monitoring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions (mmr) replaces the mechanism established under decision no 280/2004/ec. this mechanism for monitoring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions is essential for reliable and accurate greenhouse gas emissions data to be available in a timely manner. this data is crucial to whether the european union (eu) and its member states (ms) are on track to meet the objectives set and to create new and robust policies to address the challenge of climate change. the improvements set out in this report are intended to assist member states in implementing the climate and energy package; to improve the timeliness, transparency and comparability of data reported; to ensure compliance by the union and its member states with international monitoring and reporting obligations; and to facilitate the establishment of new community instruments to combat climate change.
in writing. − this regulation establishes a mechanism to ensure the timeliness, transparency, accuracy, consistency, comparability and completeness of the information reported by the eu and its member states to the secretariat of the united nations framework convention on climate change (unfccc), by providing for the reporting and verification of information on commitments under the unfccc and the kyoto protocol and decisions taken thereafter and progress made towards meeting those commitments. the mechanism provides for the monitoring of all anthropogenic emissions by sources and removals by sinks of all greenhouse gases (ghgs) not controlled by the montreal protocol on substances that deplete the ozone layer in the member states. also included are reports on carbon dioxide (co2) emissions from shipping, use of revenues generated from the auctioning of emission allowances, and other information. despite our disagreement in principle on the eu's approach to climate change and in particular to emissions trading, we believe that what is at stake here is the collection and reporting of information useful in supporting public policy making.
in writing. - i agree to improve the monitoring and reporting system to ensure compliance with the obligations and commitments undertaken by the union and the member states under current and future international agreements on climate change, reflecting the obligations arising from the united nations framework convention on climate change, the kyoto protocol and subsequent decisions adopted under these instruments with regard to greenhouse gas emissions and financial and technological support to developing countries.
in writing. − the timely provision of reliable and accurate greenhouse gas emissions data is essential to know whether the european union and the member states are delivering on the targets set and to create concrete and efficient policies to meet the challenge of climate change that is and will be occurring in europe. given the growing importance of addressing the challenge of climate change and taking into account the socioeconomic consequences that it entails for the eu, i support the european commission's proposal as it aims to: assist member states in implementing the climate and energy package; improve the compliance with deadlines, transparency and comparability of reported data; ensure compliance by the union and its member states with international obligations in the field of monitoring and reporting, in particular reporting on support to developing countries; and facilitate the creation of new community instruments to combat climate change. i believe that the proposals put forward will enable the eu to act as a single agile body in combating and implementing concrete measures with regard to climate change.

in writing. − this regulation aims to create a european online dispute resolution platform in the form of a website to act as a single entry point for consumers and traders seeking to resolve a dispute arising from an e-commerce transaction out of court. the platform will aggregate/index the alternative dispute resolution (adr) schemes of the member states that are in compliance with the adr directive. it will be available in all the official languages of the european union and will be free to use, acting as an intermediary between the consumer and the trader, thus facilitating their relationship with the most appropriate adr centre. the platform will thus facilitate dispute resolution by allowing adr entities to handle all procedures electronically and in accordance with a set of common procedural rules, which provide for the appointment of national contact points to act as 'advisers' in their respective member states. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules for the application of this regulation. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules and to monitor the implementation of the new rules.

in writing. − the creation of an area of free movement of persons and goods (schengen area) has led to a significant increase in crossborder mobility, which can be explained by several reasons: tourism (due to the increase in the average standard of living of european citizens and their longevity), professional, academic and cultural. on the move, all citizens make purchases which boost the development of international trade but which could be even greater if there were no consumer distrust of the guarantee of the products purchased. often, the cost of litigation far exceeds the value of the product purchased. the existence of a fast (90-day resolution), efficient and low-cost (with residual costs) system is an important milestone in encouraging cross-border business with clear advantages for both the consumer and the trader. i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on alternative dispute resolution for consumer disputes, amending regulation (ec) no 2006/2004 and directive 2009/22/ec (the adr directive) because i believe that the new regulation will contribute to economic growth and job creation in the european union, while strengthening and consolidating the single market.
in writing. the proposal for a directive on alternative dispute resolution (adr) for consumers is a reaction to the conclusion that the internal market is not functioning properly. the proposal lays down measures aimed at improving the functioning of the retail market, particularly with regard to improving the channels of redress for consumers. the proposal is closely linked to the online dispute resolution (odr) proposal. the report goes further than the commission proposal. while the commission proposal refers to the harmonisation of dispute procedures only in cross-border situations, the report includes national disputes. this directive will thus prevail over existing national legislation on this matter. the idea of a rapid procedure for the settlement of crossborder disputes between traders and consumers, which does not preclude the parties from having recourse to any other judicial remedy, is not at all negative (despite some of the concepts underlying it, notably the deepening of the single market). however, it is not acceptable to require national legislation to be governed by this directive when it already provides for such situations.

in writing. − a review of the current overseas association decision (oda) is planned for the period 2014-2020. the saa sets out the legal framework for promoting the social and economic development of the overseas countries and territories (octs - islands in the atlantic, antarctic, arctic, caribbean, indian and pacific oceans) and their economic relations with the eu. these islands are not sovereign states but depend on four eu member states: denmark, france, the netherlands and the united kingdom. the association of the octs with the union is the result of the constitutional links between those countries and territories and the four member states. in general, the octs enjoy a wide autonomy in economic, labour market, public health, internal affairs and customs matters. defence and foreign affairs remain, in general, the responsibility of the member states. the octs are not part of the customs territory of the union, being outside the internal market. therefore, union legislation does not apply to them. the association decision aims to strengthen cooperation with the octs, taking account of the economic and social problems they face. the rapporteur makes a number of proposals with which we generally agree. we voted in favour.

in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account the existence of potentially toxic elements resulting from radio-nuclear activities. i therefore support this proposal which aims to change the current legal basis of the tfeu in order to strengthen human protection by differentiating monitoring requirements for natural or man-made sources of radioactivity as well as for exposure of certain groups such as children and young people. this will bring european legislation into line with the current recommendations of the international commission on radiological protection.
in writing. − citizens' access to drinking water is a major concern of policies in the fields of human health and environmental protection. the commission proposal aims to incorporate the requirements for the control of radioactive substances into specific legislation under the euratom treaty in order to maintain the uniformity, consistency and completeness of radiation protection legislation at eu level. to protect public health in europe effectively and consistently, it is necessary to distinguish between what results from natural radioactivity and what results from the normal operation of nuclear installations (artificial and/or man-made radioactivity). it is recommended that the polluter pays principle be followed for the costs of sampling and monitoring in the event of artificial pollution. it is important that citizens are informed about the quality of water intended for human consumption. member states should therefore include in their triennial reports on the quality of water intended for human consumption and on nuclear safety information on radioactive substances present in this type of water. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − contamination of drinking water by radioactive substances can be caused by accidental release of radioactivity or improper disposal practices, and therefore it is essential that there is strict monitoring, particularly of water systems most vulnerable to this type of contamination, to ensure that water remains fit for human consumption. although council directive 98/83/ec of 3 november 1998 on the quality of water intended for human consumption lays down general rules and contains indicator parameters for radioactivity and tritium and corresponding control provisions, it is of concern that the requirements for the control of radioactive substances have not been applied to date. the aim of this proposal is to define harmonised requirements for the protection of the health of the general public with regard to radioactive substances such as radon and tritium in water intended for human consumption. in the event of non-compliance with this directive, it is also essential to provide for a whole range of measures to be taken immediately by the member states in order to restore water quality and reduce the potential danger to public health.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on radioactive substances in water intended for human consumption because i consider it essential to ensure that citizens are protected from the long-term effects of any radioactive substances in water. member states should ensure that consumers have access to transparent information on the potential risks of radioactive contamination of drinking water and share good practices to strengthen controls on these substances and on radioactive waste in general.
in writing. − this directive concerns water intended for human consumption. radionuclides in water intended for human consumption are currently treated under directive 98/83/ec (drinking water directive), which sets parametric values for tritium and total indicative dose. the commission should have adopted measures on the frequency and methods of controls in accordance with the regulatory procedure with scrutiny (planned for 2000). if radionuclides were treated under the euratom treaty, while all other carcinogenic contaminants, such as chemicals, were treated under the treaty, the cumulative consequences of side effects would not be taken into account. i therefore believe that the provisions on radiation protection should be dealt with in the light of the treaty.
in writing. − the quality of water intended for human consumption is currently governed by council directive 98/83/ec, including the regulation on pollutants such as toxic chemicals and radionuclides. access to drinking water is a major concern in the fields of human health and environmental protection. this proposal aims to incorporate the respective requirements not in the said directive but in specific legislation based on the euratom treaty. we must treat radionuclides in the same way as we treat all other carcinogenic pollutants, so that the cumulative consequences of the adverse effects of the different pollutants can be taken into account. having regard to the belet report (p7_ta(2011) 0055 of 15 february 2011, the provisions on radiation protection should be addressed in accordance with the treaty. i therefore agree with the amendment of the legal basis for the relevant provisions relating to environmental protection, namely article 192 (1) of the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. − water for human consumption requires the observance of stringent criteria that ensure a high level of protection of public health, for which it is essential to maintain public water services and to consider water as a public good. the report addresses two main issues: the legal consistency of the legislation on drinking water, which implies treating radionuclides in the same way as other carcinogenic pollutants, taking into account the cumulative consequences and adverse effects of the different pollutants; the inclusion in the proposal of important distinctions established by the international commission on radiological protection for natural and man-made sources of radioactivity, as well as for the different effects of exposure, in particular by age. the legal basis for the article on the environment and public health in the tfeu is to be amended on the basis of the precautionary principle and preventive action, which seems to us to be correct. the natural impact and human activities are further distinguished according to the recommendations, further changing values that take into account more exposed groups or critical ages of exposure such as infants and pregnant and breastfeeding women, this update representing a reduction in the values existing until then and therefore a higher level of protection of public health.
in writing. − water intake is one of the ways in which harmful substances are incorporated into the human body. the ingestion of radioactive isotopes or radionuclides can cause a number of health problems. in accordance with council directive 96/29/euratom of 13 may 1996 laying down basic safety standards for the protection of the health of workers and the general public against the dangers arising from ionising radiation, the contribution of practices involving a risk from ionising radiation to the exposure of the general public, taking into account cumulative long-term exposure, should be kept as low as possible. in order to ensure a high level of protection of public health, it is necessary to establish common standards of quality for water intended for human consumption which have an indicative function and to provide for monitoring of compliance with those standards.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, considering it to be a matter of paramount importance for human health from the point of view of the regulation of water intended for human consumption. the setting of parametric values, frequencies and methods for the control of radioactive substances (radon, tritium and other radioactive substances) in water intended for human consumption is undoubtedly a step forward in the protection of the health of the general public, which has not been applied so far and could lead to situations of concern from the point of view of human health. implementation of this directive is therefore equally urgent.
in writing. − water systems are extremely vulnerable to radioactive contamination, and it is therefore of vital importance that water intended for human consumption is completely safe from any potential or actual risk of contamination. the commission has therefore put forward a legislative proposal to monitor the levels of radioactivity in water intended for human consumption. i support the rapporteur in her view that the commission proposal, instead of being adopted by a non-legislative procedure, should be adopted by the ordinary legislative procedure, by changing the legal basis underlying it. moreover, the council cannot accept only the metric values of certain metals and extend them to other radioactive substances. in the light of the foregoing, i have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − water for human consumption requires the observance of stringent criteria that ensure a high level of protection of public health, for which it is essential to maintain public water services and to consider water as a public good. the report addresses the issue of legal consistency of legislation on drinking water (advocating that radionuclides should be treated in the same way as other carcinogenic pollutants) and the inclusion of important distinctions established by the international commission on radiological protection for natural and man-made sources of radioactivity, as well as for the different effects of exposure, in particular by age. the legal basis for the article on the environment and public health in the tfeu is to be amended on the basis of the precautionary principle and preventive action, which seems to us to be correct.

in writing. − on 20 february 2013, the agreement between the council and the european parliament on the 'two pack' was finalised, following a period of negotiations which began in july 2012. the report sets out measures to strengthen the supervision of euro area countries supported by financial assistance and/or threatened by difficulties or instability, ensuring their legal protection and restoring budgetary normality, avoiding contagion between countries. the level of supervision will depend on the severity of the financial difficulties and the assistance provided to the countries. it is set against the backdrop of the financial and sovereign debt crisis facing the european union today, drawing lessons from it and proposing solutions. it is assumed that preventive action at an early stage is preferable to corrective measures which intervene later in the process and may no longer avoid disastrous effects. i support measures such as the speedier adoption of commission decisions vis-à-vis member states under the enhanced surveillance procedure, the inclusion of the measures of the budgetary treaty in secondary legislation, among others, and i am therefore voting in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'economic and budgetary surveillance of member states experiencing serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability in the euro area', as i considered it necessary to reconcile greater budgetary control with greater solidarity in europe. i welcome the european commission's commitment to study the feasibility of issuing common debt bonds of the euro area countries.
in writing. - the second economic governance package was approved today by a large majority in the european parliament, which i am very pleased to see. the package includes two regulations aimed at further strengthening the economic and budgetary monitoring of the euro area. i would stress that this new regulation allows the european commission to carry out a more intensive monitoring of a member state which is facing serious financial and budgetary difficulties and is intended to enable the council to decide whether a member state should request financial assistance. the conditions are thus created to prevent the governments of the member states from indefinitely protecting a request for financial aid, as happened with the socialist government of josé sócrates, which subsequently made the conditions attached to an agreement significantly more burdensome and onerous for that state. another important innovation is that financial aid programmes are now part of european legislation, allowing the process to become more democratic and more respectful of the rule of law in which we live. finally, i would like to congratulate my colleague, mr jean-paul gauzès, on the excellent work he has done.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis has forced the european union (eu) and its member states (ms) to redouble their efforts to control their deficits and to combat tax fraud and evasion in order to avoid any damage to the financial stability of the euro area. in 2010, the commission, aware of the serious consequences of the instability of the euro, put forward a proposal for the creation of an economic and budgetary surveillance mechanism for member states experiencing serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability. however, the council considered that its implementation was not timely and delayed its approval, which had dire consequences for the european economy. we all know that the consequences of over-indebtedness in one member state can have repercussions in other member states and even worldwide. as the financial situation of several member states worsened, prompting them to ask for help, it became inevitable to adopt a regulation which, by defining clear procedures, would guarantee the financial stability of the euro area and protect member states. i voted in favour of mr jean-paul gauzès' report because it is urgent to implement a financial stability mechanism which, in line with the community method, will enable the member states to absorb asymmetric shocks and to emerge from the crisis in which they find themselves.

in writing. − on 20 february 2013, the agreement between the council and the european parliament on the 'two pack' was finalised, following a period of negotiations which began in july 2012. this report aims to ensure that member states have sound public finances and that their economic policies do not adversely affect other member states and the smooth functioning of economic and monetary union. to this end, the commission will monitor national budgets more closely. it will draw up guidelines for a harmonised structure of the member states' budget plans and may intervene if they deviate from the sgp. the draft budgets will be submitted to the commission at the same time, in line with the development of the european semester process. the need for sound public finances is emphasised as a means of strengthening the conditions for price stability and strong sustainable growth supported by financial stability in order to achieve the union's objectives of sustainable growth and employment. i support this report because it contributes to clearer and more transparent budgetary monitoring and to increased confidence in the european economy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the monitoring and evaluation of draft budgetary plans and the correction of the excessive deficit of the euro area member states, as it introduces greater control and transparency in the european commission's powers of intervention over national budgetary processes, ensuring full respect for national practices of social concertation and wage negotiation. it is essential, however, to reconcile public investment, which supports growth and employment, with the objectives of budgetary discipline.
in writing. - the second economic governance package was approved today by a large majority in the european parliament, which i am very pleased to see. the package includes two regulations aimed at further strengthening the economic and budgetary monitoring of the euro area. the purpose of this regulation is to ensure that the european institutions monitor more closely the drawing up of draft national budgets and the definition of the medium- and long-term objectives they set. in particular, if it is felt that the measures to achieve a particular objective may not be the most appropriate, or even the most burdensome, then the european institutions will have the opportunity to invite the member state to review them. another new feature of this regulation is the reinforced monitoring of a member state in an excessive deficit procedure. in this case, the member state will incur additional obligations, including the obligation to submit an intensive assessment of budgetary implementation for that year, both at the level of the general and local budgets, including all measures that may pose financial risks to that state and contribute to the existence of an excessive deficit. finally, i would like to congratulate my colleague, elisa ferreira, on her work.

in writing. - a social investment market has emerged in the european union, predominantly consisting of investment funds geared towards social enterprises where investment is still in its infancy. this regulation is part of the social entrepreneurship initiative presented by the commission in october 2011. the social entrepreneurship funds provide funding to social enterprises that act as drivers of social change and economic growth as they operate, thereby contributing to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. this legislation takes into account the special characteristics of social enterprises whose main objective is to achieve a positive social impact. this regulation lays down uniform requirements for managers of collective investment undertakings wishing to use the designation 'european social entrepreneurship fund' (esif) and the conditions for marketing collective investment undertakings under that designation, thereby contributing to the proper functioning of the internal market. it also lays down the rules for cooperation in the supervision of these funds in order to ensure that they operate in a transparent and effective manner. the european parliament considers it essential that the investments of these funds be made clearer and more transparent and that it be easier to invest in social entrepreneurship. i voted in favour of this report.

the rapporteur. - madam president, today will be the end of a long and arduous process involving many farmers, environmentalists, citizens in general, technicians, politicians and members of the media. as rapporteur for direct payments and rural development, i should like to thank everyone for the contributions they have made to make it possible, over the course of almost two years of work, to present a proposal which is a good starting point for the european parliament's negotiating mandate. i cannot fail to mention president paolo de castro, our fellow shadow rapporteurs, the rapporteurs for opinions of other committees, commissioners cioloş and potočnik and the various presidencies - the polish, the danish, the cypriot and the irish - with whom we have worked. i should also like to thank and commend the secretariat of the committee on agriculture, the secretariats of the political groups and the members of my own staff for their professionalism. it was very demanding and very complex work. in the case of my reports, it was a matter of negotiating some 4 500 amendments and including some 3 000 of them in 75 commitments, all of which were approved in the committee on agriculture. i therefore call for these commitments to be ratified and i highlight certain aspects which i consider to be fundamental and unavoidable for a greener, fairer cap and therefore closer to farmers and european citizens. we must support measures which unambiguously guarantee a greener cap, and i am referring in particular to maintaining greening in the first pillar, and to this end the reservation of a mandatory allocation of 30% of direct payments. for this greening we have confirmed the common measures: the diversification of crops, the maintenance of permanent meadows, the creation of ecological interest areas. we have introduced aspects of the european framework which make it possible to reduce the bureaucracy involved in implementing these measures, without prejudice to environmental objectives and to the benefit of farmers and national administrations in terms of reducing costs. i would also stress the obligation to set aside 25% of each member state's rural development budget for organic farming and agri-environmental measures. i welcome the consensus reached on the definition of an active farmer and the exclusion from receiving aid of areas not used for agriculture, such as golf courses and airports, which will no longer benefit from agricultural support. we have also introduced greater harmonisation in the rate of convergence of support between member states and between farmers. the commission has also proposed that the maximum amount of aid should be increased to eur 300 000 for the first 50 hectares. these two measures discriminate positively in employment. the dynamism of rural areas must be promoted and the rejuvenation of generations must be promoted urgently. so we have introduced new incentives for young people and new farmers, for local supply chains and for diversification of activity in rural areas. i therefore call for a vote on all these proposals. let me also use this last minute to speak as coordinator of the s&d group. i should like to say that my group will vote in favour of all the commitments it has made in all the reports under discussion here: direct payments, the single cap, rural development and horizontal regulation. however, we have tabled amendments on four fundamental issues, on which, unfortunately, it was not possible to reach a compromise and which were approved by comagri without the support of my group. these are, first of all, the rules on the transparency of aid recipients. my group considers it unacceptable that the european citizens cannot be given information on the use of public money. we therefore propose that the beneficiaries of the cap be made public annually. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. in other words, it is only acceptable - i will finish right away, madam president - that a farmer receives less than the hectares he has under certain agricultural practices. finally, we cannot accept that the cap regresses by a decade in environmental practices by virtually eliminating cross-compliance. it is therefore necessary to correct these negative aspects if we are to have a fairer, greener and more equitable cap in the future.
mr president, the proposals for reform of the cap which we have discussed here insist on a market-oriented and competitive model which devalues and compromises food sovereignty and food security and the sustainability of agricultural production, and will not solve problems but create others. i would therefore like to draw your attention to some of the alternative proposals we have put forward: the introduction of quota schemes tailored to the needs of each country and its relative level of production capacity, allowing differentiated development of the countries with the highest deficits; convergence of direct payments between member states by 2020 at the latest; modulation and capping of direct aid, limiting aid to the largest beneficiaries and redistributing it, benefiting in relative terms small and medium-sized producers and sustainable production; the establishment of a national preference scheme; the introduction of a maximum intermediation margins scheme, in order to promote a fair and adequate distribution of added value along the food supply chain; the creation of a public agricultural insurance funded by the european union budget.
mr president, commissioner, there is one aspect which is raising serious concerns in the european camp. there is a deep sense that we are making a serious mistake by not opposing what is now obvious - the decision to end the milk quota system as early as march 2015. the commission's studies, which are now under way, will be presented in may and we are convinced that they will prove that, ladies and gentlemen, if we do nothing now, we will have missed the opportunity to take part in correcting this error by then. that is why it is time to bring this crucial issue to the table for the whole of the negotiating team, so that we can have a say in the outcome that may condemn many of our countries and regions. that is why we must vote tomorrow in favour of the proposals which keep open the continuation of the milk quota system. if we do not vote now, then, ladies and gentlemen, we shall be unable to do anything.
answer according to the "blue card" procedure. the milk quota system allows for something that is essential in the market for perishable goods, which is the balance between supply and demand. any surplus situation on the perishables market does not create efficiency in the market, but on the contrary, it creates very serious problems for the countries suffering from these surpluses and for the neighbouring countries suffering from the spillover of these surpluses onto their markets. and this is not market efficiency, this is more problems for farmers, more european subsidies and more problems for the milk queue.
mr president, mr commissioner, a lot of time has been spent and a lot of work has been done, particularly by the rapporteurs and the shadow rapporteurs, whose commitment and dedication to this reform has been remarkable. everyone got something for their member states and no one got everything. the important thing is that the common agricultural policy remains true to its raison d'être: to ensure food in quantity, quality and diversity, guaranteeing food security for all europeans; to learn from past mistakes, becoming environmentally sustainable, adapting production to markets, guaranteeing a fair income to the producer and boosting all rural life; and to prepare for the challenges of the future by becoming more equitable, simple, transparent and competitive. finally, a word on milk quotas. we'll extend the sugar quotas and the vineyard plantation rights. we have information from a study which points to the sustainability of the milk sector in only two member states after the end of quotas. i ask everyone: let us not give up quotas until we have an effective and efficient alternative for the dairy sector in europe.
the rapporteur. - this debate confirmed what was a long negotiation we had been holding for many months. some of our differences have been exposed here, but in particular the enormous convergence we have on the need for a strong cap in the future, which reconciles competitiveness with sustainability, which contributes to solving the problems of our time, and of course climate change, and which ensures the economic and social vitality of rural areas. i am very pleased to note what the commissioner has just said and his continuing commitment to continue a fruitful dialogue, as has been the case so far. and i was also very pleased to note the speeches of some members who responded positively to those which are the main concerns of the socialist group, namely that we must come out of this parliament with a very strong mandate to strengthen our negotiating position. and this implies not only that we confirm all the commitments that have been made but also how we can go a little further on the more controversial issues which are the question of double funding, which parliament cannot accept, the question of transparency on which we have to be very firm and uncompromising and the question of the reintroduction of cross-compliance to further strengthen the environmental component of this reform. i therefore expect a very meaningful vote tomorrow in this plenary and i am sure that the european parliament will be up to the new challenges, the new responsibilities that have been conferred on it by the treaty of lisbon and that we will make history with this reform in europe.
we are being asked to discuss the 2014 budget today, which is almost the same as decorating the entrance hall of a house that has not yet been licensed because no one has yet agreed on the project, which is, of course, the multiannual financial framework. still, you can predict some things because the recipe is the same. the budget that is predicted for 2014 will not only rest on the same outdated structure of headings but, above all, will be the child of a multiannual framework whose political priorities are eternal austerity. by cutting cohesion policies, support for the most deprived, social support, the globalisation adjustment fund and so on, we are increasing divergence within europe and responding to austerity with more austerity. this parliament approved the so-called two-pack this morning. it's not packages like these we need. instead of the pre-approval of national budgets and monitoring of deficit control processes, we need solidarity measures and a budget that will generate investment and employment and reduce the obscene poverty that this european construction has created.
the deception of those who said that support for perpetual austerity, institutionalized in the budgetary treaty, would be exchanged for a strengthening of the european union budget, is now clear. the enormous achievement of those who said that the intolerable attack on democracy and the sovereignty of the peoples which is this treaty, which is economic governance and the european semester, would be counterbalanced by a budgetary increase for the sake of growth and employment. the budget which has never guaranteed economic and social cohesion, which has never ensured the redistributive function which was required in the face of capitalist integration of an asymmetrical nature, generating inequalities and imbalances, this budget, which was already a needy budget, will now be reduced. the consequences: see the case of portugal. in the next seven years, the eu's transfers will be less than what the country will pay in interest and commission alone under the so-called memorandum of understanding with the troika, but in the last five years, the balance of eu transfers to the country has already been exceeded by capital outflows in the form of interest, profits and dividends. this is the result: a country that becomes poorer as integration deepens.
blue-card question. – ms guillaume, i have to ask you, do you think that you can change the whole distribution of seats in the european parliament without changing the council? there is a balance between institutions, and what you want is really to unbalance this proportionate relationship between the council and parliament. if you accept in the council the federal rule – one vote, one state – we will accept here the rule of strict proportionality, and then you will have demography here. but you cannot have demography in the council and demography in parliament. if you have states in the council, you also have to have states in parliament.
the committee on constitutional affairs has wisely decided to limit itself to proposing a reasonable solution to find the necessary seats for croatia in the next european elections, minimising the impact on the current territorial representation of the parliament. i would obviously prefer that my country did not lose a member, but i recognise that this is a balanced solution based on an objective criterion. in the next accessions of other countries, other member states will provide the necessary vacancies. the committee on constitutional affairs also firmly rejected the opportunist attempt to use the occasion to reformulate the overall territorial distribution of members of the european parliament in favour of the large countries, against the spirit of degressive proportionality which, contrary to what some say, is not the same as strict proportionality. and the committee on constitutional affairs went further: the commission has made it clear that any future revision of the composition of parliament will also have to involve the voting system in the council. the representation of citizens in parliament cannot be separated from the representation of the member states in the council. those who want to revolutionize the composition of parliament should bear this message in mind.

mr president, the social economy is based on the use of economic principles as a means of achieving the objectives of economic and social cohesion. in this sector, the production of goods and services is aimed at economic development and the promotion of social welfare, not profit-making. the sector therefore has a key role to play in society and should be duly recognised, encouraged and supported. i am very pleased to see that the commission has taken this step. on the contrary, the so-called austerity policies have a profoundly negative impact on the activities of many institutions, aggravating an already critical situation and calling into question important projects - some of which are under way and others which, unfortunately, have not yet been born. this initiative goes far beyond this, and therefore calls for a characterization of the sector at the level of the different member states, a more effective framework and monitoring, and the development of specific lines of financing and support, either at the level of the community budget or, for example, by the european investment bank. this is in addition, of course, to the need to change the policies which are currently stifling the social economy.
in writing. the strength and importance of mutuality derives from its strong local roots, from the level of proximity responses it achieves, adapted to the environment in which it is embedded, and which are its true raison d'être and the main reason for its success. moreover, this form of social economy, with its intrinsic territorial basis, does not move in search of better profitability, because its aim is precisely to find answers to specific local needs and not to seek better business. this is their strength, which increases the resilience of the territories they enter and should therefore never be compromised. beware of the idea of multinational mutual societies: the principle of 'one man, one vote' is one of the main reasons for the success of this form of social economy and is an essential tool to ward off the temptation to focus mutual societies on profit. the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the situation of mutual societies. if we do, we will be weakening rather than strengthening the role of mutual societies with the populations they serve.

in writing. − i welcome this report, which aims primarily to highlight women's rights, but also to point out the continuing difficulties and threats they face in their quest for equality and, finally, how european union instruments can be used to support women's rights. in many countries, the design of gender-friendly constitutions is at the heart of political debate. the biggest challenges for women in egypt, libya and tunisia is to ensure women's participation in the bodies responsible for drafting the constitutions and the status of women in society which is now being discussed between modernists and reactionaries. the impact of the arab spring in morocco was different in many countries, because as we saw, many islamic parties won the general elections in 2011. the role of political islam is critical and its moulds crucial.
in writing. − the countries of north africa are in a process of political and democratic transition which began in 2010 with the so-called arab spring and in which women have played an active role. in this period of profound change, the issue of women's rights is at the heart of political debate and there is a high risk that we will see a worsening of their situation. the european union also has a role to play in promoting equality between men and women in these countries. through the new european neighbourhood policy, the european union can contribute to the building of democratic regimes and the economic and social development of its southern neighbours. i supported this report which advocates the need for these countries to incorporate the principle of equality between men and women into their constitutions and thus prohibit all discrimination and violence against women.
in writing. − the countries of north africa have been undergoing major changes, notably in terms of political and democratic transition and state reconstruction the so-called arab spring , and the outcome of this process should shape the democratic functioning of these countries and the level of respect for fundamental rights and freedoms. the dictatorial regimes in these countries have always limited the active participation of women and the effective recognition of their dignity, rights and access to justice. women's rights are one of the most debated issues in the current political process. the transitions under way can only lead to democratic societies and political systems if their constitution enshrines the principle of equality between men and women, prohibiting all forms of discrimination and violence and consolidating women's political, economic and social rights (in matters of marriage, divorce, child custody, inheritance, legal capacity, etc.). i also hope that these countries will begin to develop a strategy for the victims, particularly those who have been the victims of sexual violence in these troubled times, by providing them with the necessary economic, social and psychological support. it is up to the eu, through its new enp, to support the building of these democratic regimes as well as economic and social development.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it highlights the persistent difficulties and potential problems that women continue to face in the struggle for equality in north african countries, despite their involvement in demonstrations being key to the success of liberation movements. the eu can play an important role in this area. these issues can and should be among the eu's priorities when defining programmes and support under the european neighbourhood and partnership instrument.
in writing. - tunisia, egypt, libya and morocco are still going through a crucial moment in their history, but it has already given rise to a change of regime, leaving behind years of more or less liberal autocracy depending on the country in question. the countries concerned, targeted by the so-called arab spring, during the process of regime change and drafting of a new constitution, witnessed the emergence and relevance of women both as representatives and protesters in the demand for their rights, but also in the leadership of civil movements and the organization of non-governmental structures. such a change is therefore to be commended and encouraged. however, and because of the cultural tradition of these countries with regard to the role of women in society, more needs to be done in promoting them. i therefore agree with the rapporteur, silvia costa, that some eu instruments should be used to support women's rights and gender equality in the democratic process in these countries.
in writing. − although much remains to be done, the emancipation of women has made a significant contribution to gender equality at the level of the european union (eu). however, if the situation of women is at all acceptable at european level, the truth is that there are countries where women's rights are not respected. we all know about practices that undermine women's freedom and dignity, such as forced marriage, female genital mutilation, sexual violence and prostitution. even in countries where women have played a decisive role in the struggle for freedom and self-determination, such as those swept away by the so-called 'arab spring', their rights are being undermined, with some claiming that even the gains made under dictatorial regimes are now being called into question. i voted in favour of the report by mrs silvia costa on the situation of women in north africa because the eu must put the promotion of gender equality at the heart of its strategy to support the development of these countries - even if a change in mindset is needed - so that rural and urban communities can support the integration of women in the various sectors of civil society: services, enterprises, universities, etc.
in writing. the report expresses deep concern about the situation of women in north africa (tunisia, libya and egypt). the situation is still very unstable and disturbing. women have to face a daily battle not to win new rights, but simply to preserve the gains of the past. the report stresses that inequalities and the lack of participation of women in democratic life in these countries will prevent a genuine democratic process. the report urges the authorities of the countries concerned to enshrine irreversibly in their constitutions the recognition of women's political, economic and social rights, the prohibition of all forms of discrimination and the guarantee of gender equality in the penal codes and social security systems. it called on the commission to strengthen the integration of gender issues in the various eu interventions and to increase the financial envelope for support for women in the region. it refers to the need to facilitate access to social protection, health services, especially in relation to maternal health, sexual and reproductive rights. many of the amendments tabled by our group were adopted, which has improved the report. we appreciate all the positive points in the report, even if we do not follow an interventionist approach which goes through other points.
in writing. - this report focuses on four north african countries: egypt, libya, morocco and tunisia. despite their differences, they were all faced with regime change, elections and the reworking of their constitution. in the decades before the uprisings, women in tunisia and to some extent in egypt, morocco and libya had succeeded in getting relatively advanced legislation in place to protect their rights. yet in reality, the repressive nature of regimes, the lack of effective law enforcement and traditional perceptions of women's role have limited the achievement of true gender equality. despite progress, there is still a long way to go in terms of women's rights in these north african countries.

in writing. the report expresses deep concern about the situation of women in north africa, particularly after the arab spring (tunisia, libya and egypt). the situation is today very unstable and dramatic, since women have to face a daily battle, not to win new rights, but simply to preserve the gains of the past. the report clearly emphasizes that inequalities will impede a genuine democratic process. we agree that there must be legislation to prevent violence against women and that everyone should be guaranteed access to public health systems, that they should be protected in maternal health and that sexual and reproductive rights should be guaranteed. however, we cannot agree that the ep should decide to intervene in aspects of the political systems of these countries - such as when it advocates the introduction of quotas - which are for them alone to decide. finally, we are certain that only when these countries are free from foreign interference and are sovereign in their own resources and future will they be able to achieve levels of development which will have a positive impact on the women of these countries.

in writing. − european development policy aims at eradicating poverty in the countries with which it cooperates, including the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries. so, as this parliament votes today on the distribution of funds from the 11th european development fund, particularly as regards the financing of eu cooperation with the acp states, i am pleased to see that a large part of this budget is allocated to concrete actions to improve the welfare of the citizens of the countries concerned.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis is forcing the european union (eu) to rethink its strategy for supporting developing countries. the current budget cuts and the lack of new revenue are hampering community investment. now the watchword is financial efficiency: doing more with the same resources. the multiannual financial framework (mff) for the period 2007 to 2013, through the european development fund (edf), has made it possible to implement certain development programmes in third countries which, given the expectations created, should be maintained, since the support for the inhabitants of the poorest and most socially vulnerable regions is at stake. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report on the preparation of the new mff as regards the financing of eu cooperation with african, caribbean and pacific states and with overseas countries and territories for the period 2014-2020 (11th european development fund). despite the cuts, the eu must continue its work, not by betraying expectations or calling into question current programmes, but by directing resources where they are most effective in eradicating poverty as enshrined in the cotonou agreement.

in writing. − the mff 2014-2020 should ensure the successful implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and provide the eu with the means to recover from the crisis and emerge stronger. i therefore stress the importance of substantially increasing their investment in innovation, research and development, infrastructure and youth support, while also meeting the eu's climate change and energy objectives, improving education levels and promoting social inclusion. on the other hand, i am concerned about the lack of transparency in the way in which a political agreement was reached in the european council, both as regards expenditure and the 'revenue' part of the mff, because we must have all the relevant information available to the commission on the level of national amounts agreed, particularly in the area of cohesion and agricultural policies, including the derogations and specific allocations to each member state. finally, i express my firm opposition to a financial framework which could lead to a structural deficit in the eu budget, contrary to the treaty (articles 310 and 323 tfeu).

in writing. - according to the lisbon treaty, the council adopts the mff unanimously after obtaining the ep's favourable opinion. the ep has not yet given its opinion on the council's unanimous agreement. the ep wants flexibility, a revision that can increase the appropriations for the headings midway through the process and the existence of genuine own resources. flexibility is essential as it allows the implementation of the mff to be optimized. it is enough that the funds allocated annually to payments which are not annually implemented can be carried over and added to the budget of the following year to have a budget larger than that which was implemented in the 2007/2013 period. i am aware of the economic difficulties underlying the adoption of the proposal for a regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework (mff) for the period 2014 to 2020. however, the eu needs a flexible and modern budget that not only helps member states to solve their financial problems but also promotes growth and job creation. for these reasons i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the conclusions of the european council of 7 and 8 february.
in writing. - the agreement reached in the european council and this resolution of the european parliament, as the development of this process will make even clearer, are two versions of the same policy. the rejection of the agreement in its current form does not represent any substantive divergence as regards the amounts and priorities of the eu budget. this is also made clear by parliament's resolution of october 2012 on the mff 2014-2020, which is now taken as the guiding principle of the mandate for the negotiations that follow. we were against that resolution. so we could not support a mandate based on it. this is a further attempt by parliament to defend its own power to decide on the budget. and in that sense, it is an affirmation of a federalist vision, which does not call into question the eu's current policies, but rather confirms them. the resolution opposes the current system based mainly on contributions to the budget by each member state according to its relative level of wealth to a system based mainly on own resources, which would be based mainly on taxation. it is an option which, as we have said, further calls into question the redistributive function which the budget should have, thus maintaining and deepening existing inequalities, injustices and problems.
in writing. − the negotiations on the mff for 2014-2020 are taking place in a very adverse social, economic and financial context, in which member states are making considerable efforts to adjust their national budgets with a view to the sustainability of public finances and the stability of the banking sector and the single currency. the eu budget is part of the solution that will enable europe to overcome the current crisis by promoting investment in growth and jobs, and by helping member states to tackle, collectively and in concert, the current structural challenges, including the loss of competitiveness and the increase in unemployment and poverty. the european council conclusions on the mff represent a political agreement between heads of state or government. however, this agreement in its current form does not reflect the priorities and concerns expressed by the european parliament, and does not take into account its role and competences as defined in the lisbon treaty. parliament is, however, prepared to enter into in-depth negotiations with the council on all the provisions of the mff regulation and the interinstitutional agreement in order to ensure that the union has a modern, future-oriented, flexible and transparent eu budget that can deliver growth and jobs.
in writing. - i support this resolution which represents a firm, coherent and realistic position of parliament to start negotiations with the council on the next multiannual financial framework. the council's proposal reveals a dramatic paradox: we know that the european union is facing a crisis unprecedented in its history, a financial, economic and social crisis, and that it needs extraordinary instruments to get its economy going. at the same time, for the first time in the history of the european union, a budget is being negotiated on a downward basis. that is to say, the moment when europe most needs the means to stimulate its economy is also the moment when the council chooses to cut those means. the council then says that in the present crisis the average citizen would not understand an increase in the european budget. this is a false and demagogic argument, since 94% of the budget is invested in the member states and their economic and social development, for the creation of jobs and wealth. finally, i would like to stress the possibility that the next european parliament may be able to reopen this dossier.
in writing. − it is essential to achieve a mff that provides a stable budgetary and legal framework for the implementation of major programmes. however, the urgency of this framework cannot compromise the guarantee of essential conditions, in particular the financial means necessary to recover from the economic and financial crisis. only a forward-looking, flexible and transparent budget, with substantially increased investment in innovation, research and development, infrastructure and youth, can close the gap between the eu's political commitments and budgetary means. union expenditure should be mobilised to support sustainable growth, employment and competitiveness in line with the europe 2020 strategy. only a sound cohesion policy can therefore offer the opportunity to overcome the crisis as a key tool for catalysing growth and employment at european level as well as structural reforms at national level. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, which rejects the european council's agreement on the mff, as it does not reflect the priorities and concerns expressed by the european parliament.

in writing. − this regulation lays down the rules for the compilation and publication of key macroeconomic data in the eu. the commission proposal represents a broad and in-depth review of the european system of national and regional accounts, building on the last revision of the united nations system of national accounts in 2008. statistics are extremely important data for policy-makers, economic operators and citizens to analyse and monitor economic reality. in this sense, these data should be independent, reliable and comparable. they should be published in accordance with a precise timetable and in the highest possible quality. the commission proposal is intended to be strengthened by suggesting the publication of complete data, with a full picture of reality, as even countries with a small weight in the total gdp of the eu can have systemic effects. the published data shall have the user in mind by making the data transmission schedule clearer. the commission should also draw up a report on the quality of national accounts to be submitted to the european parliament every two years and the european parliament should have more time to examine delegated acts. i therefore support this report because i consider the above proposals to be appropriate.
in writing. − the aim of this regulation is to harmonise the rules on the compilation and publication of macroeconomic data in the european union. it is recalled that this regulation was already in force in european legislation, and what was now intended was to revise it in order to increase the level of demand for it. i think this is another important step in the desire to increase the levels of transparency and rigor in the statistical publications of the union, as well as a way of safeguarding future omissions or misinterpretations in relation to such publications.
in writing. - national and regional accounts are a way of assessing the state of our economy. it is therefore essential to have reliable data to enable us to set new targets and correct any deviations. the statistical office of the european union (eurostat) has a key role to play here, provided that the member states (ms) provide it with the requested data in a timely manner. if we take into account that one third of community aid is granted without information on the use of public money and that for years there has been no development in the collection and sharing of statistical information, we can imagine the importance of this regulation. we are often surprised, especially in countries undergoing financial assistance, by serious flaws in macroeconomic forecasts, many of them due to deficiencies in data collection and processing or the omission of relevant data, as is the case with expenditure that aggravates deficits. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague sharon bowles on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european system of national and regional accounts and i call on the member states not to be afraid to increase the transparency of the statistics they have produced in their countries and to provide the data to eurostat.
in writing. − we consider it very useful that there is statistical information at european level which allows for the comparability of economic, social and other indicators, in time and space, between and within member states, which implies the adoption of a set of common definitions and nomenclatures. we are also in favour of the use of new, automatic methods which will enable us to have access to the data collection in real time, and to make the data available to all and to make them understandable. we strongly disagree that the amendments being proposed to the provision of data on national and regional accounts are closely linked to the implementation of the european semester policies and economic governance, to the obsession with tackling the deficit in the context of a deep economic and social crisis. the adaptation proposed in this regulation is not about providing data to enable political decisions to be taken in favour of workers and the people, but rather about continuing and deepening the policies which, in countries like portugal, are causing economic and social disaster. it is information and statistics in the service of a policy that urgently needs to be defeated...

in writing. - i approve this report, on the understanding that the aspects of the 2006 maritime labour convention relating to flag state control should be enshrined in community law in a more detailed and specific way. one of the great advantages of incorporating the convention into eu law, in my view, is that it will give the convention a much stronger capacity to monitor the community, for example in infringement proceedings within the european union itself, which will further strengthen the rule of law. the european union's provisions on flag state control should undoubtedly reflect more closely what the convention specifies and expressly provides in order to avoid divergent interpretations by the member states, which could lead to unfair competition and social dumping.
in writing. − the european parliament (ep) is called upon to give its consent to a proposal for a joint directive (ep and council) on the responsibilities of a flag state in enforcing compliance with council directive 2009/13/ec implementing the agreement concluded by the european community shipowners' association (ecsa) and the european transport workers' federation (etf) concerning the maritime labour convention, 2006, amending directive 1999/63/ec. this directive falls within the framework of the maritime labour convention (mlc) which integrates many other european legal measures. for the mlc to enter into force, it needs to be ratified by 30 countries representing 33% of the world's gross tonnage. the mlc affects some 1.2 million maritime workers worldwide, covers areas as diverse as safety, working conditions, health, social security and welfare, and aims to ensure decent working conditions on board ships. since this directive, by promoting equality worldwide and safeguarding europe's interests, aims to fill the gap in european legislation which prevents the application of the provisions of title 5 of the ctm (inspection procedures and compliance with the regulatory framework), i am voting in favour of the report drawn up by my colleague, mrs pervenche berès.
in writing. − the maritime labour convention (mlc) was adopted by the ilo in 2006. this convention applies to international maritime transport and covers the minimum conditions to be observed for seafarers working on board a ship, working conditions, accommodation, leisure, food and table service, health protection, medical care, welfare and social security protection, with a view to ensuring decent working and living conditions on board ships. the eu sees the mlc as a valuable contribution to the objective of creating a level playing field in the global maritime sector by setting common minimum standards for all flags and for all seafarers. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of workers from harmful substances. one of the major advantages of incorporating the ctm into legislation is that it gives it a much stronger capacity for enforcement in the community area, for example at the level of infringement proceedings in the eu itself, which will further strengthen compliance with the law. we voted in favour.

in writing. − with the start of the next parliamentary term in 2014, the current derogation from article 14 (2) of the treaty on european union (teu) will cease to apply, with the european parliament now composed of 751 members (750, plus the president). the number of seats is currently 754. with the entry into force of the treaty of accession of croatia, 12 seats will be allocated to croatia (which currently has 12 observers). the total number of seats will therefore have to be redistributed in order to bring it into line with the number laid down by the treaty (751). in this balance, a pragmatic solution was chosen, based on a different criterion, namely to minimise the loss of seats for the member states, while respecting, as far as possible, degressive proportionality, in accordance with the principle 'no one wins and no one loses more than one seat', which would not happen in several proposals that were under discussion, which further penalized portugal, and which were the losers.

in writing. - article 14 (2) of the treaty on european union states that the representation of the population in the european parliament shall be degressively proportional, following the following principles: (1) the minimum and maximum numbers laid down by the treaty should be fully used in order to ensure that the range of seats in the european parliament is as close as possible to the electoral spectrum of the populations of the member states; (2) 'the more populous a member state is, the greater the number of seats it is entitled to'; and (3) 'the more populous a member state is, the greater the number of inhabitants represented by each member of the european parliament in that member state'. i support this report because it makes more sense to reduce the number of members of the european parliament as a result of croatia's accession to the european union and because the ceiling of 751 members must be respected. in this context, i congratulate my colleague paulo rangel on the excellent work he has done in the committee on constitutional affairs, particularly in advocating a pragmatic solution that would minimise the loss of seats for the member states. i also welcome the fact that portugal will lose only one seat in the next european parliament elections, while respecting the principle of degressive proportionality.

in writing. the motion for a resolution under consideration, tabled pursuant to rule 88 (2) and (3) and (4) (c) of the rules of procedure, concerns the definition, designation, presentation, labelling and protection of geographical indications for spirit drinks. annex ii to regulation (ec) no 110/2008 defines the categories into which spirit drinks are classified and which should be based on the ancestral practices that have given them distinctive characteristics. absinthe, a spirit drink produced in several member states by 'aromatising ethyl alcohol of agricultural origin or a distillate of agricultural origin with wormwood (artemisia absinthium l.), sandstone (artemisia pontica l.), anise (pimpinella anisum l.), fennel (foeniculum vulgare mill.) and other herbaceous plants', is not listed in annex ii to regulation (ec) no 110/2008 and the commission intends to include it. considering that the amendments which the commission intends to introduce into this regulation to include absinthe are likely to call into question the current modus faciendi, harming producers and irritating consumers, i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which opposes the draft commission regulation which sought to amend annexes ii and iii to regulation (ec) no 110/2008 of the european parliament and of the council.
in writing. - this resolution opposes the amendment proposed by the european commission to annexes ii and iii to the regulation on the definition, designation, presentation, labelling and protection of geographical indications of spirit drinks. the problem is the commission's proposed definition of absinthe. this definition establishes a minimum value of anethole of 0,5 grams per litre and a quantity of tujone between 5 and 35 milligrams per litre. however, that definition does not take into account all traditional practices for the production of absinthe, which differ in many member states, and the various traditional recipes, some of which provide for a lower level of anethole. with this definition, many producers of these absinthe variants would have to refrain from using the term 'absinthe', thus calling into question traditional practices used in the production of spirit drinks. in addition, there are also objections related to public health issues. this is because thujone, used as a flavouring substance, can cause harm to human health. for this reason, many absinthe growers have begun to use thujone-free artemisia plants. we voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i consider that the commission proposal is not compatible with the objective and content of regulation (ec) no 110/2008.

in writing. − the draft commission regulation amending annexes ii and iii to regulation (ec) no 110/2008 of the european parliament and of the council on the definition, presentation, labelling and protection of geographical indications of spirit drinks proposes to insert a definition of absinthe in annex ii, which should provide for a minimum level of anethole of 0.5 grams per litre in the drinks so designated. however, traditional practices for the production of absinthe in many member states differ to some extent and not all traditional recipes provide for a minimum level equal to the higher level stipulated by the proposal. the report says that absinthe as a product category should be defined in such a way as to ensure that traditional variants are respected and not to require that traditional methods conform to the definition proposed by the commission. the rapporteur also criticises the contradiction in annex iii, which restricts the definition of absinthe to the presence of a certain amount of thujone, ignoring the fact that some producers already use artemisinin plants which do not have thujone, or contain only trace levels of the substance.
in writing. − the definition of the spirit drink known as absinthe is difficult because the flavouring of the alcohol depends on the regional availability of the herbal plants used and consumer preference. in addition, the definition of absinthe proposed by the commission is restrictive and would imply the alteration of old artisanal recipes, which would consequently involve a change in the inherent characteristics of the drink with the potential to delight consumers and undermine their confidence in producers. i also agree with the rapporteur that the stipulation of a minimum level of tujone (alpha and beta) as part of the definition of absinthe does not add an indispensable characteristic to the definition of the drink. it is noted that regulation (ec) no 1334/2008 of the european parliament and of the council of 16 december 2008 on flavourings and certain food ingredients with flavouring properties used in and on foods already contains provisions on the levels of thujone allowed in alcoholic beverages. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
