in writing. - more than 20 years after the promise of convergence of cap payments between the various member states, gross inequalities and injustices in the distribution of cap funds persist. this report will prolong them, postponing the promised convergence beyond 2020. portugal is among the countries that receive the least aid per hectare on average (fourth from the bottom out of 27). but this time, inequalities in the distribution of cap funds could have even more destructive effects: the reason for this is that at the same time, the instruments of production regulation, such as quotas, which guaranteed each country minimum levels of production, were dismantled. the slogan, instead of food sovereignty and food security, is the orientation of agricultural policy towards the 'market' and towards 'competitiveness'. but the truth is that some are counting on three or four times as much help as others, who are asked to be "competitive". there is a continuing flow of cash to large landowners, simply because they are landowners , with no obligation to produce. among other things, our proposal to raise the minimum amount of payments to small farmers to eur 1 000, twice the amount proposed by the commission, was rejected. we voted against it.
in writing. − in the current discussion on the cap post-2013 the cap is being asked to make the necessary adjustments (by redefining its objectives and at the same time the means to achieve them) so that european agriculture is able to reconcile food security (forecasts indicate a need to increase crop and animal production by around 70% by 2050 to cope with the increase in the world population, rising income levels and the fight against hunger in the world) with environmental sustainability (while ensuring the conservation of biodiversity, sustainable management of natural resources, mitigation and adaptation to climate change, enhancing the value of rural landscapes and contributing to the economic and social vitality and cohesion of rural territories). the mandate now given to the ep is crucial to achieving a better cap for the future. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. − i support this motion for a resolution and the amendments it contains, stressing that the communication on the cap to 2020 sets out the potential challenges, objectives and guidelines for the common agricultural policy after 2013. this reform should cover all the main instruments of the cap, including regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 establishing a common organisation of agricultural markets and on specific provisions for certain agricultural products ('single cmo regulation'). in view of the scope of those amendments, regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 should be repealed and replaced by a new 'single cmo' regulation. the reform should also harmonise, streamline and simplify provisions as far as possible, in particular those covering more than one agricultural sector, in particular by ensuring that non-essential elements of the measures can be adopted by the commission by means of delegated acts. in addition, the reform must continue along the lines of previous reforms, towards greater competitiveness and market orientation and avoid and correct at all costs the market divergences that occur in these negotiations within the internal market with viable financial instruments to avoid harmful consequences in regions highly dependent on the agricultural sector.

in writing. - for many years, farmers and politicians have been calling for the urgent need to review the common agricultural policy (cap). the measures implemented in previous community frameworks have not had the desired effect and have led to many people leaving farming. the creation of agricultural markets with efficient and transparent management, properly controlled throughout the supply chain of products, will ensure fair livelihoods for farmers, the supply of goods and security for consumers. i therefore welcome the adoption of this regulation, which i consider to be a good starting point for the adoption of a new cap, at a time when the european parliament is taking decisions for the first time with full legislative powers. i would also like to stress the intention to reduce the bureaucracy in all procedures, since every year farmers have to 'cross the storm line' to receive the aid to which they are entitled. i voted in favour of this report by michel dantin and i urge the commission to start negotiations with all partners now, with the participation of the farmers' representative associations, without creating cartels, so that the new cap will enter into force on 1 january 2014.

in writing. − the european commission published in october 2011 the legislative proposals for the introduction of a reformed common agricultural policy on 1 january 2014. in the event of no agreement after 2014 for the mff, the agri committee agreed not to hold the final vote on the legislative proposals, opting for the flexibility provided for in rule 70 of parliament's rules of procedure, in order to obtain a mandate to open negotiations with the council and the commission, on the basis of the amendments adopted by the agri committee and confirmed and amended in plenary. the provisional negotiations can therefore be opened while parliament considers its position on the agreement reached by the european council on the mff. this regulation forms part of a body of four cap regulations and lays down the rules for the common organization of the markets in agricultural products. the rapporteur states his priorities in drafting amendments which take account of the specificities of agriculture and the food supply chain and enable the agricultural sector to circumvent, within defined limits, the normal rules of competition. i voted in favour and i welcome the rebalancing of forces in favour of producers achieved by the amendments to the commission's original text.

in writing. − the fukushima nuclear disaster has raised awareness of the need to review the safety of nuclear installations in europe and worldwide. although the three mile island and chernobyl accidents prompted the adoption of measures to protect nuclear power stations, in many cases, incredibly, the implementation of these measures is still suspended. the results of the comprehensive safety risk assessment carried out by the commission, with the participation of the 14 member states with nuclear power plants and lithuania (in decommissioning), plus three neighbouring countries switzerland, ukraine and croatia , have shown the existence of best practices, but unfortunately also numerous shortcomings. of the 132 nuclear reactors in operation in the eu, the vast majority need improvements in their intrinsic safety. in addition, there are weaknesses in the existing legal framework for nuclear safety which justify an urgent effort to achieve convergence in nuclear safety. i look forward to the introduction of the new nuclear safety directive and hope that the more reticent member states will finally accept that there is a real need to create stricter nuclear standards and that monitoring and verification mechanisms at eu level cannot be limited to peer review of the national nuclear safety framework.

in writing. − on 11 march 2011, following an earthquake and tsunami, a major accident occurred at the fukushima nuclear power plant in japan, causing thousands of casualties and untold damage, once again drawing attention to the safety of nuclear power plants. the european community, still reeling from the tragic consequences of the radioactive leak from the chernobyl nuclear power station, has decided to carry out an exhaustive assessment of the operating conditions of its nuclear power stations by implementing so-called stress tests (sts). although some consider nuclear energy to be the energy of the future because of its contribution to reducing co2 emissions, the seriousness of the accidents at chernobyl and fukushima is proof that it is not completely safe. i welcome the initiative to carry out stress tests at all european power stations, the results of which will form the basis of the future directive on nuclear safety, an example of european citizens coming together to ensure their safety. the safety of nuclear power stations must be improved so that citizens can feel safe and have a quality of life.
in writing. − the safety of nuclear power stations is of the utmost importance. the safety of people, workers, public health and the environment are at stake. the european council, following the fukushima accident in march 2011, concluded that 'the safety of all nuclear power plants in the eu should be reviewed'. strength tests have been defined to be carried out in two ways: a safety band to assess how nuclear installations withstand the consequences of various extreme and external events and a safety band to analyse security threats and incidents due to criminal actions. the tests shall take into account the occurrence of natural events, including tsunamis, earthquakes and extreme weather, the loss of safety systems and the management of major accidents, and shall be divided into phases which include the performance of assessments by operators, the submission of proposals for safety improvements, and the independent assessment by national regulators of the assessments carried out, where appropriate. this resolution considers that the requirements associated with stress testing could go further. in this respect, the commission is invited to carry out a more detailed analysis of the costs of improvements, which should not be borne by the taxpayers. we voted in favour.

in writing. − in the wake of the accident at the fucoxima daichi nuclear power station in japan, comprehensive risk and safety assessments ('strength tests') of nuclear power stations in the european union were carried out to assess the readiness of the plants to deal with extreme conditions such as natural disasters. on the basis of these tests, the national regulators concluded that, although there are no technical reasons for decommissioning any nuclear power plant in europe, there is nevertheless a need to implement specific improvements in the safety of the installations, the estimated cost of which, between eur 10 and eur 25 billion, should be borne entirely by the nuclear operators. parliament called on the commission to present proposals on the definition of the principles governing nuclear safety regulation for nuclear power stations in operation, in the process of being decommissioned or already decommissioned, in order to create a nuclear safety oversight mechanism at eu level and to confer responsibility for ensuring nuclear safety. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution, which seeks to harmonise and enforce the highest safety and security practices and standards worldwide in the eu.

in writing. - in 1977, a group of experts commissioned by the european commission concluded: "there is no theoretical evidence of an exposure limit below which there is no risk of developing cancer", soon after the first european legislation against asbestos emerges. it is therefore possible to say that asbestos is virtually banned throughout the eu today. despite the ban on asbestos in the eu, there is no effective monitoring system for asbestos in transport and infrastructure dismantling and eastern european member states have a high number of cancers due to the number of workers in almost daily contact with asbestos/asbestos-containing minerals and their lack of knowledge on how to protect themselves when exposed to them. i therefore support the rapporteur in urging the authorities to safely remove asbestos left in public buildings and to recognise the need for additional legislation on the recognition and compensation of occupational diseases involving contact with this mineral.
in writing. this is an own-initiative report by the employment committee which attempts to respond to the calls of the trade unions for a campaign on the use of asbestos. although there is a general ban in the eu on the production, import and manufacture of products containing asbestos, this deadly substance is still present in public and private buildings, public transport systems and everyday products. the main demand of the trade unions is the development of action plans to remove existing asbestos safely, with the aim of achieving an asbestos-free europe by 2023. to this end, they call for a complete register of products containing asbestos, improved health and safety at work, training of workers handling asbestos and recognition and compensation for asbestos victims. we consider this action plan to be urgent and we hope that the adoption of this report will have practical consequences in a short time.
in writing. - i approve this report, recalling that the european parliament considers that the diversity of enterprises should be clearly laid down in the treaty on the functioning of the european union and proposes that mutual societies be included in article 54 thereof. i would also point out that a combination of strategies and measures is needed to create a level playing field for mutuals, including a european status that equally gives them the possibility to add a european dimension to their organisation and activities, giving them appropriate legal instruments to facilitate their cross-border and transnational activities. in this respect, mutual societies may operate throughout the union in accordance with their specific governance. i believe that a statute for european mutual societies will create a voluntary system in the form of an optional instrument which will enable mutual societies to operate in different member states and even to enter countries where they do not currently exist. i therefore insist that european mutual societies be considered as a european legal form with a specific character for the union.
in writing. - since 2001, the ep has consistently called for the adoption of a european legal framework for mutual societies in the union, in order to overcome the difficulties currently faced by mutual societies and to facilitate their crossborder activities. mutual societies make a decisive contribution to the social economy by combining cost-effectiveness and solidarity, providing affordable healthcare, social benefits and insurance services to some 160 million european citizens and employing more than 350 000 people in the eu. however, without a european mutual statute, it is difficult to implement it, as there are huge discrepancies in legislation, operation and taxation between member states, including member states that do not even have a legal framework for mutual societies. i regret that the commission withdrew its initial proposal in 2006, allowing reciprocity to continue to be ignored in the internal market, and i congratulate mrs regina bastos on her report. i call on the commission to present a new initiative to create an ambitious and innovative european statute for the protection of workers and their families exercising their right to free movement, which will make it easier for mutual societies to carry out crossborder activities and enable them to benefit fully from the internal market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that mutual societies should play a more prominent role in the economies of the member states, given their potential to contribute to more inclusive growth. it is necessary to create a level playing field for mutuals, including a european status that gives them the possibility to add a european dimension to their organisation and activities.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis has brought about a significant increase in the performance of enterprises and social institutions, giving them a visibility they did not have before. in fact, they are the first and sometimes the only response to situations of great economic need. the european social sector has some 350,000 institutions providing welfare services (mainly health and family support) to over 260 million europeans, many of whom live in areas far from urban centres and this is the only support they have. the report by mr luigi berlinguer recommends that the commission adopt a regulation on the statute for a european mutual fund which will make it possible to remove all the crossborder obstacles to its activity throughout the single market and allow the crossborder merger of two or more mutual funds in order to improve their performance and gain in scale. i voted in favour because i believe that this is an excellent initiative which will boost the social economy by providing new services, creating jobs at local level and promoting solidarity. the new services will not compete with existing ones but will contribute to diversity, which is essential for growth.
in writing. - mutual societies mutual assistance societies (social security services complementary to or integrated with compulsory social protection schemes) or insurance mutuals (which may cover all types of risk to property and life), and may also in some member states provide services in other areas such as housing or credit undoubtedly play an important social role. the report calls on the commission to submit one or more legislative proposals to enable the creation of a voluntary scheme, in the form of an optional instrument, allowing mutual societies to operate at european and cross-border level. issues such as crossborder mergers of mutual societies or the creation of european mutual groups raise complex questions, which the report does not address. despite some positive recommendations, such as that mutual societies should not replace compulsory social security schemes, or that the regulation should not cover other areas of law, such as labour law, taxation, etc., potential dangers are not excluded, especially in the current political and economic context and in the context of the neoliberal policies prevailing in the eu.
in writing. − i believe that a combination of strategies and measures is needed to create a level playing field for mutuals, including a european status that equally gives them the possibility to add a european dimension to their organisation and activities, giving them appropriate legal instruments to facilitate their cross-border and transnational activities, so that mutuals can operate throughout the union in accordance with their specific governance. a statute for european mutual societies will create a voluntary system in the form of an optional instrument which will enable mutual societies to operate in different member states, and even to be introduced in countries where they do not currently exist. i therefore believe it necessary that european mutual societies should be considered as a european legal form with a specific character.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the berlinguer report which recommends that the commission should create a european mutual statute for three main reasons: (a) mutual societies play a major role in the social economy of the union which cannot be ignored, providing health care and social services to over 160 million people and employing over 350 000 people; (b) the absence of a european statute for mutual societies has been an obstacle to their full development in the internal market of the union, and it is therefore important to provide mutual societies with a european legal form which eliminates their disadvantage compared with other forms of undertaking which already have european statutes; (c) finally, it is important to safeguard the mutual societies which, as a characteristic form of organisation (in compliance with the mutualist principles), have shown the greatest resilience to the recent financial crisis, without prejudice to ensuring the conditions for their competitiveness with their commercial counterparts.
in writing. − the european status of mutual societies is essential for better integration into the single market, better recognition of the specificities of mutualism and enhancing its capacity to contribute to the achievement of the growth and employment objectives of the 2020 strategy. i would stress that it is very important that this statute should be aware of the differences between the mutual societies of each member state, since the mutual societies also reflect the size of each country, and a system which does not reduce the size of each mutual society may result in the disappearance of the mutual society system in small and medium-sized countries, as is the case in portugal.
in writing. − mutual societies are voluntary associations of natural or legal persons which, operating under democratic management and in accordance with the principle of solidarity, aim to meet the needs of their members at the expense of obtaining a return on investment. the eu, in view of the important role of mutual societies in the economy and society of the member states, especially in the achievement of strategic union objectives such as healthcare, long-term care, social protection and pensions, should provide such associations with a european status that allows them to operate on an equal footing with other forms of business in the union, facilitating the development of their cross-border activities and enabling them to benefit from the internal market. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which calls on the commission to establish precise and clear conditions for the creation of a new category of european mutual funds.
in writing. − the commission withdrew its draft proposal for a regulation on the european mutual statute in march 2006, and the european parliament has in recent years adopted several resolutions calling for a regulation on the subject and expressing its preference for a european statute. today the european parliament has asked the commission to submit rapidly, following the detailed recommendations in the annex, on the basis of article 352 or possibly article 114 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, one or more proposals enabling mutual societies to operate at european and cross-border level. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. − this report aims to establish a european legal status for mutual societies in order to enable them to operate at european and cross-border level by creating transnational mutual societies. the rapporteur considers that the european statute will be a voluntary instrument complementary to the national legal provisions applicable to mutual societies and will not affect the independence, autonomy and individual participation of its members. however, we do not see the objective that the status of mutual societies should encourage the development of the eu's internal market, i.e. a market which promotes the free movement of capital, goods and services within the framework of capitalist competition. nor do we subscribe to the principle underlying the establishment of a european legal status, namely the harmonization of commercial and civil law.

in writing. − the recent discovery by europol of a set of sponsored games has led to the need for a number of legislative measures. thus, players, coaches, referees, and presidents of sports clubs must abide by a code of conduct that lays out the dangers of match fixing, includes a prohibition of this practice, and stipulates the penalties to be applied. all eu countries should explicitly include the issue of addiction to results in their national criminal law, providing for common minimum sanctions and providing for any omissions. sports organisations, national police and judicial authorities and online gambling operators should step up efforts to combat sports addiction. the commission should coordinate these efforts at european level and create a platform for dialogue and exchange of information and best practice. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − in this resolution, the european parliament urges the council to pursue, in a rapid and ambitious manner, discussions on the proposal for a new directive on money laundering in order to address the use of online sports betting for money laundering purposes. i voted in favour of this ambition.
in writing. − the findings of the investigations by europol and commission teams revealed widespread manipulation of game results, with a total of 680 suspected games worldwide. this number is just the tip of the iceberg of a vast network of manipulation installed in the sports world. parliament considered that the addiction to results is a form of crime that generates high revenues but has extremely low conviction and detention rates, and is therefore used by criminal organisations in money laundering and drug and human trafficking, and called on the commission to encourage member states to explicitly include the issue of addiction to results in their national criminal law and to set up a specialised unit responsible for law enforcement.
in writing. − a joint europol investigation team has revealed widespread manipulation of football match results over the last few years, with 680 matches considered suspicious worldwide, 380 of them in europe, and has identified a vast network of manipulation in the sports environment, with 425 suspects and 50 people arrested. considering that transparency, accountability and democracy at the level of sports organisations are essential conditions for the sporting movement to play a role with a minimum chance of success in the fight against performance addiction and sports fraud, parliament called on the commission to develop a coordinated approach to combating performance addiction and organised crime by coordinating the efforts of the main stakeholders and by creating a platform for dialogue and exchange of information and best practice. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. − the aim of the resolution is to strengthen the fight against performance addiction in sport by each of the stakeholders and to develop a coordinated approach against organised crime, with sport organisations, police and judicial authorities at national level and online gaming operators. the measures proposed here follow the principle of zero tolerance for corruption, suggesting that sports organisations create a code of conduct for all involved that sets out the dangers of match fixing, includes a clear prohibition on the manipulation of results with penalties to be applied and prohibits betting on their own games and an obligation to report any approach or knowledge thereof in conjunction with an appropriate protection mechanism for whistleblowers. the protection of the integrity of sport begins with sport education from childhood and the training of athletes, both amateur and professional, with a view to raising awareness of the values of integrity, fair play and respect for others. the resolution does not, however, mention the importance of public sports facilities, which allow the democratization of sports, or the importance of physical education in school curricula.

in writing. the european parliament has adopted a resolution on the situation in the world of the cotton industry. cotton is a raw material which is considered to be universal and essential for agricultural activity, for processing enterprises and for world trade. although european production represents only 1% of world production, it employs some 100 000 people, mainly in greece and spain. despite its low production, the eu is responsible for using 50% of global production and is a net exporter of this product whose european industry employs over 1.8 million. the main problems facing the sector worldwide are the scourge of child labour and the environmental footprint resulting from the excessive use of pesticides, insecticides and water, polluting soils and leading to a marked loss of biodiversity. the eu, as the main importer of this material, is the largest donor to developing producer countries. despite the importance of this sector to the european economy, the eu is not a member of the international cotton advisory committee (icac), whose mission is to promote good practice. i therefore welcome the proposal for eu membership of the ccia.
in writing. - this resolution refers to various aspects related to the sustainability of the cotton value chain. it highlights the environmental problems in cotton production, such as excessive water consumption, the use of pesticides and insecticides and soil degradation, but mainly highlights the serious problem of child labour and forced labour. the resolution focuses on condemning countries that use child and forced labour, and on considering possible solutions. the commission is proposing that the ccia should set up means of independent monitoring of human rights violations in the cotton value chain by ngos. that efforts be made by the cotton-producing countries to support farmers' organizations and trade unions in order to raise income levels and improve working conditions in the cotton fields. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of workers' rights and the right to health. the resolution also calls on the commission to study a legislative proposal on an effective mechanism for tracing goods produced by child labour or forced labour. we voted yes.
in writing. cotton is among the most important crops in terms of land, an important job creator and a vital non-food commodity for rural communities, traders, the textile industry and consumers worldwide. cotton is the most widely used natural fibre, grown in over 100 countries and marketed in about 150 countries. it is estimated that around 100 million households are involved in cotton production and that the cotton sector is an important source of employment and income for more than 250 million people involved in the production, processing, storage and transport of this agricultural value chain. we must step up efforts to combat trade-distorting measures and improve transparency in commodity derivatives markets. the sustainability of the cotton sector depends on producers, traders, suppliers of inputs, textile manufacturers, retailers, brands, governments, civil society and consumers. fair trade schemes provide for closer cooperation between consumers and producers, in particular in the cotton sector, whose expertise and best practices should be assessed by the commission. that is why i am voting in favour.

he asks under the blue card procedure. mr jørgensen says that his party is very green and that others in denmark who also support the carbon market are very green. what i wanted to ask you is whether, in this green spirit, you conceive or admit any solution to this problem of reducing greenhouse gas emissions that is not a market solution, if you can conceive of any solution that does not go through the market? and second, what makes you think it's gonna work this time, which it never has, just because we've postponed the auction of a few licenses?
the years go by and reality insists on confirming what many, including ourselves, have always said: the carbon market not only does not lead to reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, but is itself an obstacle to such reductions and to decreased dependence on fossil fuels. to insist is ineffective and perverse. it has provided fabulous profits for the big polluters, who are lining up credits with more than dubious and perverse investments made in developing countries, and selling the licences that have been allocated to them free of charge. it is a system that has proved to be vulnerable to failure and fraud, such as the carousel frauds in several countries that have damaged the public purse by billions of euros. the costs of the system are borne by the taxpayers, the profits go to the polluters. the commodification and financialization of natural functions and cycles may be appealing to a dying capitalism, a new boon for speculators, but it will never be an instrument for nature conservation. the alternative to market illusions lies in a regulatory and normative approach that is effective from the point of view of environmental objectives and socially fair. we therefore want to join our voices here with the many hundreds of environmental organizations around the world calling for an end to the carbon market. alternative solutions exist and can be implemented now. member of the commission. − mr president, the commission welcomes this report by the european parliament. it is a very important issue and i would like to thank the rapporteur, ms gurmai, the shadow rapporteurs and everybody who helped with this report. the commission, as a guardian of the treaties, has a duty to monitor the implementation of eu legislation by the member states. so, all legislation regarding equal treatment shall be fully and correctly implemented by all member states. this is our position. referring to this special directive, the commission has started to monitor conformity and what the member states have been doing since 2011. then we started monitoring. following the so-called ‘test-achats’ ruling, the commission adopted guidelines to facilitate the transition to unisex pricing and enhance legal certainty in the insurance sector. the delay set by the court of justice of the european union to comply with the test-achats ruling elapsed on 21 december 2012, so we have legal certainty now. the commission will watch closely to see whether all member states have properly implemented the ruling in their respective national legislation. you are asking for a new report. i can inform you that the commission will report on the impact of the ruling in 2014 in the context of a more general report on the implementation of this directive. then the commission will also provide information about the outcome of the conformity checks of the national legislations. we consider that there is no need to propose new legislation to address the principle of unisex pricing in insurance services. the judgment of the court of justice of the european union is clear. that is why we think that legal certainty exists. the court ensures equal treatment of men and women in insurance, by declaring invalid article 5 of the directive on equal access to goods and services. the decision of the court is very clear – that is why we think that legal certainty is there, and there is really no need for further legal action on this point. promoting effective gender equality in the european union is and will continue to be a priority of the commission. as the rapporteur underlined – and we would like to agree – national equality bodies play an important role in this, and the commission can reassure parliament that it will monitor properly and accurately the situation of the equality bodies across europe. i would like to thank the european parliament for keeping gender equality in europe high on the political agenda. i would like to reiterate that the commission strives for good cooperation with the rapporteur, parliament and everybody here.
despite the progress made and the legislation passed, it is a fact that women continue to be discriminated against in various ways. we must therefore continue to tackle persistent inequalities and improve legislation. the directive implementing the principle of equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services has not produced the desired results, as in some cases it has proved to be detrimental to women. in some member states, the transposition of the directive has been incomplete or delayed, in others, national legislation has been vague and unclear, which has made its proper interpretation and application difficult and has generated legal uncertainty. discrimination in relation to pregnancy and maternity, for example in housing or in obtaining loans, as well as in access to medical goods and services, in particular reproductive health care and gender reassignment treatment, as provided for in legislation, is unacceptable. we support the proposals of the rapporteur, mrs zita grumai, whose work we thank and welcome, and of course we welcome the commission's efforts to ensure legal certainty, but we think it would be better if a new legislative text were put forward. that's our opinion.
i would like to say that i am very pleased that the commission has taken this initiative. it is unacceptable that equality between men and women should be promoted as a principle of the european union in various marketing campaigns as an unquestionable value and then in practice be given over to the lobbies of insurance companies and the financial sector, with the intention of derogating from the principle, which is unquestionable, but it seems that only in some situations. it is unacceptable that sex should be considered as a basis for differentiating the premiums and benefits of insured persons. it is unacceptable that the lives of women who want to take out insurance should be marred by questionnaires asking about their reproductive life, in particular whether they have ever had a voluntary termination of pregnancy. on the other hand, it is clear that the current directive does not address fundamental issues, in particular the content of the media and advertising, which, as we all know, are among the media that most stereotypically and discriminatoryally treat women. finally, it is important to remember that today the discrimination affecting women in access to goods and services is increasing rapidly at another level, at the most fundamental level of purchasing power and choice resulting from the differentiations in access to quality employment and access to decent wages and pensions, i.e. inequalities between men and women are deepening at the most basic levels of social life, in an unprecedented civilizational retreat, demonstrating the failure of these guiding policies of the european union.

mr president, this discussion on promoting development through trade cannot ignore the harmful effects of liberalization and deregulation of world trade in developing countries. contrary to what the heralds of free trade preach, for these countries its effects mean more poverty, more inequality, more difficulties imposed on the diversification of their fragile economies, greater dependence on and less use of natural resources, which are progressively being expropriated, development projects compromised. the promotion of development requires regulated and complementary trade and genuine development cooperation policies. the european union is now rapidly turning its back on blackmail and pressure to sign the so-called economic partnership agreements, to which these countries have rightly and understandably resisted. it is that, as free trade agreements are, they are a clear protectionism of the rich and powerful and not any help to the weak.
the european union's trade and investment policies in developing countries have practical results and consequences which need to be discussed in greater depth. it is based on the subordinate and peripheral insertion of these countries in world trade, on the enormous and growing dependence on foreign investment, which results in an increasingly fragile sovereignty and consequent compromise of endogenous development projects. to make matters worse, so-called investment agreements often stifle public policies essential to the predominance of the interests of these countries and their peoples over the interests of foreign investors. a project for the autonomous and sovereign development of these countries requires that space be made available for public policies, allowing for their sovereign use and the use of all the instruments associated with it, including expropriations, nationalizations, among others. it is the most basic democratic values and principles that require it, and any genuine development cooperation policy must recognize and respect it.

in writing. − the european network and information security agency (enisa), set up in 2004 for an initial period of five years, was extended in 2008 until 2012. in september 2010, the european commission put forward a proposal to extend the operational period until september 2013. the agency has made a valuable contribution to network and information security and meets specific needs at the european union level by promoting cooperation between all stakeholders in a more effective and efficient way than cooperation between member states would ever be able to achieve. the mandate and resources of enisa need to be strengthened in order to ensure and promote a high level of security and data protection and should ensure liaison with national authorities. it is also important that the agency's scope, missions and objectives become clearer so that its valuable resources can be better used. i therefore support this report.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'accidental catches of cetaceans' because it includes proposals to reverse the dramatic decline in the population of cetaceans in european waters, in particular through the use of acoustic deterrents.
in writing. − accidental capture of cetaceans is a threat to the survival of several species. as the fisheries committee warns, 'catfish stocks are being drastically reduced, while tens of thousands of cetaceans are killed in eu waters every year.' this sad reality must be a cause for concern for all those who recognise the need to ensure the protection of marine biodiversity. the fishing communities must play an active role in this process. existing legislation appears to be insufficient to achieve similar objectives. the european commission has been exercising powers in this area which, by virtue of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, are being reclassified. the time is right for more than mere legal compliance to be laid down, laying the foundations for concrete improvements in the way in which the protection of cetaceans and the deterrence of their capture are being verified.
in writing. the report under consideration concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 812/2004 laying down measures relating to incidental catches of cetaceans during fishing activities and amending regulation (ec) no 88/98. with the entry into force of the tfeu, the regulatory hierarchy has undergone a major reshaping, as the ep and the council have now been placed on an equal footing with regard to the ordinary legislative procedures. in addition, in order to streamline procedures, legislators have been able to use delegated acts, giving the commission the power to adopt non-legislative acts of a general nature. there is also a third level of legislation, the implementing acts. as a consequence of the tfeu, all regulations contrary to the new regulatory hierarchy have become outdated and need to be amended. i voted in favour of this report which supports the commission's proposal for 'the establishment of delegated acts to adapt the conditions and technical specifications for the use of acoustic deterrents; and the application of acts concerning the procedure and format of the reports which member states are required to submit'.
in writing. − as a consequence of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the powers conferred on the commission for the application of regulation (ec) no 812/2004 should be aligned with articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. in order to implement certain provisions of regulation (ec) no 812/2004, it is proposed to confer on the commission the power to adopt delegated acts concerning the technical specifications and conditions of use of acoustic deterrents - which we consider appropriate and proportionate and does not raise any major problems. it is also proposed to confer implementing powers on the commission in order to ensure uniform conditions for the application of the provisions of this regulation. the rapporteur accepts the commission's position but puts forward three amendments to limit the commission's powers for a period of three years (the commission proposal called for an indefinite period of time) and calls on the commission to present by 2015 a legislative proposal to ensure effective protection of cetaceans. we think the rapporteur's position is correct and we have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - unfortunately, cetacean stocks have been drastically reduced, with tens of thousands of cetaceans dying annually in eu waters. regulation (ec) no 812/2004 is mainly focused on the use of acoustic devices to prevent the accidental capture of cetaceans, although cetaceans are exposed to different threats such as habitat degradation, collisions with vessels and underwater noise pollution. we need to establish a new overall legislative framework for the protection of cetaceans, hence my vote.
in writing. − the purpose of this report is to review regulation (ec) no 812/2004 laying down measures concerning incidental catches of cetaceans in fisheries and regulation (ec) no 88/98 conferring certain powers on the commission which need to be reclassified in delegated and implementing acts. the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) establishes a new regulatory hierarchy comprising three distinct levels of acts, namely legislative, delegated and implementing acts. delegated and implementing acts allow for a faster response to new situations compared to legislative acts. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the proposal also calls for the use of renewable energy sources to be extended to include the use of renewable energy sources in the transport sector. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it an important element in improving regulation and in minimising incidental catches of cetaceans by fisheries.
in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 812/2004 of 24 april 2004 currently confers implementing powers on the commission, which should be exercised in a manner that safeguards the rights of parliament established by the tfeu. delegated or implementing acts shall allow the adaptation of the conditions and technical specifications for the use of acoustic marine mammal deterrents and the application of acts concerning the procedure and format of the reports to be submitted by member states. the rapporteur therefore agrees with the commission proposal, but proposes some amendments to it, aimed at more rigorously defining the periods of delegation of powers in order to oblige the commission to report on the results of its exercise and, consequently, to obtain a regular evaluation of the delegated acts. in view of the drastic reduction in the number and mortality of cetacean stocks, i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation, hoping that the measures adopted will ensure their effective protection against all threats.
in writing. − in order to implement certain provisions of regulation (ec) no 812/2004, it is proposed to confer delegated acts on the commission with regard to the technical specifications and conditions of use of acoustic deterrent devices, which we consider to be positive. it is also proposed to confer implementing powers on the commission in order to ensure uniform conditions for the application of the provisions of this regulation. the rapporteur accepts the commission's position but proposes three amendments to limit the commission's powers for a period of three years. we voted yes.
in writing. - i approve the renewal of this fisheries agreement, considering that it is balanced and covers the interests of both parties. furthermore, since it allows european vessels to fish in the sovereign waters of the republic of mauritius, but at the same time establishes scientific, financial and technical cooperation in the fisheries sector with a view to promoting responsible fishing in mauritian waters, cooperation on patrolling arrangements in mauritian waters and partnerships between operators with a view to developing economic activities in the fisheries sector and related sectors of common interest, i am of the opinion that once again this protocol protects both the interests of the european union and those of the republic of mauritius.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the conclusion of the fisheries agreement between the european union and the republic of mauritius. the conclusion of this agreement will help to strengthen economic activities in the fisheries sector in europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the eu-mauritius fisheries partnership agreement', considering that it is a balanced agreement which respects the legitimate interests of both parties.
in writing. - the relationship between the european union and the republic of mauritius in the fisheries sector dates back to 1989. however, at the end of the protocol 2003-2007, the parties were unable to reach an agreement on the terms of its renewal. since then, the european fleet has been obliged to operate under private access schemes. the new fisheries partnership agreement and the new protocol will contribute to strengthening mauritius' capacity to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, including through improving its monitoring and control infrastructures for fishing activities in its eez. for the european union, the conclusion of the fisheries partnership agreement and the protocol will help maintain continuity in the fisheries areas covered by agreements in the east african region and contribute to the viability of european industries by providing a medium-term framework of stability for eu vessels and the industries that depend on them. i believe that the new fisheries partnership agreement and the new protocol are balanced and serve the interests of both parties.
in writing. − the european union (eu) and the republic of mauritius have had fisheries relations for almost 25 years, the last protocol expiring in 2007. however, in the years that followed, the parties failed to reach an agreement, to the detriment of the european fishing fleet. following the resumption of negotiations in 2010, it was possible to draw up a fisheries partnership agreement, which the commission signed on 23 february 2012. the recommendation by mr antolín sánchez presedo concerns the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of a new fisheries partnership agreement and a new protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the agreement. given the record of respect for human and fundamental rights by the republic of mauritius and that this fishing activity is sustainable, not showing any negative effects at economic, social or environmental level, i voted in favour as both the new partnership agreement and the new protocol serve the interests of both parties.
in writing. the first fisheries agreements between the european union and the republic of mauritius date back to 1989. these agreements were renewed until 2007, but when the 2003-2007 protocol expired, the parties could not agree on the terms of their renewal. since then, the european fleet has been obliged to operate under private access schemes. in 2010, further efforts were made to reach a new agreement. without prejudice to certain reservations as to the full fulfilment of the conditions put forward by the rapporteur for the approval of the agreement - namely: to be an economically reasonable agreement taking into account the fishing possibilities available; to be a basis for the conservation and sustainable exploitation of the relevant fisheries resources; to constitute adequate support for the local fisheries sector - we supported the conclusion of the agreement, which will open up fishing possibilities for some segments of the national fleet, in particular tuna vessels.
in writing. − the initial fisheries agreement between the eu and the republic of mauritius started in 1989 and ran until 2007. as of that date, the parties have not yet reached a new agreement on the conditions to be adopted under the agreement. when the new negotiations for a new agreement began, an impact assessment was commissioned which did not identify any negative economic, social or environmental effects. the study did identify a number of positive consequences of the previous agreement, such as the strengthening of the european and mauritian fisheries sectors and benefits for local populations. according to this analysis, the opening of fishing opportunities in mauritian waters would not necessarily result in an increase in the total catches taken by european vessels in the indian ocean, but would contribute to a better geographical distribution of fishing effort. finally, it concluded that the mauritius fishing zone does not reveal any specific biological or environmental sensitivity. so this new agreement will be as favourable to the parties involved as it is always intended to be.
in writing. - fisheries relations between the european union and the republic of mauritius date back to the 1980s. however, at the end of the protocol's period of validity from 2003 to 2007, the parties were unable to reach an agreement on its renewal and the european fishing fleet has since been operating in these waters under private access schemes. the intensification of efforts to address this situation led to the establishment of the fisheries partnership protocol and agreement, which was initialled by the commission in 2012. the conclusion of this new fisheries partnership agreement will allow the continuation of the european fleet in east african fishing zones and will contribute to the viability of the european fishing industry operating in these waters by providing fishing opportunities to 41 tuna seiners and 45 surface longliners in return for an annual financial compensation of eur 660 000 (eur 302 500 to support the maritime and fisheries policy in mauritius). given the importance of this eu-mauritius fisheries partnership agreement and considering that the conditions laid down are balanced and of interest to both parties, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − on 23 february 2012, the commission initialled a partnership agreement with the republic of mauritius, the conclusion of which is subject to the approval of the european parliament. the main elements of the new protocol comprise the annual financial compensation of eur 660 000 per year, of which eur 357 500 for the fishing authorisation of a reference tonnage of 5500 tonnes per year, and eur 302 500 corresponding to the additional allocation granted by the eu to support mauritius' fisheries and maritime policy. in this country, fishing accounts for a relatively small part of the national gdp. therefore, the availability of fishing opportunities in mauritian waters does not reveal any negative economic, social or environmental impacts. moreover, the commission stated that the local fisheries sector, due to its characteristics, does not operate in waters where european fishing vessels are authorised to fish and, moreover, eu and mauritian vessels fish for different species. as there is no record of overfishing in the region and as the agreement does not represent any threat to the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources, nor any threat at the socioeconomic level, i voted in favour of the new partnership agreement.

in writing. - the defence of the independence of the mandate of the european parliament is the competence of the european parliament and this independence cannot be called into question. in accordance with article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members of the european parliament may not be subject to any form of search, detention or prosecution for opinions or votes they express in the performance of their duties. in this case, the attorney general of frankenthal intends to file a complaint against jürgen creutzmann, based on allegations that he committed the criminal offence of personal injury by negligence, pursuant to § 229 of the german criminal code. in his letter of 5 november 2012, the frankenthal prosecutor states that jürgen creutzmann, while driving a vehicle, allegedly disregarded the priority of another vehicle at an intersection, thus causing the collision of the two vehicles. the passenger in the other vehicle suffered serious injuries in the accident. in view of the facts which have been pointed out, and because they have nothing to do with the activity of the member of the european parliament, i am in favour of lifting the immunity of jürgen creutzmann.

in writing. - communication and information technologies, which for some time were considered immune or less permeable to the problems plaguing the european economy, are now facing serious problems which are challenging companies in the sector. one of the companies that did not survive the crisis was the italian agile, whose workers are now looking to return to the labour market. enterprises geared to innovation and information and communication technologies are essential for a union which must be able to encourage, attract and maintain them, otherwise their productive fabric will be doomed to stagnation and obsolescence. i hope that the workers helped by the egf will be able to return quickly to the labour market and lend their commitment and expertise to the recovery of such an important sector as the one in which agile operated.
in writing. - this report deals with the proposal for a decision of the european parliament (ep) and of the council on the mobilisation of the egf and falls within paragraph 28 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006 between the ep, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline and sound financial management (application egf/2011/016 it/agile, italy). on 7 march 2013, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in favour of italy to support the reintegration of workers made redundant as a result of the global crisis, following the abovementioned application submitted on 30 december 2011. this is the third application under the eu budget for 2013, mobilising eur 3 689 474, and aims to mitigate the social impact of the dismissal of 1257 workers from agile s.r.l., an ict company which, after accelerated growth at the beginning of the 21st century, closed the first decade with negative annual growth. since the application meets the eligibility criteria, i am voting in favour of this proposal for a decision and i agree with the rapporteur's recommendations for the committee on employment and social affairs to provide support and constructive input to the evaluation of egf applications.
in writing. - another application to the european globalisation adjustment fund, submitted by italy, for a financial contribution of eur 3.689.474 following the dismissal of 1257 workers at agile, a company operating in the technology and communications (it) sector. these redundancies took place almost throughout italy, in particular in the region of umbria, where another company was located, which was also closed. as has become the custom, the justification for further attacks on the right to work lies on the one hand in the major structural changes in world trade patterns and on the other hand in the recession in the it sector. the credit constraints that have arisen in the wake of the economic and financial crisis are now added. more than this fund - which legitimises the policy of dismissals and supports employers in this decision - what workers need is the implementation of investment policies that create and maintain jobs with rights. only a break with the policies currently being pursued by the eu will be able to stop this path of social and economic disaster.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the number of companies relocating is increasing, taking advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, with harmful effects for countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid is now to be granted for 1257 redundancies in the company agile s.r.l., 856 workers being covered by the measures co-financed by the egf during the reference period from 22 september 2011 to 22 december 2011. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation because i consider it necessary to exclude a number of countries from the trade preferences regime under the eu/acp economic partnership agreements. the current situation is not sustainable, as duty-free market access continues to be granted to beneficiary countries which do not take the necessary steps to ratify the agreements.
in writing. - i share the position of the european commission and my political group, which argues that it is time to end the special tariff concessions to countries which have not ratified the economic partnership agreements (epas), as they should have done. meeting the 2014 deadline is not only a sign of respect for those countries that have already signed the epas but it is a proof of seriousness in the work and cooperation between the two blocs. maintaining the 2014 deadline will also encourage the relationship between the various countries in their multiple aspects of economic, commercial and social interaction.
in writing. the recommendation under review, drafted by david martin, concerns the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending annex i to council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 as regards the exclusion of certain countries from the list of regions or states which have concluded negotiations. under the cotonou agreement, the european union and its member states (eu) have concluded economic partnership agreements (epas) with a number of acp (africa, caribbean and pacific) countries and regions. some of these countries have not completed the negotiation process by not ratifying the partnership treaty. this situation, which is incompatible with the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), creates a situation of injustice towards the compliant states. it also makes annex i to council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 outdated. i voted in favour of this report, which not only updates the annex referred to above but also aligns this decision-making with the new procedures resulting from the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. - no substantive amendments to this proposal were made between the first and second readings. we therefore reiterate our position: this proposal for a regulation constitutes an unacceptable form of pressure and blackmail on acp countries which resist - for justified reasons - signing or ratifying the so-called economic partnership agreements, which are nothing more than free trade agreements between the eu and acp countries, which could have disastrous consequences for the fragile and poorly diversified economies of these countries, opening the door to the colonization of their markets and the deepening of relations of dependence and subordination at economic level. our group proposed that the proposal be simply rejected, which unfortunately was not accepted by the majority of parliament. the idea behind the proposed postponement (which is a defeat for the european commission, which opposed it with its well-known fundamentalism in this field) is quite clear: to give the countries more time to sign the agreements and not the profound change that was required in these agreements. this is unacceptable!
in writing. − following the process of negotiating economic partnership agreements (epas) with acp regions that started in 2002 and ended in december 2007, a number of countries did not take the necessary steps to ratify an epa or conclude comprehensive regional negotiations. if countries removed from annex i were to take the necessary steps to ratify an epa, they would continue to benefit from their trade preferences and could therefore be listed again as soon as possible in order to ensure continued market access. to that end, i am in favour of empowering the commission to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu to amend annex i in order to re-include those countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this legislative resolution of the european parliament concerning the exclusion of a number of countries from the list of regions or states to which the arrangements for goods originating in certain states belonging to the african, caribbean and pacific group of states (acp) apply. this regime is that provided for in agreements establishing or leading to the establishment of economic partnership agreements. the states covered by this resolution have not taken the necessary steps to ratify the said agreements and must therefore be excluded. in this resolution, it is decided to delegate the power to the commission to ensure that these countries can be quickly re-inserted into the list after the obstacles have been removed.
in writing. − the european parliament approved, at second reading, the council's position at first reading on the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending annex i to regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 in order to ensure that countries which have concluded economic partnership negotiations with the eu can be readily re-entered into annex i to the regulation as soon as they have taken the necessary steps to ratify their agreements. i voted in favour of the amendments which give the commission the power to adopt acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu, as regards the reintegration of countries which have been removed from annex i to regulation (ec) no 1528/2007.
