in writing. - i welcome this report, considering that the european union emission trading scheme (eu ets) is a key instrument for reducing industrial emissions in the union in a cost-effective way. however, i would stress that despite the reduction in emissions already seen, the system is faced with serious imbalances. in my view, this system is one of the pillars of the european union's environmental policy and it is important to have a short-term measure which is not seen as a real solution to the current imbalances, but rather a position which ensures the stability of the system until the necessary structural measures are adopted. i am therefore in favour of postponing the implementation of this system.
in writing. - i voted against the postponement and in favour of referring the report back to committees because the epc needs a thorough review. the european system is having an effect essentially on cutting emissions in production and not in consumption. with the crisis, it has become easier for europe to meet its emission reduction targets. it is therefore urgent to review the objectives.
in writing. - at a time when the european economy is not growing and when businesses and households are generally hit by rising monthly bills, i do not think it is wise to adopt measures which may have the consequence, even if indirect, of increasing the electricity bill and making it difficult for european industry to be competitive. however, the environmental concerns underlying this commission proposal are equally valid and reasonable. i therefore welcome the fact that this report has been returned to the commission for further discussion.
in writing. − the proper functioning of the carbon market is a key instrument to stimulate economic recovery by promoting a more efficient and competitive low-carbon economy. it ultimately promotes the creation of skilled jobs. at present, the carbon price is insufficient to drive sufficiently sustainable scientific and technological innovation. by the end of 2011, a surplus of 955 million allowances had accumulated and is expected to increase. the carbon price has decreased from around eur 30/t co2 to around eur 7/t co2. the commission proposal on which this report is based follows the resolution entitled 'roadmap to a competitive low-carbon economy by 2050' in which the european parliament called on the commission to take measures to address the shortcomings of the european union emission trading scheme (eu ets) in order to ensure that it operates as originally envisaged and, before the start of the third trading period, to amend, if necessary, the regulation adopted pursuant to article 10 (4) of directive 2003/87/ec in order to implement appropriate measures that may include the retention of the necessary quantity of allowances.
in writing. − this report was intended to amend the 2003 directive on the establishment of a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the community (eu ets) in an attempt to circumvent a problem caused by the accumulation of an excess of 955 million emission allowances at the end of 2011. as the allocation of licences is much higher than demand, the price of carbon has decreased significantly. it is a consequence of the operation of this perverse and ineffective mechanism (ets/carbon market), which we have long warned against. the problem is basic. it has to do with the emissions trading scheme itself, with its principles and (market) foundations, and no cosmetic operation, such as the one now attempted, can solve it entirely. the report was not put to the vote because a motion to reject it, tabled by the conservative group, was adopted. we did not support this proposal because we disagree with the groote report on different grounds. while the right wants business as usual in the functioning of the carbon market, we oppose this instrument and want to replace it with a completely different approach, normative and regulatory.
in writing. - i abstained on this report because i felt that the balance between the interests of industry in the context of the economic crisis and environmental interests had not been struck. while it is true that this is not the right time to increase the energy costs of the various economic sectors, we cannot forget all the efforts and costs already made to reduce co2 emissions. so by returning this report to the committee responsible, i hope that the necessary consensus will be reached so that all the parties involved in this process can find common ground.
in writing. − as the allocation of carbon allowances in the eu is much higher than demand, the carbon price has decreased from around eur 30/t co2 to around eur 7/t co2. this reduction in the carbon price is insufficient to stimulate sufficiently sustainable scientific and technological innovation, and the measures envisaged to encourage investment in low-carbon technologies are ineffective. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the eu, including the eu's maritime borders, and to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the eu's maritime borders.
in writing. − the eu emissions trading scheme (eu ets) is considered a vital mechanism for reducing industrial emissions in the union through an economic logic. from the outset we have criticised this economic mechanism which subjects the environment to the logic of the market. with the current economic and financial crisis, coupled with a significant flow of external emission reduction credits from the clean development mechanism (cdm) and the restricted provisions related to the transition to a third trading period, there has been a surplus of allowances undermining the functioning of the system, demonstrating the unsustainability of the mechanism. that is why we voted against it.
in writing. − this report was intended to amend directive 2003/87/ec establishing a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the community (eu ghg ets) in an attempt to circumvent a problem caused by the accumulation of an excess of 955 million emission allowances at the end of 2011. as the allocation of licences is much higher than demand, the price of carbon has fallen significantly. it is a consequence of the operation of this perverse and ineffective mechanism (ets/carbon market). the problem to be solved is structural, it has to do with the emissions trading scheme itself, with its principles and (market) foundations, and it cannot be solved by a cosmetic operation such as the one now attempted.
in writing. - i support this report, which proposes to derogate from the eu ets directive so that action is not taken against aviation operators who do not comply with the requirements of this directive for non-european flights. i think it is essential at this time that the european union gives space for international negotiations to reach an agreement based on a global market mechanism for the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from international aviation. i also agree that if such an agreement is not approved by september 2013, the eu ets should be applied against international flights.
in writing. - i agree with the proposed changes to the greenhouse gas emission allowance trading scheme so that european airlines are not put at a disadvantage compared to their competitors on the market outside the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the 'greenhouse gas emission allowance trading scheme', considering that the derogation from the application of this scheme to intercontinental flights by september 2013 will facilitate the negotiation of a global agreement to reduce aviation emissions within the international civil aviation organisation.
in writing. − although the aviation sector is currently responsible for around 3% of total greenhouse gas emissions, these have been increasing, with the international civil aviation organisation (icao) estimating that co2 emissions from the aviation sector have almost doubled between 1990 and 2006. the icao also forecasts an increase of 63 to 88% by 2020, during which time the european union has committed to reducing emissions by 20% compared to 1990 levels. however, and despite the fact that in 2008 the eu decided to include aviation in the eu ets, the truth is that any regulation on this matter has to be on a global scale, otherwise it will not be applicable. therefore, and with a view to a more comprehensive agreement, i am voting in favour of the proposal to exclude intercontinental flights from the eu ets for emissions during 2012.
in writing. − in 2008, the european parliament and the council of ministers agreed, after a long and careful consideration, to include aviation in the eu ets. this was because of the need to address the rapidly growing greenhouse gas emissions in this sector. since 1990, greenhouse gas emissions from the aviation sector have increased by about 100%. failure to address emissions from the aviation sector would also be inconsistent and unfair to other industries and other modes of transport that are subject to regulation in the eu and member states. in 1997, the international civil aviation organization (icao) was given the task of regulating emissions from the aviation sector. it is therefore very important to reach an agreement in the international civil aviation organization (icao), as this will be the best option for everyone, including the european union. i therefore agree to suspend the application of the eu ets to intercontinental flights for one year in order to facilitate this agreement.
in writing. − the inclusion of aviation in the eu emissions trading scheme (eu ets) in 2008 is part of the response to the rapid growth of greenhouse gas emissions associated with this sector, evidenced by the fact that they have increased by 100% since 1990, the base year of the kyoto protocol. this report aims to respond to the very strong negative reactions, both from china and the us, to the measures taken by the eu in this area. following these reactions, a process was initiated within icao with a view to reaching a multilateral agreement. it is expected that this agreement will be reached by the end of this year. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's aviation sector is not excluded from the eu ets. although we believe that it would be appropriate to seek solutions to this problem in a multilateral forum, our position in principle on the market approach which has prevailed in tackling climate change (and the prospect that it will not be changed in the main) has led us to vote against this report.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of radioactive waste in the transport of dangerous goods. suspension within the european union shall not be an option for more than one year and may not be extended beyond 31 december 2013. what is not clear in the compromise is its results. for these reasons and because of the cosmetic of the surplus value of these subsidies being paid on 30 april 2013, thus covering the year 2012, the very year when the carbon price was low (between 6 and 8 euros) and when airlines can use up to 15% of the credits of the clean development mechanism (which is around 0,4 euros), we decided not to support and that is why we abstained.
in writing. - since the kyoto protocol, co2 emissions from the aviation sector have grown exponentially. this issue therefore needs to be addressed, as other industries are coming up with more stringent emission reduction criteria. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the creation of a scheme for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading in the community. the commission proposal makes it clear that it is not the eu that is standing in the way of an international agreement on aviation emissions. if, even after the adoption of this proposal, third countries do not make a genuine commitment at the level of the international civil aviation organisation (icao), this is an unequivocal sign that those who call for an international solution within icao are not genuinely committed. however, an agreement reached by icao will be the best option for all, including the european union.
in writing. − in light of the icao council decision of 9 november 2012, the european commission has announced a proposal to suspend the application of the eu greenhouse gas emission allowance trading scheme to international flights. the rapporteur welcomes the commission proposal and proposes a derogation from directive 2003/87/ec for a maximum period of one year, with the decision to be drafted in a precise manner, leaving no room for secondary interpretations. in order to ensure legal certainty, it is vital to explicitly list the requirements covered for the purpose of the derogation and the number and type of licences that air operators must surrender in order to benefit from the derogation. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the suspension cannot therefore be extended beyond 31 december 2012, when the eu expects to be able to sign an international agreement to reduce co2 emissions.
in writing. − the inclusion of aviation in the eu emissions trading system (eu ets) in 2008 is part of the response to the rapid growth of greenhouse gas emissions associated with this sector. this report aims to respond to the very strong negative reactions, both from china and the us, to the measures taken by the eu in this area. following these reactions, a process was initiated within icao with a view to reaching a multilateral agreement. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's aviation sector is not excluded from the eu ets. although we believe that it would be appropriate to seek solutions to this problem in a multilateral forum, our position in principle on the market approach which has prevailed in tackling climate change (and the prospect that it will not be changed in the main) has led us to vote against this report.
in writing. - i approve this report, given that the proposal is a piece of legislation which aims to strengthen the regulation of the banking sector. despite the delay of the trilogue which lasted three presidencies, i welcome this legislative proposal which covers all the main aspects of the banking sector, and in particular, at this time of widespread economic and financial crisis throughout the european union, the issue of bonuses, capital liquidity, differentiation and flexibility in respect of financial instruments. with this proposal we are moving towards a more just and equitable governance for citizens, paying particular attention to the fact that the responsiveness of banking institutions to market needs is vital for the resumption of growth.
in writing. − at a time when europe is seen as the epicentre of an economic crisis with increasingly devastating social, business and political effects, this legislation strengthens the capacity of the banking sector to restructure and respond to the current challenges, but for which europe is beginning to find clear answers. this report, together with the report on prudential requirements for credit institutions and investment firms, proposes a reform of the banking sector, commonly known as the 'cdr4 package'. its objective is to strengthen the regulation and stability of the banking sector so that it can actively contribute to the promotion of economic growth. the commission directive in question regulates banks' access to deposit-holding activities and provides for the supervision and evaluation of the activity of banking institutions and investment firms. this report is a good contribution to the production of appropriate legislation and to the improvement of the functioning of the european banking sector. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - as we know, the financial crisis we are experiencing was triggered by the perversion of values underlying the financial sector. obviously, the banks are not the only ones to blame. human greed and lack of proper oversight have created the conditions for this. the banks that had the most speculative products were the ones that made the most money. at this time of accountability and precautionary measures, the financial sector needs to assume its responsibilities for self-monitoring and recapitalisation if it is to regain investor confidence. however, it cannot be the citizens who pay all the costs of the crisis, including the cost of banking. i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on access to the activity of credit institutions and the prudential supervision of credit institutions and investment firms and amending directive 2002/87/ec of the european parliament and of the council on the supplementary supervision of credit institutions, insurance undertakings and investment firms in a financial conglomerate, because it is essential to increase the credibility of the financial sector through greater transparency.
in writing. − the essential objective of this directive is to facilitate freedom of establishment and freedom to provide services in the financial sector, with a view to deepening the single banking market and the free movement of capital. the harmonisation of national provisions on access to the activity of credit institutions and investment firms is introduced, the powers of the member states in regulating the financial sector are restricted, and the role of supranational organisations such as the european banking authority and the european commission itself is strengthened. countries such as portugal are thus even more limited in their ability to act in this strategic sector, being obliged to authorise the establishment of a bank or a bank branch irrespective of its economic need. one consequence will be the favouring of the financial sector by the great powers, such as germany - the banking giants who in this way seek to take over sectors which they have not dominated until now, destroying some more competitors to restore their profit rates. this legislation is clearly contrary to the national interest of countries like portugal, where the solution to the country's problems requires the nationalisation of commercial banking with a view to financing the real economy and placing it at the service of development and social progress.
in writing. − directive 2006/48/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 14 june 2006 relating to the taking up and pursuit of the business of credit institutions contains rules relating to the coordination of national provisions on the taking up and pursuit of the business of credit institutions and on the supervisory framework for credit institutions (in particular provisions governing the authorisation of business, the exercise of the freedom of establishment, the powers of the supervisory authorities of home and host member states in this field and the supervisory procedure for credit institutions). however, the financial crisis that has hit the eu has led to the need to amend this directive. the proposal contains the following new elements: provisions on sanctions, effective corporate governance and provisions to avoid excessive reliance on external credit ratings. that's why i'm in favour.
in writing. - i voted for the karas report on the directive on access to and supervision of credit institutions, which i consider to be one of the most important laws passed in this parliament. this directive is only overdue, 20 years too late. if it had been adopted at the beginning of the creation of the single market for financial services, it is very likely that the 2008 crisis would not have had the devastating impact it had on the financial sector in general and the banking sector in particular. the union is also responsible, by inertia, for the depth of the crisis, having failed to create an integrated banking system without a single system of rules at union level and without centralised supervision at the same level, instead of fragmented supervision in the 27 member states of the union. better late than never, but a preventive union action could have saved taxpayers a lot of money in bailing out banks and mitigated the recession and unemployment that so many member states are suffering from.
in writing. − the review of access to the activity of credit institutions and the prudential supervision of credit institutions and investment firms and amending directive 2002/87/ec of the european parliament and of the council on the supplementary supervision of credit institutions, insurance undertakings and investment firms in a financial conglomerate aims to ensure a diversified and sustainable eu banking culture that is primarily in the interests of the people and in this respect encourages small-scale banking activities such as mutual credit institutions and cooperative banks. i particularly agree with the points made and therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − the purpose of this directive is to give expression to the so-called freedom of establishment and the freedom to provide services in the financial sector, with a view to the deepening of the internal market and the free movement of capital. the harmonisation of national provisions on access to the activity of credit institutions and investment firms is established, the powers of the member states in regulating the financial sector are restricted, and the role of supranational organisations such as the european banking authority and the european commission itself is strengthened in harmonising and enforcing national powers and practices. countries such as portugal are thus even more restricted in their ability to act in this important sector, being obliged to allow the establishment of a bank or a bank branch irrespective of its economic need. this is a symptom of a trend which, in the wake of harmonization, is aimed at favouring the great powers such as germany and their financial sector. it is the predominance of the country of origin principle in the regulation of the sector, which will favour the already favoured banking giants who in this way seek to take over sectors which they have not dominated until now, destroying some more competitors to restore their profit rates. this legislation is clearly contrary to the national interest of countries like portugal.
in writing. − i approve this report, considering that for reasons of legal certainty and due to the need for a level playing field in the union, a single regulatory body for all market participants is a key element for the functioning of the internal market. in order to avoid market distortions and regulatory arbitrage, the first pillar measures should ensure maximum harmonisation. consequently, the transitional periods granted in this regulation are essential for the smooth implementation of this regulation and to avoid uncertainty for the markets. member states and competent authorities shall avoid adopting any divergent or dominant rules which have an impact on or undermine the principle of maximum harmonisation under the first pillar. competent authorities should be able to assess, within the applicable second pillar procedures, whether supervisory action is necessary in relation to a particular credit institution or a group of credit institutions.
in writing. − this legislation, drawing lessons from the economic crisis which is shaking europe, will provide the european financial sector with the mechanisms and foundations essential to prevent future crises, and will equip the union with the means to promote a more dynamic and stable economy. this report, together with the report on access by banks to deposit-taking activities and the assessment and supervision of the activities of banking institutions, proposes a reform of the banking sector, commonly referred to as the 'cdr4 package'. its objective is to strengthen the regulation and stability of the banking sector and its active contribution to the promotion of economic growth. the commission regulation lays down the prudential requirements to be met by institutions. capital requirements shall be appropriate and of high quality, ensuring the risk coverage of the activity of financial institutions. they should be coordinated at union rather than national level in order to ensure cohesion, stability and soundness in the functioning of the banking system. this report makes a good contribution to building a more solid banking sector, protected from any atypical shocks in the way the business operates. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - we are facing a regulatory reform of the banking sector which has been largely determined by the financial sector itself. this is shown by the history of this process and its final result - welcomed by the major european banks. moreover, this is another blow to national sovereignty and the possibility of developing this sector in the sense of its usefulness for the real economy and the needs of countries such as portugal. the intention is to promote an even greater concentration and centralisation of wealth in the big banks - giant clay-foot banks that continue to have the states dependent on them for credit and that continue to benefit themselves from the cheap credit provided by the ecb, thus extorting the national resources of countries like portugal. the containment of the growth of leverage in the banking system and the development of more robust liquidity buffers is set as the ultimate objective, but this is nothing more than a hypocritical statement aimed at masking the subjecting of the entire sector to the same rules, seeking to eliminate those that in some cases still defended - or had the potential to defend - the national specificity of each country and the financing needs of the real economy to which banks should be bound.
in writing. − the scale of the financial crisis has raised the alarm about unacceptable risks in the regulation of financial institutions. according to imf estimates, crisis-related losses incurred by european credit institutions between 2007 and 2010 are close to eur 1 trillion, corresponding to 8% of eu gdp. in order to safeguard stability and not to break the flow of credit to the economy, several measures were adopted with the costs of these to be borne by the taxpayers. the proposal proposes reforms in the sector to fill the regulatory gaps exposed by the crisis. we cannot repeat the mistakes of the past, much less impose the costs of those mistakes on the taxpayers. we must act on new prudential practices for credit institutions and investment firms.

in writing. - i welcome this report, stressing that the opening up of the market for groundhandling services in the eu must be balanced, as full liberalisation could lead to a greater degree of instability, forcing an increasing number of groundhandling service providers to leave the sector. the service companies are the backbone of air transport, so an unstable service market would lead to repeated disruptions at europe's airports as well as to significant temporary reductions in normal working hours, so-called 'lay-offs'. however, in the long term, full liberalisation could lead to the oligopoly at european level of a small number of remaining scale-up companies. such an oligopoly would be contrary to the interests of airlines, workers and passengers and would have a negative effect on competition, growth and jobs.
in writing. − ground handling services cover all ground activities (at airports) related to aviation. the revenue generated amounts to some eur 50 billion and employs more than 60,000 people in europe. the efficient provision of these services is essential for airports, air carriers, passengers and also for the optimal use of air transport infrastructure and for the performance of the aviation system in general. in view of the successive crises affecting air transport, the rapid growth of air traffic, the increase in the number of air carriers and the increasing capacity constraints at airports, it became necessary to replace the 1996 directive, which at the time constituted a first step towards the progressive opening and harmonisation of access to the groundhandling market. i believe that the opening up of the market for ground handling services in the eu must be balanced, which is why i support the commitments proposed by the rapporteur, which should allow airlines greater choice, better coordination of ground handling services at airports, and a substantial improvement in the social rights of workers as well as the essential rights of passengers.

in writing. − the ground handling services are crucial for the smooth operation of airports. there are eleven categories of ground handling services: (1) ground administration and supervision, (2) passenger handling, (3) baggage handling, (4) cargo and mail handling, (5) runway operations, (6) aircraft cleaning and servicing, (7) fuel and oil handling, (8) in-line maintenance, (9) air operations and crew management, (10) ground transportation and (11) catering. the provision of these services represents a revenue of eur 50 billion and employs 60,000 people in europe. i am not a strong advocate of protectionist policies and tend to support the liberalisation of markets, since i believe that competition is generally synonymous with a higher quality of service and a higher level of satisfaction for the end-customer, in this case the passenger. in this sense, i am in favour of the commission's proposal to liberalize this market.
in writing. − air passenger traffic rose exponentially in the first decade of this century thanks to increased purchasing power of citizens, longer life spans and, above all, the emergence of low-cost airlines. however, we cannot say that the massive increase in access to air transport has been accompanied by improvements in the 11 ground handling services at airports. the report under consideration, by artur zasada, on behalf of the committee on transport and tourism, concerns the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on groundhandling services at union airports and repealing council directive 96/67/ec. this is a market which, according to the commission, employs more than 60,000 people in the european union alone and generates revenue of some eur 50 billion. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that increasing competition from two to three operators will improve their efficiency and bring significant advantages to all passengers, not only in reducing waiting time both at check-in and boarding and at baggage claim but also in the loss of baggage.
in writing. - what was foreseen from the beginning of this process has been fulfilled: by saying what has not been said, social democracy once again fulfils its role and approves what it rejected a few months ago, under the pressure of the workers' struggle. this is another step in the process of liberalising the airport handling services sector. the commitment now reached provides for the possibility of a third ground handling operator for large airports with an annual traffic of more than 15 million passengers and 200 000 tonnes of cargo in the last 3 years. the consequences of this process of liberalization are well known to workers: loss of rights, degradation of wages and precariousness of working conditions. more liberalization, increased competition between firms and the race to reduce costs are the ingredients for the deepening of this path: the increasing degradation of working conditions, the reduction of jobs, higher requirements for workers and the weakening of passenger safety conditions. for the record, and so that workers in the sector know who is attacking their rights, the final vote on this report was supported by the ps, psd and cds.

in writing. − the european commission presented on 1 december 2012 a draft regulation on groundhandling services replacing directive 96/67/ec. the regulation aims to reduce delays and improve the quality of services for passengers. the commission proposes that these objectives be achieved by liberalising the market for shuttle services by granting market access to at least one independent third party. however, on the one hand, the ecorys study concludes that the first opening to the market increased job insecurity, and on the other hand, figures presented by eu trade unions point out that wages associated with services have fallen short of inflation and average developments. in addition to this reading of the facts, there is a lack of data relating to delays specifically to groundhandling services, weakening the legal basis of the proposals for regulations. the rapporteur warns that the marginalisation and precariousness of workers and the insecurity of the population are at the heart of attempts at liberalisation. i voted in favour, in the hope that an agreement will be reached which enshrines the rights of workers to protection and guarantees a maximum level of quality and safety.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the main objective of the proposal is to establish a ban on returns in the skagerrak. the current order, whereby in some cases very large parts of the total catch are returned to the sea, is probably the aspect of the common fisheries policy that is the most difficult for the general public to understand and support. the fact that perfectly usable fish is thrown overboard at a time when we are having a hard time feeding the world's population is considered incomprehensible and even immoral. the proposal lays down a landing obligation and the supporting rules necessary to monitor and inspect compliance with that obligation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on 'technical and control measures in the skagerrak' because it provides for measures to establish a ban on discards in the skagerrak and the obligation to land all fish, as well as the supporting rules necessary to monitor and inspect compliance with this obligation, in particular through electronic remote control systems.
in writing. − the diversity of marine species in the skagerrak and the need to regulate fishing activities there make it necessary to harmonise the technical and control measures applied by the union and norway. i hope that they strike the right balance between the interests of ecosystems and fishermen, so as to ensure the sustainability of their way of life and the protection of the natural resources underlying it.
in writing. - since 1986, eu fishing fleets have been fishing in norwegian waters in the skagerrat, the strait between southern norway and north-west denmark. however, following a complaint by norway, eu vessels have been prohibited from fishing in this area as from 1 november 2012. the negotiations were concluded on 2/12/2011, as stated in the minutes approved by the eu and norway at the meeting held in bergen. this document 'includes improvements to the control and enforcement measures applicable to fisheries in the skagerrak and recommends ways of harmonising eu and norwegian regulations on technical and control measures in the area beyond the 4 nautical miles calculated from the baselines'. i voted in favour of this report and hope that it will enter into force no later than 1 january 2014, because people do not understand how it is possible, at a time when so much is being said about the new common fisheries policy and, above all, about sustainable fishing, that fish is still being returned in good condition for human consumption at a time of global crisis when millions of people are undernourished.
in writing. - the skagerrak is a relatively small sea, with a limited number of countries having fishing interests. however, this report has acquired added importance because, due to the obligation to land all catches made in any eu fishery, provided for in the reform of the common fisheries policy under way, the measures proposed in this regulation, which go in this direction, although specific to the skagerrak sea, may become a precedent when applying the landing obligation measure. while we can generally agree with the commission proposal and the amendments tabled by the committee on fisheries, we cannot support article 11, which goes further with the compulsory installation on board of a cctv video system for the purpose of monitoring fishing activities. in our view, neither the commission's proposal nor the rapporteur's proposal even safeguards the complete exclusion of small-scale fishing from this obligation. given the specificities of this fishery, in technical and financial terms, the installation of cctv on board would be quite complicated and costly.
in writing. − the main objective of this proposal is to establish a ban on returns in the skagerrak. the current order, whereby in some cases very large parts of the total catch are returned to the sea, is probably the aspect of the common fisheries policy that is the most difficult for the general public to understand and support. the proposal lays down a landing obligation and the supporting rules necessary to monitor and inspect compliance with that obligation. we must maintain a balanced management of marine resources. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the purpose of this report is to review regulations (ec) no 850/98 and (ec) no 1342/2008 concerning certain technical and control measures in the fisheries in the skagerrak. the establishment of a working group on fishing in the skagerrak made a number of suggestions for improving technical measures and control of fishing activity and recommended the harmonisation of the european union and norwegian regulations in this field. the main purpose of this proposal is to introduce changes in the regulations currently in force, aimed at reducing the level of unwanted catches and discards, which negatively affect the sustainable exploitation of fishery resources in the skagerrak. in the context of the measures envisaged in the ongoing reform of the common fisheries policy, this proposal lays down the obligation to land all catches and the rules to support the monitoring and inspection of compliance with this regulation, and proposes the installation of an electronic remote monitoring system (rem) in the fishing fleet operating in the skagerrak. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the general approach to the proposals put forward and because i believe that the measures suggested will promote a balanced and sustainable exploitation of local fisheries resources.
in writing. the main objective of the proposed regulation is to introduce technical modifications in order to reduce the level of discards and unwanted catches, which negatively affect the sustainable exploitation of marine biological resources in the skagerrak strait. the proposal lays down an obligation to land all fish caught subject to catch limits and also lays down provisions on the treatment of juvenile catches. it is proposed that member states operating in the skagerrak install and use an electronic remote control system which replaces the traditional processing of video images transmitted to the central authority responsible for managing the system with a system for automatic recognition of information, ensuring that no fish of the species listed in annex i leaves the fishing vessel.

in writing. − i support this proposal, which aims to assess the consequences and the extent to which directive 2004/113/ec is applied in the member states, to identify existing gaps and to recommend possible solutions to fill them. the importance of reliable information and data should be emphasised. the commission needs to be more transparent in its ongoing infringement procedures and in the measures taken. the creation of a public database of legislation and case law relating to gender discrimination can be an instrument to improve the protection of victims of such discrimination. i also believe that, in view of the role played by national courts, the use of eu financial support and coordination to provide continuous training for legal practitioners working in this field is also an essential condition for the effective implementation of the directive.
in writing. - since 1957, the principle of equality between men and women has been enshrined in the treaty establishing the european community, requiring equal pay for equal work. in this context, directive 2004/113/ec prohibits any discrimination on grounds of sex in the access to and supply of goods and services. article 5 (2) however provides for a derogation from the unisex premium and benefit rule for insurance and other financial services. this derogation has been declared invalid by the court of justice of the european union as being contrary to the objective of equal treatment between men and women and incompatible with the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. the judgment of the court of justice of the european union also states that differentiations in premiums and benefits resulting from the use of sex as a determining factor in the calculation of these should be abolished. i therefore voted in favour of this report which calls on the european commission to present a summary report on the application of this directive and to propose a new legislative text with binding guidelines in order to eliminate legal uncertainties in this area.
in writing. − equality between men and women is one of the eu's objectives, which we have sought to achieve by adopting the necessary legislation, mainstreaming a gender perspective in all eu policies and promoting specific actions. directive 2004/113/ec of 13 december 2004 implementing the principle of equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services was the first legal instrument to implement the principle of equal treatment between men and women outside the labour market. although this directive should have been transposed by the end of 2007, not all member states have done so, or at least not fully. we also continue to await the report on its implementation, which should have been submitted by the commission by the end of 2010. moreover, the derogation provided for in article 5 (2) of that directive was declared invalid by the ecj (test-achats judgment), which has resulted in legal uncertainty which cannot be addressed by guidelines but by the adoption of a new legislative instrument. it is also important to take the necessary measures to strengthen the effectiveness of some equality bodies, in particular with regard to their capacity to act, the shortage of staff and the lack of adequate financial resources.
in writing. - the principle of equality is one of the pillars of democratic states governed by the rule of law. it is because i believe in the importance of this principle that i understand that men and women deserve equal opportunities and must have equal rights in the access to and supply of goods and services.
in writing. - the issue of gender equality has never been so promoted as it is now. if in europe, with the exception of the eastern countries, and in many established democracies, women have long been treated as equals from a legal point of view, the truth is that in the young democracies and in countries where human rights are not respected, there is still much to be done in this matter. at european level, we continue to find that in practice there is not always equal treatment between men and women, particularly in terms of access to and supply of goods and services, as enshrined in council directive 2004/113/ec, and it is therefore necessary to verify whether all member states (ms) have transposed and implemented it. on 8 march this parliament adopted several directives on gender equality, but we continue to see cases of discrimination on the grounds of maternity or access to credit. i voted in favour of the report drawn up by my colleague zita gurmai, not only because of the judgment of the court of justice of the european union on this matter, but also because i think that all politicians have an obligation to defend gender equality in its entirety.
in writing. − the committee on women's rights and gender equality decided to draw up this report following the judgment of the court of justice of the european union of march 2011 which found that article 5 (2) of directive 2004/113/ec, which provides for a derogation from insurance and related financial services, is contrary to the achievement of the objective of equal treatment between men and women and is incompatible with the eu charter of fundamental rights. in other words, we are talking about the non-application of the directive when it comes to differentiated insurance premiums on the basis of sex, forcing women to pay more in private pension schemes. we agree with the report's view that there should be no exceptions in this matter. discrimination in relation to pregnancy, maternity planning and maternity, access to housing, access to loans and access to medical goods and services is also inadmissible. it is important to stress that discrimination affecting women in access to goods and services is increasing rapidly at the most fundamental level of purchasing power and choice.
in writing. − directive 2004/113/ec, which applies the principle of equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services, represented an important step towards the development of gender equality legislation in the eu when it came into force on 21 december 2004. the objective of this report is to assess the impact and extent of the application of directive 2004/113/ec in the member states, to identify existing gaps and to recommend possible solutions to close them. the importance of reliable information and data should be emphasised. the commission needs to be more transparent in its ongoing infringement procedures and in the measures taken. the creation of a public database of legislation and case law relating to gender discrimination can be an instrument to improve the protection of victims of such discrimination. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the transposition and application of council directive 2004/113/ec applying the principle of equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services, as it is broadly in line with what it states.
in writing. − this report assesses the consequences and extent of application of directive 2004/113/ec, which has been in force since 21 december 2004. member states were required to transpose the directive by 21 december 2007 and the european commission was required to prepare a report to assess its application by 21 december 2010. the directive applies the principle of equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services. however, the consideration of gender as a factor in the calculation of premiums and benefits for insurance and other financial services resulted, until the implementation of the directive, in a differentiation for insured persons. a derogation from the general rule gave member states the possibility to allow proportionate differentiation in premiums where consideration of sex was a determining factor in the risk assessment. this derogation, which was granted without any time limit, was considered by the court to be contrary to the objective of achieving equality of treatment between men and women and was therefore declared invalid. i voted in favour of the report, which proposes that legal certainty be promoted in the future by means of clear and unequivocal provisions.
in writing. − the committee on women's rights and gender equality decided to draw up this report following the judgment of the court of justice of the european union of 1 march 2011 in case c-236/09 which found that article 5 (2) of this directive (2004/113/ec), which provides for a derogation from insurance and related financial services, is contrary to the achievement of the objective of equal treatment between men and women and is incompatible with the eu charter of fundamental rights. in other words, we are talking about the non-application of the directive when it comes to differentiated insurance premiums on the basis of sex, forcing women to pay more in private pension schemes. we agree with the report's view that there should be no exceptions in this matter. discrimination in relation to pregnancy, maternity planning and maternity is also inadmissible as regards differentiations in access to housing leases, loans and access to medical goods and services. it is important to stress that discrimination affecting women in access to goods and services is increasing rapidly at the most fundamental level of purchasing power and choice.
in writing. - i welcome this report, considering that the trade sector is one of the most important areas of action from the point of view of eu policy coherence in a development perspective (dpc). if used correctly, trade policy instruments can have a considerable impact on the development of poor countries. the eu's trade policy towards developing countries must aim primarily at promoting and strengthening the results of our development aid policy. promoting development worldwide, even by means other than aid, preserves the eu's core values and respects its treaty obligations. to be more effective in meeting development objectives, eu trade policy should aim to have a positive impact on local, regional and national economies, to promote the diversification of developing countries' economies and to encourage measures aimed at more advanced and income-generating production. the application of higher customs duties on processed products than on raw materials risks contributing to the failure of developing countries to break free from the role of mere exporters of raw materials.
in writing. − the trade sector is one of the most important areas of action from the point of view of the coherence of the european union's policies in a development perspective. trade policy instruments can have a considerable impact on the development of poor countries. the main objective of the eu's trade policy towards developing countries should be to promote and reinforce the results of our development aid policy. to be most effective, eu trade policy must have a positive impact on local, regional and national economies. good governance is fundamental to a country's ability to develop and benefit from trade. the european union should, through its trade policy, contribute to the introduction of good governance, not tolerating corrupt regimes, and requiring transparency and proper procedures before cooperation is initiated, as well as negotiating the inclusion of enforceable human rights provisions in all future bilateral trade and cooperation agreements. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − the eu's trade policy, when applied in a coherent and effective manner, is inextricably linked to improving conditions in developing countries. to this end, the impact of trade agreements on local and regional economies should be taken into account in the formulation of trade agreements, by encouraging production and access to globalisation by developing countries in order to reach out to more advanced and income-generating societies and not just simple exporters of raw materials. despite the progress made in the coordination of development policies in the eu, i would point out that much remains to be done, and that the development dimension of international investment agreements needs to be strengthened and the full balance between the rights and obligations of states and investors ensured. i welcome the commission's proposal to differentiate its aid to trade and to focus its attention on the countries most in need, in particular the ldcs and low-income countries, as well as the package of incentives announced by the european commission for small farms in the developing countries. i also think it is important to stress that results in this area will only be achieved if there is a policy of good governance and efficient use of resources by the recipient countries.
in writing. - history shows that no country has achieved long-term sustainable growth without openness to trade and policies to promote and complement it. the positive contribution of trade and investment to the growth and development of countries and regions is also irrevocable. i therefore vote in favour of this report. i would remind you that the eu's trade policy (tp) has clear development objectives and is guided by full respect for the principles of eu external action. i therefore regard pc and aid as complementary vectors in the eu's approach to developing countries. i recognise that the korea free trade agreement (kfta) is a pioneering approach that the eu intends to print in all its future kftas. but my experience as rapporteur for the eu-colombia/peru joint committee tells me that trade relations with developing countries require a different approach and stance than we take in economically equal negotiations, such as with korea. in developing countries, these agreements are powerful tools capable of generating many positive expectations and synergies, as they allow for greater bilateral involvement of the various parties (governments, businesses, civil society) in the implementation and monitoring of the agreement.

in writing. − the trade sector is an important area of action for eu policies from a development incentive (dip) perspective. trade policy instruments can have a significant impact on the development of the poorest countries. the eu's trade policy towards developing countries should therefore be directed towards promoting and reinforcing the results of development aid policy. the eu must play an active role in reducing poverty in developing countries. this can be done by formulating trade agreements that allow developing countries to participate in the international economy and benefit from the advantages of globalisation.

in writing. - another report linking eu trade policy with development cooperation policy. the report does, however, admit, although timidly, some of the consequences of the liberalization and deregulation of international trade for developing countries. it recognises that the integration of these countries into the international trading system, within the framework of these policies, may destroy local production and increase dependence on exports. however, instead of questioning this path and defending its reversal, he says that it has not been pursued in the best way: liberalization is not done in a moderate and gradual way, in line with the development of their productive capacities and they must make progress towards a structural transformation. this is unacceptable! the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally sound. a social and environmental touch that does not call into question the essence of these free trade agreements. but there are several positive aspects in the report: from the call for the abolition of agricultural export subsidies, to the recognition of the right of acp countries to impose restrictions on the export of raw materials, among others.

the rapporteur. - madam president, this report is the result of a long and difficult process of conciliation. i therefore thank the rapporteurs who have helped us to have such a clear position today. the role of the parliament is fundamental to the definition of european policies. i think it has been exercised inadequately. as representatives of the citizens we cannot fail to echo their concerns. to ignore them would be to add to the economic crisis a crisis of democratic legitimacy. the european parliament has a clear position on the direction the ecb is taking in the face of the widening economic recession and unemployment in the euro area, with debts growing rather than resolving. the ecb's mandate: when it comes to assessing the consequences of its monetary policy, the mandate has been defined as narrowly as possible. the ecb's mandate is defined as flexibly as possible, if not creatively, when it comes to justifying its participation in adjustment programmes, which include fiscal policy measures, structural reforms, privatisation programmes, etc. let 's be clear: the ecb's mission was defined by the political institutions, it is not written in the stars and it was not defined by the ecb itself. mr. draghi, tell us something, please: who authorized you to overstep the bounds of your mandate by, for example, defining the troika's programmes? some people believe that the independence of the ecb should prevent parliament from making any criticism of its actions. interestingly, for them, praise of the ecb is no longer a matter of independence, i.e. they think that parliament should praise when the ecb does well and keep silent when the ecb does badly or, worse still, there seem to be those who believe, against all evidence, that the ecb is infallible. much of the discussion we have had has been simply to erase any criticism of the ecb as if it were not the right and duty of parliament to give voice to the concerns of those who elected it about the course that has been taken and its consequences. tomorrow this parliament will not only vote on monetary and economic policy options, but also on whether or not we want to have a critical judgment on the performance of an institution as central to european policy as the ecb. let us consider some examples. the report praises the ecb for its decision to cut interest rates in the face of the economic backdrop, but when it comes to criticising an earlier decision to raise interest rates, some on the right have proposed to justify what was a gross monetary policy mistake. we think that mistakes should be clearly identified so that they are not repeated. the ecb has also been a key player in the adjustment programmes. these programmes are not only failing all their targets - growth, unemployment, deficit, debt - they are spreading the recession increasingly to eurozone countries, undermining the very effects of the expansionary monetary policy that the ecb has finally taken on. the ecb's double standards in the financing rules are therefore incomprehensible. it imposes draconian and counterproductive adjustment programmes on the states, it grants banks cheap financing, five times cheaper and without conditions, not even the imposition of minimum credit to the real economy, which remains at absolutely insufficient levels. the ecb has admitted in its own report of activities that it has made significant gains at the expense of the troika programmes, but there are those in this house who insist that this is not in the report of parliament and that it will not accept something as reasonable as the return of these profits to the countries to relieve the burden of the citizens who are paying them. the amendments tabled by the ppe have three main objectives: to make the evaluation of parliament a harmless exercise, to eliminate the possibility of greater transparency and accountability and to glorify the rhetoric of austerity. the questions at issue here are decisive: the limits of the ecb's mandate, democratic control and transparency now define an important part of the european political system. a regime in which a single power exercises an unlimited and self-defined mandate, without democratic control, without obligations of transparency, has a name: dictatorship. if parliament becomes irrelevant, it would allow a dictatorship of the ecb. and i conclude, madam president, by saying: the mandate on the ecb divides us because it is our lives we are talking about. this report is constructive, it proposes alternatives to get us out of the crisis, it praises and corrects, but it also criticises the ecb, because the choice we have to make is simple: we want a ecb that serves the economy and society and not financial speculation.
he asks under the blue card procedure. mr langen, in relation to what you have said, namely that we cannot extend the mandate of the ecb beyond the treaties, and i think you are referring to what is in the report, to include the objectives of growth and job creation in addition to the objective of price stability, i would like to ask you whether we cannot do that, whether we cannot even make that assessment? when did you vote for the amendment and extension of the mandate of the ecb, namely to become part of the troika, when did you vote for it? the fellow, me and all of us? because i don't remember! if we can't make references to one side, we can't make references to the other. i would like to know when you voted for this, when you accepted, with a light heart, that it cannot be extended to some things but that it should be extended to others, without us even being able to question it!
commissioner, mr president of the ecb, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to begin this debate by thanking the various rapporteurs for their work, and i hope that a solution can be found which is balanced and moderate. i would also like to pay a very special tribute to mr draghi for the great efforts he has made during his term of office and for the positive results that have been felt since the beginning with regard to the sovereign debt market. i also cannot leave here a note of strangeness about the fact that we are in april 2013 discussing the 2011 report of the european central bank, it is something that we should certainly change. the european central bank has historically played an important role in price stability. that's what the treaties say. that's what the bylaws say, too. with the crisis, it has had major interventions in the secondary debt market and a greater role for banking supervision is foreseen in the future. it's important to end a cycle that has been bad for companies, banks, states and that has been hindering growth. that's why i wanted to leave two or three notes: mr president of the european central bank, how do you see, within a framework of revision of the treaties, an extension of the powers of the european central bank so that it can intervene more, for example, in the debt market, beyond what is already determined? secondly, since the european commission and the european central bank are here, i cannot help but raise a question about some of the adjustment procedures. i belong to a state, portugal, which has fulfilled its obligations - and done so well. the european internal market is currently contracting. is it not time to review some of the economic objectives, for example in relation to the deficit, for those same countries? and thirdly, i would very much like to know what your position is on the question of bank deposits, and whether a clear word is not needed to reassure depositors in the various states?
i would like to begin this speech with three questions i would like to put to mr mario draghi. firstly, would it not be useful to amend the treaty so that the european central bank can finance the debt of the member states directly and at the same time incorporate the new responsibilities of the ecb resulting from the deepening of the union? at a time when the pernicious effects of the crisis and adjustment in some countries are calling for a wave of recovery and productive investment in europe, how do you foresee the transmission mechanisms of monetary policy actually being reflected in the provision of credit to firms which are ultimately the generators of growth and employment? and finally, what role does the ecb intend to play in this area? without funding for productive investment, without innovation, without the strong political will to change the status quo if necessary, we will not only fall short of the competitiveness we need, but also of the monetary union and the europe we want. the ecb's performance, and in particular that of the president, has been, it must be admitted, quite positive. however, i believe that the ecb should adopt an even stronger preventive stance towards stabilising the euro area, which would not be the result of a series of reactive isolated acts. the ecb, as the supervisor and guarantor of the liquidity needed for the sound functioning of the european economy, must be the engine and guarantor of a robust banking system. the loans that the ecb has been making should be accompanied by a clear incentive to use them to finance the real economy, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises. it is clear that credit institutions cannot be coerced into lending to the real economy without criteria, as the inflated leverage of the economy could trigger serious problems for the stability of the sector. however, this prudent financing must be based on the banks' ability to finance households and smes, otherwise it could have perverse, devastating effects, as the present economic crisis has shown.
madam president, mr president, mr commissioner, mr president of the central bank, i have commended you and thanked you for what you have done so far. i think it was your intervention that saved the euro. today i have two specific questions about another unconventional role of the european central bank, namely as a member of the troika, and in the short time i have i would like to put two very specific questions to you. first, last december the spanish minister of finance, luis de guindos, told the international press that europe's loan to spain would have, and i quote: a maturity of 12 and a half years, a grace period of ten years and an interest rate of less than 1% and that, at least in the first year, this rate would be very close to 0.5%. do you confirm these values and these deadlines? how do you explain, if that is so, that in countries like portugal, which is a compliant country, the rates are seven or ten times higher and the deadlines much more demanding? a second question on the profits from operations on the sovereign debt of the peripheral countries: they generated, as reported in the financial times, 14 billion euros. the value is, as is known, much higher and has been returned to greece by the shareholders who receive the profits made in these operations. have you proposed that the same practice could be extended to all the countries under the programme? in summary, i think there should be transparency in these processes and the best conditions granted to any member state should be extended to all the others. this seems to me to be the highest form of justice, countries are under the european umbrella, they are all under the programme. in the case of countries like mine, where austerity reaches unbearable limits, these movements would be a huge relief factor. please help me explain to the ordinary citizen, whose business, job or pension austerity has robbed, why this is not possible.
the rapporteur. - madam president, i would also like to thank the president of the european central bank, mr draghi, and the commissioner for their presence here and for all the comments made by my colleagues. we have a clear understanding of what unites us and what divides us, but i think we have enough material to reach agreement, at least there are central issues around which we must be united, in the name of what are the expectations of the citizens for whom we were elected. there is obviously agreement on a number of actions taken and carried out by the ecb, in particular in relation to the lowering of interest rates. that 's not what we 're talking about here . what we are talking about here is what changes can be made, what improvements can be made that are not in the ecb report and that are part of what we are here to represent the citizens for. i repeat: we are far from overcoming the crisis, we are still living in the crisis, and it is not by repeating it many times that the crisis will pass. that is why, when mr draghi comes here and talks so many times about the positive progress we have been seeing in the countries under intervention, he forgets some of the real data. he spoke several times about exports, in particular, that exports had increased after the troika's intervention. you better look at the latest statistics, because exports are declining again and it's because, with these austerity policies without any other form of approach, what we're going to have is an extension of austerity, of recession to the whole eurozone as we're already having, by the way, at this moment. and of course we cannot fail to mention that the positive evaluations of the intervention programmes have only come from the troika, and the better the evaluations, the worse the results. even the imf has already acknowledged that austerity and recession are not working. but going into what really brings us here, i just want to point out the important thing: even within the mandate of the ecb, which has been mentioned so much here, there are issues which we cannot accept and that is the proposal of this parliament. we must impose conditionality on banks that are subject to recapitalisation, we are talking about taxpayers' money, so we cannot expect them to inject money into the economy if they do not have some obligations when they do, towards small and mediumsized enterprises, towards households, putting this into practice is a matter of social justice. we must guarantee additional capital requirements for institutions that have benefited from the support of the ecb, we must be accountable to the ecb as a member of the troika, we must ask that the ecb not make profits at the expense of adjustment programmes, we must recognise the consequences of the recession on the sustainability of public accounts and finally, madam president, we must guarantee democracy, we cannot keep removing citizens from what are the most important decisions in vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i have heard with great interest the intervention of this parliament. the commission is waiting for the report of mr tavares and his group, which will come out in june. i think this very serious report will then be the basis for an informed debate in this house, leading maybe (depending on what the house decides) to conclusions which the house thinks it can draw from the very excellent work done by the parliamentarian. in general, in our democracy it is of course up to a member state to decide on the need for constitutional reform, but this reform has to be carried out with full respect for the values on which the eu is founded, in particular respect for the rule of law, and these are inscribed in our treaties and are not debatable. the treaties have not come out of the blue. they have been decided by all the countries together and in the charter of fundamental rights, which is the equivalent of a treaty. we also know from our treaties that, if the system of checks and balances required by democratic principle is at stake and there is a risk of serious breach of our values, then it is for europe to intervene. this is inscribed in article 7. this is a very strong article, and i agree with mrs harms that it is a kind of atom bomb which you have but which you think twice or three times about using. that is why i think we need to go beyond the specific situation and see what lessons we can draw from what we have discussed now and what we discussed all the other times we have been discussing these problems. the union needs a better-developed set of instruments in order to allow for better intervention if there are problems like the ones we have decided on today. i think we have all read the letter from several ministers of foreign affairs, who are calling for an intermediate instrument between article 7 on the one hand (the atomic bomb) and the infringement proceedings – the method which the commission has at its disposal in order to bring a country before the court of justice – on the other. i know there will be a discussion in the general council. we have heard from the minister that there will be a specialised conference on this topic in ireland, and i believe that the commission, as well as the european parliament, will work towards issuing of the report on proposals in that respect in june. the commission remains seriously concerned about the compatibility of the fourth amendment with the principle of the rule of law and will wait for the venice commission and the european parliament in june. it will make its contribution to the work that is under way on the basis of the treaties, by means of these two instruments. more specifically on what i have already put on the table: i did not only speak about the past two cases which we brought to the court, i also spoke about the analysis we have done on the fourth amendment, the legislation which comes out of the fourth amendment and the analysis we are doing at the moment on at least three elements of law in order to see if we can go for infringement proceedings. we will not wait until june before we embark on infringement proceedings; we just need to look at the latest documents we have received from the hungarian authorities to analyse them in a very down-to-earth and juridical way in order to see what we can take to court. i believe this was an introduction to what we are going to do in june or july – it is up to the parliament to decide – but the two reports will be of the utmost importance. until then the infringement proceedings by the commission will be on the table, and i hope that the infringement proceedings which have been decided by the court of justice will be put into practice in hungary.

in writing. − i welcome this report, starting by pointing out that delays in contracting for major infrastructure programmes and the withholding of budget support payments have led to individual commitments and payments being 13% and 16% below target in 2011 respectively. i would also like to reiterate my particular concern about the low rate of commitment of the 10th edf regional envelope (31%), just two years before the end of the programming period. in my view, it is the commission's duty to make every effort to ensure that this envelope is properly used and to draw lessons from the present delays for the next programming period. on the other hand, i welcome the introduction of the financial management basic guide to improve the knowledge of contractors and beneficiaries about financial management and eu eligibility rules. however, i would stress that the commission should improve the management of contract award procedures by making the selection criteria clearer and documenting the evaluation process better, and by improving the quality of the monitoring of grant contracts, in order to reduce the high number of errors detected in project payments.

in writing. - the report in question, by søren bo søndergaard, concerns the discharge for the implementation of the budget for the eighth, ninth and tenth european development funds (edfs) for the financial year 2011. the edf is the european union's (eu) main financial instrument for development cooperation with the so-called acp countries, i.e. the african, caribbean and pacific states, with the aim of reducing and eventually eradicating poverty. although the court of auditors (coa) refers in its opinion to the existence of a high rate of coding errors, which is a cause for concern, the fact is that the coa considers that the final annual accounts of the 8th, 9th and 10th edfs faithfully reflect, in all material respects, the financial situation of the edfs as at 31 december 2011 and that the expenditure and commitments are free from material errors. in these terms, and taking account of the report of the committee on budgetary control and the opinion of the committee on development, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the report stresses the need for the european development fund (edf) the eu's main financial instrument for development cooperation to be integrated into the eu budget. however, it welcomes the commission's commitment to propose the integration of the edf in the 2020 budget when the cotonou agreement expires. this amendment has been long sought, providing the eu's development cooperation and aid policy with more robust and predictable means, as well as being more easily scrutinised by the institutions responsible for approving the budget. the report stresses the need for greater control and supervision by the commission to prevent misuse of money and calls on the commission to train national budget managers in the beneficiary countries to improve their capacity for control and supervision. we are opposed to the paragraph on epas and the free trade agreement with the acp countries. it considers that trade relations, in accordance with wto principles, are crucial for developing countries. we can't accept that.
in writing. - all european institutions which are dependent on the budget of the european union must be strictly supervised by the court of auditors and all the bodies with this function. it is necessary to assess whether community funds are being well used, whether these institutions are meeting the objectives set and whether there is no waste of resources. in general, with a few exceptions, the institutions in question are using the funds appropriately and are meeting the objectives set. the vote in favour of the 2011 discharge report for the 8th, 9th and 10th european development funds (edf) is in that sense.
