in writing. - at the present political juncture, when many of the states of the european union, and my own in particular, are experiencing difficulties unparalleled in recent history, rather than focusing on the report i am voting on on the accounts of the european council and council, i would like to make some more general remarks. i would like to call on all these eu institutions, departments and agencies to adopt a principle of good management and a policy of restraint and austerity in their spending. the eu budget, in addition to its own resources, is mainly financed by contributions from the member states. this is why, in the current economic climate, we need to keep expenditure under control and adapt internal rules to an active policy of combating waste and establishing clear standards of good management and efficient use of public money. the eu cannot continue to demand difficult adjustments from states when there are still numerous instances of mismanagement and lack of transparency in its institutions, services and agencies.
in writing. the rapporteur proposes to postpone the decision granting the secretary-general of the council discharge in respect of the implementation of the council's budget for the financial year 2011. the basis for this delay is the old dispute between the council and parliament. the council maintains that there is a gentlemen's agreement dating from 1970 in which the council and parliament will not scrutinise the implementation of their respective budgets. the council is thus excused from sending documents relating to the implementation of the budget, from meeting or answering parliament's questions on this subject. parliament thus has no knowledge of the council's accounts, despite its participation in the discharge procedure. parliament considered that the council's expenditure should be examined in the same way as that of the other institutions. this delay is based on the council's lack of transparency and accountability. we supported this report.
in writing. - all european institutions which are dependent on the budget of the european union must be strictly supervised by the court of auditors and all the bodies with this function. it is necessary to assess whether community funds are being well used, whether these institutions are meeting the objectives set and whether there is no waste of resources. in general, with a few exceptions, as assessed by the audits known to us, we can say that the institutions concerned are making the right use of the funds made available and are meeting the objectives proposed. however, as far as the european council and the council are concerned, we continue to face less transparent situations and the absence of answers to a number of questions which have been addressed to the secretary-general of the council. i believe that all the institutions of the union have a duty to respect the same standards of transparency, and i am convinced that parliament and the council, as co-legislators, should apply the same standards of transparency, and that the council should improve its performance in this area without delay. that is why i am voting in favour of postponing the discharge for the european council and the council.

in writing. - the report under consideration, drawn up by mr gerben-jan gerbrandy, concerns the discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the translation centre for the bodies of the european union for the financial year 2011. the translation centre for the bodies of the european union (cdt), established in 1994 and based in luxembourg, is responsible for providing the translation services required for the functioning of the various eu agencies. it also takes an active part in the work of the interinstitutional committee on translation and interpretation. in the light of the report of the committee on budgetary control and notwithstanding the recommendations of the rapporteur, i am voting in favour of this report to give discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2011.
in writing. − the translation centre for the bodies of the european union was set up to provide the translation services necessary for the functioning of the specialised and decentralised agencies of the european union. this activity is extended to community institutions and bodies which have their own translation services, with the aim of absorbing any additional workloads. we reject the successive cuts to the centre's final budget, which in 2011 was 8.27%, and the proposal to reduce it by 5 posts from 2012. this proposal further feeds into our concerns, already raised in several debates, that these cuts will deepen discrimination in the use, translation and interpretation of the official languages of the european union, as well as our concerns about the need to defend multilingualism as a cultural value of the eu. we oppose dismissals and/or the limitation of the rights of workers in translation and interpretation services: this leads to a deterioration in the quality of these services and is contrary to the principle of multilingualism. we have defended the principle of permanent employment contracts for permanent posts.

in writing. - at the present political juncture, when many of the european union's member states, and my own in particular, are experiencing difficulties unparalleled in recent history, rather than focusing on the report i am voting on on the accounts of the european centre for the development of vocational training, i would like to make a few more general remarks. i would like to call on all these eu institutions, departments and agencies to adopt a principle of good management and a policy of restraint and austerity in their spending. the eu budget, in addition to its own resources, is mainly financed by contributions from the member states. this is why, in the current economic climate, we need to keep expenditure under control and adapt internal rules to an active policy of combating waste and establishing clear standards of good management and efficient use of public money. the eu cannot continue to demand difficult adjustments from states when there are still numerous instances of mismanagement and lack of transparency in its institutions, services and agencies.
in writing. - the report under consideration, drawn up by gerben-jan gerbrandy, concerns the discharge for the implementation of the budget of the european centre for the development of vocational training (cedefop) for the financial year 2011. the european centre for the development of vocational training (cedefop) is an agency whose objective is to promote and develop vocational education and training in the eu by providing information and analysis on policies, research and practice in the field of vocational education and training. in the light of the report of the committee on budgetary control and the opinion of the committee on employment and social affairs, i am voting in favour of this report to give the director of cedefop a discharge in respect of the implementation of its budget for the year 2011.
in writing. - all european institutions which are dependent on the budget of the european union must be strictly supervised by the court of auditors and all the bodies with this function. it is necessary to assess whether community funds are being well used, whether these institutions are meeting the objectives set and whether there is no waste of resources. in general, with a few exceptions, as assessed by the audits known to us, we can say that the institutions concerned are making the right use of the funds made available and are meeting the objectives proposed. it is in this sense that i am voting in favour of the discharge report of the european centre for the development of vocational training.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european centre for the development of vocational training for the financial year 2011, on the basis of the annual report of the court of auditors on the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2011, together with the replies of the institutions under audit, the statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions provided by the court of auditors for the financial year 2011, pursuant to article 287 tfeu, and the opinion of the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament, which proposes to give discharge.
in writing. − when giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament approves the good use of public funds in budget implementation, achieved in compliance with the rules. following a recommendation from the council, meps are called upon to monitor the management of appropriations by deciding on discharge on the basis of the court of auditors' reports. as regards the implementation of the budget of the european centre for the development of vocational training for the financial year 2011, and having assessed the reports of the court of auditors and the parliamentary committee on budgetary control, i supported the discharge for the implementation of the budget.

in writing. − it is regrettable that since the academy was granted the status of a community body in 2006, the court of auditors' reports on the academy's annual accounts for the financial years 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2009 have been issued in succession, raising concerns about the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions, in particular that the contract award system did not comply with the provisions of the financial regulation. for the first time in 2010, the court of auditors gave a positive opinion, having obtained reasonable assurances that the annual accounts are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular. for the financial year 2011, the budget of the academy was increased to eur 8 341 000, with 96,74% of the appropriations for commitments and 75,21% of the appropriations for payments being implemented. the academy's efforts to streamline and improve the efficiency of its governance should be recognised, as it has succeeded in improving its performance and results achieved without major budgetary impact. i am therefore pleased that the academy has been able to respond to parliament's demands and to the current budgetary challenges by reducing its governance costs.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the community fisheries control agency for the financial year 2011, on the basis of the annual report of the court of auditors on the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2011, together with the replies of the institutions audited, the statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions, issued by the court of auditors for the financial year 2011 pursuant to article 287 tfeu, the favourable opinion of the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament and the opinion of the committees on fisheries, in which i stressed the request to the court of auditors to continue its work on the supervision of the public recruitment and contracting procedures undertaken by the agency.
in writing. − when giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament approves the good use of public funds in budget implementation, achieved in compliance with the rules. following a recommendation from the council, meps are called upon to monitor the management of appropriations by deciding on discharge on the basis of the court of auditors' reports. as regards the budget of the community fisheries control agency for the financial year 2011, and having assessed the reports of the court of auditors and the parliamentary committee on budgetary control, i supported the discharge for the implementation of the budget.

in writing. - at the present political juncture, when many of the european union states, and mine in particular, are experiencing difficulties unparalleled in recent history, rather than focusing on the report i am voting on on the accounts of the european food safety authority, i would like to make a few more general remarks. i would like to call on all these eu institutions, departments and agencies to adopt a principle of good management and a policy of restraint and austerity in their spending. the eu budget, in addition to its own resources, is mainly financed by contributions from the member states. this is why, in the current economic climate, we need to keep expenditure under control and adapt internal rules to an active policy of combating waste and establishing clear standards of good management and efficient use of public money. the eu cannot continue to demand difficult adjustments from states when there are still numerous instances of mismanagement and lack of transparency in its institutions, services and agencies.

in writing. - in times of crisis, such as the present one, it is not only essential that workers' rights are defended, but also urgent that they are strengthened. only the path of progress and social justice can put an end to the swamp situation that the capitalist system has brought us. in this context, equality between women and men is an urgent objective, but unfortunately it is still a long way off. the way forward must be to combat these inequalities and to strengthen the conditions under which this fight is carried out, on all fronts. we are therefore against any proposal to merge or abolish the european institute for gender equality and for the savings to be made in the name of the economic crisis to mean staff cuts which could compromise its performance. we therefore welcome the establishment of the data and documentation centre institute.

in writing. − the european institute of innovation and technology has the express objective of contributing to 'sustainable economic growth and competitiveness in europe by strengthening the innovation capacities of the member states and the european union'. the institute awards grants to 'knowledge and innovation communities' which link together higher education institutions, the research sector and the business sector, thereby stimulating innovation and entrepreneurship. the report under review identifies some shortcomings in its functioning, such as: - low implementation rates indicating difficulties in planning and budget implementation; - payments made in 2011 after most activities had already been implemented, a practice that calls into question sound financial management; - a high level of appropriations carried over (from 2011 to 2012) which is not in line with the principle of budgetary annuality for which it is urgent to find the appropriate measures. we abstained on the discharge and voted in favour of the resolution.

in writing. − the report under review, by gerben-jan gerbrandy, focuses on the discharge for the implementation of the budget of the european medicines agency (ema) for the financial year 2011. the ema, which was set up in 1993 but only became operational in 1995, aims to protect and promote public and animal health by assessing and monitoring medicines for human and/or veterinary use. no medicinal product may be placed on the market without the favourable opinion of the agency. according to the annual accounts, in 2011, 77,7% of the agency's revenue came from the collection of fees, which increase every year, with the relative percentage income of the union contribution being 18,3% in 2011 (18,8% in 2010, or 14% if the collection of surpluses has been deducted from the total union contribution). i therefore vote against this report, taking into account the opinion of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, because i believe that, as with other agencies, the executive director of the ema should also be given a discharge in respect of the implementation of its budget for the year 2011.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european maritime safety agency for the financial year 2011, on the basis of the annual report of the court of auditors on the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2011, together with the institute's reply, the statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions provided by the court of auditors for the financial year 2011 pursuant to article 287 tfeu, and the favourable opinion of the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament and of the committee on transport and tourism.
in writing. − when giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament approves the good use of public funds in budget implementation, achieved in compliance with the rules. following a recommendation from the council, meps are called upon to monitor the management of appropriations by deciding on discharge on the basis of the court of auditors' reports. as regards the budget of the european maritime safety agency for the financial year 2011, and having assessed the reports of the court of auditors and the parliamentary committee on budgetary control, i supported the discharge for the implementation of the budget.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european maritime safety agency for the financial year 2011, noting, however, that in 2011 the budget of this agency amounted to eur 56.4 million, compared to eur 54.4 million in the previous year.
in writing. − i approve this report, starting with the fact that no appropriate measures have been taken to address the lack of transparency in the recruitment processes reported by the court of auditors in 2010 and that the court has again indicated that the agency needs to improve the transparency of these processes. i therefore urge the agency to inform the discharge authority of the measures taken to correct this shortcoming. furthermore, i am concerned that the work of the agency, which sets the pace for information security in europe and which is currently housed in purpose-built facilities on crete, would be fragmented by the division of its headquarters between athens and heraklion, which would significantly increase the agency's operating costs and would be contrary to the principle of sound financial management, adding to the financial and administrative burdens at a time when savings are needed.

in writing. − i approve this report, starting by recalling that the level of the preliminary draft estimate of revenue and expenditure for the 2014 budget, as proposed by the secretary-general in his report to the bureau, takes into account the rate of increase of 3,58% compared to the 2013 budget. i acknowledge that this proposed increase consists of legal obligations: an increase of 2,20% is due to the additional expenditure in the year in question, which is exceptional due to the election of a new parliament and the fact that it has become a truly independent democratic institution with the application of its own statute for members and their assistants, and an increase of 1,30% is due to other legal obligations. i welcome the plans of the joint working group of the bureau and the committee on budgets to study structural reforms in parliament's budget and hope that this work will present options for savings in the 2014 budget until september 2013 without compromising legislative excellence or the quality of working conditions.

in writing. - since parliament has to assess the proposal for this regulation positively or negatively and cannot make any changes to its content, this report has been drawn up with the aim of stating the position of the members clearly, for the sake of democratic legitimacy and the final result of the regulation in question. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the euro as a currency in the euro area. the need for the single supervisory mechanism and european banking resolution to be open to non-euro area countries is emphasised, and the need for a speedy and effective recapitalisation of european banks is stressed. the commission also proposes that the european stability mechanism (esm) should not be able to finance banks in non-euro area countries directly (which will be financed from the european budget if necessary), and that a new instrument be created for the indirect recapitalisation of banks in these countries, or alternatively that they join the esm and contribute to its capital. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − the creation of the balance of payments support mechanism (bop) for eu countries whose currency is not the euro is part of the process of creating different mechanisms (such as the european stability mechanism) which, hypocritically invoking financial solidarity, aim to impose on these countries measures (here called economic adjustment programmes) of impoverishment and extortion, of neocolonial cutbacks, such as those imposed on portugal, with the known results: closure of companies and destruction of productive capacity, privatisations and liberalisations, unemployment, destruction of labour and social rights, destruction of public services (health, education, social security, transport), wage cuts, increase in the cost of living, poverty. the report argues that the gnp should be guaranteed by the eu budget, which could constitute an additional burden for a budget that is clearly insufficient in the face of the crisis situation and the economic and social development needs of countries such as portugal. the final result is not a reduction in public debts and deficits but an increase in them, destroying national sovereignty and creating economic and financial dependence.

in writing. − i welcome this report, given that the aim of this proposal is to clarify and harmonise eu rules on the vat system for vouchers, which will have a positive effect on businesses by eliminating double taxation and uncertainty about tax obligations. it will also help to close the loopholes that facilitate tax evasion by certain companies that take advantage of differences between member states. the new regulation, in particular its objective of creating a digital single market, also fits well into the wider context of the digital europe agenda.
in writing. the new legislation aims to eliminate differences between national regulations on the vat arrangements for vouchers, given the serious market inefficiencies which hamper the effective development of business activities and prevent consumers from taking full advantage of the operation of pan-european schemes for voucher services. the vouchers market represents over eur 52 billion a year in the european union and the clarification of its tax regime will be essential in eliminating situations of double taxation, tax evasion and uncertainty about the tax obligations of companies, especially in relation to their cross-border activities. the european commission is proposing harmonisation of the definition of vouchers and their distinction from other means of payment, the place and time of taxation of transactions relating to them, and common rules for their distribution in the chain of intermediaries to the final consumer. other technical measures relating to the right to deduct, redemption and refund procedures, the tax debtor and other obligations of companies are also covered. i support this report because i believe it fills in the gaps in legislation which are an obstacle to the full exploitation of the opportunities of the single market.
in writing. the european union voucher market is worth more than eur 52 billion a year. this is a significant figure and has alerted the union to the need for a review of european vat legislation in order to ensure a harmonised tax treatment of vouchers in all member states. the gap in european legislation in this area has highlighted the differences between the various national regulations as regards the vat regime applicable to vouchers. these differences generate market inefficiencies, which penalise a market which is intended to be a single market for businesses and consumers. i therefore voted in favour of this report, whose proposals seek to introduce greater harmonization in the taxation of vouchers. another step towards the digital single market that will bring positive effects for businesses by eliminating double taxation situations and, ultimately, for all european consumers.
in writing. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a directive on the common system of value added tax (cvat) for the treatment of vouchers. i have always advocated greater harmonisation and simplification of vat rules in order to minimise possible market distortions, including double taxation or even no taxation at all. i therefore welcome another initiative in this direction.
in writing. the european union (eu) voucher market is worth some €52 billion a year, with telecommunications prepayments holding the largest market share at around 70%. the differences between member states (ms) in value added tax (vat) are a factor of instability and injustice which cause difficulties in the functioning of the voucher market. aware of this, the commission proposed on 10 may 2012 to update the eu vat rules in order to harmonise the tax treatment of all types of vouchers in the ms. i voted in favour of the report by mrs ildikó gáll-pelcz on the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2006/112/ec on the common system of value added tax as regards the treatment of vouchers, because it is essential to clarify and harmonise european legislation on vouchers, eliminating double taxation and combating tax evasion by companies. this regulation will provide a clear legal definition of vouchers for the purposes of taxing vat and the fixing of the time at which vat must be paid, thus taking another step towards the construction of a genuine single market.
in writing. − eliminating the risk of tax evasion and fraud by clarifying the vat treatment of transactions involving vouchers is a fair objective and deserves our support. however, as always, more than just clarifying the vat collection process, the aim of this proposal is to remove existing barriers in the internal market, to harmonise the different laws of the member states and to increase competition, which will only encourage the concentration of companies operating in this sector. this concentration is contrary to the objective of combating tax fraud and tax evasion, since it abolishes national legislation by increasing the free movement of capital, which is conducive to tax fraud and tax evasion. this is a very attractive market for large capital, representing some €52 billion a year in the eu, spread over both large and small companies. this process will not be beneficial to workers and consumers, since concentration in the sector will - as in other sectors - lead to higher consumer prices and a decrease in the quality of services or products.
in writing. − this report addresses inconsistencies in legislation which constitute an obstacle to the full exploitation of the opportunities of the single market. the commission proposal proposes harmonisation of the definition of vouchers and their distinction from other means of payment, the place and time of taxation of transactions relating to them, and common rules for their distribution in the chain of intermediaries to the final consumer. i have voted in favour of this report because of the benefits it is expected to bring.
in writing. the new legislation aims to eliminate differences between national regulations on the vat arrangements for vouchers, given the serious market inefficiencies which hamper the effective development of business activities and prevent consumers from taking full advantage of the operation of pan-european schemes for voucher services. the vouchers market represents over eur 52 billion a year in the eu and clarification of its tax regime will be essential in eliminating double taxation, tax evasion and uncertainty about the tax obligations of companies, especially in relation to their cross-border activities. the commission proposal proposes harmonisation of the definition of vouchers and their distinction from other means of payment, the place and time of taxation of transactions relating to them, and common rules for their distribution in the chain of intermediaries to the final consumer. other technical measures relating to the right to deduct, redemption and refund procedures, the tax debtor and other obligations of companies are also covered. i support this report because i believe it fills in the gaps in legislation which are an obstacle to the full exploitation of the opportunities of the single market.
in writing. the new legislation in question aims to harmonise national rules on the vat arrangements applicable to vouchers, due to the fact that there are inefficiencies in the market, which hamper the effective development of business activities. i am voting in favour of this proposal because i believe that there should be greater harmonization of the definition of vouchers and their distinction from other means of payment, and the place and time of taxation of transactions relating to them. it should also be noted that there should be common rules for their distribution in the chain from intermediaries to the final consumer. finally, it should be noted that other technical measures relating to the right to deduct, redemption and reimbursement procedures and rules which impose new obligations on undertakings are also covered.
in writing. − eliminating the risk of tax evasion and fraud by clarifying the vat treatment of transactions involving vouchers is a fair objective and deserves our full support. however, more than just clarifying the vat collection process, the aim of this proposal is to remove existing barriers in the internal market, to harmonise the different laws of the member states and to increase competition, which will only encourage the concentration of companies operating in this sector. this concentration is contrary to the objective of combating tax fraud and tax evasion, since it abolishes national legislation by increasing the free movement of capital, which is conducive to tax fraud and tax evasion. this is a very attractive market for large capital, representing some €52 billion a year in the eu, spread over both large and small companies. this process will not be beneficial to workers and consumers, since concentration in the sector will lead - as in other sectors - to more unemployment, loss of tax revenue, increased costs for social security systems, increases in consumer prices, and a decline in the quality of services or products.

in writing. - at the present political juncture, when many of the european union states, and in particular my own, are experiencing difficulties unparalleled in recent history, rather than focusing on the report i am voting on on the europol accounts, i would like to make some more general remarks. i would like to call on all these eu institutions, departments and agencies to adopt a principle of good management and a policy of restraint and austerity in their spending. the eu budget, in addition to its own resources, is mainly financed by contributions from the member states. this is why, in the current economic climate, we need to keep expenditure under control and adapt internal rules to an active policy of combating waste and establishing clear standards of good management and efficient use of public money. the eu cannot continue to demand difficult adjustments from states when there are still numerous instances of mismanagement and lack of transparency in its institutions, services and agencies.
in writing. - all european institutions which are dependent on the budget of the european union must be strictly supervised by the court of auditors and all the bodies with this function. it is necessary to assess whether community funds are being well used, whether these institutions are meeting the objectives set and whether there is no waste of resources. in general, with a few exceptions, as assessed by the audits known to us, we can say that the institutions concerned are making the right use of the funds made available and are meeting the objectives proposed. it is in this sense that the vote in favour of the europol discharge report is appropriate.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european police office for the financial year 2011, on the basis of the annual report of the court of auditors on the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2011, together with the office's reply, the statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions provided by the court of auditors for the financial year 2011 pursuant to article 287 tfeu, and the favourable opinion of the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament and of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs.
in writing. − when giving a discharge to an institution or agency, the european parliament approves the good use of public funds in budget implementation, achieved in compliance with the rules. following a recommendation from the council, meps are called upon to monitor the management of appropriations by deciding on discharge on the basis of the court of auditors' reports. as regards the budget of the european police office for the financial year 2011, and having assessed the reports of the court of auditors and the parliamentary committee on budgetary control, i supported the discharge for the implementation of the budget.
in writing. − the european parliament must give a discharge to an institution or agency, thereby declaring that it has complied with european rules on the implementation of the budget and closing its budget. i am voting in favour of discharging europol for having used its information and operational expertise to support member state authorities in 13 697 crossborder cases, which represents an increase of 17% compared to 2010. in addition, more than 25% of europol's operations were drug-related, 22 high-level investigations into human trafficking were carried out, 9 major european operations targeted criminal networks facilitating illegal immigration and operations against the sexual exploitation of children, such as operation rescue, which led to 250 arrests worldwide and the protection of 252 children.

in writing. - i approve of this report, starting with the high volume of appropriations carried over, which the court of auditors describes as 'excessive' in its report; taking note of the frontex reply in which it draws attention to the fact that a large part of the additional funds, amounting to eur 31.8 million, only arrived at the end of october 2011. i recognize that the provision of such a volume of supplementary funds relatively late in the year does indeed pose a budgetary management problem and i am aware that frontex is an operational agency and that the implementation of its budgetary programming is to a large extent dependent on external factors such as the need to respond to exceptional circumstances. i therefore urge frontex to continue to strengthen the monitoring of joint operations.

in writing. − the european parliament must give a discharge to an institution or agency, thereby declaring that it has complied with european rules on the implementation of the budget and closing its budget. the european parliament may refuse or postpone discharge. i am in favour of the discharge of the joint undertaking for the implementation of the joint technology initiative on innovative medicines, stressing that it aims to significantly improve the effectiveness and efficiency of the drug development process so that the pharmaceutical industry produces, in the long term, more effective and safer innovative medicines.

madam president, madam minister, we are discussing here today - and again - the council's block on multiannual management plans, an issue that has dragged on since 2009. the european parliament thus shows its dissatisfaction with the present situation, its commitment to resolving it and the expectation it places on the irish presidency to overcome it. the question is twofold and it must be resolved. it is primarily political, because the council has completely disregarded the new powers of co-legislature which the lisbon treaty confers on parliament. the council should not fear this strengthened democracy, but rather recognize that cooperation between the two institutions better serves the common objective of european integration. the issue is also environmental by promoting the sustainability of stocks through the implementation of multiannual management plans, a model that the future common fisheries policy establishes as a rule. multiannual plans based on scientific advice, reflecting the specificities of different resources and the diversity of fisheries in european waters, contribute to the sustainability of exploitation of fisheries resources, as well as to better long-term planning and greater stability of the sector. in addition, they may also include specific provisions limiting the annual fluctuations of the total allowable catches, creating more stable and predictable conditions for union fisheries operators. they are therefore an undeniable asset to a sustainable european fisheries sector. in view of the council's blockage of the multiannual management plans, i ask: how are we going to implement a new reform of the common fisheries policy? in fact, the question here today is: what is the irish presidency going to do about this?
this persistent institutional impasse over multiannual fisheries management plans, beyond the more immediate implications discussed here today, is giving rise to a much deeper reflection on the current fisheries management model. in recent decades, important decisions have been taken in the light of a model of centralised management that is far removed from reality - ignoring reality - and this has resulted in decisions with profoundly negative effects, often contrary to what was said to be intended. today, if anything has changed, it's for the worse. the exclusive competence of the european union in this field conferred by the treaty of lisbon deepens and enhances this centralised management. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the fishing industry. decisions that will shape the future of entire communities. but despite this, these communities are increasingly far from influencing the decision-making process that will determine, to a large extent, their future. it is democracy itself that is at stake. it is therefore urgent to reverse this course. the question of whether the european union has exclusive competence in this area is inevitably part of the change that is needed.
madam president, the treaty of lisbon has strengthened participatory democracy and representative democracy. the citizens' initiative is a very positive instrument, but it has already been said here that the rules and procedures which make it difficult to apply it must be simplified. we therefore welcome all the efforts the commission can make to facilitate genuine citizen participation in the decision-making processes of european policy. in the european year of citizens, and at a time when europe is going through a serious economic crisis, but also a political and values crisis, it is essential to deepen the dialogue between european governments, institutions and citizens. this dialogue must help to define a course for europe that meets the expectations of the people. it is crucial that citizens also participate in the construction of the european project and we must read the signs of dissatisfaction of many europeans with what is happening in europe and in their countries. we must listen to the citizens, even when they are demonstrating in the streets.
the problem here is a problem of mutual trust between the two institutions in the legislative process. i was the rapporteur for this very report on macroeconomic imbalances and i can assure you that there are no technical and political issues because the choice of indicators and the choice of the alert thresholds associated with these indicators are detailed matters and it is on the basis of this information that policies or policy changes are then defined. this means that the choice of indicators is an extraordinarily important decision to know what we are looking at and, based on the results, from what we know, from what we measure, from what we understand, to make the most appropriate decisions. i would point out to you, and the commissioner has referred to the text in question, that recital 12 of this legislation says, and i will say it in english: the commission should present suggestions for comments to the competent committees of the european parliament and of the council on plans to establish and adjust the indicators and thresholds. "this is what was agreed. that's what it says. this was the basis of our interinstitutional understanding and i ask you: does the commissioner consider that sending us information on a change in an indicator is in keeping with the spirit and the letter of this recital? i hope that the commission will look at the way in which it has made this amendment and correct the clear error of relationship, on the basis of good faith interinstitutional, which i believe has been made and which this parliament believes has been made. i shall not add anything to what the chairman of the committee, sharon bowles, has just said. there is an interinstitutional problem here which will leave scars, or, on the contrary, a clearer and more transparent method of working, side by side, in the legislative phases that follow, and there are many! so it was absolutely essential that we start to do all that remains to be done on a basis of mutual trust and not on a basis of mutual distrust.

in writing. − the visa facilitation agreement between the european community and ukraine has been in force since january 2008 and has been successful with a very low visa refusal rate of 3.3%. however, despite the success, the performance evaluation has highlighted some changes that need to be made. the newly amended agreement introduces clear improvements in the issuing of visas to ukrainian citizens. it simplifies the documentary requirements for certain applicants and increases the categories of persons eligible for a multiple-entry visa valid for one or five years. this amendment is a significant step towards the establishment of a visa waiver regime between the european union and ukraine. it also sends a clear signal to ukrainian citizens that the eu is committed to strengthening its partnership with ukrainian society and to further developing and facilitating people-to-people contacts. i therefore support this recommendation.

in writing. − the agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova on the facilitation of the issuance of visas entered into force on 1 january 2008. in the meantime, the commission has opened negotiations with moldova with a view to adopting a new agreement on visa facilitation, in particular because romania, an eu member state, has had an agreement on short-stay border traffic with moldova since october 2010. i voted in favour of this amendment because the new agreement represents a step forward from the previous one, constituting a significant improvement for the moldovan population, by allowing the issuing of visas for 90 days in every 180-day period, and also providing for visa exemption for moldovan citizens who meet certain conditions, namely holders of biometric passports who wish to stay for a short period. the amendments also cover international drivers, journalists and their technical teams, close family members of eu citizens and participants in official cross-border cooperation programmes. i welcome this new agreement which allows for a closer rapprochement between the eu and the republic of moldova as well as the improvement of neighbourly relations.
in writing. − the european parliament approved the conclusion of the agreement amending an existing agreement concluded in 2008 on visa facilitation and providing for improvements for moldovan citizens, for an intended stay of 90 days in each 180-day period. this facilitation will reduce the time and costs associated with travel to the schengen area. there is a provision for a visa waiver for short-term cases for specific categories of applicants, which we normally support. we cannot, however, fail to note that in the eyes of the european union this process is an opportunity for moldova to implement the necessary reforms in the areas of freedom, security and justice, which, in our view, is a way of exerting political pressure to implement policies which are essentially in the eu's interests. the agreement also involves the exchange of information between moldovan and eu authorities on lost and stolen biometric passport data via the interpol database, the organisation of information campaigns and the updating of computer systems for calculating the total period of stay.
in writing. − on 1 january 2008, the agreement between the european community and the republic of moldova on the facilitation of the issuance of visas entered into force. this new agreement, on which we are now giving our opinion, was negotiated between may 2011 and december 2011 and was finalised in march 2012. the new agreement provides for improved conditions for moldovan citizens to obtain visas for the eu. the amended agreement between the european union and moldova on the facilitation of the issuance of visas constitutes progress compared to the initial agreement and provides for clear improvements for the benefit of moldovan citizens. the objective of the amending agreement is to facilitate the issuing of visas to citizens of the republic of moldova for an intended stay of 90 days in any 180-day period, and to provide for visa-free travel for moldovan citizens under certain conditions. that's why i'm in favor.
in writing. − in view of the european ambitions of the republic of moldova, this agreement, as amended, represents encouraging progress and promotes people-to-people contacts, economic development, cultural and scientific dialogue, stability, security and the well-being of citizens. visa facilitation will reduce the time and costs associated with travel to the schengen area. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the facilitation of the issuance of visas to citizens of the republic of moldova will reduce the time and cost associated with travel within the territory of the european union, without however signifying a laxity in the controls on the conditions of entry and stay of moldovan citizens in the schengen area. the obligation to justify the purpose and conditions of the journey remains in force once the agreement enters into force. in the light of these developments, which bring the eu and the republic of moldova closer together, i expressed my agreement in plenary, voting in favour of the rapporteur's recommendation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the approval of the agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova amending the agreement between the european community and the republic of moldova on the facilitation of the issuance of visas, as i considered that it constitutes progress compared to the initial agreement and provides for clear improvements for the benefit of moldovan citizens.
in writing. − the european parliament approved the conclusion of the agreement on visa facilitation amending the existing agreement concluded in 2008 between the european community and moldova, which provides for improvements for moldovan citizens for an intended stay of 90 days in any 180-day period. this facilitation will reduce the time and costs associated with travel to the schengen area. the visa waiver for short-stay cases is provided for specific categories of applicants, without prejudice to the functioning of the existing border code. the european union considers this process to be an opportunity for moldova to implement the necessary reforms in the areas of freedom, security and justice, which is clearly a way of exerting political pressure to implement policies that serve certain interests. the agreement also involves the exchange of information between moldovan and eu authorities on lost and stolen biometric passport data via the interpol database, the organisation of information campaigns and the updating of computer systems for calculating the total period of stay.
in writing. - i welcome this report, noting that the economic and financial crisis is a threat to all human rights, including civil and political rights, and in particular that the crisis has had a negative impact on access to food, healthcare and education for the most vulnerable groups in society, both in urban and rural areas, and has resulted in a dramatic increase in poverty levels globally. i would remind you that it is the responsibility of governments to ensure respect for economic, social and cultural rights and to protect citizens from abuses, for example by companies and other private actors, by applying the united nations guiding principles on business and human rights, and to investigate financial crimes committed by these actors. i am also concerned that, according to world bank and un estimates, the number of people forced into poverty by the crisis is increasing by between 55 and 103 million, thus further undermining respect for human rights.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because, while people in developed countries are currently feeling the impacts of the economic and financial crisis, it is the people in developing countries who are suffering the most from the crisis, given the almost complete absence of safety nets to protect them. i therefore call for greater eu involvement in mitigating these effects in developing countries. i also think that this report is important because it stresses that respect for economic and social rights depends, among other things, on the state's ability to regulate the financial market and to distribute the available resources fairly, for example through an effective, transparent and progressive taxation system.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it reiterates the eu's determination to defend and promote human rights and fundamental freedoms as the foundation of the european union's external policy, as enshrined in the treaty of lisbon, especially in the context of the economic and financial crisis.
in writing. − human rights and fundamental freedoms are necessarily affected whenever there is a serious economic and financial crisis such as the one we are experiencing today, which has global effects. the european union feels the same way. the difficulties experienced by individuals and families are palpable, and there is a setback in what were once assumed rights. the european situation is serious and unemployment is the main scourge on its citizens. political stability and democracy have also been affected by distortions which must be avoided. the risk of social breakdown deserves greater attention and commitment from policy-makers, but it requires equal firmness in defending respect for the mechanisms of representative democracy and the rejection of populist and violent attempts to condition legitimate governance. the situation is even more dramatic in the wider context of this issue, which calls into question not only the economic, social and cultural rights of many peoples but also the very essence of their civil and political rights. while struggling to recover, the union cannot neglect the defence of those who have the least and suffer the most within and outside its borders.
in writing. the report by mrs inese vaidere is on a motion for a resolution on the impact of the current economic and financial crisis on human rights. in several debates in this parliament, many members have referred to the harmful consequences of the current crisis, both on a personal and family level, and on a professional and social level. the people most affected are those in the most vulnerable groups with food, health care and education shortages. as an immediate consequence, in addition to several suicides due to unemployment or failure to honour financial commitments, we have a significant increase in poverty levels. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution and i urge the member states to continue their official development assistance, since the negative impact of the crisis is particularly acute in the poorest countries. finally, i call on international institutions such as the imf, the wto and the world bank to take account in their decisions of the obligation to respect and enforce human rights as enshrined in international treaties.
in writing. − this report aims to assess the impact of the economic and financial crisis on human rights. it notes that even with a rapid recovery of the world economy, which seems far from possible, given the measures being taken, by 2020 we will have an additional 71 million people in extreme poverty worldwide due to the crisis. the report refers to the sharp increase in unemployment since the beginning of the crisis, seriously affecting the right to work, the right to health, education and food. attention is also drawn to the enormous failure of the so-called rich countries to meet the tenuous millennium development goals (mdgs), due to the lack of allocation of sufficient funds (the objective was to affect 0.7% of gdp) and, we add, because the eu, the us and other imperialist powers live from this profoundly unequal and exploitative world (dis) order, based on the international division of labour, reserving the role of suppliers of raw materials and cheap labour for the third world countries. the report lists some good intentions but it does not go far enough, it does not put forward any concrete proposals to deal with the problems, it does not seriously characterize the policies that led to the crisis, it does not identify those responsible.
in writing. − the financial and economic crisis affects all regions of the world, including the european union, with varying intensity. in this resolution we assess the impact of this crisis on third countries, with particular emphasis on developing and least developed countries. the financial and economic crisis is indeed a global systemic crisis and is interlinked with many other crises, such as the food, environmental and social crisis. there are some countries in north africa and the middle east that are more affected and where their populations have suffered. it should therefore be the eu's determination to defend and promote human rights and fundamental freedoms - civil, political, economic, social and cultural - as the foundation of its foreign policy, and support for all other policies, as enshrined in the lisbon treaty, especially in the context of the economic and financial crisis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution of the european parliament, in which i stress the need for further studies and analyses of the impact of the financial and economic crisis in various regions, including in the eu and in its relations with third countries, and also the need for better monitoring of the early signs of global and regional crises.
in writing. - this resolution assesses the impact of the crisis in third countries. whereas unemployment reached 200 million people worldwide in 2012, of which 74 million are young people aged 15 to 24; whereas trafficking in human beings represents a modern form of slavery, which exploits the need of potential victims to get decent jobs and escape poverty; whereas access of poor people to water, education, health care and food is restricted as part of the crisis response strategies adopted by families, the rapporteur on these human rights violations added that there is no justification for states, regardless of their income level, to compromise their obligation to respect fundamental rights. the report, which i am voting for, puts the interests of the most vulnerable at the centre of political action.
in writing. the report presented reflects the impact of the financial and economic crisis in third countries, mainly in developing and least developed countries. there is absolutely nothing shocking about this report, because it is nothing but a list of good intentions without being able to draw up a concrete proposal to tackle the problems. in the same way that an observation is made that this is a systemic crisis, nothing is said or questioned about the policies that caused the crisis and that continue to aggravate it. in addition, the report also refuses to address the impact of the crisis, even within the european union. that's why we abstained.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the response to the crisis must imperatively include multilateral cooperation coordinated at international level, both at regional and interregional level, and be based on an approach firmly articulated around human rights. i believe that although the world economic crisis is seriously jeopardising respect for economic, social and cultural rights, there is no reason for states, whatever their level of income, to compromise their obligation to respect fundamental human rights.
in writing. − the report finds that even with a possible rapid recovery of the world economy in 2020, we will have an additional 71 million people in the world who will be in extreme poverty due to the crisis. the report refers to the sharp increase in unemployment since the beginning of the crisis, seriously affecting the right to work, the right to health, education and food. attention is also drawn to the enormous failure of the so-called rich countries to meet the millennium development goals (mdgs) due to the lack of allocation of sufficient funds (the objective was to affect 0.7% of gdp) and, we add, because the eu, the us and other imperialist powers live in this deeply unequal and exploitative world order, based on the international division of labour, reserving the role of suppliers of raw materials and cheap labour for the third world countries. the report lists some good intentions, but it stops there - it does not put forward any concrete proposals to deal with it, it does not seriously characterize the policies that led to the crisis, it does not name those responsible. and as if all this were not contradictory enough, the report does not speak of the impact of the crisis on the eu and its responsibilities in the dire situation of countries like portugal.
in writing. - the proposal for a regulation on european statistics on demography provides for two different definitions of resident population, depending on whether you are providing population data to eurostat (article 3) or the population data needed to establish a qualified majority in the council (article 4). the existence of two different definitions could have political consequences, given that for the purposes of qualified majority voting in the council, member states should provide data on the resident population according to the concept of 'habitual residence' (a concept based on the temporal criterion of one year of actual residence) and not 'permanent residence', legal or registered. this issue is relevant because it has consequences for countries that are currently facing waves of immigration due to the crisis. the migratory phenomena in the european union must not have a negative impact on the number of qualified majority votes in the council or on the number of members to be elected to the european parliament. i therefore voted in favour of the amendment to delete article 4. i supported this report, but the vote on the legislative resolution was postponed.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support the european standardisation of demographic statistics, which will make it easier to compare data between member states. the availability of such statistics will allow for valid comparisons and relevant conclusions to be drawn which can support the formulation of concrete measures and policies.
in writing. - i believe that the union is facing a very serious demographic problem and that the answer to it should be based on the most reliable data. data comparability is essential for the proper handling of statistics. given that the union has sought to carry out cross-sectional assessments of all its member states, it is appropriate to expect that the available demographic data will allow for such comparability and relatively uniform treatment. the question of assessing the most demographically deprived areas and finding solutions to reverse the demographic winter and to achieve a more homogeneous distribution of populations should call for the commitment of policy-makers and civil society.
in writing. − the eu's sustainable development strategy, launched by the gothenburg european council in 2001 and renewed in june 2006, seeks to continuously improve the quality of life for current and future generations. the commission's (eurostat) monitoring report, which is published every two years, provides an objective statistical overview of progress made, based on the eu's set of sustainable development indicators. demographic statistics on population are an essential component of the estimate of the total population in the european system of accounts (esa). updating and processing data is important for the production of statistics at european level.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european statistics on demography, of which i would like to highlight the contribution made by the european parliament, and on the regions, including in the text the obligation that, where statistical data are submitted at national level by regional authorities, member states should also transmit these data to the commission (eurostat), in order to allow a more detailed analysis of the demographic situation in the union.
in writing. − in the pursuit of european standardisation and in order to ensure the quality and especially the comparability of the data provided, this proposal aims to regulate the provision and harmonisation of statistical data on the population of the member states, since these are important for the production of statistics at european level. demographic changes, in particular estimates of the percentage of the population aged over 65 and of the percentage of the active population in relation to the total population, show how regions are affected by demographic developments, with implications for future eu cohesion policy. in this respect, it is essential to follow the same principles and criteria in the production of statistics and, where statistical data are submitted at national level by regional authorities, to transmit them to the commission. for the reasons i have mentioned, i supported the report in plenary.
in writing. − the european population has been declining over the last few years, due to the decline in the birth rate and the progressive ageing of citizens. i am voting in favour of this report which stresses the need for constant updating and processing of data which are important for the production of statistics at european level. it should also be noted that the production and dissemination of european statistics should involve the relevant statistical authorities at national and regional level in order to obtain more reliable information. thus, where regional authorities provide statistical data to national authorities, member states should transmit these data to eurostat in order to allow a more detailed analysis of the demographic situation in the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it will have a financial instrument which will make it profitable for shipowners when they want to dispose of their ships legally. its aim is therefore to grow the labour market and protect workers and the environment.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on ship recycling, because it includes proposals to make ship recycling economically viable and to increase the recycling capacity, particularly for larger ships, in the eu. these measures should make it possible to stop the export of hazardous waste from the eu to non-oecd countries, including through the use of voluntary landings, which have significant environmental and health impacts.
in writing. − under the eu regulation on waste shipments, the export of hazardous waste from the eu to non-oecd countries has been prohibited since 1998. due to the various hazardous materials on board a ship, any ship that leaves the eu for dismantling is a hazardous waste. nevertheless, more than 90% of vessels flying the flag of an eu member state were effectively decommissioned in 2009 outside the oecd using the so-called 'voluntary berth' method. ship recycling is often carried out in yards with little or no standards for the protection of workers, human health and the environment, as these are the ones that offer the best prices. a financial mechanism applicable to all ships calling at eu ports, among other measures to counterbalance this situation, is now essential to make the safe and environmentally friendly recycling of ships that constitute hazardous waste competitive with other recycling operations.
in writing. − shipbreaking worldwide increased sixfold between 2007 and 2009, driven by the accelerated retirement of single-hull tankers, the crisis and the resulting overcapacity. the world fleet has almost doubled in the last ten years. working conditions, workers' rights, the protection of public health and the preservation of the environment are all matters of great concern to us. the hong kong international convention for the safe and environmentally sound recycling of ships, developed by the imo, and the basel convention, which includes some amendments, will help to improve the current situation. we support several of the provisions in the report, such as the creation of an inventory of hazardous materials, a specific recycling plan for ships over 20 years old, more explicit requirements for ship recycling yards and the exclusion of scrapping in the shipyard. but in the concrete context of the integration which is taking place, proposals such as the creation of more european taxes or a further european list (of shipyards) will inevitably result in another factor of pressure on wages, which we do not accept.
in writing. − the objective of this proposal for a regulation on ship recycling is to significantly reduce the negative impacts of recycling ships flying the flag of an eu member state, in particular in south asia, without creating unnecessary economic burdens. the scope of the commission proposal is limited to vessels flying the flag of an eu member state. it proposes that a european list be drawn up of recycling yards anywhere in the world, provided they comply with certain standards (to a certain extent above the provisions of the hong kong convention), such as the handling of hazardous materials on impermeable soils, downstream waste treatment facilities operating in accordance with eu standards for the protection of human health and the environment, but not subject to mandatory controls. uniform and environmentally friendly standards are essential in this area.
in writing. - the present report reiterates the view already expressed by this house that it is ethically irresponsible to tolerate the prolongation of situations involving the dismantling of ships which are harmful to human health and the environment. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i believe it is essential to introduce a mechanism to finance environmentally friendly ship recycling, financed by charging ships that use eu ports. the rapporteur believes that the revenue generated would go to a fund which would be used as a premium for recycling yards which comply with the provisions of the regulation. i have supported this report in order to ensure that recycling and treatment of waste is carried out in an environmentally friendly way.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the negative impacts of recycling ships flying the flag of an eu member state need to be significantly reduced. however, i voted against amendments 31 and 32 which sought to introduce a recycling fee as the imposition of such a fee would significantly increase the costs of port calls in the eu, which would result in a degradation of their competitiveness in relation to neighbouring ports outside the eu (notably in the mediterranean, black sea, baltic sea). moreover, such a rate would correspond to the unilateral adoption of a regional measure by the eu which could jeopardise the ratification of the hong kong international convention by other parties such as china, india, bangladesh and pakistan, whose provisions are essential for the improvement of recycling conditions worldwide.

in writing. - turkey has an admirable history and culture. it is an important strategic partner of the union and is at a crossroads. the question of turkey's accession to the european union raises the problem, which policy-makers usually try to avoid, of defining what is fundamental to the union and what its limits are. i am aware that many europeans see turkey as something outside of european culture, history and civilization and that its accession to the union is seen as unnatural. some governments have expressed reservations along these lines, and i believe that this is relevant to the future accession of that country. apart from these considerations, the objective criteria to be met by turkey, which would allow its accession to be discussed in more concrete terms, are still far from being met and have even been met with progress and setbacks. europe must be able to encourage turkey to continue along the path it has chosen and give it concrete reasons for hoping for a serious, productive and stable relationship with europe and for a closer relationship between its institutions and its citizens.

in writing. − the macroeconomic imbalance procedure is a policy instrument introduced with the six pack and constitutes an important pillar of economic governance in the euro area designed to prevent and correct macroeconomic imbalances in the member states, with particular attention to imbalances with potential spillover effects between countries. as part of the regulation of this procedure, the european commission should submit, for consideration by the competent committees of the european parliament and the council, suggestions on plans to establish and adapt the indicators and thresholds. however, in november 2012, an indicator was added, a situation in which the council was consulted and parliament was only informed, which was regretted by the latter institution. parliament calls on the european commission to fully respect its status as co-legislator in the field of multilateral surveillance, as provided for, inter alia, in articles 121 (6) and 136 tfeu, and to treat parliament on an equal footing with the council with regard to all union acts in this field. i therefore support this motion for a resolution.
in writing. − as part of the adoption of the first economic governance package, a set of 10 indicators was selected against which the european commission should assess the macroeconomic performance of each member state and, according to the parameters selected, decide whether or not an imbalance exists that should be corrected. according to the adopted regulation, any amendment or subsequent inclusion of indicators in the original list should be agreed in advance and communicated to the european parliament. however, this was not the case when the european commission adopted a new indicator in november 2012, which aims to ensure that intra-institutional agreements are respected and always observed, in the name of good intra-institutional relations and respect for community law.
in writing. the motion for a resolution which we have just voted on, tabled following an oral question by mrs sharon bowles on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, concerns the final version of the indicator panel for the procedure on macroeconomic imbalances. in november 2011, the commission added a new indicator on the growth rate of financial liabilities to the above-mentioned panel. under the current regulations, the commission should have consulted the european parliament (ep) before publishing the new indicator and the related alert mechanism, as the ep has the same rights as the council under the lisbon treaty. although the commission claims that the ep was consulted, the truth is that on 19 november 2012 we were informed that there was one more indicator and we were waiting to be consulted. months passed and it was only on the eve of publication that we learned about the new indicator. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because, without calling into question the need for macroeconomic quality control, i believe that the commission has not treated the council and parliament on an equal footing.

in writing. − in the field of aviation, international relations between member states (ms) and third countries are governed by bilateral air services agreements, which include a 'designation clause' allowing a third country to refuse, withdraw or suspend licences or authorisations granted to an air carrier designated by a member state. in 2002, the court of justice of the european union (eu) ruled that the 'designation clause' infringes eu law. in june 2003, the council authorised the european commission to negotiate so-called horizontal agreements with third countries, thereby allowing all eu carriers to benefit from the right of establishment and thus opening up access, without discrimination, to air links between the eu and third countries. in the present case, sri lanka has signed 15 bilateral agreements the provisions of which have to be replaced or supplemented by the provisions of a single agreement concluded on behalf of the eu. thus, article 2 provides that in exercising its rights, sri lanka shall not discriminate between air carriers of member states on grounds of nationality. i therefore support this recommendation.
in writing. - i agree with the conclusion of this agreement so that european airlines benefit from the right of establishment and non-discriminatory access to air links between the european union and sri lanka.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this recommendation. the conclusion of this agreement between the european union and the democratic socialist republic of sri lanka will allow the provisions of the 15 bilateral agreements signed between member states and sri lanka to be replaced by a single, more comprehensive agreement concluded on behalf of the european union. the horizontal agreement concluded on behalf of the european union commits sri lanka not to discriminate against air carriers of member states on the basis of their nationality. this allows all carriers in the european union to enjoy the right of establishment and access to the land routes between the european union and sri lanka in equal circumstances.
in writing. - the so-called 'designation clause' infringed community law and was contrary to the principle of equality between aircraft operators. the court of justice ruled in this respect and therefore the air service agreements in which it was incorporated had to be amended. the eu-sri lanka agreement is one of the legal instruments that needs to be revised. the parties have agreed to this and parliament must give its consent. i do so in the hope that the relationship between europe and sri lanka - which dates back to the 16th century and the arrival of the portuguese in that asian country - will be strengthened and grow to the benefit of both peoples and their economies.
in writing. - mr petri sarvamaa has presented us with a recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement on certain aspects of air services between the european union and the democratic socialist republic of sri lanka. according to the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), international relations between member states (eu) and third countries in the field of aviation, so-called bilateral air service agreements, should be established at eu level so that there is no discrimination against community carriers established in the territory of a member state but owned and controlled by nationals of other member states. in this connection, and taking into account the opinion of the committee on transport and tourism, i voted in favour of this recommendation that the 15 bilateral agreements signed with sri lanka be replaced by a single agreement drawn up on behalf of the eu so that sri lanka does not discriminate against eu air carriers on grounds of nationality.
in writing. − international relations between member states and third countries in the field of aviation are traditionally regulated by bilateral air services agreements, which are drawn up and concluded between the two parties. in the present case, sri lanka has signed 15 bilateral agreements, the relevant provisions of which are now replaced or supplemented by the provisions of a single agreement concluded on behalf of the eu, allowing all eu carriers to benefit from the right of establishment and giving them access to air links between the eu and these countries. as we have said in previous agreements of this kind with other countries, the aim is to expand and liberalize the air services market by encouraging monopolistic concentration in the increasingly privatised sector, a factor which contributes greatly to worsening working conditions, to the withdrawal of rights from workers in this sector and to the degradation of the services provided, including safety conditions. although portugal has no bilateral agreement with sri lanka, we consider that these agreements not only prevent member states from defending their flag carriers, but also represent a reduction of the sovereignty of countries in a strategic sector, compromising the safeguarding of national interests.
