in writing. − the historical archives of the european institutions are an integral part of the cultural heritage of the european union and a primary source of historical information. i therefore consider it essential that information on the european institutions be preserved, that all european citizens be given access to the historical archives of the union through public consultation and that research on the process of european integration and the values of the union be supported in this way too. the decision to concentrate the historical archives of the institutions at the european university institute (eui) in florence dates from 1984, when the european parliament, the commission and the council signed the first agreement with the eui. the proposal in this report confirms the role of the ieu as the manager of historical archives and creates a legal and financial basis for the partnership between the union and the ieu, which is why i voted in favour. henceforth, with the exception of the european central bank and the court of justice by reason of the nature of their functions, the deposit of the historical archives of the union in the eui by all european institutions shall become mandatory.

in writing. − the historical archives of the eu institutions represent an important source of information for the history and heritage of the european union. it is therefore essential to provide access to archives in a way that allows public consultation, preserves information on the eu institutions and supports research into the history of european integration. the proposal does not alter the main elements of regulation (eec, euratom) no 354/83 as regards content, such as the definition of historical archives or the type of documents and the period from which they become public. the proposal provides for minor amendments to the existing regulation, in particular the obligation for all eu institutions (except the court of justice and the european central bank) to deposit their historical archives in the eui, the principle that each institution retains ownership of its archives, the system for financing archives, the protection of personal data contained in archives and the provision of archives by electronic means wherever possible.

in writing. − the directive on takeover bids, adopted in 2004, had a transposition deadline of may 2006. although this transposition was carried out by the member states, the fact is that the implementation of the directive coincided with the outbreak of the financial and sovereign debt crisis in europe, which led to a cooling of the merger and acquisition market. these operations often require sophisticated financing, and with the difficulty of accessing credit, the market does not work as easily. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the public authorities. thus, it can be seen that between 2009 and 2010, the intra-european merger and acquisition market was virtually paralysed and is recovering very slowly. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that such market conditions do not allow a proper assessment of the application of the directive, and that 'more relevant data are needed not only to determine the need for amendments to the directive but also to define precisely the concrete measures to be taken in the future in the field of harmonisation'.
in writing. − in april 2004, the directive 2004/25/ec on public procurement in europe was published in the official journal of the european union (eu) with the aim of creating harmonised rules between all member states (em). the report by klaus-heiner lehne analyses the implementation of this directive, the provisions of which member states were obliged to transpose into national legislation by may 2006. the rapporteur considers that the onset of the economic and financial crisis in 2007 has added to the problems of implementing the rules laid down in the directive as 'the intra-european market for company controls has been virtually paralysed and is recovering very slowly'. the example of the uk market is given where takeover bids fell by 50% between 2010 and 2011. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that more relevant data is needed in this area in order to assess the need to amend directive 2004/25/ec and what concrete measures should be taken in the field of harmonisation.
in writing. − the directive provides that member states should take measures to protect holders of securities, and in particular holders of minority interests, following a change of control of companies. however, as the report states, the mandatory bid rule is the main provision for the protection of minority shareholders. according to an external study, all member states provide for exceptions to this rule. on the basis of this study, it is recognised that these derogations are often used to protect the interests of majority shareholders. however, no effort is being made to protect minority shareholders, in particular by typifying and reducing the number of situations in which this rule can be derogated from by the member states. as regards workers for whom the announcement of one of these transactions constitutes a threat to their jobs or the first sign of the deterioration of the conditions under which they carry out their activity, the directive merely states that adequate information should also be provided to the company's workers' representatives. it's not enough. the rapporteur has not incorporated the suggestions of the committee on employment and social affairs that workers' rights should be maintained throughout the whole procurement process. for these reasons, we cannot vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − after decades of failed attempts, the directive was finally adopted by the european parliament at second reading at the end of 2003 and published in the official journal in april 2004. member states had until may 2006 to transpose the provisions of the directive into their national legislation. the fact that member states have transposed the provisions of the directive shows the clear need, both in the past and today, for harmonised rules on public procurement in europe. however, it has been difficult to assess the implementation of the directive adequately in the face of the crisis we have been going through. it will therefore be necessary to wait to assess the need for amendments to the current directive.

in writing. - i think we are now in the presence of a proposal for a future regulation which enjoys a high degree of consensus in parliament. clearly, what we have heard and despite the limitations that each committee or political group may have encountered, in the end we have a highly consensual position of parliament. i believe that this time too the convergence with the commission proposal, as we have seen on many other occasions, but here i want to emphasize that it has been particularly high. the result, as the commissioner has already said, is that europe is at the forefront, and very advanced in terms of protection and in terms of ensuring the requirements they have to meet, they have to meet all the activities of exploration and exploitation of offshore platforms, both in relation to oil and gas. to put limits on the ability to incorporate new areas into new sources would be an unfortunate mistake and what you have to do is to take steps in the direction that has been taken: greater security and greater guarantees. that is clearly the way to go, in my opinion.
in writing. − in the eu, more than 90% of oil and 60% of gas are extracted from offshore operations, most of which take place in the north sea. given the importance of oil extraction to the countries that extract it and the dangers involved (as can be seen from the terrible consequences of accidents), it is essential that the union creates the conditions for the safest possible oil exploitation. to this end, it is important that there is adequate legislation with the basic safety standards for offshore oil and gas production, ensuring the safety of their extraction and supply in the eu. as a portuguese, i cannot help recalling the prestige disaster which deeply affected the galician coast, with consequences that extended beyond the portuguese and french coasts, and i would draw attention to the fact that the measures now proposed should not be confined to oil exploration and extraction but also to its transport and supply, knowing that oil tanker disasters are, unfortunately, more frequent than we would like. it is also important to review safety standards in order to reduce the likelihood of such disasters.
in writing. - environmental protection is on the agenda. it's the quality of life, ours and our grandchildren's, that's at stake. we therefore have an obligation to leave our future generations a planet at least as healthy as we found it. our dependence on fossil fuels - despite the increase in renewable energy - remains enormous and we are exploiting ever deeper deposits. the recent disaster in the gulf of mexico is an example of the lack of safety that exists in many offshore oil and gas exploration, development and production activities, as well as the devastating environmental consequences that these accidents cause. the report by mr belet is on the right track in calling for greater safety on the high seas. it is not just the safety of workers that is at stake but also the protection of the environment. i voted in favour of this report because it contains most of the proposals put forward by the various committees requiring that member states and licensing authorities can only authorise new farms after rigorous environmental impact studies and other aspects that minimise the risks of an accident.
in writing. − a number of accidents related to offshore oil and gas exploration, production and production have drawn attention to the need to guard against the consequences of these activities at various levels. the dramatic example of the deepwater horizon accident in april 2010, which killed 11 workers and triggered an environmental catastrophe, is a demonstration of this. this proposal for a directive states that it lays down minimum requirements for the prevention of major accidents and the limitation of the consequences of major accidents in offshore oil and gas operations. it considers that, as general principles of risk management, member states should require operators to ensure that all appropriate measures are taken to prevent the occurrence of major accidents associated with offshore oil and gas operations and to take responsibility for environmental damage caused. these requirements were, however, weakened during the negotiating process, which merited the opposition of our group. we supported a moratorium on all fossil resource activities in the arctic, as well as in areas considered to be geologically unstable or ecologically sensitive, which was ultimately rejected by the majority. for these reasons, we rejected the final proposal.
in writing. − accidents on offshore oil production platforms are extremely dangerous. an example of this was the april 20, 2010 accident, an explosion on the deepwater horizon that caused the death of 11 people working on the rig and a hydrocarbon spill equivalent to about 4.9 million barrels (780,000 m3) of crude oil. this accident also prompted a review of eu policies: the european commission has immediately launched a safety assessment of offshore oil and gas exploration activities in european waters. it was concluded that additional action was needed to ensure the dissemination of good practice already existing in the regulatory regimes of some eu member states across the eu through an advanced eu-wide framework. that is what we have achieved by adopting this report, and that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − on 17 september 2011, the commission presented a proposal for a regulation on concrete measures that could address the disparities and general fragmentation between member states' practices and legislation on safety in offshore oil and gas exploration, production and production. the rapporteur, considering the issues that the regulation presented by the commission may raise as regards the repeal and amendments to national legislation on this matter, recommended the change of the legal form 'regulation' to 'directive'. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the body. only an advanced framework at eu level can ensure the dissemination of good practice in offshore oil and gas exploration. i voted in favour of this in the hope that the regulatory effort on the safety aspects of offshore drilling will prevent tragedies like the one that occurred on the deepwater horizon platform.
in writing. − the 2010 deepwater horizon accident off the coast of the united states and its effects on the marine environment and humans have alerted the union to the need for legislation on the safety of offshore oil and gas exploration, exploitation and production. the aim is to disseminate best practice already existing in the member states and to create a european regulatory framework. the proposal also focuses on strengthening preventive measures and the union's capacity to respond to a disaster. the european parliament called for full independence between the body responsible for the safety of operations and the body managing the economic development of activities; the extension of the mandate of the european maritime safety agency; greater legal certainty for licensing laws; and closer cooperation between member states and third countries. the blue economy is a clear commitment of the union, which must be accompanied by preventive measures to cope with possible disasters.
in writing. - among the initiatives proposed in this report, i would stress the importance of investing in scientific research, technological development and demonstration in the field of renewable energy in order to reduce its costs for both producers and consumers. parliament stressed the importance of energy, proposing an increase from 7.5% to 8.4% of the horizon 2020 budget for the societal energy challenge, alongside an ambitious and very comprehensive work programme. i would like to stress the importance of all measures to reduce the costs of renewable energy in order to reconcile the objectives of security of energy supply, combating climate change and the competitiveness of european companies. only then will it be possible to set objectives that are both ambitious and realistic.
in writing. − sustainable growth without undermining competitiveness requires a consistent energy policy, the proper functioning of the emission allowance market and the promotion of national projects that contribute to the community's objectives of reducing emissions and increasing energy independence and clean energy production. in this context, the production of renewable energy is of crucial importance and should be encouraged and exploited consistently. i am proud that my country is a good example in this area (in 2011, in portugal, 24.9% of total energy was renewable while for the same year the eu average was only 13%) and i believe that this should be a model for other european states to follow.
in writing. - the report under consideration, by mr herbert reul, deals with the current challenges and opportunities for renewable energy in the eu's internal energy market. renewable energy sources not only contribute to combating climate change and increasing europe's energy independence, but also bring additional environmental benefits. a binding target for renewable energy sources in 2030 will signal to investors that renewable energy remains a priority. at the same time, a binding target will be a stimulus that can boost job creation, security of supply, green growth and technological and industrial leadership. it is important that countries which are well placed to meet the long-term targets on this matter, notably portugal, have this stimulus to continue on this path. it is essential that eu energy policy is geared towards the development, deployment and distribution of renewable energy with ambitious renewable energy targets for member states by 2030 in order to achieve a renewable energy economy by 2050.
in writing. − this report aims to boost the uptake of renewable energy sources (res) and to contribute to reducing europe's energy dependence on conventional energy sources, while also reducing greenhouse gas emissions. the european commission is invited to assess the costs and benefits of introducing a binding 2030 erf target. we support ambitious targets in this area. we support reducing dependence on fossil fuels, diversifying sources and increasing their sustainability. but we don't have an idyllic view of this issue. the solution to the energy problems we face is not just a transition to res. the existing models of production and consumption, i.e. the way in which the economy is organised and the energy consumption associated with them, must be questioned. it is important to reduce these consumption by changing these models. it should be borne in mind that even rdfs can have significant environmental impacts. some countries, such as portugal, are already close to some of the proposed targets (which were ultimately rejected during the vote). this does not mean that much remains to be done in the field of rationalising supply and consumption and minimising environmental impacts. public control of the energy sector is an essential factor in achieving these objectives.
in writing. − res, together with energy efficiency measures and flexible and intelligent infrastructure, are the 'no-compromise' options and will in future constitute a growing share of europe's energy supply, in terms of electricity supply, heating (which accounts for almost half of the eu's total energy demand) and cooling, and the transport sector, reducing europe's energy dependence on conventional energy sources. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's energy policy and its implementation in the member states. renewable energy sources not only contribute to combating climate change and increasing europe's energy independence, but also bring additional environmental benefits in terms of reducing air pollution, waste generation and water use, as well as other risks inherent in other forms of energy production. this is why it is so important to replace fossil fuels with more environmentally friendly sources of energy.
in writing. − the commission communication 'renewable energies: a decisive player in the european energy market' sets out a strategic framework for renewable energy policies in the european union. the communication stresses that renewable energy policies must ensure that such sources can form an integral part of the european energy market with limited but effective support where needed and with transport solutions capable of providing a flexible back-up to the electricity supply in europe. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of renewable energy sources, in particular in the transport sector. the european parliament's document calls on the commission to achieve greater convergence in the design of the european support system for renewable energy for the period after 2020. i supported this report, which calls on the commission to evaluate the european support scheme for renewable energy sources (res) with a view to a more cost-effective framework and potential.
in the light of the recent developments in the field of the environment, the commission has adopted a communication on the environment and the environment in the european union. seven flagship initiatives were defined, one of them being 'a resource-efficient europe' which aims to have 20% of total energy produced from renewable energy sources. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that europe must improve its energy independence vis-à-vis third countries and diversify its energy sources, and must increasingly rely on environmentally friendly energy sources. although in 2011 portugal already produced 24.9% of its total energy from renewable energy sources, i believe that it is premature to set a binding target of 40 to 45% in europe by 2030.
in writing. − this is an own-initiative report which aims to promote the use of renewable energy sources in order to help reduce europe's energy dependence on conventional energy sources. these are intentions which seem to us to be correct, although it would be important to set amounts for public and private investment and to promote a general survey and mapping plan for the classification and quantification of renewable energy resources. we are concerned that they are throwing renewable energy into the european internal energy market, which calls into question the sovereignty of the member states in energy policy, since this is a strategic sector for a country's economy and for the definition of its related policies. the energy poverty that is currently being experienced in several eu countries, particularly in the electricity sector, is caused by the increase in energy prices caused by successive privatisations in the sector. in portugal, the privatisation of the sector has resulted in monopolization and successive price increases - for example, in 2012, they rose by 8,9% compared to the previous year - and also in the increase in company profits that exceed all forecasts. renewables, yes, of course, but not to create another multi-billion dollar business that exploits consumers.
in writing. − the seven western balkan applicant countries are at different stages of the process of becoming member states of the european union. although they have adopted much of the necessary legislation, in many cases this legislation is not being effectively implemented, particularly in the field of women's rights and gender equality. support for equal opportunities policies is of great importance, not only in the process of accession to the european union, but above all for the economic and social development of these countries. women in the western balkans should assume a prominent role in society through active participation and representation in political, economic and social life at all levels, including in decision-making. it should be noted that the population is not properly informed about the existing legislation and policies to promote gender equality. awareness should therefore be promoted through the media, public campaigns and education programmes. in these campaigns, particular emphasis should be placed on the fight against stereotypes, discrimination and domestic violence. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − it is extremely important that gender equality policies are implemented in the balkan countries which are in the process of joining the eu. it must be ensured that women are not discriminated against and do not encounter barriers to professional advancement in top positions in both the public and private sectors.
in writing. − croatia, albania, bosnia and herzegovina, the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, montenegro, kosovo and serbia are the western balkan countries which, although they are at different stages of the eu accession process and have already started to adopt some or, in some cases, most of the legislation necessary for the accession process, in many cases this legislation is not being effectively implemented. i note with concern that in most of these countries women continue to be underrepresented in the labour market and in decision-making at economic and political levels, and that there are also marked gender gaps in wages and pensions. it is essential that in the accession process of these countries, priority be given to progress in the fight against discrimination, corruption and organised crime, especially given that 30% of the victims of crossborder trafficking in the eu are, in the vast majority, women and girls from the balkan region. it is important to carry out information and awareness-raising campaigns among the local population on existing legislation and policies to promote gender equality in order to combat stereotypes, all forms of discrimination and domestic violence.
in writing. - the conflicts in the balkans have been marked by several serious cases of sexual violence, mainly against women. we still remember with horror the reports that showed the systematic and premeditated use of rape as a weapon of war in that conflict. in all the regions of the continent which are candidates for accession, as in the european union itself, countries are required to pay scrupulous attention to equality between men and women and to ensure that women participate fully in the social, community and political life of their states. this requirement must be constant and their full and effective participation. i regret that, in all its aspects, this worthwhile subject is being used to pressure the acceding states to accept the liberalization of practices such as abortion. the union, in its desired diversity, must reject agendas which are fractured by this.
in writing. − the policy of enlargement of the european union (eu) to the east has contributed not only to the pacification of the balkan region, but also to economic growth and the implementation of democracy in that territory. unfortunately, history shows us that non-democratic regimes are those where the absence of gender equality is most felt. throughout its history, the eu has demanded that all partnership agreements respect the principles and values enshrined in its charter of fundamental rights, so as to oblige the applicant countries to gradually commit themselves to the primacy of freedom and human rights. among the measures recommended is the promotion of greater participation of women in public life. i voted in favour of the report by mrs marije cornelissen on women's rights in the balkan accession countries because, in addition to acknowledging the efforts made by most of these countries in this field, it contains a set of recommendations which will help each country to improve its performance in eradicating violence against women, their integration into the labour market and legal bodies, and their participation in politics and involvement in key sectors of society.
in writing. − in 2008, the european parliament adopted a report on this same subject. now repeat the assessment. as the rapporteurs themselves point out, this evaluation focuses more on the legislative mechanisms and the implementation of certain provisions than on an assessment of the situation of women in these countries. it is worth noting that many of the problems attributed to countries in the process of joining the eu are the same as those experienced by women in eu countries on a daily basis. these are problems that result from the dominant national and european policies. lack of protection for women victims of violence, high female employment rates, lack of access to sexual and reproductive health services, high levels of wage inequality are just a few examples. we disagree with the attempt to impose certain measures and models which tend to disregard the legitimate choices of the peoples of these countries. as for kosovo, its inclusion in the group of countries is unacceptable, since it has not been recognised as an independent country by either the un or several eu member states.
in writing. - i abstained from voting on this report. i am opposed in principle to the stipulation of quotas for women in any occupation. invariably, the reports that come to us from the femm committee refer to quotas, regardless of the subjects covered in the report. i think that this matter should be dealt with in another way, otherwise i fear we will never be able to reach a satisfactory solution. that is why i abstain.
in writing. − this owninitiative report notes that the balkan candidate countries have already adopted a large part of the relevant legislation. however, gender equality is not fully ensured in practice. the population of most countries ignores existing policies to promote gender equality. this gap between the law and its effective implementation must be bridged by awareness-raising campaigns to combat discrimination and stereotypes, alongside the growing emancipation of women, who, as they remain under-represented in the labour market, are compulsorily excluded from economic and political decision-making. in this respect, this document, which i welcome, calls for the reasonable use of pre-accession aid instruments in projects relating to women's rights and gender equality, in particular in the mechanisms and tools for the effective implementation of laws and policies in this field.
in writing. − measures to guarantee women's rights and gender equality provisions need to be more effective and enforcement mechanisms need to be monitored. i am voting in favour of this report which aims to specifically address the mechanisms for implementing women's rights in the countries applying for accession to the european union, presenting concrete measures rather than just listing the problems relating to women's rights and gender equality in general. finally, i would like to stress that i voted against the assumptions set out in the report which aimed at introducing quotas in the various countries analysed, since this is a discretionary and punitive measure for women, because with work, dedication and their own merit they can achieve important positions of democratic representation.
in writing. - it is clear that equality between men and women is an objective which must be achieved in any society which calls itself democratic. unfortunately, many of the problems which this report intends to imput as unacceptable in a country in the process of joining the eu are the same problems which women in eu countries experience on a daily basis, and which are a consequence of right-wing policies and the result of the eu's guidelines for cutting public funding. lack of protection for women victims of violence, high female employment rates, lack of access to sexual and reproductive health services, high levels of wage inequality are some examples. on the other hand, we do not think it is appropriate for the eu to want to impose political regime models - such as the introduction of the quota system in political parties or in elections to national assemblies - which are the decision of the peoples of the countries concerned alone. finally, it is unacceptable that the list of countries addressed includes kosovo, a us protectorate not recognised as an independent country by the un or by five eu member states.
in writing. - the good functioning of democracies depends to a large extent on freedom of the media. this freedom is not only operationalized through non-interference by governments in the media, but also through protective measures such as against conflict of interest between political officeholders and media control offices.
in writing. − freedom of the media is a cornerstone of the values enshrined in the treaties, namely democracy, pluralism and the rule of law itself, and plays a crucial role in their existence and survival. the fundamental rights of citizens to information and freedom of expression can only be guaranteed through the freedom and pluralism of the media, which allows journalists and the media to exercise their right and duty to inform citizens in a transparent, fair and neutral manner. it is essential to ensure that there is transparent legislation in all member states, which ensures, on the one hand, the credibility and coherence of the european space and, on the other hand, adequate protection of freedom of expression and information and media pluralism, in particular with regard to national rules on media ownership and transparency, concentration, conflicts of interest with political office and economic pressures and the independence of media supervisory authorities. i am concerned that, in the context of the current economic crisis, the number of journalists working in precarious conditions of employment and with poor access to social security has increased alarmingly.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this report which proposes the revision of the media services directive, mechanisms to ensure the independence of directors and boards of directors and measures to prevent media concentration. for pluralism, freedom and independence of the media are essential to the healthy functioning of any democracy! i would stress the importance of promoting a dual european audiovisual system in which public and private companies and the professionals who are part of them can carry out their activities, immune to any kind of political, economic or other pressures, guided by the protection of journalistic competition, information and the diversity of opinions, in full freedom of expression. i would also like to stress the important role of independent media regulators at national level in safeguarding media pluralism and independence and ensuring the objectivity, impartiality and accountability of the media in the member states. in this respect, i believe that greater cooperation, sharing of experience and best practice between entities through the european regulatory bodies platform is a positive development.
in writing. - it is fair to acknowledge that the european union enjoys a high degree of freedom of the media. this is unquestionable, especially when compared with other parts of the world. however, such a state of affairs should not distract policy-makers from the need to help maintain and strengthen it. democracy would be short-lived without a free and critical media. i hope that the crisis we are in will be an opportunity to strengthen the role of the media in monitoring policy-makers, particularly those in europe who often seem to be too distant from public opinion. the democratization of european political life will also require a freer and stronger media at this level.
in writing. - the media are a fundamental pillar of the european community and are therefore protected by the charter of fundamental rights of the european union (cdfeu), which defends pluralism and freedom of the press. although freedom of the press is a fundamental right, the truth is that sometimes in some member states it is not always recognised as such and many journalists are victims of pressure and harassment by member states. if citizens have a right to be informed, it is necessary that all member states respect the legislation protecting journalists in their physical integrity and freedom of expression. the report, drawn up by mrs renate weber on the general framework for media freedom in the european union, contains 30 recommendations which aim to clarify this matter and call not only for a reflection on the powers of the member states but above all for them to play their role in guaranteeing the existence of a free media. in fact, the hague treaty requires it as a criterion for accession. because freedom of the press is fundamental in a modern society, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - this report addresses a number of important and topical issues, such as the concentration of media ownership, the precariousness of journalists, economic dependence, political pressure, censorship, manipulation and the lack of pluralism. unfortunately, many of them fall short of what is needed to treat them. we agree with several of the principles set out in this report, such as the defence of collective bargaining. unfortunately, nothing is said about the process under way which, through various channels (the euro plus pact, the budgetary treaty, eu-imf programmes, etc.), is contributing to its destruction. and more could be said about the attack on the working conditions and labour rights of the professionals in the sector. the absence of any reference to control mechanisms and to measures (or proposals for measures) which would even minimally guarantee compliance with the principles stated is also noted. that is why we abstained.
in writing. − freedom of the media is a cornerstone of the values enshrined in the treaties, namely democracy, pluralism and respect for minority rights. freedom of the media, pluralism and the independence of journalism are essential elements for the proper exercise of the media service throughout the union and in particular in the single market, and therefore any restrictions on freedom of the media, pluralism and the independence of journalism constitute restrictions both on freedom of opinion and on economic freedom. journalists should not be subject to pressure from owners, managers and public authorities, nor to financial constraints. the european union must do everything possible to ensure that the fundamental right to freedom of expression and information, and to freedom and pluralism of the media, is respected, guaranteed, protected and promoted. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − according to article 10 of the european convention on human rights, the authorities have positive obligations to protect freedom of expression as one of the prerequisites for a functioning democracy. the effective exercise of certain freedoms does not depend solely on non-interference by the state, often requiring positive protective measures, such as: a legislative framework preventing conflicts of interest resulting from the amalgamation of political office and control over the media; a legal framework preventing concentration of ownership and abuse of a dominant position, as well as infiltration of secret intelligence agents into newsrooms; or legislation protecting journalists from pressure, intimidation and persecution. in summary, the report highlights two aspects of media independence and pluralism: the freedom of the media to provide impartial information and the freedom of citizens to access it. i supported the report calling on the commission to review the audiovisual media services directive (avmsd) by assessing the possibility of extending its scope to minimum standards relating to the protection and promotion of the fundamental right to freedom of expression and information.
in writing. − the european parliament calls on the member states and the european union to respect, guarantee, protect and promote the fundamental right to freedom of expression and information, and to freedom and pluralism of the media, and consequently to refrain from any threats to media freedom. stressing the importance of ensuring the independence of the media in the context of the general framework of freedom in the eu, i voted in favour of the document in the european parliament.
in writing. - we can subscribe to all these pretty, correct and defensible statements of principle, based on the alleged goodness of what is enshrined in the treaties, as if the real problems, also pointed out in the report, had nothing to do with the political orientation that the treaties impose and pursue. it's the usual hypocrisy. just look at what is said about collective bargaining to confirm it. it is not enough to say that it must be respected, nothing about the process of its actual liquidation (and the attempt to liquidate the unions) that is being carried out throughout the eu. it refers to the concentration of the media, the precariousness of journalists, economic dependence, political pressure, censorship, manipulation, lack of pluralism, etc., as if these situations were dissociable from the political and economic project of the eu. nothing is said about copyright, particularly when it comes to making information available on the internet/search engines. ngos are valued, without prejudice to the use which, in many cases, results from their instrumentalisation. and it is trying to refer to european bodies aspects of the regulation of media - as when it is proposed to harmonize the statute of national regulatory authorities - which are and should remain the responsibility of each country.
mr president, the proposal we have adopted today on the sustainability of pensions has several fundamental problems: the first concerns raising the retirement age so that contributions can be extended, as if unemployment were not the main problem in the european union; the second concerns raising contributions for those who work by reducing employers' contributions. to include the private sector as a guarantee of sustainability for reforms and pensions is to bring social security schemes into the casino economy once and for all. in the face of a voracious financial market that knows no bounds, people are being urged to retire and retire and to buy financial products so that they can have a decent life after a working life. to transform public systems of reform in this way is to transform them into pensions for the poor. contrary to what most of you have argued, dignity at the end of a contributory life can only be guaranteed by universal public systems which do not cut the chain of solidarity between generations and not by the model that has been adopted here, which is unacceptable from all points of view.
in writing. − the ageing population is putting at risk the financial sustainability of the pension system in all member states. it is therefore urgent to reshape pension systems in the light of economic and demographic developments in europe. i agree with the need to link retirement age with increased life expectancy, and to improve access to lifelong learning, reconciliation of work, family and private life and the promotion of active ageing. i also support the development of supplementary retirement savings to improve the income of pensioners. it is important to stress that gender disparities in employment, wages, career breaks and parttime work have a negative impact on women's pensions. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of life of women and men in the eu, and has recently launched a new initiative to improve the quality of life of women and men in the eu. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the ageing of the population represents a major challenge for pension schemes in the member states. it is a problem with profound economic and budgetary consequences in the eu, which requires immediate responses, especially given that the baby boom generation is now reaching retirement age and the working population in europe will decrease every year over the next few decades. the weak economic growth, budget deficits and debt levels, as well as financial instability and low employment have further aggravated the situation and it is urgent to develop and implement comprehensive strategies to adapt pension systems to changing economic and demographic circumstances, setting out a clear agenda to make pensions adequate and sustainable in the long term. we cannot jeopardize the right to a dignified retirement for people who have worked all their lives. but europe's social and economic success is also dependent on the success of national pension policies and reforms, as it will decisively affect the eu's ability to achieve two of the five europe 2020 targets, namely to raise the employment rate to 75% and reduce the number of people at risk of poverty by at least 20 million.
in writing. − the increase in average life expectancy, combined with the reversal of the age pyramid in the eu and the global crisis in which european economies are immersed, pose major challenges to an ageing society which will have to ensure that its elderly people have adequate living conditions and a role which, in many cases, can (and should) be active. faced with the real threat of the bankruptcy of traditional pension systems, states must take the necessary measures - not just raising the retirement age - to safeguard social security schemes in a frontal and courageous manner. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the pension system. in addition, the aim should be to make the retirement age dependent on the average life expectancy.
in writing. − all citizens want to receive a secure and sustainable retirement pension that will enable them to live out their final years with quality. that is the purpose of their work and of their discounts. if for many years this was an acquired reality, with the reversal of the age pyramid and the economic and financial crisis that has befallen us, the acquired rights have ceased to be so and the pensioners and pensioners have seen their incomes drastically reduced. i believe that intergenerational relations must remain the basis (pillar 1) of reforms in the future. however, the inevitability of the reversal of the age pyramid requires us to equalise the increase in the retirement age - as is already the case in some member states - and to encourage the use of supplementary retirement savings schemes, so as to enable all pensioners to live out their final years with dignity. i voted in favour of the report by mrs ria oomen-ruijten because i agree that there is a need for greater awareness of the problems of the financial sustainability of social security systems so that we can all have an old age with a minimum quality of life.
in writing. - if the guidelines advocated in this report (approved by the psd, ps and cds) were to be implemented, it would deal a brutal blow to the public, solidarity-based and universal social security system. the objectives are clear: to raise the retirement age, to reduce employer contributions to public social security systems by decapitalizing them, and to support the business of retirement savings plans sold by banks and from which they make millions. all under the ever-invoked and cheated pretext of sustainability. they cite the increase in average life expectancy (and the resulting burden on social security systems), but they forget that labour productivity has also increased significantly, and it is now possible to produce much more wealth with the same work. they want to take away a growing share of the wealth from those who generate it, also by stealing the right to social security. how can they forget the effects that the policies in place, as well as the unprecedented levels of unemployment they create, have on the sustainability of the system. the intention is to transform public, universal and solidarity-based pension systems into private systems, to which only those with the financial capacity to buy certain financial products will have access. obviously, we voted against it.
in writing. - pensions are being squeezed in all eu countries. euro area governments are implementing austerity measures to comply with the stability and growth pact (sgp) by balancing revenue and expenditure, or are being forced to make drastic cuts in an attempt to reduce high deficits. in addition, the population is ageing in all member states. in general, while recognising and preserving the responsibilities of the member states and the social partners, we must now create appropriate, safe and lasting systems which also contribute to greater market mobility and freedom of movement, systems which offer solutions for the present and the future. it is important that people are informed about the pensions they expect to receive. providing people with information about their pension income leads to better understanding, more careful design of preventive measures and greater accountability. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the sustainability of public-pillar pensions, i.e. government-funded through the pension sharing system based on solidarity between taxpayers, is threatened by the mutually influential development of demographic and economic indices in europe. the rapporteur notes that fertility rates remain low and average life expectancy has increased, but that there is one inescapable fact: at present, there are four active people for every pensioner, and in 2060 there will be only two active people for every pensioner. the commission therefore foresees that more people will have to work harder and longer. weighing in on the clarity of statistical forecasts, which point not only to a progressive decline in average labour force participation but also to a scenario of low economic growth, the legislative agenda must take political responsibility for a future with adequate, secure and sustainable pensions. i therefore voted in favour of the own-initiative report, which calls on the european commission to strengthen eu legislative coordination in the field of pensions.
in writing. - the proposal we have adopted today on the sustainability of pensions has several fundamental problems: the first concerns raising the retirement age so that contributions can be extended, as if unemployment were not the main problem in the european union; the second concerns raising contributions for those who work by reducing employers' contributions. to include the private sector as a guarantee of sustainability for reforms and pensions is to bring social security schemes into the casino economy once and for all. in the face of a voracious financial market that knows no bounds, people are being urged to retire and retire and to buy financial products so that they can have a decent life after a working life. to transform public systems of reform in this way is to transform them into pensions for the poor. contrary to what most of you have argued, dignity at the end of a contributory life can only be guaranteed by universal public systems which do not cut the chain of solidarity between generations and not by the model that has been adopted here, which is unacceptable from all points of view.
in writing. − several pension systems in several member states are experiencing serious difficulties in financial sustainability due to the fact that discounts are becoming lower and capital needs are increasing. in order to make social security more sustainable, i am in favour of creating pension plans that combine public investment with collective and individual retirement savings plans. i would also stress the importance of maintaining the public system which guarantees a decent quality of life for retired workers.
in writing. − the report on an agenda for adequate, secure and sustainable pensions, which follows the european commission's white paper, focuses on two areas of eu intervention on pension issues: the european semester (implementation of country-specific recommendations on pension reform) and the strengthening of the internal pension market (third pillar). the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of workers against the risks of exposure to carcinogens and to the use of carcinogens in the manufacture of foodstuffs. the real objectives of this report are clear: (1) to raise the retirement age, robbing every man and woman, at the end of a life of work and sacrifice, of a precious chunk of time that would still allow them to live as fully as possible; (2) to reduce employer contributions to public social security systems and to support the business of the retirement savings plans sold by banks, from which they make millions. it is a question of transforming public, universal and solidarity-based pension systems into private systems, to which only those with the financial capacity to buy financial products have access. surely this is not the way to make the pension system more sustainable!

in writing. − this is the second year that the european parliament has adopted an annual report on taxation, the aim of which is to help make tax collection more effective by making it a tool for promoting economic growth, at a time when crisis and consolidation dominate european discussions. the eu loses around €1 billion every year (€2,000 per european citizen) due to tax fraud and evasion. making collection more efficient is becoming urgent and central to the process of european economic recovery. one step towards this goal is to promote greater tax coordination between member states (ms), with greater exchanges of tax information and the promotion of tax planning that promotes sustainable growth. the report proposes a 'tax snake' system which, while not harmonising the tax systems of the member states, allows them to be coordinated in the light of tax increases and reductions. tax simplification should also be part of a strategy for a stronger single market in these matters. i shall vote in favour of this text because i consider it to be a positive proposal at a time when the issues of double taxation and tax evasion are major problems, causing significant budgetary losses in the eu.
in writing. - first of all, i would like to remind you that fiscal policy remains a matter of national sovereignty and that the different tax systems of the member states must be respected. however, the internal market barriers, uncertainties and misunderstandings resulting from the legal loopholes should be resolved in a timely manner. i therefore vote in favour of this report, whose proposals are designed to make tax collection in the member states more effective and to make it a catalyst for economic growth. i believe it is essential to ensure fiscal discipline and to carry out structural reforms appropriate adjustment of fiscal policies in the short, medium and long term in order to restore the credibility of fiscal policy and to reduce sovereign debts, especially when the crisis and fiscal consolidation in the member states is a current topic in european discussions. i would also like to stress the proposal to create a 'tax snake' system which will not allow for the harmonization of the different tax systems in force in the member states but rather for close coordination, in a continuous and transparent manner, which includes tax reductions and increases in the national structures.
in writing. − fiscal policy is a central element in the need to unlock the eu's economic potential. fiscal policies, while not necessarily lacking harmonisation, must be coordinated and used intelligently, particularly when the eu urgently needs to regain its place as the leading player on the world market. today, more than ever, in countries like my own, portugal, fiscal policy must be seen and conceived as a motor to support economic development. fiscal policy choices should be smart and should focus on creating tax structures that stimulate long-term aggregate demand, facilitate export-oriented activities, encourage job creation and promote sustainable development. in the framework of the planning of the national reform plan and the stability and growth plan for 2014, portugal should fully develop the role of fiscal policy as a measure to stimulate economic growth and have a clear and concrete long-term agenda that will allow us to finally have a stable and sound fiscal policy.
in writing. − the report under review focuses on the annual report on taxation, more specifically on how to unlock the eu's economic growth potential. the european tax system is very effective in relation to taxpayers with medium and low incomes but not very effective in taxing the wealthy. however, this struggle can only be successful if all member states are involved so that border transactions can be controlled. the response of most member states to the crisis has been to adopt very strict taxation measures and is leading to a large degree of tax evasion, which makes it impossible to collect taxes. the black economy in the eu has increased and we are facing the flight of hundreds and hundreds of billions of euros which leads to the loss of a trillion euros a year. i therefore call on the member states to cooperate more closely with each other under the coordination of the commission, not refusing to share the information available with other member states, so that this scourge of tax evasion and avoidance can be curbed. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the measures adopted will make tax collection more effective and an instrument for boosting economic growth and job creation.
in writing. - this report advocates tax increases. of course, the increase in vat - the most blind tax, which hits equally those who have the least and those who can least and the holders of great wealth. it advocates the expansion of the collectible to catch only the chicken-heaps, keeping intact the large capital, its profits, the mechanisms that allow it to maintain low rates of tax payment, tax exemptions and benefits, subsidies and other stewardships. a path that has been followed in portugal. as wealth is increasingly concentrated in the hands of a few and these pay fewer and fewer taxes, greater sacrifice is required of workers, who see their incomes reduced, their taxes increased and the provision of public services in health, education and social security reduced. we are opposed to this approach, which is based on greater tax justice, with a reform of the tax system that directs taxes to where wealth is actually concentrated and that ensures the revenue necessary for the full fulfilment of the social functions of the state. this will ensure not only conditions for economic growth but also, and above all, conditions for fairer and more harmonious development and social progress.
in writing. − the current debt crisis has created a number of new problems in the european union which require an appropriate adjustment of fiscal policies in the short, medium and long term. some member states have already made these adjustments, while others have not yet done so. it should be stressed that tax policy remains a matter of national sovereignty and that the different tax systems of the member states must therefore be respected, while the barriers of the internal market and the uncertainties and ambiguities resulting from the legal loopholes must be overcome as quickly as possible. it is essential to restore the credibility of fiscal policy and to reduce sovereign debt; it is unavoidable to ensure fiscal discipline and introduce structural reforms, but at the same time to give priority to growth-oriented fiscal measures and the promotion of taxes levied more on consumption than on labour, as the former are better suited to stimulate economic growth and employment in the long term. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. − the european union is going through a serious economic and financial crisis, forcing several member states to seek international help to meet their commitments to international bodies. i believe that austerity measures are necessary, but i believe that they must be balanced with other measures to increase competitiveness, job creation or economic growth, because only then will it be possible to achieve an effective macroeconomic balance and to meet the deficit and public debt ratios. i believe that taxation is crucial to improving the competitiveness of countries and the european union as a whole, and that there must be an effective fight against tax fraud and evasion, the elimination of double taxation and the reduction of the tax differential between member states.

in writing. the european parliament today approved the proposal not to convene a convention to examine the proposed extension of protocol no 30 on the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union to poland and the united kingdom, to the czech republic, as the effects of this proposal would be limited if it existed. recalling that both the conventions for the drafting of the charter of fundamental rights and for the drafting of the treaty establishing a constitution for europe were convened to deal with essential issues concerning the constitutional order of the union, including the adoption of a binding text setting out the fundamental rights and principles recognised by the union, i voted in favour of not convening a convention for the addition to the treaty on european union and the treaty on the functioning of the european union of a protocol on the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union to the czech republic.
in writing. - the protocol exempts the united kingdom and poland from the application of the eu charter of fundamental rights, countries to which the czech republic now joins. we respect the sovereign decisions of each country. we have been critical of the content of this minimalist 'charter of fundamental rights' compared with, for example, the universal declaration of human rights, the constitution of the portuguese republic or even the social charter of the council of europe. and even this content is called into question by these countries, and they are allowed to opt out, which has not happened with respect to other situations. but we cannot help pointing out the hypocrisy and contradictions of this eu: derogations, exceptions or opt-outs for 'fundamental rights' yes, but not for the rules of competition, the single market or the sacrosanct principle of the free movement of capital. this is a clear indication of the order of priorities, which is well established in the treaties.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that, in summary, protocol no 30 does not exempt the united kingdom and poland from the binding provisions of the charter. this is not a waiver clause. it doesn't change the charter. as it stands, the protocol does not appear to alter the legal position which would prevail in its absence. however, the mere existence of the protocol has given rise to legal uncertainty and political confusion, and therefore it affects all member states negatively and not just the united kingdom, poland or, prospectively, the czech republic. what is also perfectly clear is that if protocol no 30 were to be interpreted as limiting the scope or the legal force of the provisions of the charter, the result would be a reduction in the protection of the fundamental rights of british and polish citizens, thus undermining the union's efforts to achieve and maintain a uniformly high level of protection of rights.

in writing. - the charter of fundamental rights adopted in nice (2000), and made legally binding by the treaty of lisbon, is a synthesis of common european values with which all citizens can identify. these values are the result of the rich cultural heritage of the different eu countries, their constitutional traditions and legal rules, and they characterize the union not only as an economic construct but as a community of common values. although there are many doubts about the willingness of both the czech parliament and the czech people themselves to ratify this protocol, which is intended to extend the application of protocol no 30 to this country, i believe that it will not be successful in reducing the standards for protecting the fundamental rights and freedoms of czech citizens. in any event, the case law, in particular through the judgment of the court of justice of 21 december 2011, has made it clear that protocol no 30 does not exempt poland and the united kingdom from the binding provisions of the charter of fundamental rights and cannot therefore be used as an exemption clause. the protocol in question has the effect of creating legal uncertainty and political confusion, which undermines the efforts of the union to achieve a uniformly high and equitable level of protection of fundamental rights.

in writing. − the eu is an area of free movement of people and goods where all citizens should have the assurance that their rights are protected. the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters, drawn up by mr antonio lópez-istúriz white and mrs antonyia parvanova, presents us with a regulation which enshrines the right of victims in the eu and strengthens protection measures in criminal matters. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that we are dealing with an instrument which, in addition to helping the police and the judiciary to protect victims, is essential to fill the protection gap in relation to the most vulnerable and fragile people, such as women and children. it is an innovative instrument that will facilitate access to justice, ensuring conditions of free movement throughout the eu, for victims of heinous crimes such as domestic violence, sexual harassment, paedophilia, etc. victims will be protected not only in their country of origin but also in any other member state.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation aims at the mutual recognition within the european union of protection measures for victims of violence. the aim is to grant all victims recognition of the crime and the highest possible level of protection in the eu member states. to protect a person where there are serious grounds for believing that his or her life, physical or psychological integrity, personal freedom, security or sexual integrity are threatened, in particular to prevent any form of gender-based violence and violence against privacy. it applies to all victims, whether or not they are victims of acts of gender-based violence. the rapporteur stresses that it is imperative to ensure that a person who has been granted protection in one member state does not lose it when he moves to another member state. they provide for the establishment of a mechanism that eliminates intermediate formalities through the use of a uniform model certificate and a multilingual standard form. this ensures not only quick and simple recognition but also the application of protective measures. we voted in favour.
in writing. − mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters is part of a legislative package that strengthens the rights of victims in the eu and also includes a proposal for a directive on the rights, support and protection of victims of crime. this proposal responds to the need for a comprehensive european legal framework that will grant all victims of crime recognition and the highest possible level of protection within the territory of the union. the proposal for this regulation will complement the european protection order directive which ensures mutual recognition of protection measures in criminal matters. the combined application of the two instruments (criminal and civil) will allow persons who have been granted an order for protection to move freely and safely within the eu, as provided for in article 3 of the treaty on european union, and will ultimately lead to the strengthening and development of the areas of freedom, security and justice in the union. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. − trade relations between the european union and canada are based on the customs cooperation and mutual assistance agreement between the european community and canada (cmaa) of 1998. in 2005, canada expressed an interest in moving towards closer cooperation with the eu on supply chain security and risk management. since may 2011, the commission has been negotiating the draft customs cooperation agreement on supply chain security issues, aiming to strengthen the customs aspects of the security of the logistics chain of international trade. the agreement establishes a legal basis for enhanced customs cooperation between the eu and canada, and also opens the door to mutual recognition agreements on customs security, including the mutual recognition of their respective trade partnership programmes with equivalent trade facilitation measures, i.e. the eu authorised economic operator (aeo) system. in view of the fact that this agreement will be beneficial for the european economy, i supported this recommendation.

in writing. the recommendation by mr šťastný concerns the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement on customs cooperation between the european union (eu) and canada on matters relating to supply chain security. customs relations between the eu and canada date back to 1998, when an agreement on customs cooperation and mutual assistance in customs matters between the european community and canada (cmaa) was established. however, in 2005, canada proposed enhanced cooperation on security throughout the international trade logistics chain, including container security and risk management. the agreement also strengthens mutual recognition for trade partnership programmes, facilitating bilateral trade, in particular with regard to the eu authorised economic operator (aeo) and canadian partner protection programmes (pips), as is already the case with the united states of america and japan. i voted in favour of this report, which consolidates and extends customs cooperation between the eu and canada and will complement the comprehensive economic and trade agreement (ceta) currently under negotiation.
in writing. − customs relations between the eu and canada are based on the customs cooperation and mutual assistance agreement between the european community and canada (cmaa) of 1998. in 2005, canada expressed its interest in moving towards closer cooperation with the eu on supply chain security and risk management. the aim of the new agreement is to strengthen customs aspects related to the security of the logistics chain of international trade including container security while facilitating legitimate trade. the agreement establishes new provisions on issues such as risk standards, security controls, minimum standards for risk management techniques, exchange of information and data and cargo inspection. in general terms, the draft decision appears to us to be proportionate and justified.
in writing. − customs relations between the european union and canada are based on the customs cooperation and mutual assistance agreement between the european community and canada (cmaa) of 1998. in 2005, canada expressed an interest in enhancing existing cooperation with the eu on supply chain security and risk management. the draft customs cooperation agreement on supply chain security issues negotiated by the commission since may 2011 consolidates the 1998 cmaa and extends its scope. the aim of the new agreement is to strengthen customs aspects related to the security of the logistics chain of international trade including container security while facilitating legitimate trade.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement on customs cooperation between the european union and canada on matters relating to security of supply chain, considering that the new agreement on customs cooperation with canada consolidates and extends customs cooperation between the two developed partners and that it will, moreover, complement the comprehensive economic and trade agreement (ceta) under negotiation. i hope that the various protectionist strategies of the canadian authorities, which have so harmed the export of azorean dairy products, particularly cheese, will be brought to an end quickly in the interests of a transparent and fruitful relationship.
in writing. − the events of 11 september have reshaped the number and quality of policy initiatives in the field of security, and in particular supply chain security and risk management. in order to detect and inspect potentially dangerous cargoes, the various international actors have strengthened the vision and policies for more intensive and multifaceted risk management. in this respect too, the customs relations between the european union and canada deserve particular legal attention, which is reflected in risk standards, security controls and minimum standards for risk management techniques that can guarantee the safety of containers. the agreement, the conclusion of which i support, allows for mutual recognition in customs security matters, enhancing cooperation which will facilitate trade in a global context.
in writing. − the objective of the new eu-canada agreement is to strengthen customs aspects related to the security of the international trade logistics chain, while facilitating legitimate trade. the agreement establishes a legal basis for enhanced customs cooperation between the eu and canada on issues such as risk standards, security controls, minimum standards for risk management techniques, exchange of information and data, strategic partnerships in the field of cargo inspection, as well as collaboration in international fora such as the world customs organization, and also opens the door to mutually recognised agreements on customs security. for the reasons given, i voted in favour of the agreement.

in writing. - i approve the report, taking into account that when the financial crisis spread across europe in 2008, there were 17 different regulatory systems in place, all based on national rules and national rescue mechanisms. there was a certain form of european coordination, but it was related to exchanges of information and to rather informal cooperation procedures. this was not sufficient to respond to the financial sector crisis that the union has been going through in recent years. the european council and the commission are thus finally following the line taken by parliament, which has been calling for supranational banking supervision since 2002. the proposed banking union will change the way banks in the euro area are supervised by establishing a single supervisory mechanism to be set up within the european central bank. while supporting a single supervisory mechanism for the euro area, i stress the need to further strengthen the european banking authority in parallel to ensure its proper functioning to deepen the internal market in financial services and to avoid a division between euro-zone and non-euro-zone members as regards the rules applicable to the financial sector.
in writing. − the european union has been developing strategies to combat the economic crisis, which will restore confidence in financial systems and boost the growth capacity of member states' economies in a sustained manner. the european commission, the european parliament and the council of the european union have recently launched a roadmap for a stronger economic union. the creation of a banking union is part of this roadmap, the first pillar of which will be the single supervisory mechanism (ssm). while it is the ecb's responsibility to ensure the proper supervision of european banks, the european banking authority (eba) will be responsible for ensuring that the relevant legislation is implemented across the union in an integrated and harmonised manner, ensuring the smooth functioning of the single market for financial services. the report proposes that the eba should create a single supervisory guide, which is essential to ensure consistent enforcement of the regulation and ensures, within its mandate, the full and equal participation of all member states wishing to join the ssm, whether they belong to the euro area or not. pending the final vote on this matter, i shall vote in favour of this report.

in writing. − the fragile economic situation of the european union requires concerted and ambitious action by european leaders in creating the conditions for economic prosperity and restoring stability to european financial markets. in this respect, one of the key steps in restoring confidence in the recovery of the euro area economic area is the building of a solid banking union, based on a number of pillars, of which the single supervisory mechanism (ssm) is a prominent support. this report is about the creation of a ssm that will cover the financial institutions of the euro area and will be open to all other member states that wish to join it. the aim is to define how the ecb, as the ultimate supervisor of european banks, will perform its tasks, ensuring the stability of the system and maintaining its independence as the monetary policy authority. last march, the european parliament concluded some negotiations with the council of the european union on this dossier, although some doubts remain about the relevance of the ecb calling itself the direct supervisor of all european banks, and not just those of the greatest systemic importance. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. the establishment of the single supervisory mechanism, in which the ecb will play a central role, has clear objectives: the deepening of the internal market for financial services, the maintenance of the dogma of the free movement of capital and, above all, the saving of the euro. the ecb is thus taking over supervisory functions which were previously carried out by national institutions, such as banco de portugal. contrary to what the argument on which this proposal is based would have us believe, it was not for lack of supervisory mechanisms that the banks directed the bulk of their activity towards financial speculation. this is the result of the free movement of capital and the sophisticated financial products it has made possible, the crisis in the profitability of the capitalist system with the tendency of the profit rate to fall, the contradiction between the over-accumulation of capital and the contraction of markets and consumption caused by the loss of purchasing power of wages (due to their contraction) and their replacement by credit. in other words, the banks turned their main activity to financial speculation, with the complicity of the supervisory authorities and the ecb, which provided them with cheap credit and calmly and fearlessly watched them speculate with new financial instruments and so-called sovereign debts.
in writing. − over the past few decades, the union has made considerable progress towards creating an internal market for banking services. as a result, in many member states there are banking groups with head offices in other member states that hold a considerable market share, and credit institutions have geographically diversified their activities both within and outside the euro area. the current financial and economic crisis has brought europe's banking system to the brink of collapse. the integrity of the single currency and the single market is threatened by the fragmentation of the financial sector. it is now essential to step up the integration of the banking sector in order to strengthen european unity, restore financial stability and lay the foundations for economic recovery.
