in writing. the commission's communication states that the current system of the european electronic toll service is not working and needs to be redesigned. directive 2004/52/ec and decision 2009/750/ec aim to achieve the interoperability of all electronic road toll systems in the eu in order to avoid the proliferation of incompatible systems, which could compromise the proper functioning of the internal market and the achievement of transport policy objectives. the directive provides for a european electronic toll service, for which road use is declared electronically by means of a single on-board equipment. this equipment would in turn enable all drivers of light vehicles to pay tolls easily on any road or structure in the union, through a subscription contract with a single eets provider and a single item on board. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union's institutions and bodies.

the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we have reached agreement on the schengen governance package. an agreement which is not exactly what the european parliament wanted (because we were denied legitimate codecision), but an agreement which represents substantial progress compared to the current rules by strengthening the governance of schengen. an agreement that protects the right of citizens to move freely and that strengthens the security with which they do so. let me emphasize six points: first, we have opted for a european system. the evaluation mechanism will no longer be purely intergovernmental but will have a european character. the european commission will no longer be a mere observer but will be responsible for overall coordination in the evaluation and monitoring process. it will be responsible for most decisions in the evaluation process: for the annual and multiannual programme, for preparing and carrying out on-the-spot visits, and for drawing up evaluation reports and recommendations. it will be for the commission, following an evaluation, to approve the report and to propose recommendations for corrective action, which should be adopted by the council. a number of european union agencies and institutions will also be involved. secondly, we have not ignored internal borders. the possibility of assessing whether or not illegal checks are being carried out at internal borders is explicitly provided for. we know how timely this is in the light of the situations we have seen in recent years in some member states, often inspired by populist national agendas imposed by far-right parties. thirdly, we have eliminated the double standards. the candidate countries and the schengen countries should now be assessed in the same way and according to the same rules. the schengen acquis should be strictly respected not only at the time of accession but also after accession. fourthly, the preparatory inspections are over. the lack of rigor of the current mechanism was also due to the fact that inspection visits were announced far too early. one of the most useful innovations of the new evaluation system is precisely the possibility of on-the-spot visits to the internal and external borders without any prior notice being given only 24 hours in advance. fifth, we give the evaluation a meaning and a usefulness. unlike the current system, which is not legally binding and where there is only a mere peer review, the new system has mechanisms with greater effectiveness and deterrence. it will allow for an accurate assessment of the degree of compliance with the schengen rules and allow for an immediate corrective reaction in order to dispel any feeling of impunity. member states will be obliged to solve the problems identified. sixthly, we have strengthened the democratic control of the european parliament and guaranteed access to documents. parliament shall be kept informed throughout the process and shall have access to all relevant documents, including the frontex risk analysis, the multiannual and annual evaluation programme, the evaluation reports, the recommendations for corrective actions and the action plans to address the identified deficiencies. it shall have access to the member states' replies to the questionnaires. this is a major step forward in terms of transparency and the right of information of the european parliament, which had no access to any documents in the context of the schengen evaluations. mr president, parliament has assured its involvement both in the current procedure and in future initiatives in this area. this commitment is made not only in a joint declaration between the three institutions but also in the text of the law which we are about to adopt. i thank commissioner malmström and the irish presidency for all their commitment and cooperation. this commitment represents a major step forward from the current status quo, by creating a new evaluation mechanism with a more european, more transparent, efficient and rigorous character. i therefore ask for your support for this commitment, which was only possible thanks to the united and strong position which parliament has maintained throughout the negotiations. i am grateful for the cooperation of the shadow rapporteurs and of all the political groups which have never refused to support me, even those which, for various reasons, do not consider voting in favour of the final agreed version.
the rapporteur. - i would like to congratulate cecilia malmström. the commission is the main beneficiary of this process and this is a sign that we are now having a community mechanism, as parliament has always advocated. mr president, four corrections to what was said in the plenary, thanking you for all the kind words you have addressed to me. firstly, it is not true that there is an exaggeration in the reintroduction of borders. the reintroduction of border controls will be exceptional, proposed by the european commission if necessary, and decided by the council with the involvement of the member states. there is no danger here. secondly, it is not true that the free movement of citizens is going to be weakened. on the contrary, we will strengthen free movement because from now on all attempts to illegally reintroduce internal border controls will be monitored by this mechanism. thirdly, it is not true that immigration can be a cause for the reintroduction of borders. we explicitly reject that provision in the bill we're about to pass. as the commissioner has already said, this debate is not about bulgaria and romania, which should already be full members of the schengen area. but it is a way of responding to those who are afraid of bulgaria and romania by saying that they can fulfil the conditions at the time of accession and not fulfil the conditions afterwards. as soon as we have this evaluation mechanism, all the member states have to respond to all the conditions at all times, which means that this pretext no longer exists against bulgaria and romania. finally, mr president, i would like to thank once again all the shadow rapporteurs for their cooperation, including those who will vote against but who gave us all the strength during the negotiation process. i would like to mention in particular the collaboration of mr enciu, who has made many suggestions, and in particular the close collaboration with mrs renate weber, whom i thank very much.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, despite the efforts of commissioner ciolos to provide agriculture with an adequate budget, we will probably have a much smaller agricultural budget for the period 2014-2020, which will probably force us to apply the financial discipline mechanism as early as 2014. the european commission decided to use the draft budget approved by the european council on 8 february as the basis for its calculation. with this gesture, the commission surprised us by accepting as final the budget approved by the council, thus ignoring the codecision and the existence of the lisbon treaty. it is a position which shows little institutional respect for parliament and which we strongly criticise. the alternative proposal we are putting forward is consistent with the negotiating mandate which was supported by a large majority and which was given to us by this same plenary in the negotiating mandate for the direct payments regulation. it is the only one we consider acceptable at this stage of the negotiation of the multiannual financial framework. we also support the commission's proposal to exempt farmers who receive less than eur 5 000 a year from this mechanism. this is a large number of farmers - about 80% of the total in the union - but they receive only 15% of the total amount. the positive discrimination against the youngest and the constantly proclaimed simplification objectives fully justify this decision. i therefore call on this house to adopt the report we are discussing today.
the rapporteur. - mr president, i would like to draw your attention to the fact that the commissioner has always shown an impeccable relationship with parliament, and we very much appreciate his constant readiness to dialogue with us. unfortunately, the same cannot be said of the commission in this procedure. there can be no pragmatism or political realism which calls into question the balance of power between the institutions. i therefore believe that the attitude on this matter should be different, and i have already said so. i thank the members for their speeches, which essentially reaffirm the positions of parliament. i think that, whatever its content, this is a way for members to show their consistency with the mandate they have been given and at the same time reaffirm the defence of the interests of farmers in general and, for a good number of members, also of small farmers in particular.

mr president, commissioner, the policy of austerity has reached its limit. europe did not suffer a tsunami. europe has chosen and insisted on wrong and self-destructive policies. of course, there are some who benefit when capital and skilled labour flow from the periphery of europe to the centre. there are those who gain when the assets of countries, even those which are profitable - such as electricity, post offices, airlines, ports, water - are sold at a balance price, but europe as a whole loses. the imbalances within the union are growing more acute than ever, and the union is breaking up economically, socially and politically. the next council only has to take a decision to get out of denial and reverse the policy. the short-term agenda is known. it requires opening up demand in countries with surpluses, implementing at least one of the various investment initiatives that have been announced repeatedly, and creating an initiative to combat unemployment, with the awareness that without growth it will be only a palliative. it requires the creation of a social emergency pillar, because where social action is most needed is where countries cannot afford to take it. we must also ensure that banking union does not lead to a situation where deposits in peripheral banks are less secure than deposits in central banks, and we must prepare for the joint management of sovereign debt, and we await the commission's initiative on the creation of the high-level group. finally, mr president, the most important thing is to put an end to the troika. because the council is here, the commission is here... which of you is responsible for the abuses, the mistakes and the violence that the troika is imposing on the countries under its control? we must return to democracy, and that will increase confidence.

in writing. - it is time to change the direction of the current policy which has led to widespread overfishing and worrying resource fragility, as well as to fleet overcapacity or market dysfunctions, situations which the reform of the common fisheries policy currently under way must definitely resolve. to do this, fishing must be carried out in each region according to the availability of resources, scientifically monitored, and giving priority to the communities of those regions that have always fished there and to whom the future sustainability of the activity in their waters is of greatest interest. in order to save the sector from depletion by preventing, deterring and eliminating illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, there should be permanent monitoring. the commission proposal aims to strengthen its powers and clarify the list of non-compliants. it is important that scientific data and regular evaluation ensure the usefulness of their action in order to understand whether the monitoring of catches is effective. the fishermen are grateful.
in writing. - illegal fishing is a scourge affecting all coastal member states. its illegal nature makes it difficult to estimate its impact, but it undoubtedly puts the survival of threatened fisheries species and the survival of the sector itself at risk. it will be important for european fishermen who resort to illegal fishing to understand that they are putting their own activity and their families' livelihoods at risk. the european union, the fisheries sector, consumers and ecosystems have much to gain from an effective reduction in illegal fishing. the member states and the european institutions must mobilise to combat illegal fishing and hold third states responsible if they do not cooperate properly in this fight.
in writing. − the european commission proposal aims to align the iuu regulation on illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (regulation no 1005/2008) with the tfeu, in particular as regards delegated and implementing acts. the power to adopt delegated acts is proposed to be delegated, inter alia, in the following areas: to exempt fishing vessels from the obligation to report information or to set different reporting deadlines; to determine indicators for the inspection of landing and transhipment operations by third country fishing vessels; to adapt the catch certification scheme to certain fishery products obtained by small fishing vessels; to amend the list of products not covered by the regulation; to adapt the deadline for the submission of the catch certificate to the type of fishery product, the distance to the place of entry or the means of transport used. implementing powers are proposed, inter alia, for the establishment of prior notification forms, the establishment of procedures and forms for the landing and transhipment declaration. the rapporteur supports the commission's proposal as a whole. however, it proposes to limit the commission's power to adopt delegated acts in time to allow for a regular assessment of their usefulness. we voted in favour.
in writing. - illegally caught fish are often the most economically attractive. since these catches do not comply with environmental or social standards, among others, fishermen can usually sell it at lower prices. wholesale and retailers thus find it less expensive to buy this fish, although they may not always know that it was caught illegally. we must therefore fight all forms of illegal fishing. despite the great economic benefits for the players, this fight is not always easy.
in writing. − the aim of this report was to align regulation (ec) no 1005/2008 establishing a community system to prevent, deter and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing with the new hierarchy of acts defined by the lisbon treaty. in the context of the harmonisation of this regulation with the new rules of the tfeu, the commission proposal reclassified the powers conferred on it by delegated and implementing acts. the commission has used two weights and two measures as regards the european fleet or those of third countries. in relation to the latter, the application of this regulation has been limited to the listing of non-cooperating third countries in the fight against iuu fishing, without appropriate and dissuasive trade sanctions; the commission has been extremely zealous in its approach to european operators, wanting to be more environmentally friendly, protectionist and restrictive of fisheries than other operators globally, including by introducing regulations that threaten their sustainability and competitiveness, severely undermining european operators who fully comply with the strict standards set by the eu. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the amendments to the regulation contribute to a more effective fight against the scourge of iuu fishing.
in writing. − in the context of the alignment of regulation (ec) no 1005/2008 on illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing with the new rules of the tfeu, the commission has drawn up a proposal classifying the powers currently conferred on the commission by this regulation, taking into account the distinction between delegated and implementing acts. in general, the proposed amendments relate only to the types of acts to be adopted and do not change the content of the measures. there is only a significant change in the procedure applied for the inclusion or removal of third countries identified in a list of non-cooperating third countries. the rapporteur welcomes the commission proposal, but notes that whenever the proposal for a delegated act is advanced, the delegation should be limited in time in order to allow for a regular evaluation of its use. for the reasons stated above, i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation.
in writing. − in line with regulation no 1005/2008, the commission has prepared a proposal to classify the powers conferred on the commission in delegated and implementing acts. the proposal concerns only the type of acts and does not change the content of such measures. parliament welcomed the commission's proposals, but stressed that in the case of delegated acts, the authorisation to delegate should be limited in time to allow for regular performance evaluation. i therefore voted in favour of the document in the european parliament.
in writing. − i approve this report, bearing in mind that the main objective of the directive is to ensure the highest standards of dignity for the treatment of asylum seekers with regard to their reception conditions, so as to guarantee them a life in dignity, in line with international law. i also welcome the intention of this directive to harmonise national policies on reception conditions in order to limit the movement of asylum seekers between member states and to reduce administrative burdens.
in writing. − this initiative is part of the package of proposals aimed at establishing a common european asylum system. the commission proposes to amend the 2003 directive in order to ensure a higher level of treatment for asylum seekers and to harmonise reception conditions, in order to avoid secondary movements resulting from divergent reception policies between member states. it also amends its scope to include applicants for subsidiary protection. it lays down a set of common principles, at the level of the delimitation of the grounds for detention, which should be exceptional and respect the principle of necessity and proportionality, in a case-by-case assessment; of the conditions of detention (they should be placed in specific detention facilities, with rare exceptions which should, however, safeguard a certain number of conditions. the commission will continue to support the efforts of the member states to ensure that the right to education is respected and that the right to education is respected. this was the possible agreement to try to harmonize the rules for the treatment and reception of asylum seekers, seeking to bring them into line with basic human rights rules and principles.
in writing. − the most basic principles of humanity demand that the european union should seek to welcome asylum seekers with respect and concern for their welfare and that it should adopt high standards in welcoming those who need it. the maxim do unto others as you would have them do unto you has full application here. however, the practical difficulties in distinguishing between those who are actually entitled to asylum and those who use this figure to leave their countries without being exposed to any specific risk are well known. the indiscriminate reception of all those applying for entry into the european union would put social security systems under even more strain and would entail the immediate entitlement to a range of social benefits for those who did not contribute to the systems or belong to their national communities. all these issues and their seriousness necessarily impose the obligation that, without forgetting the humanity due to asylum seekers which i have already mentioned, the granting of asylum must comply with strict requirements and avoid abusive and fraudulent generalizations.
in writing. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the rights of asylum seekers are respected and that the right to asylum is guaranteed. the text also includes provisions on the protection of vulnerable persons such as minors, unaccompanied minors, pregnant women and victims of torture and violence. we are not satisfied with the amendments made by this report. the report falls short of a much needed improvement in the conditions afforded to applicants for international protection. a certain view is not avoided that immigrants in general are abusive or even potential criminals. the eu has also provided a number of instruments to facilitate the exchange of information and best practices between member states on the implementation of the union's asylum policy and on the implementation of the union's asylum policy. the levels of financial support provided are very low, access to employment can be delayed and vulnerable people are not adequately considered.
in writing. - the proposal aims to recast council directive 2003/9/ec of 27 january 2003 laying down minimum standards for the reception of asylum seekers in the member states. the commission's evaluation report on the implementation of the reception conditions directive in the member states identified a number of shortcomings in the level of reception conditions for asylum seekers, which stem mainly from the fact that the directive gives member states a wide margin of manoeuvre in setting those conditions at national level. the purpose of the amendment of this directive is to ensure higher and uniform treatment standards in the area of reception conditions for asylum seekers during the second phase of the implementation of the common european asylum system (ceas). that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the proposal amends the reception conditions directive of 2003, which lays down minimum standards for the reception of asylum seekers, and aims to ensure better and more harmonised treatment standards. in particular, it addresses the issue of the grounds for detention and includes an extensive list of rules and safeguards. it stressed access to employment, material support, health care and legal assistance, the availability of representation for unaccompanied minors, the identification of special needs and the facilitation of the commission's role in monitoring implementation. finally, as there is agreement between the european parliament and the council on important matters such as material reception conditions and health care, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − the european parliament and council directive aims to ensure high standards of treatment of asylum seekers with regard to reception conditions that allow a decent standard of living in accordance with international law. the proposal is part of a first package of proposals aimed at ensuring a greater degree of harmonisation and better protection conditions for the common european asylum system (ceas). the commission's initial proposal contains provisions on facilitated access to employment for asylum seekers, the guarantee of material reception conditions (at the level of social assistance granted to nationals), and the underlying principle that no asylum seeker should be kept in detention for the mere status of his condition. i voted in favour of agreeing to the proposal, with the amendments introduced by parliament, which clarify and make the reception rules more flexible so as to facilitate their transposition into national legal systems, while maintaining the key elements of the 2008 proposal.
in writing. - this report is part of the asylum package which aims to harmonise and improve protection criteria within the common european asylum system. the aim of this document is to standardize the conditions under which asylum seekers are received, so as to provide them with decent living conditions and to reduce the phenomenon of secondary movements between member states. i would like to stress the important changes introduced by this proposal, namely access to the labour market, access to education for minors, and similarity in reception conditions as regards the level of social assistance offered to nationals. although the union's immigration policy is cloaked in national interests, this document points to the possible agreement between the 27 member states. for these reasons, i vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - the position initially advocated in the european parliament's text (despite some equally negative aspects) has been watered down by the council, especially as regards unaccompanied minors, vulnerable persons, the right to legal assistance, the numerous possibilities for accelerated procedures at borders. it has also backed away from other unfounded and inadmissible application procedures which reflect a xenophobic and racist view of asylum seekers as potential abusers of the asylum system. the concept of a safe third country is maintained and the notion of a mass influx is introduced. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a directive on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data by the community institutions and bodies. but much more could and should have been done. nothing that has been achieved in this process changes the repressive and exploitative character of the eu's immigration policy, keeping it as a fortress europe that continues to use immigrants to the benefit of economic groups and labour exploitation relations, leaving immigrants in the hands of trafficking networks and failing to take its share of responsibility for this situation which is also caused by its foreign policy.
in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that the objective of this regulation is to increase the efficiency of the dublin system and to ensure high standards in the protection of persons under the dublin procedure.
in writing. - the recommendation for second reading of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs on the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing the criteria and mechanisms for determining the member state responsible for examining an application for international protection lodged in one of the member states by a third-country national or a stateless person (recast), report by monica luisa macovei, on behalf of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, on the amended proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the establishment of the eurodac fingerprint comparison system for the effective implementation of the regulation (establishing the criteria and mechanisms for determining the member state responsible for examining an application for international protection lodged in one of the member states by a third-country national or a stateless person) and requesting comparisons with eurodac data by the police authorities of the member states and by europol for law enforcement purposes and amending regulation (eu) no 1077/2011 establishing the european agency for the operational management of large-scale it systems in the area of freedom, security and justice (recast).
in writing. − this initiative is part of the package of proposals aimed at establishing a common european asylum system. it should therefore amend the dublin regulation of 2003 establishing the criteria for determining which member state should be responsible for examining an asylum application lodged in one of the eu member states, in order to prevent asylum seekers from multiplying their applications in different countries. ensures a higher level of protection for asylum seekers by enshrining a set of basic rights, such as the right to a personal interview in order to determine which member state is responsible for processing the application; in the case of transfer, there should be a possibility of appeal against the decision, with access to legal aid, and a provisional suspension of the transfer. asylum seekers will have better access to information, in particular on their rights. the rights of minors, and in particular of unaccompanied minors, are also strengthened. a system of early warning and crisis management is introduced to enable the member state concerned to respond quickly to a given situation, in particular by submitting a crisis management plan, the implementation of which should be monitored by the commission and easo.
in writing. the european union must use more effective criteria and means to tackle the main issues and problems facing it. in the case of applications for international protection which necessarily involve highly sensitive issues, this requirement is obviously reinforced. it is therefore legitimate to expect that the european union will promote the adoption of clear and rigorous criteria for international protection, but that these criteria will be imbued with humanity and respect for the concrete situations of petitioners and that the criteria used will allow for uniform treatment of the latter within the framework of the european union. the particular vulnerability of these people is a factor that must always be present both at the level of decision-makers at a broader level and at the level of enforcement officers who have direct contact with petitioners. no one should be exempted from this consideration, even if it cannot be done without rigor, discretion and responsibility.
in writing. − this regulation determines the member state responsible for examining an individual application for asylum. this regulation aims to prevent multiple applications by the same person in several member states by establishing a set of criteria which generally place responsibility for examining an asylum application on the member state which allowed the applicant to enter or reside in the european union. the member state responsible for examining the application shall be obliged, in accordance with its national law, to take back applicants who are irregularly present in another member state. the provisions contained therein reflect a criminalised view of immigration and immigrants or asylum seekers. a vision that seeks to hide the fact that keeping these people in a limbo of uncertainty and precariousness subjects them to the most abject schemes of exploiting their work. immigrants and asylum seekers will continue to face a horrendous cycle of repression and uncertainty.
in writing. − the proposal aims to recast council regulation (ec) no 343/2003 of 18 february 2003 laying down the criteria and mechanisms for determining the member state responsible for examining an application for asylum lodged in one of the member states by a third-country national (the 'dublin regulation'). the dublin system assessment report published by the commission on 6 june 2007 identified a number of shortcomings, mainly related to the effectiveness of the system established by the current legislative provisions and the level of protection provided to applicants for international protection subject to the dublin procedure. as announced in the asylum action plan, this proposal is part of a first package of proposals to ensure greater harmonisation and higher levels of protection within the common european asylum system. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − this proposal amends the 2003 dublin regulation, which sets out the criteria (what criteria?) and aims to better respond to situations of extraordinary pressure on member states' reception infrastructures and asylum systems and to situations where there is no adequate level of protection for applicants for international protection. the negotiations were long and the common position adopted by the council and the european parliament replaced the provisions on the suspension of transfers (closing of borders) by the creation of a rapid alert, preparedness and crisis management mechanism. this system aims above all to identify and address the root causes of problems with the potential to generate asylum crises. it also reinforces the message of solidarity and protection of fundamental rights.
in writing. − the commission's report on the evaluation of the dublin system concluded that overall the objectives of the system, in particular to establish a clear and effective mechanism for determining responsibility for asylum applications, have been largely achieved. however, some concerns remained, both in terms of practical application and effectiveness of the system. in addition, the responses to the green paper on the future of the common european asylum system (ceas) identified a significant number of shortcomings, mainly related to the efficiency of the system as well as to the level of protection of applicants for international protection subject to the dublin system. therefore, and with a view to correcting the above mentioned deficiencies, the commission decided to submit the proposal for a recast of regulation (ec) no 343/2003/ec. the main objective of the proposal is to increase the efficiency of the system and to ensure higher standards of protection for citizens who fall under the dublin procedure. i voted in favour, hoping that the proposal will indeed contribute to a better response to situations of extraordinary pressure on the reception infrastructure and asylum systems of the member states.
in writing. - this report is part of the 'asylum package', which comprises four reports. the dublin system evaluation report presented by the european commission identified a number of shortcomings and inefficiencies in the level of international protection sought by a third-country national or a stateless person. for these reasons, the ec has put forward this proposal which aims to make the system more efficient and increase the level of international protection. the common european asylum system is not a consensus issue within the union, but this document presents an early warning mechanism that identifies if a country suffers an abnormal influx of migrants, refugees and/or persons seeking international protection due to an external event, the case of the arab spring. this alert allows the union to put the schengen instruments into action and to strengthen cooperation and solidarity between the union's member states. for the reasons stated above, i am in favour of this report.
in writing. − the purpose of this regulation is to determine the member state responsible for examining an individual application for asylum. it would aim to avoid multiple applications by the same person in several member states by establishing a set of criteria which generally place responsibility for examining an asylum application on the member state which allowed the applicant to enter or reside in the territory of the member states of the european union. the member state responsible for examining the application shall be obliged, in accordance with its national law, to take back applicants who are irregularly present in another member state. they continue to look at immigrants as criminals, as terrorists, as potential abusers of the charity that in many cases constitutes the aid that is allocated to them in the eu - if they ever get it. they point the finger at immigrants to hide from society that they want to keep them in this limbo of uncertainty and precariousness in order to subject them to the most abject schemes of exploitation of their work. immigrants will continue to be repressed, put in prisons as if they were criminals, will continue to wait for long months or years without knowing if they will ever get an answer and if it will be positive so that they will often be expelled and forced to return to their country of origin.
in writing. − i approve this report, taking into account that the aim of the directive is to tackle shortcomings in the procedures for granting and withdrawing international protection status, in order to ensure greater harmonisation of protection at eu level. i would also stress that i am in favour of the line set out in this report so that withdrawal of international protection status is done through personal interviews in all cases, that better information is given, greater legal clarity, clear rules on access to the procedure, identification of vulnerable persons and their special procedural needs, as well as clearer rules on time limits and greater understanding of the rules.
in writing. − this initiative is part of the package of proposals aimed at establishing a common european asylum system, which is expected to be operational in the second half of 2015, setting common procedures and deadlines. it therefore intends to amend the 2005 directive in order to harmonise procedural guarantees in asylum procedures. those safeguards should take into account the specific needs of the most vulnerable persons, in particular by creating a mandatory identification mechanism that should allow cases requiring special attention to be recognised and the necessary support to be ensured. the rules on unaccompanied minors, for whom a representative must be appointed, are also strengthened. asylum seekers are guaranteed the right to appeal, with the possibility of access to legal assistance, where their lawyer will have access to restricted areas, such as detention centres or transit zones. there will now be concrete deadlines for a decision to be taken on an asylum application, where the three-month period can only be extended in a limited and strictly defined number of cases. the rules on training of the authorities who have direct contact with asylum seekers have also been strengthened.
in writing. − a common european asylum system will result in greater standardisation of procedures when assessing the granting of international protection status to applicants and may help to reduce the pressure on certain member states judged to be more lenient in applying the criteria for granting it. the efficiency and quality of this system will be particularly relevant in view of the conflict situations currently breaking out at european borders and which could contribute to an increase in the number of applications for international protection. i hope that the partnerships which the union is establishing with its neighbours and the demands it is making on human rights in this relationship will help to reduce the pressure for entry into the union and for the development of these countries.
in writing. - the position initially defended in the european parliament's text - which was not, it should be recalled, without a number of negative aspects - was weakened by the council, especially as regards unaccompanied minors, vulnerable persons, the right to legal assistance, the numerous possibilities for accelerated procedures at borders. it has also backed down on other unfounded and inadmissible application procedures, which reflect a certain xenophobic view of asylum seekers, seeing them as potential abusers of the asylum system. the concept of a safe third country is maintained and the notion of a mass influx is introduced. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of children in the event of a serious accident or serious injury. but much more could and should have been done. nothing that has been achieved in this process changes the repressive nature of eu policy in this area. the vision of a fortress europe persists, which continues to use immigrants in the interests of economic groups and labour exploitation relations, leaving them in the hands of trafficking networks and not taking its share of responsibility for this situation, which is already the result of its foreign policy (and not only).
in writing. − this proposal aims to recast council directive 2005/85/ec of 1 december 2005 on minimum standards on procedures for granting and withdrawing refugee status in the member states. the evaluation report pointed to the proliferation of disparate procedures at national level and to shortcomings in the procedural guarantees for asylum seekers, which result mainly from the fact that the current directive gives member states a wide margin of discretion. this directive is therefore not in a position to adequately complement the qualification directive and to ensure a rigorous assessment of applications for international protection in accordance with the international and community obligations of the member states as regards the principle of non-refoulement. this proposal is part of the initiatives to ensure a higher level of harmonisation and better standards in the field of international protection throughout the union. we hope that the measures envisaged will contribute to increasing coherence between eu asylum instruments and to streamlining and consolidating procedural arrangements in the union, leading to more robust decisions in the first instance, thus preventing abuse and increasing the efficiency of the asylum process.
in writing. − the stockholm programme, adopted by the european council at its meeting of 10 and 11 december 2009, underlined the need to establish by 2012 a common area of protection and solidarity, based on a common asylum procedure and a uniform status for persons granted international protection based on high protection standards and fair and effective procedures. the commission has put forward a proposal. today's vote is the final council position reflecting the compromise reached in informal trilogues between the european parliament and the council organised by the commission. the essential objectives of the commission proposal are maintained and the final result is clear progress compared to directive 2005/85/ec. i would highlight from the final position the principle of frontloading (i.e. improving the quality of decisions taken in the first instance to limit the number of subsequent appeals) which provides a solid set of guarantees for all asylum seekers.
in writing. − this proposal for a regulation recasts council directive 2005/85/ec, which is an integral part of the establishment of a common european asylum system (ceas), and is part of the asylum action plan. the main objectives of the proposal are to address procedural shortcomings and ensure higher and more harmonised standards of protection (thus moving towards a common asylum procedure and a uniform status); to improve the efficiency and quality of decision-making processes in the services, advice and expertise, and to encourage member states to deliver their decisions within a reasonable timeframe. the proposal also aims to simplify and consolidate procedural concepts and mechanisms and to improve coherence between asylum instruments. i voted in favour.
in writing. − this report, part of the establishment of the common european asylum system, aims to recast directive 2005/85/ec on the granting and withdrawal of international protection status. this directive aims to harmonise and simplify the criteria for granting international protection in accordance with the different legal systems, in particular in procedures and their maximum number and in interviews. at the same time, member states strengthen their powers to respond to potential abuses of the european asylum system through the accelerated procedure, when it is demonstrated that an application for international protection is abusive. parliament also reinforced the minimum rights of applicants for international protection in the 27 member states, with regard to the right to be informed, the right to be heard and the right to free legal assistance.
in writing. - i approve this report, since i consider this fund to be a sign of european solidarity towards those affected by the crisis, even if the amending budget with an increase is not yet sufficient. i should also point out that in 2010 about a quarter of europeans, or about 120 million european citizens, were at risk of poverty and social exclusion. the fund is thus an instrument to alleviate the most severe forms of poverty, particularly food deprivation, which we are currently witnessing in some of the member states. it is up to the member states to decide whether they want to use the allocations from this fund. the budget of the fund should, in my view, be reserved only for aid to those most affected by the crisis and not used for other activities of the cohesion fund.
in writing. - i have repeatedly opposed the end of european support for food distribution to the most deprived and called for it to be reconsidered. i am therefore glad that the idea is now being put into practice through this new fund and that institutions which have generously provided this support to the most deprived are not deprived of one of their main supports. i would like to highlight, because of the scope, rigour and humanity of its action, the food bank against hunger in portugal, an association which has already been visited by the european commission and which has high standards of management and implementation of concrete support, a good example to follow. i agree that the insufficient resources at its disposal will not allow it to cope with many of the situations which are currently plaguing the european union, and i hope that it can be strengthened in the future and that closer cooperation will be established with the organisations which, on the ground, are helping to end hunger and to meet the most basic needs of the citizens. a europe which also wants to be prosperous must look after those who have less and those who need it most and contribute together with the member states to the establishment of a minimum social network, a threshold which no one can cross.
in writing. − the judgment of the court of justice of the european union of 13 april 2011 ordered the termination of the european food aid programme for the most deprived (efap), which was established in 1986 and had been in existence for 25 years. the cap was based on the european union's common agricultural policy and operated according to a logic of distributing agricultural surpluses to the most deprived. the european commission has proposed the creation of a new fund to replace the eafrd, called the fund for european aid to the most deprived (feac). the european council of 8 february 2013 reduced the fund from eur 3,5 billion to eur 2,5 billion. i believe that the initial amount is the minimum allowable, that co-financing should be 100% and that the participation of the member states in this fund should be compulsory.
in writing. the creation of this fund for european aid to the most deprived (fead) is important but insufficient in view of the real needs of the population. the so-called austerity policies, especially those imposed by eu-imf programmes and implemented by national governments, have led to the increase of social inequalities, unemployment, poverty and hunger, among other social scourges. we note as a positive change, compared to the initial proposal, the increase in the budget to 3500 million for the period 2014-2020, corresponding to 500 million euros per year, similar to the defunct european food aid programme for the most deprived. we also welcome the fact that all member states must participate in this fund. although we voted in favour of the report, we are very concerned about the inclusion of the eafrd in the european social fund (esf), a concern shared by a number of social organisations. in addition to the increased bureaucracy required of social organisations to access the fund, the most worrying is the reduction that the fead will represent in the other esf headings, weakening its objectives, which will mainly affect the countries that need it most, such as portugal.
in writing. − through the europe 2020 strategy, the european union has set itself the objective of reducing by 2020 the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion by at least 20 million. this economic and financial crisis is aggravating poverty and social exclusion across the union. in 2011, almost 120 million europeans were at risk of poverty or social exclusion, an increase of 6 million in two years and now corresponding to nearly a quarter of the total population. more than 40 million are victims of severe material deprivation. one in ten people under the age of 60 lives in a household with low work intensity. the proposed support from the fund should not be considered as a substitute for the overall policies needed to reduce and eventually eradicate poverty, which remains a challenge for the union and the member states. i believe that the creation of a new fund for european aid to the most deprived would express the union's fundamental principles and values and the tangible recognition of the union's willingness to play its part in the fight against the challenges of poverty and social exclusion. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − respect for human dignity and solidarity are core values of the eu. according to article 3 teu, the union's objective is to promote peace, its values and the well-being of its peoples. unfortunately, in 2011, 40 million europeans were among the victims of severe material deprivation, and almost 120 million were at risk of poverty or social exclusion. it is therefore necessary to rethink specific actions aimed at alleviating the scourge of poverty and social exclusion. if the eu has only 2.5 billion to help citizens in need, while the us spends 100 billion to help households in need, we can conclude that the resources proposed for the esf are extremely limited and far from sufficient. the future of europe depends on our ability to stop the transmission of disadvantages from one generation to the next: children who are victims of material deprivation are in fact less likely than their better-off peers to reach their full potential as adults. i voted in favour of the regulation, hoping that the response to poverty and social exclusion will not be exhausted by the european aid fund.
in writing. − in the context of the europe 2020 strategy, the eu is committed to reducing by at least 20 million the number of people living in or at risk of poverty or social exclusion by 2020. in its budget proposal for the next multiannual financial framework, the commission allocated a budget of eur 2.5 billion to the fund for european aid to the most deprived. this fund is intended to enable member states to distribute surplus food as food aid. this will allow member states to assist around 2 million more deprived people per year, with positive results for the health, social inclusion, employment and labour market of the population. i am in favour of the fund being applied to all member states, but i do not think it should be used for any purpose other than helping the most deprived. for the reasons given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. the creation of this fund (fead) is important but insufficient in view of the real needs of the population. the austerity policies imposed by the imf/eu and national governments have led to the increase of social inequalities, unemployment, poverty and the population at risk of poverty. we welcome the adoption of the amendment, which, as we proposed, increased the budget to eur 3500 million for the period 2014-2020, corresponding to eur 500 million per year, similar to the defunct european food aid programme for the most deprived. we also welcome the fact that participation in this fund is compulsory for all member states, which could prevent member states who do not want to participate in the programme from lobbying against the existence of the efsd. however, we are very concerned about the inclusion of the eafrd in the european social fund (esf), a concern shared by a number of social organisations. apart from the bureaucracy required of organisations to access the fund, the most worrying is the reduction it will represent in the esf due to the inclusion of the fead, which will mainly affect the countries that need it most.
in writing. - i approve this report, given that the aim of eurodac is to create a much wider information technology system containing the fingerprints of asylum seekers, and it was set up to facilitate the application of the dublin system. the aim of the regulation is to identify specific and clear rules, as well as harmonised rules in all member states of the european union, both with regard to the storage, comparison and deletion of fingerprints, while at the same time providing for data security protection. i believe that all of us as european citizens have a stake in this, as do all those seeking asylum in our member states.
in writing. − the powers of access to eurodac granted to law enforcement authorities should not affect the right of applicants for international protection to have their applications processed in a timely manner in accordance with the applicable legislation. in addition, a hit on eurodac and the subsequent opening of a procedure under council framework decision 2006/960/jha of 18 december 2006 on simplifying the exchange of data and information between law enforcement authorities of the member states.
in writing. − this initiative is part of the package of proposals aimed at establishing a common european asylum system. after 10 years of operation of eurodac, where the fingerprints of asylum seekers over 14 years of age are stored, improvements are needed to make it clearer and more coherent, to allow more effective support for the application of the dublin regulation and to provide for the transfer of the operational management of the system to eu-lisa. eurodac will play an important role in the fight against terrorism and serious crime, with national police forces and europol being able to compare fingerprints collected in criminal investigations with those contained in eurodac, while stricter data protection rules and the necessary safeguards to ensure that such data cannot be used for any purpose other than the fight against terrorism and serious crime have been introduced, and with full respect for the principle of proportionality in the public interest. i regret that the council has not been ambitious enough in establishing a solidarity mechanism to allow for a more solidarity-based sharing of responsibility for the relocation of asylum seekers with the countries of the south.
in writing. − the current terrorist threat recommends that the european union should not be too cautious or naive in dealing with questions of access to its territory and should provide the necessary conditions for the monitoring of third-country nationals who, on the grounds of asylum, are residing in the union. the eurodac system is an addition to this effort. the collection of fingerprints and their provision for comparison should be understood as a consideration to be paid by those who are hosted in the european union and who cannot ignore how this circumstance can lead to abuse and how criminal networks of various kinds infiltrate and operate in the union through asylum fraud. in accordance with the maxim 'no one should be afraid', law-abiding foreign nationals should regard this system as an additional means of identifying and punishing those who commit crimes while enjoying the protection and welcome granted to them by the union.
in writing. − we oppose access to eurodac data by the authorities designated by the member states and europol. fingerprinting asylum seekers was an extremely negative step. like us, many others have rejected this further invasion of the privacy of those who come to eu countries fleeing war, conflicts of different kinds, hunger and poverty - to which eu policies so often contribute. this proposal is a further step in this profoundly negative process which allows not only the storage of data, as was foreseen with the implementation of the dublin convention, but also its access outside this framework. it is therefore deeply worrying that access to eurodac data, i.e. the fingerprints of beneficiaries of international protection, is allowed for law enforcement purposes, even up to 3 years after the status has been recognised for these persons. this regulation is inseparable from a certain xenophobic view, according to which asylum seekers and persons granted international protection have a greater potential to commit criminal acts. we voted against it.
in writing. − the eurodac system was established by regulation (ec) no 2725/2000 and compares fingerprints for the purpose of the effective application of the dublin convention. this proposal is to withdraw the 2010 proposal and replace it with a new one, with the aim, firstly, of taking into account the european parliament resolution and the outcome of the negotiations in the council and, secondly, of introducing the possibility for member states' law enforcement authorities and europol to have access to the eurodac central database for the purposes of preventing, detecting and investigating terrorist offences and other serious crimes. it has become essential that access to eurodac for law enforcement purposes be taken into account as an integral part of a balanced agreement on the negotiations of the common european asylum system package in order to complete that package by the end of 2012. that's why i'm in favour.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal to set up the eurodac fingerprint comparison system for the purpose of the effective implementation of the regulation establishing the criteria and mechanisms for determining the member state responsible for examining an asylum application lodged in one of the member states by a third-country national or a stateless person and requests for comparison with eurodac data submitted by the responsible authorities of the member states and europol for law enforcement purposes and amending the regulation establishing a european agency for the operational management of large-scale it systems in the area of freedom, security and justice. the commission proposal has a number of amendments which can be grouped into two categories: technical amendments (e.g. adaptation to the provisions of the lisbon treaty, references to the proposal for a recast of the refugee directive, internal references) and amendments aimed at clarifying the text. the other amendments aim to include observations applicable to the european data protection supervisor.
in writing. − eurodac was established by regulation (ec) no 2725/2000 on the establishment of the eurodac system for the comparison of fingerprints for the effective application of the dublin convention. the proposal for the recast of the eurodac regulation was drafted to ensure more efficient support in the implementation of the dublin regulation. the commission adopted an amended proposal in september 2009 to take account of the european parliament resolution and the outcome of the negotiations in the council and to introduce the possibility for member states' police authorities and europol to access the eurodac central database for the purposes of the prevention, detection and investigation of terrorist offences and other serious crimes. with the entry into force of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) and the abolition of the system of pillars, the proposal for a council decision has become obsolete and it is now necessary to replace it with a new proposal, which already takes into account the tfeu. in view of the rapporteur's conclusions, i voted in favour of the european parliament's legislative resolution.
in writing. - this report on the amendment of regulation no 2725/2000 is part of the asylum package, where the european commission, through the eurodac fingerprint comparison database, seeks to ensure effective application of the dublin convention. the proposal opens up the possibility for the judicial authorities of the member states and europol to access eurodac data for the purposes of preventing, detecting and investigating terrorist offences through european coordination. the data on beneficiaries will also remain available in order to monitor the abuse of the european asylum system, in particular by organised crime networks. as in previous reports on the asylum package, i am in favour of adopting this report.
in writing. − we oppose access to eurodac data by the authorities designated by the member states and europol. fingerprinting asylum seekers was an extremely negative step. like us, many others have rejected this further invasion of the privacy of those who come to eu countries fleeing war, conflicts of different kinds, hunger and misery to which eu policies have contributed greatly. this proposal is a further step in this profoundly negative process which allows not only the storage of data, as was foreseen with the implementation of the dublin convention, but also its access outside this framework. it is therefore deeply worrying that access to eurodac data, i.e. the fingerprints of beneficiaries of international protection, is allowed for law enforcement purposes, even up to 3 years after the status has been recognised for these persons. this possibility is based on an unacceptable xenophobic and racist principle that asylum seekers and persons granted international protection have a greater potential to commit criminal acts.
in writing. - i welcome this report, starting by stressing that free movement is one of the fundamental principles of the european union and the ability to move within the european union without having to face internal border controls is one of its most positive results. many people make use of this freedom, and public opinion often ranks free movement among the union's most significant achievements. i believe that the foundations of schengen cooperation are relatively solid. however, recent developments have shaken confidence in the ability of some member states to manage their borders in a way that does not undermine the free movement of persons within the schengen area. these incidents have challenged the balance that must be struck between safety and freedom of movement.
in writing. − the creation, with the schengen agreement, of a european area without border controls was an important step in building an open internal market based on the essential freedom of movement of persons. although this space is an invaluable achievement, the truth is that the balance between the necessary security within our borders and the fundamental freedom of movement has recently been a recurring theme. this is because there have been isolated cases of abuse and lack of control by some member states, which have raised the alarm about the possible need for the temporary reintroduction of internal border controls (which has also already occurred in some cases). i agree with the rapporteur on this point that a correct balance must be found which leaves member states sufficient room for manoeuvre, both in unforeseeable and foreseeable situations, to re-establish their borders, while ensuring a more collective decision-making process.
in writing. - this report provides for the possibility of temporarily reintroducing internal border controls in so-called exceptional circumstances for a strictly limited period of time. the exclusion of immigration from the list of possible reasons will be only apparent, since it is envisaged that assistance will be provided by frontex and europol, two bodies whose remit is largely (particularly in the case of frontex) to suppress immigration. it is considered that the reintroduction of internal border controls should be avoided for political reasons, as if the whole framework of this proposal were not based on political reasons. the whole hypocritical rhetoric of free movement of persons is thus once again brought to naught. they cannot for a moment allow restrictions on the free (or rather, unrestricted) movement of capital and goods. despite all the evils that the dictate has brought to the people. the people, as labour force, are allowed to move in so far as this serves the needs of capital (which controls the integration process). that's all i know. the extremely reactionary and securitarian nature of this proposal is clear. we voted against it, of course.
in writing. − free movement is one of the fundamental principles of the european union, and the ability to move within the european union without having to face internal border controls is one of its most positive outcomes. many people make use of this freedom, and it is unanimous that free movement is among the most significant benefits achieved by the union. however, in cases which can be explained, we may consider the possibility of temporarily reintroducing internal border controls. i agree with the principle of a more coordinated and collective decision-making process in the event of reintroduction of internal border controls. an eu right, such as free movement, which is benefiting a large number of eu citizens, should not be affected by the decision of an isolated member state. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, including the establishment of a european data protection supervisor.

in writing. the rapporteur stressed that any attempt to invoke new pretexts, such as migration flows, in order to reintroduce internal border controls should be categorically opposed. in the event of possible abuses of freedom of movement, which may in fact compromise the security of union citizens, there are guidelines provided for in the commission communication of 16 september 2011 on schengen governance (com (2011) 561) which provide clear indicators on how to assess, in a consistent manner, a threat to public policy and national security. the rapporteur therefore supports the adoption of these guidelines and calls on the commission to act without delay, and also invites member states wishing to reintroduce internal border controls, and the neighbouring countries concerned, to discuss this measure. i voted in favour of the report because i consider that the free movement of persons and goods is one of the fundamental principles of the european union.
in writing. the schengen package includes two reports, one on the schengen borders code and the other on the evaluation mechanism. the schengen borders code lays down the rules on external border control and the abolition of internal border control and, in exceptional cases, its reintroduction, always as a last resort and after the application of other measures. this report stresses that migration should not be seen as a threat to public policies and national security. it also reaffirms that the reintroduction of internal borders should be a joint decision and that unilateral national decisions, such as those of italy and france in 2011, should be avoided. the possibility of temporarily introducing internal borders is also added, in the event of serious deficiencies being identified, by the schengen evaluation mechanism through comitology. i approve this report as part of the schengen package.

in writing. the european parliament adopted today the draft european council decision establishing the composition of the european parliament. this decision takes account of the accession of croatia to the european union and the terms resulting from the treaty of lisbon. the european parliament will therefore have no more than 750 members in addition to the president, and representation will be degressively proportional, with a minimum limit of six members per member state and no member state being allocated more than 96 seats. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.
