in writing. the vienna convention establishes the necessary rules to ensure adequate and fair compensation for victims of damage caused by nuclear accidents by creating a special system of civil liability in the field of nuclear energy. with regard to eu member states, the union has exclusive competence with regard to the provisions contained in the 1997 protocol and member states cannot become contracting parties. however, the council proposes to authorise bulgaria, the czech republic, estonia, hungary, lithuania, poland and slovakia to ratify or conclude the 1997 protocol in so far as their accession to the eu is subsequent to the ratification of the protocol by the union. in view of the importance of the matters covered by the protocol, i support the rapporteur in his recommendation that this report be adopted.
in writing. the report under consideration, drawn up by mr alajos mészáros, concerns a recommendation to the european parliament to approve the draft council decision authorising certain member states to ratify or accede, in the interest of the european union, to the protocol adopted on 12 september 1997 amending the vienna convention of 21 may 1963 on civil liability for nuclear damage and to make a declaration on the application of the relevant rules of eu law. considering that all member states have the same rights and obligations, it is essential that there is uniformity in all matters, in particular as regards the rules governing the procedure for the recognition and enforcement of judgments in the field of nuclear damage. all victims of nuclear accidents must be treated fairly and be properly compensated. i voted in favour of this recommendation because i believe that the member states which have adopted the vienna convention (bulgaria, the czech republic, estonia, hungary, lithuania, poland and slovakia) must ratify or conclude the protocol to the 1997 vienna convention in order to be able to benefit from the compensation due to victims of nuclear accidents.
in writing. the international nuclear liability regime is governed mainly by two instruments: the vienna and paris conventions. the vienna convention was adopted in 1963 with the aim of ensuring adequate and fair compensation for victims of damage caused by nuclear accidents in the field of nuclear energy. it was amended by the 1997 protocol, which contains a new definition of nuclear damage, incorporating the concept of environmental damage and prevention measures, broadening the geographical scope, extending the period during which claims may be submitted, increasing the minimum amounts of compensation. this protocol amending the vienna convention, adopted under the auspices of the international atomic energy agency, includes provisions on jurisdiction and on the recognition and enforcement of decisions affecting provisions contained in eu law. the eu therefore has competence over the provisions of the protocol and member states cannot become contracting parties to the protocol in so far as those provisions are concerned. the council proposes to authorise the member states which are contracting parties to the vienna convention, namely bulgaria, the czech republic, estonia, hungary, lithuania, poland and slovakia, to ratify or conclude the 1997 protocol. in this context, we consider this proposal for a decision to be justified.
in writing. − international civil liability in nuclear matters is governed by two instruments: the vienna convention and the paris convention. the vienna convention was adopted to provide adequate and fair compensation to victims of damage caused by nuclear accidents by creating a special civil liability system in the field of nuclear energy. with the adoption of this regulation, the member states which are contracting parties to the vienna convention, namely bulgaria, the czech republic, estonia, hungary, lithuania, poland and slovakia, are hereby authorised to ratify or conclude the 1997 protocol.

in writing. − i approve this report, taking into account that, in the context of a thorough modernisation of state aid rules, in order to contribute both to the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and to fiscal consolidation and growth, article 107 of the treaty must be applied throughout the union in an effective and uniform manner. council regulation (ec) no 659/1999 of 22 march 1999 codified and reinforced the commission's previous practice of increasing legal certainty and supporting the development of state aid policy in a transparent environment. however, in the light of the experience gained from its application in recent situations, such as enlargement and the economic and financial crisis, certain aspects of that regulation should be amended in order to provide the commission with simplified and more effective instruments for the control and enforcement of state aid. i therefore believe that the commission must be given more effective instruments to bring about greater transparency, as the article in question provides.
in writing. - articles 107 and 108 tfeu lay down the community rules on state aid. regulation (ec) no 659/1999, which clarifies the procedural rules for the implementation of these articles, is now subject to a proposed amendment to make state aid better contribute to the implementation of agenda 2020 and to the economic prosperity of the member states. the commission's proposal aims to make the reporting process more effective and transparent and to collect and process information more efficiently. the commission will not have to adopt a formal decision on complaints that do not comply with the necessary information requirements or are unfounded, and parliament proposes the same procedure for situations where no irregularities are detected. as regards the collection of information, the commission may extend the range of sources of information and sanction officials who supply misleading or omitted information. the ep should ask the commission to investigate specific cases in certain sectors and to play a more prominent role in this area. i support this report which, by helping to eliminate distortions of competition in the internal market, is good for european citizens.

in writing. - sirpa pietikäinen has presented us with a report on a proposal for a council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 659/1999 laying down detailed rules for the application of article 93 of the ec treaty (state aid). state aid is governed by articles 107 and 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. in the light of the commission communication, it is necessary to modernise the union's policy in this area. improvements in the handling of complaints are essential to make the procedures faster, more efficient and more transparent, thus helping to discourage fraud. state aid must be aimed at the integrated development of the single market and must not undermine the proper functioning of the european union. i voted in favour of this proposal as the objective is to make state aid contribute to improving the implementation of agenda 2020 and to promoting economic growth and prosperity in the member states.
in writing. - the neoliberal approach embodied in this report is clear. it is argued that the commission should examine the cases submitted to it and take great care not to exempt too many activities from state aid control, lest some sovereign state decide to interfere with the operation of the sacrosanct free market. on the other hand, federalism is being strengthened by providing the commission with simplified and more effective instruments for monitoring and enforcing state aid, i.e. by supporting the direct collection of information from market players by the commission, replacing what was until now a sovereign competence of each member state and its institutions. another fundamental question remains to be resolved: member states with money in their budgets - the biggest beneficiaries of eu integration - can help their businesses, associations or institutions. member states which do not have it are at a clear disadvantage. this is an inequality that no legislation can solve. limiting state intervention in the economy is the aim of the eu and legislation like this. but nothing is said about the billions of euros poured into the financial sector, with the eu's blessing.

in writing. − in 2011, the parliament and the council decided by common accord to transpose the 2005 oecd export credit agreement into community law. it is expected that the annual reports of the member states will take account of this activity. the reports sent by the member states to the commission and the assessment made by the commission are far from satisfying parliament's intention to be able to assess the compatibility of export credit activities with the union's external policy. this is particularly the case for information on non-financial elements such as the treatment of environmental risks. in this respect, i support the rapporteur's request that the commission provide guidance to the member states so that in the next annual reports the commission will be able to provide parliament with an assessment of whether, in its view, the export credit activities of the member states are compatible with the objectives of the eu's external action.
in writing. − export credits are an important instrument to support trade and investment by european companies in international trade. member states' export credit activities during 2011 amounted to eur 250 billion, which translates into significant trade and business opportunities for european companies. in 2010, parliament negotiated obligations to provide stricter information requirements for member states and the commission in relation to export credits. the new reporting requirements, first applied in 2011, aim to enhance transparency and ensure monitoring of compliance with international standards for export credits and compliance with eu treaty obligations. however, the annual reports from the member states are far from meeting parliament's objectives. the rapporteur therefore made recommendations for the next report in order to help improve the information presented.
in writing. − according to article 207 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), the common commercial policy is conducted in accordance with the principles and objectives of the union's external action. credit activities are of great importance to member states in 2011 due to their total exposure of over eur 250 billion, including 260 transactions with significant notified environmental implications, which translate into significant trade and business opportunities for european companies. i am in favour of this report because it allows for greater verification of the compatibility of export credit agencies with the objectives of the union's external action and provides the necessary information on the treatment of environmental risks in the calculation of export credit agencies' premiums.
in writing. − regulation no 1233/2011 expressly aims to improve the transparency of export credit agencies (eca) by requiring member states to submit annual eca reports with elements on assets and liabilities, payment claims settled and recoveries, new commitments, exposures and premiums collected, as well as contingent liabilities that may arise from officially supported export credits; on how environmental risks, which may entail other relevant risks, are taken into account in officially supported export credits; on an assessment of the compatibility of export credit agencies with eu objectives and obligations. the rapporteur points out that there is a lack of transparency in the reports that have been known and calls for improvements at this level, increasing the content of the information provided on aces so that its impact in various areas can be more easily assessed. these are, in essence, justified concerns.

in writing. - i approve this report, starting by welcoming the fact that negotiations in the council on the creation of a statute for the european foundation have been intensified again during the irish presidency of the council. i therefore encourage the member states to take this opportunity to work towards a rapid and broad introduction of the statute, with all guarantees of transparency, in order to remove obstacles to the cross-border activity of foundations and to promote the creation of new foundations that respond to the needs of people residing in the territory of the union or working for the public good or the interests of society. i would stress that the adoption of such a statute would contribute to the realisation of genuine european citizenship and would pave the way for the drawing up of a statute for the european association. i would also stress that the european foundation must contribute to the development of a genuinely european culture and identity, with the potential to create jobs for young people, a group in which unemployment is reaching alarming levels.
in writing. - i consider it very important to harmonize the functioning of national foundations in order to facilitate their operation in the european single market, and i therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the statute for a european foundation, because this initiative will facilitate the establishment and crossborder operations of foundations in the european area, which will thus benefit from a reduction in costs and consequently from a greater availability of funds for their public utility actions.
in writing. − the commission presented in february 2012 a proposal to create a european foundation statute that would remove barriers and facilitate the cross-border activities of foundations and the transfer of donations. the statute of the european foundation provides for the introduction of minimum standards in the areas of transparency, accountability, registration, control and audit. in the field of tax law, the principles of non-discriminatory taxation of foreign foundations should apply automatically in the future and without a comparability check. i think it is important that these standards be adopted, which are more harmonized but also compatible with national regulations.
in writing. − the role of foundations in the european union is unquestionable, especially at a time of crisis like the one we are going through and with member states subject to financial assistance programmes. the foundations are active in areas as diverse as research, education, health, social action, the environment, heritage protection, culture, sport, etc. in portugal, let me mention two foundations with international appeal which are a great honour to us: the calouste gulbenkian foundation and the antónio champalimaud foundation. there are many other foundations, much smaller in size, which also carry out worthwhile activities that could go international if the conditions were right. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal, presented on 8 february 2012, to create the statute of the european foundation, which should be aligned with national regulations. i voted in favour of mrs evelyn regner's interim report on the proposal for a council regulation on the statute for a european foundation, as the benefits for all parties (citizens, donors, foundations and member states) are enormous.
in writing. − the number of public benefit foundations has been increasing, as has the range of operations (in areas such as education and research, arts and culture, social and health services and the environment), which are becoming more international in character. foundations face differences in legal, administrative and tax definitions and practices. this report aims to make this process both less costly and slower. the commission published its proposal for a statute of the european foundation (ef) in february 2012. it is intended for public-benefit foundations. the report makes a number of recommendations and amendments: the minimum level of assets of eur 25 000 must be maintained throughout the life of the foundation; the existence of a european foundation in any member state shall be for an indefinite period or for a defined period of time of not less than four years; with regard to employee representation, the negotiation process, which relates only to the information and consultation of employees in the eu, should provide for the participation of employees in the management of the fe; the registered office and the administrative head office of an elt shall be in the member state in which it is established; the proposal must be limited to a civil law instrument, while reinforcing essential elements of the public benefit concept. we abstained.

in writing. − this report is based on the new statute of the european foundation. this statute sets out minimum standards for transparency, accountability, supervision and use of funds, which in turn can serve as a quality mark for citizens and donors, thereby ensuring trust in the european foundation and facilitating its activities in the eu for the benefit of all citizens. the european foundation must operate in more than two member states and contribute to the development of a truly european culture and identity. i would like to stress, among other reasons, the potential of foundations in creating jobs for young people, a group in which unemployment is at alarming levels, which is why i also voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the disparity in the civil and tax law applicable to foundations in the member states of the european union is an obstacle to the establishment of the activities of these public-benefit organisations in other territories of the union. the high costs of administrative procedures and the legal uncertainty associated with crossborder operations prevent the development of a truly european culture and identity. considering that the establishment of a common statute for the european foundation could greatly facilitate the centralisation and transfer of resources, knowledge and donations, as well as the carrying out of activities throughout the eu, i supported this proposal for a regulation, which aims, in a time of budgetary restraint, to strengthen the activity of public-benefit entities through a civil law instrument that strengthens the recognition and equivalence of the statute of foundations in the eu territory.

in writing. - the purpose of this proposal is to establish minimum standards for working and living conditions on board ships. given the global nature of the maritime transport sector, those rules should apply to the entire sector. the responsibility for ensuring that ships comply with the relevant provisions lies with the owners, masters and flag states, and the eu must therefore provide mechanisms to ensure that the relevant standards are applied to all ships calling at union ports, irrespective of their nationality or flag. that is what this proposal is about.
in writing. − the main concern of the member states of the european union is people, whether they are european citizens or from other states. while their attention is focused on the welfare of their citizens, they also demand that all see their rights respected. mr simpson reports on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending directive 2009/16/ec on port state control of ships. the european authorities are most concerned about working conditions on board and the ship's environmental impact. as regards working conditions, it is essential that shipowners comply with the standards adopted by the international labour organisation, which are essential for the well-being and safety of workers. as far as the vessel is concerned, we all know that run-down, rusty vessels with leaking fuel or oil are sources of pollution and real threats to the environment. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because it represents a major step forward in the protection of people and the marine environment by strengthening the 2006 maritime convention and i call on the 15 member states which have not yet ratified it to do so quickly so that it can enter into force on 1 august.
in writing. − the maritime labour convention adopted by the ilo applies to international maritime transport and covers matters such as the minimum conditions to be observed for seafarers working on board a ship, accommodation, leisure, food and table service, health protection, medical care, welfare and social security protection, among others. the convention aims to set common minimum standards for all flags and all seafarers and, having reached its 30th ratification in august 2012, can now enter into force. the european union intends to amend the existing directive 2009/16/ec on port state control of ships in order to align the text more closely with the content of the convention, making it clear that international minimum standards are not a reason to prejudice existing european standards when they are of a higher level. the commission also intends to ensure an information channel with the ilo to promote the dissemination of good practice and to strengthen the confidentiality of complaints in ensuring the protection of seafarers when lodging complaints. we supported the report.
in writing. - we have long advocated measures to establish minimum standards for working and living conditions on board ships. as the shipping industry is global, these standards should be applied to the entire industry. ships which do not comply with the standards are inadmissible, because they undermine the rights of workers, but also their safety and security, as well as the protection of the environment. the responsibility for ensuring that ships comply with the relevant provisions lies with the shipowners, masters and flag states. however, not all flag states effectively enforce these provisions. failure to comply with these rules leads to unsafe conditions on board some ships, putting human lives and the marine environment at risk. the eu must therefore provide mechanisms to ensure that the relevant standards are applied to all ships calling at union ports, regardless of the nationality of the seafarers or the flag of the ship. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the maritime labour convention (mlc) was adopted by the international labour organisation (ilo) on 23 february 2006. parliament has long advocated measures to establish minimum standards for working and living conditions on board ships. given the global nature of the maritime transport sector, those rules should apply to the entire sector. measures to ensure compliance with minimum standards of working and living conditions on board ships play a particularly important role in achieving these objectives. ships which do not comply with these standards not only jeopardise the rights of workers but also their safety and security. the creation of an appropriate legislative framework is not sufficient and member states should, in addition, recruit an appropriate number of inspectors with the necessary qualifications to assess the working and living conditions of seafarers on board ships. i agree with the points made and therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − this report aims to bring european union legislation into line with the commitments it has made at international level. the maritime labour convention (mlc), adopted in 2006 and in force since 2013, replaces 37 conventions and other recommendations on the working conditions of seafarers on board. the amendment to directive 2009/13/ec thus provides for the inclusion of the implementing provisions which are provided for in title 5 of the ctm, concerning the responsibilities of the flag state in the control of this european legislation. for these reasons, i am in favour of this report.

in writing. the aim of this proposal is to support and enforce roadworthiness testing of motor vehicles with a view to improving road safety and protecting the environment. the proposal improves the application of road and technical inspection schemes, in particular where the technical conditions of vehicles create a risk to road safety, through measures such as suspension or cancellation of vehicle registration. it is therefore necessary to introduce a procedure for the registration of vehicles which ensures that vehicles which pose an immediate risk to road safety are not used on public roads, providing for the suspension and cancellation of the registration of such vehicles until they are re-approved at a new roadworthiness test. the original registration of a vehicle re-registered in another member state will automatically be cancelled. following a decision of the european court of justice, it is considered that the validity of roadworthiness tests should be mutually recognised by all member states. i therefore support this report.

in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the transport of dangerous goods by road. the inclusion and adjustment of some technical aspects is intended to introduce more precise specifications on the location of the registration, the suspension of the authorisation to drive on public roads for vehicles which constitute an immediate risk to road safety (until passing a new roadworthiness test) and the automatic cancellation of a registration in one member state when it is registered in another, as well as in the event of the vehicle being scrapped. parliament proposed adding concerns about the dimensions of registration certificates and the mention of roadworthiness tests, so as to reduce the paperwork that drivers must have in their possession at all times. it also introduces the recognition of the validity of roadworthiness tests by all member states and limits the delegation of power to the commission to a renewable period of five years instead of an unlimited period. we voted in favour.
in writing. the proposal aims to support and enforce roadworthiness testing of motor vehicles with a view to improving road safety and protecting the environment. it improves the application of roadworthiness and roadworthiness inspection schemes, in particular where the technical conditions of vehicles create an imminent risk to road safety, by means of measures such as suspension or cancellation of vehicle registration. in order to be marketed, vehicles must meet the applicable requirements for type approval, which ensures an optimal level of safety and environmental performance standards. the registration constitutes the official authorisation for the vehicle to be used on public roads and the confirmation that the vehicle meets the requirements applicable at the date. during its service life, a vehicle may be re-registered because it has changed ownership or been transferred for permanent use to another member state. it is therefore necessary to introduce a vehicle registration procedure to ensure that vehicles which pose an immediate risk to road safety are not used on public roads. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. the report introduces amendments to the commission proposal by clarifying that road inspections are only complementary to the main instrument, periodic inspection. the regulation introduces non-agricultural tractors, mainly used on public roads for the carriage of goods by road. at least 5% of the total number of commercial vehicles referred to in the regulation and registered in a member state and another 5% of commercial vehicles not registered but operated in a member state shall be inspected. furthermore, roadworthiness certificates and roadworthiness reports are required to have a standardised format across the eu and each company listed in the system should be assigned a risk profile according to a set of criteria relating to the inspections carried out on that company, in order to monitor more frequently who has a high risk profile with regard to road safety and environmental protection. we voted in favour. the application of these rules to light commercial vehicles is subject to the approval of an amendment already submitted to the tran committee and which has not been approved.
in writing. - the european parliament has always considered road safety an important societal issue. we must therefore once again give a clear signal of your commitment to road safety. alongside technical measures, it is the understanding of most that the effectiveness of road safety policy ultimately depends on the behaviour of users. for this reason, it is essential to educate, train and enforce the rules. however, the road safety system should also take account of human error and inappropriate behaviour and should correct them where possible. all actors, in particular vehicles and infrastructure, should therefore be less aggressive in order to avoid and limit the consequences of these failures for users, in particular the most vulnerable. the introduction of roadworthiness tests is therefore of the utmost importance in order to combat possible faults, especially those of vehicles.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report which calls for a clear legal framework on liability for the fitness of commercial vehicles. this is a very important issue which has consequences for the security of all european citizens. i agree with the proposals which clarify that companies operating commercial vehicles should always be responsible for the proper maintenance of their vehicles. companies shall ensure that regular inspections are carried out on those parts of a vehicle which may affect its fitness. as regards the burden, the question of liability is also clarified. since several operators may be involved in the handling and immobilization of the cargo of a commercial vehicle, responsibility should be assigned to each according to the tasks performed.

in writing. − directive 2009/40/ec lays down minimum standards for the regular roadworthiness test of vehicles. the european commission has presented new rules for vehicle roadworthiness testing which aim to further enhance road safety and ensure a high level of environmental protection by establishing common minimum standards for vehicle roadworthiness testing throughout the european union, with member states free to go further and introduce higher standards if they consider it appropriate. in this respect, the technical requirements and inspection methods laid down should be considered as eu minimum standards. member states should be allowed to maintain or introduce higher standards. the same applies to the qualification requirements for inspectors, which should also be considered as minimum. the commission also proposes to strengthen the independence of inspectors and to eliminate possible conflicts of interest. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i support maintaining the current minimum rules, which stipulate that the first vehicle inspection must be carried out after four years and subsequent inspections every two years. the mandatory inspections should also be extended to trailers weighing more than two tonnes and to caravan trailers weighing more than 750 kg.

in writing. - a car park that is inspected and controlled is an essential aspect of road safety. this proposal for a regulation lays down minimum standards and criteria in this field. the main elements of the commission's proposal are to introduce mandatory technical inspections for scooters and motorcycles, as well as light trailers of less than 3.5 tonnes, which were previously left to the member states, into european legislation. the commission also intends to change the frequency of technical inspections by proposing that, for vehicles over six years old, the minimum frequency should be increased from two years to at least one inspection per year, i.e. the application of the 4-2-1 year formula depending on the age of the vehicle, which parliament does not agree with and which is being reverted to the 4-2-2 formula, thus weakening the initial proposal, which is why our group did not agree. the report also aims to regulate the minimum technical requirements and inspection methods in the eu, as well as the qualified and independent training for inspectors, and to reduce the delegation of powers to the commission. some of the shortcomings in the report justified our abstention.
in writing. - i am of the opinion that motorcycles and mopeds should be subject to compulsory technical inspections in all eu countries, as cars are at present. only then will we be able to increase road safety and halve the number of deaths on european roads by 2020. therefore, from 2016, motorcycles should be subject to mandatory inspections in all member states. the same should apply to mopeds from 2018. the mandatory inspections should also be extended to trailers weighing more than two tonnes and to caravan trailers weighing more than 750 kg. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. the commission has presented new rules for vehicle roadworthiness testing which aim to improve road safety and ensure a high level of environmental protection. the proposal is in line with the road safety objectives set out in the white paper roadmap for a single european transport area. the proposal is based on the establishment of common eu-wide minimum standards for vehicle inspection, with member states free to go further and introduce higher standards if they consider it appropriate. the european parliament, through its committee on transport and tourism, examined the proportionality of the proposed measures to the objectives pursued. the impact of the proposed measures on citizens should be carefully assessed in order to avoid an unnecessary financial and administrative burden. i agree with the balance that the european parliament wants to strike between improving road safety and avoiding an unnecessary financial and administrative burden, and i have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − directive 2009/40/ec lays down minimum standards for the routine roadworthiness test of light vehicles, vehicles for the public transport of passengers and heavy goods vehicles and their trailers. however, it does not set them for scooters and motorcycles, a category which represents a higher risk group of users. in order to enhance road safety and considering that the scope of inspection of motor vehicles should be extended to achieve the same safety on public roads, the commission has presented this proposal for a regulation which, among other improvements, introduces mandatory inspections for scooters and motorcycles as well as more frequent inspections for certain categories of vehicles and repeals that directive.
in writing. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs for sale to the ultimate consumer. several exceptions were made for certain categories of vehicles and also according to the kilometres travelled, in particular for two- and three-wheel vehicles. from 2016, motorcycles should be subject to periodic and mandatory inspections, and mopeds in 2018. however, if the european commission considers that these measures are ineffective in reducing accidents involving motorcycles and mopeds, they may be amended and withdrawn.

in writing. − water pollution is one of the main environmental concerns expressed by eu citizens, which is why legislation must provide for appropriate means to maintain water quality and prevent water contamination. the proposal we are now voting on amends the water framework directive and the environmental quality standards directive in order to update the list of priority substances in the field of water policy as required by the water framework directive. given the technical nature of the proposal, i support the position of the rapporteur and the committee on the environment, public health and food safety.
in writing. - report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending directives 2000/60/ec and 2008/105/ec as regards priority substances in the field of water policy the report by mr seeber deals with the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending directives 2000/60/ec and 2008/105/ec as regards priority substances in the field of water policy. this proposal amends the water framework directive and the environmental quality standards directive by updating the list of priority substances in the field of water policy as required by the framework directive every four years. measures adopted in the context of the water framework directive aim at the progressive reduction of emissions of priority substances into the aquatic environment or, in the case of priority hazardous substances, their cessation or phasing out. water pollution is one of the main environmental concerns expressed by eu citizens. in their resolution of 3 july 2012 on the implementation of eu water legislation, 68% of europeans consider water quantity and quality problems to be serious. so, in addition to prevention through informed and sensitized public opinion, we must promote the necessary policies to combat water pollution.
in writing. − the adoption of appropriate measures to control chemical pollution is an important aspect of water resource management and quality assurance. the environment committee of the european parliament voted a set of amendments which included new provisions in the european commission's proposal, making it more demanding, in particular with regard to the creation of a watch list for the monitoring of substances for which there is concern about their impact on public health and the environment. in addition, three pharmaceutical substances of concern for their persistence, bioaccumulation and toxicity were included in the priority list. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use. the final proposal was thus weakened. we cannot but stress the need to ensure that the conditions for effective monitoring and intervention by the competent public bodies in defence of water quality are met, particularly in terms of the material and financial resources allocated to these bodies, which is increasingly being called into question. we reiterate our disagreements on the water framework directive and the need for further consideration of the problems associated with polluting sources.
in writing. − the adoption of this report updates the list of substances which pose a risk to the aquatic environment, with a view to ensuring better water quality. the proposal, already agreed with national governments, adds 12 new products to the list of pollutants controlled in eu waters and creates a new watch list, which includes three pharmaceutical substances. this proposal adds 12 chemicals to the list of 33 priority pollutants that are controlled in eu surface waters such as lakes and rivers. this proposal amends the water framework directive and the environmental quality standards directive by updating the list of priority substances in the field of water policy as required by the framework directive at least every four years. the water framework directive identifies a list of priority substances, including chemicals that pose a significant risk to the aquatic environment in the eu. measures adopted in the context of the water framework directive aim at the progressive reduction of emissions of priority substances into the aquatic environment or, in the case of priority hazardous substances, their cessation or phasing out.
in writing. − chemical pollution is among the causes of the increasing pressure on the aquatic environment and on the quality and availability of clean drinking water for our society, so that the adoption of appropriate measures to control chemical pollution is a central aspect of the sustainable management of water resources. i voted in favour of this report, which welcomes the commission's proposal and proposes some amendments to make the water framework directive clearer and more effective in order to ensure the good status of surface water in the union and to facilitate its application in the member states. the main changes to the proposal are: (a) introduction of new priority substances; (b) a cost-effective timetable and implementation; (c) introduction of a list of widely used substances with persistent, bioaccumulating and toxic characteristics; (d) introduction of a list of substances under surveillance; and (e) public awareness that measures to combat water pollution should not be seen as costly impositions from brussels but measures in the collective interest of citizens.
in writing. − the water framework directive, adopted in 2005, sets a target for the sustainability of water resources in terms of good ecological, chemical and quantitative status to be achieved by european water bodies by 2015. as required by this directive, the list of priority substances should be updated every four years. the commission proposal adds 15 chemicals to the list of 33 pollutants monitored and controlled in eu surface waters, including industrial chemicals, biocides, plant protection products and, for the first time, three substances of pharmaceutical relevance. the substances have been selected on the basis of scientific evidence that they may pose a significant risk. the rapporteur considers that the inclusion of three substances of pharmaceutical relevance in the list is problematic, given the overriding importance of considerations relating to human health: water policy should not directly determine the health policy of the member states. in view of the above, i support the report which seeks to adopt appropriate measures to control chemical pollution in the aquatic environment.
in writing. − chemical pollution is among the causes of increasing pressure on the aquatic environment and on the quality and availability of clean drinking water for our society, so that the adoption of appropriate measures to control chemical pollution becomes a central aspect of the sustainable management of water resources. the proposal adds other chemicals to the list of 33 pollutants monitored and controlled in eu surface waters, including industrial chemicals, biocides and plant protection products. the rapporteur welcomes the provisions in the proposal which allow member states to reduce the monitoring efforts of substances with persistent, bioaccumulating and toxic characteristics. in this respect, the document has received my vote in favour.

in writing. − the so-called de minimis aid highlights the problem of budgetary availability in each member state, creating large differences and inequalities between countries and between companies in each country, in various sectors of economic activity. to these inequalities must be added the different aids from the eu itself, as is the case with the payments under the common agricultural policy. despite our outspoken opposition to the limitations imposed by the eu on the granting of state aid by each member state, we support the exclusion of some activities and sectors proposed by the commission, even if the eu information remains scarce and uncritical, contrary to what has already happened in other situations, in particular in the dissemination of aid per active worker or per capita. we regret that the commission's proposal to exclude the transport sectors in the outermost regions from the scope of the state aid scheme and thus allow them to receive de minimis aid, which could help to improve the situation of the transport sector and the prices charged in the regions of madeira and the azores, has been deleted, a possibility which the final version of the report jeopardises.

in writing. - blue growth is essential for the european union, particularly for coastal countries. it is imperative to recognise that on the one hand there are untapped resources and on the other hand the way some are exploited today puts at risk environmental sustainability and the survival of local and regional economies most directly linked to these sectors. in the face of the current crisis, creative and environmentally responsible ways of enhancing the possible economic return from the sensible and reasonable exploitation of activities in the sea-related sectors are welcome. i hope that the european union will help to ensure that this is the case and will not hinder the work of those who are trying to overcome the crisis on the ground, or more precisely at sea.
in writing. − the european commission presented a communication on 13 september 2012 entitled 'blue growth: opportunities for sustainable marine and maritime growth'. europe is the first maritime area in the world whose sustainability should be at the heart of our concerns. this is a sector that employs 5.4 million people and represents an added value of €500 billion for the european economy. the europe 2020 strategy is making a strong commitment to this sector, setting the following targets: 7 million jobs and €600 billion in value added. in fact, there are many areas with great potential for growth, such as: maritime, coastal and cruise tourism; blue biotechnology; marine mineral resources; aquaculture; blue energy, etc. because this is a sector with great potential for growth and leverage for the european economy, i voted in favour of the report by spyros danellis on blue growth - improving sustainable growth in the european union's maritime sector, maritime transport and tourism, and i hope that by 2020 the objectives set by the europe 2020 strategy will be achieved.
in writing. − the sustainable use of the immense resource of the sea must undoubtedly be an integral part of a national project for endogenous development. the european union could and should support these projects, particularly through its budget. but that is not the predominant meaning of this report. the report addresses important and positive aspects such as, among others, maritime and coastal spatial planning that takes account of local specificities and needs, the importance of and support for seabed mapping, the need to improve working conditions for seafarers and the safeguarding of europe's environmental and wildlife heritage. but the prevailing sense is not positive. what is being advocated is further progress in the private appropriation of nature, the commodification of its resources, the liberalisation of the shipping sector and the usurpation of new spheres of national sovereignty. free zones in island areas, a european maritime transport area, motorways of the sea, the creation of a european coastguard are some of the proposals we consider unacceptable.

in writing. - i welcome this report, stressing that the cooperative model is appropriate and shows potential to generate the much-needed sustainable local responses in the hard-hit economic, social and environmental fields. i think this is a model that is clearly opposed to the ones that have led us to this crisis, which are solely focused on the pursuit of high, short-term profits, in the service of very few. cooperatives do not move, they serve the people in their regions, and they are a great form of business formation. in the current recessionary context of unemployment, insolvency and bankruptcy, a practical and ambitious push must be made to strengthen their role as a good tool for jobseekers and a good alternative for workers trying to ensure the continuity of their companies in the closure processes. we must improve its context and make it known at european level in an ambitious way so that everyone can find in it a valuable way of organising and financing their activity.

in writing. − at a time like the present, which calls for mutual help and the ability to take advantage of scarce resources, cooperatives and other areas of the social economy emerge as an example of resistance and an option to be taken into account. citizens of european countries with a less cooperative tradition should consider exploring this option more deeply. i believe that, without replacing traditional enterprises, cooperatives promote closeness and solidarity between members, by promoting a better use of the resources at their disposal and a distribution of the proceeds not based solely on the criterion of profit. i believe that the european union and the member states would have much to gain if they looked at cooperatives more closely and provided themselves with the human and technical resources to enable them to monitor their activities.
in writing. − in a time of economic crisis, when growth is a mirage, cooperatives, like social enterprises, are one of the few pillars supporting the economy in many member states. every day we see companies going bankrupt or insolvent. some are able to continue their activity by becoming cooperatives, as they are better able to withstand the crisis and often even create more jobs. cooperatives, because they put people first - at the expense of profit - should be supported and subject to a legal framework that facilitates their tasks. it should be remembered that there are more than 150 000 cooperatives in the european union, involving human resources and employing an estimated 5 million people. because i understand that cooperatives play a real social role, i voted in favour of the report drawn up by mrs patrizia toia on the contribution of cooperatives to overcoming the crisis, and i urge the european institutions to continue to support and stimulate these social enterprises.

in writing. - report on innovation for sustainable growth: the bioeconomy for europe the report by colleague paolo bartolozzi is on innovation for sustainable growth: a bio-economy for europe. the continuing increase in the world's population, the sharp increase in demand for food and energy and the scarcity of natural resources worldwide require the union to reflect on the new approach to be taken in terms of production and consumption in order to respond to these new requirements in an effective and sustainable way. the strategy for the bioeconomy can be the solution to dependence on fossil fuels and the path to smart growth. this is a great opportunity to support rural development, to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, to make the production cycle more sustainable and to spread industrial innovation throughout the value chain. i also believe that further progress in this direction should be encouraged by creating new models of production, consumption and development and more sustainable and effective lifestyles. the link between the economy, the environment and the social is the formula for the process of growth and reindustrialisation in europe.
in writing. - this report advocates a radical change in the eu's approach to the production, consumption, processing, storage, recycling and disposal of biological resources, a concern which we share. it advocates the need for research into assessing the limits of the sustainability of bio-resources, taking into account the functions of ecosystems and natural food chains as well as the human demand for food, a concern which we also share. it stresses the importance of applying the precautionary principle in the use of biotechnology, a concern which we also share. however, the report contains major contradictions, particularly in relation to biotechnologies, when it advocates faster eu authorisation procedures for biotechnological products and much faster market access. the majority of the european parliament is aware that part of the scientific data used for authorizations comes from the biotechnology monopolies that produce them and have every interest in making a profit on their investment. the majority of the european parliament is not unaware of, but rather supports, the cuts in public laboratories in many countries, particularly in portugal, which are aimed at increasingly subordinating scientific and technological research to the interests of the big monopolies and their profit motive. sustainable growth is mentioned, but there is no possible sustainability in the concept of capitalist growth.
in writing. - over the next 40 years, europe will have to face a number of social challenges. the growing world population, the continuing growth in demand for food and energy and the scarcity of natural resources worldwide require europe to reflect on the new approach to be adopted in terms of production and consumption. only then can we provide effective and sustainable responses to these new demands. the bioeconomy offers a great opportunity to address these challenges by ensuring not only greater sustainability but also support for rural development, the potential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, greater sustainability of the production cycle and the diffusion of industrial innovation along the entire value chain. the right bioeconomy strategy can be the solution to fossil fuel dependency and the way forward towards smart growth. looking further ahead, it could also be the answer to food security, economic growth and rising employment levels. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the continuing increase in the world's population, the sharp increase in demand for food and energy and the scarcity of natural resources worldwide require europe to reflect on the new approach to be adopted in terms of production and consumption in order to respond to these new requirements in an effective and sustainable way. i voted in favour of this report which sets out measures to create new models of production, consumption and development and more sustainable and efficient lifestyles, thanks to a new synthesis between economy, environment and social quality, and points out measures which can reactivate the process of growth and reindustrialisation in europe.
in writing. − the use of biotic resources within the limits of ecosystem renewal defines the sustainability advocated in the new models of the smart bio-economy. the bioeconomy allows for the production of industrial and consumer raw materials at lower costs, using less energy and generating less environmental pollution, which in turn strengthens the competitiveness of industries and increases economic growth and employment levels. in this context, support for the sector represents an investment in the future, support that encourages the creation of a clear and stable regulatory framework capable of ensuring the harmonisation of policies that intervene in the bioeconomy sectors. in the light of the rapporteur's comments, i supported the report's call for greater progress in encouraging the development of sustainable lifestyles in order to meet the demographic and climate requirements of the new century.
in writing. the european commission has published a position paper entitled 'innovation for sustainable growth: a bio-economy for europe' which aims to leverage bio-economy activities for economic growth and job creation at european level. i would point out that the bioeconomy already employs 22 million people, representing 9% of total employment in the european union, and has great potential to employ more people. the bioeconomy offers a great opportunity to address some of the challenges facing europe, helping not only to boost economic activity but also to enhance the development of new products with greater added value for citizens. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that we need to move towards a smart, sustainable and inclusive bioeconomy in line with the europe 2020 strategy, supporting innovation and investment in new techniques and business models.
in writing. − this report advocates a radical change in the eu's approach to the production, consumption, processing, storage, recycling and disposal of biological resources a concern we share. it advocates the need for research into assessing the limits of sustainability of biotic resources, taking into account the functions of ecosystems and natural food chains, as well as the human demand for food - a concern we share. it stresses the importance of applying the precautionary principle in the use of biotechnology - a concern which we also share. however, the report contains major contradictions, particularly in relation to biotechnologies, when it advocates faster eu authorisation procedures for biotechnological products and much faster market access. the majority of the european parliament is aware that part of the scientific data used for authorizations comes from the biotechnology monopolies which produce them and have every interest in making a profit on their investment and therefore supports this concept, which we reject.
rapporteur. − mr president, as i know that hungarian citizens usually listen to these debates, i will start with some words in hungarian. az unió az emberi méltóság tiszteletben tartása, a szabadság, a demokrácia, az egyenlőség, a jogállamiság, valamint az emberi jogok – ideértve a kisebbségekhez tartozó személyek jogait – tiszteletben tartásának értékein alapul. these words are the words in article 2 of our treaty on european union. the union is founded upon the values of respect for human dignity, the rule of law, democracy, liberty, equality, fundamental rights, and the rights of people coming from minorities. these words are not a bureaucratic invention; these words are not an imposition; they are the choice of our member states. hungary, in particular, not only signed these words, hungary wrote these words with other member states. so the question for our debate here today is: do we take these words seriously or not? in the european parliament we take them very seriously, we have done work for over a year examining over 500 changes to hungarian law by the government, that touch all the cornerstones of democracy – the parliament, the media, the judiciary, the electoral law, the supreme court, the constitutional court, the data protection authority; the constitution alone was changed twelve times, then a new constitution was made, then four changes to this constitution, in one year. not only the pace and the scope of the changes were unusual, but the general trend is one towards concentration of power with the majority and the government. many international institutions, including the eu and the council of europe, have expressed their concerns about this, of course. democracy is about the rule of the majority but democracy is not majoritarianism, meaning that in a democracy you have to respect the separation of powers, the independence of the judiciary and fundamental rights. we have had a permanent dialogue with the government of hungary. we have updated the working documents that we have written with all the political groups, also with comments by the government of hungary, and this is also a dialogue that we want to continue after this report is approved. we reach a very important conclusion in this report: that the changes in hungary have been systemic, that they have a general trend and this general trend moves away from the values in article 2. this is a very serious conclusion and one that needs to be taken seriously by all institutions concerned: by us, by the european commission, which we ask to provide a rule of law mechanism and an article 2 alarm agenda to deal with this, and by the hungarian government, to whom we address 30 general recommendations for the future that of course they will follow with their own timetable objectives and in a dialogue, or let us say a trialogue, with the three institutions. we also ask for an article 2 trialogue with the european council or the council of the eu. furthermore, we acknowledge that as a political institution the european parliament should be compensated by a non-political body that we could turn to. this we call the copenhagen high-level group, in order to ensure the continuity of the copenhagen criteria. this means that we are very demanding in the requirements that we make of candidate countries, but we have to ensure that we apply the same standards to ourselves. let me make very clear what this is not about. europe is a diverse place. it has republics and monarchies, federal and unitary states, unicameral and bicameral parliaments. all this is possible, within compatibility with the values of democracy outlined in the treaties. we not only respect this diversity, we cherish this diversity; but what concerns us is whether these values are compatible, or whether these changes are compatible or not with our values. the european parliament has to be here to defend, to protect and to respect these values, because europe is not only a club of democracies; we are also a union of democracy.
mr president, mr prime minister, ladies and gentlemen, i congratulate the rapporteur, mr rui tavares, on his long and difficult work and the european commission, and in particular vice-president reding, on the clear exercise of her powers as guardian of the treaties. both underline a principle that i share: the european union is no longer just a free trade area, there are common values that result from the adoption of the european charter of fundamental rights and their integration into the treaties through the treaty of lisbon. the common values include the independence of the judiciary, the guarantee of democratic alternation, the protection of personal data, transparent regulation of electoral campaigns, respect for the dignity of persons and the protection of ethnic, linguistic, racial, sexual or any other minorities, including the homeless, and freedom of the media. i would have liked the rapporteur to have stressed more clearly that the hungarian government has backed down on several points. this is very important, not only because it acknowledges that wrong solutions have been adopted, which negates the conspiracy theory, but because it underlines how positive the intervention of the community institutions has been. we are doing well not only by pointing out problems but by helping to correct those situations. and we cannot accept two weights and two measures. when it comes to values, we must have the same approach to states, whether large or small, new or old democracies, candidates or members of the union, european or from other continents. the left in this parliament cannot consider that there are problems only in hungary and the right, which wants to reject this report, does not gain credibility to point the finger at other violations in other member states of the union. that is why, for the moment, i am giving the benefit of the doubt and will abstain in the final vote. i want to believe that the common values will be reinforced and respected. that is the only way to be a union and not just a market. only then are we citizens and not just consumers. only by protecting common values do we have moral authority.
the rapporteur. - personally, i come from a small country and from a generation that was shaken by the fall of the berlin wall. that small country lived under a dictatorship for many years. when i was moved by the fall of the berlin wall, i was also moved by the lesson that the hungarians taught us to open the border and open the border not only to themselves but to the other peoples of the rest of europe. what this lesson means for my generation and for all europeans is that we will never again abandon each other, that we will defend the fundamental rights of some as if they were the fundamental rights of all. portugal lived for forty-eight years under a dictatorship, abandoned by europe. in 1956, while i was doing research for this report, i saw that the hungarians said, "we are dying for ourselves and for europe". the hungarians knew they were fighting for all of europe. europe has failed many times in the past and we always remember the end dates: 14, 39. what we have forgotten is that europe has failed every day when its institutions have not lived up to their responsibilities, and this is what i believe the lesson of today and tomorrow's vote is the lesson we must learn. we must live up to our responsibilities to our citizens every day. let me just focus on two or three very quick points. one: there are many allegations of factual errors in the report, none of which were presented. i am glad of that, i see that these are more political than factual allegations. secondly, parliament does not want new powers with this report, it is giving the commission the task of steering this process, as it should. thirdly, it is true that parliament has imperfections. one of them could be political retaliation between groups here, another could be a gentleman's agreement ("if you don't talk about my country, i won't talk about yours"). that's why we say in the report: "we are going to have a venice commission of the european union itself. let us call it a copenhagen commission, let us move towards a time when the european union can have technical advice or technical support that is completely non-political and neutral, also to collaborate with our institutions. finally, i would like to thank the hungarian citizens who agree or disagree with this report. many have written, we have answered. the responses were absolutely excellent, even moving, of respect, of recognition and of responsibility. these are the three terms, i think, that we have to keep to. the recognition that there are problems, respect for the member state but above all responsibility for the citizens of that member state. we, who were not here before and will not be here after, have to fight for the rights of citizens as if they were our rights. as the great hungarian poet petöfi sándor said, 'without rights, there is no country'. if there are no rights, there is no home; if we build european rights, we are building our common european home.
on behalf of the green group in the european parliament what we are seeing here - we had a debate on hungary, we have another on bulgaria - is the new crisis that the european union will face in the coming days. it's a fundamental rights crisis and it has the potential to be far more devastating than the economic crisis that came before it. we know that historically. we do have problems in hungary. we have had elections in bulgaria which are very doubtful in terms of their fairness and their freedom. we got a nomination for head of the secret service from a man who is a media mogul; that appointment was reversed, but it was a dangerous appointment. and we have, above all, the young bulgarians who, like every young european, want a country free of corruption, a country with the rule of law and a country where democratic rights, democratic values and fundamental rights prevail. we cannot, in fact, be in a situation where the institutions are or declare themselves powerless in the face of such a scenario. that is why the proposals we have on the table are to set up a copenhagen commission to ensure compatibility between the legislation and the union's values in article 2, to have the commission develop what is called an 'article 2 alert agenda', that is to say a mechanism for the rule of law which in fact goes within the member states because it is within the member states that the problems are and that the citizens have their problems. it is not to determine how the member states should act, but to defend in bulgaria, in hungary, in any country, the rights of european citizens who are all the same from one end to the other.
i would like to start by congratulating the rapporteur, mrs podimata, on her work and i would say that finally, finally, after five years of crisis, we have the possibility of approving tomorrow the implementation of the financial transaction tax covering all financial products and all markets, albeit at a lower rate than the one i would support for some products. but it's the least we can do after five years of crisis. so much so that it has been taken away from those who work and retire and the financial markets and the speculative markets remain untouched, which is already beginning to be a huge insult to the citizens of europe. we have to take responsibility, we have to intervene in that direction. but i would like to say that, in addition to starting to try to correct - and i hope to do so definitively - this tendency of the european institutions to play the strong hand with the weak and the weak hand with the strong, we must also not let the exemption and the exception in relation to the pension fund pass by tomorrow. for a very simple reason, taxing pension funds as financial transactions has to do with protecting the pensions themselves, because we cannot allow pensioners' money to be gambled away in the casino. and that is what has happened, not infrequently, and therefore, contrary to what has been said, we cannot allow this exception because we are talking about speculative activity and not charitable activity.
we have long advocated a financial transaction tax. a tax which, together with other measures, will help to combat financial speculation and redirect the resources of speculative financial capital towards the fight against poverty, development and social progress. in theory, with a proposal for the creation of such a tax, we would be faced with a breakthrough. in practice, this proposal can be reduced to very little or almost nothing, or else we shall see. the restricted scope of this enhanced cooperation in terms of the number of countries, the leniency towards the most speculative financial products, the exceptions for other products, the mania of pension funds, the minimum rates now transformed into maximum rates, the absence of articulation with other essential measures such as the end of tax havens through which the large and illegal movement of capital will continue, finally, what seems to be that one wants to respond to very critical public opinions of the financial system by maintaining (interruption of the speech).
the banking sector needs to be a safe and efficient sector, as has already been said, and it needs to be a sector that serves society and not the other way around, because unfortunately in recent years we have seen that it is more society that serves the banking and financial sector than the other way around. and, having said that, we have also seen that the losses have been socialized, they have been shared by all, while the benefits have been concentrated in a very few. that is why the reform of the structure of the banking sector is absolutely urgent and necessary. i should like to say that i fully supported the proposal originally put forward by the rapporteur, i do not support the compromise reached and i give just one example of the reasons why i do not support that compromise: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the feeling i get is that we are halfway there and a reform of the banking structure requires clarity both of the activities and of the institutions. unfortunately, this is not the case, and with this decision halfway down the road, we run the risk of continuing to make decisions that are irrelevant to solving the crisis and the problems we face.

in writing. − by council decision 97/836/ec of 27 november 1997, the union acceded to the agreement of the united nations economic commission for europe (unece) concerning the adoption of uniform technical prescriptions for wheeled vehicles, equipment and parts which can be fitted to and/or be used on wheeled vehicles and the conditions for reciprocal recognition of approvals granted in accordance with these prescriptions. the participation of the union in the work of the unece helps to develop and strengthen international harmonisation of technical rules relating to vehicles, thereby contributing to facilitating international trade in motor vehicles. the aim is to simplify and speed up the procedure for the commission to vote on unece regulations on behalf of the union, thus reducing the time needed for the adoption of acts within the unece framework. council decision 97/836/ec is also adapted to the decision-making procedures for agreements provided for in the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). i therefore support this recommendation.

in writing. − at international level, the united nations economic commission for europe (unece) is developing harmonised requirements to remove technical barriers to trade in motor vehicles between the contracting parties to the revised 1958 agreement and to ensure that vehicles offer a high level of safety and environmental protection. by council decision 2000/125/ec of 31 january 2000, the union acceded to the parallel agreement within the framework of the united nations economic commission for europe. that decision should therefore be amended in order to reflect the changes introduced by the tfeu to the decision-making procedure to be followed for the definition of the position of the european union in voting on regulations to be adopted by the unece and in the conclusion of agreements between the eu and international organisations. the proposal is in line with the objectives of the common commercial policy and in accordance with article 27 tfeu. the participation of the union in the work of unece helps to develop and strengthen international harmonisation of technical rules for motor vehicles, thereby contributing to facilitating international trade in motor vehicles. i therefore support this report.

in writing. the proposal aims to define the european parliament's position on the directive coordinating the laws, regulations and administrative provisions relating to undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits). it aims to define remuneration and sanctions policies and the functions of depositaries of these assets. the european parliament's report focuses on two main issues: remuneration policy and performance rates. the remuneration policy specifies that the variable salary of fund managers shall not exceed their fixed salary and half of the variable salary shall be in assets of the funds they manage. the remuneration of fund managers should be adequately publicised. performance rates, in turn, should be linked to performance, i.e. higher pay should be linked to higher performance, but the opposite should be true for below-expected performance (lower rates). in this sense, and in agreement with the proposal in question, since it seeks to reduce the likelihood of overly risky management of the financial assets of the parties involved, i vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − in recent years, as the market has developed, several discrepancies have been detected in the way each collective investment undertaking (ucits) treats depositaries' obligations and liability, remuneration policy and sanctions policy in the financial services sector. a set of common principles and rules are now laid down to be observed, particularly in the field of prudence, rigour and sound and effective risk management, in the financial services sector. i therefore regard this review as a positive sign and as another step towards the creation of a single financial market.
in writing. the well-known madoff scandal, as well as other frauds associated with investment funds, have generated a wave of indignation and alerted to the frauds to which their investors and depositaries have often been and are associated. this proposal is intended to be the eu's response, ostensibly to improve investor confidence in open-ended investment funds by creating a new regime for depositaries, rules on remuneration for all those whose activities have a significant impact on the risk profiles of ucits and harmonisation of the sanctions regime applied by member states. in practice, this proposal is part of a set of measures decided at the level of the g20 and the g8 to try to harmonize the rules of competition in the major capitalist powers and to convince the people that it is possible to moralize financial speculation and the pursuit of maximum profit. the aim is to keep the flame of the financialization of the economy burning. efforts should be directed not at moralizing financial speculation - an impossible task - but rather at putting an end to it. the economy, that is to say, the activity aimed at satisfying human needs, has no need of financial speculation, and this constitutes a real threat to the people.
in writing. − in order to take account of the potentially harmful effect of inadequate remuneration systems on sound risk management and control of individual risk-taking strategies, management companies of undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits) should be expressly required to establish and maintain, for the categories of staff whose professional activities have a significant impact on the risk profiles of the ucits they manage, remuneration policies and practices consistent with sound and effective risk management. only in this way can we avoid situations such as those which have occurred and which have given rise to the present economic and financial crisis.
in writing. − the european parliament's report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the directive coordinating the laws, regulations and administrative provisions relating to undertakings for collective investment in transferable securities (ucits) draws attention to two key issues: remuneration policy and performance fees. the remuneration policy specifies that the variable salary of fund managers shall not exceed their fixed salary and half of the variable salary shall be in assets of the funds they manage. the remuneration of fund managers should be adequately publicised. performance rates, in turn, should be linked to performance, i.e. higher pay should be linked to higher performance, but the opposite should be true for below-expected performance (lower rates). i voted in favour of this report because i agree with these measures.
