in writing. the well-known madoff scandal and other frauds associated with investment funds have generated a wave of indignation and alerted investors and depositaries to the frauds that have often been associated with them. this proposal is intended to be the eu's response - purportedly to improve investor confidence in open-ended investment funds - by creating a new regime for depositaries, rules on remuneration for all those whose activities have a significant impact on the risk profiles of ucits and harmonisation of the sanctions regime applied by member states. this proposal is part of a set of measures decided at the level of the g20 and the g8 to try to harmonize the rules of competition in the major capitalist powers and to convince the people that it is possible to moralize financial speculation and the pursuit of maximum profit. the aim is to keep alive the flame of the financialization of the economy as the central form that capitalism has found to try to counter the inexorable downward trend of the rate of profit on capital. efforts should be directed not at moralizing financial speculation - an impossible task - but rather at putting an end to it. the economy does not need financial speculation, which is a real threat to the people.
mr president, i support the general measures for environmental protection and i am in favour of the carbon market. but in the present situation of european crisis, measures which, while aimed at the good, have harmful economic consequences must be carefully weighed. in this context, i would like to express my indignation at the fact that no exception has been made for the outermost regions, which can only be reached by air. with airfares rising, it is the principle of mobility that is compromised. the residents are already geographically distant, now they are further isolated by a political decision. but the fragile economy of the islands will also be greatly affected by the decline in tourism and the competitiveness of the fresh products we export, in an economic asphyxiation which is unfair and unacceptable. this error must be corrected, and i urge you to join me in the actions i am going to take to correct it.
in writing. − i voted in favour as it is essential that the ets is kept as the main market-based instrument to fight against climate change. i was persuaded by three important amendments: an amendment ensuring that intervention in the market is ‘a one-off’; a second amendment requiring an assessement to determine whether the measure would result in ‘carbon leakage’, i.e. businesses leaving the union to avoid the higher permit price; and a third amendment creating a fund to enhance industrial innovation and develop innovative low carbon technologies.
in writing. the european union has been at the forefront of the global fight against greenhouse gas emissions. i believe that it must persevere in this attitude and seek alternative and creative ways of strengthening its economy, without getting caught up in excessive prohibitionism which could unjustifiably affect businesses and jobs. what it must aim for is therefore a fair balance between the needs of environmental protection, economic revitalisation and job creation, supply and demand.
in writing. the report by mr matthias groote deals with the timing of greenhouse gas emission allowance auctions. the excess of co2 allowances, due to the economic slowdown and the fact that supply has been higher than demand, has led to a decline in the carbon price to levels never expected when the eu emissions trading system (eu ets) was created. this reduction in the carbon price is insufficient to drive sufficiently sustainable scientific and technological innovation and has thus become a factor in reducing incentives to invest in low-carbon technologies. i agree with this proposal, in that it aims to allow the commission to freeze or postpone part of the auctions for co2 emission allowances in order to increase the price of these allowances and to encourage the development of technologies to reduce emissions in the fight against climate change. this proposed short-term measure should not be seen as a solution to the current imbalances, but rather as an option to ensure the stability of the eu ets until the necessary adoption of long-term structural measures.
in writing. - after its rejection in april, this report has been returned to the environment committee of the european parliament and is now back for a vote in plenary. the main changes were to reintroduce temporarily withheld allowances in the eu emission trading scheme (eu ets), after up to 600 million allowances were made available out of a maximum total of 900 million in a fund based on the eu funding mechanism (ner300). we reiterate that we are facing the consequences of the operation of a perverse and ineffective mechanism - the ets/carbon market. consequences we have always warned of. the problem is fundamental, it has to do with the emissions trading system itself, with its principles and (market) foundations, and no cosmetic operation, such as the one now attempted, can solve it entirely. we advocate replacing a market approach with a normative and regulatory approach, in a framework for reducing emissions that does not depend on or feed into financial speculation. in both the 2005-2007 and 2008-2012 periods, the ets did not reduce emissions. the decreases after 2008 are mainly due to the economic and social crisis.
in writing. - i again abstained from voting on this report. i think it would be prudent to find a solution that would appeal both to industry, which is now more in need in the face of the crisis we are going through, and to environmentalists and renewable energy advocates. i think that this proposal, as it is presented, takes greater account of the second position. hence my vote.
in writing. − the emissions trading system (ets) has created the first and largest carbon market and a carbon price at eu level. in this context, implementing powers have also been delegated to the commission with regard to the timing, administration and other aspects of the auction system. currently, due to the significant impact of unexpected macroeconomic developments, the carbon price has decreased considerably. as a consequence, the combination of increased supply with reduced demand led to decreased prices in the carbon market. in the light of these exceptional circumstances, parliament is invited to adopt a commission proposal to correct these imbalances between supply and demand of licences by adopting short-term measures to ensure the stability of marketing, until the necessary adoption of long-term structural measures.
in writing. − the eu emissions trading scheme is a key instrument for reducing eu industrial emissions cost-effectively. despite seeing emissions decline since its inception, the system is currently facing serious imbalances. the current economic crisis, combined with a significant influx of external credits from the clean development mechanism (cdm) for reducing emissions, as well as a number of regulatory provisions relating to the transition to the third trading period (2013-2020) have led to a significant excess of allowances. that is why this report seeks to clarify the legal provisions on the timing of auctions for allowances and has therefore voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. - after its rejection in april, this report has been returned to the environment committee of the european parliament and is now back for a vote in plenary. the main changes were to reintroduce temporarily withheld allowances into the eu emission trading scheme (eu ets) after up to 600 million allowances were made available out of a maximum total of 900 million in a fund based on the eu funding mechanism (ner300). we reiterate that we are facing the consequences of the operation of a perverse and ineffective mechanism - the ets/carbon market. we advocate replacing a market approach with a normative and regulatory approach, in a framework for reducing emissions that does not depend on or feed into financial speculation.
in writing. - i approve this report. based on the rapid alert and response system for communicable diseases established in 1998, the commission proposal sets out measures to strengthen the european union's response capacity in preventing serious crossborder health threats and to equip it with means, networks and structures, complementary to those already available, to combat threats, by extending the risk assessment and coordination measures currently applied to communicable diseases to all health threats of biological, chemical or environmental origin, by strengthening the role of the health security committee with a view to better coordination of crisis management measures, by improving crisis management preparedness, by requiring each member state to draw up, consolidate and maintain updated national preparedness and response plans for crossborder health crises, by coordinating with the european commission and other member states and by recognising the possibility of taking joint action to combat a crisis situation, by accelerating the adoption of the necessary measures to combat the crisis and by coordinating with the european commission and the other member states the possibility of taking emergency measures to combat a crisis situation, by strengthening the role of the health security committee with a view to better coordination of current crisis management measures, by requiring each member state to draw up, consolidate and keep up to date its national plans for preparedness and response to health crises, in a coordinated manner, and by the european commission and by the other member states, the possibility of taking action necessary measures to combat a crisis.
in writing. − the european commission presented on 8 december 2011 a proposal for a decision providing the means and structures for an efficient protection of all european citizens against a wide range of cross-border health threats. the commission proposal aims to strengthen the eu's response capacity to prevent serious crossborder health threats and to provide it with means, networks and structures complementary to those available to it to combat the threats. the committee therefore advocates extending the scope of the directive to cover threats arising from the misuse of medicinal products and the placing on the market of implantable or defective medical devices. the mandate of the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) outside the field of communicable diseases should be further defined and a regular dialogue between the european commission and the european parliament should be established in order to allow the european parliament to be adequately informed about the activities and the proper functioning of the rapid alert and response system. equally important is the ongoing cooperation between the european commission and the member states. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i am satisfied with the results of mr pargneaux's report. in times of crisis, we need central coordination and, above all, we need to improve communication and collaboration between member states. the prevention of critical situations such as avian influenza or e. coli bacteria is based on transparency between member states, their immediate capacity to react, individually or in groups, and on current cooperation between pre-crisis medical and veterinary units. when we talk about serious cross-border health threats, we should not forget the correlations between poverty and population health and the social and financial problems we face. poverty is one of the main drivers of malnutrition, as well as lack of access to adequate medical services and treatment. our immune systems are essential to deal with crises and epidemics, but priority must be given to the proper implementation of the proper nutrition and care plans for babies, children and their mothers. increase access to appropriate medicines for those suffering from noncommunicable diseases and minimise the number of people affected by the epidemic. and finally, let me congratulate the rapporteur on his work on this exceptional report.
in writing. − recent public health emergencies, such as the h1n1 influenza pandemic, the volcanic ash cloud or the e. coli outbreak, have reinforced the evidence that no country can tackle a cross-border public health crisis alone. these threats do not know national or geographical borders and may affect sectors other than health, such as civil protection, energy and transport. the existing surveillance and control network in the union currently only has specific mechanisms to ensure the monitoring of communicable diseases, to give warning and to coordinate the eu response in this area, and has no competence in relation to all other serious cross-border health threats. i therefore support this proposal for a decision which aims to establish a coherent framework by strengthening and rationalising the eu's capacities and structures so as to enable the union to respond effectively to such crises. it will allow the scope of the rapid alert and response system to be extended to all serious cross-border threats. it provides for enhanced cooperation on risk planning, preparedness and assessment. it also provides for a strengthening of the union's response capacity by providing the necessary resources, networks and structures to complement those already in place.
in writing. the report by mr gilles pargneaux deals with the proposal for a european parliament and council decision on serious crossborder threats to health. the 2009 h1n1 pandemic, the 2010 volcanic ash cloud and the 2011 e. coli outbreak prompted the proposal for a decision providing the means and structures for the effective protection of all european citizens against a wide range of cross-border health threats. the commission proposal, based on the rapid alert and response system for communicable diseases established in 1998, sets out measures to strengthen the eu's response capacity to prevent serious crossborder health threats and to provide it with means, networks and structures complementary to those already in place to combat the threats. this proposal is important in that it seeks to ensure the coordination and efficiency of the response in the event of serious health threats. the importance of a coherent and coordinated crisis communication strategy is crucial in these types of situations as was evident in the e. coli/stec o104 crisis.
in writing. − the commission has put forward a proposal providing for means and structures for the effective protection of citizens across the eu against a wide range of crossborder health threats. this decision lays down the roles, duties and responsibilities of the main actors and structures at eu level, as well as the arrangements for cooperation and coordination between the various institutions. among other things, the report provides that member states may refer the threats concerned to the health security committee for a coordinated response. calls for the adoption of guidelines and other awareness-raising material on the health and hygiene measures to be followed by citizens in the event of serious cross-border health threats. these measures include information on good hygiene practices in healthcare settings, food establishments, schools and daycare centres, leisure facilities and also in the workplace, and should take into account current who recommendations. in view of the data storage involved in the cooperation and coordination processes, attention is drawn to the fact that the controllers should take appropriate measures to protect such personal data and to ensure respect for individual rights, freedoms and guarantees. we voted in favour.
in writing. − the eu's capacity to deal with serious crossborder health threats, such as those caused by the coronavirus, e. coli in 2011 and h1n1 influenza in 2009, will be strengthened by the new rules adopted here. the proposal improves the rapid alert and response system set up in 1998 and facilitates the joint procurement of vaccines by member states. the new rules introduce a common procedure for the joint procurement of medical countermeasures, in particular of vaccines against a pandemic, in order to give member states the possibility to benefit from group procurement on a voluntary basis. as regards pandemic vaccines, in the context of limited production capacities worldwide, this procedure will be carried out with the aim of enabling participating member states to have more equitable access to vaccines in order to help them better meet the vaccination needs of their citizens.

in writing. − i welcome this report, considering that the global financial crisis of 2008 has highlighted shortcomings resulting from the long-standing deregulation of financial services. the crisis quickly spread to the real economy, severely affecting growth, employment and public finances. taxpayers were called upon to help bail out failing financial institutions in order to protect the stability of the system. at the same time, it was recognised that the financial sector was under-taxed compared to other sectors of the economy due to the vat exemption and that it should contribute more significantly to the costs of the crisis. the itf is a socially fair and progressive tax and the ideal tool to enable the tax burden to be shifted from taxpayers to the financial sector, given its multiple functions. therefore, the european parliament resolution of 8 march 2011 on innovative finance at global and european level states that the eu should promote the introduction of an itf at global level; if this is not possible, the eu should, as a first step, implement a european itf.
in writing. - this report is the fourth in which parliament expresses its opinion on the financial transaction fee. since it is not yet possible to apply this rate on a global scale, it will be implemented by the enhanced cooperation method in 11 eu countries: belgium, germany, estonia, greece, spain, france, italy, austria, portugal, slovenia and slovakia. in view of the origins of the financial crisis and the damage caused by the financial sector to the european economy, the objective of this proposal is to ensure that the financial sector is taxed fairly in relation to other sectors of the economy, to discourage activities that involve too high a risk, to complement existing legislation in preventing future crises and to reduce the fragmentation of the internal market in indirect taxation, and to generate additional revenue at a time of severe financial consolidation. the european parliament proposes that the tax be applied under the issuance principle also to otc derivatives, that the ownership principle be reintroduced and that the residence principle be strengthened, so as to reduce the propensity for tax evasion. the legislation should be applied as uniformly as possible in order to minimise the likelihood of escape. my vote is in favour.
in writing. - mrs podimata presents a text on the proposal for a council directive implementing enhanced cooperation in the field of financial transaction tax. the crisis, which, as we all know, was caused by the speculative behaviour of some banks, calls for maximising all the revenue that can be channelled into the investment so necessary for economic growth and job creation. one of the ways we can get more resources is by introducing a tax on all financial transactions, but in such a way that there is no evasion or loopholes. despite some divergent views, i believe that this is a good and positive agreement which should be applied in equal circumstances to all markets. however, the application of this tax cannot be passed on to citizens but to banking institutions, taxing speculative transactions and providing greater stability to the financial sector. i welcome the agreement reached, although i regret that it was not possible to reach an agreement at 28 or at least in the whole euro zone. because the interest of the european citizen must come first, i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive and i hope that it will come into force on 1 january 2014.
in writing. - in theory, this cooperation would be a step forward in the implementation of a financial transaction tax, which we have long advocated. in practice, everything can be settled for very little or almost nothing. of course, because we are dealing with enhanced cooperation by 11 countries, leaving out all the others, who do not accept even the slightest of the advances made by this proposal. secondly, because the amount of the tax will be fixed by each country, so it is not difficult to predict that there will be a race to see who sets the lowest. and because the large illegal traffic will continue through the offshore - the sites of economic crime that the eu keeps untouched. it's just a way of responding to public opinion and criticism of the financial system, without actually touching the financial system. in europe, almost €5 billion of public aid has been used to rescue the banking and financial system over the past three years. the only reference to the use of the amounts that would be generated points to the proportional decrease in member states' contributions to the eu budget! the real cost of the crisis is paid by the workers and the people, by small businesses and the real economy of countries like portugal.
in writing. − the enhanced cooperation procedure allows a group of at least nine member states to move forward with an initiative proposed by the commission, as soon as it is found impossible to reach a unanimous position within a reasonable period. it applies only to policy areas requiring unanimity and is intended to overcome the situation where certain countries are prevented from moving forward with a common approach due to the reluctance and lack of agreement of others. the proposal approves the opinion on the specific elements of the financial transaction tax (ftt) to be applied by 11 member states, including portugal. the introduction of a tax covering a wide range of financial instruments is advocated, with rates of 0.1% on shares and bonds and 0.01% on derivatives.

in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that latvia has made considerable economic progress in the last decades since its transition to a market economy. economic reforms have been key to this progress, increasing competitiveness and facilitating its integration into the eu economy, but also into the wider world economy. the successive governments in latvia have also been exceptionally strict in their approach to structural reforms. the latest reforms implemented in 2009-2010 saw considerable wage cuts and tax increases during the crisis. these austerity measures were very successful and paved the way for latvia to emerge from the crisis. despite the high short-term costs, latvia has managed to implement credible policies that put the country back on a stable growth path. as a result of massive capital injections that continued to largely finance the large expansion of the construction and consumer sectors, the current account deficit reached an all-time low of -22,5% of gdp in 2006. it was radically corrected in the severe crisis of 2009-2010, resulting in a surplus of 8,6% in 2009. since then, the current account has been stabilised at a slightly deficit level of -1,7% in 2012 and is expected to remain stable.

in writing. − the european union bases its functioning on principles and values that uphold the rule of law and respect for human rights. the new hungarian government, led by viktor orbán and supported by a parliamentary majority, has adopted constitutional rules that are contrary to eu values, notably the necessary independence of judges from political power - contrary to european legislation -, the lack of protection of minorities or the lack of freedom of the press. not to mention an election law tailor-made for the ruling party. the judgment of the court of justice of the european union itself was not taken into account. these violations of fundamental freedoms and the rule of law prompted an analysis of the political situation in hungary by the parliamentary assembly of the council of europe on 13 june. the european commission, in its capacity as guardian of the treaties, has identified four incompatibilities with european legislation, although hungary has committed itself to bringing its constitution into line with european legislation. because it is necessary to show hungary that it cannot continue to violate eu principles and values, i voted in favour of the report by mr rui tavares on the situation of fundamental rights: standards and practices in hungary.
in writing. - this report addresses extremely worrying political developments in hungary. it ignores others of equal gravity, such as the attempt to outlaw the hungarian communist workers' party by prohibiting the use of words such as communism, socialism and liberation. in hungary there is a continuing degradation of the political, labour and social rights of workers and the people. unemployment and emigration are skyrocketing. the poverty wages and pensions, poverty, high prices, the gradual destruction of public services, the attack on workers' freedom of association and organisation are other factors which help to make up a very worrying picture. the concern about this reality is justified. but we do not support the attempt to whitewash the eu's own responsibilities in this situation, which, moreover, has parallels in some (and only some) of the factors described with what is happening in other countries. nor do we accept that this eu, which has a heavy responsibility for the deterioration of the political, economic and social situation in many member states, such as portugal, should now be seen as the good cop, the defender of democracy and human rights, for whose deterioration it has been responsible.
in writing. - the hungarian situation is very delicate and cannot be analysed on an ideological basis. i think the rapporteur has forgotten this aspect in this report, which is supported by the left represented in the ep and rejected by the political groups on the right. when the vote is split, as is the case, something was not taken into account in the discussions before the reports were adopted. the vote in committee was already very divided, which already indicated a great deal of controversy, both on the subject and on the content of this report. although there may be some positions of the hungarian government with which i do not agree, i consider that the amendment of a constitution inherited from a communist regime is the prerogative of that government alone. i do not see, as the rapporteur does, any matter which is so reprehensible that it would lead to the application of article 7 of the european treaty.
in writing. − the european commission and the european parliament recognise that the european union is not just a free trade area, there are common values which result from the adoption of the european charter of fundamental rights and its incorporation into the treaties through the treaty of lisbon. the common values include the independence of the judiciary, the guarantee of democratic alternation, the protection of personal data, transparent regulation of electoral campaigns, respect for the dignity of persons and the protection of ethnic, linguistic, racial, sexual or any other minorities, including the homeless, and freedom of the media. some of these aspects are not yet being fully respected in hungary, despite the positive response to the european commission's calls, which is why i decided to abstain in the vote on this report.
in writing. - while recognising that some situations raise concerns and perplexities from the point of view of respect for the values on which the eu is founded, the truth is that the hungarian authorities have been following the commission's observations and recommendations, a fact which, being of enormous importance, is virtually omitted in this report. i therefore voted against this resolution because i consider that the report does not provide a complete and accurate analysis of the situation in hungary and its complexity.
in writing. − a member state must respect the basic principles of the rule of law and the separation of powers. the european union should not point to and demand the application of democratic principles and the rule of law from external partners when there are internal doubts about their actual application. the hungarian government is accused of violating the impartiality of the judicial system, obscuring the electoral law, abusing the power to pass laws and attempting to control the different national hierarchies. in addition to these complaints, the hungarian government has backed down on some measures following a recommendation from the european commission. for these reasons, i abstain on this report, pending the settlement of these points between hungary and the european institutions.
in writing. - this report uses real and extremely worrying political developments in hungary to openly promote interference in the internal affairs of that country and thus create the conditions for the implementation of the same policy using, however, different means. it aims to take advantage of the current situation in the country to try to legitimize and impose its power and the power of the eu treaties - the same ones that are invoked to impose the regression in labour and social rights, especially in portugal. it is not the purpose of this report on fundamental rights to counteract the degradation of the political, labour and social rights of hungarian workers and people, the increasing unemployment and emigration, poverty wages and pensions, poverty, high prices, the gradual destruction of public services, the attack on workers' freedom of association and organisation. nor was it to denounce the attempt to outlaw the hungarian communist workers' party by prohibiting the use of words such as communism, socialism and liberation, which is an act of the utmost gravity. the imposition of political programmes in the light of eu principles is also a form of ideological control and domination and interference which we do not support.
in writing. − i welcome this report, starting by stressing that member states should implement flood prevention programmes through comprehensive and preventive strategies, stressing that emergency policy, including prevention and response to emergencies, requires closer involvement of regions, cities and local communities, which should be encouraged to include emergency policy in their strategies. stresses furthermore that investments in flood prevention under the relevant programmes require adequate financial resources, as this is an important instrument enabling member state governments to develop and implement flood prevention policies; and stressed that investments in support of disaster prevention should follow an ecosystem-based approach.

in writing. - some central european countries (hungary, austria, slovakia and germany) were hit by a weather catastrophe at the beginning of june, triggered by unprecedented rainfall, which killed more than 100 people, injured hundreds and affected thousands more. this tragedy, similar to the one that occurred in 2012, has shown some improvements in the way it has been dealt with, although some intolerable problems remain, such as the delay in the payment of grants awarded under the structural funds that take time to reach the rightful owners. the recurrence of these floods draws our attention to the whole problem of climate change and calls for preventive and mitigating measures. it is at such times that solidarity from member states is needed, especially as it is the most vulnerable communities that are most affected. i voted in favour of this joint motion for a resolution and i urge the european authorities to make available the funds available as soon as possible so that the affected regions can quickly recover the damage caused so as to normalise all their economic and social activity.
in writing. − floods in some european countries have caused serious damage in several regions, affecting infrastructure, businesses, agriculture and rural areas. they have destroyed elements of the natural and cultural heritage, causing deaths and injuries and forcing thousands of people to flee their homes. the people affected deserve our full solidarity. this solidarity must be translated into practical action by mobilizing the resources needed to deal with the damage and to repair the affected areas as quickly as possible. that is why we supported this resolution. it is almost three years since this parliament adopted a report on the prevention of natural and man-made disasters. this report defined a set of actions to be prioritised for eu support to member states to correct risk-inducing situations, in areas such as the recovery and protection of watersheds, the protection/remodelling of inhabited areas particularly vulnerable to certain types of disasters, among others. the report also called for, among other things, a review of the solidarity fund, making it more rapidly mobilisable. three years later, disasters are coming and going and the commission has done almost nothing to implement parliament's recommendations. it's time to act!
in writing. − there has recently been a major natural disaster in the form of floods in many european countries, notably austria, the czech republic, germany, hungary, poland, slovakia, france and spain, which have caused severe damage to cities, towns and municipalities, as well as to infrastructure, businesses, agriculture, rural areas, and which have destroyed elements of the natural and cultural heritage, causing deaths and injuries and forcing thousands of people to leave their homes. we must therefore pool all the efforts and all the available mechanisms to deal with this catastrophe and try in some way to minimise the suffering of the affected populations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on floods in europe, which sets out measures to prevent these disasters, and in which i stress the call on the commission and the member states to pay particular attention to the planning and review of policies on sustainable land use, ecosystem absorption capacities and best practices, and to the enhancement of the capacity of flood control and drainage systems in order to prevent the severe floods that occur throughout the union.
in writing. − the soils of central europe, before the may-july rains, already exceptionally saturated and with record humidity levels due to precipitation caused by cyclone christoffer, did not absorb the rainwater derived, leading to a flood scenario that caused serious damage to cities, towns and municipalities in europe. the catastrophe caused deaths and injuries, forced people to leave their homes and destroyed elements of the natural and cultural heritage. in this context, the commission considers it urgent to strengthen the capacity to prevent natural disasters, urging member states to pay particular attention to planning and reviewing spatial planning policies in order to make them more sustainable. it is therefore important to ensure the financing of prevention tools and the proper use of the european union solidarity fund in aid to the affected countries.
in writing. - i am in favour of this motion for a resolution because i consider it crucial to reduce the complexity of the procedures for applicants and the institutional delays for the activation of the european union solidarity fund. in addition, the criteria for designating a regional disaster need to be clarified to avoid rejection requests, which already amount to 66% of the total. the natural disasters that have shaken europe have gone from extraordinary to commonplace. it is therefore necessary to move forward now with the amendment to the european union solidarity fund, which has been blocked in the council since 2005. 62% of the applications received by the commission since 2002 relate to regional disasters, of which only 23% were accepted and the remainder rejected. it is these percentages that show us that quantitative criteria must be applied to the acceptance of applications. the thresholds for regional disasters should also be relaxed, since they are no longer an exception but a frequent reality. we must act now on behalf of the european citizens.
in writing. − floods in some european countries have caused serious damage to towns, cities and villages. it is urgently necessary to undertake the reconstruction of areas destroyed or damaged by disasters in order to repair the related economic, social and environmental losses and impacts. the resolution welcomes the tireless efforts of member states' civil protection and security units, rescue teams and volunteers to save lives and minimise damage in the affected areas and states that emergency policy, including prevention and response to emergencies, requires closer involvement of regions, cities and local communities, which should be encouraged to include emergency policy in their strategies. the council and the commission are called upon to take all necessary measures to ensure the rapid and adequate provision of financial assistance from the european union solidarity fund and to alert the public to the urgency of the release of this financial assistance to the countries affected by this natural disaster. we're obviously in agreement.
in writing. − i approve this report, taking into account that the gpan report concluded that excessive risk-taking, excessive debt ratios, inadequate capital and liquidity requirements and the excessive complexity of the banking system in general caused the financial crisis. while the regulatory reforms address these weaknesses, the group concluded that further structural reforms are needed, including the legal separation of certain risk finance activities from banks that accept deposits within a banking group. the purpose of the separation is to make the most socially critical parties safer and less tied to high-risk business activities, and to limit the ransom paid by taxpayers. i agree with this report as it sets out several core principles, including reducing complexity, enhancing competition, limiting the interlinking of risk and trading activities, improving corporate governance, creating a responsible remuneration system, promoting effective bank resolution and recovery, strengthening banks' capital and making credit available to the real economy, which are key to bringing about a change in the banking culture.
in writing. − the study carried out by the high level expert group set up by the european commission in 2012 concluded that the causes of the financial crisis are deeply linked to excessive risk-taking, very high debt ratios, inadequate capital and liquidity requirements and excessive complexity of the banking system. the study thus concludes that legal separation of banks' risk-taking financial activities is essential to ensure the protection of the most socially critical activities, limit losses imposed on taxpayers and make banking structures simpler, transparent and easily recoverable. this report is the ep's main contribution to this subject. it sets out several core principles, including reducing complexity, enhancing competition, limiting the interlinking of risk and commercial activities, improving corporate governance, creating a responsible remuneration system, promoting effective bank resolution and recovery, strengthening banks' capital and making credit available to the real economy, which are key to bringing about a change in the banking culture. i am voting in favour of this report and look forward to the commission's proposals on this subject in the autumn.
in writing. - since the start of the crisis, more than €1.6 billion of state aid (12.8% of eu gdp) has been granted to the banking sector, leading to a sharp increase in member states' public debt. since then, the european union has been strengthening the acquis in terms of prudential banking and financial supervision rules and in october 2012 a high level expert group produced a report on a possible structural reform of the eu banking sector. the report analyses the current business models followed by european financial institutions and looks at possible ways of making them less volatile and less prone to risk. i therefore agree with the decision taken today to ask the european commission to look at this report in more detail and to consider the need for further reform of this specific sector.
in writing. − in 2012, the european commission set up a high-level group to assess structural reform of the banking sector, which concluded that the causes of the financial crisis lie in several pillars: toxic financial products, excessive debt, lack of liquidity and complexity of the banking system that made supervision difficult. in order to avoid similar situations in the future, we must create a sound banking system based on strong structures, which guarantees consumer protection. the separation between financial activities considered to be speculative or risky and current operations is essential in order to protect small savers. we need to strengthen the banking system by having simpler, more transparent and more recoverable banking institutions. structural measures such as increased bank capitalisation, improved supervision and increased liquidity are needed. only then will we be better able to protect citizens and taxpayers. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague arlene mccarthy on structural reform of the eu banking sector because it introduces measures that reduce complexity, strengthen competition, limit systemic risk, improve corporate governance and make credit available to small and mediumsized enterprises, the backbone of the european economy.
in writing. − the structural reform that the banking sector needs is one that leads to the recovery of its primary function of supporting economic activity and its objective of meeting the development needs of the people. this can only be achieved by regaining political control of the development process, by subordinating economic power to democratic political power, and by putting the need for a dominant and dynamic public financial sector on the agenda. the role of the public financial sector needs to be strengthened (through renationalisation or direct negotiation) in order to promote economic development, support productive and job-creating investment, support micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, the cooperative and social sector and households. this requires the rejection of the process of concentration and centralisation of the sector, with the promotion of bankruptcies, mergers and acquisitions, via the so-called banking union and its control by the ecb and the financial capital structures. and it is necessary to change the statutes, the guidelines and the false autonomy of the ecb, ensuring the equal presence of the states in its management, in order to ensure effective political control by the member states, control by each country of its national central bank and monetary policy.
in writing. − in february 2012, the high level expert group (hleg) was established to address the question of whether further reforms to the structure of the eu banking sector would reduce the likelihood and impact of bank defaults and ensure the continuation of critical economic functions in the event of a default, in order to better protect retail customers. this report aims to define core principles, including reducing complexity, enhancing competition, limiting the interlinkage of risk and trading activities, improving corporate governance, creating a responsible remuneration system, promoting effective bank resolution and recovery, strengthening banks' capital and making credit available to the real economy, which are key to bringing about a change in the banking culture. i believe it is essential that the reform of the eu banking structure provides a safe, stable and efficient banking system that responds to the needs of the real economy, customers and consumers and supports the provision of credit to the economy, in particular to smes and start-ups.

in writing. − the report of the committee on budgetary control assesses the progress made since the implementation of the action plan for an integrated internal control framework, which started in 2006. the aim of the implementation of this roadmap was to fulfil the european commission's commitment to reach a positive statement of assurance (pda). the rapporteur therefore regrets that the commission's commitment to reach a full positive statement of assurance has not been met and points out in particular that in its report on the statement of assurance for the financial year 2011, the court of auditors concluded that payments were affected by material errors, although it also considered that the supervisory and control systems were, in general, partially efficient. there is a fundamental discrepancy between the court of auditors, which believes that errors can be avoided, and the commission, which relies on subsequent financial corrections and the recovery of funds. the rapporteur therefore urges the member states to strengthen the monitoring of programme implementation at grassroots level. i voted in favour of the report.

the rapporteur. - madam president, commissioner, minister, ladies and gentlemen, the draft legislative resolution which we are debating today and voting on tomorrow seeks to make available macrofinancial assistance from the european union to the republic of georgia in the amount of eur 46 million and is the result of long negotiations with the council and the commission, which have only just been concluded at the conciliation stage. it should be stressed that the point of disagreement between parliament and the council on this point has never been a matter of substance and whether or not this country fulfils the conditions to deserve such assistance. parliament has supported the granting of assistance to georgia from the outset. the question has always been whether, in the light of the new rules resulting from the treaty of lisbon and the 2011 comitology regulation for the approval of the memoranda of understanding on macro-financial assistance, the advisory procedure, as advocated by parliament, or the examination procedure, as advocated by the council, should be adopted as a general rule. two interrelated political issues were at stake in this process. one of a procedural nature, but no less essential for this parliament, is to know what mechanism to adopt and what degree of control the member states must have over the commission's implementing acts in these agreements in the light of the regime arising from the treaty and the comitology regulation. the second political question is to what extent the powers of control of the member states in the council should extend to the commission's executive powers, diminishing its executive autonomy, given that parliament has no power of control over the commission. this process in georgia provides answers to these questions and safeguards the positions of principle which parliament has always taken. but it also provides answers not only to this case of georgia but also to all the pending cases, such as kyrgyzstan and jordan, and to future cases of macrofinancial assistance from the union to third countries. in fact, in parallel with the present case of georgia, a framework regulation for macrofinancial assistance in general was being negotiated, with our colleague metin kazac as rapporteur. however, on 8 may this year the commission informed parliament that it had withdrawn the proposal for a framework regulation because it did not agree with the codecision between parliament and the council for the case-by-case allocation of macrofinancial assistance. the commission intended to grant this by means of an executive act. the withdrawal of the commission proposal on the eve of what was expected to be the last of the trilogue brought the framework regulation to an end. however, in an exemplary process of collaboration and creativity, parliament and the council concluded a virtual regulation between them and transformed the agreement thus reached into a joint declaration to be attached to the decision on assistance to georgia and to be applied henceforth to all other pending and future cases of macrofinancial assistance from the union. the political agreement, the political compromise, has thus been given a formal expression. the joint declaration adopted by parliament and the council, together with the decision on georgia, which the commission has already declared that it accepts, sets out three important points which have always been defended by the european parliament: the commission has also taken note of the fact that the council has adopted a decision on the establishment of a european monitoring centre for drugs and drug addiction (emcdda) in the framework of the european union's action plan on drugs and drug addiction. in conclusion, this has been a complex and time-consuming process, and i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr metin kazac, the irish presidency of the council for its flexibility and also the vice-president of this parliament, mr alejo vidal-quadras, who was the chairman of the conciliation committee of this parliament.

in writing. - cybercrime is a problem that we need to tackle with the utmost urgency. i welcome the inclusion of a new aggravating factor for offences committed through the misuse of personal data, as this is one of the most common forms of cyberattack today. this report is important for the defence of the interests of the european union and its citizens.
in writing. − information systems have become an essential element for political, social and economic interaction in the union, and it is therefore necessary to ensure the proper functioning and security of these systems in the union, within an effective and comprehensive framework of measures to prevent and combat cybercrime. recent attacks in europe have brought attention to the various emerging threats, in particular the occurrence of simultaneous massive attacks against information systems and the increased use of so-called botnets for criminal purposes. this directive should therefore replace the 2005 framework decision by establishing common minimum rules on the definition of criminal offences and sanctions in this area (covering the various consecutive stages of the criminal offence), such as unlawful access to information systems, unlawful interference with the system or data and unlawful interception of communications. it should also allow for enhanced cooperation between national authorities and relevant community agencies, such as eurojust, europol and the european cybercrime centre and enisa. it is imperative that the 12 member states that have not yet ratified the convention on cybercrime, which provides a coherent legal framework covering the various aspects of crime, do so as soon as possible.
