in writing. − in recent years, our dependence on information systems has increased exponentially, making us increasingly vulnerable to cyberattacks, which are particularly serious when they target institutional systems and businesses. recent attacks have exposed the vulnerability of institutions and networks that we would have considered to be properly protected, revealing the need for strategies that ensure cybersecurity. the use of all these technologies, which are becoming increasingly essential for institutions, businesses and citizens, depends to a large extent on the implementation of a clear strategy to ensure that these information infrastructures are secure.
in writing. - the increasing use of information systems has given rise to increased concern among citizens, who are only now beginning to realise the real extent of the problem. many of us who use the internet every day are not aware of how our data, many of it personal, is flowing along the information highways. cases like julian assange (wikileaks) and snowden show how even information considered secret or confidential can eventually be leaked. the espionage continues and in more pronounced ways than we can imagine, and often by those we consider friends. the confidence of citizens is seriously shaken and it is urgent that the authorities responsible take measures to protect personal data. i voted in favour of the report by mrs monika hohlmeier on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on attacks against information systems and repealing council framework decision 2005/222/jha, because we need a set of minimum criminal rules which, by punishing these violations, prevent these attacks. because it is an international crime, it is necessary for member states to strengthen their cooperation with interpol.
in writing. - in addition to the aspects of harmonisation, the application of identical regimes to often different legal realities and cultures, the imposition of mandatory criminal sanctions and the disconnection of democratic participation in the definition of legislation and its implementation, this directive reflects a purely criminalising view of this phenomenon. the way forward could have been different, by relying on preventive policies in the member states instead of repressive methods. instead, this legislation fails to protect the ordinary user and facilitates its criminalisation, as there is a wide variety of imprecise definitions that can risk extending the scope of application to ordinary users. secondly, it does not advocate the responsibility of the producers and operators of large it systems, who should be obliged to take measures to protect the reliability of the systems and to ensure the protection of the rights and guarantees of the users.
in writing. − this proposal aims to replace council framework decision 2005/222/jha of 24 february 2005 on attacks against information systems. this framework decision aimed to strengthen cooperation between judicial and other competent authorities, including police authorities and other specialised law enforcement services in the member states, by approximating their criminal law provisions on attacks against information systems, introducing eu legislation to crack down on offences such as unlawful access to information systems, unlawful interference with the system and unlawful interference with data, as well as specific provisions on the liability of legal persons, jurisdiction and exchange of information.
in writing. - agreeing with the need for better exchange of information related to cybersecurity between member states in the context of growing concerns about potential attacks against information systems, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the proper functioning and security of information systems in the union are vital for the development of the internal market and of a competitive and innovative economy and an adequate level of protection of these systems should therefore be ensured. on 24 february 2005, eu member states reached agreement on this matter and council framework decision 2005/222/jha was adopted. on 14 july 2008, the commission published a report on the application of that framework decision, noting that new threats had emerged since its adoption and that they needed to be addressed. in particular, the emergence of simultaneous large-scale attacks against information systems and the increased criminal use of so-called botnets should be addressed in an appropriate and effective manner. taking into account the need to address these and other gaps, the commission has moved forward with this proposal for a directive, which replaces framework decision 2005/222/jha, introducing cyber-attack adjustments in order to subject attacks against information systems in all member states to effective, proportionate and dissuasive criminal sanctions and to improve and encourage cooperation between judicial and other competent authorities in this field. i voted in favour.
in writing. − the protection of public and private information systems is becoming increasingly difficult to ensure, as there is a trend towards an increase in the number of cyberattacks, with increasingly sophisticated and complex methods. the proposal for a directive aims to introduce criminal sanctions for the so-called botnet attack. in addition to the imposition of criminal penalties, this directive also establishes a more preventive approach. i am in favour of this report because i believe it is essential that european legislation evolves in line with society.
in writing. - in addition to the aspects of harmonisation, the application of identical regimes to often different legal realities and cultures, the imposition of mandatory criminal sanctions and the disconnection of democratic participation in the definition of legislation and its implementation, this directive reflects a purely criminalising view of this phenomenon. the way forward could have been different, by relying on preventive policies in the member states instead of repressive methods. instead, this legislation fails to protect the ordinary user and facilitates its criminalisation, as there is a wide variety of imprecise definitions that can risk extending the scope of application to ordinary users. secondly, it does not advocate the responsibility of the producers and operators of large it systems, who should be obliged to take measures to protect the reliability of the systems and to ensure the protection of the rights and guarantees of the users.
in writing. − i approve this report, considering that data protection reform is underway at eu level through the revision of directive 95/46/ec and its replacement by the proposed general data protection regulation and data protection directive on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data by the competent authorities for the purposes of the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties, and the free movement of such data. however, i express serious concerns, while reiterating my continued support for transatlantic efforts to combat terrorism and organised crime, with regard to prism and other similar programmes, as, if the information currently available is confirmed, it may involve a serious breach of the fundamental right to privacy and data protection of eu citizens and residents, as well as the right to private and family life, confidentiality of communications, the presumption of innocence, freedom of expression, freedom of information and freedom of enterprise.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution on alleged spying by us authorities on the offices of eu institutions and on the emails and phone calls of officials. this kind of practice is completely unacceptable and, if confirmed, could seriously damage good transatlantic relations.
in writing. − in the field of the fight against terrorism and the prevention of organised crime, international judicial cooperation and transatlantic cooperation are essential, which in many cases involves the transfer of personal data, which should be carried out in accordance with the applicable legal rules. however, recent news reports have highlighted possible violations of the fundamental right to privacy and data protection of eu citizens and residents, as well as the right to private and family life, confidentiality of communications, presumption of innocence, freedom of expression, freedom of information and freedom to conduct a business by nsa surveillance programs. these allegations, because of their fundamental importance, must be fully investigated and explained by the us authorities.
in writing. the joint motion for a resolution which we have just voted on, tabled pursuant to rule 110 (4), replacing the proposals from the epp, s&d and alde political groups, concerns the surveillance programme of the united states national security agency, the surveillance bodies in several member states and their impact on the privacy of citizens of the european union. many internet users are not aware of how their data, many of it personal, is flowing along the information highways. the espionage continues and in more pronounced ways than we can imagine and often by those we consider friends. cases such as julian assange (wikileaks) and snowden show the extent to which information considered secret or confidential can eventually be disclosed and give this matter relevance. citizens are very concerned about the lack of protection of their private sphere. i voted in favour of this resolution because it draws attention to the international security - or lack thereof - of internet networks, since the fight against terrorism cannot be used as an excuse for citizens' breaches of their right to privacy.
in writing. the european parliament has been forced to take a stand on the report by the european parliament on the european union's relations with the countries of central and eastern europe. the european union has been accused of spying by the us authorities. its true meaning will only be known in the times to come. for now, inflammatory statements of indignation aside, the servility shown by the authorities of france, italy, spain and portugal in the case of the plane of bolivian president evo morales is illustrative of the posture of subservience to the us that continues to prevail on this side of the atlantic. will there be a serious follow-up to the calls for a suspension of the passenger name record (pnr) and terrorist financing tracking programme (tftp) agreements? are these positions to be seriously considered when, at the same time, the same majority expresses its support for the transatlantic efforts to combat terrorism and organised crime, that is, an almost unconditional support for the set of legal and political tools that fuel the spying, the arrest, the transport, the torture and the death of millions? many questions remain...
in writing. the eu has always supported transatlantic efforts to combat terrorism and organised crime. the controversy over prism and other similar programmes has again called into question the means of fighting this fight. although, if the information currently available is confirmed, these means may be a serious violation of the fundamental right to privacy and data protection of eu citizens and residents, as well as the right to private and family life, confidentiality of communications, the presumption of innocence, freedom of expression, freedom of information and freedom of enterprise, i believe that the fight against terrorism and the prevention of new and serious attacks must always be in the first place.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this joint motion for a resolution on the surveillance programme of the us national security agency, surveillance bodies in various member states and their impact on eu citizens' privacy, in which the european parliament mandates its committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs to conduct an in-depth inquiry into the matter, in collaboration with national parliaments and the eu-us expert group, and to report the results by the end of the year by: (a) collecting all relevant information and evidence from eu and us sources (finding facts); (b) investigating the alleged surveillance activities of us authorities as well as those carried out by certain member states (identifying liability); and (c) assessing the impact of surveillance programmes on the fundamental rights of eu citizens.
in writing. − this report instructs the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs to draw up a study on the impact on the privacy of european union citizens of the surveillance programmes of the us national security agency and the intelligence services of several member states. the results are to be communicated by the end of the year and will be achieved in collaboration with national parliaments and the eu-us expert group. taking into account article 7 of the tfeu, which provides for the right of citizens to respect for their private and family life, their home and their communications, and also taking into account article 27 of the vienna convention on diplomatic relations, which obliges the accredited state to allow and protect the free communication of the diplomatic mission of the accredited state, parliament, while reiterating its support for transatlantic efforts to combat terrorism and organised crime, expresses serious concern at the recent revelations about these surveillance programmes, which, if confirmed, could imply a breach by member states of the fundamental right of eu citizens to privacy and data protection, as well as a breach by the united states of the convention.
in writing. - the revelations by edward snowden constitute a situation of extreme gravity. we now know that, in addition to the millions of european citizens who are spied on and whose data is transferred to the united states under the pretext of the fight against terrorism, the european institutions (commission, council and parliament) are also the target of espionage by that friendly country. the council and the commission have so far been timid and lax in their requests for explanations. i abstained on the joint resolution because, although it condemns the large-scale espionage to which europeans are being subjected, there was no courage to do the only thing that was necessary: to suspend immediately the negotiations on the transatlantic free trade agreement until the situation was clarified and the dismantling of the espionage network was guaranteed. europe, once again, is kneeling before the united states.
in writing. the european parliament has called for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to play a full part in the fight against terrorism. the security which the states must guarantee to their citizens must be accompanied by the protection of the fundamental rights of the citizens. such surveillance should be carried out by a limited number of competent authorities and data collection should only be carried out in the event of very serious suspicions. for these reasons, i think it is important that an inquiry into this issue be launched in the libe committee, in collaboration with the national parliaments and the us and eu expert group. finally, i would stress that it is essential that the free trade agreement between the united states and the european union guarantees the protection of the data of european and american citizens.
in writing. the european parliament has called for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to play a full role in the fight against terrorism. will the arrests or even condemnations voiced by the majority of the ep in relation to the allegation of espionage by the american authorities be followed up seriously? will there be any serious follow-up to the demands for the eventual suspension of the agreements on passenger identification registers (pnr) and the terrorist financing tracing programme (tftp), or for data protection not to be compromised in the context of the negotiations on the free trade agreement with the usa? are these positions to be seriously considered when, at the same time, the same majority expresses its support for the transatlantic efforts to combat terrorism and organised crime, that is, almost unconditional support for the set of legal and political tools that fuel the spying, arrest, transport, torture and death of millions of people in countries determined by us, nato and eu interests? the doubts remain but the record of whitewashing and acquiescence of the majority of the ep to us actions on this and other issues did not indicate a serious follow-up.
in writing. − i approve this report, starting by asking european political parties to nominate their candidates for the presidency of the commission sufficiently in advance of the date of the elections, so that they can prepare an effective campaign at european level and focused on the european issues included in the party platform as well as in the programme of their candidates for the presidency of the commission. i also recommend that member states take all necessary steps to ensure that the agreed measures are effectively implemented in order to support citizens who wish to vote or stand for election in states other than their own. finally, and in view of the high abstention rate in the previous european elections and the period of political and economic crisis in the european union, i urge the member states to organise a public campaign to encourage citizens to take part in the elections in order to fight against the fall in the turnout.
in writing. - i would like to thank the rapporteur and all the colleagues who have contributed to the final outcome of this report. i welcome the closer link between national sovereignty and european sovereignty, between national parliaments and the european parliament, because these elections allow europeans to express their sovereignty by indicating their membership of europe. i would like to highlight the possibility of nominating a candidate for president of the commission who, although not on the ballot, contributes to increasing the european debate and the sense of european integration.
in writing. − next year will see the first elections since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which has strengthened the democratic legitimacy of the eu decision-making process, giving more powers to the ep and consolidating its role as co-legislator, and at the same time has sought to bring the citizens of the union closer together, notably through the introduction of the citizens' initiative. increasing transparency and deepening debate across the eu is essential to encourage and facilitate citizen participation in the 2014 european elections. according to eurobarometer data, more than 80% of european citizens say they would be more motivated to vote if they were given more information about the programmes and objectives of candidates and parties, the impact of the eu on their lives and the elections themselves. i support the recommendations that candidates for the ep and candidates for the presidency of the commission should be appointed sufficiently in advance to enable them to prepare a vigorous and effective campaign, which includes a european dimension in politics. it is necessary to increase citizens' awareness by keeping them informed before and during the election campaign, in particular through information campaigns, the use of airtime and the organisation of public debates, giving citizens the opportunity to make their voices and concerns heard.
in writing. − the low turnout at the european elections suggests that ways of improving the organisation of the elections and of promoting greater popular interest and participation in the elections should be assessed and decided upon. without the cooperation of all the political actors this improvement will not be possible. among these, the crucial role of political parties is growing, which should try to resist the temptation to make the european elections another opportunity to discuss essentially national politics and focus on the undeniable reality that european politics today does not just exist as it should be understood, its importance and a perspective of full participation in its conduct. i hope that the next elections will be a reversal of the negative trend we have seen and that the european elections will be a moment par excellence for the affirmation of a european public and political space in which everyone is invited and called upon to participate.
in writing. - next year, another election will take place to elect the new european parliament. as we know, the european elections are the ones which motivate citizens the least, and therefore have the lowest turnout. this fact leads eurosceptics to claim that this experiment in transnational democracy is a failure. as 2014 marks the start of a new cycle with a new multiannual financial framework, we must work to ensure that the elections are not seen as a failure. to reverse this situation, parties must be deeply involved in campaigns to clarify their electoral programmes. we must fight for our ideas for the development of the european union (eu) and explain the commission's options for what the eu should do. the aim is to bring the eu closer to citizens so that they feel that what the european parliament (ep) approves, despite being based in brussels and meeting in strasbourg, affects them more than they might think. i therefore welcome the practical arrangements for the 2014 european elections, in particular as regards the election of the ep president, whose campaign can bring a more interesting and motivating political debate.
in writing. - the ruling classes are using the eu crisis to try to legitimize the path of recession and destruction, to perpetuate the policies that are at its origin and to deepen its anti-democratic character. the next elections to the european parliament are part of this process. the formula chosen is: - a mystification of what is really at stake in these elections; concealing the fact that this is a process of choosing, in each country, the parties, their programmes and their candidates, adding to it the suffrage character of the candidate of each european party for the presidency of the european commission (ec); - to divert the debate from clarifying the proposals and alternatives of each party, on the pretext of promoting what they call a real debate at eu level, reproducing at european level the national farce of the election of the prime minister; - to impose a debate between supposed european parties, to legitimize these supranational structures, in what will also be an alleged suffrage of these same parties (created by the eu, subject to respect for its operating rules and programme and dependent on its funding), all this at a time when the break with the eu, its policies and orientations, is a fundamental condition for the emancipation of the peoples and the construction of another europe. we obviously voted against it.
in writing. − the 2014 european elections will be the first since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. they will be of great importance and, as a result, the european union is taking important steps towards a genuine economic and monetary union, of which democratic legitimacy is a cornerstone. the treaty of lisbon has strengthened the union's democratic foundations. it reinforces the role of the eu citizen as a political actor in the eu, establishing a strong link between citizens, the exercise of their political rights and the democratic life of the union. the role of the european parliament as the union's representative democratic assembly was underlined by the treaty of lisbon. moreover, by introducing the citizens' initiative, the lisbon treaty allows eu citizens to participate more directly and fully in the democratic life of the union. we will make these elections the most competitive and the most identifiable for european citizens with their representatives in the european institutions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the duff report on practical measures to improve the organisation of the 2014 european parliament elections, which i have been working on as s&d group shadow rapporteur, because it sets out a set of measures which, if adopted, will be a strong impetus for the creation of a genuine parliamentary democracy in the eu by next year's elections. the presentation by european political parties of their candidates for president of the european commission and a political programme for the government of the union, the holding of public debates between the candidates for president of the commission to discuss political programmes, and the fact that ballot papers in european elections now include the identification of european political parties together with the corresponding national parties are measures which make a decisive contribution to the europeanisation of european elections. the european elections will be truly european, not only because they will be contested on the basis of european political agendas and with the involvement of european political parties, but also because they will be decisive for the choice of the european government. and this is an essential condition for strengthening the democratic legitimacy of the eu project in the eyes of the european people.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on improving the organisation of the 2014 european parliament elections, which calls on all political parties at all levels to adopt democratic and transparent procedures for the selection of their candidates for the elections to the european parliament and for the presidency of the commission.
in writing. − at a time of crisis such as the one europe is currently experiencing, when it is necessary to move towards deeper integration, it is essential that the european institutions, and in particular the european parliament, strengthen their democratic legitimacy. to this end, it is essential that we create the conditions for european citizens to be able to participate actively and in an informed way in the political life of the union. the measures advocated here, which i was very keen to see adopted at afco, will certainly contribute to creating a genuine european political awareness, making the 2014 elections more transparent and more european: increasing the visibility of european political parties, the nomination by european political parties of their candidates for the presidency of the commission, the timely dissemination by national parties of their lists of candidates and the encouragement of the participation in the electoral process of european citizens of other member states. these are all proposals which i am sure will increase the turnout in the european elections and help to raise citizens' awareness of specifically european issues. i therefore welcome their approval.
in writing. − this own-initiative report contains a set of recommendations to be made to both member states and european political parties regarding the upcoming 2014 european parliament elections. i voted against proposals to dictate to political parties how to choose their candidates for the ep or for the commission presidency. i abstained in the final vote because, although some of the recommendations allow for a deeper debate on the various policy options at european level, there is a clear attempt to convey the message that this is a direct election of the president of the commission, which is not true.
in writing. − the next european elections have been brought forward to 22-25 may 2014 in order to facilitate the appointment of the new college of commissioners who will take office as soon as possible. i think it is extremely positive that the european political parties have already presented their candidates for president of the european commission and that these should be the subject of a fruitful debate in the various member states. i would also like to stress the positive aspect of the fact that the names of the political parties and their logos appear on the ballot paper. finally, i urge the european authorities and political parties to develop a broad european campaign to promote citizens' rights and the importance of voting in the next european elections, thereby increasing the level of participation of the 500 million europeans.
in writing. - the ruling classes are using the eu crisis to try to legitimize the recession and destruction and to deepen their anti-democratic character. the next elections to the european parliament are part of this process. it is not intended to hide the fact that this is a process of selecting, in each country, the parties, their programmes and their candidates, and that the candidate of each european party for the presidency of the european commission is a suffragette; the aim is to impose a debate between supposed european parties, to legitimize these supranational structures, and to impose a supposed suffrage for these same parties (created by the eu, subject to compliance with its operating rules and programme and dependent on its funding). we voted against it.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that events such as the arab spring in the middle east and north africa have once again laid bare the problematic relationship between democratisation and human rights issues, which constitutes a liability when arms are traded with these countries, just as the events of the arab spring have once again demonstrated the absolute necessity and importance of the common position and its eight criteria, as well as of wider international agreements such as the arms trade treaty. i believe that a proactive approach should allow future initiatives and reports to draw on these lessons, especially when it comes to the spread of arms sold to non-state actors, as in the case of libya, and the possibility of direct transfers to rebels, as in the case of syria. in this context, i welcome the fact that the european union has a single, legally binding international framework capable of improving the control of arms exports, particularly to regions in crisis and to countries with a poor human rights record.
in writing. − arms exports and transfers have repercussions on human security, human rights, democracy, good governance and socioeconomic development. for this reason, it is important to strengthen the policy of control of exports of eu military technology and equipment, which should be integrated into a transparent, effective and commonly accepted and defined arms control system. the defence industry remains an important sector both industrially and in terms of job creation in the european union. the criteria of the common position must also be taken into account in the process of restructuring the european defence industry, which is essential for small and medium-sized enterprises, which create jobs. the developing countries remain the main target of arms sales abroad by their suppliers. events such as the arab spring in the middle east and north africa have once again laid bare the problematic relationship between democratization and human rights issues, which is a liability when trading arms with these countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because it encourages the participation of european and non-european countries in the arms export control system, on the basis of the common position and the arms trade treaty. although the eu is the only union of states worldwide to have a single, legally binding international framework in this area, it remains a matter of concern that the eight criteria of the common position are not being interpreted and applied consistently in the member states.
in writing. - the control of exported arms is particularly complex because of the speed of transport and communications we are experiencing today and the increased portability and lethality of many of the weapons produced. this difficulty should not prevent the european union from seeking to control the destination and use of arms it exports and from doing so in a serious and rigorous manner, without this being a substitute for the specific competences of each member state in this respect. the particular sensitivity of this market and the implications for international security and stability call for caution and responsibility when exporting and for the ability to monitor the use and disposal of exported arms. these tasks are not easy and, despite the restrictive nature of the legislation in force, they are prone to neglect. it is the responsibility of the union and its member states to meet and live up to the standards of standards it has set.
in writing. - the export of arms is a matter which divides politicians and citizens. we all want to see the end of guns for the sake of peace. but the truth is that weapons often have a deterrent effect. at the level of the european union and other arms exporting countries , this is a multi-million euro business and employs millions of workers. if we cannot stop the international trade in arms - and we also know that they often end up where they should not - we must regulate this sector in a way that makes it more responsible and properly controlled. weapons are not commodities like other commodities, and they require risk assessment and monitoring of their progress. i voted in favour of this joint motion for a resolution on arms exports, and more specifically the implementation of council common position 2008/944/cfsp, as it clarifies and improves the rules of this trade by standardising procedures at the level of the 28 member states. the eu should assess arms exports outside the eu and ensure that they do not risk human rights violations or be used to promote regional instability.
in writing. - the control of arms exports is of the utmost importance. the establishment of legal instruments can be of the greatest benefit. the arms trade, and in particular its export, is still the most profitable business for the military-industrial complex and its existence is a condition that feeds the trafficking whose profits continue to flow through tax havens for their laundering. as the resolution endorsed by our group advocated, there is a need for greater transparency in the registration of arms exports and public knowledge of them, with regular information on licences issued by each member state, the goods, the category, the total number of products and the end user, as well as the need for member states to assess the risks of corruption before issuing an export licence. it is also of the utmost importance that more effective political and democratic control of these processes be put in place. this resolution follows a difficult procedure in a specialised committee, which did not allow the adoption of a report drawn up by a member of our group. the whole process and the result of the vote, with the rejection of the first resolution voted, shows that for the majority of this parliament the military-industrial complex is still in charge.
in writing. − the s&d group was forced to abstain in today’s vote on the motion for a resolution on arms exports put forth by the right-wing aisle of parliament. the motion presented by the s&d group, together with the greens and gue, was rejected by the right-wing ppe, alde and ecr because these groups, despite verbally committing to a transparent and accountable arms control regime, refrain from demanding a more compelling implementation, which is what the s&d, greens and gue called for in a joint motion voted down today. by failing to call for a more demanding regime, the right-wing frustrates the implementation of not only the 2008 council common position on arms exports but also the foundational european principles and values, and is undoubtedly invalidating the eu’s efforts in conflict resolution, peacebuilding, the rule of law and human rights in the world. the time has come for member states and the eu council to take responsibility for arms deals and that is why the s&d group decided to abstain in today’s vote.
in writing. − the european union must have a single, legally binding international framework capable of improving arms export control, particularly for crisis regions and countries with a poor human rights record. however, in addition to the participation of european countries, third countries must also be represented in the arms export control system established on the basis of the common position. we must bear in mind that the eight criteria of the common position are interpreted and applied with varying degrees of rigour in the member states of the union, and that a more uniform interpretation and application of the common position and all the commitments deriving from it is therefore necessary. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this joint motion for a resolution on arms exports, which calls on the commission and the member states to implement the eu's commitments to combat the illicit accumulation and trafficking of small arms and light weapons (salw) and their ammunition, and recalls that these commitments are aimed at assisting third countries in stockpile management and similar efforts to control salw and ensure the regular transfer of military goods, in order to prevent member states from supplying countries from which weapons originate for abusive uses.
in writing. − the implementation of council common position 2008/944/cfsp on the european union's contribution to combating the accumulation and proliferation of small arms and light weapons ensures minimum standards for member states in arms control. these provisions are intended to regulate the transfer of military goods, i.e. arms exports, in order to prevent supplies to countries where they give rise to abusive uses. the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide monitoring mechanism for the implementation of the common position, which would be based on the principle of the free movement of goods and services, and would be based on the principle of the free movement of persons. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. − the european union now has a single, legally binding international framework capable of improving arms export control, particularly for crisis regions and countries with a poor human rights record. parliament welcomed the participation of european and non-european countries in the arms export control system and the conclusion of the arms trade treaty. however, i do not consider the request made in this joint motion for a resolution for an additional criterion to the eight already in place to be relevant and have therefore voted against the document.
in writing. - we consider that the control of arms exports is of the greatest importance and that the establishment of legal instruments can be of the greatest benefit. the arms trade, and in particular its export, is still the most profitable business for the military-industrial complex and its existence is a condition that fuels trafficking - the profits of which continue to flow through tax havens for laundering. as the resolution endorsed by our group advocated, there is a need for greater transparency in the registration of arms exports and public knowledge of them, with regular information on licences issued by each member state, the goods, the category, the total number of products and the end user, as well as the need for member states to assess the risks of corruption before issuing an export licence. it is also of the utmost importance to ensure that these processes are subject to more effective political and democratic control, which means respecting and valuing the sovereignty of the institutions of each country and their participation and control in these processes.
in writing. − i approve this motion for a resolution, welcoming the opening of negotiations on a trade in services agreement and the eu's participation in these talks from the outset in order to promote its interests and defend its views on the format and structure of the agreement. i regret, however, that the council has given a mandate without taking account of the opinion of the european parliament. i believe that the critical mass has not been reached to extend the benefits of this future agreement on trade in services to all wto members and that therefore the most favoured nation clause of the gats should not apply to it. i also believe that keeping open the possibility for other countries, including emerging economies, to participate in these negotiations should not reduce the level of ambition of the agreement, since only a high level of liberalization and convergence of disciplines will be able to convince these countries to join the negotiations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i consider it important to include the eu in the negotiations on a trade in services agreement in the wto in order to promote its interests and defend its views on the format and structure of the document. it is important that this agreement safeguards and differentiates services of general interest, as they provide vital safety nets for citizens and promote social cohesion at municipal, regional, national and eu level.
in writing. − on 15 february 2013, the european commission proposed to the council to open negotiations for a new international agreement on trade in services. the commission received a mandate to take part in the multilateral agreement on services on 18 march. currently, in addition to the eu and its 27 member states, 20 other wto members have agreed to take part in the negotiations. all service sectors will potentially be covered by this agreement. i agree with this opening of negotiations and i hope that this future agreement will bring benefits to the european economy and will lead to an increase in employment levels within the union.
in writing. the motion for a resolution tabled by mr vital moreira on behalf of the committee on international trade, following a statement by the commission pursuant to rule 110 (2), concerns the opening of negotiations on a multilateral agreement on services. services (e-commerce, tourism, construction, financial and cultural services, etc.) are the key sector of the european economy. they account for the largest number of jobs and more than half of our exports. one aspect to be taken into account is the need for trade liberalisation which can benefit our economy, although there are sectors such as water, energy, waste collection, among others, which are considered basic services and whose privatisation must be carefully considered. the opening up of the services market is a positive step, but it must be done with respect for all those involved. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because it seeks to negotiate an ambitious agreement to enable the services sector to join the world trade organisation (wto). the european parliament, by adopting this resolution, takes another step towards aligning the eu's trade policy.
in writing. the resolution follows the opening of negotiations on an agreement on trade in services. it is argued that the eu plays an important role in trade in services as the world's largest exporter of services. it considered that all initiatives relating to this agreement should be properly framed within the wto framework and regretted that trade in services had been neglected by the doha round. it regrets that the brics countries are not part of these negotiations, because they are markets where trade and investment in services are growing and where obstacles, particularly to foreign investment, are more significant. it is moving with objectives that the commission should take into account when negotiating market access commitments: promoting an ambitious agenda for eu offending interests, notably in business services, ict services, financial and legal services, e-commerce, maritime and air transport services, environmental services, tourism and construction. the intentions of those who support this resolution are thus crystal clear: to defend the offensive interests of big business against the interests of the people. we are facing the challenge of the tedious and repetitive neoliberal argument about the wonders of free trade. we voted against it, of course.
in writing. - i believe that the multilateral trading system, embodied in the wto, remains the most effective framework for achieving open and fair trade worldwide. i believe that we should give greater importance to services, as they are one of the engines of the european economy in the 21st century, increasingly important for job creation and economic growth.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on the opening of negotiations for a multilateral agreement on services. the resolution stresses that the eu negotiating mandate was proposed without an impact assessment. the european parliament considers it essential that an impact assessment be carried out and calls on the commission to put into practice its intention to carry out a sustainability impact assessment and to consult relevant stakeholders on social, environmental and other concerns. it also called for the evaluation to be published in order to take account of its conclusions in the negotiations.
in writing. − the multilateral agreement on services, which is part of the wto, aims to develop multilateral rules to ensure that investment is conducted in a more systematic and uniform way between the contracting states. however, although the general agreement on trade in services (gats) has been amended by 129 wto members, most have not made the commitments envisaged. recognising the growing importance of trade in services for the development of the world economy in general and of the european union in particular, the commission proposed a negotiating mandate, adopted by the council, to promote the interests and defend the eu's views. the report also calls for the commission to set clear objectives when negotiating market access commitments. i voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted against this resolution because the agreement that is being sought will have the consequence of deregulating public services in europe, leading to privatisation, increased costs and lower quality of services provided, and subsequently to a decrease in accessibility to them by those who need them most.
in writing. - i believe that the multilateral trading system, embodied in the wto, remains the most effective framework for achieving open and fair trade worldwide. however, i acknowledge that new bilateral and multilateral initiatives were needed to boost trade negotiations in geneva, due to the impasse following the 8th wto ministerial conference in december 2011. however, it must be stressed that all initiatives must remain within the wto framework, which is why the future agreement on trade in services must be multilateralised. this agreement should follow the format and structure of the gats, including the notion of positive listing of commitments, and take up the gats's definitions, principles and core standards on treatment, market access and national disciplines. for the reasons i have mentioned, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. - i approve of this report, starting by pointing out that the norwegian government proposed these measures without consulting its eu counterparts beforehand, as would have been appropriate in the context of the strong bilateral relations that exist. i therefore question the economic logic behind these measures, which may result in a reduction in trade, harming all parties involved, in particular norwegian consumers and, in the long term, also norwegian farmers. i therefore call on the commission to assess the potential negative effects of the tariff increase on eu exporters and farmers and i urge the norwegian government and parliament to withdraw the measures. finally, i ask the commission to specify the measures it intends to take in the event that norway refuses to reconsider its decision, in particular to protect, if necessary, employment and production in the agricultural sector of the union.
in writing. − the eea agreement lays the foundation for norway's equal access to the internal market. economic and political relations between the european union and norway are excellent. the bilateral agreement in force since january 2012 renewed the preferential, reciprocal and mutually beneficial legal framework for the granting of trade preferences for agricultural products, including meat and dairy products. through this agreement, the european union and the kingdom of norway have extended the mutual liberalisation of trade in agricultural products, granting duty-free access, establishing tariff quotas and reducing import duties for a wide range of agricultural products. the indicators of economic growth, employment and inflation show no sign of any negative impact of the global economic or financial crisis on the norwegian economy. i believe that negotiations should be opened with the norwegian authorities in order to find a mutually satisfactory solution for the import/export of agricultural products. i hope that norway will remain an integral part of the internal market and will not resort to further disintegrating and unilateral measures.
in writing. - while it is true that norway does not join the european union of its own accord, it is also true that the union has very close links with norway in a wide range of areas, including trade. i therefore regret that, instead of opening up even more to a close relationship with the union, norway has chosen to unilaterally increase customs duties on agricultural products. i hope that this situation can be reversed and that trade in agricultural products can flow more freely and mutually beneficial.
in writing. − norway is a country with a trade surplus which has signed a preferential agreement for customs goods so as not to impede trade flows between the european union and norway. however, as of 1 january 2013, it introduced a set of protectionist measures by imposing customs duties on imports of food products such as cheese and sheep and beef. this is not a new situation, for it has done the same with fish and oil. given the strong relations between norway and the european union and the fact that the eu is norway's main trading partner, we are obliged to denounce these protectionist measures, especially since the parties have committed themselves to a progressive liberalisation of trade. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution, tabled following a question with oral answer by mr vital moreira and mr christofer fjellner, because the eu was not consulted beforehand on these measures, which not only violate international law but also cast a shadow over relations between norway and the eu at a time when the review of the existing agreement, scheduled for next year, is approaching.
in writing. − the agreement on the european economic area (eea) lays the foundations for norway's access to the internal market by providing for a gradual liberalisation of trade in agricultural products. in 2012, a bilateral agreement between the eu and norway renewed the granting of trade preferences for agricultural products, including dairy products and meat. in january 2013, norway increased customs duties to a level considered by this resolution to be very high, affecting eu exporters of certain types of cheese, sheepmeat and beef, and introduced a new import duty on hydrangeas. the resolution criticises the protectionist measures implemented by norway, which it considers harmful to trade, accusing norway of violating the letter and spirit of the bilateral agreement. it called on the commission to enter into negotiations with norway immediately in order to find a mutually satisfactory solution and to specify the measures it intends to take in the event of norway's refusal to reconsider its decision. the fundamentalists of free and unregulated trade do not accept that a country sovereignly adopts the measures it deems necessary to regulate trade and defend specific productive sectors. we obviously voted against it.
in writing. − as a member of the european economic area (eea), norway benefits from the internal market, but agriculture and fisheries are excluded from free movement under the 1992 agreement on the european economic area. the latest agreement between the kingdom of norway and the european community on the basis of article 19 of the eea agreement entered into force in july 2003. between march 2008 and january 2010, further negotiations took place, culminating in the current draft agreement, which will increase trade in agricultural products between the eu and norway. i cannot therefore agree with norway's unilateral decision to oblige european exporters of certain types of cheese and sheep and beef to pay ad valorem customs duties of 277%, 429% and 344% respectively on the norwegian market as from 1 january 2013, given that this measure was preceded by the introduction of a new import duty of 72% on hydrangeas. although these measures are authorised by the world trade organisation list for norway, they violate the letter and spirit of the bilateral agreement. hence my vote.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on the increase of norwegian customs duties on agricultural products, in which the commission is asked to continue negotiations with the norwegian authorities in order to find a mutually satisfactory solution for the import/export of agricultural products.
in writing. − the present motion for a resolution questions the logic behind the measures imposed by the norwegian government with the introduction of new, protectionist and trade-damaging customs duties between the eu and norway, which are in clear breach of the letter and spirit of the bilateral agreement in force since january 2012. given that recent socioeconomic indicators deny any sign of a slowdown in the norwegian economy, we conclude that the justification for these customs measures proposed by the kingdom of norway does not lie in the current crisis context. however, it would be expected that the norwegian government, within the framework of existing bilateral relations, would consult the member states in advance to justify the envisaged customs duties, even before they were applied. the norwegian government and parliament are therefore urged to lift the tariff quotas as of this date, in the hope that the political bodies involved will not resort to unilateral measures in the future.
in writing. − whereas, in accordance with article 19 of the eea agreement, the contracting parties undertake to pursue their efforts to achieve a progressive liberalisation of trade in agricultural products and whereas the bilateral agreement in force since january 2012 renewed the preferential, reciprocal and mutually advantageous legal framework for the granting of trade preferences for agricultural products, including meat and dairy products, the european parliament regrets the recent measures imposed by the norwegian government, which it considers to be protectionist and trade-damaging and which constitute a clear breach of the letter and spirit of the bilateral agreement; the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the definition of the term 'competition' and to extend the scope of the term 'competition' to include the use of the term 'competition' in the definition of the term 'competition'. i therefore voted in favour of the document.
in writing. − the agreement on the european economic area (eea) lays the foundation for norway's equal access to the internal market. article 19 of the eea agreement states that the contracting parties undertake to pursue their efforts to achieve a progressive liberalisation of trade in agricultural products. in 2012, a bilateral agreement between the eu and norway renewed the granting of trade preferences for agricultural products, including dairy products and meat. however, in january 2013, norway increased the customs duties to a very high amount, affecting eu exporters of certain types of cheese, lamb and beef. this resolution criticises the protectionist measures implemented by norway. we believe that countries should be sovereign in deciding such matters.
in writing. − i support this report, considering that it is essential to exploit the full potential of the digital single market in order to make the eu a more competitive and dynamic knowledge-based economy, to the benefit of both its citizens and its businesses; and considering that the eu must act now to maintain its competitive advantage worldwide, particularly in high-growth sectors such as the internet platform and the it applications industry. in my view, ubiquitous connectivity, based on unimpeded access to broadband and high-speed internet networks, universal and equitable access to internet services for all citizens and the provision of spectrum for wireless broadband services, is an essential prerequisite for the development of the digital single market. furthermore, given that the eu economy is undergoing major structural change, which has repercussions on its global competitiveness and its labour market, the adoption of a true digital single market is therefore urgent.
in writing. - ict now plays a key role in promoting economic growth. they have promoted market restructuring, changed the way business is done and continue to offer a great opportunity for innovation. we need to invest in ict as one of the main pillars to promote growth and job creation, especially in the context of the economic crisis that the world economy is going through. more than building broadband or ict support infrastructure, europe needs to tap the potential of the internet in all sectors of the economy and harness it for economic recovery.
in writing. − the existence of a competitive digital single market is becoming more important and more inescapable in our society. technological developments, especially in terms of the provision of information, content and knowledge on the net, have been extremely rapid and, in just over a decade, have dramatically changed the digital landscape with the massification of the internet and mobile communications. it is therefore important to look to the future and to think about how these new facilities of the digital age can be put at the service of citizens and businesses, by modernising administrations and bringing them closer to those who are administered.
in writing. - the internet is a means of information and communication that knows no borders. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules and to monitor the implementation of the new rules. this requires investment in the structures to promote broadband so that it is available across europe - which will create jobs and legal standardisation. in addition to strengthening confidence in the internal market, this is an opportunity to create an additional 25% of jobs in the digital sector. the new information and data transmission technologies are an accelerator of the development of the european union and consolidate the functioning of the european single market. it is a way of internationalizing small and mediumsized enterprises and modernising their operations. i voted in favour of the proposal which follows a statement by the commission on the need to strengthen confidence in the digital single market, which has unanimous support in this house because its advantages are more than obvious in terms of economic growth and job creation, as well as in the widespread free and universal access to online services by all citizens and businesses on equal terms.
