in writing. − this resolution raises some concerns about consumer protection and trust in e-commerce, especially for more vulnerable groups such as the elderly and the disabled. however, we cannot depart from the central and cross-cutting objective of this resolution: the promotion of the liberalisation of the digital market. it is beginning to see the need to exploit the full potential of the digital single market to make the eu a more competitive and dynamic economy. to this end, member states should apply directives and regulations relating to the single market fully and effectively. the digital single market is being developed to meet business interests, rather than being geared towards the defence of the general interest, the public domain and free access to the public.
all austerity measures begin by affecting the most vulnerable in society first and most severely, and among all the social losses that are added up, one of the initial and essential is that of recourse to the provision of health care, both in terms of diagnosis and treatment and in the prevention and treatment of disease. in this context, i would like to stress that not only is access to health care a fundamental right of citizens, but health is also a fundamental condition for the well-being of the individual and the harmony of his personal life, for his professional activities and his contribution to society. it is therefore important to recognise that cuts in health care, so-called short-term cuts, may have long-lasting harmful effects, both personally and socially. among these, i would highlight the worsening of poverty among the most vulnerable and social inequality, but also the increase in risks to public health, for example from the increase in infectious diseases. i therefore welcome the initiative of this report, which i support.
in writing. - i welcome this report, considering that its aim is to identify a number of issues arising for groups considered to be vulnerable, for some groups where needs are becoming more and more evident and new, and for potentially vulnerable groups, in the context of current changing conditions, such as personal indebtedness. the committee thanks the various organisations which have provided it with up-to-date information. it is clear that the care sector for the elderly and people with physical or learning disabilities on the one hand, and those providing support for children or young people, or other individuals with special needs on the other, are increasingly under threat as costs are reduced and demands are increased. health care delivery faces similar challenges. such cuts, whether in services or benefits, affect not only those in need of care but also those who provide it. government budgets are being cut!
in writing. - poverty is an offence against human dignity. social inequality continues to develop in certain parts of the eu, due to the deterioration of the situation of already vulnerable groups, where many of the poor become even poorer. this trend has significant implications for the poverty reduction and inclusive growth targets of the europe 2020 strategy. some social security systems, especially those that assume a certain family-based structure, or those whose rights may be conditioned by certain working standards, also appear less able to cope with the growing pressures caused by the crisis, especially with regard to child poverty. troika interference in national budgets implies that the eu is seen as having a direct effect on areas that are primarily the responsibility of the member states. the eu should be seen as a promoter of solutions. comprehensive assessments of the social impacts caused by changes to social security systems and health service delivery are essential to prevent a bad situation from becoming worse, creating long-term problems and undermining other policy objectives.
in writing. − the dramatic increase in unemployment and uncertainty caused by the current economic and financial crisis has had disastrous consequences on health disparities, not only between member states but also within each member state: inequalities both between people living in different regions and between more and less favoured groups. those inequalities result from differences that are associated with factors such as living conditions, health behaviours, education, occupation and income, health care, disease prevention and health promotion services, and member states' policies, which influence the quantity, quality and distribution of those factors. with a view to achieving the eu's objective of economic growth and social solidarity set out in the lisbon strategy, it is essential to set up accompanying measures at eu level, which can support the actions developed by member states by fostering greater coordination and encouraging the exchange of good practices to eliminate such inequalities. it is important to help member states to make appropriate use of cohesion policy, the structural funds and the opportunities provided for under rural development policy and the cap market policies. they should also define effective policies, including actions to eliminate social disparities in health in general and actions specifically targeting the most vulnerable groups.
in writing. − the crisis we are experiencing, coupled with measures to curb health spending or reduce social support, has made it more difficult for the most vulnerable groups, such as the elderly and the disabled, to access health and medicines. it is therefore essential to make a balanced adjustment in the health sector, giving priority to cutting unnecessary expenditure and changing the paradigm so that we can support more those in need without overburdening the state. it is increasingly essential that states choose the right spending and implement reforms that create a fairer and more efficient model of health and medicines spending, without putting an undue burden on budgets and without hampering access for the most deprived. the way forward will be to promote equity in access by ensuring differentiated support for the most vulnerable groups.
in writing. − all people are born free and have the right to basic services such as health, food, education, etc. it is the responsibility of public services to ensure that these rights are respected. the economic and financial crisis has reduced the protection of people, particularly in relation to health. many citizens, after months of unemployment, renounce health insurance, which further worsens their quality of life. health care costs rise, wages fall, and problems pile up. in times of crisis, it is the most vulnerable who suffer most, especially children, the elderly and women, whose universal right to regular medical care is often called into question. i voted in favour of the report by jean lambert on the impact of the crisis on access to health care for vulnerable groups because, especially in times of crisis, we need to increase medical support for the most disadvantaged, provide quality health services for children and the elderly and fight against ethnic or religious discrimination against minorities.
in writing. − this own-initiative report is positive, highlighting a number of problems faced by vulnerable populations in accessing healthcare. the problem of access to health care is exacerbated by the consequences of the deepening crisis, as the report says. and what is more, the so-called austerity measures taken in the name of the solution to this crisis make matters worse. in this respect, the report fails to fully relieve eu policies and institutions of responsibility for the implementation of these measures in the member states. the report criticises the reduction measures implemented in the health sector, accompanied by the introduction of moderating rates, the increase in non-reimbursable expenditure and cuts in preventive health care. all very right. but i could and should have gone further. two amendments were adopted which we proposed and which valued public services publicly owned and managed, with democratic participation by their users and called for further consolidation of national health services to meet the needs of populations, especially the most vulnerable groups.
in writing. - the committee on employment and social affairs has for some time been concerned about the effect of these austerity measures on society in general and on vulnerable groups in particular. this own-initiative report seeks to identify a number of issues that arise for groups considered to be vulnerable, for some groups where needs are becoming more and more evident and new, and for potentially vulnerable groups, in the context of current changes in conditions, such as personal indebtedness. the need to have accurate, comparable and as up-to-date as possible data is a priority in order to find the right antidotes to minimise the impact of the crisis on these groups.
in writing. − the interference of austerity measures in national budgets is putting the european union at risk of losses caused by reforms under way in some member states. this implies that the union is seen as having a direct effect on areas which are primarily the responsibility of the member states, such as health and social care. in this context, the committee on employment and social affairs intends not only to identify a number of issues concerning the effects of austerity measures on groups considered to be vulnerable - migrants, children, precarious workers, the elderly and people with disabilities - but also to call for the responsibility of the union, which, with its potential for interference in national budgets, should also be a promoter of solutions. in fact, the removal of support for those who need it most, while it may lead to short-term spending cuts, ultimately creates lasting problems and should therefore be rejected.
in writing. - in view of the impact of the crisis, parliament called on the commission to require member states to provide information on the austerity measures implemented, to carry out social impact assessments of the austerity measures and to include in its country-specific recommendations recommendations which take into account the social and economic impact of such measures in the medium and long term. parliament also called on the commission and the member states to monitor, in cooperation with all relevant actors, and to address, in the context of national reform plans, national policies that go against the 2020 poverty reduction target. i therefore voted in favour of the document.
in writing. − this own-initiative report is quite positive, highlighting a number of problems faced by vulnerable populations in accessing healthcare. the problem of access to health care is exacerbated by the consequences of the deepening crisis, as the report says. we believe, however, that the main problem lies in the measures taken in the name of the potential solution to this crisis. in this respect, the report fails to fully discharge european policies from the implementation of austerity measures in the member states. the report criticises the reduction measures implemented in the health sector, accompanied by the introduction of moderating rates, the increase in non-reimbursable expenditure and cuts in preventive health care. two amendments were adopted which we proposed and which valued public services - publicly owned and managed, with democratic participation by their users - and called for a further consolidation of national health services to meet the needs of populations, especially the most vulnerable groups.
in writing. - i approve of this report, considering that hybrid television is an important technological step towards convergence of the media, which has the merit of calling into question important regulatory decisions in this sector. when adopting the audiovisual media services directive, it was decided that linear services would be subject to a coherent regulatory system, while non-linear services would be treated less restrictively, on the grounds that services have a different social function. in all member states, the linear services of public and private television stations assume, in addition to their impact as mass media, a high socio-political importance, which is often regulated by law. despite technological convergence, television has not lost its popularity or its socio-political importance. as linear media continue to reach a wider audience, they should be subject to strict regulatory requirements. this consequent differentiation, which has so far been achieved by means of progressive regulation under the scsa directive, is increasingly approaching its limits, especially with the development of hybrid television, or at least raises a number of issues and problems which must be solved by specific legislation.
in writing. − audiovisual media services are very important for society and democracy as carriers of identities, values and meanings, and require specific regulation in an increasingly convergent world. it is necessary to examine the need to review the audiovisual media services directive and other existing requirements in the media and networking regulation as regards the provisions on the location and non-discriminatory access to platforms for content providers and content operators by broadening the concept of platform in order to adapt existing mechanisms to new realities. we must be aware of the future challenges of connected tv in terms of the competitiveness of the sector, making it possible to relax more the quantitative constraints on advertising, and its advantages and disadvantages must be presented. i regret, however, that there are vast regions throughout europe with limited internet infrastructure. in order to exploit the potential of connected tv, it is essential that consumers have access to high-speed internet.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report for advocating the extension of the scope of the audiovisual media services directive to cover all operators of portals and hybrid platforms. it is necessary to ensure that devices, platforms and portals are designed on the basis of an open model, so that non-discriminatory and technologically neutral access to all content can be ensured.
in writing. - hybrid television is the type of television that combines access to the traditional television service and internet access on a single screen, thus promoting media convergence. this raises important issues in the field of competition law, economic law and privacy and data protection, but not only, as media are recognized educational, informative, entertainment and surveillance functions. european legislation must therefore be particularly attentive to these new realities and must adapt to new products placed on the market.
in writing. the report by mrs kammerevert on hybrid television is very timely, as the directive in force is outdated. the technological advance in this sector is enormous, not only because of the advent of digital television, but also because of the range of services and products that the television industry offers us. the reality of audiovisual media has changed and we must keep pace with its evolution and modernisation. we cannot treat the media as a commodity that sits in a warehouse waiting to be sold. hybrid television enables the citizen not only to access television programmes but also a range of products and services via the internet. this requires us to adopt a regulation which maintains the balance between what is offered to us and our freedom of choice. i voted in favour of this report, which calls for a revision of the audiovisual and social media services directive, because we need a regulation to protect consumers, especially children and young people, and to reorient the provision of content in the interests of citizens. we cannot let the providers tell us what's going to be on, because we have to guarantee the quality of the content.
in writing. - hybrid television is a major technological step which gives the user access not only to classic television programmes but also to the internet, irrespective of the technological platform used in the broadcast. the same screen thus brings together different services such as traditional television, video rental, internet and video-text, which in turn are covered by regulatory frameworks with very different degrees of regulation. the report encourages the commission to review the audiovisual media services directive and other existing requirements in the media and networking regulations by broadening the concept of platform to adapt existing mechanisms to new realities. an important and sensitive issue addressed is the protection of minors and protection against discrimination and hate-filled content. although the report addresses this issue within the existing liberalised framework for media and audiovisual services, concerns are raised about the provision of public services and ensuring respect for freedom of expression, information and the press. the report is also lacking in the firm defence of a public service of radio and television.
in writing. - hybrid television is an important technological step towards media convergence, which has the merit of calling into question important regulatory decisions in this sector. it is important to seek to establish an appropriate balance of power between market players, in particular device manufacturers and content providers, and especially in the case of integrated services. it is also necessary to prevent certain content providers from gaining an unfair advantage in relation to the dissemination of their content. i think there is still a lot to be discussed, but here is an important first step in the implementation of hybrid television.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on hybrid television (hybrid systems combining television with the internet and allowing users to browse between television channels and internet services, including illegal audiovisual content pages) which calls for respect for the provisions currently in force on the protection of minors, the prohibition of advertising certain products for health reasons, the prohibition of incitement to racial hatred, the distinction between news and advertising content, transparency in the fields of intellectual property and privacy, among other provisions which are part of the community acquis and cannot be circumvented on the pretext of technological developments. in particular, it is requested that providers of hybrid television services and equipment from non-eu countries be informed that the applicable law is that of the country of origin of the service provided and not that of the country where the provider has its head office.
in writing. the definition of hybrid television implies that the same television set can capture and display both programmes from the conventional linear service and audiovisual content via the internet connection. this ambivalent nature raises a legal problem with regard to the regulation, to very different degrees, of linear and nonlinear services. to date, media harmonisation in legislative matters has been successfully implemented by the audiovisual media services directive. however, this directive is increasingly reaching its limits, especially with the development of hybrid television, which is a problem that can only be solved by specific legislation. the european union must therefore ensure free and fair competition between services and content, by providing the necessary legislative instruments to guarantee uniform conditions of competition, the plurality of content, the diversity of opinions and freedom of information. i voted in favour.
in writing. - hybrid television is an important technological step towards media convergence which has the merit of calling into question important regulatory decisions in this sector. the audiovisual media services directive should be further developed to cover portal and hybrid platform operators globally. those that largely determine the diversity of content and opinions that reach the end-user should also be subject to such regulation in order to safeguard that diversity of content and opinions. parliament therefore urges the commission to examine the need to review the audiovisual media services directive and other existing requirements in the media and networking regulations, such as the telecommunications package, with regard to the provisions on location and non-discriminatory access to platforms. i therefore voted in favour of the document.
in writing. - hybrid television is a major technological step forward which gives the user access not only to classic television programmes but also to the internet. the report encourages the commission to review the audiovisual media services directive and other existing requirements in the media and networking regulations by broadening the concept of platform to adapt existing mechanisms to new realities. for example, advertising on traditional television has a time limit, but not on the internet. an important and sensitive issue addressed is the protection of minors and protection against discrimination and hate-filled content. although the report addresses this issue within the existing liberalised framework for media and audiovisual services, concerns are raised about the provision of public services and ensuring respect for freedom of expression, information and the press. the report fails to mention the importance of defending a public service of radio and television and to slowly shift this responsibility, which is the responsibility of the states, to some private operators.

i would also like to thank my colleague arlene mccarthy for her work. it is exactly five years ago this september that we had the lehman brothers scandal, and we continue to live with the problems of market abuse, insider trading, market manipulation, opacity, lack of transparency, immorality every day. i think we can and should use that very word in this case: immorality. there are manipulations ranging from the altering of numbers, the interference with interest rates, the scandal of the benchmark indices and many more that we could identify. and it is quite true that in all the countries of the european union we continue to see every day news that appears on the front pages of newspapers, revealing individuals or institutions that had access to this information. and as hard as it is to prove, the truth is that no attempt is made to prove this crime and there is total impunity still going on. there are very few cases where these crimes have been punished. now, it's not because they're committed by individuals in suits or jackets, or by institutions that feel they're beyond what society's normal sanctions are, that they shouldn't be punished. they should be punished and they should go to prison if that is the case, because for criminals the result should be prison, regardless of what we are talking about. and only with concrete sanctions and concrete regulation can we finally talk about the financial market at the service of society, and not the shame we have been witnessing for five years now.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, two points. the first one is about the reciprocity mechanism. i agree that complete reciprocity in visa matters must be our objective. when a member state notifies that a third country has decided to make its nationals subject to a visa requirement, all member states should react collectively by giving a common response to a situation affecting the union as a whole. we cannot allow citizens of the union to be treated differently. this is the approach of my colleague mr díaz de mera, and i agree with him completely. secondly, the question of the reintroduction of visas, i.e. the temporary suspension of the exemption from the visa requirement. i would stress that this mechanism should only be activated in very specific cases of urgency where there has been a substantial and sudden increase in the number of irregular immigrants or unfounded applications for international protection. i agree with the approach taken by andrey kovatchev in the committee on foreign affairs, who stressed that this mechanism cannot be automatic. and i agree with him when he stresses that the visa exemption is only one aspect of the wider relations between the union and a third country or region and that for that reason the reintroduction of the visa requirement cannot be dissociated from this wider process and should not call into question the coherence of the european union's external policies. i share with many colleagues the idea that the european parliament should have more than the information rights it has, but i am very sensitive to the argument of my colleague mr díaz de mera, whom i have respected for a long time. if a broader commitment is not possible, it is better to take this first step than to be left with nothing. it is better that parliament should participate in the right to information than that we should continue with the system that is in force at the moment.

in writing. - i welcome the report as it is adopted, as its main objective is to defend the role of the european parliament in relation to the commission's proposal to amend the adoption of delegated and implementing acts. in general, the proposed amendments relate only to the types of acts to be adopted and do not change the content of the measures. however, certain issues proposed as implementing acts do not concern uniform conditions for the application of the regulation and their use involves de facto exclusion of parliament.
in writing. the need to conserve fisheries resources by protecting juveniles of marine organisms has been felt for some time. the european union and the member states share this need and share the same concern about the risks of non-renewal of marine organism populations and the consequent depletion of available fisheries resources and irreversible damage to biological diversity and the environment. the commission's proposed amendments to council regulation (ec) no 850/98 aim to improve the capacity and speed of the european response to these challenges and bring it into line with the rules of the lisbon treaty. i believe that parliament's version improves on the original version of the european commission, in particular because it introduces into the text the need for the commission to be periodically accountable for the powers delegated to it.
in writing. - the proposal to confer implementing powers on the commission in respect of: technical standards for the measurement of mesh size, square mesh and wire mesh; technical standards for the manufacture of net fabric materials; the list of devices which may obstruct or otherwise reduce the effective opening of the meshes of a fishing net; the transmission of lists of vessels for which a special fishing permit has been issued for use of beam trawls; technical standards for the measurement of engine power and size of fishing gear; the obligation for member states to ensure that fishing effort levels are not exceeded in certain areas of ices division ixa; temporary measures whenever the conservation of stocks of marine organisms requires immediate action.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 850/98 provides for certain technical conservation measures, it applies to the taking and landing of fishery resources in maritime waters under the sovereignty or jurisdiction of the member states. the commission proposal aims to align this regulation with articles 290 and 291 tfeu, concerning delegated and implementing acts. however, the rapporteur considers that articles 39, 40 and 41 of regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 establishing a community control system to ensure compliance with the rules of the common fisheries policy already provide a framework for the monitoring, certification and verification of engine power of fishing vessels and that these issues should therefore not be seen as implementing acts. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. − i agree that in order to allow certain provisions of this regulation to be updated to reflect effectively technical and scientific progress, acts should be adopted in accordance with article 290 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. such acts should be used for the procedures to be adopted for the conservation and maintenance of fishery resources through technical measures for the protection of juveniles of marine organisms. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - the aim of this report is to review regulation (ec) no 850/98 on the conservation of fishery resources through certain technical measures for the protection of juveniles of marine organisms. following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, regulation (ec) no 850/98 needs to be aligned with the new rules of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), which establishes a new regulatory hierarchy comprising three distinct levels of acts, namely legislative, delegated and implementing acts. in this context, the commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in respect of the division of regions into geographical zones, the rules for the use of nets and the rules for determining the percentage of target species caught by vessels. the commission's powers in terms of implementing acts relate mainly to technical measures for the construction and measurement of the mesh size of nets and technical standards for the measurement of engine power and the size of fishing gear. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it an important element in improving the regulation on technical fisheries management measures to protect juveniles of marine organisms.
in writing. - this proposal for a regulation is based on the new hierarchy of rules established by the lisbon treaty and aims to align regulation (ec) no 850/98 with the treaty. the commission proposes to be empowered to adopt delegated acts with regard to technical measures for the protection of juveniles of marine organisms, however, the rapporteur, while welcoming the proposals for amendments to the regulation drafted by the commission, notes that the implementing powers claimed in the text do not relate, as required by article 291 tfeu, to this third level of the hierarchy of rules. the rapporteur believes that the commission is moving forward with certain proposals for implementing acts, when in fact these proposals concern exceptions which supplement and amend certain non-essential elements of the legislative act, and therefore they should be delegated acts, limited in scope to the extension of the delegation, in order to ensure regular evaluation of their usefulness. the lucidity of the argument, judged in conjunction with the political group i belong to, supports my vote in favour.
in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 850/98 on the conservation of fishery resources through certain technical measures for the protection of juveniles of marine organisms needs to be brought into line with the new treaty rules on delegated and implementing acts. with the exception of some slight adjustments to the powers conferred on the commission in the field of delegated acts, the document largely maintains the commission's proposals, which is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, considering that while all the member states of the european union have the institution of marriage, not all have the institution of registered partnership and that the subject of the choice of law applicable to registered partnerships would therefore necessarily have to be limited to those member states which have this institution.
in writing. - the increasing mobility of people in an area without internal borders is reflected in a significant increase in unions, whatever their form, between nationals of different member states or residents in a member state other than that of their nationality. the registered partnership system is a form of union other than marriage, which is defined by the national law of each member state. this system is enshrined in the legislation of four member states for opposite-sex couples and in the legislation of 12 member states for same-sex couples. the recognition in a member state of a decision on the property consequences of a registered partnership is intended only to enable the property consequences determined in that decision to be enforced, without requiring the member state concerned to recognise the partnership underlying the property consequences giving rise to the decision. i therefore support this proposal which seeks to ensure that all eu citizens can enjoy the same equality and property rights, irrespective of the nature of the union, but with due regard for the national law of the member state concerned. the creation of a clear and coherent regulatory framework will provide greater legal certainty for the citizens concerned and bring clear benefits to the functioning of the internal market.
in writing. − it is essential that in the eu area registered partnerships with links to more than one member state can have their rights enforced in any of them. the aim is to achieve a degree of harmonisation of the schemes, which guarantees legal certainty for those involved, while maintaining the principle that the definition of such schemes is a matter for the member states.
in writing. − in 2007 there were some 211 000 registered partnerships in the eu, of which more than 41 000 had some link in terms of property regimes to more than one member state. of these unions, 8 500 (4%) ended in separation and 1 266 (0.6%) in the death of one of the partners. the institution of registered partnership is growing with the development of citizen mobility in europe. in the case of registered partnerships, even more so than in the case of marriages - the provisions vary greatly from one country to another, which creates legal uncertainty. in the event of a dispute, the partner who has the best advice available may - as in the case of couples united by marriage - decide to go to a court which applies the law which seems to him to be more favourable. this proposal substantially improves the legal situation of the couples involved.
in writing. − this report aims to contribute to the resolution of issues associated with the union of two partners, including disputes, in particular in relation to decisions to be taken in terms of property regimes (in more than one eu country). according to the report, the persons involved often face complex issues, especially as regards the law applicable to their case and the competent court. the laws vary widely from country to country in the case of registered unions, which creates legal uncertainty. to overcome these problems, the report proposes the legal recognition of certain rules for partnerships in property regimes with links to more than one member state. despite our well-known reservations about the harmonization of private civil law, the objectives pursued here seem to us to be fair and the proposal in the report acceptable.
in writing. − the increasing mobility of people in an area without internal borders is reflected in a significant increase in unions, whatever their form, between nationals of different member states, as well as in the presence of these couples in member states of which they are not nationals, often accompanied by the acquisition of property located in the territory of several countries of the union. this proposal aims, in particular, to create a clear legal framework in the european union covering the determination of the competent court and the applicable law for the property aspects of such partnerships and to facilitate the circulation of decisions and acts between member states. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − in 2007, there were some 211 000 registered partnerships in the eu, of which more than 41 000 had some link in terms of property regimes to more than one member state. of these unions, 8 500 (4%) ended in separation and 1 266 (0.6%) in the death of one of the partners. when, in the context of litigation or during the union of two partners, there are decisions to be taken in terms of property regimes, the persons involved are faced with very complex issues, especially as regards the law applicable to their case and the competent court. it is true that - in the case of registered unions even more so than in the case of marriages - the provisions vary greatly from one country to another. this situation creates considerable legal uncertainty. in addition, in the event of a dispute, the partner who has the best advice available may - as in the case of couples united by marriage - decide to go to a court which applies the law which seems to him to be more favourable. in the interests of legal certainty, i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation which seeks to change this situation by proposing the possibility of choosing the law applicable to registered partnerships.
in writing. − partnerships registered in the eu generate considerable legal uncertainty, especially because they raise complex issues in the context of the dissolution of the partnership or during the merger of two partners. the rapporteur considers the commission proposal to be relevant, but argues that a single document could contain the discriminatory regulation of two different regulatory objects, as she does not agree that there is a substantive difference in content between the two proposals. the main point of the text is that the proposal does not allow for the choice of the law applicable to registered partnerships, justifying to the commission that the differences in the law of the member states would be remedied by linking the law of the state of registration of the partnership. the rapporteur, however, asked the european agency for human rights for an opinion, which concludes that another justification is needed in relation to the possibility of choice of law by couples. the rapporteur therefore proposes a rule which would allow registered partnerships to choose the law applicable to their property rights. i voted in favour of the report because i consider the proposed adjustment to be appropriate, in a laudable effort to bring the law into line with the charter of fundamental rights of the european union.
in writing. − a registered partnership is a form of union other than marriage, the specific content of the notion of registered partnership being defined by the national law of the member states. in march 2011, the european commission presented a proposal for a regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matters of the property consequences of registered partnerships. the proposal aims to create a clear legal framework in the european union covering the determination of the competent court, the law applicable to the property aspects of such partnerships and facilitating the circulation of decisions and acts between member states. i am in favour of this report because i believe that there is a need for legal clarification of the issues relating to the property effects of registered partnerships, so that there are no different interpretations in the different member states.
in writing. − this report aims to help solve problems arising in the context of litigation or during the union of two partners, when there are decisions to be taken in terms of property regimes (in more than one eu country). the report explains that the persons involved face very complex issues, especially as regards the law applicable to their case and the competent court. the laws vary widely from country to country in the case of registered unions, which creates legal uncertainty. the report proposes that the legal recognition of certain rules should be introduced to overcome these problems in the case of partnerships in terms of property regimes with a link to more than one member state. we agree with the objective, although we have serious reservations about the harmonization of private civil law, considering that coordination of judicial institutions is preferable.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, considering that this report is essential to ensure equal rights in the choice of law for different forms of legal union and for the purposes of cross-border recognition, without derogating measures, in line with the council conclusions on fundamental rights and the rule of law adopted on 7 june 2013 as well as the 2012 commission report on the application of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union.
in writing. - freedom of movement and the increasing mobility of persons in an area without internal frontiers have contributed to a significant increase in the number of unions between nationals of different member states, or of couples residing in a member state of which they are not nationals, where this is often accompanied by the acquisition of property situated in the territory of several countries of the union. the number of couples in the eu who have a link with more than one member state is estimated at around 20 million and they face numerous obstacles and complex issues, including the applicable law and the competent forum. the aim of this initiative is to address the practical and legal difficulties faced by transnational couples in the union, both in the day-to-day management of the couple's property and at the time of sharing (in the event of divorce or death of one of the spouses), thus enabling these couples to know more easily which courts and legislation apply to their property rights, and to facilitate the circulation of decisions and acts between member states. i therefore support the creation of a clear and coherent regulatory framework and the establishment of simpler, clearer and more accessible procedures.
in writing. − one in seven marriages in the eu involve nationals from more than one member state. this raises relevant property issues, in particular the application of the law on married couples' property regimes. as i have said, there must be some degree of harmonisation of the systems of marriage, which guarantees legal certainty for those involved, while the definition of these remains a competence primarily of the states.
in writing. − in 2007, more than one in seven couples in the eu (16 million) had a link with more than one member state, as did more than one in seven marriages (310 000) and divorces (137 000). in total, some 637 000 transnational marriages ended in divorce or the death of one of the spouses. the persons involved are confronted with complex issues, in particular as regards the applicable law and the competent court. the question of property regimes also arises in the management of assets during the marriage. they may also have repercussions on third parties, as in the case of real estate transactions or credit operations. the legal provisions underlying matrimonial property regimes vary widely between member states, as do the rules on the choice of court. in practice, therefore, it may be the case that the court with jurisdiction in one member state will assess the case in matters of property regimes differently from the court with jurisdiction in another member state. the aim is to reduce legal uncertainty.
in writing. the proposal for a report aims to create a regulatory framework in the european union for the determination of the competent court and the law applicable to matrimonial property regimes, with the aim of facilitating the circulation of judgments and acts between member states. these legal actions often concern the settlement of property, when a couple separates or when one of the spouses dies. the report aims to clarify the matrimonial property regimes as regards the applicable law and the competent court. although we are aware of our reservations about the harmonization of private civil law (we believe that greater coordination and cooperation between the judicial institutions is preferable), we recognize that the objectives pursued by this report are fair and relevant.

in writing. − in 2007, more than one in seven couples in the eu (16 million) had a link with more than one member state, as did more than one in seven marriages (310 000) and divorces (137 000). 390,000 international marriages ended in the death of one of the spouses. in total, some 637 000 transnational marriages ended in divorce or the death of one of the spouses. in all such cases, it is important to discuss and clarify the matrimonial regimes. in may 2011, the commission presented two parallel proposals on matters of matrimonial property regimes and registered partnerships, which include provisions on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments. i voted in favour of the proposal on matrimonial property regimes and succession rights. the legal situation of the couples concerned has been substantially improved. this proposal introduces simpler, clearer and more accessible procedures in the field of civil justice. the increase in mobility means that even more couples will be affected in the future, and this regulation is therefore welcome, since regulatory certainty and clarity, as well as consistency with other legal acts of the european union, are essential.
in writing. the rapporteur proposes a number of amendments to clarify the scope of the regulation, in particular by clarifying the demarcation between this regulation and other areas of law. proposals for the adaptation of rights in rem are aligned with the regulation on succession rights. as regards the amendments proposed in the context of the provisions on the election of the court, the report only supplements them with amendments of a technical nature. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. finally, in the field of recognition, enforceability and enforcement, it is proposed, in view of the complexity of the procedures, to maintain the procedure for the enforcement of a judgment and to incorporate the corresponding provisions of the regulation on the succession rights. the law on matrimonial property regimes does not provide for a counterpart to the certificate of succession and it therefore appears essential to regulate the recognition and enforceability of instruments of matrimonial property regimes in the member states. given the need to improve the legal status of the legal provisions underlying the eu's matrimonial regimes, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - article 67 (1) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides that the union is an area of freedom, security and justice, with respect for fundamental rights and for the different legal systems. point 4 of that article provides that the union is to facilitate access to justice, in particular through the principle of mutual recognition of judicial and extrajudicial decisions in civil matters. this regulation does not cover the concept of marriage, which is defined by the national law of each of the 28 member states. on the contrary, this regulation takes a neutral position with regard to this concept, without affecting the definition of it in the national legislation of the member states. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that there should be rules of private international law applicable to matrimonial property regimes, especially at a time when there is a growing trend towards marriage between people from different countries. i also think it is important that the proposal covers jurisdiction, the applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial matters exclusively to situations of a transnational nature.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, considering first of all that clear common rules on access to a lawyer represent another step towards making the protection of fundamental rights a reality throughout the european union. i would also stress the efforts of my political group in ensuring that the principle of confidentiality was included in the directive in the negotiations without any possible derogation, and in establishing clear rules on the use of derogations under this directive so that all derogations were proportionate, strictly limited in time, so that it was not based solely on the seriousness of the alleged offences and so as not to prejudice the overall fairness of the procedure. we have also succeeded in ensuring that all suspects and accused persons have access to a lawyer in both member states of the proceedings.
in 2009, it was decided to start a phased approach, in which procedural rights in criminal proceedings should be dealt with in stages, and a roadmap was adopted, setting out six measures as a basis for future action. the progress made in the last three years is notable, with the adoption of the first two directives, which aim to guarantee the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings and the right to information respectively. this next step aims to address the divergences between member states as regards the provisions governing access to a lawyer, as well as their practical application, which raises doubts as to whether there is an adequate level of access to an effective defence in criminal proceedings and also calls into question the principle of mutual trust and mutual recognition. it thus provides that all suspects or accused persons shall have the right to access a lawyer as soon as possible and in a manner which enables them to exercise their rights of defence effectively. it also guarantees the right to communicate with family members, employers and consular authorities. i congratulate the rapporteur on the agreement she has been able to reach on the principle of confidentiality without any derogations. i support the commitment reached and hope that member states will swiftly implement it.
in writing. − i am a lawyer by profession and am fully aware of the irreplaceable role of lawyers' participation in the administration of justice, the importance they play in defending the most vulnerable and the need for their involvement in legal proceedings from the earliest stages. the fact that a person is detained under a european arrest warrant inevitably raises questions as to the detainee's actual ability to understand a trial that will be conducted in a language that may not be his or her own, and exacerbates the feeling of unprotectedness and alienation inherent in the deprivation of liberty. it therefore requires special attention and care. this misunderstanding and conditioning may compromise the fairness of the trial and the right to an effective defence. i am not unaware that the backlog of fundamental rights may increase the cost of justice, but i believe that fundamental rights should prevail over a purely financial perspective on this issue. that said, i believe that the union and the member states must cooperate to provide national courts with the human, technical and budgetary resources necessary to fully implement these rights, which, because of their importance, cannot risk being merely semantic.
in writing. − this proposal establishes the basic principle that all suspects or accused persons should be granted the right of access to a lawyer as soon as possible and in a manner which enables them to exercise their rights of defence effectively. it also specifies that in any case these rights must be granted before the commencement of any interrogation, in the performance of any procedural act or in the taking of evidence and in the case of deprivation of liberty. it also identifies the content of the right, stresses that meetings between the suspect or accused person and his lawyer must be confidential, lists the derogations allowed from the general principles and provides for rules in the event of waiving the right to a lawyer. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - this report defends the right of all suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, whether or not they have been deprived of their liberty, to have access to a lawyer in a timely manner, so as to enable the person concerned to exercise his right of defence. in addition, member states shall ensure that suspects or accused persons deprived of liberty have the right to communicate without delay with a third person, such as a family member designated by them, or to be visited by their consular authorities; the right to speak and correspond with them and to obtain legal representation through them. this is a set of fundamental rights which are enshrined in this proposal and which deserve our full support. that is why we voted in favour of the report. however, we cannot fail to stress that this process is taking place in the context of other advances in the supranationalization of key aspects of justice, in particular the european arrest warrant, with which we disagree.
in writing. - the european parliament has long called for stronger protection of the rights of victims of crime on the one hand and of the suspect and accused on the other. this proposal establishes the basic principle that all suspects or accused persons should be granted the right of access to a lawyer as soon as possible and in a manner that enables them to exercise their rights of defence effectively. it also specifies that in any case these rights must be granted before the commencement of any interrogation, in the performance of any procedural act or in the taking of evidence and in the case of deprivation of liberty. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the provisions of the european convention on human rights and the case law of the european court of human rights are not uniformly implemented and respected by the member states, which gives rise to divergent rules in the european union. parliament has repeatedly stressed the need to strengthen the procedural rights of suspects and accused persons, stressing the need to strike the right balance between freedom, justice and security. the need to strengthen mutual trust has become even more imperative with the implementation of the programme on mutual recognition of judicial decisions in criminal proceedings. legislation adopted at eu level over the past few years has improved the efficiency of prosecutions and the enforcement of sentences across the eu, yet there is a consensus that the lack of measures at eu level to promote the rights of citizens as suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings in another member state has created a sense of imbalance in eu justice policies. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this proposal which seeks to make up for this lack of measures to promote the rights of citizens as suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings.
in writing. − the proposal for a european parliament and council directive aims at implementing a convergent normative standard, in line with the provisions of the european convention on human rights and the case law of the european court of human rights, which, in the area of the right of access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings and the right of communication after detention, ensures that citizens' rights are fully respected and their safety guaranteed when travelling. the directive should be implemented in all member states irrespective of their case law. the approach to the legal instrument now moves away from the ambitious claim of the framework decision on procedural rights put forward by the commission in 2004 and instead proposes a more realistic approach. given the urgency of guaranteeing minimum rights to a fair trial throughout the european union, in particular when suspects are detained as a result of a european mandate, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - article 82 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) enshrines judicial cooperation in criminal matters in the european union. it is based on the principle of mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions. i would point out that on 30 november 2009 the council adopted a roadmap for strengthening the procedural rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, calling for measures to be taken on the right to translation and interpretation, to receive information on rights and on the charge, to receive legal advice and assistance and to communicate easily with family members, employers and consular authorities. i am in favour of this amendment to the directive because i believe that those involved in judicial proceedings should have the right to be equally protected and to receive special support if they are outside their country of origin, thus allowing for close monitoring by the authorities.
in writing. - this report deserved our support because it defends the right of all suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, whether or not they have been deprived of their liberty, to have access to a lawyer in good time, so as to enable the person concerned to exercise his right of defence. in addition, member states shall ensure that suspects or accused persons deprived of liberty have the right to communicate without delay with a third person, such as a family member designated by them, or to be visited by their consular authorities, the right to speak and correspond with them and to obtain legal representation through them. this is a set of fundamental rights which are enshrined in this proposal and which deserve our full support. however, we cannot fail to stress that these rights could be enshrined by strengthening cooperation between states, without resorting to supranationalization of the central aspects of justice, in particular through the european arrest warrant, by removing them from the sovereignty of states and their duty to safeguard the rights of their citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report as this directive is the first european legislation in the area of bank loans for house purchase and the first legal text on financial reform focused on the retail banking product. housing loans are the most important financial commitment in the lives of european households and this market represents 52% of the gdp of the european union. the agreement reached by the council will help to revive the economies of many member states, while avoiding the irresponsible bank lending for housing that was at the root of the last crisis. in addition, in my view, this directive sets out the path and principles for a thorough reform of the european bank housing loan market to be implemented by the member states over the next two years.
in writing. the european parliament's report sets out new rules for the housing mortgage market, with the aim of ensuring greater transparency for all citizens who wish to buy a house with bank credit. given the high indebtedness of households, this legislation will help to combat this chronic problem. the new legislation aims to ensure that consumers do not take on risks to which they will not be able to respond appropriately. in this sense, from now on, anyone who wants to buy a house will get detailed information on the conditions of the loan to be acquired, with impartial advice on credit conditions, a cooling-off period, as well as a long-term analysis of the sustainability and solvency of the bond. in the event of default, the debtor will have more guarantees that his income is not fully seized in order to maintain a decent life, and the possibility of surrendering the property for full settlement of his obligations to the bank is ensured, if the parties so agree in advance. in view of the benefits and protection which this new law will bring to portuguese families, i support this report.
in writing. − this european parliament report aims to approve new rules for the housing mortgage market, with the aim of ensuring greater transparency for all citizens who intend to buy a house using bank credit. given the high indebtedness of households, this legislation could help to combat this chronic problem, one of the causes of the current crisis. the new legislation aims to ensure that consumers do not take on risks to which they will not be able to respond appropriately. in this sense, from now on, anyone who wants to buy a house will receive detailed information on the conditions of the loan to be acquired, with impartial advice on the credit conditions, a cooling-off period, as well as a long-term analysis of the sustainability and solvency of the bond. in the event of default, the debtor will have more guarantees that his income is not fully seized in order to maintain a decent life, and the possibility of surrendering the property for full settlement of his obligations to the bank is ensured, if the parties so agree in advance. in view of the benefits and protection which this new law will bring to portuguese families, i support this report.
in writing. − this directive seeks to improve the rules on credit agreements for the purchase of residential immovable property in order to make them fairer and more transparent for the contracting parties, in particular for the debtors. in portugal, 82% of credit granted to private individuals is for the purchase of residential property and since 2008 there has been an increase in bad debt in this same sector. the european parliament has therefore introduced new rules aimed at giving private individuals greater protection in this type of contract, in particular the prohibition of such contracts being dependent on the purchase of other insurance or financial products from the same bank, the possibility, by agreement, of the property covered by the contract being sufficient collateral for the payment of the loan and the termination of the contract, a period of at least 7 days for the debtor to reflect on accepting the contract, among others. the market for credit for house purchase, given its importance for households, should be properly regulated and transparent, allowing for a truly informed choice that reflects households' ability to pay.
in writing. - this proposal aims to limit the risks involved in buying a house, to better inform the consumer before the contract is concluded and to avoid the irresponsible granting and taking of loans which were one of the causes of the financial crisis. mortgages are often the most important long-term financial commitment a family makes. in 2009, mortgage lending accounted for 52.3% of eu gdp. the aim is to ensure that consumers are better informed about the risks and costs of taking out a mortgage before buying a house and are better protected in the event of non-payment. the new provisions also strengthen the transparency requirements on floating rate and foreign currency loans. lenders will have to provide clear and comprehensible general information on credit agreements, for example the range of different options available for repayment of the credit and any consequences of default. the consumer will be entitled to a seven-day cooling-off period before signing the mortgage contract, so that he can compare offers, assess their implications and make an informed decision. after the conclusion of the contract, you will also have a seven-day period for exercising the right of termination.
in writing. - this report seeks to introduce greater transparency into the process of granting loans for the purchase of housing, in particular: the provision of clearer, more detailed and properly explained information; an adequate check of the solvency of the individual or a family before credit is granted to them; and the need to properly adjust loan/value ratios, loan/income, debt/income. in essence, the report ends up keeping intact the mechanisms that allow banks to accumulate fabulous profits by extorting individuals and families. the main responsibility for credit problems continues to lie with the borrower, not the lender - the banks, who will continue to control the mechanisms of spreads and interest rates and to operate with impunity. in addition to the problems with credit agreements, there is also a desire to erode the power of the institutions of national sovereignty to define policies for the granting of credit, particularly in public banks, by centralising and harmonising these decisions, while also continuing the policies of replacing wages by credit. these are policies and guidelines that do not guarantee the fundamental right to housing as established by the constitution of the portuguese republic.
in writing. - with this proposal we are taking the first steps towards the creation of an internal market in mortgage credit. the mortgage market in the eu accounts for almost 50% of gdp, thus revealing its importance. on the other hand, taking out a mortgage is one of the most important financial decisions in anyone's life, involving a financial commitment that may last for decades. it is therefore important to combat irresponsible lending and borrowing in order to avoid a repetition of the conditions that led to the current financial crisis. that is the direction this proposal is going, hence my vote in favour.
in writing. − mortgages are often the most important long-term commitment a family makes. they are essential for access to homeownership (about 70% in the eu) and are of great economic importance. in 2009, mortgage lending amounted to €6 126 billion 52.3% of eu gdp. between 1998 and 2009, the market grew in almost all member states, although due to the crisis, there has been a decline since 2008. i voted in favour of this report which seeks to regulate mortgage markets in the eu to ensure that, before buying a house, consumers are better informed about the risks and costs of taking out a mortgage and better protected in the event of non-payment. the new provisions also strengthen the transparency requirements on floating rate and foreign currency loans. lenders will have to provide clear and comprehensible general information on credit agreements, for example the range of different options available for repayment of the credit and any consequences of default.

in writing. − the current financial crisis has shown the irresponsible behaviour of some market players, which has damaged the foundations of the financial system, creating a certain degree of distrust among all parties, including markets, banks and customers, with serious economic and social consequences. i believe that financial literacy needs to be improved, in particular by providing more and better information on the interest rates that are available to citizens, the exchange rate risks involved in transactions or changes in the economic climate that ultimately harm the businesses concerned. i support this report in its efforts to improve the conditions for the establishment and functioning of the internal market by approximating the laws of the member states and by creating new standards for certain services. finally, i believe that it is essential that a system of good practice be adopted between the different member states and financial institutions so that the information made available to customers is always better.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, considering that under the new rules aimed at combating insider dealing and market manipulation, the same requirements will be imposed on all member states which must ensure uniform market conditions and investor protection in the european union. i think this is the beginning of a long journey in european and world financial reform.
in writing. − the abuse of inside information and market manipulation cause many distortions in financial markets, causing instability and putting the functioning of a system at the mercy of private interests, which is deprived of its role in financing the real economy efficiently and fairly. insider trading occurs when someone uses information that is not publicly available to trade for their own benefit or that of another. it can happen when a market maker uses confidential information to buy shares in a company and gain illegitimate gains. this lack of transparency in the market destroys the confidence of economic operators in the market and undermines its functioning. the regulation extends the market abuse control legislation to all instruments traded on over-the-counter markets, multilateral trading facilities and other organised trading facilities. at the same time, it will tighten controls on the flow of information and allow access to information exchanged in the course of investment firms' activities, imposing sanctions on the perpetrators. this will improve investor protection, preserve the integrity of markets and ensure greater control of market manipulation. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − this directive aims to list and delimit what is to be understood as market abuse in financial markets. in particular, from today, criminal authorities will only need to prove that there has been an improper sharing of information, rather than having to prove that there is a direct and explicit link between a particular sharing of information and the effect of it on a particular financial product. another relevant point will be the obligation for all member states to implement a criminal law which is truly coercive in such situations. this directive is part of a series of initiatives which have been taken by the european institutions to better regulate the financial services market and to prevent further economic crises such as those we are still witnessing today.
in writing. − this regulation establishes a common regulatory framework on market abuse in order to ensure the integrity of financial markets in the union and to promote investor confidence in those markets. indeed, a transparent, efficient and integrated financial market requires market integrity. the proper functioning of securities markets and public confidence in markets are essential conditions for economic growth and prosperity. market abuse situations undermine the integrity of financial markets and public confidence in securities and derivatives. market abuse is the umbrella concept of all unlawful behaviour in financial markets and for the purposes of this regulation it should be understood as consisting of insider dealing or insider trading and market manipulation.
in writing. − the current financial crisis has highlighted the importance of a transparent and integrity-based capital market. it is therefore necessary to strengthen financial supervision and regulation and to establish a framework of high standards, agreed at international level. the evaluation of the market abuse directive (mad) currently in force has revealed a number of problems that have had a negative impact on the transparency and integrity of the market. the initiative thus aims to increase market integrity and investor protection, while ensuring a single set of rules and a level playing field and making securities markets more attractive for raising capital. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on insider dealing and market manipulation (market abuse). the proposal for a regulation establishes a specific definition of inside information in respect of emission allowances. the commission considers that the conditions for the use of the financial instrument are met, and that the conditions for the use of the financial instrument are met. the information to be disclosed will normally relate to the physical activity of the reporting party, such as capacity and use of facilities. the european parliament supports the commission's proposal to include emission allowances in the market abuse framework, to ensure that organised trading is always carried out in regulated trading facilities, complying with virtually identical requirements of transparency, organisation and market surveillance.
