in writing. − when an individual has inside information and uses that information to acquire or dispose, for his own account or for the account of a third party, directly or indirectly, of financial instruments to which that information relates, it is considered that there is a change in the normal market rules. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that the abuse of inside information eventually becomes a disruption of the normal functioning of the market and a serious blow to the principle of transparency which should be applied. i believe that measures are needed to deepen the market, since this is essential if europe is to return to a new phase of economic growth, job creation and wealth creation.
in writing. - this proposal does not create the conditions necessary to deal seriously with illicit - in many cases even criminal - behaviour on financial markets. instead of putting an end to the growing financialisation of the economy, the free movement of capital and financial speculation in the capital markets - which are largely responsible for the crisis we are facing - only a few palliatives with limited effect are defined. the proposal excludes from its scope monetary activities and the management of public debt, maintaining this haven which has served speculation and through it the imposition of the destruction of social and labour rights of a civilizational dimension in countries like portugal. it also promises to grant national supervisory authorities a number of discretionary rights, such as access to private premises and the seizure of documents and records of electronic communications, data transmission and telephone conversations, both of investment firms and of communications operators, excluding such validation activities by entities, including judicial entities, which verify the objectivity of their justification and the good faith with which they are conducted. it sets out as one of its methods of investigating these illicit activities the use of internal whistleblowers from the organisations to which it proposes to pay incentives. the notorious buffoons are paid for their activity.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, considering that the adoption of a basic regulation will have a direct impact on the use of technical measures in the baltic sea, the straits and the oresund and will bring about significant changes to the regulation under discussion. proposing such amendments at this stage raises the risk that these amendments will not be in line with the provisions of the basic regulation. however, we believe that the commission should propose new and amended regulations on the use of technical measures in the baltic sea, the straits and the sound.
in writing. − the need to bring existing legislation into line with the lisbon treaty's dictates as to the type of acts to be adopted by the european commission has led to several changes to these diplomas. council regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 did not escape this rule. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a regulation on the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. i consider this a prudent approach and one which seeks to facilitate the achievement of possible consensus in the important debates on a subject of such importance to the member states as fisheries and the conservation of fishery resources.
in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 of 21 december 2005 on the conservation of fishery resources in the baltic sea and the great belt, small belt and øresund straits through the application of technical measures confers on the commission powers to implement some of its provisions. following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the powers conferred on the commission by regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 should be aligned with articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. implementing powers should be conferred on the commission in order to ensure uniform conditions for the implementation of regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 as regards measures adopted by member states applying exclusively to fishing vessels flying their flag. the powers to adopt detailed rules for the implementation of regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 are no longer necessary. the provision conferring such powers should therefore be deleted. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 lays down certain technical measures for the conservation of fishery resources in the waters of the baltic sea and the great belt, small belt and øresund straits. that regulation provides, inter alia, for specific provisions on the size and type of all components of fishing gear, including the mesh. the commission proposal aims to align this regulation with articles 290 and 291 tfeu, concerning delegated and implementing acts. it proposes the introduction of delegated acts in the following areas: to amend the rules on the construction of certain gears, such amendments to reflect changes in the standards of selectivity of fishing, new technical knowledge in construction materials or modifications in gear fittings that may increase the selectivity of gears. furthermore, implementing powers are conferred on the commission in order to ensure uniform conditions for the application of regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 as regards measures taken by member states applying only to fishing vessels flying their flag. the rapporteur, giving his general agreement to the commission's proposal, proposes that the delegation of powers to the commission should be limited in time.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal from the european parliament and the council amending council regulation (ec) no 2187/2005. however, i would point out that since 2010 the commission has had the opportunity to use the delegation of power provided for in article 290 tfeu in several of its proposals for regulations and directives. in this way, a number of delegated acts have already been adopted. i think it is time to examine the use of this procedure and draw conclusions about the way in which the monitoring system has worked, so as to prevent or correct any excesses or abuses which might obstruct the democratic rules of the community of law which is the european union.
in writing. - the purpose of this report is to review council regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 on the conservation of fishery resources through the application of technical measures in the baltic sea, its straits (belts) and the sound, in view of the need to align it with the new comitology established under the lisbon treaty. the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) establishes a new regulatory hierarchy consisting of three distinct levels of acts, namely legislative acts, delegated acts and implementing acts. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover the transport of dangerous goods by road. i voted in favour of the report because i agree with most of the amendments to this regulation.
in writing. − the numerous disputes surrounding the application of the regulation at hand compel the rapporteur to propose a new draft regulation which is profoundly amended, the effectiveness of the measures defined being reviewed in order to ensure their full compatibility with regulation (ec) no 2187/2005. however, at this stage, when the commission, parliament and council are still negotiating the future of the common fisheries policy, it would be unwise to go beyond the normal process of adapting the rules to the changes required by the treaty of lisbon. the rapporteur therefore accepts the proposal to align the regulation on the conservation of fishery resources in the baltic sea by replacing the current council decisions with implementing decisions, while introducing a provision on the need for the commission to propose a new draft regulation to control the use of technical measures. in considering the advantages of giving the eu the possibility to react quickly to the application of measures in accordance with the directives, by means of implementing acts provided for in the lisbon treaty, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the purpose of this document is to align council regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 on the conservation of fishery resources in the baltic sea and its straits (the belts) and the øresund by means of technical measures with the new rules of the treaty on the functioning of the european union as regards delegated and implementing acts. the adoption of a new regulation on the common fisheries policy will have a direct impact on the use of technical measures in the waters of the baltic sea, its straits and the sound, which will require further adaptations of the regulation on this area. the rapporteur, however, considered it premature to move forward with such changes at this stage. for the reasons given, i voted in favour of the document in parliament.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which calls for the need for a complete integration and interconnection of the energy market, in order to reduce costs and focus on renewable energy and energy efficiency and smart buildings. in my view, a stronger european internal energy market will result in security of supply, lower energy costs for consumers and industry and, in the end, contribute to a more sustainable economy. in my view, it is up to the member states to implement it fully on the ground.
in writing. − an open, competitive, integrated and flexible european energy market will maintain security of supply and achieve lower and more transparent prices, improving european competitiveness and contributing to economic growth and consumer welfare. end-users are at the heart of the internal energy market and must be adequately protected and informed through facilitated access to information in order to enable them to fully exercise their rights and to encourage them to play a more active role in stimulating market competitiveness. the lack of full implementation of legislation relating to the internal energy market remains one of the main obstacles to the completion of this market. in this regard, member states should fully transpose and implement all relevant eu legislation, in particular the third energy package, as soon as possible, and the european commission should take action against member states where implementation has been unduly delayed. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i welcome the principles included in the buzek report of creating an integrated, open, well-regulated and competitive internal energy market. an integrated internal market, together with investment in science and research to develop new technologies, will ensure clean, cheap and affordable energy for all european citizens. affordable energy for all is a key objective for the competitiveness of european industry and for the well-being of people.
in writing. − sustainable growth without undermining competitiveness requires a consistent energy policy, the proper functioning of the internal energy market and the development of national projects that contribute to the community's objectives of reducing emissions and increasing energy independence and clean energy production. the proper functioning of the internal market, which is more open and transparent, has the potential to maintain security of supply and lower prices for consumers.
in writing. − member states have committed themselves to meeting the deadlines for the full completion of the internal energy market by 2014 and for the abolition of energy islands in the eu by 2015. indeed, a completed internal energy market is indispensable for the union's energy security and sustainability and is also key to competitiveness, economic growth and job creation in the union. the aim is to improve coordination and cooperation of energy policies between member states in a spirit of solidarity and to create efficient and secure cross-border energy systems, which will represent a major european added value. there is no doubt that the development of domestic resources will give rise to new trading platforms in the eu, as well as to the spot markets for gas and electricity, which represents a real opportunity for the eu and the member states to determine their own energy prices, including at regional and local level.
in the case of the commission, the commission has already taken the initiative in the form of a report on the implementation of the directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. the liberal and commercial propaganda is here explained to the last detail in defence of the implementation of the third energy package. the wonders of liberalization, of sacrosanct free competition and competitiveness - always propagated and always, but always denied by reality - are repeated to the point of nausea. but who is celebrating, who is benefiting and has always benefited from the privatization of public energy services? it was not the workers, it was not the small and medium-sized enterprises, it was not the households, who were dealing with substantial increases in their energy bills. it was the large economic groups that came to dominate the sector, it was the large transnational monopolies that accumulate enormous profits at the expense of a service that should be public and serve the real interests of the people. we voted against it, of course.
in writing. − the european internal energy market and the respective national energy markets must be competitive and offer genuine choice and transparent information to all consumers, who play a central role in the energy market. the completion of the internal energy market is also essential to reduce energy prices and costs and to achieve affordable and competitive prices in the short, medium and long term. there can be european added value through better coordination and cooperation of energy policies between member states in a spirit of solidarity and through the creation of efficient and secure cross-border energy systems, thus generating synergies through better management of energy supply and demand, facilitated by smart technologies at the distribution system level. the internal energy market must function properly if final consumers are to derive the greatest benefit from it. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the buzek report on the internal energy market because there can be no single european market without an integrated energy market, given the importance of energy. only an internal energy market can guarantee access to energy for eu businesses and citizens on equal terms throughout the union. for the union to fully achieve these objectives, it is essential to ensure the completion and deployment of fully connected cross-border energy networks and efficient energy transmission infrastructures that eradicate energy islands in the eu. this applies from the outset to the iberian peninsula and to cross-border energy connections. the eu should explore the possibility of creating a european investment fund, as proposed in the report, financed by a compulsory contribution from energy consumption, a point which, however, did not receive the necessary majority. the single energy market requires direct involvement of the union and sources of own financing.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this own-initiative report on the functioning of the internal energy market because i agree with most of its premises. an open, competitive, integrated and flexible european energy market will maintain security of supply and lower and more transparent prices, enhance european competitiveness and contribute to economic growth and consumer welfare, and it is therefore urgent to remove the remaining physical, regulatory and administrative barriers that hinder the open and efficient functioning of the market. however, only a stable regulatory framework will be able to attract the investments needed for the continued development of this market.
in writing. − considering how essential the completion of the internal energy market is for the union's energy security and sustainability, the roadmap outlines an energy policy based on three fundamental pillars: reducing dependence on fossil fuel imports, which exposes countries to the market power of their sole supplier, whose pricing policy does not always follow a market logic; promoting energy efficiency, including the modernisation of the distribution network, fully integrated in a european context, and intelligent cross-border; and investing in technology and innovation, leading to the development of cheaper, more effective and simpler technologies. to this end, it is imperative to make sufficient funding available for the development of the internal market, whether through the use of regional development funds, cohesion funds or other structural funds to help with future energy and climate challenges. northern and eastern europe are dependent on gas imports from a single source, the member states remain an energy island due to insufficient infrastructure links with the rest of europe, and investment in the energy sector is at historically low levels. i voted in favour.
in writing. − an internal energy market is only possible if member states fully transpose and implement union legislation, in particular the third energy package. the report calls for the union and the member states to take a stand to make this market more transparent, competitive, easy to manage and to offer european citizens a free choice and competitive prices. the union must also take account of the outermost regions, which, as islands, are cut off from the rest of europe by gas and electricity networks. for this reason, consumers pay a higher price for the same access. a more effective effort and coordination by the union, the member states and third countries is therefore needed for a genuine internal energy market.

in writing. − energy efficiency, a key priority for the european commission and the member states, is at the heart of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, with one of its objectives being to increase energy efficiency by 20%. reducing consumption through energy efficiency is the most sustainable way to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, leading to a reduction in imports of around 25%. thus, local and regional authorities must be given appropriate powers and responsibilities, not only in relation to energy supply and use, but also in relation to the achievement of energy efficiency objectives. member states should introduce simple and non-bureaucratic procedures in their operational programmes for the use of funds intended to improve energy efficiency in households. they should also share best practices in designing national energy efficiency funds, where european structural and investment funds can be used as capital contributions. the european commission should continue to improve the quality and dissemination of practical information on energy efficiency available to local and regional authorities. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − in a region of the world with a large energy deficit, the issue of energy efficiency is of strategic importance and cannot therefore fail to be seriously considered by european and national policy-makers. the energy available to the union should be used prudently and efficiently in order to prevent and prevent, as far as technically possible, its waste and misuse. europe's potential for energy efficiency is not being realised. energy efficiency measures under cohesion policy have not had a uniform effect throughout the union and are far from being considered an absolute success. the commission has therefore decided to continue with the work already started and to maintain and strengthen the energy efficiency measures under this policy. national, regional and local authorities, as well as businesses and citizens' groups, must be actively involved in this challenge for all.
in writing. − at the heart of the eu strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, the benefits of energy efficiency have long been recognised in the eu. however, the eu faces a huge challenge in meeting its target of reducing total energy consumption by 20% by 2020, in which policies to promote energy efficiency can and should play a more decisive role. energy efficiency requires the use of fewer means of energy production for an equivalent level of service or economic activity. reducing consumption through energy efficiency is the most sustainable way to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, thus leading to a reduction in imports of around 25%. the european structural and investment funds should contribute to encouraging private investment in energy-efficient products, transport modes, buildings, industries, works and services, and can also help to reduce the costs of energy bills for public authorities and allow for a more efficient use of public resources.
in writing. − the eu strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth is very important and the benefits of energy efficiency have long been recognised in the eu. the challenge to meet its target of reducing total energy consumption by 20% by 2020 is great, in which policies to promote energy efficiency can and should play a more active role. improvements in energy efficiency are crucial for europe's competitiveness and a win-win option in the fight against climate change. investment in energy efficiency measures can bring immediate and tangible benefits to households and businesses, such as cost reductions, the creation of employment and growth opportunities, and an incentive to transition to a low-carbon economy. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. − the aim of this report is to promote the development of a new european union strategy for fisheries and aquaculture in the adriatic and ionian seas basin, with the aim of substantially boosting the development of sustainable economic activities with positive effects on coastal communities and inland border areas. the adriatic and ionian seas constitute an important maritime zone covering seven countries: four member states (italy, greece, slovenia and croatia), one candidate country (montenegro) and two potential candidate countries (albania and bosnia and herzegovina). although there have always been strong economic and social relations between these countries - now strengthened by the eu accession process - the adriatic and ionian area has remained economically, environmentally and culturally heterogeneous. riverside countries currently share many resources, including fisheries resources, and therefore face a number of challenges directly or indirectly linked to the development of the fisheries and aquaculture sector, such as sea pollution, coastal erosion, differences in economic development of coastal areas and increasing urbanisation. there must be a joint effort to develop a common strategy for fisheries in the adriatic and ionian seas.
in writing. - the aim of this report is to promote a new european union strategy for fisheries and aquaculture in the adriatic and ionian sea basins, which will substantially boost the development of sustainable activities with positive impacts on the coastal communities of these sea basins. this important maritime zone encompasses seven countries with strong social and economic links, although with considerable environmental, cultural, social and economic heterogeneity. this group of countries shares a range of resources and faces similar challenges in their fisheries and aquaculture sectors, which makes it absolutely vital to foster international cooperation between neighbouring countries to promote sustainable exploitation and joint and coherent management of fisheries and aquaculture activities. the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against fraud and for the commission to be able to take action to combat fraud. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the measures proposed can promote a balanced and sustainable development of fisheries and aquaculture activities in this important geographical area.
in writing. − with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the european parliament has become a full-fledged co-legislator for the fisheries and aquaculture sector and therefore intends to play its role in defining the new eu macro-regional strategy for fisheries and aquaculture in the adriatic and ionian seas. the objective is to promote the development of sustainable and responsible economic activities whose beneficial effect does not compromise the protection of fishery resources and the specific geomorphological and bathymetric characteristics of the adriatic-ionian basin. although there are some examples of good interregional cooperation (such as the establishment of special zones), much of the adriatic sea basin remains part of international waters, which determines the need for closer cooperation with neighbouring countries with a view to concluding bilateral and multilateral agreements, which will advance the harmonization and standardisation of fisheries management rules. in this respect, my vote supports parliament's report on the strategy for fisheries in the adriatic and ionian seas and calls on the commission to promote the measures envisaged.

in writing. − one of the main aims of this report is to raise awareness of the need to improve the efficiency of multilingualism, without compromising the overall quality and without calling into question the right of members to use in parliament the official language of their choice. the european union (eu) is the only entity in the world to have an official multilingualism policy based on 24 official languages. in 2011, there were 5263 days of sitting and approximately 100 000 days of interpreting, of which 47,74% were provided by external interpreters and 52,26% by actual interpreters. parliament's interpretation service is of a high quality. despite the measures taken by the bureau in the context of full multilingualism in interpreting with efficient use of resources, costs remain considerable and resources are not always used efficiently. in 2010, an amount of eur 6,05 million was made available, which was not used due to late cancellations. the commission notes that the aid granted to the beneficiary was limited to the minimum necessary to cover the costs of the project. over the past three years, €15.93 million was wasted due to late applications and cancellations.
in writing. - this report is intended to strike a further blow at the principle of multilingualism. in addition to the cuts made in previous years (in this year's budget they were over 20%) they advocate further cuts in the future, even with the addition of an official language, with the entry of croatia, and taking into account the additional costs that this entails. as always, the cuts are justified on the pretext of increasing the efficiency of interpretation services. the effects of the cuts already made in the quality and scope of services and in the limitation of the right of members to express themselves and to work in their mother tongue are ignored. there are already clear shortcomings in interpretation services, such as the absence of interpretation for some languages in committee and delegation meetings where the respective members are present, or in numerous working meetings such as meetings of shadow rapporteurs and others. this report also sets out the way forward for the promotion of precarious employment among interpreters, putting their jobs and their rights at risk. this is unacceptable. for these reasons we voted against.

in writing. − online gambling is one of the fastest growing service activities in the eu, with annual rates of almost 15% and an estimated annual revenue of €13 billion by 2015. it continues to develop in parallel with the rapid evolution of online technologies. the online gambling sector differs from other markets due to the risks involved in terms of consumer protection and the fight against organised crime, as recognised on several occasions by the court of justice of the european union. in this regard, it is recommended that common uniform and pan-european security standards be established for electronic identification and cross-border electronic verification services. strengthen the exchange of best practices between member states on enforcement measures, the development of secure and traceable payment solutions, and consider the feasibility of measures to block financial transactions to ensure that consumers do not fall into the hands of illegal operators. operators should also warn minors on their websites - in a clear and unambiguous manner and in prominent characters - that their participation in online gambling is illegal. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - the online gambling market is growing steadily and, although its turnover is in the millions, it is still largely unregulated, with all the dangers this poses to consumers. this is therefore an area which lacks attention and self-regulation. however, in line with what is advocated by the vast majority of states, the powers in the field of gambling should remain with the member states, and the eu may establish guidelines and guidance in respect of the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. − gambling is not a normal economic activity because of its potentially negative social and health impacts, notably compulsive gambling, the impact and costs of which are difficult to quantify. gambling can be highly addictive and should therefore be addressed in the legislative proposal for the benefit of consumers and the integrity of this sport. online gambling may pose a higher risk of addiction than traditional face-to-face gambling, in particular due to easier access and the absence of social control, although further research and data are needed in this area. a high level of consumer protection, in particular for the most vulnerable, needs to be ensured. in addition, the provision of gambling services defined by each member state has to comply with union law in order to reduce the social costs and harmful effects of gambling activities. the commission and the member states should take action against illegal gambling services. in this context, member states are called upon to take repressive measures against illegal gambling offers.
in writing. - this report expresses concerns which we believe are justified with regard to online gaming. the commission has already stressed that these can lead to serious gambling addiction problems; it has stressed that access to these types of games is easier, particularly for young people; and it has pointed out that they can be used as a means of money laundering. we follow these concerns and some of the solutions that are proposed, such as the right of any customer to self-exclude from all dealers; the need for greater regulation of advertising; and the obligation for all companies providing these services to register as authorised entities in the eu. we do not share some of the report's views on the internal market. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules on gambling are respected.

on behalf of the green group in the european parliament madam president, commissioner, there is no harder statistic on what is happening to young people in europe at the moment than the asymmetry between certain countries where half the young people are unemployed and the other half in precarious, poor quality underemployment and countries like germany where less than 10% of the young people are unemployed. this means that we are experiencing a supranational crisis that is cutting our continent in half and to which, for the most part, our states have been trying to give national answers. that is not the right way of responding to this crisis, as commissioner andor has stressed on several occasions. we need a community response more than an intergovernmental response, which is what we are still talking about. the funding we have from the multiannual financial framework is affected by this. countries basically want to use only funds that were already allocated for other purposes and we ended up with a funding of 6 billion euros for 7 years which is clearly insufficient for the needs of economic recovery, in particular in the youth sector. we are also pursuing policies which are aggravating the problem, such as austerity policies in the southern countries. if we want austerity not to be stupid austerity, it is essential that the commission, the european central bank, the troika institutions and eurostat itself stop considering certain expenditure - investment in education or youth - as expenditure which is equivalent to others. we can't stop this spending. the result of the cuts in these areas, we've been seeing in countries like mine, portugal, young people are emigrating en masse to brazil, to angola, to many other countries and many of these young people don't return, making us lose decades of investment. europe, finally, also has a serious problem with its higher education. if you look at the latest shanghai ranking of world universities, in the top 50 there are very few universities from the european union and very few from the eurozone, and here i want to say something very clearly to our colleagues from the epp: it is very sad that you have come here crying crocodile tears because of the situation of young people, but when it was necessary to choose between a report on education and another on gastronomy, the epp colleagues chose the report on gastronomy and that also means that there is a huge hypocrisy in this debate.
the question is why has unemployment increased exponentially in the european union since the start of the crisis? because the nature of this crisis is the system itself, the capitalist system, it's a crisis of overproduction and overaccumulation and the system is trying to ensure capital accumulation by deliberately destroying jobs that also allow for greater exploitation of workers and by transferring wealth directly from the pockets of workers to the banks. unemployment is not accidental. the european semester, economic governance, the policies of the european union, the european commission, through the troika, are policies that advocate more or less covertly the promotion of unemployment, the reduction of wage values and the withdrawal of social and labour rights. that is the problem with this parliament. it is not worth trying to defend job creation when policies are being adopted which lead to the daily and massive destruction of jobs, policies which put young people in the dramatic situation they are in today. we are not opposed to a european youth guarantee or a similar mechanism, but we will never support a model which replaces actual work and which acts as a mechanism for companies to confuse the labour factor. young people have the right to decent, quality work, which will enable them to build their life projects in safety, but as long as there is no structural break with the economic policies which are the answer of capitalism, therefore the european union's response to this crisis, unemployment will continue to grow and this discussion will be only an ironic discussion of appearances, with no concrete results in the lives of young people.
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to thank my fellow rapporteur for her good work in tackling this very important and serious issue - youth unemployment in the european union - which has reached alarming levels, with six million young people out of work and more than seven and a half million young people not in work, education or training. southern europe is being particularly hit. in greece and spain more than half the young people are unemployed. in my country, portugal, the youth unemployment rate remains above 37%. youth unemployment has a profound impact on people, society and the economy. we cannot therefore resign ourselves to the fact that the most qualified generation is always being excluded and not allowed to participate in the economic growth that europe so badly needs. we cannot abandon our young people and we cannot waste our human resources and our talents. we can't afford to lose this generation. the situation calls for a swift response by the european union. i therefore welcome the plan to combat youth unemployment, which must be implemented with great political vigour and adequate financial means. i would stress the youth guarantee so that all young people up to the age of 30 who are not in education, employment or training can return to work or to education or training within four months. i also stress the reform of the eures portal to support mobility in the union and the creation of a quality framework for traineeships and the apprenticeship alliance to facilitate the transition from education to work. in addition, education systems in the member states need to be more agile in filling gaps and anticipating labour market needs in terms of skills.
mr president, the management of the european eel population faces an unavoidable difficulty: the enormous scarcity of scientific data to support such management. a problem which is aggravated by the shortage of recruitment for this species in several important countries, such as portugal, whose public research institutions with responsibilities in this field are suffocated and almost paralysed. in this context, it is of little use to produce demanding regulations if they are not accompanied by the financial resources to implement the necessary measures. the threat factors to the eel are diverse. all must be considered and guarded. the fishermen cannot be the only ones to pay the costs of the urgent recovery of this species. the illegal fishing of hake, stimulated by the uneven european framework currently in place, places a very strong strain on the resource. it is this phase, the younger phase, rather than a possible ban on fishing for yellow or silver eel, which in our view is not justified. it is the stage of the movement that should be the focus of concern and action.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament. the internal market has been achieved in other areas, or, to put it another way, we have crushed the weakest productive systems and conquered their markets, particularly in the peripheral countries, in several other areas of economic activity, and the major european economic groups have long wanted to take over the services sector as well. the rapporteur recalls that this amounts to 70% of the gdp of all the countries of the european union. they also want to promote in this sector the monopolistic concentration which always results from free capitalist competition in the single market. they want to promote competition among workers by forcing the general devaluation of the workforce, the attack on rights and wages. on this path they face some difficulties. difficulties that force them to moderate their pace and even force some retreats. it is worth remembering that it was because of the services directive that in 2006 there were great demonstrations in several european countries that culminated in large european demonstrations. demonstrations rejecting the opening to the market of areas where historically the states have exercised their social function through public services. demonstrations that have had to face, and will have to face in the future, refusing to dismantle public services, a civilizational achievement of the people and that are now attacking to provide good business for some large economic groups at the expense of rights, progress and social justice.
he asks under the blue card procedure. mr reul and president barroso forgot to measure the state of the union by the growth of inequality between rich and poor countries and between rich and poor citizens in each member state. what does mr reul have to say to the german citizens who are going to vote this month, very concerned about what they are spending on the bailed-out countries, while germany is gaining on loans and has even saved 41 billion euros on low or negative interest rates, while the bailed-out countries are financing themselves at exorbitant interest rates and their public debt keeps growing? what do you think the greek, portuguese, irish and spanish citizens think of this blatant denial of what the euro and the union should be?
mr president, mr president of the commission, i would also like to welcome the lithuanian presidency, as this is the first occasion that i have had to be in contact with the lithuanian presidency of the council. mr president, i would like to say at this point, which is the time before the elections to the european parliament, when there is a state of the union address, that as a portuguese and as a member of the epp, i am proud of the work that the commission has done and, in particular, of the presidency that dr durão barroso has had here over these ten years, and in particular also over these five years. a non-arrogant pride, just like the one you have defined here that we europeans should have. i just wanted to make two points. firstly, what i think is fundamental for this commission to leave as a legacy is the idea that there should be more solidarity and more cohesion. i think that at the moment the countries which are in economic and financial crisis, particularly the peripheral countries and the countries of southern europe, have set an example of great determination in carrying out structural reforms and need signs of cohesion from the european union and the strongest countries in the european union. and so it is essential that this line be followed. and the second point i would like to make here, which for me is a great source of hope and should be a great goal for the future: the european union is a serious partner of the united states. i think that the example that the syrian case gives us is also an example of the strengthening of western values. when the solution we have to choose between dictatorship and terrorism, western values are reinforced, and therefore a serious economic partnership, opening markets with the united states, reviving the centrality of the atlantic, i think it is the project that can also revive european solidarity.
the economic and financial crisis that has hit the world has put the european institutions at the centre of the solution to the crisis. economic integration has since become a pillar of the eu2020 strategy and member states are now closer on economic, monetary and financial policies. despite some progress in economic growth in the european countries, we are facing a huge social crisis with 26 million unemployed, the vast majority of them young people with qualifications. we cannot ask for more without creating a framework for future growth. it is therefore urgent to approve the next multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, as this will be the source of investment for many european regions. we must support and facilitate access to european finance for smes, the basis of the european market. we must complete the banking union so that we have preventive and corrective measures for a future crisis like the one we are experiencing today. we want more europe where there is added value. we want more solidarity when situations are negative for some member states and positive for others. a political union which makes the decision-making and institutional process faster and more effective.
the president of the european commission has tried to mythologise the european union project in a somewhat triumphant tone, proclaiming the union's project and values, the heroic way it has stood up to adversity and the need to defend it. but why do we have to defend it? why is the eu a vehicle for ensuring people's rights and a life of dignity? no, on the contrary. we must defend it because it is the european union. a common project in barroso's rhetoric, a project of creating inequality in the daily reality of workers. barroso's speech was thus devoid of concrete content and heavy on abstract mystifications that are far, far away from the real world. barroso also bet on the argument that change is here, the signs of economic recovery are finally appearing after our efforts. portugal has been an example - growth returned to the country after a series of negative quarters. the portuguese economy, as we know, has not grown, what has happened is that the pace of the recession has slowed down slightly and circumstantially. the portuguese are living through a real social drama, with the prospect of worsening through the already announced measures of redundancies and pension cuts. but barroso's rhetorical demagogy ignores the concrete.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, taking into account that there is a growing number of languages at risk of extinction, and that there is a need to assess the situation of these languages to raise awareness at european level of the implications of their disappearance and the need to reactivate them in order to prevent their disappearance and preserve their richness in our society. in my view, the promotion of the union's languages, as well as those at risk of extinction, is a vital challenge that europe must face for a real future, in order to promote its wealth and attract new customers around its heritage, especially among the younger generations.
in writing. - linguistic and cultural diversity is one of the basic principles of the european union, enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights which states that the union will respect cultural, religious and linguistic diversity. endangered languages should be understood as an integral part of europe's cultural heritage and not as a vehicle for political, ethnic or territorial aspirations. all languages, including endangered languages, reflect historical, social and cultural knowledge and expertise. in this regard, member states that have not yet done so should ratify and implement the european charter for regional or minority languages, pay increased attention to and support the pursuit of higher education and research, with particular emphasis on endangered languages. the european commission should propose concrete measures for the protection of endangered languages and support research into the acquisition and revitalization of endangered languages. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that all languages, including those threatened with extinction, reflect historical, social and cultural knowledge and skills, as well as a mentality and a kind of creativity that are part of the richness and diversity of the european union and the basis of european identity. i therefore believe that linguistic diversity and the presence of endangered languages in a country should be seen as an asset, not a burden, and should be supported and promoted.
in writing. − linguistic diversity is part of europe's heritage and as such must be preserved and promoted. all people have the inalienable right to speak their own language and each is a separate set of historical, social and cultural knowledge as well as a human experience. however, a large number of the languages spoken in europe are seriously endangered and some of them may disappear in this century. a language may be endangered for a number of reasons, including the difficulty of transmitting the language between generations, the reduction in the number of speakers or the fact that a language is confined to a small and/or remote geographical area. that is why i am in favour of all european languages being used, preserved and promoted, as is done in this house.
in writing. - linguistic and cultural diversity is one of the basic principles of the european union, enshrined in article 22 of the charter of fundamental rights, which states that the union shall respect cultural, religious and linguistic diversity. all european languages are equal in value and dignity and are an integral part of their respective cultures and civilizations, contributing to the enrichment of humanity. cohesive multilingual societies that manage their linguistic diversity in a democratic and sustainable way contribute to plurality, are more open and have better conditions to integrate the richness represented by linguistic diversity. all languages, including those threatened with extinction, reflect historical, social and cultural knowledge and skills, as well as a mentality and a type of creativity, which are part of the richness and diversity of the european union and the basis of european identity. i therefore support this report and call on the european union and the member states to become more aware of the extreme threat to the future of many of europe's languages, which are classed as endangered, and to commit themselves vigorously to the creation of a policy to safeguard and promote the unique diversity of the union's linguistic and cultural heritage.
in writing. - the lisbon treaty reinforced the objective of safeguarding and promoting the cultural and linguistic heritage of the european union in all its diversity. the european union and the member states should therefore be aware of the real threat to the future of many of europe's languages, which are classified as endangered, and should be actively engaged in creating a policy to safeguard and promote the unique diversity of the union's linguistic and cultural heritage. ambitious policies for the proactive revitalisation of these languages should thus be supported, with a reasonable budget allocated to this end. it was important that member states develop action plans for the defence of endangered languages based on the exchange of good practices already existing in a number of linguistic communities in europe. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on endangered european languages and linguistic diversity in the european union. the notion of linguistic diversity in the european union covers both official and co-official languages, regional languages and languages not officially recognised by the member states. this report draws the attention of the governments and regional authorities of the member states to the fact that the survival of an endangered language is a pre-requisite for the survival and development of the community which uses it and that, therefore, in formulating policies for its safeguarding, account should be taken not only of the cultural and educational aspects but also of the economic and social dimensions.

in writing. − we welcome the recognition that all european languages are equal in value and dignity and that they are an integral part of their respective cultures and civilizations, contributing to the enrichment of the human being. we also support the view that all languages, including those threatened with extinction, reflect historical, social and cultural knowledge and expertise. when we say that speaking is how we understand each other, what we mean is that it is with language that we build or deconstruct ourselves - as individuals, as communities or as peoples. we know that language has often established itself as a fundamental pillar of resistance to various forms of oppression. let us remember that the roma people have found in their language an amazing factor of unity and courage that even the concentration camps of nazi-fascism could not crush. we therefore understand that there are no minority languages - there are languages. the disappearance of any one of them makes us all poorer. this is why it is urgent to adopt measures to revitalize the language, accompanied by the necessary funding, in order to reverse the situation where the death of the last speaker of a language usually leads to the extinction of that language.

in writing. − the european environment agency is headed by an executive director who is appointed by the management board on the basis of a list of candidates proposed by the commission following a call for expressions of interest published in the official journal of the european union and other written media or on the internet. the aim of the proposal is to harmonise the procedure for appointing the executive director of the european environment agency with other procedures used in other agencies. the aim is to give the european parliament the formal right to hear the selected candidate, giving him the opportunity to make a statement and then subjecting him to a question period by members. the involvement of the european parliament in the appointment of this post will certainly make the process more democratic, and we are therefore not opposed to what is proposed in this report.

in writing. − amending budget no 4/2013 aims to amend the staffing of the european gnss agency by adding 20 posts, allegedly due to the new tasks entrusted to it, of the eacea executive agency by extending its mandate by adding 15 posts, and of the court of justice by adding 7 posts for the new advocate general of the court. the commission claims that the budgetary impact of the new posts is nil, since the new posts are compensated by equivalent reductions in the commission section. our abstention is justified by our doubts about the political options underlying this decision, in particular the european gnss agency and the practical impacts of devoting more staff to projects such as the global navigation satellite system (gnss), the european version of which is galileo, and which may have implications for the process of militarization of the eu and its link with nato. doubts are all the more justified as the newly created places presuppose the extinction of others whose impact is unknown.

in writing. − the promotion of biofuels has been one of the key elements of eu policy as they not only increase the sustainability of transport but also improve the security of energy supply and support economic development. the amendment to the renewable energy directive aims to minimise the impact of indirect land use change on greenhouse gas emissions. i welcome the agreement reached which supports a gradual transition from conventional to advanced biofuels, provided that technological progress allows it, while minimising the harmful effects on european industry.
in writing. − the renewable energy directive set the objective of achieving an overall 20% share of energy from renewable sources in the eu and a 10% share of this type of energy in the transport sector by 2020. such targets are ambitious but necessary to consolidate greater independence from fossil fuels. today we have adopted a balanced text which, while not undermining the clean energy objectives, does not place too much pressure on european industry.
in writing. − with this vote, the european parliament is arguing that the share of energy from conventional or first generation biofuels, produced from cereals and other starch-rich crops and sugar, oil and other energy crops grown on land, should not exceed 6% of final energy consumption in transport by 2020. the target for 2020 is currently set at 10%. the share of energy from advanced or second-generation biofuels, such as those produced from algae or waste, shall represent at least 2,5% of the final energy consumption in the transport sector in 2020. i am calling for the greenhouse gas emissions resulting from the increasing use of agricultural land for biofuel production to be taken into account.
in writing. − the renewable energy directive set a target of 20% of energy from renewable sources in the eu and 10% of energy from renewable sources in transport by 2020. at the same time, the fuel quality directive sets a binding target of 6% reduction in the greenhouse gas intensity of fuels used in road transport and non-road mobile machinery. these two directives are of the utmost importance if we are to achieve the objectives set for 2020.
in writing. - i voted for the lepage report on amendments to the renewable energy directive to reduce the mandatory quotas for first generation biofuels (produced from food species such as maize) and to favour second generation biofuels (waste, for example), because the regime in force so far has proved to put pressure on food prices and on harmful land use (deforestation and environmental degradation). the promotion of non-fossil fuels cannot sacrifice other, more important values and interests. the need to correct that directive shows the costs and the damage that can be caused by a certain ecological fundamentalism, based more on dogma and fashions than on informed judgement and informed choices.
in writing. − the promotion of biofuels has been one of the key elements of eu energy and climate change policy. the reasons for this are varied and sensitive: biofuels not only increase the sustainability of transport but also improve the security of energy supply and support economic development by creating new sources of income in rural areas. the main driver of its development has been the fight against climate change. on the basis of these assumptions, i voted in favour of the european parliament's legislative resolution of 11 september 2013 on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 98/70/ec on the quality of petrol and diesel fuels and directive 2009/28/ec on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources, in line with the line of the epp group.
in writing. − the europe 2020 strategy aims to have around 20% of the total energy consumed in the european union come from renewable sources, and it should be noted that in the automotive sector this figure should represent at least 10% of final energy consumption. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that it is necessary to diversify renewable energy sources and to focus more and more on different energy sources, as they contribute to greater environmental sustainability and to reducing greenhouse gases. it should also be stressed that the automotive industry must have time to adapt to these changes in the energy sector and that the european investment bank should be particularly important in providing finance for the industrial changes that will need to be developed in the future.
in writing. − member states are obliged to use 10% renewable energy in transport by 2020, coupled with a 6% reduction in ghg emissions, leading to increased demand for biofuels. this increased demand is also translated into increased demand for land, resulting in land use change, including fragile ecosystems, forests, peatlands and grasslands on cultivated land. this phenomenon is called aius. the commission recognises the reality of the aius phenomenon but, instead of proposing the integration of the aius factor in the calculations for reducing greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions, it proposes a 5% limit for biofuels from food crops. it also proposes a rapid switch to advanced biofuels from waste and waste products for which land use change is considered to be nil. data on raw materials for the production of these biofuels are still scarce and there is a backlog of safeguards and sustainability criteria to avoid negative economic and environmental consequences. given that demand can make it more profitable to produce agrofuels than food, the key issue in biofuel production is to advocate for food reserves and food production to be safeguarded.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it aims to protect and increase the species.
in writing. − european eel populations have been declining sharply, raising concerns about the survival of the species and the possibility of measures to reverse this trend. the ones currently in force have not demonstrated the ability to do so. moreover, like other regulations, it must be adapted to the existing provisions of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the many unknowns surrounding this species warn against maximalist solutions and against options that are too soft to protect it properly. attention and continuous monitoring of future developments in this matter and frank collaboration by member states and key players in the sector are recommended.
in writing. − the european eel stock is facing a multitude of problems: overfishing, loss of key habitats, pollution, parasites, changes in ocean currents as a result of global climate change, etc. the latest scientific advice from the international council for the exploration of the sea (ices, 2012) on the european eel is that the state of the stock unit remains critical and urgent action is required. the stock is outside safe biological limits and the current fishing activities are not sustainable. as a consequence of the entry into force of the eel management plans, restocking increased with around 22 million mussel and 10 million yellow-eels mostly used for restocking in 2012 and the landing data of mussel in 2010 and 2011 were higher than in 2009 (wgeel, 2012). despite the widespread and growing use of restocking as a conservation measure, ices (2011) has harshly criticised its effectiveness. we consider it of the utmost importance that the commission should examine the implementation of the restocking measures in order to determine whether or not they have actually contributed to the increase in the biomass of the breeding population of european eel.
in writing. − the conservation of species is one of the eu's major concerns, as this is the only way to maintain a sustainable and economically viable ecosystem. the european eel population is facing a multitude of problems: overfishing, loss of key habitats, pollution, parasites, changes in ocean currents as a result of global climate change, etc. therefore, the solutions are not easy, just as there is no one person in charge. we must therefore find solutions that restore the eel population levels, otherwise the eel will become extinct. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the objective of this report is to review regulation (ec) no 1100/2007 laying down measures for the recovery of the stock of european eel in order to bring it into line with the comitology (reclassification into delegated and implementing acts) established by the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) following the implementation of the treaty of lisbon. in this reclassification of acts into delegated and implementing measures, it is essential to find a solution that is based on a sound legal basis and safeguards the rights of parliament as established by the tfeu. the rapporteur generally agrees with the attribution of implementing acts to the commission for the approval of the eel management plans, but considers that this regulation is not sufficiently comprehensive to ensure an effective recovery of the eel population. for this reason, the rapporteur went far beyond the comitology issues for compliance with the tfeu, introducing numerous substantive amendments to the report relating to management plans, reductions in fishing effort, restocking operations, various obligations (technical and monitoring measures, data collection and reporting) and sanctions for member states, which is why i voted against this report.
in writing. − the objective of this proposal is to align council regulation (ec) no 1100/2007 laying down measures for the recovery of the stock of european eel with the new rules of the treaty on the functioning of the european union as regards delegated acts and commission implementing acts. the european eel stock is currently facing a range of problems: overfishing, loss of key habitats, pollution, parasites, changes in ocean currents due to climate change, and others related to the eel's own biology and management, all of which require a response from the european union, as highlighted in the document. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − this draft regulation of the european parliament and of the council, establishing the union customs code by recasting the modernised customs code adopted by regulation (ec) no 450/2008, constitutes the most far-reaching reform of the customs legislation of the european union. the union customs code seeks to ensure the necessary balance between the aspects of supervision and control by the customs authorities of the member states, which is important for the protection of the financial interests of the european union and its member states and the safety and security of the eu and its residents, human and animal health, the environment and consumers. given the full computerisation and dematerialisation of customs procedures and the necessary development of computerised systems, a transitional period until 31 december 2020 is established for the full development and implementation of such systems and, consequently, for the full application of the new rules. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - the customs union is seen by those who advocate it as an essential element for the functioning of the single market and will therefore only function properly if there is a common and coherent application of common and modern customs rules and systems. the report calls for full harmonisation in such areas as: the use of common electronic systems by all member states; the creation of an integrated and common system for the collection of duties; the use of electronic data processing techniques; the use of common levels and modes of control over goods. the harmonisation of the union customs code (ucc) raises specific concerns relating to the safety of citizens and the economic aspects of the code. for example, there is no clear explanation of how and under what conditions the use of electronic systems applied in all member states will be made. who's going to control these systems and the information that can be shared by these systems? in addition, the creation of a unified system of customs duties raises concerns about who will be responsible for the collection and use of revenue, but also about how to find a common price in the context of harmonisation.

in writing. - this proposal concerns the agricultural accountancy information network (aran), set up in 1965 to meet some of the requirements of the common agricultural policy (cap), in particular as regards the certification of yields and the analysis of the economic performance of agricultural holdings. over time, fadn has evolved and the network has spread to all eu member states. to date, it is the only harmonised microeconomic database, as a similar approach has been followed in all member states. it is an important tool for framing and evaluating agricultural policies, as it collects data on income, production factors and output from a sample of farms, representative at eu level, on an annual basis. therefore, the fitd allows the commission to analyse the economic and structural situation and to assess a whole range of indicators related to income, productivity and production costs. the rica is thus a key tool for assessing the performance of agricultural holdings. with the new cap, it will have to make some adjustments which will be discussed in this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to update the requirements and criteria associated with the agricultural accountancy information network, so as to make it possible to analyse the economic and structural situation and to assess a whole range of indicators relating to the income, productivity and production costs of european agricultural holdings, with a view to gaining greater knowledge in order to be able to draw up new agricultural and rural development policies. aspects such as income, factors of production and production itself are essential to this design. i also share the rapporteur's view on the amendments to the treaty which will make it possible to transform outdated, duplicated and obsolete legislation into a genuine, practical and representative mechanism for collecting information, while at the same time retaining the autonomy of the member states in drawing up the plan for the selection of accountancy holdings. finally, i also believe that a specially designed website containing icao data and reports should continue to exist.

in writing. − the directive 2011/92/eu on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment (eia directive) is one of the cornerstones of european environmental law. it allows numerous public projects, such as the construction of bridges, ports, motorways or landfills, to take environmental impacts into account. in 28 years of application, this directive has proved to be effective and balanced, but it is urgent to adapt it to the new political priorities of the union, such as the soil strategy, the roadmap for a resource efficient europe and the europe 2020 strategy. it is therefore important to update and modernise without distorting the original spirit and maintaining the balance between a high level of environmental protection and an investment-friendly attitude and sustainable development.
in writing. − directive 2011/92/eu, which concerns the assessment of the effects of public and private projects on the environment, covering a wide range of projects in the environmental impact assessment (eia), is central to the union's environmental policy. the commission proposes a number of amendments which i support, including: only projects with significant environmental impact are subject to eia; broadening of the criteria and deadlines for decision; clear and transparent timetables at all stages of eia; possibility of public participation in the different stages of environmental impact assessment; independence of experts in the analysis of reports; promoters are obliged to provide corrective action. for a smart, sustainable and inclusive europe, natural resources must be preserved and safeguarded.

in writing. the european parliament approved the conclusion of the negotiated agreement between the european union and cape verde on the facilitation of the issuance of short-stay visas for the citizens of both parties. the agreement provides for a set of simplified conditions for issuing multiple-entry visas, a visa exemption for certain categories of persons, visa extension facilities, among other proposals. i therefore voted in favour of the document in parliament.
in writing. − the european parliament approved the conclusion of the agreement on the facilitation of short-stay visas on a reciprocal basis between the european union and the republic of cape verde, which provides for improvements for cape verdean citizens with regard to an intended stay of 90 days in each 180-day period. this facilitation will reduce the time and costs associated with travel to the schengen area. however, we cannot fail to stress the elitism in the granting of visas. the agreement introduces simplified conditions for the granting of multiple-entry visas valid for five years for members of governments or permanent members of official delegations and for one year for scientists, journalists and students. this agreement is in line with the application of the so-called blue card, which is part of the eu's immigration policy, which divides, classifies, selects and discriminates against immigrants according to their level of education, their social and economic status and the definition of labour needs.

the rapporteur. - i would like to begin by thanking all the contributions of colleagues who have enriched the report i have been asked to draw up on the maritime dimension of the common security and defence policy. the european parliament's vision for the development of a european maritime security strategy - which is due to be adopted by the council in december - is even more essential in times of economic and financial crisis in the union, placing the emphasis on the imperative of rationalising and articulating national and european civil and military means and capacities to ensure maritime security on the european union's coasts, in its neighbourhood and globally. maritime safety is vital to the functioning of democracy, to the rule of law and respect for our citizens and to economic progress in the union. it depends on the fluidity of global sea flows. 90% of the union's external trade and 40% of our internal trade is transported by sea. this report thus seeks to identify the elements which currently restrict the ability of member states and the union to act in a coordinated manner in defence of europe's security and interests in the oceans. in the face of threats such as organised crime, trafficking in human beings, arms and drugs, terrorism, piracy, environmental and ecological risks and also to stop the misuse of the extraordinary economic opportunities, the extraordinary economic riches that the sea offers us. we are making concrete proposals here for the union to overcome the current shortcomings and failings and to build a truly strategic maritime policy which, in compliance with international law and in particular the united nations convention on the law of the sea, integrates the defence and security aspects by promoting the synergy of civil and military resources and capabilities of the union and the member states, including the development of the necessary industrial and technological base, which creates jobs and implies innovation and creativity. the development of the maritime dimension of the common security and defence policy is essential for the union's positioning as a global actor providing security. it is crucial for the fulfilment of its international obligations and for dealing with risks and threats to the security of citizens and the european continent. these challenges are so often beyond our own backs, our closest neighbors. let us look, for example, at those resulting from the identification of the sea flows which will intensify, for example, the transit between the atlantic and the pacific oceans with the enlargement of the panama canal planned for next year. there are tremendous economic opportunities, no doubt, but there are also tremendous challenges and threats. what about the piracy phenomenon which triggered the deployment of operation atalanta off the coast of somalia, the first european union naval mission under the common security and defence policy? it demonstrates the need for the development of these naval capabilities and their positioning beyond our shores. in fact, piracy, which used to be in somalia or the indian ocean, is now in the atlantic ocean, in the gulf of guinea, alongside human trafficking, drug trafficking and arms trafficking. we have terrorist networks that, as we know, are targeting the european continent itself. so our states must understand that in this time of crisis the mottos pool and share or smart defence in the framework of nato must have a practical translation and this also applies to maritime capabilities. they have to rely on the european defence agency to make the savings that are necessary to invest in the equipment that we absolutely need to have an integrated maritime policy with the use of our civil and military capabilities. only in this way will we be able to serve the european citizens and the role europe must play in the world as a global provider of security, including in the oceans.
rapporteur. − mr president, i would like to take the opportunity to congratulate my colleague, ms giannakou, on her report. her philosophy and her approach to the matters dealt with there very much coincide with those of my own report – which has been adopted by the committee on foreign affairs and on which we will vote tomorrow – on the maritime dimension of the csdp. the thinking is similar, as are the concerns: with the resources needed for pooling and sharing these capabilities and the need to plan for the future. these things are essential, as it is essential to actually understand the major threats and challenges. i also want to thank my colleagues for all their contributions. i very much agree with what mr danjean said about financing for the csdp and all the effort in terms of
