in the last two years, a construction company called açomonta has been practicing modern slavery on portuguese workers on the border between france and luxembourg, who are not paid the minimum wage and are housed in inhumane conditions, crowded together, sleeping in warehouses. the company received more than €67 000 from the european social fund, a scandal that is not unique. today, with the european commission and the european union's much-loved policies to promote unemployment, workers are forced to work under any conditions. in the 21st century, with 19th century conditions. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the safety and health at work of workers is not compromised. but the data is scarce and non-existent. it is necessary to investigate them seriously, knowing that many of the cases are not even reported to the authorities, they remain silent and in the fear in which many workers live today. prevention, proper supervision, public investment, combating the precariousness of work that is always associated with the number of accidents and the absence of health and hygiene conditions at work, the criminalisation of work accidents - these are urgent steps that are difficult to achieve with the policies of the european union, which increasingly devalue and deprive workers of dignity.
mr president, commissioner, the protection of the health and safety of workers is a priority for the european parliament. as the european strategy expired in 2012, we naturally want to know when the commission will present a new strategy and what the reasons for this delay are. parliament has played a key role in improving legislation on working conditions, which should be adapted to people's abilities and needs, not the other way around. parliament has approved improvements to legislation on the protection of pregnant workers, women who have recently given birth and women who are breastfeeding, the so-called maternity leave directive, for which i am the rapporteur. in july 2008, the commission presented a proposal for a revision of that directive. in october 2010, the european parliament approved my report. unfortunately, the matter remains blocked in the council, without the commission having taken any steps or exercised any pressure on the council to unblock this important matter. parliament has also stressed - and has been referred to by several speakers here today - the need to improve legislation on the protection of workers against rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases. these diseases affect some 120 million people and represent a major burden on health and social security systems. in the european union alone, 25% of long-term absenteeism is due to rheumatic and musculoskeletal disorders. i have been following this matter because i am chairman of the parliamentary interest group on musculoskeletal diseases. it is therefore clear to me, commissioner, that we need a new strategy, one which is adapted to the new realities and to the evolution of society itself.
youth unemployment is the biggest problem facing europe, more serious than the budget deficit and sovereign debt crisis. in some member states, such as spain and croatia, it is above 50%. and yet, this is the most qualified young generation ever. the situation is dramatic and tends to worsen. it is therefore essential that the european funds which will enable the european youth guarantee to come into force, which will be able to offer young people a job, a traineeship or further studies, no later than four months after completing their studies or enrolling in an employment centre, be released immediately. i also support the strengthening of the current financing proposal of eur 6 billion, which is clearly insufficient. the eu cannot say that tackling youth unemployment is a priority and not provide the means to achieve it. according to recent estimates, we need around eur 10 billion to ensure that access to the european youth guarantee has a truly european dimension. in the present context, this funding cannot be seen as a burden, it is an investment to get out of the crisis.
the european response to the crisis has been too weak, insufficient and too late. however, if banking union is complete by the end of this mandate, we will have made significant post-crisis progress. the banking system, especially in europe, is the pool that irrigates the real economy. the function of banking is to turn the savings of many into investment that creates wealth and employment. when he ceases to fulfill these functions and lives on speculative games and high-stakes gambling, he jeopardizes the entire survival of the community. neoliberal theses have allowed toxic financial products to flood the markets, and the option of not regulating the financial system has also allowed banking to become contaminated. when the bubble burst, the entire system was in jeopardy. the states had to save the banks, while being financed by them. the death spiral between banks and states almost killed the euro and the european union, destroyed the real economy and wiped out jobs. we must draw all the lessons from this historic disaster. building a banking union seemed impossible before the crisis. today it begins to be a reality. but the important thing is that the reform momentum is not lost. the european parliament is aware of this urgency, as is the commission, and has shown it by working seriously and rapidly. we're building a building on three pillars. a building is only solid if its pillars are coherent with each other. in a single market, both the rules to be followed by banks and the criteria for their supervision must also be uniform. this first pillar will be formally completed today when we vote on legislation that puts the ecb at the heart of the single supervisory system, in close coordination with the eba and the national supervisors. parliament has demanded transparency in the decisions of the supervisory board and active participation in the appointment of its officials, which is normal in a democracy, and this week's negotiations have proved it right. but it will be of little use to obey common rules if, when a bank goes into crisis, it is returned to the national authorities to be bailed out by taxpayers' money. the new legislation we'll finalize by the end of the year imputes losses to shareholders and other creditors in a clear hierarchy. i congratulate the commission on this proposal and we congratulate it on having put forward before the summer the proposal for the creation of a common european resolution fund funded by all banks according to their risk profile. negotiations between parliament and the council on the third pillar, the harmonization of deposit guarantee funds, have also been reopened. nothing is complete, but there is finally a vision for the european banking system that is more than words. we hereby recognise the principles advocated by our political group and the objectives and instruments proposed by this parliament in its owninitiative report of 2010. the negotiating processes are far from over and there is always the risk of concessions to vested interests. but can the citizens count on an active, cooperative european parliament, determined to build banking legislation that stimulates the financing of the real economy, not speculation, that protects the taxpayer from the wrong choices of shareholders and managers, and that protects european depositors from risks they never decided to take on? we hope that the other partners, in particular the council, will be imbued with the same spirit. the economic and social disaster - and i will finish this now - which still persists in the wake of the 2008 crisis does not allow any escape from responsibility (...) in writing. − i voted in favour of this report describing the ombudsman's activities in 2012. i welcome the ombudsman's achievements during his ten-year mandate, including his work to promote a culture of service and good administration in the eu institutions and as a guardian of transparency.
in writing. − the ombudsman's activity in 2012 was intense. 740 complaints fell within the ombudsman's remit and 1720 fell outside it, the lowest number in the last ten years. in more than 75% of cases, the ombudsman helped the complainant by opening an inquiry (18.3%), referring the case to the competent body or advising the complainant on which body to turn to (57.1%). we can thus see that european citizens see the european ombudsman as a body to which they can turn in their relations with the eu institutions.
in writing. − following a ten-year mandate, the european ombudsman has retired and the european parliament, in this report, thanks the ombudsman for the results achieved during his ten-year mandate, in particular his work to promote a culture of service and good administration in the eu institutions and as a guardian of transparency. the ombudsman formally submitted his last annual report to the president of parliament on 21 may 2013 and presented his report to the committee on petitions on 28 may 2013 in brussels. i voted in favour of this annual report on the activities of the european ombudsman in 2012.
in writing. − the annual report of the european ombudsman for 2012 was formally presented to the president of the european parliament on 21 may 2013. i am in favour of this report which summarises the ombudsman's activities in the year under review and in which it can be seen that 465 inquiries were opened (an increase of 18% compared to 2011) and 390 inquiries were closed (an increase of 23% compared to 2011). overall, as in 2011, the ombudsman helped more than 22 000 citizens by handling their complaints (2442 cases), responding to their requests for information (1211) or providing advice through the interactive guide on his website (19 281). nikiforos diamandouros was first elected ombudsman in 2003 and subsequently re-elected in 2005 and 2010, and i would like to congratulate him on the work he has done and which has contributed greatly to supporting and enlightening european citizens.
in writing. − the european ombudsman has stated that after 10 years he will leave public life at the level of the european union and return to his previous activity as an academic, student and active private citizen. this is therefore its latest annual report, in which it reports that in 2012 it opened 465 inquiries (an increase of 18% compared to 2011) and closed 390 inquiries (an increase of 23% compared to 2011), having helped more than 22 000 citizens in processing their complaints (2442 cases), requests for information (1211) or advice on its website's interactive guide (19 281). the ombudsman reports that he has participated in more than 50 bilateral events and meetings, including with members of the legal community, business associations, think tanks, ngos, representatives of regional and local administrations, lobby and interest groups, academics, high-level political representatives and public officials. we acknowledged the ombudsman's work and voted in favour. we do not consider that this figure fills the way in which the eu imposes and conditions the lives of eu citizens, countries and their sovereign institutions in an undemocratic way on a daily basis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the common visa policy is a key element in the field of immigration, giving visas an essential role as a tool to control irregular immigration.
in writing. − freedom of movement within the schengen area depends on the existence of an effective and coherent common visa policy. some third-country nationals have, however, taken advantage of the possibility of visa-free travel for the purpose of irregular migration. the visa waiver is granted to the holder of a visa who is a national of a member state of the european union or a third country and who is a national of a member state of the european union or a third country, and is issued in accordance with the conditions laid down in the schengen acquis. the amendment of the reciprocity mechanism, which is the guiding principle of our common visa policy, is also of particular importance, because the current system is not working efficiently. we need a more effective mechanism to enable the union to respond more quickly if there is a breach of the principle of reciprocity. only in this way can we ensure the existence of a european unity and strengthen solidarity between member states. the agreement reached, while not perfect, was the best possible. i commend the rapporteur, mr díaz de mera, for his perseverance and for the excellent work which has enabled this commitment to be reached. i regret that we have not been able to change the comitology procedure with regard to the introduction of the suspension clause in such a way as to reserve a more appropriate role for the ep in the whole process.
in writing. - regulation (ec) no 539/2001 establishes the list of third countries whose nationals are subject to the visa requirement for crossing the external borders and the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from that requirement. this regulation lays down the conditions under which nationals of a third country may benefit from the exemption from the visa requirement for short stays in the territory of the european union. the report makes a number of amendments to that regulation, including the introduction of a safeguard clause allowing for the temporary suspension of the exemption from the visa requirement in an emergency situation, the amendment of the reciprocity mechanism, the establishment of definitions in accordance with the community code on visas, ensuring visa-free conditions for third-country nationals, refugees and stateless persons, various categories of third-country nationals and holders of passports or visas issued by entities governed by international law, and finally the adoption of provisions on the obligations of member states under international agreements. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - the common visa policy is a key element in the field of immigration, giving visas an essential role as a tool to control irregular immigration. the proposal to amend the regulation is the commission's reaction to the recent misuse of the community visa system. it was found that a significant number of third-country nationals were travelling to the union territory to apply for international protection without objective reasons, taking advantage of the visa waiver. it is intended to introduce the possibility of suspending the visa exemption but the mechanism should only be activated in very specific cases of urgency and where a significant and sudden increase in the number of irregular immigrants or unfounded applications for international protection has been detected. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - the aim is to implement mechanisms of a kind of 'cordon sanitaire' in the face of potential migratory waves resulting from the eu's neo-colonial policies and new hotbeds of military conflict, with all that this generates and from which the eu is not separated. the amendments introduced by this proposal to the visa-free policy, and above all to its suspension, continue to give the european union, and in particular the commission, powers at the heart of the sovereignty of states over relations with third countries and over their immigration policy, particularly over the granting of visas. the introduction of these amendments speeds up the suspension mechanism based on the denunciation of a single member state by implementing so-called reciprocity measures which, in practice, open or close borders according to the state of relations with a particular country and its greater or lesser compatibility with the interests of the eu and also with the interests of the labour force at the moment in the eu. what is all too clear is that these amendments further deepen the vision inherent in schengen and deepened by the lisbon treaty, considering immigrants from third countries as potential criminals, beneficiaries of the generosity of eu asylum policy, or violators of public order.
in writing. − the european union has been developing strategies and mechanisms to combat the economic crisis with the capacity to restore confidence in financial systems and to boost the growth capacity of the member states' economies in a sustained way. the european commission, the european parliament and the council have recently launched a roadmap for a stronger economic union. the establishment of a banking union, the first pillar of which will comprise the creation of a single supervisory mechanism, is part of this roadmap. while it is the responsibility of the european central bank to ensure the proper supervision of european banks, the european banking authority will be responsible for ensuring the integrated and harmonised application of the relevant legislation, ensuring the smooth functioning of the single market for financial services. the report proposes that the european banking authority should create a single supervisory guide, which is essential to ensure consistent application of the regulation, and ensure, within its mandate, the full and equal participation of all member states wishing to join the single supervisory mechanism, whether they belong to the euro area or not. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the european union has been developing strategies and mechanisms to combat the economic crisis with the capacity to restore confidence in financial systems and to boost the growth capacity of member states' economies in a sustained manner. the european commission, the european parliament and the council of the european union have recently launched a roadmap for a stronger economic union. the establishment of a banking union, the first pillar of which will comprise the creation of a single supervisory mechanism (ssm), is part of this roadmap. while it is the ecb's responsibility to ensure the proper supervision of european banks, eba will be responsible for ensuring the integrated and harmonised application of the relevant legislation, ensuring the smooth functioning of the single market for financial services. the report proposes that the eba should create a single supervisory guide, which is essential to ensure consistent enforcement of the regulation, and ensure, within its mandate, the full and equal participation of all those who wish to join the ssm, whether they belong to the euro area or not. i shall vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - a set of two legislative documents was adopted today creating a single supervisory authority for banking, the first pillar towards the creation of a european banking union. we are thus facing a historic milestone in the completion of economic and monetary union, which the recent economic and financial crisis had shown to be too weak and fragmented to cope with the adversities. from today, the european central bank will be the ultimate supervisor of all banks and financial institutions in the european union, and together with national supervisors it will ensure the correct application of the new capital requirements rules, supervise stress tests and check on the solvency conditions of banks. it was therefore necessary to review and adjust the rules and powers of the eba (european banking authority) to make them compatible and functional with the new powers that the ecb and the eba itself will now exercise. this is an essential and decisive step towards ending the fragmentation of this important economic sector and strengthening the european union on the world stage.
in writing. - this report aims to give the european banking authority more powers and competences in the supervision of banking institutions, in particular by creating a single rulebook to allow better control of the activities of these institutions within the european union. given that the financial crisis we are experiencing was created by the malfunctioning and lack of supervision of banking, greater supervision and regulation is needed to prevent future crises. we must be more ambitious and demanding in this respect and give the eba even more powers so that it can carry out its duties fully and transparently. i abstained.
in writing. − the creation of a single supervisory mechanism is fundamental to the creation of a european banking union, which should be based on a single set of rules for financial services, also integrating the harmonisation of the different national deposit guarantee schemes and a common european resolution framework. the banking union should be based on appropriate checks and balances, accountability between political institutions at eu and national level and bodies with supervisory responsibilities at both eu and national level. the european supervisory authority will have a very important role to play in preventing future crises in the financial sector.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu) no 1093/2010 establishing a european supervisory authority (european banking authority) as regards its interaction with the regulation conferring specific tasks on the european central bank concerning policies relating to the prudential supervision of credit institutions.
in writing. − the various european institutions have been working on a roadmap for the achievement of a genuine economic and monetary union, including concrete proposals to preserve the unity and integrity of the single market for financial services. i would like to congratulate all those involved in the preparation of this proposal which gives the european central bank greater supervisory powers, creates the european supervisory authority (european banking authority), ensures the improvement of the single market and greater cohesion in the european union. finally, i would like to stress that i see the single supervisory mechanism as the first step towards the creation of a genuine european banking union, based on a single set of rules for financial services, which also includes the harmonization of the different national deposit guarantee schemes.
in writing. - once again, the decisions taken by the majority in the ep are dominated by the neoliberal dogmas of deepening the internal market for financial services and guaranteeing the free movement of capital. after supervision comes resolution and after that something that says defend bank deposits. the concerns are evident in creating mechanisms to facilitate eu intervention to save some banks, as has been happening in recent years - without such mechanisms being in place - and to let others down. this is therefore a process of concentration and centralisation of financial capital at eu level. these mechanisms cast suspicion on certain banks, especially those in the peripheral countries, in order to concentrate financial capital in the banks of the great powers or to subordinate even more the economic groups of each country to the large transnational capital and its strategies not only to maintain but to deepen the speculative process. harmonization after harmonization, loss upon loss of sovereign power in each country and the situation of the majority of the workers and peoples, especially in countries like portugal, is worsening, while their power to decide or influence the decision is being reduced very significantly.
in writing. − the fragility of the european economic situation caused by an unprecedented crisis has forced the eu to develop concerted and ambitious actions to sustain the creation of conditions for economic prosperity and to restore stability to european financial markets. in this sense, one of the fundamental steps towards restoring confidence in the recovery of the union's economic area is the construction of a solid banking union, based on a number of pillars, of which the single supervisory mechanism is a prominent support. this report deals specifically with the creation of the single supervisory mechanism which will cover the financial institutions of the euro area and will be open to all other member states wishing to join it. the aim is to define how the ecb, as the ultimate supervisor of european banks, will perform its tasks, ensuring the stability of the system and maintaining its independence as the monetary policy authority. in march the european parliament concluded negotiations with the council of the european union on this dossier, which are contained in this report. after the conclusion of the interinstitutional agreement with the ecb, its accountability to parliament is clarified and this report will be adopted with my support.

in writing. − i agree to confer on the ecb the specific supervisory tasks which are crucial to ensure a consistent and effective implementation of the union's policy on the prudential supervision of credit institutions, with other tasks remaining the responsibility of national authorities. the ecb's tasks should include measures taken to promote macroprudential stability. the ecb should perform the tasks conferred on it with a view to ensuring the safety and soundness of credit institutions, the stability of the financial system of the union and of each of the participating member states, and the unity and integrity of the internal market, thereby also ensuring the protection of depositors and improving the functioning of the internal market. the conferral of supervisory tasks on the ecb should be consistent with the framework of the european system of financial supervision (esfs), established in 2010, and with its underlying objective, namely the development of a single set of rules and the enhancement of supervisory convergence across the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the thyssen report (and also the giegold report) on the single prudential regulation of credit institutions at union level by the european central bank, in the belief that this is one of the most important steps towards building a genuine economic and monetary union. a real qualitative leap, as the president of the european parliament said. i have been arguing for many years that there cannot be an integrated market for financial services, including a growing number of banks with cross-border activities, with fragmented regulation at national level and without federal regulation at union level. i also consider that this failure constituted one of the major shortcomings of the architecture of the euro and of the internal market for financial services, and contributed decisively to the spread of the financial crisis in 2008/2009. the single banking supervision - the main pillar of the banking union - can therefore only be welcomed by all those who are committed to the eu's progress. let us hope that the other two pillars - the bank resolution mechanism and the deposit protection system - will also have a positive outcome.

in writing. − the economic and financial crisis currently affecting most member states has brought europe's banking system close to collapse, with a serious blow to the integrity of the single currency and the single market. i therefore vote in favour of this report, because i believe that it is urgent to intensify the integration of the banking sector and to strengthen european unity, restoring much-needed financial stability and laying the foundations for economic recovery. i would also like to stress that the ecb should be given specific and well-defined tasks with a view to promoting the safety and soundness of credit institutions and the stability of the financial system in the eu and in each of the participating member states of the eu.
in writing. - as the report itself acknowledges, the current crisis has brought europe's banking system close to collapse. the establishment of the single supervisory mechanism, in which the ecb will have a central role, is intended not to interfere with the essential things: the functioning of the internal market for financial services, the free movement of capital. the ecb is thus taking over supervisory functions which were previously carried out by national institutions, such as the banco de portugal. contrary to what the argument on which this proposal is based might suggest, it was not for lack of supervisory mechanisms that banks turned the essence of their activity to financial speculation, but this resulted first of all from the contradiction between the overproduction and overaccumulation of means of production and the contraction of markets and consumption caused by the loss of purchasing power of wages (due to their contraction) and their replacement by credit. in other words, the banks turned their main activity to financial speculation, with the complicity of the supervisory authorities and the ecb, which provided them with cheap credit and calmly and fearlessly watched speculation in new financial instruments and so-called sovereign debts.
in writing. − the loss of biodiversity is accelerating. the preservation of biodiversity is essential for the socioeconomic vitality of europe. to participate in the preservation of biodiversity, it is necessary that the benefits arising from the use of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge are shared today in a fair and equitable way. i agree with all the rapporteur's proposals because they aim to ensure that the european union takes its place and its leading role in current and future international negotiations, by promoting a progressive position in order to rapidly arrive at an ambitious global multilateral mechanism that can meet the challenges of preserving biodiversity and its sustainable use.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation aims to transpose the nagoya protocol, which provides for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits for all uses of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge. the commission proposal thus provides a solid basis for building an effective european-wide system of access to and sharing of the benefits arising from the use of genetic resources in the eu.
in writing. − the loss of biodiversity is accelerating. some 60% of ecosystems have been degraded in the last 50 years (fao, 2010). beyond an ethical and moral responsibility, the economic and social impact of this decline is enormous: 7% of global gdp will be lost annually by 2050 (teeb report, 2010). paradoxically, it is in biological diversity that lies an inexhaustible source of innovation and discovery in the field of scientific research, technological applications or health, food, cosmetic and other products. in this way, the preservation of biodiversity is not only essential for the future of all humanity, but also for the socioeconomic vitality of europe and all citizens, who are the direct beneficiaries of its use. we must work to combat the loss of biodiversity, as this will contribute to economic development and job creation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the implementation and ratification by the union of the nagoya protocol - on access to genetic resources and the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from their use. i voted in favour of agreeing with the european parliament's position that this european regulation should be as close as possible to both the spirit and the letter of this international treaty. the commission proposal provides a solid basis for building an effective system at european level. however, full compliance with the nagoya protocol requires some mechanisms to be strengthened, as parliament suggests. if the question of access to resources is left to the sovereignty of the member states, it is important to present a clear community framework on the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from the use of natural resources.
in writing. − the union has implemented an eu biodiversity strategy for 2020, which commits to increasing its contribution to preventing global biodiversity loss by 2020. i would point out that this protocol includes research and development related to the genetic and/or biochemical composition of genetic material - e.g. dna, genes, etc. a number of industries, including the pharmaceutical and food and drink industries, use genetic material for research purposes that improve the quality of life of european citizens. i support this report which encourages the use of genetic resources for research, development and marketing purposes, some of which also use traditional knowledge associated with genetic resources.
in writing. − the proposals for amendments to the regulation are all intended to give the european union a leading role in current and future international negotiations, promoting a progressive position in order to reach an ambitious global multilateral mechanism quickly. whatever supranational attitude the eu is intended to adopt in this area, we do not fail to agree with the basic question of stopping degradation and preserving biodiversity. we are, however, alert to the contradictions within community policies which undermine this very objective. the main action points focus on improving the chain of use of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, enhancing transparency and legal certainty, and on progressive compliance in new uses of genetic resources for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits for all uses of genetic resources, as enshrined in the convention on biological diversity and the nagoya protocol. a final proposal is to create a european union benefit-sharing fund to be funded by the users of genetic resources with a view to preserving the world's biodiversity. we voted yes.

in writing. − the european union is increasingly dependent on imports from third countries for energy supply, and this needs to change to ensure that climate, energy and growth objectives are met. decentralised and small-scale energy production provides an opportunity for households, small and medium-sized enterprises and communities, both urban and rural, to work together to tackle climate change by becoming energy producers. for the eu to achieve its long-term renewable energy targets, microgeneration must be a key element of future energy production. microgeneration contributes to increasing the total share of renewable sources in the eu's energy mix and allows for efficient electricity consumption close to the production site, avoiding losses in transport. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution which stresses the importance of promoting renewable energy cooperatives at local level, both in rural and urban areas, in the need to increase public support for renewable energy and to promote awareness and participation of citizens in small-scale energy production, improving access to renewable energy and generating investment.
in writing. − microgeneration is a concept that benefits smes, european consumers and local and regional authorities. in line with the union's objectives of a green and smart economy, microgeneration consists of the generation of heat and cooling that meets the individual needs of individuals, smes and local communities. microgeneration technologies include wind turbines, heat pumps, solar panels and photovoltaics. for this sector to succeed, there needs to be a real european energy market, the creation of incentives at national level and the de-bureaucratization of access to the national grid. at european level, there should be an application of incentive strategies and policies. the union must maintain its leading role in combating climate change and micro-generation has a role to play here that should not be forgotten. for these reasons, i shall vote in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. − microgeneration is the small-scale production of heating/cooling and distribution of electricity by individuals and smes to meet their own needs. the different forms of small-scale production suggest that microgeneration covers a number of different technologies: hydroelectric, geothermal, solar, marine and wind energy, heat pumps, biomass. the resolution points to important factors such as the technical development of micro-generation units, the deployment of intelligent energy infrastructures, and effective short, medium and long-term support policies to encourage this energy production. however, the old maxim of the proper functioning of the internal energy market, which is no longer new, is not being abandoned, just that it is the guarantor of the continuation of the policy of handing over this sector to the large energy companies. it is also clear that these are largely responsible for the energy poverty that is currently being experienced in the eu, which affects 125 million people in the union, depriving them of access to energy, a situation generated mainly by the increase in energy prices. we warn against using micro-generation to hold consumers accountable for lowering the price of their energy bill, in order to continue to guarantee the fabulous profits of european energy companies.
in writing. − the slow progress in eliminating the gender pay gap has significant demographic, social, legal and economic consequences. reducing gender inequalities by eliminating the gender pay gap will bring benefits not only to women but also to society as a whole. the elimination of the gender pay gap should not be seen as a cost but as an investment.
in writing. - equal pay for men and women seems to me to be a matter of basic justice, which enshrines the principle of equal pay for equal work. that is why i am concerned that the gender pay gap is widening in europe, and i support the european parliament's call for the commission to support member states in reducing the gender pay gap with the aim of eliminating the gender pay gap by 2020. in addition to equity requiring equal rights for men and women, the law must also take account of gender-specific needs, which in the case of women is evident in areas such as maternity protection and reconciliation between work and family life. that is why, in addition to the just demand for equal pay, it is essential that women are not systematically penalized in the workplace for being women and mothers.
in writing. −despite the considerable body of legislation in place for almost 40 years, the measures adopted and the resources deployed (the eu-wide disparity was 17.7% in 2006, 17.6% in 2007, 17.4% in 2008, 16.9% in 2009 and 16.4% in 2010), the gender pay gap remains a persistent problem, currently standing at 16.2% across the eu. the application of the principle of equal pay for equal work and work of equal social value is crucial to achieving gender equality. reducing gender inequalities by eliminating the gender pay gap will bring benefits not only to women but also to society as a whole. the elimination of the gender pay gap is not a cost but an investment. directive 2006/54/ec is not sufficiently effective in addressing the gender pay gap and in achieving the objective of gender equality in employment and occupation. the commission should therefore review directive 2006/54/ec without delay and support member states in promoting good practices and implementing policies to reduce the gender pay gap.
in writing. - i consider that the application of the principle of equal pay for equal work and work of equal value is crucial to achieving gender equality, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution by the european parliament on the implementation of the principle of equal pay for men and women for equal work or work of equal value, which calls for the promotion of good practice and the implementation of policies to reduce the pay gap between men and women.
in writing. − the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) states in article 8 that in all its actions, the union shall aim to eliminate inequalities and to promote equality between men and women, while underlining in article 157 that member states shall ensure the application of the principle of equal pay for men and women for equal work or work of equal value. however, what this motion for a resolution shows us is that the gender pay gap is still a reality in the different member states. according to the latest data, this disparity at union level has been decreasing, but at a relatively slow pace. in 2006, the wage gap in the union was 17,7%, in 2007, 17,6%, in 2008, 17,4% in 2009, 16,9% in 2010 and 16,4% in 2011. we need to look at this problem in a different way. in 40 years of european legislation the problem still persists. the member states must look at this as a structural problem which has a negative impact on the growth of their own economies.
in writing. - it is necessary for member states to have adequate legislation but also to have the means to enforce it. today, employers circumvent the law by feminizing occupational categories, setting lower wage values in these, although they are categories that can be equated to those predominantly performed by men. only a close inspection can detect these cases. recommendations can be important. however, the desire to put an end to such discrimination is fruitless if the eu's labour policies are not changed. when the european commission, in the framework of the troika, insists on flexibility, on the individualisation of employment contracts, on the weakening of collective bargaining, it is not protecting women and promoting wage discrimination. despite this contradiction and the resolution not to reject these policies, we agree with the principles set out.
in writing. − cyberspace and cybersecurity should be one of the strategic pillars of the security and defence policies of the european union and all member states. e-commerce and online services are a vital force of the internet and are essential to achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. it is therefore necessary to develop a strategic communication policy on cybersecurity in the union, cyber crisis situations, strategy review, public-private collaboration and public warnings and recommendations. the european commission and other actors should therefore develop cybersecurity and cyber resilience policies that provide for economic incentives to promote high levels of cybersecurity and cyber resilience. member states should adopt national cybersecurity strategies as soon as possible. the union's cybersecurity policy should ensure a secure and reliable digital environment that is designed to ensure the protection and preservation of fundamental freedoms and the respect for fundamental rights. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − cyberspace and cybersecurity should be one of the strategic pillars of the security and defence policies of the eu and all member states. it is essential to ensure that cyberspace remains open to the free flow of ideas and information and to freedom of expression. i welcome the european union's cybersecurity strategy and the proposal for a directive on measures to ensure a high level of network and information security across the union. it is necessary to develop a strategic communication policy on cybersecurity in the eu, cyber crisis situations, strategy review, public-private collaboration and public warnings and recommendations.
in writing. − dependence on information and communication technologies and on cyberspace is a reality at virtually all levels of society. an attack on some of these means risks having practical consequences in terms of the security and defense of populations and the infrastructures that serve them, compromising communications and transport, rendering health systems unable to act, triggering the activation of war arsenals, exposing and misappropriating defence and trade secrets, allowing the diversion of funds, among many other negative possibilities. in addition, threats and attacks are becoming increasingly sophisticated, which is why our ability to prevent, detect and respond must also be highly sophisticated. that is the way we must go to protect cyberspace.
in writing. − cyberspace and cybersecurity should be one of the strategic pillars of the security and defence policies of the eu and all member states. it is essential to ensure that cyberspace remains open to the free flow of ideas and information and to freedom of expression. there should therefore be a joint eu cybersecurity strategy. this proposal for a directive lays down measures to ensure a high level of network and information security throughout the union. in the face of the growing importance of the internet and cyberspace for political, economic and social transactions, not only in the union but also in relation to other actors worldwide, we need to maintain a very effective cybersecurity policy to safeguard it, as network security will contribute to the improvement of the internal market and to economic growth and job creation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution, which, among other things, recalls the need for a high level of network and information security. network and information security is not only necessary for the maintenance of services that are essential for the proper functioning of society and the economy, but also for safeguarding the physical integrity of citizens by enhancing the efficiency, effectiveness and secure operation of critical infrastructures.
in writing. − cybersecurity needs to be addressed jointly by the union and the member states, and by the union and global actors, as the challenges it presents have no terrestrial limitations. it is therefore important that the union cybersecurity strategy is taken into account in the member states, so that they themselves adopt national policies. organized crime and terrorism are now developed partly via the internet. certain movements for political, social and cultural change are also born in this space. in parallel, the strength of the union's internal market and europe 2020 is based on e-commerce and online services. we have to align the potentials and the dangers of cyberspace. i am in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that we need to create capable national legal systems, in coordination with other global actors, and to educate individuals about the challenges that cybersecurity poses to us.
in writing. - this is an unacceptable resolution. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the eu, including the eu's maritime borders, and to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the eu's maritime borders. we also oppose the linking of cybersecurity to the eu's external defence policy. the council also called for greater cooperation with nato and considered it important to establish closer cooperation with the united states on the exchange of information. it is incredible, especially at a time when the information and surveillance systems set up by the us on eu institutions and citizens are becoming increasingly well known. it only demonstrates, once again, the eu's complete submission to us imperialism and a total disregard for individual and collective freedoms and guarantees.
in writing. − information and communication technologies are at the heart of the digital society and currently account for around 20% of the european union's annual productivity growth and 4.5% of its gdp and generate 25% of private investment in r & d. they can make an extraordinary contribution to growth and jobs. the commission should also be able to use the information provided by the member states to support the implementation of the union's policy on digital services. to this end, alongside the need to remove barriers to the digital single market of the european union, it is a top priority for the eu to invest in optimized and fast broadband internet infrastructure in order to fully exploit the potential of the digital economy. the european commission should make proposals to carry out a fundamental review of the regulatory framework for electronic communications. the crucial measures announced in the digital agenda for europe, with particular emphasis on resilient and reliable infrastructure and services and the data protection regime, should also be implemented. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − the main objective of the digital agenda for europe should be to reduce inequalities between member states, in particular in terms of access to fast and ultrafast, fixed and mobile broadband infrastructure. unlocking the potential of the digital economy in the eu would have a high multiplier effect on the economy, leading to higher growth and more jobs. unlocking this potential is one of the most important reforms for growth and competitiveness to help the eu emerge from the current crisis.
in writing. − the existence of a competitive digital single market is becoming more important and more inescapable in our society. technological developments, especially in terms of the availability of information, content and knowledge on the net, have been extremely rapid and in just over a decade have drastically changed the digital landscape with the massification of the internet and mobile communications. it is therefore important to look to the future and to think about how these new facilities of the digital age can be put at the service of citizens and businesses for europe's growth and competitiveness.
in writing. − the main objective of the digital agenda for europe, adopted in 2010, should be to reduce inequalities between member states, in particular with regard to access to fast and ultra-fast, fixed and mobile broadband infrastructure. information and communication technologies (icts) are at the heart of the digital society, currently accounting for around 20% of the eu's annual productivity growth and 4.5% of its gdp, and generating 25% of private investment in r&d in the eu, and are susceptible to being affected. it is estimated that by 2020, 50 billion devices will be connected to the internet and that by the end of 2017, data traffic will increase 15-fold. the digital agenda and the achievement of a digital single market should therefore be at the heart of the eu's efforts to create growth and emerge from the crisis. in fact, the digital economy is growing at seven times the rate of the rest of the economy and the completion of the digital single market could provide an annual stimulus of eur 110 billion;
in writing. − a new digital agenda for europe is essential if there is to be a digital revolution from which all european citizens benefit. however, this requires the involvement of all citizens in the process, so that they become actors in the new digital society. but for this to be possible, a major investment effort is needed to close the digital divide that currently exists in the eu. we must not forget that informed and enlightened citizens contribute to increasing europe's potential. the digital agenda and the achievement of a digital single market must therefore be at the heart of the eu's efforts to create growth and emerge from the crisis, remove the barriers to the digital single market and thereby create jobs and growth in the eu. we must not forget that the digital economy is growing at seven times the rate of the rest of the economy and that the completion of the digital single market could represent a stimulus worth €110 billion a year.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on the digital agenda for growth, mobility and jobs, which stresses that, alongside the need to remove barriers to the eu's digital single market, it is an absolute priority for the eu to invest in optimized and very fast broadband internet infrastructures in order to fully exploit the potential of the digital economy.
in writing. − the digital agenda for europe aims to create a digital single market, based on fast and ultra-fast internet and interoperability, where all european citizens have the same access. the document calls for the abolition of roaming in europe, since it is consumers, individuals and businesses, who bear the excessive costs. the completion of the internal market presupposes the completion of a digital market. at the same time, it remains important to bring more services online in the civil service. however, we must not forget that part of society is still at a low level of education in broadband issues. i am voting in favour of this motion for a resolution, stressing that the importance of the digital market has not been taken into account in the cef, particularly by the member states.
in writing. - the digital agenda is based on the digital single market without barriers and aims, which we disagree with, to combat what they call a fragmented market in national markets with artificial borders and which cannot be considered a single economic market in which competition is encouraged. this is the way not only to complete privatisation of the telecommunications sector or what remains of it, but also to create a communications market at eu level. in addition to the exacerbation of european markets to the detriment of national public services, the false promises of lower consumer prices, which have already been exposed, in the most diverse sectors of activity, are here reflected. we also believe that a digital agenda at the cutting edge rejects any commercialisation of knowledge, education and research. we therefore do not accept that the positive objectives of the report - such as the fair recognition of the lack of funding in the 2014-2020 mff - are disfigured by the ambiguities and variations of the european single market.

in writing. the central element of this report is the defence of the deepening of the process of militarization of the eu as the european pillar of nato, with a view to greater articulation and complementarity of its powers in the division of labour in the world. the aim is to gain advantage in the processes of strategic domination of the increasingly scarce raw materials and energy resources on which the major powers and eu monopolies are dependent, as well as domination over trade routes and markets. the comprehensive approach advocated here also aims at preparing a set of military and civilian means and their greater interoperability, ensuring a strengthened eu intervention capacity, freer from the impediments of national sovereignty, the delays of a greater or lesser democratic decision-making process in each country. it aims to impose political powers and establish cooperative military alliances with its interests where the interests of the eu's major powers' monopolies are at stake. it aims at the destruction of national sovereignty by promoting processes of interference and contempt for international law and the un charter. the alternative to the militarisation of the eu exists: the effective implementation of a system of security and cooperation in europe, based on the principles of the helsinki charter.

in writing. − this report aims to be a starting point for common strategies for member states, criticizing the eu action plan on unaccompanied minors (2010-2014) presented by the european commission. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council. it considers that any action in relation to an unaccompanied minor must be based on two principles: the best interests of the child and the protection of the rights of the child. it is intended that these two principles should not be overridden by the laws on migration. it therefore advocates a ban on the placement of minors in detention centres, the provision of specialised services (accommodation, psychological and legal support, access to education, health care, the appointment of a legal guardian), the condemnation of invasive age assessment techniques, the conditionality of return on the best interests of the child, the creation of training conditions for officials and agents, including on gender issues. we voted yes.

i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this. the so-called shortcomings of the eu emissions trading scheme are but the finished demonstration of the ineffectiveness and perversity of market instruments such as carbon trading. the carbon market is ineffective in terms of the objectives it claims to achieve, as its operation to date demonstrates. it is perverse, because it may even lead to results contrary to what it claims to be. it could be used for a lot of things: for a new haven for financial speculators; for creating another billion-dollar machine for generating fictitious financial assets. it's not good for protecting nature. with this instrument, the eu's message is clear: why invest in environmentally friendly technologies when you can buy the right to pollute? leaving the achievement of environmental objectives to the whims of the market can only lead to bad results. it is a pity that even some environmentalists or some who claim to be such have not yet realized this. the question we should be asking the european commission is another: when will the market approach be replaced by a regulatory approach, which applies the principle of common but differentiated responsibility in a fair and proportionate way?
i am very pleased that the commission has taken this opportunity to make a statement on the subject. mauritania is recognized as a country with immense fisheries resources. nevertheless, its fisheries sector is still at a very early stage of development, which is a sign of the failure of the declared development cooperation objectives set out in agreements with the european union at least 15 years ago. we stand for the inalienable right of every country and every people to decide in a sovereign manner on the exploitation of its natural resources. several provisions of this new agreement correspond to the fair and legitimate exercise of this sovereignty by mauritania, to the fair and legitimate defence of its interests. this is the case, for example, with the obligation to land catches in mauritanian ports, the hiring of seamen or the rules on supply. the european commission is required to take account of the diversity of the fleet using these vessels, their problems and specificities, and their legitimate aspirations and expectations, in its actions and in particular in the negotiation of agreements of this kind. it is clear that this agreement is damaging to the fishing sectors of some countries, especially in the smaller-scale fishing segment. the european commission has failed to safeguard the interests of these segments in the negotiations and is now being asked to either renegotiate the agreement, if that is still possible, or to assess its impact and take compensatory measures, without which a number of coastal communities could see a situation that is already in deep crisis worsen.
mr president, commissioner, fisheries partnership agreements are essential from an economic point of view for the european fleet because of the fishing opportunities they open up, from a social point of view for third countries because of the financial and social compensation they receive and for the world fisheries sector because of the strict sustainability standards to which the european fleet is bound and which are not met by other fleets, which as a rule take the place of europeans when they withdraw. the eu-mauritania fisheries agreement is the eu's most important with a third country in terms of catch volumes, variety of fishery products, annual financial compensation granting access to mauritanian waters to some 100 european vessels from 12 member states and with fishing opportunities for eight different categories. the first version of the agreement was frankly unsatisfactory to the european fleet, which supported the negative vote of the committee on fisheries. however, this vote and the constant pressure from the rapporteur, whom i thank for his work, have made it possible to renegotiate some of the technical conditions laid down in the protocol and to introduce adjustments at various levels, which could significantly contribute to improving the cost-benefit ratio and the level of use of this protocol by the european fleet, which allows me to vote in favour of the fisheries agreement.

the european parliament has already expressed its views on the situation in the middle east. however, corruption has long undermined the ability of the european union to promote reforms in third countries to effectively combat corruption and to prevent, detect and punish complicity by european public or private sector actors in third countries with a serious impact on human rights, justice, good governance and sustainable development in those countries. we need to ensure that what we do within the european union is consistent with what we promote outside it, and to do that we also need to ask ourselves how we are instigators, or even accomplices, in the phenomenon of corruption and the colossal illicit capital flight that is diverted from resources for education, health, and other basic services in developing countries. we must therefore put an end to bank secrecy, increase transparency about the real owners of companies, strengthen european legislation on money laundering and improve our criminal laws, by criminalising illicit enrichment and giving european courts jurisdiction to try all corruption crimes, even when committed abroad. we will thus be responding to the demands of our own citizens who are well aware that the present crisis - which exposes the glaring economic asymmetries and the obscenely growing social inequalities in europe itself - is also the result of the corrupt practices that financial and economic deregulation of recent decades has allowed to flourish. from spain, overwhelmed by the scale of the bárcenas case, to greece, where a former defence minister was sentenced to 20 years in prison today for corruption in the purchase of german submarines, to portugal, where the defence minister responsible for the purchase of german submarines in contracts rife with corruption and fictitious counterparts is now deputy prime minister and the then prime minister is president of the european commission, without ever having been heard by the judiciary, which nevertheless investigates the contracts and the companies involved. finally, in this disturbing context, european citizens demand that politicians, who are us, not only act with integrity and diligence, catch and punish the corrupt, but also effectively prevent corruption. in our member states, in the european union and in relations with third countries, because we cannot fight corruption in third countries without starting at home. we propose many measures in this report. we propose, for example, to take inspiration from the magnitsky act, adopted by the us congress with a new strategy for dealing with human rights violations, in particular those committed against anti-corruption activists. but there is no reason why a similar eu law should be restricted to russian officials involved in the murder of lawyer magnitsky. in this report we call for a mechanism that lists and imposes specific sanctions, such as travel bans to europe and asset freezes parked here, against officials of any country involved in serious human rights violations and judicial manipulation against corruption whistleblowers, journalists and human rights activists. as regards our cooperation with third countries, the utmost integrity and transparency in the flows of development aid must be ensured. entities contracting with the european union must disclose their structure and ownership. in this report we call for reforms to budgetary transparency, which is why we demand budgetary transparency in return for financial support to the budgets of third countries. in the field of corporate social responsibility, we think that the european union should take the lead, we think that lists should be drawn up of companies convicted of corruption within or outside the european union so that they are prevented from participating in public tenders in the union, at least until they correct and guarantee integrity. we believe that this is an incentive not only to integrity in the internal procedures of companies, but to create a global environment conducive to the economic and commercial activities of our companies. finally, in this report we ask for clear guidelines for the protection and follow-up of information provided by any individual who reports on illegalities and abuses of power in the use of public resources of the union or of the member states. we have to create an international legal framework, which is indispensable in order to protect the so-called whistleblowers, those who give information that is indispensable to detect and to punish and prevent corruption.
mr president, i would like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur, i think this is a timely report, the subject is an important and topical one. the european union must set an example, it must adopt stricter rules, not only on its own territory but also in its relations with third countries in the field of cooperation. it has been said here, and i stress it, that we must not forget that inequalities and social injustices are at the root of the economic crisis we are suffering and that it is the greed of some, the fraud of others and the deregulation of the financial sector that have brought us to where we are, that is to say with so many sacrifices being imposed on so many citizens. the divorce between citizens and politicians is notorious, and that is why we must adopt exemplary procedures and ensure that there is transparency in all our activities, whether in the financial sector, the economic sector or political activity.
the fight against corruption, if it is to be effective, cannot ignore the culture in which these practices tend to proliferate. the so-called structural adjustment programmes that the imf has been imposing for decades in the four corners of the world and that the european union is now imposing on the peripheral countries, programmes based on privatisation, the emptying of public assets, the opening up to business of areas that were previously protected from the market, such as public services, in short, the prevalence of private interests over the public interest, these policies, in addition to the trail of destruction, unemployment and poverty they leave, create the conditions for a growing promiscuity between political and economic power and for the development of corrupt practices, while weakening public mechanisms for monitoring and combating these practices. a policy to combat corruption must be based above all on preventing it and must necessarily break with these policies.
this report recognises the clear trend towards increasing regional inequality in the european union. but how did we get here and what is needed to reverse this path? the first point is that the deepening of integration, the single market, common policies, their neoliberal matrix, by their very nature capitalist, lead to unequal development, inevitably to divergence. this is a dynamic that the manifestly insufficient resources allocated to cohesion have never been able to counteract. secondly, to reverse this trend requires a fundamental change in the policies of the european union. it requires the recognition of the right of each country and region to development and the encouragement of the full exploitation of its endogenous potential. it calls for a substantial increase in the allocations for economic and social cohesion and not for their weakening as envisaged in the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. it also requires conditions for mobilising cohesion funds and other funds from the eu budget to avoid their being wasted, facilitating the mobilisation of national counterparts and putting an end to unacceptable macroeconomic conditionality rules.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the effects of major structural changes in world trade patterns. the fund may not exceed a maximum amount of eur 500 million. this is the fifth mobilisation of the fund under the 2013 budget for a total amount of eur 1 164 930 for italy. it concerns 529 redundancies in anovo italia s.p.a. and jabil cm s.r.l., italian ict companies, 480 workers being covered by the measures co-financed by the egf during the reference period from 20 march 2011 to 20 december 2011. the amount of the proposed financial contribution will leave more than 25% of the annual maximum amount allocated to the egf for interventions during the last four months of the year, as provided for in article 12 (6) of regulation (ec) no 1927/2006.
in writing. − this is the sixth application to be examined under the 2013 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 2 594 672 from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for italy. the commission has also decided to initiate the procedure laid down in article 93 (2) of the eec treaty in respect of the dismissal of 1030 workers in the automobile manufacturer de tomaso automobili s.p.a., a company in italy. as has been the case, the justification for further attacks on labour rights lies on the one hand in changing geographical patterns of consumption, in particular the rapid growth in asian markets from which eu manufacturers are reaping less benefits, coupled with credit constraints resulting from the economic and financial crisis. more than these funds which in a way legitimize the policy of dismissals and support employers in this decision, what workers need is the implementation of investment policies that create and maintain jobs with rights. only a break with the policies currently being pursued by the eu will be able to stop this path of social and economic disaster.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to italy, which applied for a financial contribution from the egf in the form of an application egf/2012/008 it/de tomaso automobili following 1030 redundancies in de tomaso automobili s.p.a. and 1010 workers were covered by the measures co-financed by the egf during the reference period from 5 july 2012 to 28 august 2012.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the effects of major structural changes in world trade patterns. as a consequence of these structural changes in world trade patterns resulting from globalisation, the car manufacturer de tomaso automobili s.p.a. went into liquidation in april 2012 and, failing to find a viable solution, resorted to 1 030 redundancies. parliament recognised that growth in the eu automotive industry was far below that of its main competitors and recognised that, despite the union being the world's leading car producer, the decline in market share had put increased pressure on companies already constrained by credit constraints as a result of the impact of the economic and financial crisis. considering that the application meets the eligibility criteria laid down in the egf regulation, i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision to mobilise the fund from the egf reserve, for a total amount of eur 2 594 672, in favour of the reintegration of the 1 010 workers concerned into the labour market.
in writing. − regulation no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 established the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support workers who have lost their jobs as a result of structural changes in the global economy. i, the undersigned, declare that i am satisfied with the request to mobilise the amount of eur 2 594 672 to obtain a financial contribution from the egf, following 1 030 redundancies in de tomaso automobili s.p.a., of which 1 010 workers were covered by the co-financed measures during the reference period from 5 july 2012 to 28 august 2012. finally, it is important to ensure that the egf supports the individual reintegration of workers made redundant into stable employment and that such assistance can only co-finance active labour market measures leading to lasting and long-term employment.
