in writing. − i approve of this report, considering that corruption in the public and private sectors perpetuates and aggravates inequalities and discrimination when it comes to equal civil, political, economic, social or cultural rights, and further emphasise that it is proven that acts of corruption and violation of human rights involve the misuse of power, lack of accountability and discrimination in various forms. moreover, corruption is inevitably detrimental to the economic and social development of a people. i am therefore convinced that there must be coherence between internal and external policies so that the european union is credible and valued as the highest level of transparency and accountability in external aid and also with regard to the public budgets to be requested by the european union in relation to the budget of the european union and external aid. in supporting the political role of the european union, i also advocate the highest level of corporate responsibility for human rights.
in writing. - i welcome the report adopted today by the european parliament which proposes that the eu adopt an anti-corruption law, similar to the us sergei magnitsky act, which provides for visa bans and asset freezes for officials of third countries who are responsible for human rights violations. the commission should propose legislation requiring european companies to ensure that their acquisitions do not support perpetrators of corruption, conflict and serious human rights violations, including through the implementation of controls and audits. member states should adopt legislative and other measures to criminalise illicit enrichment in all eu countries, establishing that illicit enrichment with intent i.e. the substantial increase in the assets of a public official, without the latter being able to reasonably justify it on the basis of his legitimate income constitutes a criminal offence.
in writing. − given the negative effects of corruption not only on the public image of states but, more importantly, on their economic and financial performance, an integrated approach by the union to this issue is essential to limit the non-transparent use of development aid. corruption in the public and private sectors damages democracy, governance and state institutions, thus deteriorating the whole human rights environment, which is why the eu must take a firm and determined approach to preventing and combating corruption in third countries.
in writing. − corruption should be broadly interpreted and defined as the abuse, for personal, individual or collective gain, directly or indirectly, of powers entrusted to it, and that acts of corruption include, inter alia, the crimes of bribery, embezzlement, trafficking in influences, abuse of power and illicit enrichment. corruption undermines democracy and the rule of law, exacerbates unequal, unjust and discriminatory outcomes in the fair enjoyment of human rights, whether civil, political and economic or social and cultural rights. moreover, corruption disproportionately affects the most disadvantaged and marginalised groups in society, including by preventing their equitable access to political participation, public services, justice, security, land, employment, education, health and housing. according to the world bank, corruption accounts for 5 percent of the world's gdp ($2.6 billion), with an annual budget of over $1 trillion paid in bribes. the eu must lead by example in the fight against corruption. the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion is also important in this area. it is important that banking secrecy and tax havens be ended on a global scale.
in writing. the report makes positive recommendations which should be taken up, such as advocating the end of banking secrecy or rules for greater openness and transparency in eu project funding, making them more scrutinized. but there are clear shortcomings and inadequacies, both in relation to tax havens - where the need to put an end to them needs to be clearly and unequivocally defended - and in relation, for example, to the effects of the imf's so-called structural adjustment programmes, or in relation to the root causes of corruption. the opening up of markets, natural resources and energy to the domination of eu monopolies, favouring their expansion, creates the breeding ground for corruption to proliferate. the same can be said of privatization and the many other impositions of the said adjustment programmes, which increase the promiscuity between political and economic power. whether in developing countries or in europe. the example of portugal is a good one. the strategy advocated here is almost exclusively aimed at combating corruption, to the detriment of a more effective approach that would involve prevention measures. the report also calls for the establishment of a european network of national laboratories for the development of new technologies. quite the opposite.
in writing. - corruption can be considered as one of the main causes of the increase in inequality, injustice and discrimination when we talk about the equitable enjoyment of human rights. the eu can only become a credible and influential leader in the fight against corruption if it addresses the problems of organised crime, corruption and money laundering within its own borders in an appropriate way. i hope that the recent anti-corruption report will identify areas vulnerable to corruption in the member states and in turn help to strengthen anti-corruption efforts, facilitate the exchange of good practices, identify eu trends and stimulate peer learning, with a reinforced respect for commitments at eu and international level.
in writing. − the anti-corruption information report, to be published by the european commission, is a step towards the european union establishing itself as a credible and influential leader in the fight against corruption by adequately addressing the problems of organised crime, corruption and money laundering within its borders. in fact, the identification by the commission of areas vulnerable to corruption in the member states is expected to help strengthen efforts to fight corruption. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. corruption is an old phenomenon, rooted in the mentality of the societies in which it occurs, which is an obstacle to transparency in public and private enterprises and to convincing denunciation of the harmful effects of inequity. anti-corruption efforts should therefore focus primarily on early education in respect for justice and fairness. states are thus called upon to apply the revenues of resource exploitation and the market, ensuring respect for human rights, in particular as they are affected by corruption. efforts to combat abuse of power usually focus on prevention and deterrence. one involves the aforementioned education about the nature and effects of corruption, the other seeks to promote measures that increase the risks, costs and uncertainties associated with corrupt practices. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally sound use of energy.
in writing. − the existence of corruption perpetuates the effects of inequality, injustice and discrimination in respect of human rights. the eu can only be an influential and credible leader vis-à-vis third countries if it can tackle the problems of organised crime, corruption and money laundering and contribute to the monitoring and accountability of such activities. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. - while including positive aspects that should be valued (notably the defence of the end of banking secrecy), this report leaves out practices and policies that are responsible for the spread of this phenomenon. the strategy advocated here focuses almost exclusively on the fight against corruption, to the detriment of a more effective approach that would involve prevention measures. the report does not set out measures to tackle the root causes of the growth of corruption in the eu's relations with third countries, namely the opening of markets to domination and the expansion of the eu's monopolies, its natural and energy resources, the geostrategic and diplomatic domain. not only does it not denounce but it also supports the eu's policies of interference in the internal affairs of third countries, the manipulation of internal political, religious and ethnic disputes, the fomenting of conflicts (of which syria is an example), the search for political and economic allies willing to alienate the sovereignty of their peoples in order to better satisfy the interests of their own group, the eu and its great powers. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances.

in writing. − on 12 december 2012, the recast of the brussels i regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition of judgments in civil and commercial matters was signed. the regulation introduced a number of important improvements, in particular the abolition of the exequatur procedure, which means that it will be much easier in the future to enforce a decision in another member state. this process of reformulation has not covered certain aspects of the rules on jurisdiction which apply to labour law. labour law is a particularly sensitive area and one in which the european union has only a relatively small influence. the aim is to protect workers, collectively and individually, who are usually the weakest party in employment relations, while also ensuring legal coherence and preventing national legal traditions from being overridden in the field of labour law, ensuring, as far as possible, that jurisdiction and the applicable law coincide. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the recast of the brussels i regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters has introduced a number of important improvements, in particular the abolition of the exequatur procedure, which means that enforcement of a judgment in another member state will be much easier in the future. however, the scope of the recasting process did not cover certain aspects of the rules on jurisdiction which apply to labour law. labour law is an area in which the european union has only a relatively small influence. however, the union has established rules governing which courts in the member states have the right to decide disputes, including in the field of labour law, in cross-border situations. the aim of the amendments proposed in the report is to protect workers, collectively and individually, who are generally the weakest party in employment relations, and also to ensure legal coherence and to prevent national legal traditions from being overlooked in the field of labour law, ensuring, as far as possible, that jurisdiction and the applicable law coincide.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it introduces amendments which can help to better protect, collectively and individually, workers, who are generally the weakest part of industrial relations. it is essential to ensure legal consistency and to prevent national legal traditions from being overlooked in the field of labour law.
in writing. - labour law is still a matter for the states, with the european union having relatively little influence. each state has built its own system of protection for workers and it is not for the european union at this time to try to standardize legislation in this area. however, with a view to the free movement of workers and capital within the european union, the eu must establish rules governing which courts in the member states have the right to settle disputes, including in the field of labour law, in cross-border situations.
in writing. - the report by mrs evelyn regner is entitled 'improving private international law: rules of jurisdiction applicable in the field of employment'. the incorporation of the maritime labour convention into eu law gives a much stronger supervisory capacity in the community area, for example at the level of infringement proceedings in the european union itself, which will further strengthen the enforcement of the law. i therefore consider it important, within the framework of the eu's competences in this area, to have an approach based on transposing the mlc as fully as possible into this directive. it should be noted that this proposal is in line with the commission white paper of 28 march 2011 entitled 'roadmap for the single european transport area towards a competitive and resource-efficient transport system', which announces a social agenda for maritime transport.
in writing. this own-initiative report deals with the question of jurisdiction in labour law matters under the brussels i regulation. the rapporteur recalls high profile european court cases in relation to individual employment contracts and strikes (laval, viking, etc.) in which national provisions on labour law were undermined by european rules. we agree with the rapporteur's view that one of the principles of private international law at the judicial level is the protection of the weaker party, that is, in this case, workers. the report contains correct proposals, of which we would like to highlight: - in respect of the strike, the courts of the member state in which the strike has taken place or is to take place shall have jurisdiction; - as regards individual contracts of employment, amendments should be made to ensure that jurisdiction is exercised by the courts of the member state with the closest connection to the employment relationship; - the removal of the shopping forum the possibility of choosing a forum not because it is the most appropriate for adjudicating the dispute, but because the laws that that court will use will lead to the application of the law that is most favourable to the person who brought the action.
in writing. - the brussels i regulation has brought greater protection to workers in their relationship with the employer, particularly when they are in a cross-border context. with this regulation we intend to improve the previous one, in particular with regard to the most vulnerable part and the deepening of legal issues. this is the only way to ensure greater protection for the worker in the event of a labour dispute. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − this own-initiative report aims to improve private international law: rules of jurisdiction applicable in the field of employment are primarily intended to protect the worker, the weakest party in the employment relationship. the rapporteur proposes amendments to the brussels i legislation on labour law rules, suggesting the creation of a forum for industrial action disputes, in accordance with the rome ii regulation, in the place where the industrial action is or will be brought and proposes that in cases where the employee sues the employer, a recast of the reserve clause where there is no usual place of work, so that it is agreed that the place of work is the place from which the employee received day-to-day instructions. in view of the unanimity in the vote on this report in the committee responsible, i voted in favour of these proposals.
in writing. − the union's competence in terms of labour rights is limited to crossborder issues, in particular the decision of the court which is to rule on a given dispute. however, although this competence is exclusive to the member states, this own-initiative report invites the commission to take account of a number of improvements in the next amendment to the brussels i regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters. the proposals concern collective actions, individual contracts of employment, proceedings against the employer and proceedings against the employee.

in writing. - i support this report, as it is of paramount importance to ensure that the maritime labour convention and the highest standards of the european union are applied to seafarers. ships shall have on-board procedures which allow seafarers to complain about shortcomings in european union legislation. such complaints shall be handled in a fair, effective and appropriate manner. in addition, each member state shall establish effective inspection and enforcement of maritime working conditions to ensure that the living and working conditions of seafarers on board ships meet international standards.
in writing. − the maritime labour convention adopted by the international labour organisation applies to international maritime transport and covers matters essential to ensuring decent working and living conditions on board ships, and also provides for procedures for the application of these provisions. the convention can be considered the first maritime labour code for over 1.2 million seafarers as well as for ship-owners and maritime nations worldwide. the maritime labour convention is a valuable contribution to the objective of creating a level playing field in the maritime sector worldwide by setting common minimum standards for all flags and for all seafarers. i therefore supported this report which proposes to improve directive 2009/13/ec and ensure that it is given the appropriate means of implementation in the european union. the proposed amendments aim to strengthen the responsibility of member states in the exercise of their flag state powers.
in writing. − the aspects of the maritime labour convention (mlc) 2006 relating to flag state control should be enshrined in community law in a more detailed and specific way. one of the major advantages of incorporating the ctm into eu law is that it will give it a much stronger capacity to monitor the community area, for example in infringement proceedings within the european union itself, which will further strengthen compliance with the law. the eu provisions on flag state control should more closely reflect what the mlc specifically and explicitly provides to avoid divergent interpretations by member states which could lead to unfair competition and social dumping.

in writing. − i agree that the aspects of the maritime labour convention (mlc) 2006 relating to flag state control should be enshrined in union law in a more detailed and specific way. one of the major advantages of incorporating the ctm into eu law is that it gives it a much stronger capacity to monitor the community area, for example in infringement proceedings within the european union itself, which further strengthens compliance with the law.

in writing. − the maritime labour convention (mlc) was adopted by the international labour organisation in 2006. this convention applies to international maritime transport and covers matters such as the minimum conditions to be observed for seafarers' work on board a ship to ensure decent working and living conditions on board ships. the eu sees the mlc as a valuable contribution to the objective of creating a level playing field in the global maritime sector by setting common minimum standards for all flags and for all seafarers. the report also calls for the eu to be able to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu is able to take action to combat terrorism. the report, which we supported, sets out the responsibilities of flag states in areas such as: each state must assume its responsibilities towards ships flying its flag; authorization of recognized organizations to carry out inspection tasks; maritime labour certificate and declaration of conformity of maritime labour; inspection and enforcement; on-board complaint procedures.
in writing. − the maritime labour convention (mlc) was adopted by the international labour organisation (ilo) in 2006. it applies to international maritime transport and covers such essential matters as the minimum conditions to be observed for seafarers to work on board a ship, working conditions, accommodation, leisure, food and table service, health protection, medical care, welfare and social security protection and their observance and enforcement, in order to ensure decent working and living conditions on board ships, and also provides for procedures for the application of these provisions. the convention can be considered the first maritime labour code for over 1.2 million seafarers worldwide, as well as for ship owners and maritime nations worldwide. the mlc, adopted in 2006, provides for general rights and protection at work for all seafarers, regardless of their nationality and the flag of the ship.
in writing. − this report calls on the member states of the european union to assume their responsibilities as flag states more effectively and consistently. the rapporteur believes that the aspects of the maritime labour convention (mlc) of 2006, which aim to ensure decent working and living conditions on board ships on international voyages or between foreign ports, should be enshrined in community law in greater detail and specificity. eu provisions on control by the state under whose legislation the ship is registered or licensed should reflect more closely the aspects of the ctm in order to avoid divergent interpretations by member states, as such divergences could lead to unfair competition and social dumping. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the maritime labour convention (mlc) provides for the general rights of maritime workers and covers essential issues in the maritime sector, such as the minimum requirements to be observed for the work of those on board a ship (title 1 of the mlc), working conditions (title 2 of the mlc), accommodation, leisure, food and table service (title 3 of the mlc), health protection, social security, medical care and welfare (title 4 of the mlc) and their observance and application (title 5 of the mlc), to ensure decent working and living conditions on board ships. this report indicates that the aspects of the ctm relating to control by the flag state should be enshrined in community law in a more specific and detailed way. this will strengthen law enforcement as it gives the mlc a greater oversight capacity in the community space. the states are thus directly responsible for the ships flying their flag. by implementing ctm in all european ports, with the changes to the responsibilities of the flag state, we are ensuring a level playing field for the global maritime sector, which employs over 1.2 million people.
in writing. − the maritime labour convention (mlc) was adopted by the international labour organisation in 2006. this convention applies to international maritime transport and covers matters essential to the lives of seafarers such as the minimum conditions to be observed for seafarers' work on board a ship (concerning working conditions, accommodation, leisure, food and table service, health protection, medical care, welfare and social security protection) to ensure decent working and living conditions on board ships. the objective of this convention is to create a level playing field in the maritime sector worldwide by establishing common minimum standards for all flags and for all seafarers. the rapporteur believes that one of the major advantages of incorporating the ctm into eu legislation is that it will give the commission a much stronger capacity to monitor the community, for example in infringement proceedings within the european union itself, which will further strengthen compliance with the law. states should assume their responsibilities in relation to ships flying their flag. we have voted in favour of this convention because we believe it protects this sector of the profession, which is often isolated and unprotected.
mr president, i welcome the adoption of this proposal because we are faced with legislation of the utmost importance in the essential control of smoking and in the present and future improvement of the public health of millions of europeans affected by the disease and the many hundreds of thousands who die prematurely every year as a result of tobacco use. reducing tobacco consumption, especially among young people, is an imperative that no responsible person can fail to pursue and where no greater interest can be evoked to override it. that is why we welcome this directive in all its aspects which genuinely defend health. however, there were aspects where the proposal for a directive went too far. i therefore thank the socialist group for having made an exception by submitting to the plenary alone my amendment to safeguard the unfair and unjustified discrimination against azorean tobacco, for reasons having nothing to do with health, and i welcome the fact that parliament has corrected this injustice with its approval of azorean tobacco.
in writing. - i approve this report, with the amendments made, considering that the commission proposal required that 75% of the outer area of tobacco packages be occupied by health warnings. but it went further, requiring that the size of these warnings should not be less than 64 mm high and 55 mm wide, thus endangering the production of the two tobacco factories in the azores, which produce 30% and 50% of this type of cigarettes and directly employ 133 workers. i welcome the results achieved in that the 64 mm and 55 mm dimensions of the warnings have been removed, which means that the european parliament is in favour of continuing to use regular sized packages manufactured in the azores. reducing tobacco consumption, especially among young people, is an imperative which no responsible person can fail to pursue and which no major interest can evoke to override. i therefore want to safeguard the non-discrimination of azorean tobacco.
in writing. - smoking remains the leading cause of preventable deaths in the eu, killing around 700 000 people a year. according to commission figures, 70% of smokers start smoking before the age of 18. according to the same source, public health expenditure in the eu for the treatment of tobacco-related diseases amounts to some eur 25.3 billion per year. the measures taken by the eu over the years to combat smoking have helped to reduce the number of smokers in the european area from 40% in 2002 (in the eu15) to 28% in 2012 (in the eu27). i welcome the amendments adopted today to the proposal for a revision of the tobacco products directive because i believe that they help to dissuade young people from smoking.
in writing. the report by mrs mcavan deals with the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states relating to the manufacture, presentation and sale of tobacco and related products. smoking is still the biggest cause of preventable deaths in the eu with around 700 000 deaths a year. the number of smokers in the eu has fallen to one in four europeans, but the worrying fact is that 94% of smokers have become addicted before the age of 25 and 70% before the age of 18. for this reason, i would like to stress the main objective of the updated rules: to make smoking less attractive to young people by taking a determined approach to all the factors that contribute to smoking initiation. this directive does not aim to impose a ban on smoking. i therefore agree with most of the measures that contribute to this, such as the space for health warnings on tobacco packages, the progressive ban on the use of flavourings and smaller packages, and the regulation at european level of nicotine-containing products, which are now covered by the current directive.
in writing. - while the aim of this directive is to protect health and prevent more young people from starting to smoke, it also has the objective of improving the functioning of the internal market, which is worthy of note. the proposal adopted provides for more restrictive measures than directive 2001/37/ec as regards the dimensions of health warnings on cigarette packages, which must cover 65% of the sides of the pack. we note as positive the fact that the final result for portuguese brands of regular tobacco, in terms of the size of the warnings, respects their continuity and national production. despite the positive steps taken in banning distinctive flavours (fruit, menthol, chocolate, etc.) in cigarettes and slim cigarettes, the industry's interest prevailed in the objective of protecting public health and preventing young people from taking up smoking. we welcome the inclusion of a proposal from us which affirms the responsibility of the member states for the protection and prevention of public health, providing assurances, public monitoring and counselling of young people, and public campaigns for tobacco prevention, particularly in schools, and considering that universal and free access to tobacco cessation counselling and treatment is essential.
in writing. − this new directive on the manufacture, presentation and sale of tobacco and related products is a revision of the 2001 directive, updating it with new scientific findings, advances in prevention, the impact of tobacco dependence on public health and taking into account new market developments. the new directive focuses on prevention, particularly among young people, as the latest studies indicate that 94% of smokers start smoking before the age of 25. the new prevention measures are not prohibitory in nature and are not framed in such a way that existing smokers cannot continue to smoke. the new directive ensures that current smokers are covered by general public health measures; however, the new measures focus on a significant increase in preventive action to combat the high number of deaths caused by tobacco, as well as the financial burden it imposes on health systems. we voted in favour of the new directive.
in writing. - the tobacco industry is undoubtedly very important for the eu economy. however, we must also be concerned about the public health issue. tobacco-related deaths in the eu are increasing. i think this directive is balanced in terms of increasing the rules that alert smokers, as well as new smokers, to the harmful effects of tobacco.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the mcavan report on tobacco, despite some dilution in the plenary vote, because the commission's legislative proposal represents an important step forward in the fight against tobacco addiction. measures such as increasing the size of the warning on the harmful effects of tobacco or banning additives that may make tobacco consumption more desirable may hinder or attenuate the attraction of new consumers, especially among young people. the adoption of this legislative initiative is not only a victory over the powerful tobacco lobbies - the tobacco producing countries and multinational companies - but also and above all a victory for the health systems of the member states of the european union, which are being costed impressive sums by tobacco-related diseases. individual freedom to smoke remains, but now more informed and less constrained by the interests of the tobacco industry.

in writing. - i welcome the new protocol to the eu-mauritania fisheries agreement, which grants access to mauritanian waters to a hundred vessels from 12 member states, including portugal (spain, portugal, italy, greece, france, the united kingdom, malta, the netherlands, germany, poland, lithuania and latvia). the protocol assumes an agreement of €110 million per year, of which €70 million will be paid by the eu (67 million for access to resources and €3 million for sectoral support) and the remaining €40 million will be paid by industry in the form of fees for fishing licences. thank you very much.

in writing. the report by mr gabriel mato adrover deals with the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities between the eu and mauritania and the financial contribution. mauritania is a nomadic country which, despite having some of the richest waters in the world, has no tradition in the field of fishing. the absence of a national fishing fleet and the lack of economic resources and political will have led mauritania to prefer to cede the exploitation of its resources to foreign fleets, including the eu. the agreement grants access to some 100 vessels from 12 member states: spain, italy, portugal, greece, france, the united kingdom, malta, the netherlands, germany, poland, lithuania and latvia.
in writing. − this is the most important fisheries agreement signed by the eu in terms of fish volume, product diversity and financial amounts involved. several provisions of this new agreement correspond to the fair and legitimate exercise of mauritania's sovereignty over its resources and the fair and legitimate defence of its interests. the agreement grants access to mauritania's waters to fleets from 12 countries, including portugal, and includes fishing opportunities for pelagic, demersal, fish, crustaceans and tuna. for cephalopods (dust), fishing opportunities were set at zero, as mauritania considered that at present there is no surplus (in relation to the fisheries of the local fleet) to allow the granting of fishing opportunities in this category. this will be particularly damaging to some fleets. in negotiating such agreements, the european commission must take account of the diversity of the fleets using them, their problems and specificities, their just and legitimate hopes and expectations. i didn't always know how to do that. this agreement is an example of that. where such negotiations result in clear damage to some fleets, the european commission should consider measures to mitigate their negative impacts. this is particularly important in the current situation of deep economic and social crisis affecting the sector.
in writing. - mauritania is a nomadic country which, despite having some of the richest waters in the world, has no tradition in the fishing industry. the mauritanian authorities have therefore decided to cede the exploitation of their resources to foreign fleets, including the eu. in economic terms, fisheries account for 50% of export earnings and 29% of gnp. export and processing companies are essentially mixed enterprises. fisheries also generates a high number of jobs, accounting for 36% of jobs in the modern sector. in its relations with mauritania, the eu should help the economic and social development of the country so that there are adequate conditions for the promotion of foreign investment. the eu should also provide sectoral support so that mauritania can manage its fishing activities with its resources in a sustainable way and combat illegal fishing by applying the principles of good governance and respecting international regulations on the law of the sea. this is clearly the most important fisheries agreement for the eu in terms of volume, variety of fishery products and financial consideration. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. − genocide refers to the deliberate killing of persons, including fetuses, of a particular sex, on the basis of gender. it can occur before or after birth. the main cause of this phenomenon is the preference for male children in some societies. however, genocide is a worldwide problem that is not confined to certain countries. gender discrimination against girls and women is unacceptable and constitutes a violation of human rights. the consequences of this barbarity reveal an increase in the number of missing women in the world population to almost 200 million. the impacts are also economic and social. the fight against genocide requires states to support the promotion of an educational and social environment in which women and men, girls and boys are treated equally, by strengthening women's opportunities to access a full and equal partnership in society. on the other hand, states should develop and promote effective legislation and policy frameworks that address the root causes of gender inequalities. for these reasons i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on a comprehensive eu strategy for fisheries in the pacific region, as it puts forward proposals for a long-term fisheries strategy in the western and central pacific area, which takes into account the need to coordinate policies in order to enhance synergies and benefits for both the pacific states and the eu states.
in writing. − the pacific is extremely rich in fish and is the largest fishing area for highly migratory species, and in particular tuna, with 80% of the world's catch. the establishment of a long-term strategy for the western and central pacific could allow for greater coordination of union policies. this will increase potential synergies, thus achieving a multiplier effect of mutual benefit for the pacific states and the union countries and increasing the union's visibility in the region. the future fisheries strategy must not ignore the partners in the cotonou agreement. in view of the potential amendments to this agreement, this fisheries strategy should be an integral part of a new approach of the union to relations with these countries. it is recalled that during the period 2006-2011, the union was the second largest donor of development aid in the western and central pacific region , after australia.
in writing. the report by mrs carmen fraga estévez deals with the eu's overall strategy for fisheries in the pacific region. it takes into account the need to coordinate european policies in order to enhance potential synergies, achieve a multiplier effect, maximise the beneficial effects for both pacific states and eu states and increase the visibility of the eu in the region. this report focuses particularly on the western and central pacific, which is very rich in fisheries resources. i therefore agree that, in the framework of future post-cotonou relations with the acp-pacific countries, the fisheries strategy should have a regional approach that strengthens the position and role of the eu in the western and central pacific region;
in writing. - this own-initiative report calls for a long-term eu strategy for fisheries in the western and central pacific. it also called on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's external relations are not jeopardised by the threat of a nuclear war. we are talking about a region rich in fishery resources, dominated by island states, acp countries, and where illegal, unregulated and unreported fishing is rife. we broadly agree with some of the guidelines expressed in the report, such as the increase in the appropriations for assistance to the fisheries sector of the countries in the region under the european development fund, the fight against illegal, unregulated and unreported fishing and the promotion of sustainable fishing in the region. however, the strategy in question is based on an unconcealed ambition to maintain relations of inequality and dependence, as is shown by the subordination of the strategy to the context of the epas (the so-called economic partnership agreements). these are, as is well known, free trade agreements which the eu has been putting strong pressure on a number of acp countries and regional blocs to sign. we have tabled amendments to delete all references to epas. they were rejected. we reject the report.
in writing. − the aim of this report is to recommend the establishment of a long-term fisheries strategy in the western and central pacific, taking into account the need to coordinate european policies in order to enhance potential synergies, achieve a multiplier effect, maximise the beneficial effects for both pacific states and eu states and increase the eu's visibility in the region. the pacific has a very high fishery value, being the largest producer of highly migratory species. with this report we seek to develop the countries associated with this eu comprehensive strategy for fisheries in the pacific region.
in writing. − this own-initiative report aims to recommend the need for a long-term fisheries strategy in the western and central pacific that reflects the necessary coordination of european policies, enhances potential synergies to achieve a multiplier effect and increase europe's visibility in the region, and maximises the benefits for eu member states and pacific states. in this respect, it is worth noting the enormous importance of the pacific region in terms of fishery resources, in particular tuna species, which account for around 80% of the world's catches, and which is why the western and central pacific tuna-fishing fleet has increased significantly, reaching currently around 280 vessels. on the contrary, the eu fleet in this region is limited to only four trawlers, representing about 2% of the total fleet and 7% of the total trawl catches. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this report because i consider that the measures proposed by the rapporteur are intended to consolidate the strategic presence of the eu fleet in this pacific region and to promote the defence of the interests of european operators interested in developing fishing activities in this region of the world.
in writing. - this own-initiative report aims to establish a strategy for fisheries in the western and central pacific. this area is mainly made up of acp countries, which have a very rich fishery value, and it is intended that there should be coordination of the fisheries policies in the union with those in the pacific, with the aim of providing a sustainable development of this sector, while increasing the union fleet in these waters. in parallel, it is important that the amendment to the cotonou agreement, which governs eu-acp relations, takes account of this strategy and the need for lasting and transparent solutions for the sustainable promotion of fisheries resources. i am voting in favour of this report because i consider it an excellent document which identifies and enumerates the challenges facing the union in terms of development aid and trade.
in writing. - i welcome this report, considering that in developing countries, fisheries are a sector that generates wealth and employment, as well as a source of protein for the population. i note that conflicts over maritime zones are mainly due to the exploitation of marine resources which have become limited or even scarce, in particular due to the over-exploitation and unsustainable use of part of them in the mediterranean and the black sea, and stress that for several coastal developing countries, marine resources are a fundamental basis for their future development and food security. i stress that the resolution of disputes concerning the delimitation of maritime boundaries and the establishment of fisheries protection zones must take place in full accordance with international law. i also stress the need for the european union to continue to support coastal developing countries in implementing sustainable fisheries management plans in their territorial waters and in effectively combating illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
in writing. − by 2025, urban development in the mediterranean could reach a level of 60% with one third of the population concentrated in coastal areas, doubling the needs for water and fisheries resources. 75% of the fish stocks in the mediterranean sea are overexploited. the legal regimes governing vessels' access to national fisheries vary according to the country of origin of the vessel. an essential aspect of good ocean governance is the peaceful resolution of maritime disputes and the delimitation of maritime boundaries. considers that maritime management in the mediterranean and black sea requires a higher level of political cohesion and cooperation among the coastal countries concerned; stresses the important role of bilateral cooperation and international agreements, given that most black sea and mediterranean countries are not part of the eu and are therefore not obliged to respect eu legislation. the eu must use its diplomatic resources to promote dialogue between member states and third countries to ensure that they respect the principles of the eu's common fisheries policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on fishing restrictions and jurisdictional waters in the mediterranean and black sea conflict resolution, because it proposes to improve cooperation with neighbouring countries and to strengthen the management of shared stocks. the conclusion of cooperation agreements on sustainable fisheries is also encouraged, in order to ensure the protection of european coastal and territorial waters, the exclusive economic zones and the conservation of marine resources.
in writing. − the specific characteristics of the mediterranean and the black sea, as well as the increased competition for marine resources, have given rise to regional tensions and disputes between coastal states over maritime areas. it is urgent to seek to reduce their impact and to promote joint and responsible management of these resources through a regional approach to the conservation and fishing of species in these waters that takes into account the dangers arising from the concentration of populations in coastal areas, increased maritime traffic and over-exploitation of resources. in order to keep up to date, i quote from arturo pérez-reverte's column of 3 may 2010: for años me crucé en el mar (...) con barcos (...) brought to the slaughter. and so, by matching the boils with european legislation, by locating the tuna with airplanes, by surrounding it with ultra-modern technology, by searching ever further afield, in sicily and the libyan coast, and by taking it in cages to the places of concentration and slaughter, cuatro linces have become made of gold, while the bluefin tuna that for centuries has been crossing the strait of gibraltar, a silver and red treasure that has sprinkled its ancestral lake in our cupboards with greek, latin and arabic words, is extinguished without remedy.
in writing. - the report by mr nikolaos salavrakos deals with fishing restrictions and jurisdictional waters in the mediterranean and black seas; urban development in the mediterranean could reach 60% by 2025, with one third of the population concentrated in coastal areas, thus doubling the needs for water and fisheries resources. the mediterranean and black seas have particular characteristics in terms of oceanography, fisheries, environment and socioeconomy. the report calls on all coastal states to step up their efforts to phase out overfishing in the mediterranean and black seas, as the depletion of stocks will increase the potential for conflict in this region.
in writing. − this report calls for more efforts at regional, national and eu level to regulate access to resources in mediterranean and black sea waters. the rapporteur believes that existing disputes can be resolved with existing legislation, including at international level, by encouraging bilateral and international agreements, given that most mediterranean and black sea countries are not part of the eu and are therefore not subject to their legislation. it also advocates the establishment of exclusive economic zones and protected areas, in which conservation and management measures are adopted, in order to promote sustainable fishing and facilitate the control of fishing activities by combating illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. while generally agreeing with some of the measures and guidelines proposed, we disagree with others, such as advocating greater use of eu resources (diplomatic and other) in intervening with the countries of the region and in the territorial waters, continental shelf and maritime resources themselves.
in writing. − urban development in the mediterranean will be huge by 2015, with one third of the population concentrated in coastal areas, thus doubling the needs for water and fisheries resources. the mediterranean sea carries 30% of the world's maritime traffic. the mediterranean and black seas have particular characteristics in terms of oceanography, fisheries, environment and socioeconomy. the mediterranean and black sea basins have a very slow rate of water renewal (around 80 to 90 years and 140 years respectively) and are therefore extremely vulnerable to marine pollution. the increase in competition for declining fish stocks and marine resources is a cause for concern, leading to regional tensions and possible disputes between coastal states over maritime zones. efforts at regional, national and eu level to strengthen the regulation of access to resources are therefore needed. we must step up efforts to phase out overfishing in the mediterranean and the black sea, as depletion of stocks will increase the potential for conflict in this region.
in writing. − this own-initiative report aims to highlight the need for a greater level of political cohesion and cooperation in maritime management between the countries of the mediterranean and black sea basins. the rapporteur calls for the eu to use its diplomatic resources to influence member states and third countries to ensure that the principles of the eu's common fisheries policy are respected, noting that increased competition for the exploitation of marine resources can trigger conflicts with third countries. it is therefore urgent that the member states and the eu develop joint initiatives to ensure the security, control and protection of european coastal and territorial waters, exclusive economic zones (eezs), the continental shelf and marine resources, in order to avoid international flashpoints. the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of national authorities responsible for the protection of the marine environment. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the measures proposed can make a significant contribution to improving maritime management in the mediterranean and black sea basins.
in writing. - this report is based on the over-exploitation of stocks and marine resources, which leads to escalating tensions and disputes between the coastal states of this sea basin. the rapporteur therefore calls on the commission and third countries to establish a regional approach to conserve species, taking into account the transnational dimension of fisheries and the migratory nature of species. for the reasons mentioned above, i am voting in favour of this report.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, madam president, commissioner, for many years we have heard in this house, in official speeches and we have read in official documents that the main objective of the union is to invest 3% of gdp in research. so far, no country in the union has been able to achieve this and we know that austerity has had the opposite effect, which is to reduce ever more investment in terms of gdp in research and innovation. more than a third of the countries in the union are investing less than 1%. we are told, however, and we hear it loud and clear in this house, from president barroso, from the different political groups, from the council, that it is through research that we are going to get out of the crisis, we say that this is the solution that is at hand. however, what we see is that our researchers have increasingly precarious links or that they are fired, that their projects are not funded or that they are often even forced to emigrate to other parts of the world where research and science are better treated than in europe. there are, however, another 3% which is much talked about in this house and which have merited all the attention and enormous intervention of the union's institutions, i am referring to the 3% of the deficit, which have been much more closely followed than the 3% of research. now, for those of you who thought 3% was equal to 3%, we realize that it's not, because 3% of the deficit is gold and 3% of research is plastic, at best. the question i put to you, commissioner, is very simple: are you prepared to fight for 3% of research as your colleague olli rehn has fought for 3% of the deficit, or have you given up that fight?
madam president, the whole world has just learned this afternoon that the nobel prize in physics has been awarded to two europeans, mr higgs, a briton, and mr englert, a belgian. the truth is that these two great scientists who 30 years ago conceptualized that result had to wait 30 years for its realization, demonstration at cern. all this was european and as strange as it may seem, madam president, these two men did not know each other. it was last year when we invited them here to the stoa annual lecture, which i had the honor of chairing, that's when they first met. this tells us that europe has immense potential, but that we still live far apart within our borders. and there is much to be done, madam president: the state of the era has been unsatisfactory both in terms of the mobility of researchers and the portability of pension funds, social security systems, the lack of cooperation between universities, the lack of coordination of national resources with science funding. we are far from reaching 3%, but it is particularly unsatisfactory in terms of the convergence of scientific and technological potential in the different regions. the framework programmes are an island in the middle of nowhere, they have provided incentives for this collaboration, they have fostered competition at european level, they have promoted scientific excellence and they have encouraged the convergence of agendas. this is why better and more effective monitoring of member states' contributions to the era is needed.
mr president, the istanbul convention is a great step forward. it is the first international legally binding instrument for preventing and combating all forms of violence against women. this convention advocates the inclusion of the principle of equality between men and women in national legal systems and the repeal of all discriminatory laws and practices. this convention provides for measures to raise awareness and educate and also for measures to create specialised and immediate support services for women victims of violence. my country, portugal, has been leading the process of ratifying the istanbul convention. it was the first european union state to ratify it last february. other than that, only italy. i hope that the other member states will quickly follow this good example because combating violence against women remains a priority. unfortunately, this phenomenon is universal and affects all cultures and social backgrounds with dramatic consequences for the victims, their families and society. the union must make an effort in this area. i am grateful to the commissioner and the council representative for their words, but i would like to ask: first, what concrete measures will the european institutions take to speed up the ratification process of the istanbul convention? secondly, the european union must be a strong ally of the member states in the elimination of all forms of violence against women. how do you intend to support the member states in this fight, especially those countries where this phenomenon is most pronounced?
mr president, violence against women is a serious violation of human rights and i therefore ask the commissioner when will there be a european directive on gender-based violence? we know that every year, in every country, women die as victims of violence. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european parliament is able to exercise its right to vote in the european parliament. nor is it clear that the istanbul convention, adopted in 2011, has not yet been ratified by the various member states. pressure is needed on member states to do so quickly, as it needs 10 countries to ratify it before it can enter into force. on the 11th, we will mark the international day of the girl child. we also have a symbol that is malala, who is a strong candidate for the sakharov prize, meaning that while all of this is important, we need to act and we need proper legislation to protect women.
i think that parliament should support the european commission's initiative to launch negotiations for a bilateral investment treaty between the european union and china. the commission also found that the chinese exporting producers had a significant market share in the union market. in fact, china is a major european investment destination and the union is one of the targets of chinese investment and therefore it makes perfect sense to negotiate an investment treaty between the two economies. however, this mandate cannot be a free mandate, it must be conditional. the first condition is that the priority objective is to correct the existing asymmetry in access to reciprocal investment and to establish a level playing field given the extensive barriers to foreign investment on the chinese side. in addition, the union should set limits on direct investment for security or other reasons, e.g. exclusion from the audiovisual sector, and ensure the principles of non-discrimination between national and foreign companies, ensure a level playing field between private and state-owned enterprises, define the rights but also the obligations of investors, preserve the policy space of both parties, e.g. in environmental regulation, prevent social and environmental dumping, safeguard intellectual property rights and ensure the transparency of investor state dispute settlement. the union cannot but take advantage of this opportunity to establish a kind of european model investment treaty which will serve as a precedent for the forthcoming negotiations on investment treaties. and i think the union cannot lag behind the united states, whose model international foreign investment agreement of 2012 includes all these requirements. this resolution is also very timely for the european parliament because the council is due to approve its negotiating mandate on 18 october and we hope that it will take account of this resolution of the european parliament.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the day after its adoption by the commission, the european parliament adopted a resolution on the proposals for a european banking union, stressing that any relevant change in supervision, including transfers of powers to other institutions, should be accompanied by an equivalent increase in transparency and accountability by these institutions to parliament, which should have the right to put all questions and full powers in respect of appointments and procedures of a budgetary nature. the agreement reached provides for strong parliamentary scrutiny of the exercise of the ecb's supervisory functions, through regular exchanges of views with the relevant parliamentary committee, closed oral debates with the committee's bureau and improved access to information, including to the non-confidential parts of the minutes of the supervisory board. full cooperation between the two institutions in the field of investigations is also guaranteed.
in writing. − on 28-29 june 2012, the european council called for the creation of a banking union based on three pillars: single banking supervision, a european resolution fund (resolution mechanism) (for banking sector failures) and a european deposit guarantee scheme. in the course of the negotiations between the european parliament and the council on the proposal for the single supervisory mechanism, parliament requested that, in addition to the regulation conferring specific tasks on the european central bank with regard to policies relating to the prudential supervision of credit institutions, an interinstitutional agreement be concluded between parliament and the european central bank. the agreement reached provides for strong parliamentary scrutiny of the exercise of the supervisory functions of the european central bank, through regular exchanges of views with the competent parliamentary committee, and improved access to information, including to the non-confidential parts of the minutes of the supervisory board. full cooperation between the two institutions in the field of investigations is also guaranteed. the draft interinstitutional agreement provides for parliamentary scrutiny of the selection process for the president of the supervisory board, which is welcomed. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this report and i call for the single supervisory mechanism to be implemented quickly so that the financial system is stable and can guarantee the necessary financing for the european economy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it advocates strong parliamentary scrutiny of the ecb's supervisory functions, through regular exchanges of views with the relevant parliamentary committee and better access to information, including the non-confidential parts of the minutes of the supervisory board.
in writing. − in the context of the creation of a banking union, the european parliament and the european central bank agreed on a set of rules aimed at strengthening parliament's democratic control over the ecb's new supervisory powers. this interinstitutional agreement between the european parliament and the ecb arises in the context of the creation of a single european supervisory system, under which the ecb becomes the ultimate body for european banking supervision. the aim of this agreement is to regulate the relationship between the two institutions in such a way as to safeguard the independence of the ecb and the confidentiality of its supervisory activities and to allow the necessary democratic control and legitimacy over the ecb's actions.
in writing. − the institutional agreement (ia) in question is the result of negotiations which were concluded at the beginning of september 2013 and which allowed the european parliament to vote in favour of the single supervisory mechanism (ssm) regulation. in june 2012, the european council called for the creation of a banking union for euro area countries based on three pillars, namely a single banking supervision, a resolution mechanism and a european deposit guarantee scheme. in september 2012, the commission's proposals for a single supervisory mechanism were adopted, which give the european central bank a supervisory role over banks both in the euro area and in member states wishing to participate in the ssm. parliament called for an interinstitutional agreement (iaa) between parliament and the ecb to be concluded in addition to the regulation conferring specific tasks on the european central bank with regard to policies relating to the prudential supervision of credit institutions. this agreement would have to refer to the practical arrangements for democratic accountability and control over the exercise of the tasks conferred on the ecb. the agreement reached reflects parliament's requirements and provides for strong parliamentary scrutiny of the exercise of the ecb's supervisory functions, through regular exchanges of views with the relevant parliamentary committee, closed oral debates with the committee's bureau and improved access to information, including to the non-confidential parts of the minutes of the supervisory board.
in writing. - an agreement between the european central bank and the european parliament, which is supposed to be about democratic accountability and control, does not legitimise a process which is essentially illegitimate, undemocratic and an attack on the sovereignty of the peoples. whatever the role of this parliament, it does not legitimise the usurpation of supervisory powers of national institutions, in particular the banco de portugal, by the ecb, with its false independence, intrinsically linked to the interests of large financial capital, to the maintenance and deepening of the speculative process and to a policy whose objective is the so-called price stability and the control of inflation, imposing the destruction of social, labour and national rights. the eu is using the crisis to create mechanisms that facilitate even greater concentration and centralisation of financial capital. the highly secretive nature and very limited access of members - and without any participation by the institutions of national sovereignty - to information on the ecb's activities in the framework of the single supervisory mechanism, in the process of selecting the chairman of the supervisory board, as well as the total absence of political, democratic control of its actions, demonstrate what we have been denouncing in relation to its undemocratic functioning and that these mechanisms will not mean any greater supervision and control of banking activity.
in writing. − this agreement provides for strong parliamentary scrutiny of the exercise of the ecb's supervisory functions through regular exchanges of views with the relevant parliamentary committee, oral discussions behind closed doors with the committee's bureau and improved access to information, including to the non-confidential parts of the minutes of the supervisory board. full cooperation between the two institutions in the field of investigations is also guaranteed. the draft ida also provides for parliamentary scrutiny of the selection process for the chairman of the supervisory board. the ep can thus exercise its supervisory function properly. a single supervisory mechanism is essential to restore confidence in the eu banking sector.
in writing. − the institutional agreement (ia) in question is the result of complex negotiations which were concluded at the beginning of september 2013 and which allowed the european parliament to vote in favour of the single supervisory mechanism (ssm) regulation. in the course of the negotiations between parliament and the council on the proposal for a single supervisory mechanism, parliament requested that, in addition to the regulation conferring specific tasks on the european central bank with regard to policies relating to the prudential supervision of credit institutions, an interinstitutional agreement (iia) be concluded between parliament and the ecb. that interinstitutional agreement should lay down, in accordance with article 20 (9) of that regulation, the practical arrangements for democratic accountability and oversight of the ecb in the exercise of the tasks conferred on it. the committee on constitutional affairs examined the merits and found the agreement to be valid in the light of the treaties. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the committee on constitutional affairs was asked to examine the substance of the interinstitutional agreement (iaa) between parliament and the european central bank, which aims to define the practical arrangements for democratic accountability and control over the exercise of the tasks conferred on the ecb. the examination focused on an overall assessment of the institutional validity of the supervision requested by parliament, considering the conditions of the interinstitutional agreement to be valid in all respects. thus, the conferral of supervisory powers approved in the committee responsible and subject to the provisions of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) should counterbalance the conferral of powers to the ecb, which implies a significant responsibility for the financial stability of the union, with appropriate accountability requirements. my vote takes account of the principle of openness to approve the conclusion of this interinstitutional agreement on the practical arrangements for democratic accountability and control.
in writing. − the interinstitutional agreement (iia) is the result of complex negotiations between the european parliament and the european central bank (ecb) for the creation of a banking union in the euro area countries, which presupposes a single banking supervision, a european resolution fund and a european deposit guarantee scheme. the ssm ii provides for strict parliamentary scrutiny of the exercise of ecb supervisory functions and the process for selecting the chair of the supervisory board, as well as for full cooperation between the two institutions in the context of investigations. i am voting in favour of this report because it is in line with the iia.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that this directive is very important in the union's environmental policy. its scope covers some 200 types of projects, from the construction of bridges, ports, motorways and landfills to intensive poultry or pig farming. the eia directive establishes the simple but fundamental principle of informed decision: before approving the implementation of a public or approved project likely to have an impact on the environment, the competent authorities of the member states are legally obliged to obtain the information necessary to carry out an environmental impact assessment. i am convinced that a truly sustainable development model needs to be adopted throughout the union and i express my full and unwavering support for the commission's proposal. the proposed amendments are therefore intended to strengthen the proposal by completing it, with the aim of making it even more incisive and effective, simplifying transposition into national legislation and facilitating the achievement of environmental protection objectives.
in writing. − directive 2011/92/ec aims to ensure the environmental sustainability of projects falling within its scope, from the construction of bridges, ports, motorways, landfills, etc. over its 28 years of application, the directive has been successful, but some shortcomings have also been identified which have given rise to a significant number of legal conflicts. to address these problems and to bring the text of the directive into line with the new priorities of the union, the european commission has put forward this proposal for a revision. the proposal introduces biodiversity, the use of natural resources, climate change and the risks of natural and man-made disasters among the factors on which the impact of a project should be assessed. it is also intended to strengthen the role of the public concerned at all stages of the procedure and to ensure full independence between the competent authority and the prosecutor in order to ensure the credibility of the whole procedure and to exclude any conflict of interest. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i agree with the proposed revision which aims to streamline procedures and increase the quality of assessments, introduce new factors to assess environmental issues, improve the quality of information used in the eia and simplify procedures.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the environmental impact assessment of certain public and private projects, taking into account the need to review this directive in the light of new political, legal and technical challenges and to align this legislation with eu priorities on the environment, biodiversity, use of natural resources, climate change and natural disasters. a strengthened directive will bring environmental, health and economic benefits through simplified and more efficient procedures.

in writing. - the report by mr zanoni deals with the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending council directive 2011/92/eu on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment. the current directive is a key element of eu environmental policy. its scope covers hundreds of project types, from the construction of bridges, ports, motorways and landfills to intensive poultry or pig farming. certain problems of harmonisation and interpretation of certain provisions have been identified and a revision is now required to bring the text of the directive into line with the new political priorities of the union, such as the soil strategy, the roadmap for a resource efficient europe and the europe 2020 strategy. i believe that in this review it is essential that the principle of informed decision before approval of a project likely to have an impact on the environment is maintained, with the involvement of the public and with experts who have the necessary technical skills to carry out the tasks provided for in the directive in a scientifically objective manner and with complete independence from the developer and the competent authorities themselves.
in writing. − the directive in question refers to environmental impact assessment (eia), which is essential to safeguard the public interest and the conservation of nature in decision-making on public and private projects, taking into account their effect on the environment. the practical experience of the eia over the last 25 years, despite the positive aspects it has brought to light, shows that improvements are possible by learning from experience and adapting the procedure to the changing political, legal and technical-scientific context. unfortunately, the vote in plenary has weakened the proposal considerably. a number of positive aspects have been lost because of the right-wing votes. we particularly regret the rejection of our proposal, which enshrined the right of the public to request an eia procedure for projects of interest, through mechanisms of active participation involving the population, local authorities and associations, including ngos. we are fighting for transparency and accessibility to the public, particularly via the internet, and for their comments to be taken into account in order to improve the quality of decisions and to contribute to raising awareness of environmental issues. on the positive side, we stress that the mandatory completion of the eia procedure in the case of shale gas exploration projects (the fracking controversy) has been enshrined.
in writing. − directive 2011/92/eu contains a legal provision requiring an environmental impact assessment (eia) for public or private projects likely to have significant effects on the environment, before their authorisation. it is agreed that the main objective of the directive has been achieved, the principles of environmental assessment have been harmonised across the eu by introducing minimum requirements with regard to the type of projects subject to assessment, the main obligations of the developer, the content of the assessment and the involvement of the competent authorities and the public. the overall objective of this proposal is to adjust the provisions of the eia directive in order to address its shortcomings, taking into account current environmental and socio-economic changes and challenges. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − directive 2011/92/eu on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment (eia directive) is the basis of the union's environment policy. over its 28 years of application, this directive has had some success in harmonising the principles of environmental assessment at european level, but it has only been subject to three minor amendments, when the political, legal and technical context has evolved considerably. it has therefore become necessary to revise it in order to adopt a model of truly sustainable development throughout the union. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the present report revises directive 2011/92/eu on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment (eia directive). this review aims to bring the legislative framework into line with the new political priorities of a union whose political, legal and technical context has evolved considerably. in line with the union's priorities, new factors to be taken into account when assessing projects likely to have an impact on the environment are introduced by means of legislation; these include biodiversity, the use of natural resources, climate change and the risks of natural and man-made disasters. the strengthening of the proposal, along with the above-mentioned alignment of procedures with the union's priorities, contributes to simplifying procedures, in particular as regards transposition into national law. given the urgency of providing the union with an instrument to ensure the sustainability of projects to be carried out on european territory, i voted in favour of the european parliament's proposal for a directive.

in writing. − this proposal for a recreational craft and watercraft directive updates the current european union rules on safety and environmental performance requirements for craft designed for private use activities. this proposal does not apply to vessels designed and used for the commercial carriage of passengers, which are regulated by directive 2009/45/ec and directive 2006/87/ec. the basic requirements that vessels will have to meet relate to stability and buoyancy, engine and electrical safety, and exhaust and noise emissions. to that end, products covered by this directive may only be placed on the market if the general safety requirements are met. the installation of on-board storage tanks or water treatment systems for vessels equipped with sanitary facilities will be mandatory to better protect the marine environment. the ce marking shall be extended to all internal or column driven engines without integrated exhaust. i therefore support this report.

in writing. - i approve this report. in line with the opinion of the european commission and the council, that after several rounds of negotiations, armenia is now ready to conclude the visa liberalisation agreement. the simplified visa system can give a new impetus to cooperation, and in particular to the mobility of citizens, which will be simplified thanks to the liberalized visa system. the new rules will make the procedures faster (the decision will have to be taken within 10 days, in urgent cases two days or less), cheaper (the visa fee for processing applications of armenian citizens will amount to eur 35) and less bureaucratic (the documents to be presented in relation to the purpose of the trip have been simplified for some categories of persons, in particular for close relatives, members of official delegations, students, teachers, businessmen, scientists, etc.) and there are also simplified criteria for issuing visas allowing multiple entries. the armenian government has already abolished the visa requirement for eu citizens with effect from january 2013. the conclusion of the agreements on visa liberalisation and readmission is a very important step in the mutual relations between armenia and the eu.
