in writing. − in defending the strengthening and good relations with neighbouring countries, the european union must give priority to promoting the values and basic principles of its construction and development, in favour of a community acquis which values the enlargement of the democratic area, the rule of law, good governance and human dignity. the visa facilitation contributes to the strengthening and implementation of the european neighbourhood policy action plan for armenia, enabling cooperation and mobility of citizens to be given a new impetus, and could accelerate economic and political integration with a region that also includes azerbaijan, belarus, georgia, moldova and ukraine.
in writing. - visa facilitation agreements have been linked to readmission agreements and seen as part of the same policy to combat illegal immigration. we are in favour of facilitating the issuing of visas. but as we have been denouncing, these agreements function as a bargaining chip between the eu and some third countries, for which the aim is to achieve greater visa facilitation (generally for their economic elites), in exchange for the readmission, cheaply, of the majority of their immigrants, usually workers, who seek work and a better life in eu countries. this in practice opens the way to the expulsion of all workers who, in the hope of a better job and life, immigrate to another country but find themselves confronted by a criminalizing, repressive and inhumane policy of the eu, which manages the entry and exit of immigrants in accordance with the interests of the workforce at any given moment. in other words, a policy in which immigrants, placed in an illegal situation, are exposed to networks of exploitation and trafficking of immigrants, with the perverse effect of further pressuring the reduction of wages and labour and social rights in eu countries.
in writing. − the partnership and cooperation agreement (pca) has played an important role in the mutual relations between the eu and certain third countries for several years. since the late 1990s, the european union has concluded 10 apt, one of which with armenia, which entered into force on 31 may 1999. the agreement provided a framework for cooperation in a number of areas, but there are no provisions on visa facilitation. in september 2011, the european commission proposed the opening of negotiations on a visa facilitation agreement between the eu and armenia, which was signed on 17 december 2012, but requires the approval of the european parliament before it can enter into force. the eu has already concluded visa facilitation agreements with nine non-eu countries. as far as the countries of the south caucasus are concerned, so far only an agreement of this kind has been concluded with georgia, but negotiations with azerbaijan are already under way. the time has now come to approve this eu-armenia agreement which will greatly facilitate the issuing of visas between both parties.
in writing. − in the joint declaration on an eu-armenia mobility partnership of 27 october 2011, the parties decided to establish a mobility partnership based on reciprocity, with the aim of better managing legal and labour migration, including circular and temporary migration. the european parliament's report concludes, in line with the opinion of the european commission and the council and after several rounds of negotiations, that armenia is now ready to conclude the visa liberalisation agreement. in view of the positive opinions and with no objections, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the draft legislative resolution approves the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european union and the republic of armenia. the opinion of the committee responsible is in favour of the conclusion of the agreement which will facilitate the issuing of visas, thanks to the liberalized visa regime. the partnership agreements are based on the principles that guided the creation of the union and provide frameworks for cooperation in various fields, including economic cooperation, but the eu-armenia agreement did not include provisions for visa facilitation. in the light of the above, my vote supports the progress on visa liberalisation as committed in the eastern partnership summit declaration of may 2009.
in writing. − partnerships with third countries promote the european union's action on the international scene, which is based on the principles which guided its creation. the 1999 partnership and cooperation agreement with armenia played a central role in the country's mutual relations with the eu, but no provisions were made at that time on the issue of visas. the european neighbourhood policy action plan has also opened up new opportunities for partnership, including the start of dialogue on the movement of persons, readmission and visas. at present, and after all these steps and negotiations, armenia is ready to conclude the visa liberalisation agreement. this simplified visa system could boost cooperation and, above all, the mobility of citizens. not only will the procedures be faster, cheaper (a fee of €35), but much less bureaucratic, and there will also be simplified criteria for issuing visas authorising multiple entries. as this is an essential step for the mutual relations between armenia and the eu, i support the conclusion of this agreement.
in writing. − readmission agreements are inseparable from visa facilitation agreements and part of the same policy of combating illegal immigration. in practice, as we have been denouncing, these agreements function as a bargaining chip between the eu and some third countries, for which the aim is to achieve greater visa facilitation (generally for their economic elites), in exchange for the readmission, cheaply, of the majority of their immigrants, usually workers, who are looking for work and a better life in eu countries. it is basically a question of expelling all those workers who, in the hope of a better job and a better life, emigrate to another country but are confronted with a criminalising, repressive and inhumane policy which manages the entry and exit of immigrants in accordance with the interests of the labour force at any given moment and the extortion of the greatest possible surplus value from their work. a policy in which immigrants, often illegals, are subjected to the most despicable exploitation in employment and society. it is the logic of the international division of labour, through which the eu seeks to impose on third countries such as armenia the role of suppliers of cheap labour. we voted against it.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that another, deeper level of integration is needed in the form of an association agreement, recently negotiated between the parties, which will strengthen cooperation between armenia and the european union. i am in favour of and approve of the conclusion of this agreement, which will mainly facilitate the mobility of citizens, which is essential for building contacts between people. however, i call on the commission to monitor the implementation of the two agreements in order to identify any uncomfortable provisions that need to be corrected so that the benefits of the simplified visa regime can be fully exploited. i also believe that negotiations should be intensified with regard to the conclusion of similar agreements with azerbaijan, the last country in the south caucasus region.
in writing. - i am in favour of and approve of the conclusion of the agreement, which will mainly facilitate the mobility of citizens, in particular those residing without authorisation.
in writing. − the conclusion of this readmission agreement, together with the visa liberalisation agreement and the recently negotiated association agreement, are very important steps towards strengthening cooperation between armenia and the eu. it will thus allow the eu to play a more active role in the south caucasus area and will enhance mobility and people-to-people contacts, which are essential elements for the development of economic, social and cultural links with this area. to balance the visa facilitation agreement, effective measures are needed to prevent and control illegal immigration flows. this readmission agreement thus aims to establish, on a reciprocal basis, rapid and effective procedures for the identification and safe return of national citizens, third-country nationals and stateless persons residing without authorisation in the territory of the other party. having ratified several important international conventions, including the geneva convention relating to the status of refugees, and being a member of the eastern partnership, which is based on commitments to safeguard the principles of international law and fundamental rights, i believe that armenia has the necessary requirements to ensure that the rights of the persons covered by the agreement are respected.
in writing. - as a complement to the facilitation of the issuing of visas for armenian citizens, i believe it is important to agree with armenia how the readmission of persons residing in the european union without authorisation will be processed in the country. these two strands respect the european union's priorities on immigration: organising legal immigration and combating illegal immigration. this agreement should contribute to the understanding of armenian citizens of the need to comply with legal requirements when immigrating to the union and further engage the union with the aim of promoting the acceleration of political association and deepening of economic integration of armenia in line with the objectives of the eastern partnership of the european neighbourhood policy.
in writing. − as part of the process of strengthening relations with armenia and the effective implementation of the european neighbourhood policy, the european union should ensure mechanisms for the mobility of citizens that ensure an environment of mutual trust and transparency with neighbouring countries, such as armenia. it is in this context that the agreement between the eu and armenia on the readmission of persons from both sides residing without authorisation on the other side of the border is of particular importance, establishing a basis of reciprocity, fast and effective procedures for the identification and safe and orderly return of such persons, facilitating the mobility of citizens and fostering contacts and coexistence between persons of different nationalities.

in writing. - i approve and support the commission proposal, which responds to parliament's resolutions of march 1998 on the green paper on the general principles of eu food law and of june 2001 on the white paper on food safety. i particularly support the introduction of general principles and conditions for the use of claims and welcome the creation of the list of nutrition claims, conditions for comparative claims, the distinction between health claims relating to bodily functions and those relating to the reduction of disease risk or the definition of a consumer based on the ecj judgments. however, there are several aspects of the proposal which need improvement. furthermore, i believe that a ban on all general and implied health claims would be a disproportionate measure. existing legislation on misleading advertising and food labelling already prohibits the use of misleading claims. i therefore believe that it would be preferable to enforce existing legislation more consistently and more effectively than to introduce legislation whose good implementation is unlikely.
in writing. − i support this draft regulation and stress the importance of creating a list of permitted health claims for food other than those referring to the reduction of disease risk or to children's development and health.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on permitted health claims for food, considering that nutrition and health claims must not be false, ambiguous or misleading.
in writing. − it is essential to ensure that consumers are properly informed so that they know exactly what food they are consuming and can make an informed and conscious choice without being told characteristics that are not entirely true or factual. this may indeed be the case with food-related health claims. i therefore vote in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. − as regards the health claims regulation, in force since 2006, nutritional profiles are still to be implemented. it's extremely difficult to divide food into good and bad food. there's only one good and one less good diet or lifestyle. so it makes no sense to evaluate food individually. i therefore disagree that an arbitrary and unjustified condition should now be introduced for a health claim. this is not the correct way to establish nutritional profiles.
in writing. − the commission proposal to amend regulation no 432/2012, which the european parliament resolution sought to oppose, aims to introduce carbohydrates in the annex (list of permitted health claims) with the health claim carbohydrates contribute to the maintenance of normal brain function. this claim may only be made if the consumer is informed that the beneficial effect is obtained with a daily intake of 130 g of carbohydrates from all sources. the rules for the use of the health claim are further laid down only for foods containing at least 20 g of carbohydrates metabolised by humans, excluding polyols, and containing the nutrition claim low in shakers or no added sugars, ensuring that the use of the claim will not contribute to an increase in the consumption of sugars, taking into account dietary recommendations. we believe that the claim and the transparent rules for its use are correct, given the clear information that is intended to be made available to the consumer, and we therefore supported the commission's proposal by voting against the resolution which objected to it.
in writing. − nutrition and health claims must not be false, ambiguous or misleading as provided for in article 3 (2) (a) of regulation (ec) no 1924/2006. the draft commission regulation amending regulation (eu) no 432/2012 establishes a list of permitted health claims made on foods other than those referring to the reduction of disease risk or to children's development and health.

in writing. the resolution objecting to the commission proposal which essentially amends three annexes to regulations relating to: (i) specific rules for food business operators on the hygiene of food of animal origin; (ii) rules on official controls for trichinella in meat; and (iii) the conditions under which meat from animals which have been subjected to emergency slaughter outside the slaughterhouse is fit for human consumption was rejected. the commission proposal calls into question the work of official veterinarians, reducing their tasks and making their work more difficult. as a result, the number of unchecked and unverified body parts may increase. in addition, given the rapid processing rate of large slaughterhouses, the changes in question could lead to situations where potential hazards to human health are not detected, where meat unfit for human consumption may enter the food chain, or where abnormalities such as abscesses or tumours are not detected in breach of animal welfare rules, and if organs are not properly examined, the likelihood of epizootic disease detection may even be reduced. we voted against the commission's proposal.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 853/2004 specifies hygiene rules for food of animal origin. regulation (ec) no 854/2004 lays down the general principles for official controls, including compliance with community legislation on hygiene, animal by-products and animal welfare, and provides that the official veterinarian is responsible for determining whether meat is fit for human consumption. chapter i of section i of annex i to that regulation specifies that the veterinarian must ensure that the procedures carried out by food business operators are followed at all times, ensuring that the meat is free from any abnormalities or pathophysiological changes, and that additional examinations such as incision and palpation may be carried out for this purpose. the amendment to the regulation proposed by the commission would allow such additional examinations only if epidemiological data or food chain information, ante-mortem inspection findings or post-mortem visual detection of relevant anomalies indicate risks to public or animal health or animal welfare. this change may result in potential hazards and/or abnormalities not being detected, as meat unfit for consumption may enter the food chain, putting human health at risk.

in writing. - we voted in favour of this resolution and we regret that it has been ignored by the majority of this parliament. the resolution was intended to reject a proposal from the european commission which, under the false pretext of greater safety (an argument which, not by chance, the commission borrows from the major airlines), seeks to change the rules on flight time, opening the door to longer working hours for pilots and cabin crew. this proposal contradicts the available scientific studies and evidence, presented in at least five reports, relating to the factors of fatigue, night work and sleep deprivation. working and safety conditions are compromised with flight periods exceeding 10 hours and a maximum combined duration of prevention periods and flight duty periods subject to a maximum of 18 hours. it is unacceptable that the safety of crew, pilots and passengers is jeopardised by requiring 11-hour working hours, affecting workers' rights and their lives in order to serve the interests and profits of the aviation monopolies once again. we note once again that the right and the social democrats have joined hands to increase this burden on the big employers in the sector.
in writing. − the european commission proposal was intended to create a single legislation for civil aviation safety, as it sets limits and ceilings that do not exist in current european legislation and updates, according to scientific criteria and after consulting stakeholders, facts such as maximum flight and standby time. i believe that the commission's proposal is appropriate to the requirements of the sector and the desirable safety levels in this activity, and i therefore disagree with the position taken by the rapporteur and the committee responsible and voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution by the committee on transport, which proposes to reject the european commission's proposal to implement new rules containing a large number of provisions against what scientific experts consider to be safe, allowing, for example, working hours of up to 22 hours for pilots and cabin crew or night flights lasting between 11 and 12 and a half hours when scientific work on this subject rejects working hours in these conditions exceeding nine or ten hours. we will continue to fight against this and other decisions which insist on putting financial interests ahead of the common interest.

in writing. − the european commission (ec) proposal on ftl aims to create a single legislation for civil aviation safety, as it sets limits and ceilings on elements that do not exist in current european legislation and updates, according to scientific criteria and meetings with stakeholders, facts such as the maximum weekly and night flight time, maximum standby limits, extension of the period considered to be night. from the implementing measures the ec has presented the so-called certification specifications on ftl, to establish minimum rules in the member states. where the rules of a particular member state are more protective than those of the ftl, they shall override the harmonised rules of the ftl. for these reasons, and because i believe that the ec is balancing the safety of pilots and crew in their daily work, i am voting against this motion for a resolution, since it is intended to overturn the proposals put forward by the ec.

in writing. - i support this report in supporting the continuation and development of the eurosur system, since border surveillance is an area where union action undeniably has a european added value compared to purely national measures. illegal immigration and cross-border crime are by their nature phenomena that extend beyond the territory of the member states. it should be noted, however, that the proposed financing scheme for eurosur is very complex, resulting from the three different levels of management (direct centralised management, indirect centralised management and shared management) and the financing schedule. in addition, as regards expenditure on the national coordination centres and measures implemented in neighbouring third countries, i would point out that there are no criteria for allocating resources.
in writing. − free movement is one of the fundamental principles of the european union, and the ability to move within the community without internal border controls is one of its most positive results. on the other hand, free movement is also fundamental to the success of the single market in europe. in this respect, schengen should be strengthened by better management of the external borders of the european union with the aim of ensuring full and mutual trust between member states. member states should therefore cooperate with neighbouring third countries in order to protect migrants, prevent irregular migration and combat cross-border crime. personal data should be shared and processed through eurosur only when necessary and in duly justified cases, with appropriate safeguards. furthermore, no personal data should be shared with third countries. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i welcome the new european border surveillance system (eurosur), approved today by the european parliament, which will better protect the eu's external borders and the lives of migrants. eurosur will improve the detection, prevention and combating of irregular migration and organised crime and help save the lives of migrants when they are in danger. member states will ensure respect for fundamental rights and the principle of non-refoulement, which prevents them from handing migrants over to a country where their life or liberties are threatened. thank you very much.
in writing. − the european border surveillance system - eurosur - is expected to become operational later this year, from 2 december, in all member states at the southern and eastern external borders (including portugal) and will be operational in the remaining member states from 1 december 2014. with a view to better sharing responsibilities in the management of the eu's external borders, this system will allow member states' authorities to cooperate and share operational information with each other and with frontex in order to reduce the loss of human life at sea, as well as to strengthen internal security by preventing cross-border crime such as trafficking in human beings and drug smuggling. it should thus contribute to improving the situational awareness and the response capacity of the member states and of frontex, with a huge potential to detect emergency situations and prevent tragedies like last week's in lampedusa from happening again. cooperation with neighbouring third countries is also of particular importance in ensuring the effectiveness of this system. it has also been safeguarded that the exchange and processing of personal data through eurosur may only take place where strictly necessary and in duly justified cases, with appropriate safeguards.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it promotes the exchange of information and improves cooperation between member states and between the agencies involved in border surveillance. the proposed system is essential for a better sharing of responsibility in the management of external borders and for a better response to the influx of migrants into the european area, which often ends in tragedy.
in writing. - the tragic events off lampedusa are a striking example of the human despair and the difficulty that some member states, especially those exposed to illegal immigration, feel in controlling their borders, which are the external borders of the union. i deeply regret what has happened and regret that thousands of people have already lost their lives trying to reach european shores in search of better living conditions. i am in favour of a european union which is in solidarity with those who suffer the most and able to welcome them in cases of need, but at the same time i recognise the fundamental duty of the member states to ensure the stability of their populations and the sustainability of their states. i reject as a starting point for the debates on immigration and asylum both the idea of a fortress europe and the idea of an open-door europe. these maximalist positions do nothing to contribute to a thorough debate and to the difficult decisions which this matter necessarily entails. eurosur can be an important means of achieving this balanced strategy of firmness and humanity.
in writing. − improving the control and surveillance system at the external borders of the european union is an imperative to ensure greater reliability and effectiveness of free movement in the european area. it is in this context that i value the completion of the european border surveillance system (eurosur), which can also be crucial in helping member states to respect international maritime law and save the lives of migrants, especially from north africa. in this process, it is also crucial to ensure the exchange of information and to improve cooperation with neighbouring third countries, between member states and between the agencies involved, in particular europol, the eagf, the european maritime safety agency (emsa), the community fisheries control agency (cfp) and the european union satellite centre (eusc). i would, however, like to draw attention to the fact that the proposed funding scheme for eurosur is very complex, given the three different levels of management (direct centralised management, indirect centralised management and shared management) and the funding schedule covering the current mff and the 2014-2020 mff. it is therefore urgent to ensure that measures are taken to avoid jeopardising the budgetary support for the operation and implementation of the system.

in writing. − free movement is one of the fundamental principles of the european union, and the ability to move within it without having to face internal border controls is one of its most positive outcomes. many people make use of this freedom, and public opinion ranks free movement among the most significant benefits achieved by the union. as far as our economy is concerned, too, free movement is fundamental to the success of the single market. schengen cannot be abolished. it should instead be strengthened through better management of the eu's external borders in order to ensure full and mutual trust between member states. eurosur aims to strengthen the control of the external borders of the schengen area. eurosur shall establish a mechanism for member states' authorities carrying out border surveillance activities to cooperate and share operational information with each other and with the agency in order to reduce the loss of life at sea and the number of illegal migrants entering the eu undetected, as well as to enhance internal security by preventing cross-border crime such as trafficking in human beings and drug smuggling. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. the report by mr panayotov is on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending directive 2006/66/ec on batteries and accumulators and waste batteries and accumulators as regards the placing on the market of portable batteries and accumulators containing cadmium for use in cordless power tools. this proposal aims to amend the directive by limiting the exemption for the use of cadmium in portable batteries and accumulators for cordless power tools until 31 december 2015. considering that the total market share of nimh batteries in the eu cordless power tool market is relatively low compared to nicd and li-ion batteries, which are mainly used in the nordic countries, and considering the harmful effects of cadmium on the environment, i agree with this limitation. however, i accept that an extension of the exemption for another year would allow for a reasonable compromise, protecting the interests of both consumers and businesses while ensuring the protection of the environment and human health. this additional time is sufficient for technological development, sharing of best practices, learning and innovation in this field.
in writing. − directive 2006/66/ec prohibits the placing on the market of portable batteries or accumulators, including those incorporated into appliances, with a cadmium content exceeding 0.002% by weight, providing for the exception for alarm and emergency systems, medical equipment and cordless power tools. this directive provides for the european commission to review the exemption for cordless tools and proposes a limited exemption until 31 december 2015, taking into account the effects of cadmium on the environment and health. a text negotiated with the council and the commission was adopted giving the exemption for cordless tools another year to allow the recycling industry and consumers along the chain to make the necessary adjustments to alternative technologies. the commission has also provided information on the number of active substances in the product concerned, the number of active substances in the product concerned and the number of active substances in the product concerned. emergency alarm systems, including emergency lighting and medical equipment are also exempted from the application of that directive. these are changes which we consider reasonable and acceptable.
in writing. − directive 2006/66/ec of the european parliament and of the council prohibits the placing on the market of portable batteries or accumulators, including those incorporated into appliances, with a cadmium content exceeding 0,002% by weight. however, an exemption is provided for alarm and emergency systems, including emergency lighting, medical equipment and wireless power tools, authorised until 31 december 2015. there are, however, still some constraints to this being possible. therefore, an extension of the exemption for another year would allow for a reasonable compromise, protecting the interests of both consumers and companies in the value chain. at the same time, the protection of the environment and human health would be ensured, and at the same time additional time would be needed for technological development, sharing of best practices, learning and innovation in this field. the commission notes that the exemption for nicd batteries is not limited to the period from 1 january 2015 to 31 december 2016. that's why i'm in favour.
in writing. − pursuant to article 4 of directive 2006/66/ec, the commission is to review the exemption for cordless power tools. the current proposal aims to amend the directive by limiting the exemption for the use of cadmium in portable batteries and accumulators for cordless power tools until 31 december 2015. in view of the effects of cadmium on the environment, the commission's proposal is welcomed. the deadline was set by the commission following an impact assessment which combined the socioeconomic and environmental dimensions of the removal of nicd batteries from cordless power tools by comparing the environmental impact of the removal of cadmium over time. the european parliament suggests extending the exemption for nicd batteries for another year, until 31 december 2016, thus ensuring additional time to allow all economic operators along the value chain to adapt the relevant alternative technologies in all regions of the eu in a uniform manner and in line with the natural business cycle of cordless power tools. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − cadmium is a heavy metal that produces toxic effects when it accumulates in the environment and in the body, even in small amounts, as it remains for an indefinite period and can cause irreversible damage. it is a metal that is available in various forms and substances, including batteries for cordless power tools. when used for this purpose, cadmium can be 100% recycled, substantially reducing the risks to the environment and human health. the commission notes that the exemption for nickel-cadmium batteries is not limited to the period from 1 january 2015 to 31 december 2016. at the same time, this additional time will promote technological development, sharing of best practices and innovation in this area.

in writing. − a high level of security in the eu and the schengen area can only be ensured if there is coherent, effective and concerted european action in the fight against crime and criminal networks. the exchange of information between member states for the purposes of criminal investigation, prevention and detection of crime and ensuring public order and security forms the basis for police cooperation in the eu, which is of particular importance in an area without internal border controls. the existing legislation and agreements have been complemented by eu systems and instruments such as sis ii or the europol information system. the commission's communication confirms what we have been advocating for a long time: the current range of tools is sufficient and no new law enforcement databases or new eu-level information exchange tools will be needed at this stage. it is necessary to improve the application of existing instruments and streamline the communication channels used, as in the case of the prüm decision, which should have been transposed by august 2011, but several member states have not yet exchanged data under this decision due to lack of human and financial resources.

in writing. − indeed, crossborder crime is increasing globally and potentially more acute in the european union, not only because of the elimination of internal borders which facilitates mobility, but also because of the increasing capacity of criminal networks to operate internationally and in several countries, with concerted and simultaneous intervention by multiple partners and in different areas. it is therefore imperative to ensure more effective cross-border mechanisms for the exchange of information and better coordination of operational activities, which allow for an increase in the efficiency of crime prevention and response capacity. it is also important to ensure respect for privacy and data protection, as well as the principles of proportionality, transparency and accountability in the access to and use of available resources and data. the training of european police should also be improved as a factor contributing to strengthening mutual trust between the different police forces and, at the same time, to improving the exchange of information and cross-border cooperation.
in writing. - the report finds that crossborder crime is increasing in the eu. in doing so, it ignores or omits the many decisions which are at the root of this phenomenon, such as the free movement of capital, the deregulation of the financial sector, the deepening of the single market, and others. in doing so, it maintains intact the macroeconomic orientations that are at the root of the increase in organised crime and proposes the automation of information exchange processes, including cross-border access to national databases, using existing channels such as europol. we are in full support of the fight against crossborder organised crime, but we believe that if we do not use the above-mentioned macroeconomic instruments, this fight will be totally ineffective, apart from the fact that we are automatically allowing organisations without any democratic control, such as europol, to have access to national databases which may contain sensitive information, which is clearly dangerous for the rights, freedoms and guarantees of citizens.
in writing. − the internal security strategy calls for the development of a more effective global model for information exchange. the exchange of information on criminal activities across borders forms the basis for police cooperation in the european union and is particularly important in an area without internal border controls. in the face of the increase in cross-border crime in the eu, an efficient and secure exchange of police information that respects data protection and fundamental rights is becoming increasingly important. the wide range of means of collecting, processing and sharing information among eu police authorities thus needs to be further coherent and consolidated in order to increase the security of eu citizens. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the assessment of the different instruments, channels and means available in the eu for the crossborder exchange of police information finds that the current range of different instruments, channels and means is complex and dispersed, leading to ineffective use of the instruments and inadequate democratic oversight at eu level, as well as in some cases to misuse of the function and access. this resolution calls on the commission to review community and national legislation, including international (bilateral) agreements, governing the cross-border exchange of police information and to carry out an independent external evaluation of existing instruments for the exchange of police information in the european union in order to assess their measurable impact.
in writing. − the stockholm programme takes on board the need for greater coherence and consolidation of the means of collecting, processing and sharing information between police authorities in the european union. at a time when crossborder crime is on the rise in the eu, it is extremely important that there is this police cooperation with the exchange of information on criminal activities, always respecting data protection and the fundamental rights of citizens. it is also recommended that existing tools and channels for this purpose be streamlined, such as the automatic use of the europol channel, which will allow for better information exchange. i believe that crossborder cooperation and the improvement of the exchange of information will strengthen mutual trust between police forces, and i therefore support this motion for a resolution.

in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that the right to petition the european parliament by citizens and residents of the european union, individually or on behalf of associations, is an ancient right, conferred by the treaty on the functioning of the european union (article 227) and by the charter of fundamental rights of the eu (article 44). the right to petition is an essential democratic instrument, as it provides members of the european parliament with a realistic assessment of issues of concern to citizens and demonstrates that the european parliament is prepared to intervene directly to promote and protect citizens' rights.
in writing. - the often proclaimed aim of bringing elected representatives at european level closer to the electorate is given a privileged instrument in the petitions submitted to the european parliament. i would therefore like to see it more widely disseminated and more frequently used by citizens. if the importance and irreplaceable nature of representative democracy in our political system is clear, so too is the need to respect the concerns and initiatives directly promoted by groups of citizens. the fact that the european union has dedicated this year to its citizens shows how far citizenship issues cannot be confined to electoral and trade union participation. there is a wide range of issues and causes today that mobilise people and to which policy-makers cannot, or at least should not, be indifferent.

in writing. − in 2012, the committee on petitions registered 1,986 petitions, most of them concerning fundamental rights, the environment, the internal market and the economic and social crisis, figures which are not at all unconnected with the difficulties faced by the people in each member state in the context of the structural crisis of capitalism and the so-called austerity policies in the eu. the commission has decided to accept 1 406 petitions, of which 853 were sent to the commission for further examination and 580 were declared inadmissible. as regards the statistical analysis presented in this report, the majority of petitions concern the eu as a whole (27.3%), followed by spanish (15.0%), german (12.5%) and italian (8.6%) cases. the report includes a recital stating that thanks to the work of this committee, water has been declared a public good by the european parliament. however, the paragraph in the article that operationalizes the recommendation to the european commission merely states that water is a common good. this inconsistency, which is obviously clever, is intended to remove the public character of services, distorting the firm fight of the populations against the privatization of this resource. it is in line with other positions adopted by the european parliament in this respect, which thus shows that it takes account of the genuine aspirations and concerns of the citizens.
in writing. − in 2012, petitions by citizens and residents of the european union mainly focused on alleged gaps in eu law in the areas of fundamental rights, the environment, the internal market and property rights. it considers that the petitions bear witness to the fact that there are still frequent and widespread cases of incomplete transposition or misapplication of eu law. fundamental rights remain a central theme of the petitions submitted, raising issues relating, inter alia, to the rights of persons with disabilities, the rights of children, property rights, the right to free movement, including the portability of social security rights, without any form of discrimination on any grounds, the protection of freedom of expression and privacy and the right of access to documents and information. it is to be hoped that in the near future the member states will be able to transpose into their legislation all the rules and directives adopted in the eu to deal with the fundamental rights problems which continue to concern european citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i agree with the considerations made, in particular that the committee on petitions would perform its role and tasks better and that its accountability, visibility and transparency would be better ensured if the means for it to raise issues of importance to eu citizens in plenary were strengthened and if the possibility of calling witnesses, conducting inquiries and organising hearings were improved.
in writing. - the right to petition the european parliament is an ancient right conferred by the treaty on the functioning of the european union (article 227) and the charter of fundamental rights of the eu (article 44). it is an essential instrument for democracy, as it makes members aware of the issues that concern citizens, showing that the ep is prepared to act in defence of their rights. the committee on petitions received a total of 1986 petitions in 2012, an increase compared to 2011, but which shows a recognition of the importance given to this democratic act. the members of the committee on petitions are responsible for accepting, examining and acting on all petitions submitted, giving petitioners answers containing conclusions, recommendations or even referrals to other institutions or bodies. this is a way for members to become aware of the issues that concern their constituency directly, thereby addressing their concerns, doubts and even suggestions. for the reasons set out above and in view of the activities of the committee on petitions in 2012, i am in favour of the adoption of this report.
the european union has its own responsibilities in the impasses and blockages in international negotiations. it claims leadership in efforts to combat climate change but persists in its own emissions reduction targets below those recommended by the ipcc. but more than setting goals, a realistic definition of the means to achieve them is needed. ironically and sadly, it is the deep economic crisis that we are in that is the one that is doing the most to curb greenhouse gas emissions. focusing on market instruments which have already shown their failure, their ineffectiveness and their perversity, the european union insists on refusing to face the need to diversify the instruments used to achieve reduction targets. for many, the climate is still more a pretext for lucrative business opportunities than a reason for serious and genuine concern about the future of the planet we inhabit. it is important to point out here the inconsistency of policies, for example, of liberalization and deregulation of international trade, which significantly increase the greenhouse gas emissions inherent in meeting human needs. and by the way, it's also important to remember the millions who, since 2009, have announced themselves to mitigate and adapt to climate change with great media hype. what do you do with this money? what about the so-called fast-track financing and what should follow it?
climate change is a global challenge, the effects of which can be minimized, mitigated, but it is inevitable and will bring demographic changes, new diseases, problems for farmers, serious difficulties for civil protection agencies. this means that all states, and on a global scale, all levels of government and every citizen, are called upon to fight this battle. i expect broad commitments, shared and coordinated action and binding targets at global level accompanied by a sanctioning regime. i hope that the warsaw conference will not be a conference anymore but rather a key moment for a global agreement. the european union must set an example and continue to play a relevant, ambitious, credible and leading role. to this end, the european union must also take up its commitments already adopted and, in resolutions, also take up the objectives in this area, in particular the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. moreover, the current crisis cannot be an excuse for forgetting, for lessening environmental concerns, quite the contrary, it is an environmental policy like the one the european union has been advocating, which stimulates innovation and investment in environmental goods and services, which can generate jobs and also export opportunities.
climate change is a real threat to people and the planet. the next conference is therefore crucial to reach a binding global agreement in 2015. there can be no more delays. it's our survival at stake. i was at cop 11 in 2005, in montreal, canada. we are already at cop 19 and since then, progress has been very limited. this year it is up to a member state, poland, to host and chair the proceedings, and it is important that, also symbolically, the eu maintains its ambition and leadership and reaffirms the need for an international agreement. i would like to remind you that women and children are more vulnerable to the impacts of climate change, such as water and food shortages and natural disasters. combating climate change is also a human rights issue.
the european union should prepare its position on the global agreement. i would like to mention a few principles which i consider to be fundamental to the new international agreement. firstly, the agreement must not divide the world into two groups of countries, as the kyoto protocol does, the industrialized countries and the developing countries. a system is needed where each country contributes to the common effort according to its responsibilities and capabilities. secondly, we must combine the targets assigned to the economies of the different countries with common and global objectives to be adopted by specific industrial sectors, which are subject to carbon leakage. thirdly, the framework should be more flexible and accommodate a wider range of initiatives, in particular bottom-up initiatives, for example, relating to cities and energy efficiency. fourthly, market mechanisms must remain at the heart of the global agreement and fifthly, cooperation in scientific research and technological development must be a crucial objective in the next agreement.
i welcome this important initiative by the commission, which is only too late. three years after the treaty of lisbon, the european union still lacks a horizontal legislative framework on taking measures against third countries to enforce their rights under bilateral and multilateral international trade agreements. in the face of the growing number of commercial disputes and other situations calling for action by the union, it is crucial that we can respond quickly and that we have an effective and credible instrument to safeguard the economic interests of the union. until now, this could only be done by ad hoc legislative measures, on a case-by-case basis, which before the lisbon treaty was done by the council on a proposal from the commission. after the treaty of lisbon, this is no longer possible, given the delay in the ordinary legislative procedure. the commission's proposal to create a general legislative framework which would then enable the commission to take action where necessary by means of implementing acts is therefore welcome. the mere existence of this regulation is in itself a deterrent and therefore fills a serious gap in the union's legal order. in conclusion, parliament should adopt a clear and predictable common framework so that the union can deal in a timely manner with any illegal commercial actions and strengthen the union's capacity.
the negative effects of liberalization and deregulation of international trade are so evident that even the pioneers of free trade have come to recognize, at least formally, the need for some level of regulation, however minimal. or, to use her familiar warmongering rhetoric, herself elucidative as to the purposes she serves, the need for so-called defensive retaliatory measures. experience shows that in the context of liberalization we do not have enough instruments, which, when they are used, if they are ever used, have already done a lot of damage. we need a regulated international trade, oriented towards complementarity and not towards competition between products, producers and countries. a competition in which everyone loses: workers, populations and the environment. the european union's exclusive competence in the field of trade policy has served, and serves only, as experience shows us, to defend the so-called offensive and defensive interests of the great european powers, interests which are often different from, or even antagonistic to, those of other countries, in particular the member states with weaker economies.

what is needed is to close the gender pay gap and to allow reconciliation between family and professional life.

in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 establishes a system of exceptional trade measures in favour of countries and territories participating in or linked to the eu's stabilisation and association process. in practice, it grants an exceptional and unlimited exemption from customs duties on the eu market to almost all products originating in albania, bosnia and herzegovina, croatia, kosovo, the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, montenegro and serbia. this asymmetric liberalisation would, under normal circumstances, violate the wto rules on non-discrimination. however, these trade preferences with respect to the western balkans are explicitly authorised by a wto derogation until 31 december 2015. these are therefore measures taken within the wto framework which are consistent with its logic. all western balkan countries benefit from preferential trade arrangements, including individual tariff quotas, under stabilisation and association agreements or interim agreements on trade. a specific tariff quota for wine of 20 000 hl is now allocated to kosovo and the overall annual tariff quota for wine from all these countries is reduced proportionately from 50 000 hl to 30 000 hl. the total volume of concessions is thus not changed. we have not, however, voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the european union grants unlimited exceptional duty-free access to the eu market for almost all products originating in the countries and territories benefiting from the stabilisation and association process, through council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 of 30 november 2009, with the exception of wine and baby beef, which remain subject to tariff quotas. the aim of these measures is to revitalise the economies of the western balkans through privileged access to the eu market. the resulting economic development will promote political stability throughout the region. kosovo has demonstrated its potential to export wine to the union and exporters need a stable and reliable framework. this proposal approves a tariff quota of 20,000 hl of wine for kosovo, to be deducted from the 50,000 hl provided for in regulation (ec) no 1215/2009.
in writing. − the proposed regulation is based on a reasonable approach which aims to create a level playing field for wine imports into the eu from the entire western balkans region. the report stresses that the allocation of a specific tariff quota for wine originating in kosovo does not imply an overall increase in the overall tariff quota for wine authorised for import to the western balkans, but only changes its distribution, correcting the alleged unfavourable position of kosovo wine exporters. furthermore, the level of the wine quota allocated to kosovo is based on previous trade in that product and, as this is the usual method for determining the levels of the quotas, there does not appear to be any disproportionate allocation of wine to kosovo compared to the individual tariff quotas allocated to the rest of the western balkans region under the stabilisation and association agreements or the interim agreements. for these reasons, and in view of the urgency of this legislative procedure in order not to disrupt trade after 31 december 2013, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − the union has an exceptional tariff framework for almost all products from bosnia and herzegovina, serbia, albania, croatia, macedonia, montenegro and kosovo, agreed by the world trade organisation until 31 december 2015. this preferential treatment of access to the union market does not apply to wines, as an import quota has been imposed. however, the stabilisation and association agreements and the interim agreements provide for specific quotas for the wine products of the respective country. however, kosovo is completely excluded, benefiting only from the overall import quota. i am voting in favour of this report because i think it is important to correct this asymmetry which is damaging the kosovo wine market compared to its peers.

in writing. − in vitro diagnostic medical devices (ivds) are devices intended for use outside the human body (in vitro) that can be used in the laboratory or near the patient, covering a wide range of tests such as self-testing for blood sugar, hiv testing and dna testing. without proper diagnosis, there is no possibility of adequate treatment or prevention of disease. the current directive does not prevent the marketing of low quality ivd medical devices, and there are cases where a low quality hiv test (with an abnormally high number of false negatives) has been marketed in the european market. the report aims to ensure greater transparency and control in medical devices, as well as greater protection and information for patients, and to provide a higher level of safety for medical devices on the market. the report proposes a new classification system (taking into account individual and public health risk), the introduction of the concept of informed consent for genetic testing (pre-natal and for diseases manifesting throughout adult life), genetic counselling, protection of minors and persons with disabilities. we voted in favour.
in writing. the report aims to approve new rules on in vitro diagnostic devices used in pregnancy, dna or hiv tests. in vitro diagnostic medical devices cover a wide range of products such as pregnancy tests, hiv screening tests, dna tests, etc. there are thousands of different devices with different risk categories. the rules adopted today are designed to ensure patient safety. new rules on patient consent to the use of a device for genetic testing purposes were introduced and the setting up of an ethics committee was advised. the rules adopted today are designed to ensure patient safety. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − medical ivd devices are, as their name suggests, diagnostic devices that can be handled not only by professionals in a laboratory setting, but also by the average citizen at home. ivds cover a wide range of tests, among which blood sugar tests, hiv tests and genetic tests stand out for their regularity of use or the potential impact of the results they produce. specifically as regards genetic testing, due to the complexity of its full interpretation and understanding, the potentially devastating nature of its not necessarily correct results, the negative impacts on family members who did not seek or want any genetic information, the ease of misuse, it is necessary to establish an appropriate legislative framework that prevents the undesirable consequences of the use of such icds. this is what can most easily be ensured by making prior genetic counselling compulsory. in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, the member states will have a preponderant role in this area in national legislation, based on that established at european level.
in writing. − this proposal for a regulation aims to replace the directive on in vitro diagnostic medical devices, taking account in particular of the inconsistency in the interpretation of the existing rules in the member states, while at the same time protecting public health and safety and removing obstacles to the functioning of the internal market. the aim is to broaden and clarify the scope of the legislation, align the definitions with international practice, establish a medical device coordination group, among other measures, taking into account that in vitro diagnostic medical devices are medical devices intended for use outside the human body and cover a wide range of tests such as self-testing for blood sugar, hiv testing and dna testing. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. − in vitro diagnostic medical devices (ivds) are devices intended for use outside the human body in vitro, which can be used in the laboratory or near the patient, covering a wide range of tests such as self-testing for blood sugar, hiv testing and dna testing. the current directive does not prevent the marketing of low quality ivd medical devices, and there are cases where a low quality hiv test (with an abnormally high number of false negatives) has been marketed in the european market. the report aims to ensure greater transparency and control in medical devices, as well as greater protection and information for patients, and to provide a higher level of safety for medical devices on the market. we voted in favour.
in writing. − i welcome the commission's proposal to review the current regulatory framework for medical devices. the revision was, in my view, particularly necessary, given that this is a framework of 20 years and many improvements have been made to the existing legislation. however, i think that many other amendments should still be made to the text. i think that the commission proposes a text structure which is not entirely satisfactory, because it does not reflect the sequence of activities which need to be carried out before a medical device can be used safely. the second chapter already refers to the making available of devices, their free movement, or even reprocessing, before mentioning the classification of devices or the selection of the approval procedure. the order used also places the emphasis on the placing of devices on the market and their free movement within the eu, leaving considerations such as patient safety and public health (classification, approval procedure and clinical investigations) in the background.
in writing. − this report aims to regulate the safety, quality and efficacy standards of medical devices placed on the market in the european union. recent events, such as the scandal of fake silicone breast implants, have brought these issues to the public's attention. the european legislation regulating this sector is 20 years old and needs to be revised. the new regulation thus ensures greater safety for medical devices, not only for patients but also for healthcare professionals who use and handle them, and improves access to important information on medical devices for the public and healthcare professionals. i therefore support this report.

in writing. the report by mr roth-behrendt is on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation amending directive 2001/83/ec, regulation (ec) no 178/2002 and regulation (ec) no 1223/2009 and aiming to regulate the safety, quality and efficacy standards of medical devices placed on the market in the eu. there are hundreds of thousands of types of medical devices currently available on the market in the european union, such as rapid dressings, syringes, catheters, blood collection devices, sophisticated implants and life-support technologies. the current legislative framework is 20 years old and a review is now necessary after the shortcomings identified in recent years, such as the lack of transparency and the rapid approval and placing on the market of medical devices. the lack of research in patients and insufficient clinical data ultimately put patients themselves at risk. it is therefore important to ensure that new regulations are in place to ensure that medical devices are safe not only for patients but also for healthcare professionals who use or handle them, not to mention the layperson who comes into contact with the devices.
in writing. − following the serious problems experienced in several countries with silicone breast implants and metal hip implants, the european commission has drawn up a proposal for a regulation on medical devices. the medical devices covered by this regulation are any instrument, appliance, equipment, machine, implant or software designed for the diagnosis, prevention, monitoring or treatment of disease, ranging from simple ligaments to more complex life support instruments such as pacemakers or implants of various kinds. the regulation aims to increase the transparency of procedures, improve information for patients, improve control under notified, subcontracted and subsidised bodies, lay down requirements for internal staff of national authorities and notified bodies and stricter rules for devices that can be reprocessed. the aim of the proposal has also been extended to medical devices for aesthetic purposes, with the aim of improving traceability to allow, for example, a rapid withdrawal of devices from the market. the final result of the vote substantially weakened the proposal that came out of the specialised committee on the environment, public health and food safety. nevertheless, positive steps have been taken in the face of a situation whose persistence is unacceptable and dangerous, and we have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − medical devices such as breast implants, pacemakers and hip replacements should be subject to tighter safety assessment across the eu, as agreed in this report. the proposed standards also aim to improve traceability to allow, for example, a rapid withdrawal of devices from the european market. medical devices cover a wide range of products, from household items such as quick-fix bandages, contact lenses, to dental fillings, x-ray machines, pacemakers, breast implants, hip replacements, etc. there are thousands of different types of devices on the market, classified into different risk categories. recent events, such as the scandal over fraudulent silicone breast implants and the problems caused by certain metal-on-metal hip replacements, have brought these issues to the public's attention. these new rules are intended to strengthen the safety controls on medical devices, ensuring better traceability of medical devices and strengthening the supervision of certification bodies by national authorities with a view to ensuring patient safety. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the roth-behrendt report on the proposal for a regulation on medical devices, but with the same reservations as i always have about voting on such lengthy and technical legislative instruments without being able to properly assess their impact. firstly, this is a matter which is largely of a technical and regulatory nature and should not be included in any legislative instrument of parliament. the question arises whether the possibility of delegating regulatory powers to the commission could not be used more generously. secondly, i think that the unilateral issuing of regulatory instruments on medical devices could increase the regulatory divergence between the union and our main economic partners, increasing the barriers to international trade. as the union negotiates an ambitious trade and investment treaty with the us, including the approximation of regulatory standards, i believe that legislative instruments such as these should be subject to an impact assessment of their implications for the union's international trade and also be subject to prior consultation in the regulatory dialogue with the us and other important trading partners of the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report which lays down stricter safety assessment rules for medical devices. the rules adopted today by the european parliament also aim to improve the traceability of dms so that, for example, in the event of a defect or risk, their holders can be quickly identified and/or withdrawn from the market as quickly as necessary. these new standards also seek to strengthen the supervision of certification bodies by national authorities with a view to ensuring patient safety. certification bodies, which often use subcontractors, should in future have permanent scientific staff with sufficient experience and training to assess the medical functionality of devices. patients should be provided with an implant card so that they can be identified and alerted in the event of incidents with similar products.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the main cause of the problem is the current incentive for shipowners to go to the sites with the lowest standards, since they are the ones who pay the highest price. i believe that a mechanism should be introduced to finance environmentally friendly ship recycling. all ships using ports in the european union should pay a tonnage-based fee. the fees would go to a fund which would offer a premium to ship recycling yards that comply with the provisions of this regulation, making them competitive. the premium would only be paid for the recycling of ships flying the flag of the european union for at least two years. such a measure would increase the value of european union ships, as the listed shipyards could offer a higher price to the shipowner and as such dissuade shipowners from changing flags, while ensuring that a last-minute change of flag is not rewarded.

in writing. − advertising fraud can take many forms, the most common being payment forms, internet domain names, trademark fraud, work from home and get-rich-quick schemes. deceptive commercial practices can lead to market failures or distortions of competition, impairing the ability of companies to make informed and effective choices, and also have an impact on consumers, who end up paying more for products and services. in this connection, it is argued that the exchange of information between member states should be improved and that member states should set up a national focal point to which companies can turn to report their complaints and from which they can obtain information on judicial and non-judicial remedies. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − there is a need to protect companies against misleading commercial practices and to ensure that standards are effectively applied. additional measures are needed in the areas of prevention and information, law enforcement and criminal prosecution. international cooperation in combating such practices is also very important.
in writing. − the single market is a growth engine that provides consumers with more choice and better prices, and in this context it is essential that there is a dissemination of goods and services that provides consumers with better information and the possibility of making comparisons between different products, thus contributing to increasing competition. however, it is essential that companies using advertising as part of their business strategy do so honestly and with the utmost professional diligence. fraudulent commercial practices can take a variety of forms, such as fraudulent payment forms, schemes operated by fraudulent directory publishers, among others, which create market failures, distort the decision-making capacity of businesses and distort competition, and also have a serious impact on consumers. unfortunately, the level of protection for companies varies greatly between member states, with only belgium and austria, for example, having specific rules prohibiting the submission of misleading directory forms. i therefore support the strengthening of existing rules, in particular by introducing a clearer definition of misleading commercial practices, the creation of a blacklist of prohibited misleading commercial practices and the adoption of effective, proportionate and dissuasive sanctions.
in writing. - misleading advertising practices have a detrimental effect on consumer and business confidence and a very negative economic impact. i therefore welcome the commission communication on protecting businesses against deceptive commercial practices and ensuring that standards are effectively applied. in a globalised world highly dependent on technology, particular attention should be paid to deceptive practices on the internet, which are carried out under the guise of anonymity.
in writing. the report by mr cornelis de jong is aimed at misleading advertising. the most prominent of these deceptive advertising practices are schemes operated by publishers of misleading directories, whereby a dishonest company sends out forms inviting companies to fill in forms which in reality mean the involuntary signing of a contract which normally binds them for a minimum of three years to be included in a business directory for an annual price of eur 1000 or more. the level of protection of companies varies widely between member states. only austria and belgium have included in their legislation a specific prohibition of schemes operated by publishers of misleading directories. i believe that protecting companies against deceptive commercial practices and ensuring effective enforcement of the rules is worth making an extra effort. i agree with additional measures in the field of prevention and information, law enforcement and criminal prosecution. deceptive commercial practices are not a european phenomenon. the commission therefore stresses the importance of international cooperation in combating such practices.
in writing. the rapporteur welcomes the european commission's communication on the protection of enterprises, especially micro and small enterprises, against deceptive commercial marketing practices. it also called for the eu to take action to combat fraud and corruption. the report makes concrete proposals which can help in this fight. the rapporteur stresses the need for a greater and better exchange of information between member states and calls on them to set up or assign a national focal point to which companies and other victims can report misleading practices and through which they can obtain information on judicial or non-judicial recourse and help in prevention. the rapporteur supports the creation of a blacklist of deceptive commercial practices and calls on the member states to adopt legislation enabling victims of deceptive commercial practices to take collective action in proceedings against dishonest companies. in general, despite some reservations and disagreements, the objectives pursued by this report are positive and deserve our agreement.
in writing. − misleading advertising practices can take many forms, the most common being companies that produce business directories, payment forms, internet domain names, fraud in relation to trademark protection, fraudulent business opportunities, work from home or get-rich-quick schemes. the negative impact of deceptive, misleading and unfair advertising practices on economic growth, in particular for smes, and on fair competition in the internal market is of great concern, especially in the least developed member states, which are facing the worst effects of the financial crisis. we must continue to do everything possible to put an end to this kind of practice which only harms economic growth and development. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − fraudulent commercial practices can take a variety of forms, most notably schemes operated by fraudulent directory publishers, whereby a dishonest company sends out forms inviting companies to complete or update the company's name and contact details, apparently free of charge. the signatories later discover that they have in fact involuntarily signed a contract that normally binds them for a minimum of three years to be included in a company directory for an annual price that can exceed eur 1000. i voted in favour of this proposal which welcomes the commission communication on the protection of undertakings against deceptive commercial practices and the effective enforcement of standards and which suggests additional measures in the field of prevention and information, law enforcement and criminal prosecution to strengthen the proposal. the european parliament stressed the importance of international cooperation in combating deceptive commercial practices, which are not a purely european phenomenon.
in writing. - there are various forms that deceptive commercial practices can take. for example, some forms in company directories, where only later do the signatories discover that they have signed a contract binding them for a minimum of three years, paying annually 1000 euros or more. there are also invoices for services that were not actually ordered, and misleading offers for domain name extensions on the internet. currently, of all member states, only belgium and austria have legislation specifically prohibiting this scheme operated by misleading directory publishers. it is important to protect businesses against these practices and to ensure that the rules are effectively applied. there is also a need to highlight the importance of international cooperation, as these deceptive commercial practices are not unique to the european union.
in writing. the european commission has presented a communication to protect businesses, especially micro and small enterprises, against misleading commercial marketing practices. the rapporteur welcomes the communication but considers that deceptive commercial practices go beyond european borders and advocates international cooperation in combating such practices. the report therefore makes concrete proposals which can help in this fight. the rapporteur stresses the need for a greater and better exchange of information between member states and calls on them to set up or assign a national focal point to which companies and other victims can report misleading practices and through which they can obtain information on judicial or non-judicial recourse and help in prevention. the rapporteur supports the creation of a blacklist of deceptive commercial practices and calls on the member states to adopt legislation enabling victims of deceptive commercial practices to take collective action in proceedings against dishonest companies. the objectives pursued by this report are positive, although we do not agree that the motives for these actions are related to the question of competition in the internal market.

the proposal for a regulation on the european maritime and fisheries fund, which we are discussing here today, has been improved on an initial proposal from the european commission which was simply
