in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that drug precursors are legal substances used in the manufacture of drugs. until now, medicines have been excluded from the scope of the regulation. unfortunately, drugs containing ephedrine and pseudoephedrine, used to treat constipation, flu symptoms or allergies, are diverted to synthesise methamphetamines. the fact that the regulation does not cover medicinal products makes it impossible, in my view, for member states to confiscate or intercept easily shipments of medicinal products containing ephedrine or pseudoephedrine which are suspected of being misused. i therefore believe that medicinal products should be included in the definition of scheduled substances and that a new category of substances should be created to allow for better control of scheduled substances. furthermore, i consider that the fact that the definition of scheduled substances stipulates precisely that the precursor must be easily extractable from the mixture in order to be considered a scheduled substance contributes to limiting significantly the number of medicinal products that could possibly be considered scheduled substances and, therefore, the impact on trade in medicinal products.
in writing. − this commission proposal for revision aims to fill a legal gap in regulation (ec) no 111/2005, which lays down rules for the control of trade in drug precursors between the european union and third countries. until now, medicinal products have been excluded from the scope of the regulation. unfortunately, drugs that contain ephedrine and pseudoephedrine are diverted to synthesize methamphetamines. the fact that the regulation does not cover medicines makes it impossible for member states to confiscate or intercept easily shipments of medicines containing ephedrine or psudoephedrine suspected of being misused. the committee therefore advocates the inclusion of medicinal products in the definition of scheduled substances and the creation of a new category of substances to allow better control of scheduled substances. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i agree with the rapporteur that this proposal is of the utmost importance in filling a legal gap in the regulation. drug precursors are legal substances used in the manufacture of medicines and drugs. drug precursors should be subject to export, import and transit controls, which vary in severity depending on the risk of diversion.
in writing. − the control of drug precursors is essential in the fight against narcotic drugs to prevent these chemicals, which have a wide range of legal uses, for example in the pharmaceutical, cosmetics and perfume sectors, from being diverted from legal distribution channels to the illicit manufacture of narcotic drugs. a specific regulatory framework has been established at both international and eu level to control the legal marketing of drug precursors with the aim of preventing their diversion for illicit purposes, thus contributing to reducing the supply of illegal drugs. however, medicines containing ephedrine and pseudophedrin (used for colds or allergies) and which allow the illicit production of methamphetamine are not covered. i therefore support this initiative which aims to fill the existing gap in terms of eu control of these medicines when they are exported or in transit through the customs territory of the eu. methamphetamine markets are expanding in europe, with illegal methamphetamine laboratories seized for the first time in 2009 in several european countries, demonstrating the need and urgency for us to strengthen this control by allowing member states to confiscate or intercept shipments of this type of medicines suspected of being diverted for illicit purposes.
in writing. − drug precursors are legal substances used in the manufacture of drugs and are already subject to controls in the context of export, import and transit, more or less strict in terms of the risks of diversion. this proposal aims to fill a legal gap in council regulation (ec) no 111/2005 which excludes medicinal products from its scope. given that medicinal products containing ephedrine and pseudoephedrine, used to treat constipation, flu symptoms or allergies, are often diverted to synthesise metha-amphetamines, there is a need to cover them in the current legislation.
in writing. - as regards the consolidation and updating of the mechanisms for the supervision and control of drug precursors between the european union and third countries, this report is an important contribution to the fight against the proliferation of drugs and narcotic products. the proposal seeks to fill the legal vacuum in the eu and in the control of its borders with regard to legal substances used in the manufacture of drugs, such as medicines containing ephedrine and pseudoephedrine, which are excluded from the list of controlled substances in the context of exports, imports and transit. these are examples of commonly used medicines for colds, flu and allergies, which can be manipulated and from which so-called drug precursors can be extracted. the creation of a new category for such products will facilitate and simplify controls on trafficking in these substances.
in writing. − the european commission's proposal to revise regulation 111/2005 aims to fill a legal gap in that regulation, which lays down rules for the control of trade in drug precursors between the eu and third countries. the commission decided to include medicinal products containing ephedrine or pseudoephedrine in the scope of the regulation. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'closed circuit' to cover the whole of the electrical network. the commission has established a specific scheme for these medicinal products which does not correspond to any of the schemes provided for in the different categories. these medicinal products are subject only to the obligation of prior notification of export. the rapporteur proposes that medicinal products be included in the definition of scheduled substances and that a new category of substances be created to allow for a better nuance of control applicable to scheduled substances. the rapporteur believes that the inclusion of a new medicinal product in the annex to the regulation should not be subject to the codecision procedure. this is because drug traffickers are more adaptable than the process of adopting the regulation in the codecision procedure. the position taken in the report is generally justified and correct.
in writing. − there is currently a serious gap in eu legislation regulating the trade in drug precursors. this regulation closes that gap. drug precursors are legal substances used in the manufacture of drugs. for example, acetic acid is used in the manufacture of heroin. drug precursors are subject to controls in the context of export, import and transit, varying in severity according to the risk of diversion. the precursors which are controlled and listed in the annex to the regulation are designated as scheduled substances. until now, medicines have been excluded from the scope of the regulation. unfortunately, drugs containing ephedrine and pseudoephedrine, used to treat constipation, flu symptoms or allergies, are diverted to synthesise methamphetamines. the fact that the regulation does not cover medicinal products makes it impossible for member states to easily seize or intercept shipments of medicinal products containing ephedrine or pseudoephedrine suspected of being misused. the adoption of this regulation fills that gap. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − drug precursors are legal substances used in the manufacture of drugs. for example, acetic acid is used in the manufacture of heroin. drug precursors are subject to controls in the context of export, import and transit, varying in severity according to the risk of diversion. the precursors which are controlled and listed in the annex to the regulation are designated as scheduled substances. until now, medicines have been excluded from the scope of the regulation. unfortunately, drugs containing ephedrine and pseudoephedrine, used to treat constipation, flu symptoms or allergies, are diverted to synthesise methamphetamines. for this reason, the european commission has decided to include medicinal products containing ephedrine or pseudoephedrine within the scope of the regulation. in view of the above, i have voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − i am in favour of and broadly support the proposal, as only small quantities of drug precursors are needed for the production of illicit drugs and, given that these precursors are produced globally in large quantities, great care is needed to ensure that drug precursors are not diverted from legal trade in the european union. eu action in this area will therefore force traffickers to move their activities to other parts of the world, encouraging other regions of the world to follow the eu's example. in addition, i believe that the proposal allows for legal trade and use of acetic anhydride without imposing unnecessary administrative burdens on companies. at the same time, it allows the competent authorities to monitor trade flows more closely in order to detect and block illegal diversions.
in writing. − drug precursors are chemicals widely used for different industrial processes, production of plastics, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, etc., but can also be used for the production of illicit drugs. the current regulatory framework has defined a licensing and registration system to monitor the trade in drug precursors in the european union, imposing specific obligations on the companies involved and on public authorities. however, in recent years the european union has faced some international criticism for its allegedly lax control measures. in order to strengthen control, it is argued that registration and licensing requirements should be simplified and harmonised across the union in order to avoid market fragmentation and to prevent criminals from taking advantage of the 'weaker link' in the union's internal market. the creation of a european database, which would provide the necessary transparency and improve the monitoring of all drug precursors in the european union, is also advocated. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − this proposal is very important in preventing the diversion of domestic trade in acetic anhydride, the main drug precursor used in the manufacture of heroin, as well as in extending the registration requirement to include users of the substance.
in writing. - although drug precursors are legal substances, mostly produced by perfectly suitable entities, the fact is that their use in the manufacture of illicit drugs often leads to their diversion. in addition, since only small quantities of drug precursors are needed for the production of illicit drugs and since these precursors are produced globally in large quantities, close monitoring is needed to ensure that drug precursors are not diverted from legal trade in the eu. this is what this proposal does by making the rules on drug precursors more stringent.
in writing. − the european union must ensure an effective legal framework to combat drug trafficking. in this context, products that constitute so-called drug precursors merit particular attention and concern, reinforced by the fact that they are chemicals that, in addition to being used for the production of illicit drugs, are widely used for different industrial processes, such as the production of plastics, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, perfumes and detergents. a legal framework is therefore needed to reconcile the interests, objectives and competitiveness of european industrial activity with the need to improve the response capacity of the institutions in the control and surveillance of the traffic in drug precursors in the eu, as is the case in particular with acetic anhydride, which is legally used for the production of plastics, textiles, dyes, photochemical agents, perfumes, explosives and aspirin, but also used illicitly for the production of amphetamines, cocaine and especially heroin, with a strong impact on mortality associated with drug use in the eu.
in writing. − the european union has been criticised internationally for the lack of control measures on drug precursors or the permissive nature of legislation in some member states. criticism has focused mainly on acetic anhydride, a substance that is legally used to produce plastics, textiles, dyes, photochemicals, perfumes, explosives and aspirin, but can also be used illegally to produce heroin, cocaine and amphetamines. this is the main drug precursor for the production of heroin (which, in turn, accounts for the majority of consumption, with huge associated mortality rates). we agree on the need to strengthen controls on operations which could lead to the illegal use of substances, by combating the diversion of chemicals from the legal trade chain to the illicit production of drugs. this can be achieved through more transparent registration and more restrictive licensing requirements. it would be important to take some steps to strengthen the legislation in each country.
in writing. − drug precursors are chemicals that are widely used for different industrial processes (production of plastics, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, perfumes or detergents) but which can also be used to produce illicit drugs. drug precursors are rarely produced for criminal purposes, which aim to use them in the production of illicit drugs, as the manufacture of drug precursors requires substantial industrial infrastructure. instead, criminals often try to divert the legal trade in drug precursors, either by stealing or by buying. this regulation proposes to create a new eu-wide database of information on seizures of drug precursors in the eu, listing all licensed or registered operators and end-users of drug precursors in the eu. i believe that this new regulation is a significant improvement on the previous one and will better prevent the use of drug precursors for illicit purposes.
in writing. − drug precursors are chemicals that are widely used for different industrial processes (production of plastics, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, perfumes or detergents) but which can also be used to produce illicit drugs. drug precursors are rarely produced by criminals who intend to use them in the production of illicit drugs, as the manufacture of drug precursors requires substantial industrial infrastructure. instead, criminals try to divert the legal trade in drug precursors, either by stealing or by buying. in the report annexed, the commission proposes the creation of a new eu-wide database of information on seizures of drug precursors in the eu, with a list of all licensed or registered operators and end-users of drug precursors in the eu. the aim is to combat this problem more effectively and the proposal contains valuable improvements over the current situation. the introduction of delegated acts will provide the commission with the flexibility to react quickly to changing circumstances as well as to deal with resourceful drug traffickers, while ensuring adequate parliamentary oversight of any changes. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − in recent years, the eu has been criticised internationally for the lack of control measures on drug precursors or the permissive nature of legislation in some member states. criticism has focused mainly on acetic anhydride, a substance that is legally used to produce plastics, textiles, dyes, photochemicals, perfumes, explosives and aspirin, but can also be used illegally to produce heroin, cocaine and amphetamines. this is the main precursor drug for heroin production. the need to strengthen controls on operations that could lead to the illicit use of these substances is clear, by combating the diversion of chemicals from the legal trade chain to the illicit production of drugs. the creation of an eu-wide database for this purpose is not a sine qua non condition for achieving this objective. in addition to the risks associated with the proliferation of databases whose proportionality, purpose and use raise serious suspicions of possible violations of the freedoms and guarantees of citizens - as the existence of other databases and their access has demonstrated - this objective can be more easily achieved by strengthening the legislation of each country.
in writing. - i support this motion for a resolution, understanding that e-justice has an important role to play in enhancing mutual trust and understanding and thus supporting the mutual recognition of judicial and administrative decisions, a major principle of the legal system of the european union. in this connection, i would point out that e-justice systems, by their very nature, tend to reduce the costs of judicial and administrative procedures, in particular by automating the exchange of information, the service of documents and the translation of certain procedural documents. i believe that they are in the interest of all the stakeholders in the legal system and that, for reasons of cost-effectiveness, projects should remain voluntary. at the same time, i welcome the development of e-justice tools to facilitate the use of certain european union instruments, such as the european order for payment procedure and the european small claims procedure, as well as information systems in the field of justice and home affairs, in particular the european criminal records information system (ecris) and the schengen information system (sis ii).

madam president, commissioner, living well within the limits of our planet is the motto that gives the title to the european union's 2020 environmental action programme. if we consider that living well applies not to a privileged few but to the general population, the question arises as to whether it is possible within the framework of the dominant economic and social system on a planetary scale. whether it will be possible to shape a harmonious and sustainable relationship between nature and society within the framework of a system that, in marx's words, either grows and accumulates or dies. a system which, for that very reason, is constantly confronted with the limits of a land which, being generous, is finite. in the face of this, the solution cannot be to paint capitalism green. it cannot be the commodification of nature and its resources or so-called services, the promotion of the private appropriation of what is and must be for everyone: from drinking water to clean air, from fertile soil to biodiversity, from hydrothermal springs to mineral deposits. it is also important to remember that the environment does not exist separately from everything else. we need, of course, an action programme on the environment, a programme which is not just a mere spin off of a fraudulent, albeit green, neoliberal booklet. but we also need, i would say above all, to integrate environmental objectives into a very broad set of sectoral policies, including agriculture, fisheries, industry, energy, trade and others. the conclusion here is that profound changes are needed in the european union's current policies in all these areas. it is that with these policies, living well within the limits of our planet will be nothing more than a slogan emptied of substantive content and every day contradicted by political practice. thank you very much.

countries. there are situations in which it is particularly important to revive certified productions which, due to extreme circumstances, have been declining but have competitive potential. lourinhã spirits in portugal, which currently lack enough vine to establish themselves on the market, are an example. another important aspect is the possibility of additional support for wine producers in disadvantaged regions such as islands. i would like to say that, in addition to the negative economic, social and environmental impacts, traditional vine-growing also has cultural and even tourist value. finally, i would like to give the example of the pico vineyard in the azores, which has been designated a unesco world heritage site and which really needs support for the restoration of areas suitable for growing this vine.
in writing. now that the cap has been changed in the last reform of the cmo in 2008, with the creation of a system of authorisation for vine planting and the possibility of information and promotion campaigns, it is necessary to give wine operators time to adapt to all these changes. it seems that a new reform of the sector is in preparation, which includes the creation of new categories of wine. changes in wine quality policy, oenological practices or volume control measures may put wines with a geographical indication at risk. but we should not question this wine-production model which characterises the sector, since it is growing and represents a considerable part of the wine production of the ors, almost 20% in the azores. it is therefore necessary to know whether you are planning a further reform of the sector, what your objectives for this sector are in the coming years and how the potential of the internal market can be exploited, particularly in wine tourism, as this can be part of the solution to attract investment to the most disadvantaged regions.

in writing. − i am of the view that the post-2020 agreement will have to integrate the various binding and non-binding provisions adopted under the un framework convention on climate change and the kyoto protocol into a single comprehensive and coherent regime binding on all parties. the post-2020 agreement should not divide the world into categories of industrialized or developing countries, but instead require each country to contribute according to the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities. i therefore believe that emission reductions calculated on the basis of a number of indicators, such as gdp per capita, access to technology and the quality of life index, among others, are a valid instrument and have therefore voted in favour of the document.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that in order to try to provide a text which responds to the urgent need to combat effectively the phenomena of organised crime, corruption and money laundering, we must in fact draw attention to phenomena which, by virtue of their global dimension, now require an equally large response. the european union must respond to this challenge by equipping itself with the appropriate tools to meet it, based on the most advanced legislative model in the member states. in this context, i suggest a homogeneous and coherent legislative framework to strike at the economic heart of organised crime and to strengthen judicial and police cooperation at european and international level. i believe that further efforts must be made to promote a faster and more flexible public administration, less corruption-prone, more responsible politics, a faster and more credible criminal justice system, a healthier entrepreneurship, a more transparent banking and professional system and adequate measures to combat money laundering, in order to prevent crime from continuing to generate profits at the expense of the legal economy, businessmen and law-abiding citizens.
in writing. - vat fraud generates a loss of revenue for the eu of €100 billion per year. the cost of corruption amounts to some €120 billion a year, or 1.1% of the eu's gdp. small-scale corruption in the public sector represents a loss of eur 20 million for the union. some 3,600 international criminal organisations operate in europe, 70% of which are made up of members from several countries, and 880,000 people are subject to forced labour in eu countries. i welcome this report on organised crime, corruption and money laundering, which contains measures on the confiscation of assets of criminal organisations and their reuse for social purposes, the abolition of banking secrecy and the introduction of a european-wide corporate taxation.
in writing. − organized crime has taken advantage of the new opportunities brought by economic globalisation and technological progress and has become a transnational and global phenomenon with devastating economic and social effects. moreover, organised crime, corruption and money laundering, although still distinct phenomena, are now in many cases intertwined. the new sophisticated forms of organised crime, corruption and money laundering require effective and strong measures, and the globalisation of criminal networks also requires a global and joint eu response, and here is an important contribution to that end.
in writing. − this report is the result of intensive and in-depth work involving the most diverse sectors and actors of society, and responds to the recognised need for the european union to equip itself with the appropriate tools to combat organised crime, corruption and money laundering. the number of international criminal organisations operating in the european union is estimated at 3600, 70% of which include elements from different countries and currently operate in a geographically heterogeneous range, misusing the opportunities offered by economic globalisation and new technologies. this is a phenomenon whose complexity, gravity and negative effects on economic development and social equity are compounded by its global dimension. it is a challenge for the european union, which must act in a determined and concerted way, ensuring a more advanced model of legislation in its member states.
in writing. - despite positive aspects such as the lifting of banking secrecy and the imposition of some limitations/penalties on companies based in tax havens the report falls far short of what was required. the general approach is one of repression, not prevention and combating at the source, as would be necessary. the report does not go to the heart of the matter, but serves to justify measures to create new supranational bodies which, by their nature, cannot compensate for the attack being made at national level on bodies which are fundamental in the fight against and control of phenomena such as organised crime, corruption and money laundering. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of tax havens. no measures are proposed to attack the free movement of capital, which is essential to the flourishing of these criminal practices. the so-called banking union is being defended as a useful way for banks to escape the regulatory and legislative control of political and democratic power, continuing to function as centres for money laundering of the most shameful origin: drug trafficking, human trafficking, corruption, etc.
in writing. - the european parliament's special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering has done an excellent job, resulting in the document now adopted, which raises issues of great importance. the document proposes, for example, measures on the confiscation of assets of criminal organisations and their reuse for social purposes, the abolition of banking secrecy and the introduction of a european-wide corporate taxation. the cost of corruption amounts to 1.1% of eu gdp. a european action plan for 2014-2019 to eradicate organised crime, corruption and money laundering is proposed. there is still much to be done to eliminate corruption in the eu, but the adoption of this report is an important step in that direction. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report by the european parliament's special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering, which proposes, among other measures, the confiscation of assets of criminal organisations and their reuse for social purposes, the abolition of bank secrecy and the introduction of a european-wide corporate taxation. it is important to combat this scourge, as the cost of corruption amounts to 1.1% of eu gdp.
in writing. − organised crime, in addition to violence and intimidation, also includes corruption, ranging from money laundering to fraud and tax evasion. in an era of globalisation, there are some 3600 international criminal organisations operating in the european union, of which 70% have a wide range of activities, as they are made up of members from several countries. the following report sets out the need to combat the phenomenon of organised crime and calls on the european union to do so urgently. it thus suggests a homogeneous and coherent legislative framework, which also aims to strengthen judicial and police cooperation at european and international level. the activities of the special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering included meetings with a number of experts, representatives of the various european institutions, academics, judicial authorities and other interested parties. i believe in a europe which makes the eradication of crime a priority, and i therefore vote in favour of adopting this report.
in writing. - despite some positive aspects advocated in the report, the general approach is one of repression rather than combating at the source, as would be necessary. the majority of the ep does not make the necessary self-criticism of the responsibilities it has in this matter, nor does the eu as a whole. on the contrary, i did. it uses this report to move forward with a further withdrawal of powers which are at the heart of the sovereignty of states, in particular over their justice systems. the proposal to set up a criminal investigation body and an internal investigation agency, a mechanism to monitor the effectiveness of criminal justice systems and a european public prosecutor's office are examples. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the taxation of capital. no measures are proposed to tackle the free movement of capital and the phenomena of corruption, organised crime and money laundering which continue to flourish in this way. and the so-called banking union is being supported, which will be a useful way for banks to escape the regulatory and legislative control of political and democratic power, continuing to function as centres for money laundering of the most shameful origin: drug trafficking, human trafficking and corruption.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the european neighbourhood policy aims at creating an area of prosperity and good neighbourliness, based on the values of the union and characterised by close and peaceful relations at regional level, promoting a strong and sustainable democracy, the rule of law, political and economic reforms, a sustainable social market economy in the countries neighbouring the european union and creating a circle of friends of the union and friendly relations between them, which therefore constitute the major guiding principle for assessing progress which in turn should be the contribution to the security, solidarity and prosperity of each party. in this context, i condemn the negative effects of the policies of border closures in the european union's neighbourhood, and in particular between the eastern partnership countries and the countries applying for eu membership. furthermore, taking into account that the multilateral dimension of the neighbourhood policy provides a unique opportunity to bring together all countries and stakeholders in the regions and to contribute at political level to the development of democracies in these regions, i could not agree more with the establishment of an effective european neighbourhood policy.
in writing. − this resolution underlines the importance of a differentiated and incentive-based approach to the eu's neighbouring countries. the different countries have different situations but one common denominator - the eu's active role as a partner in building democracy and respect for the rule of law, human rights and fundamental freedoms.
in writing. - as shadow rapporteur and former co-rapporteur of the last two european parliament resolutions on the european neighbourhood policy (enp), i have followed this complex dossier closely. i therefore congratulate mr panzeri (s&d) and mr saryusz-wolski (ppe) on their excellent work and commitment, which have once again enabled this parliament to express its views with one voice on this comprehensive union policy, which has a positive effect on geographical, social, economic and political realities as diverse as those found along the baltic and red seas. i would first of all like to stress the insistence on the principle of more for more, which obviously means less for less if our partners do not apply the universal principles of respect for human dignity on which our union is founded. i also welcome the continued support for the democratic transition processes of our neighbours to the south and east, both in terms of capacity building and in terms of economic and financial support and poverty reduction. although it seems obvious, i think it's always important to remember these principles. finally, i welcome the inclusion in the report (following my proposal) of the ultimate objective of a greater euro-mediterranean economic area, which should be the culmination of the processes of economic integration between the south and the south that have already begun.
in writing. - there are many tensions at the union's borders and many particular challenges facing the union in its relations with its neighbours. the pursuit of closer relations with its majority is a noble purpose on the part of the union which thus seeks to expand democracy, human rights, the rule of law and freedom and justice in trade. unfortunately, these european efforts have been opposed by countries which consider that their strategy of geostrategic hegemony is undermined by european meddling, which points to a path of parity instead of subordination and compromise instead of domination. this issue cannot be avoided and must be addressed directly to the states which do so, so as to allow the union's neighbours to make free choices about their own future. when european resolve is called into question, the union must not waver or be intimidated by unreasonable pressure. their neighbours are strategic partners who deserve respect and support when they are under pressure. only if she stays by his side will she be worthy of his support.
in writing. − the european neighbourhood policy plays a key role in promoting a wider area of prosperity, freedom and respect for human rights, social equity and sound and sustainable democracies. it is also crucial for social stability and a peaceful environment. the economic and social crisis which the eu has faced in recent years - and still faces - cannot lead to the neglect of good neighbourly relations and partnership policies which promote better economic and social development in the most disadvantaged regions surrounding the european area. the 2012 interim reports should be duly analysed for both positive signs of developments and indications of setbacks, in order to allow the development of plans and mechanisms capable of strengthening partnerships and the success of european good neighbourly policies.
in writing. - this resolution clearly emphasises the imperialist character of the european union. in the wake of other resolutions on the european neighbourhood policy, a position of open interference in the internal affairs of sovereign countries, the promotion and conclusion of the so-called association agreements and free trade treaties is affirmed. these countries are being pressured to accept the interests of the eu's great powers and their monopolies, relinquishing the instruments of sovereignty over their economy, their resources and the promotion of the interest of their peoples. the text includes principles such as more for more or less for less, which, as the text itself makes clear, are aimed at establishing relations which have nothing to do with the specific and mutual interests of the countries concerned and of the eu countries as a whole. it is a question of extending the deception of the possible opening of the eu market, to then create a relationship of dependence and subsequently dominance by the stronger pole the eu. there is no lack of guidelines and mechanisms to achieve the objectives pursued. political parties and civil society (those promoting policies that defend the interests of the eu and of the monopolies of these countries) will be supported to promote the goodness of eu policies.
in writing. − the european neighbourhood policy aims to strengthen the partnership between the eu and neighbouring countries and societies in order to build and consolidate healthy democracies, strive for sustainable economic growth and manage cross-border links. i believe that the analysis of the various interim reports, which deal with the situation of many of our neighbours, shows that the eu's neighbourhood policy has been delivering results. although there is still a long way to go, i believe we are on the right track in making the fundamental principles on which the eu is based known to our neighbours. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution entitled 'european neighbourhood policy: towards a strengthened partnership'. position of the european parliament of 4 july 2012 (not yet published in the official journal) and decision of the council of 6 july 2012. i do so by underlining the important role played by civil society in the reform and transition processes and in political dialogue in neighbouring countries, and therefore urging the eu to strengthen cooperation with civil society in these countries by supporting it through a range of different funding instruments.

in writing. - i welcome this report, while reiterating the importance of cohesion policy as the main investment instrument, which plays a key role in combating the crisis, reducing regional disparities and putting the european union and its regions on the path to sustainable growth. i therefore stress the importance of ensuring adequate budgetary means, in the context of the negotiations on the 2014-2020 framework, for the european union's structural and investment funds, noting in particular their significant share of investment in a number of areas such as employment, innovation, sustainable development and support for smes. at the same time, i am deeply concerned about the sharp fall in public and private investment in the productive economy, especially at local and regional level. i believe that decisive action is needed to reform product and labour markets, adopt prudent wage policies, base the future growth model on innovation and shift production to high value-added activities, given that a sustainable economic policy requires very favourable conditions for the creation of new businesses.
in writing. − this own-initiative report is the result of an evaluation by the european parliament of the country-specific recommendations proposed by the european commission in the context of the european semester process. this year's report is presented against a more favourable backdrop of strengthening of the banking sector, positive indicators in the state accounts and in the economy in general. european policies and structural reforms are beginning to produce visible positive results. the committee also calls for the introduction of a european system of national accounts for the financial year 2000 and for the establishment of a european system for the financial year 2000 to be used by the commission to monitor the implementation of the budget. i consider that this report represents an active and positively contributory position of the european parliament in the debate on european economic governance and therefore i shall vote in favour of it.

in writing. − as adopted in the last revision of the stability and growth pact, for which i was one of the rapporteurs, the european parliament, after an exchange of views with the national parliaments, gives its views on the country-specific recommendations proposed by the european commission and adopted by the council. i would remind you that it is the country-specific recommendations which guide the drawing up of the national budgets of the member states and which represent an engine for the convergence of economic policies. thus, according to eurostat data, only one euro area country was in surplus in 2012, reflecting the adverse conditions in which budgets for 2014 are being planned. i therefore consider it essential that there are policies at european level to stimulate growth and job creation which can counterbalance the demanding fiscal consolidation measures being implemented. in particular, i call for the urgent need to implement the pact for growth and jobs, with an estimated budget of eur 120 billion agreed in june 2012, and to make available the eur 180 billion of additional investment from the eib.

in writing. − the european semester was presented as a mechanism for coordinating the economic policies of the different member states. since coordination is not an end in itself, it is important to see what the content of the policies that are to be coordinated is. we are faced with a mechanism to tie each country to a path of civilizational regression, of attack on rights, of levelling down living and working conditions in europe. a dossier which involves the emptying of the institutions of national sovereignty, democratically legitimized, transformed into mere verbiage, authentic puppets of the eu directory. the rapporteur - and this is significant - a portuguese socialist - spreads socialist flowers throughout the report. it presents as a major advance the recommendations for the surplus countries to invest and increase wages, in order to buy the product of the work of workers who are poorly paid in countries like portugal, which are destined to be increasingly subordinated and peripheral in the process of the international division of labour. but it also makes clear the positive reception of the country-specific recommendations put forward by the commission. what are these recommendations? for portugal: compliance with the deficit targets set by the troika, further reductions in the wage bill, reduction in public consumption, so-called permanent fiscal consolidation measures, privatisations, and so on. obviously, we voted against it.
in writing. the report on the european semester for the coordination of economic policies between eu countries calls for more attention to be paid to growth, employment and investment. the report also stresses the need to revise the current troika model into a community system subject to democratic control. due account should be taken of the constraints imposed by economic adjustment programmes on the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives for growth and jobs. we must find out where we went wrong in the solutions to solve the crisis so that we can rectify what has gone wrong, so that we can make the necessary corrections.

in writing. - i approve of this report, considering that in a period of economic crisis and austerity, it would be almost impossible to emphasise environmental policy, as this would be interpreted as a secondary priority or, in other words, as a constraint or a hindrance to economic growth and employment. this short-term and divisive vision should be replaced by an effective combination of environmental messaging and economic and industrial concerns, bringing together all stakeholders in an innovative and progressive approach. in my view, action on the environment has very high costs as does inaction in this area but it also has benefits that neither public finance nor private investors can ignore during the current period. for this reason, environmental concerns should not remain the adjustment variable but should be integrated into the various sectoral policies. by proposing a general framework, the seventh environment action programme can serve as the european union's major environmental manifesto to its citizens and the rest of the world and as the founding act of a european green new deal for 2020, guaranteeing greener growth and creating jobs.

in writing. − implementing an environmental policy in a time of economic and financial crisis is a challenge, as environmental actions generate very high costs. however, an environmental policy that provides favourable conditions for the competitiveness of the economy, i.e. a low-carbon and sustainable economy, is essential. this report underlines the need for a european green new deal in horizon 2020. i also stress the importance of environmental legislation, which should seek greater coherence and simplification, while respecting the principles of smart regulation. the natural capital of the european union and its biodiversity must be safeguarded. this requires intensified efforts to combat environmental dumping and carbon leakage. given the urgency of a long-term environmental perspective for 2050 that provides an environment conducive to investment, growth and job creation, i am in favour of adopting this report.
in writing. − the development of the european union's environmental policy has been established through environmental action programmes since the 1970s. this seventh action plan sets out the objectives to be achieved and identifies the measures and actions it considers necessary for their implementation. the report identifies a set of objectives with which we agree, including protecting, conserving and enhancing the eu's natural capital. however, the pathways identified, such as market mechanisms, the polluter pays principle, the emissions trading scheme, the eu 2020 strategy, not only do not allow some of these objectives to be achieved, but also contribute to pushing the member states and the eu further away from achieving them. it insists on a purely market-based approach to environmental problems, favouring profit generation and its concentration in large economic groups, at the expense of speculation around the carbon price, among other illusory instruments, which contribute to the increased commodification of natural resources and environmental solutions, removing the public character of policies, financing and services.
in writing. − i welcome this report, considering that this proposal for a recast of the council bss directive is another step towards improving protection against exposure to ionising radiation. one of the aims of the recast is to eliminate the inconsistencies in the existing legislation, which has been achieved in several parts of the proposal and there is little to change. many of the aspects of radiation protection covered by the directive, which sets basic safety standards, work extremely well in practice, which also indicates that there is little to change. the proposal also aims to incorporate the latest scientific data and experience in the field of radiation protection into existing legislation. on the other hand, natural radiation sources should be included for the first time in the bss directive, with a view to ensuring better protection of the general public. this deserves my appreciation. however, in the field of landfill, the planned registration obligations may lead to conflicts in terms of the targets for the disposal of the different radioactive substances. to prevent this from happening, i propose to amend the requirements for naturally occurring radioactive materials.

in writing. the report by mr thomas ulmer deals with protection against the dangers arising from exposure to ionizing radiation. the proposal for a recast of the council basic safety standards directive brings together, on the basis of article 31 of the euratom treaty, the medical radiological exposure directive, the hass directive, the external workers directive, the public information directive and the bss directive 96/29/euratom. i believe that natural radiation sources should be included in the bss directive in order to ensure better protection of the general public. in the field of medical exposure, we must avoid duplication with respect to medical devices emitting ionising radiation, i.e. we must avoid that medical devices operating with ionising radiation fall within both the scope of the medical devices directive and the basic safety standards directive. bureaucratic delays for manufacturers and operators of such devices should be avoided.
in writing. − exposure to ionising radiation has harmful effects on health. under normal conditions, the doses are very low, which prevents the observation of clinical effects in tissues. however, there is a possibility of late effects, especially cancer. it does not appear possible to establish a threshold dose for this purpose: any exposure, however small, can lead to cancer later in life. the likelihood of late effects appears to be dose proportional. this requires a specific approach to radiation protection based on the principles of justification, optimisation and dose limitation, which are the cornerstone of the protection system established several decades ago by the international commission on radiological protection (icrp).
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposals for amendments to the council directive laying down the basic safety standards for the protection of human health against the dangers arising from exposure to ionising radiation. one of the aims of the recast is to eliminate the inconsistencies in the existing legislation, which has been achieved in several parts of the proposal and there is little to change. many of the aspects of radiation protection addressed by the basic safety standards directive work extremely well in practice, which also indicates that there is little to change. the proposal also aims to incorporate the latest scientific data and experience in the field of radiation protection into existing legislation. in this respect, euratom legislation has always followed the scientific recommendations of the international commission on radiological protection (icrp), which had expressed the need for adaptations to the current radiation protection system, and these recommendations have now been incorporated into the proposal for a directive.
in writing. − article 191 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) provides the legal basis for the preservation, protection and improvement of the quality of the environment and for the protection of human health, including against the dangers arising from exposure to ionising radiation. i support this report which lays down the basic safety standards for the health protection of the general public, workers, patients and other individuals exposed to medical radiation against the dangers arising from ionizing radiation, with the aim of ensuring a uniform minimum level of protection in the member states. i would also like to stress that the presence of radioactive substances in the environment has an impact on the health of the general population. in addition to environmental exposure pathways, the protection of the environment as a whole, including exposure of biota, should be considered within a comprehensive and coherent framework.

in writing. - i welcome the report adopted by the european parliament today, because it is based on the assumption that the overall objective of the regulatory framework for electronic communications should continue to be to promote a sectoral ecosystem of competition and investment that benefits consumers and users, encouraging the creation of a genuine internal market in communications and promoting the union's overall competitiveness.
in writing. − electronic communications are an integral part of the daily lives of citizens and institutions. the absence of legal certainty in the regulation of telecommunications markets and the predominantly national character of telecommunications markets hamper their progress and delay their dissemination. the possibility should therefore be envisaged not only of evaluating the existing framework but of seeking to improve it by means of the active participation not only of the competent european and national institutions but also of the main actors and stakeholders in this field, bearing in mind that a balance is sought, as harmonious as possible, between the specific interests of each state in this respect and those of final consumers. i believe we must move towards an increasingly open market, with increasingly intelligible rules and where consumers can make an informed and conscious choice of services that are appropriate to their needs.
in writing. − the impact of electronic communications on the lives of citizens and institutions is certainly growing and with a very wide and accelerated potential for progression. it is clear that any consolidated strategy for growth and development, whether at economic, social, cultural, legal or other levels, must take the digital dimension as a determining factor. its role is highly incisive in the economy at global level and, in particular, in the single, unified and competitive european market. the universality of the internet and cybersecurity require consolidated measures of common legislation and co-regulation. in order to stimulate innovation, increase consumer choice, reduce costs and increase efficiency in the deployment of high-speed electronic communications infrastructures, a combination of various measures and all available technologies should be explored and offered to consumers. a pan-european auction of fourth and fifth generation wireless services with a limited number of licences serving the entire eu territory would allow the provision of pan-european wireless services and undermine the foundations of the poor roaming service.
in writing. − one of the key points of electronic communications is to reduce the costs and increase the efficiency of deploying high-speed electronic communications infrastructures by making greater use of best practice across the eu, thus improving the conditions for the establishment and functioning of the internal market, a field which supports the development of virtually all sectors of the economy. it is common ground that, irrespective of the technology used, civil engineering works constitute the dominant part of the overall costs of network deployment, with estimates of up to 80% for certain technologies. we must continue to invest in the development of electronic communications, which are a key element of economic development and growth and which are transversal to all economic sectors.
in writing. − the successive regulations in the field of electronic communications, which led to the current framework, have worked well to date, bringing dynamism to the industry and benefits to consumers and other users. as mentioned above, however, there are a number of issues which need to be taken into account in the next revision of the framework. this does not mean that the framework is inadequate, but it does show the speed of change in the sector. i voted in favour of this report, which presents constructive proposals, feasible solutions and compromises between the many contradictory aspects. this is a task of great economic importance, with enormous potential for impact positive or negative on citizens and which requires caution as well as thorough debate and analysis.
in writing. − the following report calls for a thorough review of the current legislative framework, specifically as regards the coordination of european electronic communications. a single market is crucial and there are a number of measures which can contribute to this objective. one of these is radio spectrum, on which an inventory of the use of frequencies by the member states was drawn up in a first programme. the net neutrality of the internet, which requires careful deliberation, and the extension of the current regulation to over-the-top (ott) services should also be highlighted. however, despite the positive results of these measures, the internal market for electronic communications remains incomplete, especially as regards the regulation of the sector. i therefore vote in favour of adopting this report.
in writing. − in november 2007, the commission's proposals for the regulation of electronic communications emerged, and were adopted by the parliament and the council two years later (november 2009) after long and difficult negotiations. the assessment now being made concludes that the internal market for electronic communications remains incomplete, for example, with no pan-european operator. this assessment is intended not only to promote further liberalisation of the communications market but also to expand privatisation of these services, including the dispossession of the public sector to private interests. the concept that they so much criticize, that the fragmented market is harmful, is only the reproof of what is still left of the guarantee of a public service provided by the state to the populations with regard to electronic communications, which often have social and tariff concerns that no private company has. this is the stumbling block which the monopolies of electronic communications find in the so-called unification of the market, so fundamental to concentrate the provision of this service on a handful of economic groups, to the detriment of guaranteeing the access of the populations to the services and the sovereignty of the member states.

the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud. - mr president, commissioner, investing in erasmus is investing in european youth. erasmus+ is the new european programme for education, training, youth and sport. this programme will aim to improve students' skills, personal development and their employment prospects. youth unemployment is a serious problem in europe. the committee on budgets has therefore given priority to all youth policies, especially those relating to employment. in this sense, erasmus+ is the programme with the largest budget increase in the next community framework: compared to the previous period, a 40% increase with a total budget of eur 13 billion, demonstrating the commitment of the committee on budgets and this parliament to the future of our youth.
in writing. the person who has a mobility experience is never the same person again, because he or she is valued personally and professionally in different contexts, which gives him or her a greater preparedness and capacity to adapt and innovate in his or her work. any improvement in the skills of citizens is essential for our competitiveness, especially when it creates new prospects for the younger generation, which is facing difficulties in finding employment. and in the sense that we all gain from cooperative initiatives, all of europe must be involved in this effort, from the azores to helsinki. education and training are thus extremely important areas in the present context and therefore deserve increased attention from the european union. to this end, the programmes we are discussing today must be financed in such a way as to increase the number of opportunities for participation and to ensure that appropriate support is provided from the origin to the country of destination of the participants, so that all those who wish to take advantage of this initiative can do so.

the multiannual financial framework is an instrument which creates stability by defining the headings, the corresponding financial amounts, the programmes, the policies and the priorities. the unanimity required in the council for the adoption of the multiannual financial framework has been and will always be a difficult problem to overcome, especially when we have member states threatening, blackmailing and seeking to veto if the conditions they impose are not met. this is the possible financial framework, with the improvements introduced by the european parliament. we have achieved greater flexibility, we have achieved anticipation and increased funding for the promotion of employment and, in particular, for youth employment. we got a commitment to a review by 2016. i would like to stress one point which i consider very positive: the setting up of a high-level group for the reform of the budget of the european union as regards own resources. in fact, only with own resources and genuine own resources can we increase the budget, which corresponds to about 1% of gross domestic product and is financed by national budgets to the tune of about 85%. this situation leads each leader in each member state to seek a juste retour. i therefore hope that this financial framework will be voted on and that this reform of the own resources of the budget of the european union will be successful.
i would like to welcome the new period of community aid but i cannot because this gift is poisoned. it is combined with a new philosophy: the council and above all the commission are given a free hand to cut or suspend the structural funds already contracted when the deficit and debt targets are breached. these sanctions are unjust, firstly because they are cumulative with what we have already negotiated in the six pack; secondly because they penalise only some member states, which are the most vulnerable, and secondly because they punish citizens, businesses, regions which have little to do with the violations in question. there are two other types of rape, the bona fide ones. firstly, the breach of good faith when we, the parliament and the council, with the support of the commission, negotiated the actual six pack sanctions which may amount to 1% of gdp; the second violation is that the role of community funds is to help those countries which, in the process of integration, abandon trade defence instruments, abandon the exchange rate, abandon monetary policy, abandon budgetary policy and need the funds to achieve real convergence which is lacking. you can't change the rules in the middle of a game. what the commission is proposing, and what the council has insistently and unanimously accepted, is a blow to the citizens' confidence.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, the three largest groups in the european parliament say that this 2014 budget was the best possible result, given the conditionality of the council's positions (i would like to ask the socialist group whether françois hollande and the french government are not also part of the council), but this is not true, this agreement is a miserable result compared to the one of 2013. there was, yes, the alternative of rejecting the deal and going to the 12th until we could get a better one. but it is worth asking ourselves: what can one expect from a european budget in times of recession and austerity? there are two possible answers. on the one hand, little is expected, given the political composition of the council and the commission and the majority of the european parliament, but on the other hand, it is in times of recession that the redistributive and solidarity-based nature of the budget is most needed to reduce the divergence between countries and regions and to help to revive the economy. in a budget which is falling considerably, money is being transferred in a juggling act: youth employment is withdrawing money from the european social fund, the fund for the most vulnerable is seeking funds from the territorial cohesion funds, the lampedusa tragedy is being responded to by increasing pro-frontex funds rather than by changing immigration policy. this budget is another missed opportunity, but it is a tragedy for the citizens of europe. the vote in favour today, from the right to those who call themselves leftists, is a punishment for the citizens of europe and cannot be forgiven.

the budget for the multiannual financial framework which we have adopted today is a step towards abandoning europe, towards abandoning a europe of solidarity and a europe of cohesion. if this parliament did not have the courage to oppose the demands of some of the governments, it is worth pointing out here, too, that in the case of portugal, prime minister pedro passos coelho was complicit in this budget and in this multiannual financial framework because the proposal had to be approved unanimously in the council and it would have been enough for pedro passos coelho not to have voted on it in february, and therefore what portugal and other countries will suffer in the coming years in terms of the brutal cuts in research and cohesion funds, which will not allow, contrary to what is said, to revive the economy, is the responsibility of this parliament but it is also the responsibility of the governments.
in writing. - i approve this report, starting by regretting the cuts made in all the ceilings and in particular in the ceiling for expenditure under cohesion policy. it should be recalled that in order for cohesion policy to continue to be an effective instrument for increasing strategic investment with proven added value and for putting the european economy back on the path to growth and productivity, it was necessary to maintain cohesion policy funding at least at the level of the period 2007-2013, as this is the absolute minimum compatible with efficient funding. i also express my concern about the inclusion of article 8, which refers to macroeconomic conditionality, in the draft regulation, which weakens parliament's position in this area. similarly, it should be recalled that one of the preconditions for the adoption of the regulation, which was laid down by the european parliament's resolution on political agreement on the multiannual financial framework for 2014-2020, is that there is political agreement on the relevant legal bases, in particular as regards points that are also reflected in the multiannual financial framework regulation for 2014-2020.

in writing. − the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 comes at a particularly sensitive time for the european union and, in particular, for some member states, including my own. i think it is appropriate that the financial framework should reflect the need for restraint which is also felt by the states and the citizens, but i do not think it can be restricted to the point of calling into question the full exercise of the powers which are vested in the european union. i hope that the new financial framework will make a positive contribution to the european union's more rapid and flexible action, committed to serving the member states and the peoples of the union, in particular those most in need of its solidarity and its support for cohesion.
in writing. - the mff allows for institutional peace and stability. each member state and each beneficiary of the funds and programmes will know what they can count on for the next seven years. it aims to implement the europe 2020 strategy to achieve the objectives set in employment, education, research and innovation, combating climate change and poverty reduction. we must manage our financial resources as efficiently as possible. the mff has, at 2011 prices, an amount of eur 960 billion in commitment appropriations and eur 908 billion in payment appropriations. this was the result of more than two years of intense negotiations. the greatest difficulty is that this agreement requires unanimity. i recall that the united kingdom threatened to veto the mff 2014/2020 if it had an amount higher than the current one (mff 2007/2013). this was the possible agreement where the european parliament made important gains over the initial proposal of the member states in terms of flexibility, the youth employment initiative, the fund for the disabled, own resources and the revision of the mff. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - for the first time, we are facing a reduction in the eu budget in nominal terms compared to the previous programming period. by approving this proposal for the 2014-2020 mff, the majority in parliament is doing what it said it would never do. he takes what he said for what it is and accepts what he severely criticized. this mff represents less than 1% of the gnp of all eu countries, a reduction of 3.7% compared to the current level, in a context of worsening economic and social crisis in the eu, particularly acute in countries such as portugal. our country sees eu transfers fall by more than 10% compared to the previous mff (2007-2013). the mff, which has never had the funds, means and political priorities to make an effective contribution to helping to bridge the gap between countries (which would require at least twice the current amounts), inherits a deficit of eur 15 billion and only promises without guarantees to mobilise the amounts now decided. the blackmail of the (mis) so-called net contributors is foreseen, who have not only determined the amounts and priorities for the mff, but will use these decisions (along with others in the framework of the european semester) to impose, in the neo-colonial style, political guidelines on countries with the weakest economies and facing a serious recession. we obviously voted against it.

in writing. − on 8 and 9 february, the european council approved a final compromise proposal on the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020. after several rounds of negotiations between the european institutions, it was finally possible to reach an agreement on the financial perspective for the next seven years of programming. i welcome the agreement reached which gives europe and the member states a budget to boost a new period of economic growth and job creation, with the structural funds to be channelled into specific areas of economic activity rather than into major infrastructure. i would also like to take this opportunity to stress that this agreement will support youth employment, make the european union more innovative, design new transport, telecommunications or energy networks and also reduce poverty levels in the world.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that for the first time new provisions relating to the multiannual financial framework introduced by the treaty of lisbon have been used, in particular with regard to the increased role and prerogatives which these provisions confer on the european parliament. however, i would stress that, together with its results, the long and laborious negotiation process, both within the council and at interinstitutional level, constitutes an unsatisfactory implementation of the new provisions on the multiannual financial framework. furthermore, i denounce the negotiating strategy of the council, whereby its negotiators were subject to the conclusions of the european council of 8 february 2013 on matters falling within the scope of the ordinary legislative procedure, thus preventing both arms of the legislative authority from carrying out appropriate negotiations. i therefore conclude that, in accordance with article 312 (5) tfeu, further working arrangements should be defined in the future in order to facilitate the adoption of the multiannual financial framework, ensuring that the legislative and budgetary powers conferred on parliament by the tfeu are fully respected.

in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the 1994 acp-eu agreement on government procurement has a limited number of signatories, mostly developed countries. one of the objectives of the revised acp is to increase the current number of members. it thus offers incentives to developing countries, including the possibility of applying temporarily higher thresholds and of gradually integrating entities and sectors, with the aim of facilitating opening up to external competition. it is not clear, however, that the revised special and differential treatment clause for developing countries improves the rules currently in force. the new text allows for additional protection, on a transitional basis, of the markets of developing countries, whereas currently exemptions can be negotiated without being limited in time. the new text does not, however, provide developing countries with significantly greater access to the markets of the other acp countries. despite positive progress in terms of procurement procedures and transparency, countries are not expected to sign this agreement unless it is demonstrated that the benefits outweigh the costs.
in writing. − the government procurement agreement (gpa) is a legally binding international agreement on access to government procurement markets to which some wto members are parties. ensuring the provision of services of general interest to the population, including access to essential services such as water supply, housing, waste management, health care, education and culture, remains one of the most important functions of a government. each country takes a different approach to balancing this task with the need to spend the scarce public resources available efficiently and to seek the best quality and value of services and goods purchased. public procurement is also an essential instrument for stimulating employment and economic activity in a region and for promoting a high level of environmental protection and decent working conditions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this recommendation because i consider that the proposed revision of the agreement on government procurement improves the quality of the main text, providing greater clarity and transparency in the award procedures. this agreement will ensure the quality and accessibility of the provision of services of general interest to the population, including access to essential services such as water supply, housing, waste management, health care, education and culture.
in writing. - given that public procurement represents millions of euros annually, its economic importance cannot be called into question. the revised acp, which we now approve, provides eu companies with legal certainty for access to foreign markets. the review of the agreement has provided the eu with market access opportunities in terms of the enlargement of covered entities (notably by eea countries and by countries such as canada, south korea, the united states, israel, taiwan and hong kong (china)), in terms of the coverage of goods and services and in terms of thresholds for covered goods and services (notably by japan, korea and israel). the eu has thus secured some €30 billion in new market access opportunities.

in writing. − the agreement on government procurement (gpa) is a legally binding international agreement on access to public procurement markets to which some wto members are parties. the eu's participation, given the powers that the treaty illegitimately confers on it in trade matters, is binding on all its member states. one of the objectives of the review of the acp is to increase the current number of signatories, which is relatively limited, by extending it to developing countries. this agreement on public procurement is part of the neoliberal logic of gradually opening up to the market areas where states have traditionally exercised and, in some cases, still exercise their social function through public services. it is these public services that they want to dismantle, opening them up to external competition. the countries party to this agreement, when holding tenders, may not distinguish between foreign and national tenderers. the commission has therefore decided to initiate the procedure laid down in article 93 (2) of the treaty in respect of the aid scheme for the supply of electricity to the coal industry. public procurement - an important tool for protecting jobs, the economy and the environment - has long been the target of voracious appetites. the rapporteur lists some of the areas that big transnational capital wants to tackle: water supply, housing, waste management, health care, education and culture, among others. obviously, we voted against it.
in writing. − the government procurement agreement is a legally binding international agreement on access to public procurement markets to which some wto members are parties. this multilateral agreement, which was negotiated in parallel with the uruguay round in 1994, entered into force on 1 january 1996. the agreement has two parts: the main text, which lays down the rules applicable to tenders and ensures the transparency of procedures and equal treatment of tenderers, and the scope, which is made up of annexes on the conditions of access to the public procurement market. in conducting calls for tenders in the field of covered contracts, the parties may not distinguish between foreign and national tenderers. i voted in favour of this proposal to ratify the revision of the acp which raises the quality of the main text and establishes the rules applicable to contracts, bringing greater clarity and transparency to them.
in writing. − the agreement on government procurement (gpa) is a legally binding international agreement on access to public procurement markets. it is an agreement which is divided into two parts: a main text with the rules applicable to tenders and the scope containing annexes on market access and the specificities of the market. a revision of the acp is proposed to improve its quality and efficiency. some of these include the possibility of using electronic auctions, thereby reducing the notification period, the creation of a centralised database, free of charge, containing the notices of competition published by the various ministries, and new selection rules excluding from the award procedure companies guilty of serious crimes or breaches of professional ethics. it also introduces revised standards for technical specifications on environmental matters, simplification of statistical reporting obligations and new provisions for developing countries wishing to join the acp.

in writing. − in november 2011, the european commission presented its proposal for a regulation on a new multiannual programme for education and training, youth and sport for the next 7 years. renamed erasmus+, this programme brings together all current programmes and actions in the field of education: higher education (erasmus, erasmus mundus, tempus and bilateral programmes between the eu and third countries), school education (comenius), vocational education and training (leonardo da vinci), adult education (grundtvig) and youth (youth in action). the programme also covers sport, providing for the award of grants to young sportsmen. the aim of the programme is to improve students' skills, personal development and their employment prospects. the budget for the period 2014-2020 is eur 14,7 billion, which represents an increase of 40% over the last 7 years. thanks to the new loan guarantee mechanism, students wishing to study for a master's degree in another eu country will be able to benefit from more favourable conditions. erasmus+ will support partnerships between educational institutions and businesses, with the aim of improving students' employability and developing entrepreneurial skills. i therefore support this report.
