in writing. − the eu's programme for education, training, youth and sport, now called 'erasmus+', will have a budget of €14.7 billion for the next period 2014-2020. erasmus+ now covers school education (comenius programme), higher education (erasmus), international higher education (erasmus mundus), vocational education and training (leonardo da vinci) and adult education (grundtvig) and aims to offer young people the possibility of studying or doing a training placement abroad. this new programme, instead of grants, provides a mechanism for guaranteeing loans to master students, which we do not agree with, since it pushes students into debt before they have completed their studies. it should be noted that under the pre-bologna system, students had the possibility of accessing mobility grants in any of the five years of training. under the current bologna process, scholarships are only available for three years, and master students are now subject to the debt system the eu is now proposing. the richest have access, the poorest are excluded. it is also inequality that is the most striking feature of this new programme.
in writing. − erasmus+ is an eu programme for education, training, youth and sport, which brings together all current programmes and actions in the field of higher education (erasmus, erasmus mundos, tempos), school education (comenius), vocational education and training (leonardo da vinci), adult education (grundtvig) and youth. it is a programme which we support because it gives young people the opportunity for exchanges and development in education and training. although this programme was one of the few to receive a considerable increase in the next budget of the european union, we are opposed to the proposal to institutionalize a new system of loan guarantees. we believe that this loan guarantee system will encourage students to go into debt to pay for their education. this will have consequences especially for the most disadvantaged young people. we also believe that this proposal leads to a situation where only those who can afford it will be able to pursue university education. because we stand for education for all, i abstained.
in writing. − the proposed programme brings together all current programmes and actions in the field of education: higher education (erasmus, erasmus mundus, tempus and bilateral programmes between the eu and third countries), school education (comenius), vocational education and training (leonardo da vinci), adult education (grundtvig) and youth (youth in action). it also includes provisions for jean monnet activities and a separate chapter on sport. i voted in favour of this proposal, which welcomes the commission's intention to reduce the fragmentation and overlap in the current programmes and calls for the need to better identify and give greater visibility to specific activities in the field of education and youth. the need to keep the different programmes identified is also noted.

in writing. − the eu's programme for education, training, youth and sport, now called erasmus+, will have a budget of €14.7 billion for the next period 2014-2020. erasmus+ covers school education (comenius programme), higher education (erasmus), international higher education (erasmus mundus), vocational education and training (leonardo da vinci) and adult education (grundtvig) and aims to offer young people the possibility of studying or doing a training placement abroad. this new programme provides a mechanism for guaranteeing loans to master students, which we do not agree with, since it pushes students into debt before they have completed their studies. this is an aspect which is becoming even more serious in the context of the structural crisis of capitalism, with very high levels of youth unemployment in several member states. it should also be noted that under the pre-bologna system, students were entitled to mobility grants for five years of training, and under the current bologna process, they are entitled to grants for only three years, and master students are now entering the system of indebtedness that the eu is so proud to offer them.

in writing. the cef is a pan-european financial instrument which aims to bring the single european transport area to life. in order to make access to finance more flexible and easier, in coordination with the structural and investment funds, the cef has a dual network with specific objectives, deadlines and funding for the main and secondary networks. in recognition of the difficulties in implementing large-scale projects in cohesion countries, eur 10 billion has been specifically allocated to the cef to be used only in the core network and/or in horizontal actions in the eligible countries. the commission will also be able to provide information on the implementation of the new financial instruments. for this reason, i see this financial instrument as complementary to the erdf and the cohesion fund, since while the former will support investment in transport infrastructure, the eff will allow support for transport and intelligence systems, which increase their efficiency and safety, and support for motorways of the sea.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation establishes the connecting europe facility and lays down the conditions for granting union financial assistance to trans-european networks, in particular to projects considered to be of common interest in the transport, telecommunications and energy infrastructure sectors. the objectives include a 20% reduction in ghg emissions compared with 1990, a 20% increase in energy efficiency and a 20% increase in the share of renewable energy by 2020, all of which remain important. this regulation also lays down the allocation of resources under the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, which, out of the eur 33,242 million allocated to the mechanism, allocates eur 5,850 million to the energy sector and eur 26,250 million to the transport sector, of which eur 11,305 million will be transferred from the cohesion fund to be spent in accordance with this regulation. we cannot agree to withdraw cohesion funds for the purpose of deepening the single market by transferring public money to large private and public-private transport networks. it is clear that the move under way is intended to contribute to greater liberalization in the sectors concerned, with the railway, energy and postal and telecommunications sectors currently being the ones targeted by economic interests.

in writing. the report by mr georgios koumoutsakos and mr ismail ertug deals with the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on the guidelines for the development of the transeuropean transport network. this is a very important project in the european union. the transeuropean transport network is indispensable for the common market and for the mobility of eu citizens. it contributes to economic, social and territorial cohesion and to the creation of economic growth and employment. transport is the backbone of a thriving economy and a key to social cohesion and integration in our society. it is essential to ensure that all regions of the european union are competitive in the european market. an accessible and efficient transport infrastructure is essential for this. from an environmental point of view, we know that in urban areas transport causes problems of congestion, noise and air pollution, with a negative effect on air quality and the quality of life in cities. the demand for transport is very sensitive and so we have to offer the public convincing alternatives to enable the necessary changes.
in writing. - this regulation aims to develop a trans-european transport network, comprising rail, inland waterway, road, sea, air and multimodal transport infrastructures, with the aim of creating a 'single european transport area', which will be the backbone of the common market. these objectives, which favour some large countries in particular, will take some eur 11 billion out of the cohesion fund over the next seven years, which will be transferred from the public domain to the private sector either directly or through public-private partnerships. territorial cohesion is considered a priority here. however, we cannot accept that funding for the overarching cohesion objectives (economic and social components) is withdrawn at a time of crisis, when the 2014-2020 mff has been reduced in cohesion amounts by 8,4% compared to the previous period, when it needed to be increased. we have always said that new cohesion objectives, such as territorial cohesion, require additional resources, and that the development of the transeuropean transport network cannot be achieved by concentrating public funding on the private sector, nor by withdrawing funding from the fund which enables the regions to close the gap between them economically and socially.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation approving the union's guidelines for the development of the transeuropean transport network because there can be no true european single market without an integrated european transport network. the creation of a trans-european transport network, conceived, designed and implemented at european level in the interests of the member states and the union but above all in the interests of citizens and businesses, is an essential condition for the deepening and integration of the internal market and, consequently, for economic growth and job creation in the union. the rapid and efficient movement of people and goods within the union is a requirement for the competitiveness of the union and its enterprises, and very significantly of portuguese enterprises, not only in the internal market but also on a global scale. and this is a reality that cannot be ignored, especially in the current context of economic crisis. in the case of portugal and spain, this project is of particular importance, given the 'decentration' of the iberian peninsula and the pyrenees wall.
in writing. − the trans-european transport network (ten-t) is one of the key projects of the european union. it is the backbone of the common market, indispensable for the mobility of eu citizens, for economic, social and territorial cohesion and for the creation of economic growth and jobs. the ten-t has identified the following problems: a significant delay in the realisation of many ten-t projects, difficulties in project financing in times of economic crisis, lack of coordination between the different centrally and decentrally managed funding instruments, and a lack of information and statistical data on project financing, in particular on financial support from the structural and cohesion funds and the eib. i voted in favour of this proposal, which seeks to overcome all these problems by creating a new dynamic for the implementation of projects.
in writing. − the trans-european transport network (ten-t) is a union policy which sets out the guidelines for the different modes of transport. this defines the main and secondary networks and the components that are part of each mode of transport. the planning, development and operation of the ten-t is in line with the transport white paper and should contribute to strengthening social, economic and territorial cohesion. together with the list of infrastructures present on the main and secondary networks, the ten-t sets out the definitions and elements to be taken into account by the connecting europe facility. it is also stressed that the outermost regions still need to optimise their accessibility for goods and passengers, including maritime and air transport, with the european continent in order to allow their integration into the internal market. the union's links with third countries are also being strengthened. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it an important asset for the european union and the creation of a single transport area.

in writing. - i welcome this report, considering that the commission proposes the creation of a new structure for the ess, with a view to improving coordination and partnership in a clear pyramid structure. one aspect of this rationalization is the concentration of comitology powers in the hands of the esc. i do not think that this alignment exercise raises any problems for parliament. its main objective is to replace the regulatory procedure with scrutiny by delegated acts in the nine existing legislative texts. as regards the remaining cases of the old comitology (with a right of parliamentary scrutiny, i.e. without the possibility of a veto) in these nine legislative acts, which have been practically retained as implementing acts and were not included in the commission proposal, i consider that they are not problematic for parliament, given that they concern formats/forms of transmission or derogations for some member states. in fact, these are usually questions reserved for implementing acts. i would like to point out that some amendments are necessary in order to bring back the wording agreed in the common understanding between the three institutions on delegated acts.
in writing. − i agree with the amendments made in the report to bring back the wording agreed in the joint understanding between the three institutions on delegated acts. i also believe that the period of delegation should not be indefinite, and i therefore also support the proposal to limit it to five years, tacitly extended by periods of equal duration.
in writing. − statistics on agriculture and fisheries are important indicators for gauging the state of the respective sectors and the success of the policies implemented. the compatibility of legislative acts with the treaties in force is required by the need for systematic uniformity, intelligibility and coherence of the union legal order.
in writing. the report by mr de castro deals with the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending certain legislative acts in the field of agricultural and fisheries statistics. the commission proposal aims to amend nine legislative acts in the field of agricultural and fisheries statistics in order to bring them into line with the new institutional context, while at the same time seeking to rationalise the european statistical system. in 2009, the european parliament defined the european statistical system (ess) as a partnership between the european statistical authority, which is the commission (eurostat), and the national statistical institutes (nsis) and other national authorities responsible in each member state for the development, production and dissemination of european statistics. with a view to improving coordination and partnership in a clear pyramid structure, the commission proposes a new structure. the esc will be the highest policy-making body and will concentrate comitology powers.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation aims to amend nine legislative acts in the field of agricultural and fisheries statistics, taking account of the references to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny, in the light of the criteria laid down in the treaty, and aligning them with the new institutional context. the commission proposal also aims at streamlining the european statistical system, taking into account a partnership between the european statistical authority (eurostat) and the national statistical institutes and other national authorities responsible for the development, production and dissemination of european statistics. one aspect of this rationalisation is the concentration of comitology powers in the hands of the european statistical system committee. the report shall include a standard clause on the preparation by the commission of a report on the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period. the report and the amendments it contains raise no major problems, which is why we voted in favour of it.

in writing. − i approve this report, taking into account that the convention aims to establish a framework for bilateral or multilateral cooperation with a view to preventing and controlling pollution of transboundary watercourses and ensuring the rational use of water resources. in 2003, the parties to the convention expressed their willingness to allow countries outside the unece region to become parties to the convention in order to promote cooperation on watersheds worldwide. in 2003, the european community participated in the meeting of the parties, which adopted the amendment allowing any state which is a member of the united nations to accede to the convention upon approval by the parties. with the amendments in force, the convention will be especially important for countries bordering the unece region, such as afghanistan, china, iran and some central asian states. in the light of the above, i recommend that parliament approve the amendment to articles 25 and 26 of the convention in order to open the convention to the whole world and to allow accession by countries not covered by unece who so wish.

in writing. the report by mr matthias groote deals with the draft council decision on the acceptance, on behalf of the eu, of the amendment of articles 25 and 26 of the convention on the protection and use of transboundary watercourses and international lakes. the convention aims to establish a framework for bilateral or multilateral cooperation to prevent and control pollution of transboundary watercourses and to ensure rational use of water resources by the countries members of the united nations economic commission for europe (unece). the eu is currently one of the few parties that has not yet formally accepted the amendment of articles 25 and 26 in accordance with article 218 (6) tfeu. the 6th world water forum called on the commission to promote the entry into force of amendments to the helsinki convention in order to extend this instrument to countries other than those that are members of the unece. i therefore believe that the amendment to articles 25 and 26 of the convention should be approved in order to open the convention to the whole world and to allow accession by countries not covered by unece who so wish.
in writing. − the convention of the united nations economic commission for europe (unece) on the protection and use of transboundary watercourses and international lakes aims to prevent and control pollution of transboundary watercourses and to ensure the rational use of water resources through bilateral or multilateral cooperation by unece countries. the eu has been a party to the convention since 1995. since water resources are often shared natural borders between neighbouring countries, they must cooperate and adopt measures for the sharing of their protection and environmental monitoring, as well as measures for their rational use, prevention and control of pollutants, information exchange and alarm systems. an amendment to the convention was proposed and adopted in 2003 allowing countries outside the unece region that are un members to become parties to the convention in order to promote cooperation in the field of watersheds by taking measures for the effective protection of these resources worldwide. in 2012, the amendment was formally accepted by two thirds of the parties, but not by the eu, as formal acceptance of this amendment requires the approval of the european parliament - which we have now voted in favour of.
in writing. − in april 2013, the commission published a proposal for a council decision on the acceptance of the amendment to articles 25 and 26 of the unece convention on the protection and use of transboundary watercourses and international lakes (the helsinki convention). the convention aims to establish a framework for bilateral or multilateral cooperation to prevent and control pollution of transboundary watercourses and to ensure rational use of water resources by the countries members of the united nations economic commission for europe (unece). in 2003, the parties to the convention expressed their willingness to allow countries outside the region covered to become parties to the convention in order to promote cooperation on watersheds worldwide. the convention, as amended, will be of particular importance for countries bordering the unece region, such as afghanistan, china, iran and some central asian states. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this report which approves the amendment of articles 25 and 26 of the convention in order to open the convention to the whole world and to allow the accession of countries not covered by unece.
in writing. − the convention on the protection and use of transboundary watercourses and international lakes provides a framework for bilateral or multilateral cooperation to prevent and control pollution in these watercourses. it is recommended that countries outside the unece region be allowed to become parties to this convention in order to promote cooperation on watersheds worldwide. in this way, the convention becomes especially important for countries such as afghanistan, china, iran and some central asian countries. i am in favour of adopting this recommendation because i believe that pollution should be minimised.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that iter is a unique large-scale project in the world. with the conclusion of the agreement on the establishment of the international fusion energy organisation iter (eu, japan, russia, usa, china, republic of korea and india) for the joint implementation of the iter project, the community has committed itself to hosting and leading the construction of iter and, it is expected, its future operation. in my view, fusion energy research and development will have to overcome the reduction in the european union's nuclear power powers. this barrier can be effectively addressed by exploiting synergies between the research activities of international participants, member states and the private sector, as well as between scientific disciplines and technology sectors. this international effort will also help to strengthen the framework for fusion research and innovation, and is essential for the long-term future of the fusion programme. in order to keep the temperature increase to 2 oc, the reduction in global emissions will result in a limited use of fossil fuel-based energy. in this context, iter is a key element of energy research as well as of the strategic energy technology plan.

in writing. − the report by mr remek deals with the proposal for a council decision adopting the supplementary research programme for the iter project (2014-2018). iter is a worldwide project on the establishment of the international fusion energy organization iter (eu, japan, russia, usa, china, republic of korea and india). fusion is a process that occurs in nature. unlike nuclear fission, which releases energy when a heavy atom splits into two lighter elements, fusion releases energy when the nuclei of two light atoms join together, for example, when two hydrogen nuclei fuse to form a single new atom. this process releases a huge amount of energy without emitting any greenhouse gases. unlike in fission, there is no chain reaction in fusion. fuel is inexhaustible, as it can be derived directly from hydrogen isotopes. i believe that budgetary control and more economic management must be ensured by improving the awarding of contracts. equally important is the evaluation in the context of the coordination of project and european contribution quality assurance and control.
in writing. − the objective of the proposal for a council decision is to define the financing scheme applicable to the eu contribution to the iter project for the period 2014 to 2018 through a 'supplementary research programme' under the euratom treaty. the council follows the recommendations made by the commission that eu funding for the iter project after 2013 should proceed outside the multiannual financial framework (mff). it is therefore proposed that the supplementary research programme be set up. in the proposal for a council decision, this 'programme shall be financed by contributions from the member states, based on a mobilisation rate applied to each member state's gni as defined for the purpose of calculating the contribution to the general budget of the eu'. the rapporteur believes that the iter project should be financed by the mff and through eu own resources. the rapporteur also proposes to increase the budget of the iter project to cope with unforeseen events and in the name of the advancement of scientific research. we share the view that scientific knowledge and technological development must be advanced in this field too. but we cannot ignore the colossal amount of resources that have been channeled into this project, under natural and understandable criticism. that is why we abstained.
in writing. − in 2012 the council decided to consult parliament on the adoption of the supplementary research programme for the iter project (2014-2018). the european economic and social committee called for more investment in r & d of technologies with an energy potential that respects the environment, including the development and exploitation of fusion energy. the eesc also strongly opposed the commission's proposal to withdraw the iter (international thermonuclear experimental reactor) project from the multiannual financial framework. fusion releases energy when the nuclei of two light atoms join together, for example, when two hydrogen nuclei fuse to form a single new atom. this process releases a huge amount of energy without emitting any greenhouse gases (ghgs). the strategy for the development of fusion as a credible option for commercial ghg-free energy production will respect a roadmap with important milestones for achieving the 2050 electricity production target. unlike in fission, there is no chain reaction in fusion. i voted in favour of this proposal which aims at producing an inexhaustible and environmentally friendly fuel.

in writing. - i approve this report, taking into account that the three countries, lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria, had old nuclear reactors in operation which, in the opinion of the international community, were too old and could not be adapted to the minimum safety standards required at an economically acceptable cost. in the context of the negotiations on accession to the european union, the three countries committed themselves to shutting down and subsequently dismantling these nuclear reactors by agreed dates. recognising that early shutdown represents exceptional social, environmental, economic and financial burdens, the european union has committed to provide financial assistance by the end of 2013 for the decommissioning of these reactors and to address the consequences of early shutdown. the current proposal also makes a number of simplifications. a single council regulation is provided for for the union's financial support to bulgaria, lithuania and slovakia under the multiannual financial framework (mff) 2014-2020, instead of the three previous, separate and independent regulations. this regulation does not provide for any exceptions to the financial regulation.
in writing. − the rules in force in the central and eastern european countries before accession were less stringent than the rules applied in the eu at the time. in addition, some of these states were still operating old soviet-made reactors which could not be adapted to the minimum safety standards required at an economically acceptable cost. for this reason, lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria undertook upon accession to dismantle reactors found to be non-compliant. this has required intervention and financial assistance from the eu, which we now approve to be extended over time.
in writing. the report by mr giles chichester deals with the proposal for a council regulation on european union support for nuclear decommissioning assistance programmes in bulgaria, lithuania and slovakia. the international community considered the old nuclear reactors in lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria to be too old and could not be upgraded to the minimum safety standards required at an economically acceptable cost. so the three countries have committed themselves to shut down and dismantle these nuclear reactors. early closure represents exceptional social, environmental, economic and financial burdens and the european union has therefore committed to providing financial assistance until the end of 2013. the beneficiary member states updated their estimates and found a deficit of 2 500 million in relation to the current available budget at national and programme level. i believe that the commission should carry out, in close cooperation with the member states and beneficiaries, a mid-term and a final evaluation of the achievement of the objectives, the level of results and impacts and the efficiency of the use of resources, adjusting the appropriations allocated to the programme. i also believe that the lack of funding puts the completion of the decommissioning procedures in doubt.

mr president, commissioner, if we approve this cohesion policy, portugal will receive over 21 billion euros over the next seven years, a crucial sum to boost a new dynamic of economic growth and job creation. but this was not an easy process. the commission notes that the aid granted to the beneficiary was granted in the form of a grant of eur [...] per beneficiary. it was a very difficult negotiation between the european institutions, including here in the european parliament. after more than a year and a half of negotiations, more than 2 000 amendments and more than 70 trilogues, we have finally reached an agreement which greatly improves the applicability of the structural funds in my region, madeira. is it a perfect deal? of course not ! is that the deal? of course i did! with this agreement, we are in a position to approve a cohesion policy which will guarantee madeira financing of eur 844 million, which will offset the costs of the outermost regions by eur 30 per inhabitant and ensure the standardisation of co-financing rates at 85%. this agreement will make it possible to finance airport and port infrastructure and the creation of shipping lines, which are essential to reducing our peripheral position in the european union. the priority now is that this package should be adopted here, that it should enter into force quickly and that it can be implemented, thereby promoting a cycle of economic growth and job creation that is capable of restoring hope to the citizens of europe. thank you very much.
we are approving the cohesion policy and its instruments, which are indispensable for overcoming the crisis. in the face of the scarcity of funds available, european funds are crucial for financing growth and employment policies in the eu. many of our problems stem from competitive imbalances within the union, which are the main cause of the external deficits that lead to indebtedness. we are only concerned with maintaining the objectives of reducing regional disparities, especially in the most disadvantaged areas. but we had to fight hard to keep these goals from being compromised. examples are the maintenance of funds for the outermost regions at acceptable levels or their ability to access crossborder cooperation for the first time, creating new export opportunities. i cannot, however, fail to stress our opposition to macro-conditionality. this is perhaps the most negative aspect of the new programme. it is an unacceptable principle that only certain states should be penalised twice or that funds and investment capacity should be withdrawn from a region because of the failure of the member state concerned to comply. thank you very much.
the new european funds do not offer solutions to reverse the growing gap between the biggest beneficiaries of the eu's single market and common policies and the countries with the weakest economies, such as portugal. these funds - now called the structural and investment funds, which correspond to the former structural and cohesion funds - are reduced overall by 8.4% compared with the previous financial framework. in addition, the objectives and scope of funding are becoming more restrictive. macroeconomic conditionality (to be added to the european semester/economic governance and the budget treaty) establishes a permanent blackmail, threatening cuts or suspension of payments in case of non-compliance with the dictates of the eu institutions. a blackmail that increasingly conditions decisions on priorities and how the funds will be implemented decisions that are increasingly outside the institutions of national sovereignty. the aim is, of course, to promote investment in private or privatised infrastructure, or to promote the (well-known) public-private partnerships. the structural and cohesion funds, which for years have been presented as the panacea for all the problems of the weaker economies, are far from compensating for the extremely negative impact of the destruction of their productive apparatus and their growing dependence and subordination.
mr president, i congratulate vice-president viviane reding on her initiative and my fellow rapporteurs rodi kratsa-tsagaropoulou and evelyn regner on their excellent work in advocating and promoting the balanced representation of men and women in board positions in publicly traded companies. the various calls for self-regulation have not had any significant effect. this proposal is therefore timely and justified. it is justified because, firstly, women represent almost 60% of all university graduates in the union; secondly, despite being highly qualified, women continue to be unjustifiably under-represented on the boards of european companies. and this proposal is timely because at the current rate it would take several decades to eliminate this imbalance. i agree with the objective of a minimum 40% presence of men or women among non-executive directors of listed companies by 2020 and i agree with transparent selection processes with clear and non-discriminatory criteria on the qualifications and competences of candidates regardless of gender. the european parliament is thus sending a clear signal to the council. this is another step in the defence of equality between men and women, which europe has been defending for the last 50 years and of which this parliament should be proud. thank you very much.
the proposal under consideration, although it covers only companies with more than 250 employees and an annual turnover of more than eur 50 million, can help to correct the gender imbalances in decision-making processes. it could be more ambitious, but it is a first step towards ensuring women's access to economic power. the directive also represents a smart investment in business management. it is proven that companies with more women on their boards perform better than those with less female representation in top positions. on the other hand, gender studies have highlighted that women have a different management style, as they avoid risk and favour a long-term perspective. the european parliament's amendments significantly improve the commission's proposal, particularly as regards sanctions, by adding mandatory sanctions rather than merely indicative ones. the financial and economic crisis presents a unique opportunity to make important structural changes in the macroeconomic and financial architecture for global development, reflecting equitable and human rights-based principles and taking into account the perspective of gender equality and women's rights.
i would like to begin by pointing out a mistake which i think some of the speakers have made. and the mistake is this: they are the ones who think that the division of the european institutions into cities and countries should be the same for all types of institutions. we cannot confuse the council, the commission and parliament with the other institutions, because they are constantly interacting, they are constantly interlinked. the political heart of the european union must therefore be based in the same city for practical reasons and for constitutional reasons of better political control. this has nothing to do with the central bank, the court of justice or the administrative agencies because these institutions are independent of the political heart and can therefore be, without any disadvantage, based outside that political heart. secondly, it is said here that we are defending polycentrism, that we want to defend polycentrism, but what is happening at the moment is that the european parliament itself is polycentric, so to speak, and this has costs. in addition to cost, it causes a huge strain on all the people who work in this institution and therefore hinders the exercise of the activity. i would also like to say this: i also congratulate the rapporteurs because, for me, the reason for choosing a single seat should not be a symbolic reason related to the history of europe, nor a practical reason related to costs, but a constitutional reason, a political reason. a parliament which wants to be an effective parliament must have the right to choose the way, the time and the place of its meeting. this is essential. without this parliament will not be able to assert itself, and for those of us who believe, as i do, in greater integration and even in a federal project, this is a sine qua non condition for us to assert ourselves, even if it means disregarding a decision of the court or even the treaties. only when parliament takes its destiny into its own hands will it be able to be a real parliament.

reinforcement of the oldest community policy, which europe needs today as much as in the past and which allows us to continue to be leaders on the world market, to remain at the top of food quality and food safety and to keep europe's rural areas alive and sustainable.

from the beginning of this process we have been fighting for a genuine cap, capable of becoming a fairer policy in the distribution of aid, more sustainable and competitive, guaranteeing productive and profitable farms throughout the union. the truth is that in many respects we have not gone as far as we wanted to go and in others we have fallen short of what was needed, as in the dairy sector. we have, however, managed to move the cap in the right direction by giving value to producer organisations, agricultural research and innovation, supporting young farmers and simplifying processes for small farmers by introducing risk management and insurance systems in production and incomes. we are concerned, however, about areas which have not been resolved by the reform and which it is essential to resolve, such as the continuation of milk production in the outermost regions and in mountain regions, the abuse of a dominant position in the food chain and in the dairy sector.

in writing. the european commission strategy, presented on 22 november, focuses mainly on the implementation and enforcement of measures already adopted. the aim is therefore to bring the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework into force as early as january 2014 and for member states to start applying this funding to sustainable value-added projects capable of creating jobs and growth. the commission also stressed that the completion of economic union required the closure of certain issues, notably banking union, the internal market, the digital agenda and the adoption of the single supervisory mechanism fund. for the first time, the commission has detailed a list of priorities it wants to see adopted: the railway package, the long-term investment fund, the telecommunications package, the european union's emissions trading scheme for aviation. at a turning point, with a new framework programme for 2014-2020, the union and the member states need to implement a coordinated strategy aligned with the eu2020 objectives. only a joint, defined and coordinated response can revitalise europe from the economic crisis that has gripped the world since 2008.

in writing. − the european union solidarity fund aims to ensure rapid, effective and flexible assistance to the population of a member state and countries negotiating its accession in the event of a major natural disaster. this fund complements public funds from member states in emergency situations, in particular for the urgent rehabilitation of infrastructure, temporary accommodation and emergency services to meet the immediate needs of the population, as well as for the cleaning up of the areas affected by the disaster. in the summer of 2012, romania was affected by drought, a huge drop in agricultural production, numerous fires and water shortages. in may and june 2013 germany, austria and the czech republic were affected by catastrophic floods. following the disasters, the countries concerned requested assistance from the european union solidarity fund. in accordance with the eligibility criteria, the mobilisation of eur 400 519 089 in commitment and payment appropriations from the european union solidarity fund was approved to alleviate the pain, suffering and losses of the people affected by these disasters. i therefore support this report.

in writing. the agreement between the european union and russia aims to improve cooperation between the two partners in the control of the trade in drug precursors. the agreement establishes cooperation between the two parties for the control of trade in certain chemicals and mechanisms for mutual administrative assistance in the form of data exchange. this agreement contributes to a clear european strategy based on a common approach by the major trading powers, in particular the producers and consumers of drugs, with the aim of putting an end to the drug trade affecting them by strengthening and jointly and ambitiously controlling the international trade and exchanges in these precursors, which make the production of many synthetic drugs possible. the aim is therefore to reinforce the obstacles to traffickers by means of greater control of the points of origin and destination of the chemicals and medicinal products concerned, without endangering the lawful trade in these products. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - the european union and the russian federation share an interest in effectively combating drug trafficking. both societies suffer from the scourge of drug addiction. they therefore have a strong interest in coordinating this fight and in promoting joint actions that can enhance their respective responses to a problem of such magnitude. drug precursors are not illegal in themselves but may be subject to illicit use. this dual use suggests caution in trade and vigilance in use. i hope that this agreement will prove fruitful and that it will be another important step towards convergence of positions and strengthening of cooperation and trust between the european union and russia.
in writing. the report by mr proust deals with the draft proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the russian federation on drug precursors. drug precursors are legal substances that can be used in the chemical process of manufacturing synthetic drugs. ex: acetic acid which is used in the manufacture of heroin. this international agreement was signed on 4 june 2013 at the eu-russia summit in ekaterinburg and aims to control the bilateral and legal trade in products that are misused and illegally used in the manufacture of drugs. i think it is essential that this agreement be guided by a high degree of trust and transparency between the two parties. the european commission should establish good cooperation relations with the russian federal customs service in the fight against drugs.

in writing. − i approve this report in view of the fact that the eric regulation1 was adopted by the council in 2009 to facilitate the establishment and operation of european research infrastructures in non-economic ways. many of the projects included in the roadmap of the european research infrastructure strategies forum plan to use the eric as a legal instrument to create and operate research infrastructure. however, the eric regulation provides for a distinction and difference of treatment between member states, associated countries, non-associated third countries and intergovernmental organisations. associated countries, in particular norway, have clearly indicated that they intend to contribute, as host countries or as members, to a significant number of erics in the pipeline, if they have voting rights in erics identical to those of the member states of the european union, especially when they are the host country of an eric, which implies a significant contribution to its activities. since the purpose of the proposed amendment to the eric regulation is to put an end to this distinction, i have no objection to its approval.
in writing. the amendment is not without its major comments. the need to develop european research infrastructures and the importance of these infrastructures for the vitality of european science and research and the economy itself is also important. it is worthwhile to see investment in research and science as a priority and to resist the temptation to look for immediate results or applications. history shows that discoveries apparently devoid of practical use have proved essential to the viability of later inventions, designs and systems. while the lisbon strategy's blueprint has failed, its ambition to make the union the most competitive economic area based on technology and innovation - can and should continue to guide policy-makers, entrepreneurs, universities and research centres - is no less true.
in writing. the report by ms sartori deals with the proposal for a council regulation amending regulation (ec) no 723/2009 on the community legal framework for the european research infrastructure consortium (eric). the eric regulation was adopted by the council in 2009 to facilitate the establishment and operation of european research infrastructures in non-economic ways. this regulation created a new legal instrument at eu level for the creation of european research infrastructures with legal personality recognised in all member states. i agree with the aim of the proposed amendment to the eric regulation to put an end to a situation where associated countries are not eligible to become host countries or members of an eric because their voting rights do not currently correspond to the financial support they would provide for eric projects.
in writing. − the european research infrastructure (eric) regulation was adopted in 2009 to facilitate the creation and operation of european research infrastructures in non-economic ways. many of the projects included in the roadmap of the european strategy forum for research infrastructures (esfri) plan to use the eric as a legal instrument to create and operate research infrastructure. this report aims to change the rules for setting up an eric by making them more flexible. it also aims to enable associated countries to participate fully in the establishment and operation of eric consortia as members or as host countries and to contribute to those infrastructures. this is without prejudice to the importance of simplifying the creation of world-class research infrastructures in europe, with the added value they can bring in terms of enhancing the quality of research and teaching, the links established between researchers and, in general, their positive socio-economic impact. however, we do not agree that the creation of large infrastructures will only create more opportunities for excellence, which will lead to certain countries being the main beneficiaries of the process. we want everyone to benefit, even those who cannot set up centres of excellence, to enable the democratisation of research in the most diverse fields.
in writing. − the eric regulation was adopted by the council in 2009 to facilitate the establishment and operation of european research infrastructures in non-economic ways. this regulation created a new legal instrument at eu level for the creation of european research infrastructures with legal personality recognised in all member states. the purpose of the proposed amendment to the eric regulation is to put an end to a situation where associated countries are not eligible to become host countries or members of an eric because their voting rights do not currently correspond to the financial support they would provide to eric projects. the proposed amendment to the regulation provides that an eric must be formed by at least one member state and joined by at least two member states or associated countries. it also provides that member states or associated countries shall jointly hold a majority of the voting rights in the general assembly. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − the eric (european research infrastructure consortium) regulation has implemented a new legal instrument at european union level for the creation of european research infrastructures with legal personality recognised in all member states. this proposed amendment to the eric regulation aims to put an end to the current situation where associated countries are unable to meet the conditions to become host countries or members of an eric. i believe it is very important that the associated countries should have the opportunity to participate fully in the creation and activities of the eric consortia, which is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. − the regulation on a european research infrastructure (eric) was adopted by the council in 2009 to facilitate the establishment and operation of european research infrastructures in non-economic ways. this regulation created a new legal instrument at eu level for the creation of european research infrastructures with legal personality recognised in all member states. the associated countries, in particular norway, have clearly indicated that they intend to contribute, as host countries or as members, to a significant number of eric consortia that are in the pipeline, if they have voting rights in erics that are identical to those of eu member states. thus, the objective of the proposed amendment to the eric regulation is to put an end to a situation where associated countries are not eligible to become host countries or members of an eric. our concern with this system is that the creation of large infrastructures may only allow for more opportunities to achieve excellence in research in various fields, leading to certain countries being the main beneficiaries of the process. we want everyone to benefit, even those who cannot set up centres of excellence, to enable the democratisation of research in the most diverse fields.
i voted against this report because it confirms what was already the tendency, which was defined yesterday in this house, to impose macroeconomic conditionality, that is to say, to penalize twice the countries in difficulty if they do not meet the deficit and debt criteria. no sanctions of any kind are acceptable. we already have sanctions in the economic governance package that can go up to 1% of gdp and now these sanctions are being joined by sanctions relating to the structural funds that have nothing to do with the non-compliance with the deficit or the debt. this is another report which confirms that the european project is no longer a solidarity project and therefore cannot be supported.
i would like to say that i voted against this report for the same reasons as i voted yesterday against the multiannual financial framework. instead of a europe of solidarity, we have a europe of punishment, and in this report, as in the multiannual financial framework, what is envisaged is that countries which do not meet the debt and deficit target will be doubly penalized, in this particular case, in this report, with regard to the structural funds, the cohesion funds and the social funds. the countries which are not meeting the deficit and debt targets are the ones which have been punished the most, which have no possibility of public investment, and the adoption of these clauses only perpetuates austerity and increases the debt without any possibility of public investment.

in writing. the framework for esf action is laid down in the common provisions regulation. this regulation aims to define the mission, scope and investment priorities of the esf for 2014-2020. the general policy orientation for esf activities is to be strongly linked to the integrated guidelines of the eu 2020 strategy and to the country-specific recommendations developed in the framework of the european semester. the aim is to push for a more neoliberal strand of the esf, which is clear when one of the esf's investment priorities is: modernisation of labour market institutions such as public and private employment services, improving labour market fit-out, including measures to increase cross-border national mobility through mobility schemes and improved cooperation between institutions and relevant parties. however, there are positive aspects to the regulation, such as the allocation of a minimum of 20% of the total esf resources to the fight against poverty and social exclusion. there are other positive aspects, relating to equal opportunities and non-discrimination, the fight against early school leaving, vocational education and training, lifelong learning, work-life balance.

in writing. the framework for esf action is laid down in the regulation on common provisions. this regulation aims to define the mission, scope and investment priorities of the esf for the period 2014-2020. the commission's original proposal was retained. the general policy orientation for esf activities is thus to be strongly linked to the europe 2020 integrated guidelines. the commission intends to put a more neoliberal element at the bottom. thus, in the article on the scope of intervention they consider that one of the esf investment priorities is: modernisation of labour market institutions such as public and private employment services, improvement of labour market fit, including measures to increase cross-border national mobility through mobility schemes and better cooperation between institutions and relevant parties. however, positive aspects were included in the regulation, such as the obligation to include a minimum amount of 20% of each member state's total esf resources to strengthen its support for the fight against poverty and social exclusion. we think that this fund should be strengthened and that it should not be subject to the principle of macro-conditionality, as it will be from now on. we abstained.

in writing. − the european territorial cooperation programme aims to strengthen territorial cohesion by sharing good practices and experiences between regions, to give a new impetus to the development of joint projects between european union territories and to create networks between regions with common resources and strategies. i am voting in favour of this regulation because, in the negotiations that have taken place, the european parliament has succeeded in introducing a flexibility of 150 km in crossborder cooperation programmes, so that madeira and the azores can receive more money to promote cooperation with neighbouring regions and benefit from more european funds in this area of programming. the importance of developing projects between the outermost regions and third countries is also emphasised, thus giving a new strategic impetus to relations between madeira and cape verde. in addition, the ors should receive at least 150% of the funds they received under the erdf in 2007-2013 and an additional financial envelope of eur 50 million for interregional cooperation projects.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that in the context of the legislative package for cohesion policy as proposed by the commission, the cohesion fund is part of the new common strategic framework funds which will cover the structural funds, the cohesion fund, as well as the european agricultural fund for rural development and the european maritime and fisheries fund. although the commission is proposing a new framework for the funds, the scope and specific objectives for the cohesion fund are not drastically changed compared to the current programming period. in its proposal for a regulation laying down common provisions for all the funds which will replace the current general regulation (the gfr), the commission advocates a different structure of missions and objectives for the funds, assigning them to the investment for growth and jobs goal in order to contribute to the union strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. it should also be noted that the issue of macroeconomic conditionality was widely discussed and it was ultimately decided to leave decisions on this issue to the drc negotiations, which were considered the most appropriate framework to address the problem from a more general perspective.
in writing. − i welcome the cohesion funds for 2014-2020 approved by the european parliament, which should help regions make investments that will enable them to overcome the current economic crisis. over the next seven years portugal will receive eur 19.6 billion (at 2011 prices) and will benefit until the end of 2015 from the increase in the maximum rate of community co-financing from 85% to 95%. in particular, i am pleased that the new cohesion policy rules are less bureaucratic and that they support projects in areas such as innovation, research and energy efficiency.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the cohesion fund, as it will make it possible to provide financial support to member states with lower per capita incomes by co-financing key projects and infrastructure, in particular in the area of the environment, which will help to support the transition to a low-carbon economy in all sectors, promote adaptation to climate change and risk prevention and management, as well as protect the environment and promote energy efficiency.
in writing. − the cohesion fund is part of the new common strategic framework funds which will cover the structural funds, the cohesion fund, as well as the european agricultural fund for rural development and the european maritime and fisheries fund. in the proposal for a regulation laying down common provisions for all the funds which will replace the current general regulation, the commission advocated a different structure of missions and objectives for the funds, assigning them to the investment for growth and jobs goal in order to contribute to the eu strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. the cohesion fund will also contribute to this objective and mission by supporting member states with a gross national income per capita below 90% of the eu-27 average, thus enabling a larger share of the eu population to be covered.
in writing. − the cohesion fund is intended to help member states whose gdp per capita is less than 90% of the eu-27 average to reduce economic and social backwardness and to stabilise the economy. it supports investments in the ten-t transport networks and in the environment. it will support energy-related projects, provided that they have clear environmental benefits, for example by promoting energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy. it will support investments in climate change adaptation and risk prevention, in the water and waste sectors, in low-carbon transport systems and in urban transport. in view of the importance of the cohesion fund, i regret once again the reduction in funds for this area for the 2014-2020 mff, as the amount allocated to it in the current framework has been reduced from eur 71 billion to eur 68.7 billion (at constant 2011 prices). in this context, i would stress the position already taken by the european parliament and reiterated by the rapporteur on the need for increased resources to achieve the political and legal objectives also agreed by the member states for 2014-2020.
in writing. − the cohesion fund - which is now subject to macroeconomic conditionality and the european semester - has been reduced compared to the current financial framework (2007-2013). that means less money and more difficulties in using it. moreover, priorities are inadequate in the face of real needs. countries like portugal, which need to increase national production, maintain and create jobs, raise wages, are denied the supposed solidarity that would come from the funds, and their right to sovereign development is conditioned on them, in accordance with the rights and aspirations of their people. a significant part of this fund will be earmarked for the connecting europe facility. investment in network infrastructure linked to water and waste collection and distribution is promoted, citing the need for its rationalisation, with the clear aim of promoting its privatisation. the fight against climate change is one of the main objectives and the specialisation of regions and countries with weak productive sectors is one of them. by mystifying environmental problems, those responsible for them and the necessary measures. asymmetries in development are perpetuated, condemning large regions of countries such as portugal to a model of labour force providers and natural reserves where the projects of multinationals that dominate so-called green technologies and infrastructure will be implemented with public funding.
in writing. − cohesion funds will be subject to common provisions in several areas of programming and financial management. the cohesion fund, the erdf and the esf will continue to be subject to another set of common specific rules on programming, management and monitoring. although the commission is proposing a new framework for the funds, the scope and specific objectives for the cohesion fund are not drastically changed compared to the current programming period. as regards investment priorities (article 3), environmental issues have received particular attention, with a major commitment being made in the water and waste sectors, where investments are not only intended to meet the requirements of the union's environmental acquis, but also to respond to needs identified by member states that go beyond those requirements. support for the natura 2000 network and green transport is also a result of this approach. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the cohesion fund aims to support member states with a gni per capita below 90% of the eu27 average to integrate into the european union's single market by financing essential transport infrastructure and promoting compliance with environmental standards, through support for energy-related projects, provided that they have clear environmental benefits, such as the promotion of energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy. i am voting in favour of this cohesion fund regulation because portugal and madeira are largely benefiting from the changes introduced during the negotiations. the european parliament has succeeded in widening the range of eligible projects, so that those in the area of transport infrastructure can now be financed, particularly those most useful to the portuguese maritime (commercial and passenger ports) and air transport regions. in addition, in the next programming period (2014-2020), the structural funds may also support inter-island transport systems, intermodal links or the urban regeneration of madeiran cities.

in writing. the objectives of the european groupings for territorial cooperation (egtc) are simplification and rapid authorisation, legal certainty, reduction of red tape and extension of their scope to the areas of public transport, energy, water supply, health, education and vocational training. apart from the objectives and the framework, the provisions for the employment of staff of the egtcs are controversial in this proposal. the regulation for the new programming period proposes a light version of the bolkestein directive, providing that members of egtcs may choose between the labour law of the country where the grouping is based and the national law of the officials concerned. as we have said before, what is at stake is not mutual cooperation, based on solidarity and the sovereignty and complementary interests of the countries involved, which we would agree with, but rather the removal of the obstacles to the sovereign and national development models that persist.

in writing. - i approve this report in view of the fact that over the years many member states have taken initiatives to combat effectively the problem of gender imbalance. some member states have sought to increase the low representation of women on boards through the adoption of legislation, thereby considerably speeding up the process of achieving a balanced representation of men and women on boards. others have limited themselves to encouraging proactive initiatives and measures taken by enterprises, which has proved to be quite useful but still insufficient to achieve tangible results. in this context, it is important to note the heterogeneity that exists in the european union, both in terms of measures and results. in my view, in order to effectively meet the challenges it faces in the vulnerable context of the current economic crisis, the european union must use all the human capital it has at its disposal to achieve growth and promote competitiveness and improve the financial performance of enterprises. measures aimed at achieving a better balance between men and women on boards of directors contribute to this objective.
in writing. − in 2012, in the european union, only 8.9% of the chief executives of large companies were women. and women held the position of chairman of the board of directors in only 2.4% of the companies. if the european situation is worrying, the portuguese situation is no better. in october 2012, only 7,4% of the board members of the largest portuguese companies (listed in the psi 20) were women. this is about half the european average of 15.8%. none of these portuguese companies had a woman as chairman of the board of directors (the european average is 3.3%). and none of these companies had a woman as ceo (the european average was 2.4%, as you can see from the top of the building). equality between men and women is a fundamental right enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. but the reasons for fighting for gender parity in top positions are not just about social justice issues. gender parity at the top contributes to improving the performance and competitiveness of companies.
in writing. - as i have said many times in this house, men and women must be treated equally, given the same rights but with special consideration for their needs, which in the case of women is particularly evident in areas such as maternity protection and reconciling work and family life. but i do not agree that gender equality is achieved through quota systems. quotas are the undermining of women, who are promoted to certain positions solely on the basis of their gender and not on the basis of their competence, ability or appetite. the commission's intention to apply them to private undertakings is therefore inadmissible. finally, as a staunch supporter of the principle of subsidiarity, i believe that many of the issues discussed in this report, although important and relevant, should remain within the sphere of the autonomy of the states.
in writing. − gender equality, particularly the challenge of establishing equal access for men and women to positions of power and influence, is a key challenge for the european union. the eu has been a major player in this area and has taken on a clear role as a global player in the fight against discrimination. however, despite the best efforts that have been made, the goal of gender equality is far from being achieved. it is therefore important to ensure that legislation is as effective as possible in order to reinforce this european desire. we all stand to gain from the prevalence of merit and greater transparency in the recruitment of executives to the boards of companies and public institutions. in this context, it is of great importance to establish a clear common strategy for all member states with a view to achieving the common objective of achieving by 2020 a minimum of 40% for the under-represented sex among non-executive directors in privately listed companies, with that deadline being lowered to 2018 for publicly listed companies.
in writing. − the aim of this proposal for a directive is to substantially increase the number of women on boards of directors of companies across the eu - a goal which we can share. however, it does so by setting a minimum target of 40% of members of the under-represented sex among non-executive directors of listed companies and by requiring companies in which the number of members of the under-represented sex is below that percentage to apply, in order to achieve that target, pre-established criteria in their selection procedures to fill those positions. in other words, it does so by resorting to the logic of quotas, in a way that is not without ambiguities and contradictions and with which we disagree. there are aspects of the report which merit our agreement. we disagree about others. but at a time when the economic and social crisis and its effects are worsening, when women are being hit the hardest, when gender inequalities are widening, when the situation of women workers is worsening, the priority given by the commission to this issue of gender equality in the boards of directors is questionable to say the least.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report as a whole, but against the creation of a measure, albeit temporary, aimed at establishing a clear common strategy for all member states to achieve a common objective: the presence of at least 40% of the under-represented sex among non-executive directors by 2020 for privately listed companies, and by 2018 for publicly listed companies. i am a strong supporter of gender equality, considering that the quota system should be applied very carefully and not generically, and i consider it to be an unfair and harmful interference in the economic activity of companies.
in writing. − in november 2012, the european commission put forward a proposal that aims to substantially increase the number of women on boards of directors of companies across the eu, setting a minimum target of 40% of members of the underrepresented sex among non-executive directors of listed companies. i am in favour of actions to promote greater gender equality in the workplace, boardroom renewal, promoting the issue in business schools and new ways to encourage sociocultural change. however, i am against the setting of quotas at any time, and in this case the aim is to set a minimum quota limit of 40% for the underrepresented sex on the boards of directors, which is the factor which led me to vote against the regulation in question. i believe that the quota system should not be implemented under any circumstances, and that citizens should be able to reach business or political positions according to their competence, university studies or technical knowledge to the detriment of their gender. i also believe that the european authorities should not interfere in the executive and non-executive management bodies of private companies.
in writing. − this proposal for a directive aims to substantially increase the number of women on boards of directors of companies across the eu by setting a minimum target of 40% of members of the underrepresented sex among non-executive directors of listed companies and by requiring companies with less than this percentage of members of the underrepresented sex to apply, in order to achieve this target, pre-established criteria to fill these positions, with the exception of small and medium-sized enterprises in 2020. the situation in 2012 was as follows: 85% of non-executive members and 91.1% of executive board members are men, while women represented 15% and 8.9% respectively. the report supports this position and considers that companies that fail to comply with the rules of this directive should be obliged to explain the reasons to the competent national authorities of the states and should be sanctioned. this is another make-up operation to pretend to strengthen equality between men and women, when most women are losing the labour, social and economic rights so essential to their independence. this reality will not change one iota with this directive.
in writing. - i approve this report, stating that from the beginning of this process i have been fighting for a genuine reform of the cap capable of becoming a fairer policy in the distribution of aid, more sustainable and competitive, guaranteeing productive and profitable agricultural holdings throughout the union. the truth is that in many respects we have not gone as far as we wanted to go and in others we have fallen short of what was needed, as in the dairy sector. we have, however, managed to move the cap in the right direction by giving value to producer organisations, inter-branch organisations, agricultural research and innovation, supporting young farmers and giving simplified treatment to small farmers, introducing production and income risk management supported by insurance systems. i would like to conclude by saying that i am concerned, however, about the areas which have not been resolved by the reform and which are essential to resolve, such as the continuation of milk production in the outermost regions and in mountain regions, the abuse of a dominant position in the food chain and the lack of mechanisms for regulating supply in the milk sector.
in writing. − this regulation lays down the rules for the financing of expenditure under the cap, including rural development, the agricultural advisory system, the management and control systems to be set up by the member states, the system of cross-compliance and the clearance of accounts. it is, of course, imbued with the spirit of reform. the path outlined here is that of deepening the general guidelines of the cap, i.e. that of liberalization and deregulation, which leaves portugal further away from what should be the first objective of an agricultural policy: ensuring food security and food sovereignty in each country in a sustainable way. we voted against it. the hundreds of amendments we have proposed to the various regulations have shown that it is possible to achieve another result, namely by giving guarantees to small farmers and family farming. it was proposed that the scandalous inequalities in direct payments between countries and producers should be eliminated by 2020, and these inequalities persist with this reform. we are in favour of another regulation of the markets, capable of ensuring fair prices for production and instruments for regulating production, adapted to the needs of each country and its relative level of production capacity, allowing differentiated development in countries with higher deficits.
in writing. − the attempt to concentrate in a single instrument all the provisions and requirements for the implementation of the common agricultural policy has the meritorious purpose of making them more readable and accessible, which was not always easy, and is another attempt to make it more rational and efficient and less bureaucratic. the financing, management and monitoring of the cap must not only meet criteria of reasonableness, adequacy and proportionality but also be capable of being understood and scrutinized. it is therefore called upon to increase transparency and to make a constant effort to reduce bureaucracy.
in writing. − the common agricultural policy (cap) has been thoroughly redesigned and adapted to the challenges and needs of the new times, in a process of optimising resources and mechanisms which is also based on the experience of the 51 years of the cap, which has been very successful in meeting the objectives of providing eu citizens with enough food at affordable prices, while respecting food security and ensuring a decent standard of living for farmers. in this context, the reform of the cap must cover all its main instruments, regulation, financing and monitoring. a reform that will help implement a greener cap and correct the problem of low farmer incomes: the average wage of a non-agricultural worker in the eu is 40% lower than the average wage of a non-agricultural worker in the eu. the new cap will respond to the challenges posed by a highly competitive global market, climate change, soil saturation, population growth, ageing populations and rural neglect. farmers face a twofold challenge: to produce more food on an economically viable basis, and at the same time to protect nature and safeguard biodiversity. to do this, the cap must rely on research and innovation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the financing, management and surveillance of the common agricultural policy, as i considered that the compromise text resulting from the trilogues significantly improves on the commission's initial proposal. in this particular case, i would like to highlight as a particularly positive factor the fact that the horizontal regulation lays down reasonable rules on expenditure in the agricultural advisory system, the management and control systems to be implemented by the member states, the cross-compliance system and the clearance of accounts, so that they are feasible without any increase in complexity or bureaucracy.
in writing. − this proposal is part of the legislative package on the reform of the common agricultural policy (cap) from 2014, in whose legislative procedure the european parliament for the first time decides on an equal footing with the council. the main results of the document are the new control and sanction systems, the alert system, the reduction in the number of controls and the reduction of the risk related to the control procedure, the reduction of bureaucracy, better proposals on the agricultural council system and the monitoring and evaluation of the cap. i therefore voted in favour of this document.
