in writing. - while the interinstitutional agreement reached is not the ideal one, it is nevertheless the one that is possible in highly sensitive and technical matters such as agriculture. it is not too much to recall the priorities for rural development: fostering knowledge transfer and innovation; strengthening competitiveness; promoting the organisation of food chains and risk management; restoring, preserving and improving ecosystems; promoting resource efficiency and the transition to a low-carbon economy; promoting social inclusion, poverty reduction and economic development in rural areas. it is particularly clear that the social function of agriculture goes far beyond food production. without this notion it is not possible to understand much of the policy options which arise in particular from the needs of territorial occupation, of protecting the environment of the settlement of populations. i would stress parliament's concern to provide young farmers with better conditions for carrying out their activities. i hope that young people who wish to do so will be able to take up agricultural projects and that they will be able to do so in a sustained way so as to rejuvenate the sector and give it the new vitality that the union so badly needs.
in writing. - rural development is a european priority. given that almost 60% of the population of the 28 eu member states live in rural areas and that these cover 90% of the territory, the importance of a living and sustainable natural area for european citizens is clear. here too, technological and organisational innovation, as well as innovation and knowledge transfer, must remain at the heart of the rural development strategy. more emphasis should be placed on private investment and increased coordination between research institutions and other stakeholders in rural areas in order to strengthen support for the competitiveness of these regions. i would also stress the concern and the need to solve the problems of young farmers with access to agricultural land by enabling the member states to have recourse to more support and financial instruments. in this context, i support the present report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on support for rural development by the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd).
in writing. − this regulation lays down the general rules for eu support for rural development financed by the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd). it defines the objectives to which rural development policy should contribute and the specific priorities in this area, including the strategic context of rural development policy, measures, rules and programming, management, monitoring and evaluation, based on shared responsibilities between the member states and the commission. the proposal for a regulation follows the logic of the cap reform, which we have been criticising. in general, it does not reflect, as it should, the needs of supporting and enhancing national agriculture, especially small and mediumsized farmers and family farming, thus helping to reverse the economic, social and human desertification of the rural world. it is regrettable that the need to use socioeconomic criteria in addition to biophysical criteria (predominantly oriented towards the reality of some countries to the detriment of others) is not considered in the definition of less-favoured areas, as we have proposed. the gradual abolition of payments in areas which are no longer considered as less-favoured will have very negative effects. all this aggravates the shortcomings of this programme and the regulation now proposed.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on support for rural development by the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd) because i consider that the compromise text resulting from the trilogues significantly improves the commission's initial proposal. in the case of the eafrd, i would point out as particularly positive the increase in support for investment in the forestry sector, which has traditionally been neglected, the 85% co-financing for all the axes, simplified cross-compliance, a crop insurance system with community funding and incentives for producer organisations to achieve scale-up and mergers. i would stress the inclusion of support for new irrigation, mainly for the southern countries, and in particular portugal, which was completely absent from the commission proposal.
in writing. − this proposal is part of the legislative package on the reform of the common agricultural policy (cap) from 2014, in whose legislative procedure the european parliament, for the first time, decides on an equal footing with the council. the proposed new regulation builds on the existing system whereby member states develop programmes tailored to their specific needs within the eu. knowledge transfer, innovation, the organisation of the food chain, risk management, young farmers and environmental protection are key themes under this regulation. i therefore voted in favour of the document.
in writing. - i abstain from voting on this report. from the beginning of this process i have been campaigning for a genuine reform of the cap, capable of becoming a fairer policy in the distribution of aid, more sustainable and competitive, guaranteeing productive and profitable farms throughout the union. the truth is that in many respects we have not gone as far as we wanted to go and in others we have fallen short of what was needed, as in the milk sector. we have, however, managed to move the cap in the right direction by giving value to producer organisations, inter-branch organisations, agricultural research and innovation, supporting young farmers and giving simplified treatment to small farmers, introducing production and income risk management supported by insurance systems. i am concerned, however, about the areas which have not been resolved by the reform and which are essential to resolve, such as the continuation of milk production in the outermost regions and in mountain regions, the abuse of a dominant position in the food chain or the absence of supply regulation mechanisms in the milk sector.
in writing. the common organisation of the markets should respond to one of the major problems facing millions of producers in the eu: ensuring fair prices for production; prices that compensate farmers for their work. instead, the cmos have become an obstacle to this. it could more properly be called the common disorganization of markets, such is the deregulatory and liberalizing spirit that inspires it. the end of milk quotas is having very serious consequences. the situation will only get worse when the liberalized market is flooded with milk from abroad at impossible prices, wiping out domestic dairy farms. then the ps, psd and cds - who approved this reform - will come crying crocodile tears over spilled milk. it is vital to maintain milk production quotas and to extend them to other sectors, quotas adjusted to the production needs of each member state and its relative level of installed production capacity, in order to allow the differentiated development of countries with the highest deficits in their respective sectors. we have put forward a number of important and innovative proposals, such as the creation of a maximum intermediation margin scheme or the introduction of a national preference scheme in countries with a persistent agri-food balance deficit. they were rejected.
in writing. - the common organization of the markets within the framework of the cap could not fail to play a significant role in its present reform. i would like to draw attention to the organizations of the market in sugar, wine and olive oil. the individual approach to each sector leads to greater care for each one and the challenges they face in practice, seeking to provide farmers, producer associations and consumers with more guarantees of the proper functioning of the agricultural market, which avoids excessive income gaps, favours the quality of products in circulation on the market and takes into account the non-exclusively productive dimensions of agriculture.
in writing. − in the context of the reform of the common agricultural policy, also framed in the new multiannual financial framework for 2014-2020, the common organisation of the markets is an essential component and a high priority. improving regulation and reducing red tape for farmers are at the heart of the new regulation's concerns, which should contribute to the objectives set out in the cap reform. in a more efficient, intelligent, inclusive and sustainable europe, all excessive and unjustified administrative burdens and costs need to be eliminated. the harmonization, rationalisation and simplification of provisions and regulations is a priority. expenditure must be targeted at specific objectives to ensure the sound management of european funds with a view to providing basic public goods through a multifunctional cap.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a common organisation of the markets in agricultural products (single cmo regulation) because i consider that the compromise text resulting from the trilogues significantly improves the commission's initial proposal. in the case of the single cap, i would point out as particularly positive the strengthening of the negotiating role of producer organisations and inter-branch organisations, the expansion of private storage, the establishment of a risk management system based on the setting up of mutual funds and the decisions taken in the wine and sugar sectors which allow them to evolve and adapt to the markets without any upheavals. i regret the treatment of the milk sector because of the absence of concrete measures to ensure its sustainability in our country and in the azores region after the end of milk quotas. in general terms, i believe that the cmu has safeguarded important mechanisms for the stability of agricultural markets.
in writing. − this proposal is part of the legislative package on the reform of the common agricultural policy (cap) from 2014, in whose legislative procedure the european parliament, for the first time, decides on an equal footing with the council. the proposal contains some substantial amendments to the regulations on the common organisation of the markets in agricultural products currently in force, in particular in an attempt to improve the functioning of the food chain by facilitating cooperation between farmers. a safety net for crisis situations on agricultural markets is also maintained. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. − i approve this report, taking into account the new rules for direct payments which should ensure a fair and sustainable distribution of resources. i also support the idea of an ambitious greening of direct payments to farmers, which is one of the answers to today's environmental and social challenges. however, i believe that the current proposals are insufficient to allow the creation of advanced systems of sustainable agriculture, which are fundamental to the sustainable territorial development of rural areas. in this connection, i propose that measures be implemented to take greater account of rural areas in europe. on regional development, i call for a higher proportion of annual national ceilings to be allocated to supplementary support for rural development. in the same vein, i am opposed to any reduction in the amounts devoted to rural development. it is also important to claim that member states may decide before 1 august 2013 to apply the basic payment scheme at regional level, in which case they should define the regions according to objective and non-discriminatory criteria.

in writing. - this proposal for a regulation sought to give priority to the ecological component and to small farms and young farmers in direct payments. i hope that these will help to make the sector more attractive and competitive and will enable countries with high-quality products such as portugal to further improve their production capacity. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' in the definition of the term 'commercial vehicle'. i welcome the rapporteur's efforts to find appropriate solutions in a difficult context of budgetary contraction.
in writing. − as an essential subject of the common agricultural policy and a major priority of the current reform, direct payments to farmers should better reflect the public service provided by farmers, particularly in relation to efforts to protect the environment. the term 'greening' is now applied to agricultural policy: 30% of direct aid will be conditional on the promotion of more environmentally friendly farming. direct aid should also be distributed more fairly and targeted at active farmers, supporting activity in the most disadvantaged regions. this will allow a balance to be struck between income support and the new public challenges, integrating environmental requirements in the first pillar of the cap in the form of a strong ecological component. by linking financial support to actions beneficial to the environment and climate, the reform seeks to involve all farmers in this issue and thus provides a new justification for supporting farmers' income. in addition, the financial interests of the union will be respected.
in writing. - the outcome of the negotiations between parliament, the council and the commission, if anything new has been brought about in relation to the reform proposal previously voted, has been for the worse. there is still a scandalous disparity in the distribution of direct payments to farmers between countries, farms and producers, which is even more marked than in the previous parliament proposal. portugal will also receive an average payment per hectare significantly lower than the european average at the end of 2020. this inequality will have all the more serious effects if, unlike in the past, the instruments of regulation of production and markets which still existed in the past, in particular production quotas, and which guaranteed each country the right to produce, are dismantled. it is this right that is at stake, even more clearly, with this reform. the inclusion, which we proposed, of a significant capping and modulation of the millionaire sums that are allocated to large landowners (without even being obliged to produce) was refused. this would allow a redistribution of amounts to small farms, while at the same time minimally balancing the distribution of direct payments between producers. recognising the lack of legitimacy of the cap in the eyes of farmers and the general public, this reform sought to counter it and achieve that legitimacy. it does, however, maintain and in some cases exacerbate all the vices of the present cap.

in writing. - i approve this report by saying that i, like the whole european parliament, am in line with the other institutions of the european union and committed to allowing the cap reform to enter into force on 1 january 2014. however, it seems unlikely that all aspects of the cap reform can be implemented by 1 january 2014. transitional provisions are therefore necessary to define the technical arrangements which will allow for a smooth adaptation to the new conditions, while ensuring the continuity of the different forms of support under the cap. as regards direct payments, it is necessary to provide sufficient time for member states, paying agencies and farmers to prepare and to be informed in sufficient time and in detail of the new provisions applicable. therefore, the main elements of the existing schemes should be extended until the financial year 2014 and adjusted by the transitional provisions.

in writing. - i welcome this report by stating first that the global financial crisis and the unprecedented and prolonged economic recession have seriously affected economic growth and financial stability and have led to a sharp deterioration in financial, economic and social conditions in the member states. in particular, some member states are already facing or are at risk of facing serious difficulties, including problems of economic growth and financial stability, as well as a deterioration in the government deficit and debt situation, also reflected in the international economic and financial environment. while substantial measures have already been taken to counterbalance the negative effects of the crisis, including changes to the legal framework, the impact of the financial crisis on the real economy, the labour market and citizens is being widely felt. pressure on national financial resources is increasing and more urgent action is needed to reduce it by making the best and most efficient use of the funding provided by the structural funds and the cohesion fund.

in writing. − due to the economic and financial crisis, the commission considers that it is necessary to extend the application of the measures adopted in regulation (eu) no 1311/2011. this regulation concerns the application of an increased co-financing rate to member states which are under (let us say, rather: are victims of) so-called adjustment programmes. this increase, corresponding to 10 percentage points above the current co-financing rate applicable to each priority axis, is authorised for interim payments made under the cohesion fund and the structural funds. as was the case with the above-mentioned regulation, we approved the commission's proposal to increase cofinancing. this is a measure we considered necessary long before it was adopted, only having sinned too late. the assumptions underlying it remain valid and as such its extension is both right and necessary. this is not an act of eu solidarity. this measure does not lead to any increase in the funds available to these countries. it is only a sign of flexibility, allowing for easier mobilisation of the funds already earmarked for these countries. however, in the conditions in which these countries find themselves, with historically low levels of investment, even the co-financing rates now envisaged could be problematic.

in writing. − in the structural funds for the period 2007 to 2013, a scheme is in place where article 77 of regulation 1083/2006 gives member states, under a financial assistance programme, the possibility to have their requests for reimbursement of expenditure to the european commission paid with an increase of 10 percentage points over the current co-financing rate, which is increased from 85% to 95%. i understand that there was an eligibility gap between 31 may 2014 and the end of the current programming period, where portugal would not benefit from the 10 percentage point increase, despite continuing to be in economic recession and implementing severe austerity measures. in this respect, i voted in favour of this report, as it includes the amendment i tabled to extend the top up until the end of the programming period (december 2015) rather than ending at the end of the financial assistance period (may 2014).

in writing. − this amendment to regulation (ec) no 1083/2006 on the financial allocation of the european social fund (esf) for the period 2007-13 provides for an additional amount of around eur 150 million for the esf for three member states: france, italy and spain. these increases in national esf allocations were agreed at the june european council, not only to cope with the economic crisis, but mainly to compensate these three countries for the negative impact on them as a result of the choices made in the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. we have nothing against the increase in esf funding for these countries. on the contrary, we have argued for the need to increase this money in general. that is why we voted in favour of this amendment. but the discrimination that is done here is unacceptable. there is nothing, nothing at all, to justify the fact that the support for these countries should not also be extended to other countries in difficulty, such as portugal. once again it proves that not all states are equal in this eu. in return for the negotiations which took place behind the council's desk, additional funds were finally mobilised for three large countries, while others which needed as much or more were excluded. it should be recalled that portugal will lose, in the period 2014-2020, 10% of the funds it received in the period 2007-2013.

in writing. − the purpose of this report is to establish a new protocol to the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and kiribati, an island state in the central pacific ocean. the western and central pacific ocean region is the most important area for tuna fishing, accounting for about 55% of the total world catches of these species. the eu tuna fleet has a strong interest in fishing in this region, with purse seiners and longliners operating in this area since the late 1990s. this three-year protocol grants access to kiribati waters to 10 eu fishing vessels (four trawlers and six longliners), corresponding to an annual reference tonnage of 15 000 tonnes. the total eu financial contribution is eur 4 428 000, divided between eur 3 975 000 for access to the eez for quiribati and eur 453 000 for support to its fisheries sector policy. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this report because i consider this protocol to be fairly balanced and beneficial for both parties, allowing the continuation of the activity of the european tuna fleet, opening up prospects for the national fleet and consolidating the eu's strategic presence in this pacific region.

in writing. - i approve this report. the locations chosen for the headquarters have always been the subject of a delicate political compromise. this report, however, focuses on the seat of the european parliament, since it plays a distinct and unique role as the only institution directly elected and accountable to european citizens, and its role has, since its creation, witnessed the most significant changes of all the institutions. in the face of increased powers and responsibilities, notably with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which placed the european parliament on a par with the council in its role as co-legislator, the council has significantly changed its way of functioning and its working methods. i therefore believe that in order to fulfil the tasks assigned to it by the treaties and to meet the expectations of its electorate, parliament must have the right to organise itself in a modern and appropriate way and, to that end, it must initiate a procedure to amend article 341 and protocol no 6.

in writing. − in the new times of demand for more efficient responses and cost-effectiveness of resources, it is also pertinent to analyse the cost-benefit ratio with regard to the geographical dispersion of the headquarters and workplaces of the institutions of the european union, with particular emphasis on the european parliament. according to the european parliament's 2014 budget estimates, expenditure directly related to the dispersal of three workplaces (strasbourg, brussels and luxembourg) is between eur 169 million and eur 204 million per year. in 2011, the time spent on monthly travel to plenary sessions is estimated at 69 562 days for officials and other servants (an expenditure of eur 16 652 490) and 31 316 days for accredited parliamentary assistants (equivalent to eur 5 944 724). taking into account that the definition of the seat of the institutions and their places of work is a matter for the member states alone and is regulated by the treaties, i support the initiative to promote studies and analyses on this geographical dispersion, while not ignoring the financial and economic implications that may result from a change in this matter.
in writing. - this report again addresses the controversial question of the location of the european parliament's seat. the functioning of parliament in brussels and strasbourg and the monthly migration that goes with it have undoubtedly become the subject of increasing critical attention. the general public has come to believe that these regular trips, because of the costs involved, are excessive and unjustified. the rapporteur's report reiterates the view that parliament should be given the prerogative to determine its own working hours and place of work. at present, this is prevented by the treaty, which clearly states that the european parliament is to be seated in strasbourg, where the 12 monthly plenary sessions, including the budget session, are held. the additional plenary sessions shall be held in brussels. the committees of the european parliament meet in brussels. the general secretariat of the european parliament and its departments remain in luxembourg. this is the provision which is now being amended by a revision of the treaty to allow parliament to decide on the location of its seat and its internal organisation. although we do not fully follow the set of arguments which are often put forward on this issue, it seems clear to us that changes in this area are necessary to reduce unnecessary and unjustified expenditure.
in writing. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of life in the european union, including the establishment of a european centre for the development of vocational training. the maintenance of two workplaces, with the obligation to hold 12 plenary sessions in strasbourg, undermines the rational and effective organisation of the ep's work and has a negative impact on the image of the ep and its members in the eyes of its electorate. as the data in this report show, in addition to the budgetary and environmental costs of the current situation, the profound changes in the ep's powers, in particular the increase in the number of procedures in which it is co-legislator, alongside the council, and which has resulted in a 150% increase in interinstitutional meetings, make it advisable for the ep to work from a single workplace at the headquarters of the other institutions of the union's government. it is not just a question of the cost of the two seats, much less the convenience of members, but above all a question of the efficiency of the functioning of the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report in which the european parliament defends its right to decide where and when to hold its meetings. the european parliament, the only parliament which has no power to decide on its own seat, calls for the initiation of a process of revision of the treaties with a view to proposing the necessary amendments to enable it to decide on the location of its seat, which is currently fixed by the member states by unanimity. several studies make it undeniable that the parliament would be more cost-effective if it were located in a single place.
in writing. − according to article 341 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the seat of the institutions of the european union is to be determined by common accord of the governments of the member states. protocol no 6 annexed to the treaties provides that the european parliament shall have its seat in strasbourg, where the 12 monthly plenary sessions are held, that meetings of parliamentary committees shall be held in brussels and that the general secretariat shall be located in luxembourg. i am voting in favour of this report which aims to review the treaties and ensure that the european parliament can choose its official seat. i have long advocated that the official seat should be in brussels, because of the location of most of the european institutions, the ease of establishing official contacts, scheduling meetings with ngos or other representatives of civil society. i would remind you that the additional costs of the geographical dispersion of parliament have been estimated at between eur 169 and 204 million, or about 10% of the ep's annual budget. i would also point out that the current system also incurs unnecessary additional environmental, organisational and logistical costs, with estimates of between 11 000 and 19 000 tonnes of additional co2 emissions alone.
in writing. - the functioning of the parliament in brussels and strasbourg and the monthly migration that goes with it has undoubtedly become the subject of increasing critical attention. the general public has come to believe that these regular trips, because of the costs involved, are excessive and unjustified. the rapporteur's report reiterates the view that parliament should be given the prerogative to determine its own working hours and place of work. at the moment, this is prevented by the treaty, which clearly states that the european parliament is to be seated in strasbourg, where the 12 monthly plenary sessions, including the budget session, are held. the additional plenary sessions shall be held in brussels. the committees of the european parliament meet in brussels. the general secretariat of the european parliament and its departments remain in luxembourg. this is the provision which is now being amended by a revision of the treaty to allow parliament to decide on the location of its seat and its internal organisation. it seems pertinent to us.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to begin by thanking everyone for their commitment to horizon 2020. i would like to thank the european commission and the commissioners and their services for their continued availability to discuss and further develop the ideas that parliament has been suggesting over the last two years. i would also like to thank all the other rapporteurs, shadow rapporteurs, other members, advisers to the political groups and the itre committee secretariat for their commitment and cooperation. finally, a word of deep thanks to the various presidencies, with special reference to the irish presidency which has shown great flexibility and openness in the negotiating process. i think that the final agreement we reached was very positive and that parliament's role was important in this process. the only point on which i was disappointed, as were many colleagues, was the budget for horizon 2020, which, although increased by 35% compared to the current framework programme, which corresponds to eur 79.4 billion, fell short of the eur 100 billion advocated by parliament. i would like to highlight what i consider to be the main contributions of the european parliament. parliament has created a new pillar dedicated to widening participation, in which mechanisms have been introduced to allow a better geographical distribution of the allocation of funds without compromising the principle of excellence of projects and participants. parliament also introduced important measures to promote the employment of qualified young people. the largest part of the horizon 2020 budget is dedicated to the recruitment of researchers, technicians, engineers and entrepreneurs. i would point out, for example, that for every billion euros in horizon 2020, 2 500 marie curie fellowships or 4 000 innovative smes can be funded. as regards the participation of smes, parliament also managed to secure a budget of eur 8.6 billion for smes, of which eur 3 million is dedicated to the instrument called the sme instrument. finally, several scientific and technological areas are strengthened by this agreement. i would like to stress, as a matter of urgency, clean energy with renewable sources, energy efficiency and the introduction of a new horizontal area entirely devoted to maritime issues. i strongly believe that horizon 2020, being the largest research and innovation funding programme in the world and covering the entire innovation cycle, will make a difference in increasing the competitiveness of european industry, in overcoming the crisis we are going through and in reducing unemployment, especially unemployment among young people with qualifications. thank you very much.
the rapporteur. - i would also like to begin by thanking all the colleagues who have been involved in this process. we have been discussing research policy for several years now and the last two years have certainly been very intense. but i would also like to thank, in a very particular way, the staff of the itre commission secretariat, all the assistants and advisers who were involved, because they have done a lot of work and without them it would not be possible for us to be here today discussing so many legislative packages relating to research with the results we have obtained. as regards the strategic innovation agenda, it focuses mainly on the european institute of innovation and technology and this is the heart of what we have tried to do, i in conjunction with my colleague philippe lamberts, who was responsible for the report on the regulation of the european institute of innovation and technology itself. the eit, as i shall call it, is a key instrument for completing the knowledge triangle and is the only one which actually completes it, involving universities, research centres and the private sector. it is also an absolutely fundamental instrument for strengthening the capacity of innovation in europe and the eit has been organising itself in recent years around what have become known as the innovation and knowledge communities. i think the overall assessment of this house is that this is a project that has gone well. however, it was a project that was underfunded and a project that was still very unknown to the general public and even to the general public working in science and technology. and so with this report, with this proposal together with mr lambert's proposal, we are seeking to strengthen the role of the eit. we need the eit to become a true european-wide institute of innovation and technology and not an unknown or almost unknown entity, as it was until now, but we need this institute to be truly an institute and not just the sum of the innovation and knowledge communities. i would also like to mention another point which has to do with what the proposals for new priorities for action are, new areas for developing the european union's innovation capacity. we know that innovation does not exist in the abstract, it depends on the definition of political priorities. this was probably one of the most intense debates we have had in the development of this process, but we ended up with a redefinition of priorities that puts health and active ageing first and raw materials second, which are scarce as we know, particularly with regard to sustainable exploitation of raw materials, recycling and replacement. there will be two other openings for the creation of new innovation and knowledge communities, but these were the ones that were defined as the first two priorities in the agreement we reached. the third point i would like to make is that we have made efforts to avoid the concentration of resources for both research and innovation in the european area. innovation can never benefit the european union as a whole if it remains concentrated in only two or three countries, and that is why we have made an effort to re-establish decentralization, geographical distribution as one of the fundamental criteria. and so we have added a new instrument, the regional innovation scheme, which allows certain regions that are not included in the innovation and knowledge communities to take advantage of the installed capacity they have for the development of innovation and which can favour regions in the direction of greater job creation, greater inclusion, and this is one of the points that changes the commission's original proposal the most, but on which we have all agreed and which i think is a very interesting point to develop. finally, a note on the budget: the eit was funded with 300 million euros, we were able to increase that funding to 3 billion euros. i think that this is a good investment, that it is a significant increase and that we should know how to make good use of it because investment in science is surely one of the most important in the context in which we live today.
for the gue/ngl group well, an agreement is an agreement and there have been interventions here which show well how this agreement can be supported for reasons so different from each other. but we made a deal. that is the part, i think, that is most important to stress. however, i would like to take this opportunity to say what i see as the good parts of this agreement, and they are, of course, that we have managed to rescue the social sciences and the humanities, which had been relegated to the background in the initial perspective presented by the european commission. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. it also involves increasing support for smes, whereas initially this proposal was so geared towards large industry. i think we cannot ignore the fact that it is the largest percentage of the european industrial fabric and that it provides access to the largest number of jobs in the european context, especially at a time of crisis such as this. it also makes it easier to cooperate in research with regions such as africa, latin america and others. it also goes through the possibility of us accessing open access in terms of publications, scientific research results, of going that way, because it's public money we're talking about. it is also the fact that we can increase investment in fundamental research, in basic research, by increasing the budget for the european research council. that said, there are some things i don't like very much: i don't like public-private partnerships very much, i don't like the money that's being spent on research and security very much, but from all of the things that have been mentioned i would like to say, precisely because it's an agreement, that it's a good thing that stem cell research got in. it would not be a step backwards from what we have been doing and so it is. in deals, there are parts that we like more, parts that we like less. i would just like to see more investment in the areas which are most decisive for job creation and for getting out of the crisis, because we talk about this, but in the end the targets fall short of what we say in the initial declarations.
mr president, commissioner, horizon 2020 is the most important instrument for the union's science and innovation policy. and it aims at many things, among them responding to the scientific community, to the complaints of the scientific community, promoting the simplification of administrative rules, contributing to scientific excellence and collaboration, bringing science closer to the commercialization of results and also facilitating technological innovation and the competitiveness of companies. it is the main budgetary instrument of the union for achieving a knowledge-based economy and therefore i cannot help but express disappointment at the financial allocation of the programme which has just fallen far, far short of what was expected. i regret the concentration on very large-scale initiatives which make it difficult for new entrants and smaller entities to gain access. this concentration does not guarantee excellence, nor the desired convergence between member states in terms of innovation. it has only the nearest practical application of knowledge in its favour. the european innovation ecosystem needs to be more effective and serve a dynamic and sustainable economy.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioners, tomorrow we will be voting on horizon 2020. it is an important programme for europe but it is crucial for countries like portugal, whose investment in science and innovation is highly dependent on european funding, especially in times of crisis like the present one. horizon 2020 will bring many opportunities to countries in portugal's situation, because it is a programme with simple rules and a very suitable and favourable funding model; because it covers the areas of greatest expression for europe and for countries like portugal (health and energy, transport, sea, environment, social sciences and humanities); because it introduces modes of participation designed for institutions with little experience in international projects, although they are excellent, such as twinning, return grants, era chairs, innovation vouchers; because it has a second programme for smes worth €8.6 billion. the conditions are therefore in place for countries such as portugal to increase their participation in horizon 2020, leading to: first, an increase in the employment of qualified young people, countering the brain drain phenomenon we have seen in recent years; second, an increase in internationalisation and consequently an increase in the competitiveness of smes; third, the improvement of the living conditions of all europeans and all those living in europe who will benefit from the results of scientific research in such important areas as health or the environment. thank you very much.
the rapporteur. - the debate was quite interesting and intense, and there were two issues which were probably the most controversial. i should like to take this opportunity to make a few comments on these two issues. i am referring, of course, to the question of israel's participation and the question of embryonic stem cells. on the question of israel, if we respect international law and the right to life, we must ensure that the european commission's communication of july this year on the non-financing of israeli entities involved in the occupation of the palestinian territories is complied with. it is a matter of international law and respect for human life. the agreement provides for research on embryonic stem cells to be carried out in accordance with ethical principles and in compliance with national, european and international legislation. here too, and again, it is a matter of complying with international law. either one is a perfectly reasonable point. i'm glad you're on the same page. this agreement cannot be held hostage to dogmatism, fundamentalism, nor can it be left on the sidelines and in defiance of international law and respect for human life. that said, i would like to end by saying only that the european union remains a very unequal space, with very different capacities of the different member states, in the different institutions, to be able to access research resources. the european union is even more unequal as a result of the crisis and in many countries the only, if not almost exclusive, recourse to european funds is to be able to finance research. and that is why i hope that horizon 2020 will prove to be an instrument for a more cohesive european union, because that is the only way we can be better, when we are more equal. thank you very much.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group, the question of financing micro, small and mediumsized enterprises is now a matter of life and death in this sector which is so important for the economies of countries. the policies of competitiveness in the framework of the single market, the religious panacea of the european union, have already, over time, left behind thousands of small businesses, especially in countries with weaker economies and difficult competitiveness. but today, the situation is worse. in countries like my own, portugal, dozens of small and mediumsized enterprises are closed down every day. they're families and workers who see their lives destroyed overnight. the lack of financing by the banks is certainly one of the causes of this misfortune. we therefore consider it important to create credit lines, although we know that the intermediaries will make a profit at the expense of this problem. but today, when we visit traders, small manufacturers, food and agricultural producers, associations of small businessmen, the reasons they find for their risk of bankruptcy are different: the decline in purchasing power, in domestic consumption, in the internal market of their countries. it is true that the cuts in pensions and wages, the redundancies, so cheerfully promoted by the european union, particularly in the implementation of its pacts of aggression with national governments through the troika, are leading to the daily ruin of thousands of small and mediumsized enterprises throughout the european union. and why would young people want to risk investing and going into debt when the economic picture in their country is devastating and is predicted to get even worse?
smes have been experiencing great difficulties in accessing credit, especially in the countries most affected by the economic crisis, which is affecting their competitiveness, hindering their dynamism and growth. and they're so important that five-sixths of new job growth in the united states is associated with smes. we agree with the main lines of action introduced by this regulation, in particular the financial instruments which facilitate access to debt and risk capital mechanisms, as well as support for internationalisation, administrative and regulatory simplification and support for sectors such as small tourism operators, which is so important and promising today. unfortunately, the cosme programme is only a seed, it has a very insufficient amount, so it requires an intelligent application to be able to be multiplier. thank you, sir.

member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, good morning. this is an early start on life! first and foremost, let me thank and congratulate the rapporteur, ms haug, and the shadow rapporteurs, for their constructive work on the commission’s proposal for the establishment of the life programme for the environment and climate action. the final result is good news for the environment and good news for the fight against climate change. almost eur 3.5 billion will be available between 2014 and 2020 to support projects and initiatives targeting environmental and climate-related challenges. this represents a 43% increase compared with the 2007-2013 period and is an important step towards enhancing the impact of this particular financial instrument, even if the means are small in relation to the challenges we face. the european parliament’s work over many years has contributed to making a real success of the life programme. life has helped people take action to protect nature where they live and where they work; it has helped policymakers improve the quality of their work and it has helped businesses to innovate and create jobs. when we talk here today about the regulation, the trialogues and the budget for the programme, it all may seem rather theoretical and bureaucratic but many of you have seen the real results, and the benefits on the ground, of life projects in your regions – doing very necessary work. the outcome of the negotiations on the new programme will take these benefits a step further. traditional projects, due to their success and the fact that they achieve important results with relatively little money, will remain at the core of the proposal. the commission welcomes in particular the strengthening of integrated projects. this will help reinforce a more strategic approach to implementing environment and climate-related policies and will mobilise other eu funds for environmental and climate objectives. the provisions on capacity building and on dissemination and exchanges of best practice will help people develop quality projects and will spread the benefits of action on the environment across the whole union. this has helped increase confidence among member states that excellent projects can be developed and that the practice of fixing national allocations can be phased out. finally, the commission welcomes the possibility of using financial instruments to support climate and environmental projects. by combining public and private sources of funding, these instruments will attract more investment to combat climate change and protect natural capital. they will add value to traditional projects by leveraging additional funds and increasing the overall impact of the programme. while the commission fully supports the outcome as far as the substance is concerned, some of the changes introduced to our proposal require us to make two statements: first, on the use of the no-opinion clause for the adoption of implementing acts in connection with the maximum funding that a single integrated project may receive; and, second, on the status of funding of biodiversity in overseas countries and territories. the commission will pass the full text of these statements to the plenary service for recording in the minutes. they will be published in the official journal together with the regulation.
maximum amount that a single ip may receive the commission attaches high importance to ensuring a proportionate distribution of funds among integrated projects in order to fund as many integrated projects as possible and guarantee a balanced distribution of integrated projects among all member states. in this context, the commission will propose when discussing the draft work programme with the members of the life committee the maximum amount that a single integrated project may receive. this proposal will be submitted as part of the methodology for project selection to be adopted as part of the multiannual work programme. status of funding biodiversity in octs the commission attaches high importance to the protection of environment and biodiversity in overseas countries and territories, as is illustrated by the overseas association decision proposal which includes these sectors in the areas of cooperation between the european union and octs and outlines the different actions which could be eligible for funding by the european union in this regard. the best preparatory action has been a successful initiative that has been embraced by octs and has delivered tangible results for biodiversity and ecosystem services. as best is drawing to a close, the commission is favourably considering following up on it under one of the new instruments, namely global public goods and challenges programme under the development cooperation instrument. this specific possibility for funding biodiversity in octs will be complemented by the opportunities offered under article 6 of the life programme for the period 2014-2020.
on behalf of the s&d group. i would like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur, mrs haug, on her excellent work. the life programme has been supporting projects of the highest relevance. we welcome an improvement in the budgetary allocation but consider it to be below requirements. the agreement reached ensures funding for projects in the priority area nature-biodiversity, which can stop irreversible losses to the environment but also to society and economies, as the cost of biodiversity loss could reach 7% of gdp by 2050. as there are disparities between member states in the use of available funds, we welcome the capacity building in the regions with the lowest use of funds, as well as the increase in co-financing rates in the economically less developed regions. the budgetary difficulties of some member states cannot be translated into a reduction in investment in the environment and climate areas because this would have catastrophic results. the financing of integrated projects makes it possible to integrate environmental and climate issues into all european union policies and the implementation of environmental legislation, job creation and growth, which we also consider to be positive.
the life programme is the only european union programme devoted exclusively to the environment. over the years, both the concrete results achieved and the capacity it has shown to stimulate and involve various organisations and local actors have proved the importance of this instrument, which would justify an increase in its appropriations. we are in favour of at least 1% of the european union budget being allocated to this programme. unfortunately, we are a long way from that goal. the relative success of life does not, however, remove the need to address some of the problems that have been evident in recent years. this new regulation does so only in part. the levels of life implementation by country are very different, the co-financing requirements and the lack of support for the preparation of proposals have led to many projects being stranded. in many countries, the annual number of projects selected has often fallen short of their national indicative allocation, a difficulty which has become more acute in recent years. the new concept of integrated projects poses challenges and requirements which cannot be ignored. finally, we have always maintained that new objectives must be matched by new and strengthened means. it is important that new climate objectives are not pursued at the expense of the weakening of nature conservation and biodiversity, this was and should continue to be, in our view, the core of the life programme.
in writing. − i approve this report, considering that the proposal for a regulation on horizon 2020 is a solid basis, which takes account of the european union's needs in the scientific and research fields, while ensuring a certain degree of synergy with cohesion policy. there is, however, room for amendment, particularly in activities aimed at strengthening the development and participation of regions, cities and local authorities, which is not sufficiently covered in the proposal, although the commission has urged member states to include these activities in their operational research programmes in the next programming period. i believe that horizon 2020 should also take greater account of the geographical diversity of the european union and support research initiatives in all member states, which would reinforce the regional dimension of science and research policy. in this context, the territorial and transnational dimension should be strengthened.
in writing. − horizon 2020 is the name of the european framework programme for research and innovation which will run for the period 2014-2020 and which is a core section of the europe 2020 strategy. the programme aims to strengthen the link between research and innovation by converting scientific breakthroughs into innovative products, thus responding to the challenges posed by globalisation (e.g. climate change, energy security and ageing population). horizon 2020 will meet the needs of businesses, universities and institutes in terms of fast and simplified access to finance. i believe that this programme is a practical solution to the crisis in europe.
in writing. − the commission's proposal for horizon 2020 brings together for the first time under a single common strategic framework for research and innovation funding different elements which have so far lacked a common perspective: the successors to the seventh framework programme and the competitiveness and innovation framework programme, together with the european innovation institute. with the aim of revitalising the european economy, the europe 2020 strategy focuses on research and innovation to enable the eu to become a knowledge-based economy, which will allow for more balanced, diversified and sustainable growth.
in writing. − the proposed regulation for the framework programme for research and innovation 2014-2020, called horizon 2020, sets the framework for support for research and innovation activities in this period. it advocates better exploitation of the economic and industrial potential of innovation, research and technological development policies. we are faced with a programme which, broadly speaking, clearly subjugates science and r & d to the market. the intention to direct funding towards research and innovation that can be brought to the market is clear. public-private partnerships are the tool of choice for putting public money to private ends. the emphasis is on channelling resources predominantly to so-called research excellence, and this approach will continue to exclude many research institutions and structures which, by not meeting the requirements for excellence, will be excluded from funding. the innovations introduced in the regulation, such as the new concept of the path to excellence, do not substantially alter this framework, which is overall detrimental to the interests of countries such as portugal and its institutions. portugal is now a net contributor to the framework programme, that is, it puts more money into it than it takes out. we do not believe that this regulation adopts the necessary solutions to help reverse this situation.
in writing. − this document is part of the legislative package for the horizon 2020 programme, which will run from 2014 to 2020 and which, for the first time, brings together all funding for research and innovation. horizon 2020 has three dimensions: scientific excellence, industrial leadership and societal challenges, and synergies with cohesion policy should be created across the various programmes and their funding. i voted in favour of this document, which i consider essential for the future competitiveness of the union in the next multiannual period.
in writing. − the regulation that this report creates, called horizon 2020, the framework programme for research and innovation 2014-2020, sets the framework for support for research activities and for exploiting the economic and industrial potential of innovation, research and technological development policies. this central objective is clearly negative because it subordinates science to the interests of the market. the commission is also proposing to increase funding for research and innovation of excellence, a new concept which will exclude many research institutions and structures which, by not meeting the requirements of such excellence, will be excluded from the pool of applicants for funding. public-private partnerships are the tool of choice in this regulation for public money to serve private ends, even more so in an area whose suitability is important to ensure research for research's sake and not to serve private interests.
in writing. − i welcome this report, bearing in mind that horizon 2020 is intended to bring about a major shift towards greater innovation in europe and, in my view, a budgetary increase of only 6.19% is unlikely to bring sustainable results. i therefore emphasize once again parliament's request for 100 billion for this programme. i am concerned that the setting of reimbursement rates would be too high, which could considerably limit the number of projects that can be funded under horizon 2020, thereby reducing the overall impact of the programme and possibly undermining the implementation of the innovation union flagship initiative and the europe 2020 strategy. this issue could become even more important as the outcome of the negotiations on the next multiannual financial framework could leave horizon 2020 with an even smaller financial framework than the one currently proposed. from an economic point of view, the financing of activities close to the market must follow a more clearly defined concept. finally, i would stress that union funding for research and innovation must seek to provide a substantial leverage effect in terms of private investment.
in writing. − horizon 2020 is the name of the european framework programme for research and innovation which will run for the period 2014-2020 and which is a core section of the europe 2020 strategy. this regulation introduces measures which simplify the participation of beneficiaries considerably, which will, on the one hand, streamline administrative procedures and, on the other hand, allow for a wider participation of smaller entities and groups with lighter administrative structures.
in writing. − the regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down the rules for participation and dissemination in horizon 2020 is part of the package of proposals establishing the eu's research and innovation programme for 2014-2020. it lays down rules according to the different types of funding that may be granted to certain entities for research and related support activities and according to the possibilities for dissemination and exploitation of the results of such research. the proposals to simplify the rules and to increase the participation of smes and the flexible methods of financing are welcome.
in writing. - the main problem with the programme is that the objectives and criteria for funding are oriented towards economic, market and industrial interests, to the detriment of scientific research and development that responds to social needs and advances knowledge and understanding of the world around us and its phenomena. the emphasis on research by placing barriers to excellence in access to project funding does not contribute to the objective of balanced scientific development in all member states. the involvement of economic and industrial interests in research and the preferential channelling of funds towards public-private and other private partnerships are priorities which do not deserve our support. the report advocates reducing the complexity of existing financing rules, which would not be a bad thing in the first place. however, this also means that, as large private companies have access to funds in the same way as public and non-profit entities (secondary and higher education establishments, research organisations and even smes), and their investment in research is much more substantial, their absorption capacity of eu public funding is much higher than that of public entities, many of which will not even see any funding to develop their research. we voted against it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european union's research and innovation framework programme for the next seven years. horizon 2020 has a budget of eur 70,2 billion (2011 prices) and facilitates the participation of young researchers and small and medium-sized enterprises. the programme covers all scientific areas such as health, information and communication technologies and energy. in the chapter on participation rules, i would highlight as positive the following aspects: a wider acceptance of the usual accounting practices of beneficiaries, a single set of rules for the financing of all actions undertaken by participants under h2020, reduced requirements for time recording systems and the inclusion of vat in the definition of eligible costs.
in writing. − this document is part of the legislative package for the horizon 2020 programme, which will run from 2014 to 2020 and which, for the first time, brings together all funding for research and innovation. this proposal provides for a wider acceptance of the usual accounting practices of beneficiaries, a single set of rules for the financing of all actions undertaken by participants under horizon 2020, as well as reduced requirements for time-registration systems and the inclusion of vat in the definition of eligible costs. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. − the regulation lays down specific rules for participation and dissemination in indirect actions carried out under the regulation establishing the horizon 2020 programme. the main problem with the programme is its objectives and funding criteria, which are oriented towards economic, market and industry interests, to the detriment of scientific research and development for the advancement of science by science, in support of public policies for the development of society, rather than its concentration on entities that convey private objectives. we believe that promoting research by placing barriers to excellence in access to project funding not only does not contribute to the public service objective necessary for the creative and innovative fruition of science, but also nullifies the positive results that science and research bring to our society. we voted against it.
in writing. - i approve this report, starting by stating that the eit is not a programme, nor a network, but an institute. it certainly operates within a programme and creates technology and innovation networks with many different partners, but it is an institute with an important role to play, which is not the role of a mere administrator, coordinator or facilitator of its kics. as an institute, it should be approached in a very specific way, different from other sections of horizon 2020. as not only a direct innovation instrument but also an educational one, the eit introduces a genuine education dimension into the european union's research and innovation policy. in this respect, i believe that the eit can strengthen its role in this area. to achieve this goal, several things are necessary. an ambitious agenda for the above activities will certainly help to solve the problem. effective communication is also needed. i believe, however, that a major breakthrough with regard to the future premises of the institute will be a key element in this strategic plan.
in writing. − the european institute of innovation and technology is a key initiative to deliver europe 2020 strategy promoting the interaction between research, education and innovation. its development, with an adequate budget, will contribute to a modernised higher education system and to a more entrepreneurial environment, resulting in innovative products and services in the market. i should like to underline the importance of the creation of regional clusters connected to the knowledge and innovation communities for the success of this project.
in writing. − the capacity for innovation is part of the dna of western civilization, which has always sought not only to overcome the barriers of theoretical and practical knowledge but to give it useful application to the lives of its populations. this path has benefited greatly from the central role of universities as centres of knowledge production and transmission. i hope that the european institute of innovation and technology can draw on the personalist and universalist tradition of european universities and aim for research activity that increasingly knows no borders, prioritises work and innovation, and aims at excellence in processes and outcomes. the eit can play a decisive role in the future of european innovation and technology. i hope so.
in writing. − this strategic innovation agenda (sip) sets out the priorities and functioning of the european institute of innovation and technology (eit) for the period 2014-2020. the eip takes into account the experience gained at the eit to date and aims to reflect the reality of the european innovation situation. the rapporteur expresses concerns and makes recommendations which we can call sensible. all current or potential stakeholders in the eit's activities, including businesses, higher education institutions and research organisations, as well as national and regional authorities, are referred to for consultation. but we do not separate this report from the broader context of horizon 2020, on which we have expressed a number of concerns, in particular with regard to the commercialisation of knowledge and research, as well as the establishment of public-private partnerships and the channelling of european research funds to projects considered to be of excellence, with all the barriers to funding that this concept represents for research institutions below this level. moreover, our abstention is consistent with the position we took when the eit was set up.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european union's research and innovation framework programme for the next seven years. horizon 2020 has a budget of eur 70,2 billion (2011 prices) and facilitates the participation of young researchers and small and medium-sized enterprises. the programme covers all scientific areas such as health, information and communication technologies and energy. the strategic innovation programme of the european institute of innovation and technology (eit) is a key instrument and addresses the knowledge triangle, involving universities, research centres and the private sector. it is also a key instrument for strengthening the capacity for innovation in europe. innovation can only benefit the eu as a whole if it is decentralised, which is what this document attempts to do, placing geographical distribution as one of the key criteria. a new instrument, the regional innovation scheme, has also been created, which allows certain regions not included in the innovation and knowledge communities to take advantage of their existing capacity to develop innovation and which can help regions to create more jobs.
in writing. − this document is part of the legislative package for the horizon 2020 programme, which will run from 2014 to 2020 and which, for the first time, brings together all funding for research and innovation. the european institute of innovation and technology (eit) is a major innovation partner in europe, but also one of the main centres for research and scientific and technological exchange, for the dissemination of good practice and for a culture of knowledge sharing. the eit may enhance its role by hosting and organising major conferences, seminars, technology exhibitions and specific training actions, degree course modules or packages for school education, summer courses, the eit fellowship programme, in addition to the existing eit-labelled master and phd programmes, which should be further developed. for the reasons given, i voted in favour of the document.

in writing. − i welcome this report, given that to recover from the multiple crises it is facing, europe must find ways to develop its capacity for innovation, to provide sustainable and efficient solutions to societal challenges, such as those identified in the horizon 2020 initiative, but also to employment and value creation. the institute represents the european union's first attempt to integrate the three sides of the knowledge triangle (higher education, research and innovation). through the activities of the knowledge and innovation communities (kics), the institute promotes closer interaction between universities, research centres and businesses, with the aim of bridging the gap between research, education and entrepreneurial activities, with a view to improving the eu's innovation capacity. to date, the institute appears to be a successful and promising instrument for conducting innovation-oriented activities in a comprehensive and simple way, involving partners from the private and public sectors and universities in a dynamic innovation process. therefore, i support the gradual increase of the budget from 2014 to 2020 as proposed by the commission and the launch of new kics.

in writing. − the european institute of innovation and technology, which was born of the lisbon strategy and unfortunately did not achieve the desired results, is nevertheless an important bet for the future of the union. its activity deserves not only to continue but to become increasingly established in the global research and technology landscape, involving the three components of the strategic triangle that must cooperate in order to enhance its activity: teaching, research and innovation. i wish the eit a great future, in line with european ambitions in this sector.
in writing. − the eu2020 strategy, with the weight of objectives and measures that have led to flexible labour relations, increasing and facilitating redundancies, among other policy failures on which its agenda has focused energies, gives a prominent role to the european institute of innovation and technology as a positive contribution to its flagship theme: smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. the regulation, to which this report proposes some amendments, creates the european institute of innovation and technology, which is naturally part of the achievement of the objectives of the horizon 2020 framework programme by integrating the knowledge triangle of higher education, research and innovation. we have many criticisms of the programme in question, given the links it establishes between the financing of research development structures and economic and industrial interests, with the clear preferential channelling of funds to the private sector to the detriment of public research. our position on the creation of the european institute of technology, when the regulation was adopted in 2008, was very critical, following the position taken by several research organisations. with these intentions and on the basis of these principles, we cannot adopt such a regulation.
