in writing. − i approve this report, considering that the overall competitiveness of european smes is hampered by institutional, market and policy gaps, such as lack of access to finance, markets and regulatory burden. as a result, european smes have weaker productivity and slower growth than their counterparts in other parts of the world, and have more difficulty successfully adapting to change than larger companies in europe. these difficulties were further aggravated by the economic crisis of 2008, which disproportionately affected smes. i warmly welcome the proposal for the cosme programme, which is the only european union spending programme specifically aimed at stimulating smes. however, given its limited budget, cosme should focus on actions that have the greatest impact and leverage. so i suggest that you focus on three areas: reducing the administrative burden, access to finance and access to markets.
in writing. - the european business fabric is 99% smes, 90% of which are micro-enterprises. these figures show the importance of these companies to the european economy. the cosme programme is crucial for these companies, particularly in their access to finance and to markets. cosme, which is aimed at all smes and has a budget of €2.5 billion, should focus on actions that have the greatest impact and leverage. i would stress the importance of the actions aimed at improving the framework conditions for sustainable competitiveness, the actions aimed at promoting entrepreneurship, the actions aimed at improving access to finance for smes and, finally, the actions aimed at improving access to markets.
in writing. − supporting smes and stimulating competitiveness and entrepreneurship is essential for an effective exit strategy and economic recovery of eu countries. smes are to a large extent the backbone of our economy and without them the eu cannot hope to have a realistic and effective policy for growth, jobs and innovation.
in writing. − the existence of sufficient financing for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (msmes) is more than ever a matter of survival for this sector, which represents a large part of the economy of our country as well as of other european countries. many smes are closing down every day. competition policies within the single market, such as those proclaimed by the eu2020 strategy and part of the objectives of the cosme programme, are the same ones that lead companies to close their doors every day. the rhetoric of strengthening competitiveness, sustainability, youth entrepreneurship, market access is an illusion. very few micro, small and mediumsized enterprises will find in the guidelines of this report the lifeline they need. the cuts in pensions and wages, the redundancies, promoted by the eu, are dictating the daily ruin of thousands of smes across the eu. this is a report full of good intentions, on the one hand with scarce resources and faulty distribution, and on the other hand with proposals, such as the development of entrepreneurship, which are dangerous for our youth and which do not take into account the role of the state, given the crisis that we are experiencing today in portugal and in europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european union's research and innovation framework programme for the next seven years. horizon 2020 has a budget of eur 70,2 billion (2011 prices) and facilitates the participation of young researchers and small and medium-sized enterprises. the programme covers all scientific areas such as health, information and communication technologies and energy. the overall competitiveness of european small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) is hampered by institutional, market and policy gaps, such as lack of access to finance, markets and regulatory burden. under the future mff (2014-2020), the eeas will be replaced by the programme for the competitiveness of enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises (cosme). following its decision to bring research and innovation closer together, the european commission (ec) has proposed to bring innovation-related activities of the current esi funds under horizon 2020, the new framework programme for research and innovation. cosme will therefore focus on competitiveness, growth and entrepreneurship. cosme will be the only eu spending programme specifically aimed at stimulating smes.
in writing. − the programme for the competitiveness of enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises (cosme) is a support programme for small and medium-sized enterprises which, together with horizon 2020, replaces the current framework programme for innovation and competitiveness. unlike horizon 2020, which is based on business creation, cosme is growth-focused, providing €2.3 billion (in current prices) for businesses and entrepreneurs from 2014 to 2020. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. - the question of whether there is sufficient funding for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises is more than ever a question of survival for this sector, which represents a large part of the economy of our country, where reality shows us that dozens of smes are closing down every day. the competitiveness policies within the framework of a single market, such as those proclaimed by the eu 2020 strategy and which are part of the objectives of the cosme programme, are the same ones that lead companies to close their doors every day. the cuts in pensions and wages, the redundancies, so cheerfully promoted by the eu, particularly in the implementation of its pacts of aggression with national governments through the troika, are leading to the daily ruin of thousands of smes throughout the eu. this is a report full of good intentions, but it is accommodated by scarce resources and advocates proposals such as the development of the illusion of entrepreneurship as a miracle solution, which are dangerous for our youth, given the crisis that we are experiencing in portugal and in europe today.
in writing. − i welcome this report, considering that the next horizon 2020 programme will reinforce europe's leading position in a field where europe has lost ground in multiple areas. achieving this goal requires that europe's strengths be precisely identified, but it also implies that europe's weaknesses be recognised and corrected. as for its strengths, europe has world-leading researchers, entrepreneurs and companies, a set of deeply rooted values and traditions, a vibrant culture of creativity and diversity and the largest internal market in the world. finally, european business and civil society are actively engaged in emerging and developing economies around the world. however, at the same time, europe has a number of shortcomings: under-investment in our knowledge bases, unsatisfactory structural conditions and, finally, too much fragmentation, together with too much bureaucracy and the weight of the administrative machinery. as such, the proposal represents a real step forward: it strikes the right balance between the three pillars scientific excellence, industrial leadership and society challenges.

in writing. − i share the view that the european research area should be geared towards scientific excellence, industrial leadership and societal challenges, and should have the committed participation of its key actors. these three components will not only help to reinforce each other but will also make the progress made in this area more solid and sustainable. i believe that the union's return to progress and development will depend on the emphasis given to research and innovation and the way in which their strategic importance is effectively recognised, an importance which must be realised in a real and productive way. i congratulate the rapporteur on her excellent work and i hope that research and innovation will be one of the main engines of the european union in the future.
in writing. − scientific excellence, industrial leadership and societal challenges are the three priorities that guide horizon 2020. behind these rhetoric lies a practice that channels the bulk of available r & d resources to institutions, public-private partnerships and companies, all of which are said to be of excellence, in some large countries. a practice which has made countries such as portugal, in recent years, a net contributor to the research framework programme. this report acknowledges this reality in part, but it is unlikely that the measures it proposes will change substantially as required. funding will be channelled to those projects which meet the criteria reflected in the programme's objectives, i.e. those projects which aim to exploit better the economic and industrial potential of innovation, research and technological development policies. here the so-called industrial leadership, the great european industry, will assert its interests. our vision of science and research differs in key aspects from the vision set out in this programme.
in writing. − this document is part of the legislative package for the horizon 2020 programme, which will run from 2014 to 2020 and which, for the first time, brings together all funding for research and innovation. horizon 2020 should be designed to actively contribute to the construction of the european research area (era). for this reason, horizon 2020 should be more than a funding programme and should have a structural effect on the organisation of research at european level. specific measures are therefore proposed that can contribute to building a stronger and more efficient era, relating to governance, project size and type, barriers to entry, gender equality, youth employment, dissemination and exploitation, strengthening of dialogue between science and society and international cooperation. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - scientific excellence, industrial leadership and societal challenges are the three priorities driving horizon 2020. behind these clichés, it is important to realize that scientific excellence is the criterion that allows the selection of institutions, public-private partnerships and companies. many institutions will in practice be excluded from the possibility of receiving funding from this programme. funding will be channelled to those who meet the criteria reflected in the programme's objectives, i.e. to projects that better exploit the economic and industrial potential of innovation, research and technological development policies. the industrial leadership is playing an important role here and it is likely that it will continue to promote its interests, particularly those of large european industry. science and research will now contain in its formula the aspects of their economic value and the profit they can generate, as well as being tied to the political interests of the european union. we do not agree with this approach to funding research and innovation projects which must first of all seek to serve the needs of people and society. this decision establishes the specific programme for the implementation of horizon 2020 within the three priorities mentioned above.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that reliable and accurate european statistics play two vital roles as a public good: are the basic elements for decision-making by policy-makers and serve as a barometer for analysing the state of the economy and society, offering assurances to other governments and financial markets. however, events in recent years have shaken public and market confidence. a 2008 eurobarometer survey found that 45% of citizens do not trust economic statistics, a result virtually identical to the 46% who trust them. since then, we have seen how misleading and fraudulent statistics can contribute to political and economic unrest. indeed, the sovereign debt crisis was undoubtedly exacerbated by public and market scepticism about the accuracy of statistics on government debt and deficit levels. in this context, this regulation comes at an opportune time. we need to rebuild public confidence in statistical data. the adage goes, once statistics are politicized, they are quickly devalued. this is why it is essential to exclude politics from the production of statistics.
in writing. − reliable and accurate european statistics are essential, not only as a basis for policy-making but also as indicators which serve as a basis for analysing the state of the member states' economies and societies. the proposals in this report include the need for countries not to delay the dissemination of their statistics and lay down the rules to be followed by member states and their services in producing statistics. the purpose of this text is to clarify how the european statistical system (ess) will work in a way that is reliable, transparent and consistent. to this end, the eeas should be sufficiently resourced, have the necessary independence and adequate oversight (with sanctions for infringers if necessary). it is also foreseen that the director of eurostat will develop a greater interaction with parliament, to which he will have to render democratic accountability and discuss statistical production and governance policies. in view of the above and considering that public surveys have shown a low level of trust of european citizens in european statistics since 2008, i support this report as i believe that it will bring a more reliable statistical system that deserves the trust of all europeans.
in writing. - reliable and accurate european statistics are essential, not only as a basis for policy-making but also as indicators which serve as a basis for analysing the state of the economy and society in the member states. the proposals in this report include the need for countries not to delay the dissemination of their statistics and lay down the rules to be followed by member states and their services in producing statistics. the purpose of this text is to clarify how the european statistical system (ess) will work in order to make it reliable, transparent and consistent. to this end, the eeas should be sufficiently resourced, have the necessary independence and adequate oversight (with sanctions for infringers, if necessary). it is also foreseen that the director of eurostat will develop a greater interaction with parliament, to which he will have to render democratic accountability and discuss statistical production and governance policies. in view of the above and considering that public surveys have shown a low level of trust of european citizens in european statistics since 2008, i support this report which i believe will bring about a more reliable statistical system that deserves the trust of all europeans.
in writing. − reliable and accurate european statistics are essential, in particular for policymakers' decision-making, and serve as a barometer for analysing the state of the economy and society, offering assurances to other governments and financial markets. a report by the european court of auditors calls for a transition to a european statistical system that ensures professional independence, sufficient resources and effective supervision, including the application of sanctions in cases of non-compliance with quality standards. for the production of clear and independent statistics, i agree that the nsis should be free from any political interference, at national or european level. the appointment of the heads of the nis must be made in a transparent and fair manner, under parliamentary control.
in writing. − this report calls for a transition to a european statistical system that ensures professional independence, sufficient resources and effective supervision, including the application of sanctions in cases of non-compliance with quality standards. although it sets out objectives and principles which we can support, as regards the processing and collection of economic statistics, it presents others which are totally contradictory to the first and which we do not support. quality statistical production requires competent and qualified public services with sufficient resources, independent of economic power. the state is responsible for the accuracy and authenticity of statistical data. it is therefore your responsibility to provide these services. we cannot agree with the statement that statistics support and serve the monitoring of the results of the so-called economic governance (the six pack), that is, the guidelines of those who run the european institutions, the european bureaucracy and the interests it serves. the statistical indicators must be based on a full knowledge of social and economic realities and must not be selected with a view to pursuing political objectives which are, moreover, totally contrary to the defence of development and social progress.
in writing. − the purpose of this text is to clarify how the european statistical system (ess) will work in order to make it reliable, transparent and consistent. to this end, the eeas should be sufficiently resourced, have the necessary independence and adequate oversight (with sanctions for infringers, if necessary). reliable and accurate european statistics are essential, not only as indicators underpinning the analysis of the state of the economy and society in the member states, but also as a basis for policy-making. the proposals in this report include the need for countries not to delay in disseminating their statistics and lay down the rules to be followed by member states and their services in producing statistics. in view of the above and considering that public surveys have shown a low level of trust of european citizens in european statistics since 2008, i support this report which i believe will bring about a more reliable statistical system worthy of the trust of all europeans.
in writing. − reliable and accurate european statistics are vital as a public good. however, in recent years public and market confidence in these data has been declining. this regulation is a response to this problem, as it seeks to exclude policy from the production of statistics, for example, it is proposed that member states be prohibited from delaying the dissemination of periodic data. clarifying the functioning of the european statistical system esa is crucial to ensure its reliability, transparency and consistency. the eeas shall be sufficiently resourced, independent and adequately supervised. the director-general of eurostat should be brought closer to the european parliament by encouraging debate on statistical production and governance policies. the european parliament must also be accountable to the european parliament. these measures build confidence in the european statistical system, which is why i support the following report.
in writing. - i approve this report, considering that the social change and innovation programme proposed by the european commission brings together three existing programmes - progress, eures and the european microfinance facility - into a new programme. in my view, the european commission's proposal to merge the three programmes in 2014 has been misplaced in terms of priorities. instead of optimising the three programmes and making them more effective, the objectives and measures are diluted following the merger. there is no substantive link between the three instruments. while common rules are formulated in part i, explicit references are also made to three distinct sub-programmes. i am of the opinion that, apart from an administrative simplification for the european commission, the merger of the three programmes does not bring any direct added value to european citizens. it is also noted that the commission proposal is extremely vague on many points, giving the commission a great deal of leeway in the implementation and design of the programme.
in writing. − the increase in unemployment in several countries and regions of the union has made even more evident the need for cross-border coordination and coherence on social and employment issues. i hope that the philosophy of the programmes now merged into the european union programme for social change and innovation will be preserved and that this merger will not take away their flexibility and responsiveness but rather contribute to enriching this response.
in writing. - in the current context, this programme can be important, important if, in fact, as it states, it aims to promote quality employment, which in our view are jobs with social and labour rights. the scepticism comes from the current social backsliding in several countries, of which the eu is an active and responsible part. we therefore hope that voluntary mobility, as stated in the report, will be that and not forced emigration, as is the case in many eu countries today. no country can develop without its young people, without the qualified staff it has trained. we have been advocating from the beginning for increased funding for microcredit. instead of the proposed 21%, we proposed to allocate 30%. public investment in the real economy, in productive investment, is essential at this time. finally, the concept of social entrepreneurship is misleading. public services have been shut down in several countries under the blackmail of the cuts. we will not accept that business is made from the sale of these services, which should be public and free. what is needed is their enhancement and diversification, responding to existing and emerging social needs. we do not accept its destruction to make way for such social entrepreneurship.
in writing. − the european commission created the social change and innovation programme by merging three existing programmes: the progress funding instrument, in the area of employment, social protection and inclusion, working conditions, combating discrimination and gender equality; eures, in the area of worker mobility; and the progress european microfinance instrument, which facilitates access to micro-credit. despite being opposed to this merger, the rapporteur and the council have reached compromises which allow us to adopt this report today. a single governance for programme implementation, monitoring and evaluation, horizontal partnerships between programmes, transparency in the application of funds and strengthening of the principle of partnership and dialogue with the social partners and non-governmental organisations are some examples. for these reasons, i am in favour of approving this programme.
in writing. - in the current context, this programme can be important, important if, in fact, as it states, it aims to promote quality employment which, in our view, is employment with social and labour rights. the scepticism comes from the current social backsliding in several countries, of which the eu is an active and responsible part. we therefore hope that voluntary mobility, as stated in the report, will be that and not forced emigration, as is the case in many eu countries today. no country can develop without its young people, without the qualified staff it has trained. we have been advocating from the beginning for increased funding for microcredit. instead of the allocated 21%, we propose to allocate 30%. at the moment, public investment in the real economy, in productive development, is essential. finally, the concept of social entrepreneurship is misleading. today, public services are shutting down in many countries under the blackmail of cutting spending. we will not accept that business is made from the sale of these services, which should be public and free, and which are being deliberately destroyed to benefit such 'social entrepreneurship'. weighing the report's strengths and weaknesses, we abstained.
in writing. − i welcome this report, starting by pointing out that the selection of life projects is mainly based on their quality and their contribution to european added value, with a focus on demonstration/transfer potential and environmental/climate impact. experience from previous life programming periods has shown disparities between member states in the use of available life funds. some countries or regions have been able to prepare high quality projects repeatedly and secure their matching funds, and have therefore received overall more support through the life programme. this situation continued even after the introduction of the complex system of indicative national allocations in life+ (2007-2013). there is no doubt that the glaring inequalities in the allocation of projects have to be addressed in the new life regulation. i believe that european solidarity and responsibility sharing mean something different: member states and regions with low project selection rates need to be supported to achieve higher quality in their projects.
in writing. − as the epp shadow rapporteur for an opinion in the committee on budgets on the life programme, i supported the proposal put forward by the european commission to increase the co-financing rate for life projects to 70% of eligible costs. exceptionally, the maximum co-financing rate for projects in less developed regions is 80% of the eligible costs. in addition, vat costs should still be eligible in the case of project beneficiaries that do not have to recover vat costs in accordance with the vat rules in their member state.
in writing. − regardless of the more or less catastrophic nature of the information we are being given about the environment and climate change, it is imperative to recognise the need to take care of environmental preservation and to contribute to climate security. i believe that the environment and climate action programme, the fruit of a difficult but committed commitment, is animated by these aims and aims to equip the union with instruments appropriate to the scale of the challenge and to enable us to leave to our children, in the best possible conditions, the territory we love and received from our parents.
in writing. the report by mr jutta haug deals with the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation establishing a programme for the environment and climate action (life). the life programme has been a considerable success in addressing the environmental and climate challenges facing europeans. it is an effective and well-targeted instrument, and is highly appreciated by local, regional and national public administrations, ngos, research institutions and smes. i would like to emphasize in this report the integrated projects, which under life are a concrete tool for integration. the aim of these projects is to support, along with other eu funds, the implementation of the most important environmental legislation. i believe that all projects should have a significant potential for job creation and growth. integrated projects should foster the creation of constructive and lasting cooperation between the different sectors, which will improve the coherence of eu spending.
in writing. − with its shortcomings and limitations, the life programme has been able to achieve positive concrete results in the field of nature conservation and biodiversity. the success of this programme proves the importance of its maintenance and reinforcement. we have proposed a significant increase in appropriations - to allocate at least 1% of the eu budget to life. with this proposal, we are a long way from that goal. there are still some problems, evident over the last few years, which need to be addressed, such as the levels of implementation by country. many projects have not yet been realised due to lack of support for project development and co-financing requirements. in many countries, the annual number of projects selected has often fallen short of their indicative allocation, a problem which has become more acute in recent years. the new concept of integrated projects presents national administrations with challenges and requirements which cannot be ignored, otherwise more resources will be wasted or they will be concentrated on the same resources as before. we also believe that new objectives must be matched by new and strengthened means. it is important that new climate objectives are not pursued at the expense of the weakening of nature conservation and biodiversity this has been and should continue to be the core of the life programme.
in writing. − to endow the life programme environment and climate action programme with an adequate budget and a significant share of overall eu spending is a strong indicator that the european union is serious about its environmental and climate commitments. over the past 20 years, this programme has been a huge success, appreciated by various public administrations, ngos, research institutions and small and medium-sized enterprises. life projects are selected on the basis of their quality and demonstration potential and environmental impact. however, the need for european solidarity with regard to member states with a low rate of project selection should be safeguarded in order to achieve a geographical balance. they should be supported through training and advisory services with a view to achieving higher quality in their projects. the life programme promotes the conservation of nature and biodiversity, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i approve this report, considering that the fiscus programme, as proposed by the european commission, should be a single successor to the existing customs 2013 and fiscalis 2013 programmes. the fiscus programme, announced at the beginning of november as part of the wider package of the mff, is designed to merge the two programmes into one for reasons of simplification. this is an eu programme which should not have an impact on tax policy, which is a primary competence of the member states. however, i have serious reservations about the proposed merger of the two legal bases. the two programmes have different and distinct objectives and contexts and therefore should have different legal provisions on implementation, evaluation, monitoring and control. furthermore, since the commission has kept separate overall budgetary amounts for each of the programmes and has expressed its interest in preserving the identity of the programmes, it would be logical that the best way to ensure this would be to keep the programmes separate.
in writing. − this commission proposal is part of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. in the discussions on the fiscalis programme 2014-2020, the main points emphasised by the european parliament were the need to combat tax fraud and evasion, double taxation, aggressive tax planning, the need for an integrated functioning of tax systems in line with the functioning of the internal market, and also increasing cooperation between countries. the programme could facilitate networking, joint actions and training for tax staff and could also finance computer systems to ensure the efficient exchange of large amounts of information between national tax administrations. the european parliament made some concessions in the negotiations with the commission and the council of the european union, particularly as regards the establishment of indicators for evaluating the programme in question in the member states. considering that this proposal contributes to the protection of the financial interests of the eu and the member states and to the improvement of the capacities of their tax authorities, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − this commission proposal is part of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. in the discussions on the fiscalis programme 2014-2020, the main points emphasised by the european parliament were the need to combat tax fraud and evasion, double taxation, aggressive tax planning, the need for an integrated functioning of tax systems in line with the functioning of the internal market, and also increasing cooperation between countries. the programme could facilitate networking, joint actions and training for tax staff and could also finance computer systems to ensure the efficient exchange of large amounts of information between national tax administrations. the european parliament made some concessions in the negotiations with the commission and the council of the european union, particularly as regards the establishment of indicators for evaluating the programme in question in the member states. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the financial interests of the eu and the member states and to improve the capacity of their tax authorities.
in writing. − the fiscus programme, as proposed by the european commission, should be a single successor to the existing customs 2013 and fiscalis 2013 programmes. the fiscus programme, announced at the beginning of november as part of the wider package of the mff, is designed to merge the two programmes into one for reasons of simplification. despite the possible gains in terms of simplification, i have doubts about the merging advantages of these two programmes which are (and should continue to be) distinct.
in writing. - this proposal, while recognising some of the obstacles and distortions in the internal market, fails to take a critical stand against the mechanisms which provide for tax evasion and avoidance, i.e. the free movement of capital - the pillar of neoliberalism. no concrete measures are presented against the abolition of tax havens, nor is there any reference to taxation of the financial profits of large economic groups, or taxes on capital income. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. while cooperation in the field of taxation is important and necessary, we cannot ignore the fact that tax policy is a fundamental instrument of economic and social policy, in the definition of which obvious political criteria and objectives weigh. strengthening the mechanisms for computer systems, information exchange and staff training, which are intended to make the national tax authorities subject to a harmonisation with a class seal, without taking into account the specificities of the different member states, is not sufficient for an effective fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. we voted against it.

in writing. − the objective of this proposal is to establish a single action programme for taxation in the eu, through cooperation between tax authorities, to strengthen the internal market and to support the fight against tax fraud, tax evasion and aggressive tax planning. the proposal fails to take a critical stand against the mechanisms that provide for tax evasion and avoidance, i.e. the free movement of capital and the single market; the commission has not yet taken any concrete measures to put an end to tax havens; it does not deal with the taxation of the financial profits of large economic groups, or with taxes on capital income. the commission is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover all the member states. while cooperation in the field of taxation is important and necessary, we cannot ignore the fact that tax policy is a fundamental instrument of economic and social policy. the reinforcement of computer systems, information exchange and staff training mechanisms, which are intended to make the national tax authorities subject to harmonisation with a class seal, is not sufficient for an effective fight against tax fraud and evasion. we voted against this report.
in writing. - i approve this report, first of all expressing my great satisfaction that the commission has already taken into account parliament's request to split the previous proposal on the fiscus programme into the customs and fiscalis programmes. however, for reasons of visibility and legal clarity, the general and specific objectives and the operational objectives should be defined in the articles of the regulation. taking into account the dynamics of new customs challenges and the need to protect citizens against security risks arising from international trade in goods, greater emphasis should be placed on the harmonisation and standardisation of customs control procedures and the fight against fraud. in addition, as the commission proposal makes several references to indicators, it is important to establish the process for developing these indicators in order to monitor and assess the value and impact of the measures taken under the programme. in order to ensure the necessary degree of flexibility in this process, it is appropriate to empower the commission to carry out this activity within the framework of the annual work programme.
in writing. - the union's customs policy must seek to strike a balance between the protection of consumers and european production and the opening up of new markets, the increasing flow of goods or the quest for tariff disarmament and the need to impose charges on certain products. the division of the commission's proposal into two specifically oriented towards customs and tax matters shows the chamber's disbelief in the alleged advantages of their merger. i hope that the action programmes will achieve their intended aims and help the union to take concrete and firm steps in these particularly sensitive areas.
in writing. − the multiannual action programme for the customs sector for 2014-2020 (customs 2020) will ensure the continuation of the previous programme and aims to facilitate and strengthen cooperation between customs authorities in the eu. the programme also aims to contribute to the implementation of the eu 2020 strategy by strengthening the functioning of the internal market. the programme calls for full harmonization of customs procedures and controls. this implies the harmonization of all aspects relating to the collection, electronic data processing techniques and the use of common levels and modes of control over goods. in a world where trade is dominated by large transnational corporations, this programme aims to reflect and serve the interests of these same transnational corporations by reducing the time it takes for goods to move and simplifying customs procedures. simplifying, however, from the point of view of proper customs procedures and with a view to combating them, is not the same as facilitating. it is not by chance that the community texts often speak of facilitation rather than simplification. on the other hand, the loss of sovereignty of the member states over their customs policy raises concerns about who will be responsible for the collection and use of revenue, but also about how to find a common price in the context of harmonisation.
in writing. − the customs 2020 programme calls for action by the european union in the field of customs cooperation and customs union in the european area. a number of amendments to the programme regulation are proposed, in particular as regards the definition of the general, specific and operational objectives of the programme. the committee also calls for greater emphasis to be placed on the harmonization and standardization of customs control procedures and the fight against fraud. the possibility of allocating the budget of the annual work programme to respond to any changes in political priorities is also desirable. we must ensure effective protection of the eu's external borders and to do this we must strengthen technical capacities and ensure constant support for the various actions of the customs authorities.
in writing. − the multiannual action programme for the customs sector for the period 2014-2020 (customs 2020) will ensure the continuation of the previous programme and aims to facilitate and strengthen cooperation between customs authorities in the union. the amount of assigned revenue in accordance with article 21 (3) of the financial regulation is estimated at eur 100000. the programme requires the full harmonisation of customs procedures and controls, which implies the harmonisation of almost all aspects of collection, electronic data processing techniques and the use of common levels and modes of control over goods. in a world where trade is dominated by large transnational companies, this programme would have to reflect and serve the interests of these same transnational companies by reducing the time it takes for goods to move and simplifying customs procedures. now, simplifying is not the same as facilitating. it is not by chance that the community texts often speak of facilitation rather than simplification. the loss of sovereignty of the member states over their customs policy raises concerns about who will be responsible for collecting and using the revenue, but also about how to find a common price in the context of harmonisation.
in writing. - i approve this report, given that the negotiations on the omnibus ii directive have not yet been concluded. the deadline for transposition, which was until 30 june 2013, should be extended for a final time. if this date is not changed, the solvency ii directive will have to be applied without the transitional rules and other important adaptations provided for in the omnibus ii directive. in order to prevent this from happening and to ensure the legal continuity of the current solvency provisions (solvency i) until the full entry into force of the solvency ii package, it is proposed to extend the relevant transposition deadline provided for in directive 2009/138/ec for the last time until 31 january 2015. it is also important that supervisors and insurance and reinsurance undertakings are given some time to prepare for the implementation of the solvency ii package. therefore, it is proposed to extend the date of application of the solvency ii package one last time to 1 january 2016. this will enable supervisory approval procedures to be initiated, for example on internal models and company-specific parameters.
in writing. − in this report, the european parliament endorses the european commission's position on the solvency ii directive. the solvency ii project aims to review the prudential regime for insurance and reinsurance in the european union, with a view to enhancing supervision of these activities, enhancing risk control, prudential measures and standardising activities and reporting systems. due to delays in the negotiations of the omnibus 2 legislation, it has become necessary to postpone the transposition and entry into force of this directive. in this respect, member states will defer the transposition of the directive into their national legislation. the date initially planned for 30 june 2012 is now 31 december 2014. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the amount of the capital injections in question. the report does not therefore alter the content of the proposed directive, but only approves the date of its transposition in the member states. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. − this report proposes a directive postponing the dates for transposition and application of directive 2009/138/ec, giving supervisory authorities and insurance and reinsurance undertakings sufficient time to prepare for the implementation of the new insurance sector supervisory architecture, the creation of the european supervisory authority (eiopa). as you know, we were against this new architecture of so-called supervision. directive 2009/138/ec of the european parliament and of the council establishes a risk-based system for the regulation and supervision of insurance and reinsurance undertakings in the eu. this directive recognises the importance of insurance guarantee schemes (igs) in reducing the risks faced by policyholders and, where appropriate, by policyholders in the event of the insolvency of an insurance undertaking, by minimising the likelihood of an insurer going bankrupt and the resulting disruption to policyholders or, as the case may be, policyholders. the report therefore calls for the postponement of the transposition of directive 2009/138/ec (solvency ii) and the repeal of the directives to 1 january 2014. the content of this report being eminently technical and in view of our critical position towards eiopa and the directive in question, we abstained.

on behalf of the gue/ngl group, the failure of the last three decades of the common fisheries policy is evident. a centralised management, far removed from reality, unaware of the profound diversity of fisheries in europe, has had disastrous economic, social and environmental results. however, the lisbon treaty has given the european union exclusive, rather than shared, responsibility for the management of living marine resources, thus aggravating the whole problem. the constraint that this institutional framework represents for the implementation of a local authority management system that best serves the objectives of sustainability was evident throughout the process of discussing the reform. the change in this institutional framework is a persistent need which we will have to meet sooner or later. it is significant that the one which was presented as one of the pillars of this reform and a mainstay of the proclaimed regionalization - the multiannual plans - persists, entangled in an institutional conflict that is not visible, which foreshadows, here too, the confirmation of the old maxim that something must change in order for everything to remain the same.
the reform of the cfp, which has been achieved after a long process of analysis, proposals and negotiations, is fairly balanced, especially if we take into account the commission's original proposal which neglected the balance, now closer, between the three fundamental pillars of the cfp: environmental, social and economic. the major problems arise precisely from the imbalance between the three pillars and the underestimation of the differences between industrial and small-scale fisheries, between monospecific fisheries in the north and multispecific fisheries in the south. i am referring to the objective of achieving maximum sustainable yield wherever possible by 2015 and at the latest by 2020, which is achievable for clean fisheries, but very difficult for multi-species fisheries. the same applies to the timetable for complying with the obligation to land all catches, which is very demanding for mixed fisheries in the south, which catch a wide variety of species and specimens of varying sizes, and require adaptations to the logistical conditions of vessels and port infrastructure. in this context, i regret that the regionalisation of the cfp has always been more of an ideal than a reality. in any event, the new cfp brings with it some very positive aspects, such as the scientific basis for policy decisions, the establishment of multiannual management plans, the creation of recovery zones for stocks, increased protection of sensitive biogeographical areas, the strengthening of the powers of the advisory councils, etc. let us support the sector to help it in this transition to take advantage of the new instruments that have been established.
the cfp reform now presents the opportunity to improve proximity management, promote sustainability and the exploitation of resources and the viability of coastal communities dependent on fisheries from a more specific view of our regions. the rejection of transferable quotas was very important in this respect. the cfp, with its financial instruments, must also ensure that the necessary support is given not only to the fishermen but also to the scientific community in order to achieve the objectives. it is essential that areas identified as sensitive biogeographically are now also protected from under-exploitation by external fleets, as is the case in the azores. the adoption of a jrc for the outermost regions also makes an indispensable contribution to the promotion of this ecosystem approach which takes account of our sensitive nature and our specific characteristics. finally, we must now ensure that foreign traders are treated equally in international trade.
the situation of the sardine fishery in the north-east atlantic requires a discussion that goes beyond the fishing levels of iceland and the faroe islands. it is the allocation of quotas between member states itself that deserves serious discussion on the basis of up-to-date information on the status of the resource and its stock. the evolution of the stock has led, for example in portugal, to a higher relative abundance of the species in national waters in recent years, so that the current portuguese quota is inadequate in relation to the actual situation of the resource, as is shown, moreover, by the fact that the quota is normally closed much earlier than in other countries and in a situation of proven abundance of the resource. the resource allocation keys between member states shall monitor the evolution of the stock and the relative abundance of resources in each zone. this is the only way to avoid that, in the name of relative stability, absolute stability, which is unfair and unsuitable for reality, is actually imposed.
this report is a good example of the desirable work that can be done in parliament between the various political groups. and also between divergent interests, as sometimes happens between the fishing industry and environmentalists. it started with a radical proposal from the commission and came to a consensus report, which preserves the fundamental principles of protecting sensitive habitats and maintaining reasonable operational conditions for the fleet. a realistic and pragmatic proposal was put forward, focusing on research into deep-sea habitats and the impact assessment of fishing gear targeting deep-sea species, and providing for measures to protect vulnerable marine ecosystems, the location of which should be identified by the member states and communicated to the commission. i think that this agreement, which is so difficult to achieve and a true example of parliamentary work, cannot and must not be broken tomorrow.

he asks under the blue card procedure. i would like to ask mr capoulas santos what his position was when, a few years ago, indonesia, which was illegally occupying east timor, made an agreement with third countries for the exploitation of oil in the timor sea. i ask you today, what was your position then, did you consider this agreement fair and acceptable?
answer according to the "blue card" procedure. mr president, in the light of international law, an agreement which ensures that the occupying power uses the exploited resources for the benefit of the population is considered legal. this is guaranteed in the moroccan agreement, it was not guaranteed in the oil exploration agreement then carried out by indonesia in the territory of east timor.
we have said this on several occasions and we reiterate it here: we have nothing against a fisheries agreement with morocco, an agreement which is fair, which respects the principles of sustainability and which is mutually beneficial. but an agreement which, in addition to moroccan waters, includes resources over which morocco has no sovereignty in the light of international law is an illegal agreement, which we cannot accept. the inclusion of the waters of western sahara in this agreement, which the european commission is unfortunately insisting on, is contrary to the decision of the international court of justice and to several united nations resolutions. it's an affront to international law. moreover, given the situation on the ground, this is a demonstration of the value of the hypocritical human rights clauses which the european union puts into its agreements. it is worth remembering that even the united states has explicitly excluded products from western sahara from its trade agreement with morocco. meanwhile, the european commission insists on illegality. let us hope that this parliament will not follow in his footsteps.
since december 2011, when parliament rejected the eu-morocco fisheries agreement, the european fleet has had to leave moroccan waters, with a high loss that has been accumulating until today. here, as in other waters of third countries where the union stops fishing, its position is occupied by other interests which, unlike what happens among us, ignore human rights and neglect both the fair remuneration of the indigenous populations and a sustainable management of fisheries. in view of the reasons for parliament's negative vote in 2011 and the guidelines of the resolution adopted on the same day, the agreement presented here today responds to the objections of the past by following the recommendations of that time. that is what is objectively unquestionable. this protocol is compatible with international law, more environmentally sustainable, more economically viable than the previous one. it provides for an increase in fishing opportunities of up to 33%, based on scientific advice, an improvement in the cost-benefit ratio between the financial contribution and fishing opportunities, a change in fishing areas and the operational conditions of the fleet, and the monitoring by the european union of the use of sectoral support and its socioeconomic impact on a geographical basis, ensuring that part of the financial compensation is actually applied in western sahara. voting against the agreement would harm the european fleet and the people of sarawak, by breaking good relations between morocco and the european union, the only fishing power in the region that respects human rights. in writing. − the rights, equality and citizenship programme now includes the well-known daphne programme, the only european programme for preventing and combating all forms of violence against children, young people and women. in europe, 18 women are killed every day, 12 of them by their partners or other family members. more than one in ten have experienced sexual violence and 26% of children and young people report cases of physical violence in childhood. to continue to combat this scourge, it was essential to make the prevention and combating of this type of violence a specific objective of the future programme and to retain the name daphne to identify projects related to this objective. adequate and balanced funding is also ensured. it is therefore a great victory for the european parliament to be able to continue with the new programme as a tool at the disposal of the non-governmental organisations that fight violence against children, young people and women every day. i am voting in favour of this text.
in writing. − the justice programme for the period 2014-2020, integrated into the next multiannual financial framework (mff), aims to create a european area of justice, supported by judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters. this new programme succeeds and synthesises three existing programmes: civil justice (jciv), criminal justice (jpen) and drug information and prevention (pipd), and promotes greater rationalisation of costs and means and more effective approach to objectives. this new programme is based on three essential objectives, with which i tend to agree: to promote the effective, comprehensive and consistent application of union law in the field of judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters, to facilitate access to justice and to prevent and reduce the demand for and supply of drugs. given the fundamental and strategic importance of judicial cooperation in a free and borderless area, i am voting in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − the commission proposal aims to create the justice programme 2014-2020. the general objective of the programme is to contribute to the establishment of a european area of justice by promoting judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters. in order to achieve the overall objective, the programme should fulfil specific objectives, including the effective, comprehensive and consistent implementation of eu legislation in the fields of judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters. the report covers a range of issues such as european added value - the rapporteurs consider that all members of the judiciary and judicial officials, when exercising their functions, should be aware that they are part of a european judicial system - and training issues, which are considered a key factor for the programme. our group has tabled amendments relating to the drugs approach, both in terms of health and crime prevention, respect for the principle of subsidiarity and the lack of judicial staff. our critical position on the european area of justice and on concepts such as a common european judicial culture or the replication of successful institutions is well known. we voted against it.

in writing. - the regulation establishes the rights, equality and citizenship programme for the next seven years, with a set of objectives, such as respect for non-discrimination, prevention, combating racism and xenophobia, combating violence against children, young people and women, promoting and defending the rights of people with disabilities, promoting equality between women and men, as well as a further set of good intentions with which we obviously agree. in fact, these objectives are daily disregarded and called into question by eu policies. that is a sad contradiction. in an opinion we drew up, which was adopted by the committee on women's rights and gender equality, we argued that the commission and the council should consider the issue of gender equality as a specific objective in the rights and citizenship programme, and also maintain the daphne programme as an independent sub-heading of this programme. the general recognition of the daphne programme's results is proof that it should continue to contribute to the objectives it sets itself with adequate funding and a well-defined percentage allocated, which should not be confused with other objectives, notably those relating to the internal market.
in writing. − the stockholm programme emphasised that the development of an area of freedom, security and justice remains a priority for the european union. this is intended to create an area in which the rights of individuals, as enshrined in the treaty on the functioning of the european union and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, are promoted and protected. in particular, this programme should promote the rights conferred by european citizenship, the principles of non-discrimination and equality between men and women, the right to the protection of personal data, the rights of the child, the rights deriving from union consumer protection legislation and the freedom to conduct a business in the internal market. that is why i am voting in favour.

in writing. − the european union is founded on values such as human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law, human rights and fundamental freedoms. values which are common to all the member states and which are part of what i believe to be the european identity. this report establishes the rights, equality and citizenship programme for the period 2014-2020. an initiative to create a space where equality and the rights of persons are promoted and defended, as enshrined in the treaty on european union, the treaty establishing the european union, the charter and the international human rights conventions to which the union is a party. it is a programme that aims to develop activities to prevent and combat racism, xenophobia, homophobia and any other form of intolerance. it also advocates for the rights of people with disabilities, promotes gender equality and combats violence and abuse. to this end, various activities such as workshops, seminars, conferences, training and communication campaigns are suggested.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because in september 2013 russia announced a ban on imports of moldovan wines and spirits in retaliation for its efforts to expand ties with the eu, and the eu would therefore like to compensate for at least part of the losses by extending trade preferences for moldovan wine.
in writing. − this project establishes autonomous trade preferences for the republic of moldova, eliminating all customs duties on industrial products and improving access of agricultural products to the eu market. in accordance with regulation (ec) no 55/2008, the autonomous trade preferences apply until 31 december 2015. the application of that regulation after 1 january 2013 depends on the successful completion of certain procedures in the world trade organisation. the european union has launched these procedures and the timeframe for their completion is currently unknown. therefore, until the wto procedures are concluded, it is necessary to ensure the continuity of trade flows of the republic of moldova until 31 december 2015. in addition, it is necessary to ensure legal certainty for economic operators that they will be able to continue to import under the regulation governing autonomous trade preferences. it is therefore necessary to provide that the autonomous trade preferences are applied without interruption until the date set by council regulation (ec) no 55/2008 for their expiry. i am voting in favour of this text.
in writing. − the need to maintain the uninterrupted character of the autonomous trade preferences justifies the amendment of council regulation (ec) no 55/2008. the commission has also taken into account the fact that the union's macro-financial assistance to moldova is limited to the minimum necessary to ensure the proper functioning of the union's macro-financial assistance. the trade facilitations enjoyed by moldova should facilitate its development and contribute to the prosperity of its population, as well as to the approximation of european union standards with regard to democracy, human rights, respect for the rule of law and freedom of trade. i hope that the maintenance of autonomous trade preferences will contribute to this rapprochement and allow the maintenance of trade flows between this country and the european union.

mr president, by approving the fisheries agreement between morocco and the european union, this parliament has given the green light to an agreement which is illegal under international law, which violates the decision of the international court of justice, which violates several united nations resolutions and which may even be more original than the agreement itself concluded by the united states, which excluded the waters of western sahara, as the european union should have done. morocco is trading with resources that are not its own, including the waters of western sahara that are also not its own, and therefore legitimizes the occupation of these territories. we could have supported democracy, human rights and freedom with this vote, but what parliament did was take the side of the oppressor and therefore support the opposite of what i have just said, we must decide once and for all whether the european union and the european institutions think it is worth fighting for human rights or not, because with this vote what it has shown is that they are very hypocritical.
in writing. - i vote in favour. i believe it is important to move forward with the establishment of fishing opportunities in order to make the activity resulting from them mutually beneficial and based on economic, social and environmental sustainability. however, from a political point of view, all the legal and human rights and property issues of the people of western sahara must be assessed.
in writing. − since december 2011, when parliament rejected the eu-morocco fisheries agreement, the european fleet has had to leave moroccan waters, with a high loss that has been accumulating until today. in view of the reasons for parliament's negative vote in 2011 and the guidelines of the resolution adopted on the same day, the agreement presented here today responds to the objections of the past by following the recommendations of that time. that is what is objectively unquestionable. this protocol is compatible with international law, more environmentally sustainable, more economically viable than the previous one. it provides for an increase in fishing opportunities of up to 33%, based on scientific advice, an improvement in the cost-benefit ratio between the financial contribution and fishing opportunities, a change in fishing areas and the operational conditions of the fleet, and the monitoring by the european union of the use of sectoral support and its socioeconomic impact on a geographical basis, ensuring that part of the financial compensation is actually applied in western sahara. i am voting in favour of this text.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation on the eu-morocco fisheries partnership agreement: protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution, by including a clause on respect for democratic principles and fundamental human rights, and by ensuring that any failure by morocco to comply with this protocol could lead to its suspension. the agreement also provides for legal obligations to ensure the sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources on the basis of enhanced scientific cooperation. the approval of the protocol will allow the resumption of fisheries relations with morocco, while ensuring that the geographical impact of the social and economic benefits arising from it is monitored, since part of the financial compensation will be used to benefit the entire population, including that of the territory of the sahara under moroccan administration.
in writing. - i fully agree with and support my colleague, mrs carmen fraga estévez, whom i would like to greet, as this new protocol contains very important improvements compared to its predecessor and responds to the concerns of the european parliament and of countries such as portugal. the fisheries agreement between the european union and morocco will authorize 14 portuguese vessels to fish in moroccan waters. this protocol could allow the resumption of fisheries relations with morocco on a new basis, much more in line with the eu's objectives, both from the economic and financial point of view and from the point of view of social and environmental sustainability.
in writing. the report by mrs carmen fraga estévez deals with the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol between the european union and the kingdom of morocco setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the kingdom of morocco. the european commission has been opening negotiations for the signing of a new protocol. the fishing categories in this agreement are the same as in the previous protocol and, although the number of vessels is reduced from 137 to 126, the fishing opportunities are increased by 33%. the fishing zones have been modified to better adapt to the needs of the fleets and to allow certain requirements imposed by morocco to be met. i therefore consider that this protocol is compatible with international law, is environmentally sustainable and at the same time more cost-effective than the previous one.
in writing. - it is regrettable that, after a fair rejection of the renewal of this agreement in 2011, given its illegality in the light of international law, the european commission insists on the inclusion of the waters of western sahara in the agreement - a fact which is at the basis of this illegality - and that parliament assesses and accepts it. we have nothing against a fisheries agreement with morocco. a fair, sustainable and mutually beneficial agreement. but an agreement which, in addition to moroccan waters, includes resources over which morocco has no sovereignty in the light of international law is an illegal agreement, which we cannot accept. the commission has also been asked to provide the necessary information to the authorities in the member states, and this is all the more so since the legitimate representatives of the sarawak population have not been given the opportunity to be heard, as would be required by international law and the successive un resolutions on the natural resources of non-self-governing territories. the comparison with the situation in east timor during the illegal occupation by indonesia is inevitable. at that time the portuguese people were rightly indignant and mobilized against the agreements made by indonesia with third countries for the exploitation of oil from the timor sea. some of those who were against these agreements then are now hypocritically approving the conclusion of this fisheries agreement, trying to forget the obvious parallels.
in writing. - i voted against the european parliament's ratification of the eu-morocco fisheries agreement because i believe that the agreement, as negotiated, is contrary to international law. the agreement includes a clause to ensure that the geographical spread of the social and economic benefits of eu sectoral support is monitored, meaning that part of the financial compensation will go to the benefit of the entire population, including that of the sar. it's an improvement over the previous version, which was rejected in 2011. however, this clause does not guarantee that morocco will implement the agreement in accordance with the wishes and interests of the sarawi people. moreover, the commission is unlikely to press morocco to do so, given the general nature of the clause. to be in line with international law, the agreement would have to provide expressly how much it will benefit the indigenous people of western sahara, affirming morocco as the de facto administrative authority of the territory of western sahara. on the other hand, representatives of the sarawi people should have been consulted during the negotiations, which did not happen. i therefore voted against ratifying this agreement on grounds of principle, consistency and conscience.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the new eu-morocco fisheries agreement because it is clearly more advantageous for portugal. the agreement now approved provides for better technical conditions for our fishermen. under the previous protocol, the eu paid a lot of money to fish in areas with few fish resources and therefore little economic return. portugal has always had a great tradition of fishing in morocco, particularly in the catching of white swordfish. portugal still has 14 licences under the new protocol and still has 1 555 tonnes of pelagic fish, which means that portugal now has more fish to fish. in this way, the interests of eu fishermen operating in this area are safeguarded.
in writing. − following the european parliament's refusal last december to approve the one-year extension of the fisheries protocol with morocco, which expired on 27 february 2012, the european commission has started negotiations for the signing of a new protocol. this new protocol provides for fishing opportunities and technical measures. the total cost of the protocol per year is around eur 40 billion, and the rapporteur considered that the new protocol contains several improvements over the various aspects that would lead to the rejection of the previous text. for the reasons given, i voted in favour of approving the protocol.
in writing. - it is regrettable that, after the rejection of the renewal of this agreement in 2011, in view of its illegality in the light of international law, the european commission insists on the inclusion of the waters of western sahara in the agreement - a fact which is at the basis of this illegality - and that parliament assesses and accepts it. we have nothing against a fisheries agreement with morocco. as long as it's a fair deal, that respects principles of sustainability and mutual benefit. but we cannot accept an agreement which, in addition to moroccan waters, includes resources over which morocco has no sovereignty under international law. this is an illegal arrangement. the fact is that the legitimate representatives of the sarawak population have not been guaranteed the hearing which would be required in accordance with international law and successive un resolutions on the natural resources of non-self-governing territories. we cannot help drawing a parallel with the situation in east timor during the illegal occupation by indonesia. at that time the portuguese people were rightly indignant and mobilized against the agreements made by indonesia with third countries for the exploitation of oil from the timor sea. some of those who were against these agreements then are now hypocritically approving the conclusion of this fisheries agreement, trying to forget the obvious parallels.
