in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. convention no 170 was adopted at the 77th session of the international labour conference on 25 june 1990 and entered into force on 4 november 1993. the aim of the convention is to prevent and reduce chemical-induced workplace illness and injury and to enhance the protection of the general public and the environment. convention no 170 states that the protection of workers from the harmful effects of chemicals also contributes to the protection of the general public and the environment and that access to information on chemicals used in the workplace is necessary. it states that all chemicals must be assured that they are assessed for hazard and that employers must obtain information from suppliers on the chemicals used at work so that they can put in place effective programmes to protect workers from the hazards. we voted for it, of course.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it proposed parliament's consent to the conclusion of the protocol against the illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms, their parts and components and ammunition, which will complement the united nations convention against transnational organized crime, which is a global instrument in the fight against organized crime and the trafficking of firearms.
in writing. − arms trafficking is one of the illicit activities that most threatens the internal security of the eu, and it is therefore important that the union continues to combat this form of organised crime effectively. the promotion of ratification of international conventions should be part of this strategy. the firearms protocol is the first global instrument to combat transnational organised crime and the illicit trade in firearms. it establishes a very useful multilateral framework and a set of minimum standards relevant to all participating states, aimed at preventing, combating and eradicating the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts, components and ammunition. the conclusion of this protocol is therefore consistent with the eu's current policies against transnational crime, which aim to step up the fight against illicit trafficking in firearms, including export control and traceability and the reduction of the proliferation and spread of small arms worldwide. given that there are currently still four member states which have not signed or even acceded to the protocol, i support its ratification by the eu, which will make the provisions of the protocol legally binding for all member states, within the framework of european competences.
in writing. − the ratification by the european union of the protocol on the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts, components and ammunition will make the provisions of the protocol legally binding on all member states within the limits of european competence. the importance of this protocol for preventing the illicit trafficking of firearms, which benefits and largely finances criminal and terrorist groups, is noted, and i am voting in favour of its ratification.
in writing. the report by mrs véronique mathieu houillon deals with the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the additional protocol to the united nations convention against transnational organized crime on the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts, components and ammunition. this convention is the first global instrument to combat transnational organised crime and the illicit trade in firearms. i consider the exchange of information provided for in article 12 of the protocol to be very important in this respect, since crime knows no borders and all forms of trafficking, such as arms trafficking, can only be effectively combated if everyone cooperates. it is essential to exchange information on criminal groups, methods, routes and means used, illicit firearms, authorised manufacturers, dealers, importers and exporters. i am voting in favour of this protocol because i believe that it will help to improve the safety of european citizens without, however, harming the legal users of firearms.
in writing. the report gives parliament's consent to the conclusion of the additional protocol to the united nations convention against transnational organized crime on the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts, components and ammunition. the protocol applies to the prevention of illicit manufacture of and trafficking in firearms, their parts, components and ammunition, and to the investigation and prosecution of offences defined in accordance with article 5 on criminalisation, which requires each country to adopt such legislative and other measures as it deems necessary to make criminal offences, including the manufacture, trafficking, falsification or erasure, removal or alteration of marks on firearms, their parts, components and ammunition, where such offences are transnational in nature and involve an organised criminal group. the protocol shall not apply to transactions between states or to transfers by states where its application would prejudice the right of a state to act in the interests of national security in accordance with the charter of the united nations and with respect for its sovereignty in this matter. this document also deals with loss and seizure, firearms marking and prevention, deactivation, licensing, security measures and information. we voted in favour.
in writing. − this protocol allows for better prevention of and fight against illicit trafficking in firearms by better controlling weapons through their marking and import and export authorisations, and by strengthening cooperation and the exchange of information between states parties. i believe that this protocol can enhance the security of european citizens without, however, harming the legal users of firearms.
in writing. − the united nations international convention against transnational organized crime, adopted on 15 november 2000, is the first global instrument to combat transnational organized crime and the illicit trade in firearms. three protocols clarify the convention by providing for specific measures to combat specific crimes. the protocols cover, respectively, trafficking in human beings, trafficking in migrants and the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms. the protocol on the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms was signed on 16 january 2002 but its conclusion was postponed pending the adaptation of european legislation. i voted in favour of this report which proposes the adoption of this protocol, since the protocol allows for better prevention and combating of illicit trafficking in firearms, better control of weapons through their marking and import and export authorizations, and strengthening cooperation and the exchange of information between the states parties.
in writing. − this document proposes the ratification of a protocol to prevent, combat and eradicate the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts, components and ammunition. this will enhance the safety of european citizens without harming legal users of firearms. the document contains a number of measures, such as the penalisation of the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, and the forgery and suppression of firearms' markings. this marking of firearms at the time of manufacture, import and transfer between countries should be ensured by member states so that the manufacturer, the country and the year of import can be identified. cooperation between member states is strongly encouraged through a single point of contact to strengthen the capacity to prevent, detect and investigate such illegal activities. the rapporteur also stresses that the illicit trafficking of firearms and their components and ammunition benefits criminal groups and terrorists, as it provides a form of extra income, thus increasing their destructive potential.
in writing. the report gives parliament's consent to the conclusion of the additional protocol to the united nations convention against transnational organized crime on the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts, components and ammunition. it also applies to the investigation and prosecution of offences defined in accordance with article 5, which provides that each country shall adopt such legislative and other measures as it deems necessary to establish criminal offences, including the manufacture, trafficking in, counterfeiting or erasing, removing or altering marks on firearms, their parts, components and ammunition, where such offences are transnational in nature and involve an organised criminal group. the protocol shall not apply to transactions between states or to transfers by states. this document also deals with loss and seizure, firearms marking and prevention, deactivation, licensing, security measures and information. we are of course in favour of increased cooperation in the exchange of information and the development of strategies against criminal groups involved in the illicit trafficking of arms, although this increased cooperation should not be reflected in increased surveillance of individuals and groups not involved in these criminal networks.

in writing. the report by mrs véronique helmut scholz deals with the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of an agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the people's republic of china pursuant to article xxiv:6 and article xxviii of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) 1994 relating to the modification of concessions in the schedules of the republic of bulgaria and romania in the context of their accession to the european union. with the accession of the republic of bulgaria and romania, the european union has enlarged its customs union. the european union therefore had to enter into negotiations with wto members with negotiating power on the lists of any of the acceding members in order to agree on a compensatory adjustment that satisfies all parties and counterbalances the increase in the consolidated duties and the consequent significant losses. i therefore agree with this agreement with the people's republic of china, as it is entitled to have its previous trade rights re-established, which were slightly degraded by the enlargement of the customs union when romania and bulgaria joined the eu.
in writing. - with the accession of bulgaria and romania, the eu has enlarged its customs union. thus, under wto rules, the eu had to enter into negotiations with wto members with negotiating power on the lists of any of the acceding members with the aim of reaching an agreement on a mutually satisfactory compensatory adjustment to compensate for the increased consolidated duties and the consequent significant losses. this is the case in china. on 29 january 2007, the council authorised the commission to open negotiations with countries entitled to compensation. negotiations with the people's republic of china resulted in a draft agreement in the form of an exchange of letters, which was initialled on 31 may 2012. the rapporteur accepts the agreement and considers that this compensation agreement is an example of the eu's intention to respect the rules of the multilateral trading system, with the wto at its core. our assessment of this report and our vote on it are inseparable from our critical position on the wto, its role and its consequences. we therefore refuse to submit to their logic.

in writing. − the report considers that finland is entitled to a financial contribution under the european globalisation adjustment fund for the application submitted following the dismissal of 4,509 nokia workers, 3,719 of whom are covered by the co-financed measures, with eur 9,810,000 being mobilised. this instrument makes it possible to grant financial support to workers who are made redundant, which is necessary but not always sufficient in the event of the loss of a job. but this problem does not solve the underlying issue, nor can it hide it. the destruction of jobs and unemployment are inherent in the capitalist system and its structural crisis. it is this crisis that leads every day to the closure and relocation of businesses. the solutions must be translated into active employment policies and any policy which leads to increased unemployment and precariousness in labour relations must be rejected (liberalisation, privatisation, etc.). the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work.
in writing. − the eu is an area of solidarity and the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of it. these supports are essential to help the unemployed and the victims of displacement in a globalised context. the increasing number of companies relocating to take advantage of the low labour costs in several countries, notably china and india, has had a detrimental effect on countries which respect workers' rights. the egf is intended to help workers who are victims of the relocation of companies and is essential to facilitate access to a new job. the egf has already been used in the past by other eu countries and this aid should now be granted to finland, which applied for a financial contribution from the egf in the form of an application egf/2013/001 fi/nokia, following 4 509 redundancies at nokia, of which 3 719 workers were covered by the measures co-financed by the egf during the reference period from 1 august 2012 to 30 november 2012.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. on 16 october 2013, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the egf in favour of finland in order to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by nokia plc, nokia siemens networks and 30 of its suppliers and subcontractors as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns due to globalisation. this is the ninth application to be examined under the 2013 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 9 810 000 from the egf in favour of finland, based on 4 509 redundancies in nokia plc, nokia siemens networks and 30 of their suppliers and subcontractors, with 3 719 workers covered by the measures co-financed by the egf during the reference period from 1 august 2012 to 30 november 2012. since all the necessary conditions for the activation of this financial assistance mechanism have been met, i have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − regulation no 1927/2006 of the european parliament and of the council of 20 december 2006 established the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to support workers who have lost their jobs as a result of structural changes in the global economy. i agree to the request to mobilise eur 9.810.000,00 for the redundancies in nokia plc, nokia siemens networks and 30 of their subcontractors. i believe that the european commission should step up support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns, helping them to reintegrate into the labour market.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it gives the green light to the mobilisation of the egf in germany. the request concerned 959 redundancies in the solar sector between 15 november 2012 and 15 march 2013, of which 875 redundancies will benefit from personalised measures supported by egf funding.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of international trade and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. as from 1 may 2009, the scope of the european globalisation adjustment fund was extended to include support for workers made redundant as a direct consequence of the economic, financial and social crisis. at a time when we are faced with a serious financial, economic and social crisis, with rising unemployment as one of the main consequences, the european union should use all the means at its disposal to react, particularly with regard to the support to be given to people who have lost their jobs. i have therefore supported this report concerning the mobilisation of eur 2 305 357 from the european globalisation adjustment fund for germany to support the 875 workers covered by the egf co-financed measures of the 959 workers made redundant by first solar manufacturing gmbh.
in writing. - according to the report, the fact that a company the size of first solar reduced its activity meant a 4% increase in the percentage of the number of unemployed in the land of brandenburg, germany. this circumstance indicates the extent to which this company was relevant in the regional context and how the closure, relocation or reduction of the activity of companies of this magnitude has serious, direct and indirect impacts on the life of the communities in which they were located. first solar is also reportedly facing direct competition from the chinese market for solar power production and does not appear to have been able to reverse the declining trend of its business as a result of globalisation. apart from the mobilisation of the fund, which is justified, there will be a need to reflect deeply, at european level, on the way in which the business fabric of the union has been affected by globalisation and to consider ways in which the worsening of the situation can be prevented and the revival of economic activity promoted.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers affected by the effects of major structural changes in world trade patterns. the fund may not exceed a maximum amount of eur 500 million. this is the tenth application to be examined under the 2013 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 2 305 357 from the egf for germany. it concerns 959 redundancies at first solar manufacturing gmbh, 875 workers being covered by the measures co-financed by the egf. because what is at stake is improving the support provided to workers in difficulty and avoiding the misuse of public money, i voted in favour of this proposal.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the commission and the government of canada have finally reached political agreement on key elements for an economic and trade agreement, despite the controversy surrounding the human rights clause, which is a standard clause in all agreements with third countries, and the eu has and must act consistently when concluding all agreements, and there should be no preferential treatment for any partner.
in writing. - as i said earlier, canada and the european union share a set of values which make them not only trade partners but natural allies in the global geostrategic framework. in fact, on both sides of the atlantic there is the same civilization which would gain a great deal by further strengthening the relations between its peoples. it would be useless to talk at length about canada's historical links with europe and the contribution its citizens made to the liberation of the european continent in the two world wars that ravaged it. i can only welcome the possibility of concluding such a partnership agreement and appeal to both sides to commit themselves to the speed of its negotiation and the quality of its outcome, which will benefit us all.
in writing. − the report recognises the complementary nature of the eu-canada strategic partnership agreement (spa) and the comprehensive economic and trade agreement (ceta). the establishment of these agreements with canada aims to open up markets between the two parties, combining these agreements with the north american free trade agreement (nafta) to form a large transatlantic market involving the eu, canada and the usa. these agreements, which have not yet been concluded, are an aspiration of the monopolies on both sides of the atlantic, a desperate attempt by big capital to get out of the crisis in which it is immersed, by accelerating the process of concentration and centralisation of capital and the strengthening of these blocs to face the increasing competition at world level. the workers and the people will be the greatest victims of agreements which will further destroy the sovereign instruments of defence and management of the economies of the weaker countries, such as portugal. this agreement will strengthen the dominance of the large monopolies, which will have a freer hand in forcing redundancies and lowering wages, creating conditions of competition which will be intolerable for smes, small and mediumsized farmers and family farming.
in writing. − since 2011, the eu and canada have been negotiating comprehensive economic and trade agreements, such as the ceta (comprehensive economic and trade agreement), whose negotiations have now been concluded, and the epa (strategic partnership agreement), which is still under negotiation. the report, while highlighting the complementarity of the two agreements, highlights and reinforces the democratic values and principles governing cooperation between the eu and canada, draws attention to the necessary measures to prevent abuse of the suspension mechanism by either party, and encourages the signing of both agreements. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report which contains the european parliament's recommendation to the council, the commission and the european external action service on the negotiations for a strategic partnership agreement between the eu and canada and in which parliament calls on the commission to make the necessary progress to conclude the agreement swiftly, insisting that all eu agreements with third countries should adopt appropriate safeguards to ensure that there is no abuse of the mechanism for suspending the rights agreed by either party and insisting that such conditionalities be part of the strategic partnership agreement with canada to ensure the consistency of the eu's common approach in this regard. for these reasons, and because this agreement can significantly benefit portugal and the azores, i voted in favour of this proposal.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential, in the context of the financial crisis, to avoid the interoperability of the global financial system, which has several flaws in the risk management process, being hindered, in particular, by a contagion effect. i also believe that it is essential that the security and stability of the financial system be increased within the eu.
in writing. - the economic crisis we have been through has made it clear that contagion between market players needs to be countered, mainly by preventive action. this own-initiative report focuses specifically on csds and csds as critical market infrastructures that require, as a matter of priority, robust recovery and resolution rules accompanied by efficient risk management. while other non-bank institutions such as insurance companies, asset managers and payment systems also need strengthened rules, the international debate on these is still developing. as crisis management has transferred significant risks from individual actors to centralised hubs, the risks of these central entities also present increased instability, which now needs to be properly addressed. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the measures advocated are part of the final construction of the stability of the european financial system and important for the protection of the assets of the clients of the institutions under this jurisdiction.

in writing. − over the past four years, the european union has been paying particular attention to the financial sector in order to make it more robust and less susceptible to systemic crises. thus, efforts have been made to achieve a level of legislative harmonisation with regard to the solvency requirements of credit institutions, the rules on the supervision and supervisory bodies of credit institutions, and the rules on the recovery and resolution of the banking sector. however, the financial system is not limited to credit institutions, and the european parliament has therefore sought to give attention to non-bank intuitions which also operate in the market. i therefore support the rapporteur in calling for minimum governance and risk management requirements for these institutions.

in writing. − this report sets out a framework for the recovery and resolution of institutions such as central securities depositories (csds), insurance companies, asset management companies and central counterparties (ccps). ccps and csds are essentially mutual funds that provide cover for losses resulting from the trading of derivative products. what is needed is a ban on the marketing of these products and the subsequent dismantling of these mutual funds. the marketing of derived products is partly responsible for the price increases in agricultural products and other basic goods, which have resulted in the ruin of many small and mediumsized farmers and the starvation of millions of people. among these financial products are also the so-called swaps - derivative and high-risk financial products subject to quotation - which are generating huge losses for several public companies in portugal. as regards insurance companies, although it is important to ensure their recovery and resolution, avoiding serious consequences for their beneficiaries, the only way to ensure that they are not used in speculative processes and that they effectively fulfil their social function is to promote their nationalisation, placing the entire financial sector at the service of economic growth and economic and social development.
in writing. − the financial crisis has shown the degree of interoperability of the global financial system when failures in the risk management process of any major market player have the potential to spill over through a contagion effect. as part of the overall effects of making the financial system more resilient, all market participants need to have a better understanding of how their business will operate or be orderly reduced in stressed circumstances. non-banking institutions also have to be prepared to suffer the consequences of financial crises and become resilient enough to deal with them safely. nevertheless, an appropriate framework for the recovery and resolution of such institutions is necessary.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the european economy, with the support of european policy, should concentrate on those areas which already offer considerable potential in terms of economic growth and innovation. i also believe that the space industry has considerable potential to generate economic growth, create jobs and thus also achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − the european space industry, despite accounting for only 35,000 jobs, generates a consolidated annual turnover of over eur 6.5 billion. numerous services depend directly or indirectly on space-related technology, and it is also a key sector for economic growth and innovation, especially in the area of satellite communications. this is why this is an area with considerable potential for economic growth and innovation with the european galileo satellite navigation programme and the copernicus earth observation programme (gmes) as well as the development of satellite communications in general.
in writing. - this report deals with the subject of european space policy. one of the major concerns expressed here is that the eu is heavily dependent on the us space industry. the aim is therefore to develop a european policy which is independent of imports. to this end, it is considered necessary to develop all space programmes, instruments and industry, such as the copernicus/gmes programme, alongside the creation of a genuine eu internal market for space products and services. we are aware of our reservations about the framework in which some of these mechanisms are being developed. the support of copernicus/gmes to eu external action services in terms of security services, in addition to preventing destabilising effects in third countries in crisis or emerging crisis, are provisions in the report that justify our reservations. we believe that space should be used only for peaceful purposes, for the benefit of all mankind, by deepening cooperation between member states, between them and other european countries with a relevant research heritage in this field, as well as at international level, in order to use the potential of space exploration in a peaceful way and for the advancement of humanity and knowledge.
in writing. − space represents a source of progress for europe which can be put to the service of a large number of objectives and policies, but europe's competitiveness in the field of space depends on new technical developments. in addition to competition from new emerging space powers such as india and china, the european space industry faces other challenges in relation to its international competitors, such as a lower budget. following the commission's guidance, this report suggests further initiatives to improve and make the eu's performance in this important sector more competitive.
in writing. − despite being a niche industry with just under 35 000 highly skilled employees, the space industry generates a consolidated annual turnover of over eur 6.5 billion. numerous services depend directly or indirectly on space-related technology. at the same time, the space sector is a driving force for economic growth and innovation. many non-space industry sectors benefit from the technological achievements of the space industry. i voted in favour of this report, which sets out a number of measures to exploit the potential for economic growth in the space sector in order to create jobs and thus also achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. the european space industry faces enormous obstacles to its development. in addition to international competitiveness, with the emerging economies of china and india, europe is not developing its potential because: the budget available and military expenditure are very low and synergies between the civil and military components are almost non-existent. a technologically advanced and independent space industry, making use of existing projects such as galileo, copernicus and the communication system in general. this requires member states to strengthen cooperation between themselves, to implement appropriate legislation and to demonstrate commitment in this area by creating an environment conducive to private investment. i am voting in favour of this report because i believe that the benefits in this area are enormous.
in writing. − this report builds on the mandate given in article 189 of the treaty for the definition of a european space policy, defining the communication from the european commission that space policy is a key element of the europe 2020 strategy and that it should be geared towards achieving its objectives. one of the major concerns of this report is that the eu today is heavily dependent on the us space industry, and it is thus seeking to develop a european policy that is independent of imports. to this end, the eu considers it necessary to develop all its programmes, instruments and industries in this area, as exemplified by the copernicus/gmes programme. we have serious concerns about the economic framework surrounding the space industry and the uses of such instruments, particularly when they are considered for military purposes. in fact, the description of copernicus/gmes support to eu external action services with regard to security services clearly states that it is to prevent destabilising effects in third countries in crisis or emerging crisis. in our view, space should be used only for peaceful purposes, for the benefit of all mankind, by deepening cooperation between member states as well as at international level. we abstained.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i consider the full development of cloud computing to be of strategic importance for the completion of the digital single market. the cloud strategy addresses many aspects that affect the need for greater convergence and harmonisation in order to remove all existing barriers, for example: broadband deployment, consumer protection, intellectual property rights, data protection, product-specific regulation and payment transactions. i also believe that the development of the cloud in europe has extraordinary potential to become a powerful driver for the completion of the digital single market.
in writing. − the european commission estimates that cloud computing revenues could reach €148.8 billion and that 60% of total server load will be virtualised by 2014. due to the highly commercial nature of cloud systems, the future strategy should address a wide range of issues, from technological issues related to the development of cloud systems, to technical issues such as legal aspects related to data privacy and security, which pose major obstacles to the general acceptance of cloud infrastructures. the public sector, including the european commission itself, should take the lead, not only because of the productivity gains that can be achieved through easy access to the best performing applications and technologies at affordable costs, but also because, in addition, citizens could benefit from more efficient and innovative public services. the full development of cloud computing is of strategic importance for the completion of the digital single market and its development has extraordinary potential to become a powerful driver for the completion of the digital single market. i therefore support this report.
in writing. − cloud computing is the storage, processing and use of data on remote computers, accessed via the internet, giving users the possibility to control almost unlimited computing capacity, develop a large number of new services, while allowing substantial reductions in it costs. in addition to cost savings and substantial efficiency improvements across the economy, it also has a significant environmental impact, as it allows for more efficient use of equipment. it is a major technological advance with enormous potential, but it should be wary of the risks it entails, in particular due to the fragmentation of the digital single market, where there are different national legal frameworks, creating uncertainty in terms of applicable law, enormous complexity in terms of managing services and usage patterns, covering multiple jurisdictions, as well as a problem in terms of trust and security, with regard to the protection of personal data, contracts, consumer protection or criminal law. in order to reduce the risks as well as the obstacles to the deployment of cloud computing services in the eu, we need greater convergence/harmonisation, with the adoption of general, clear and rigorous measures, as well as the urgent completion of the reform of the legislation on data protection.
in writing. − cloud computing, a dynamic concept, has only recently entered the lives of citizens and businesses and is already taking up a significant space, making it essential and urgent to ensure that its use and its desired generalization do not in any way compromise intellectual property, consumer rights, security or privacy. the benefits of cloud storage are clear, reducing costs for consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises, mainly those in the outermost or remote areas, reducing barriers to market entry and enabling the creation of new services. i am convinced that cloud computing, which has not yet been fully exploited, represents a window of opportunity for the eu to invest in innovation and development, in the completion of the digital single market or in the dynamisation of electronic commerce. to this end, it must have legislation and instruments defining the rights and obligations of citizens, businesses and public bodies using these services, removing the barriers resulting from legal fragmentation between states. i am voting in favour of this report because i consider cloud computing to be a valuable tool for job creation and for responding to the economic and financial crisis in the eu.
in writing. − the european commission estimates that cloud computing revenues could reach €148.8 billion and that 60% of total server load will be virtual (cloud) by 2014. the economic and commercial prospects of the cloud are therefore very promising and there is therefore a justification for investing in its development. this, together with the space industry sector on which we have already voted today, is an innovation sector with tremendous potential for development and for creating jobs and wealth, which cannot be wasted.
in writing. − this own-initiative report welcomes the commission's position to exploit cloud computing in europe to the full, with the development of a coherent approach to cloud computing services, but considers that a legislative instrument would have been more effective in achieving the objectives. cloud computing aims to provide security and reliability commensurate with the increased risks of concentrating data and information in the hands of a small number of operators. it is also proposed to harmonise member states' rules and legislation to eliminate jurisdictional fragmentation and ensure the digital single market and promote common leadership in the public sector through a european cloud partnership, considering that there will be productivity gains through easy access to applications and technologies with better performance and low costs, and that citizens could benefit from more efficient and innovative public services, in particular in health, education and transport services. cloud computing represents a positive technological development, which must however ensure effective data protection and use of information away from the interests of the markets and private operators that have access to it. we have to be careful and we have reservations which justified our abstention.
in writing. - cloud computing, which until recently was just a trend, is now a reality that allows a range of tasks to be carried out without the need for a computer hard drive. this report highlights the full economic potential and efficiency benefits of this technology, but leaves a caveat as to the security and data protection risks that cloud computing may entail. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. − companies around the world are increasingly realising the productivity gains they can make by easily accessing the best business applications and/or dramatically enhancing their infrastructure resources at affordable costs. in this regard, the european commission estimates that cloud revenues could reach €148.8 billion and that 60% of total server load will be virtualized by 2014. i voted in favour of this proposal as the development of cloud in europe has extraordinary potential to become a powerful driver for the completion of the digital single market.
in writing. − cloud computing has been developing significantly in recent years. the european union has always been at the forefront of key research and development issues and it is therefore logical that horizon 2020 should play a key role in stimulating research and technological development in the field of cloud computing. full portability, interoperability and open specifications need to be ensured. the commission should be able to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 290 tfeu concerning the definition of the concept of 'public cloud service provider' and the definition of the concept of 'public cloud service provider'. there is also a need to establish secure and fair contractual conditions, which go beyond the simple differentiation between contracts between businesses and consumers and those between businesses only. the commission will also continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules and to monitor the implementation of the new rules and regulations. further convergence is needed for an effective cloud computing strategy. and it should be underlined that this is a powerful step towards completing the digital single market.

in writing. the european commission has published a communication on the implementation of the single market in the eu. the report highlights the contradictory aspects between the interests of the member states and those who want to see the communications sector in an open and liberalised market, far from the inconvenient national interests which are said to complicate the definition of common positions and make it more difficult to reach agreements. we were against the telecommunications package and its aims of liberalization and privatization of this sector of activity and we also rejected the bodies set up to defend this policy line, which has already shown its negative results. this body monitors the implementation of the regulatory framework for the completion of the internal telecommunications market, which serves the interests of the economic groups that dominate the sector, to the detriment of the defence of the rights and interests of end users. the report makes a number of recommendations for improving the functioning of the agency and its relations with national authorities. however, the real impact on the population and the member states of the implementation of the telecommunications package policies, in particular the impact of consumer prices, is not mentioned in this report.
in writing. − the body of european regulators for electronic communications (berec) was set up to contribute to the shaping of technical and political guidelines for the completion of the internal market, with the dual aim of providing regulators with the maximum possible independence and of making the implementation of the regulatory framework by regulators more consistent across the eu. i consider that berec has been functioning properly and fulfilling its tasks. however, the evaluation report of that body states that berec has the capacity to improve its performance. berec should improve particularly in its degree of independence, which is not yet sufficiently visible in view of its youth.
in writing. − the purpose of this report is to set out parliament's views on the evaluation of the body of european regulators for electronic communications (berec) and its office. the report indicates that overall berec is generally working well under current conditions. thanks to berec (and its predecessors), mutual trust between the national regulatory authorities (nras) has been progressively strengthened, contributing to the effective achievement of berec's objectives. however, this report sets out a more ambitious and internal market-oriented set of objectives for berec and its structure. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. the following report assesses the performance of berec body of european regulators for electronic communications and its office. the feedback provided is positive, as berec has strengthened the trust between the national regulatory authorities, thus contributing to the achievement of the proposed objectives. however, there is still room for improvement, largely due to berec's recent history. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union. it calls for greater responsibility on the part of the agency and for it to speak out on key issues, set priorities and advise the european institutions in order to harmonise the single market.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the common fisheries policy, because it includes proposals for a more sustainable exploitation of marine resources, including requirements to end overfishing, allow the rebuilding of stocks in line with the principle of maximum sustainable yield, prohibit discards and create marine protection areas and no-take zones in the eu.
in writing. − in the collective effort to adopt and implement a common fisheries policy that is truly at the service of consumers, businesses and the protection of marine resources, the european institutions, the member states, the scientific community and those interested in this activity cannot remain outside its debate and implementation. the european commission has repeatedly stated that the objectives of the common fisheries policy are to protect stocks against overfishing, to guarantee fishermen an income, to ensure that consumers and the processing industry are regularly supplied at reasonable prices, and to exploit living marine resources in a biologically, environmentally and economically sustainable way.
in writing. the report by mrs ulrike rodust refers to the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the common fisheries policy (cfp), amending council regulations (ec) no 1954/2003 and (ec) no 1224/2009 and repealing council regulations (ec) no 2371/2002 and (ec) no 639/2004 and council decision (ec) no 2004/585. the reform will help to tackle problems such as the constant overfishing of the seas, since under the new text the council of the european union will be obliged to act in a sustainable way in the context of its annual decisions on catch quotas. as coastal and artisanal fisheries are environmentally friendly, important for gastronomy, tourism and the economy, we must give them special attention in the implementation of the common fisheries policy (cfp). i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the cfp contributes to the economic, environmental and social sustainability of this sector.
in writing. - this adoption decides on a key part of the future common fisheries policy (cfp). as expected, the negotiations with the council did not bring about any substantial changes to the proposal adopted by parliament at first reading. we are therefore justified in maintaining our position against this basic regulation. this is a reform driven by a legal and institutional framework which, as a result of the lisbon treaty, gave the eu exclusive (and not shared) competence in the management of living marine resources. this is a constraint on the implementation of local management, which is the best way of achieving the objectives of a fisheries policy: ensuring the supply of fish to the population, within a framework of good conservation of resources, and promoting employment and the economic and social development of coastal communities. an embarrassment that sooner or later will have to be removed. if the prevalence of highly centralised and remote management has been a problem over the past few decades, the conditions are not in place to change this situation. the multiannual plans - presented as one of the pillars of this reform and the banner of a supposed regionalization - persist entangled in an institutional conflict with no end in sight.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the new common fisheries policy because i consider it a key document for the future sustainability of the eu's fisheries sector. the new cfp has greater environmental concerns, for example, it prohibits discards, since almost 20% of what was caught was thrown overboard. countries should promote sustainable fishing by providing incentives to vessels using selective fishing gear or fishing methods with a reduced impact on the environment. the new cfp now has long-term plans drawn up by the ec - multiannual plans, which set out rules to protect fish stocks, catch limits, with the sole objective of achieving a maximum sustainable yield by 2015 and in exceptional cases by 2020. each member state now has more money available to collect data on scientific knowledge, to know more about each species, size and breeding. in view of the average age of portuguese vessels, around 26 years, the increase now planned in support for the modernisation of small vessels is very important. the cfp also places a strong focus on aquaculture as a way of compensating for the increase in fish consumption and the decline in fish stocks.
in writing. - this reform of the common fisheries policy will finally make it possible to tackle the most important problems facing the common fisheries policy, namely overfishing. all stocks should be managed in future in accordance with the principle of maximum sustainable yield. parliament has also made an important demand in this area, namely that the principle of maximum sustainable income should become a binding principle applicable to all subsequent decisions. this includes future multiannual plans as well as autonomous council decisions on total allowable catches. the council of the european union will thus be obliged to act in a sustainable manner in the context of its annual decisions on catch quotas. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour of the document.

in writing. - as we said during the first reading vote, the current common market organisation (cmo) for fisheries - one of the pillars of the common fisheries policy, which has existed since 1970 - is far from guaranteeing the stability of fisheries markets and fair incomes for producers. in this context, a thorough and ambitious reform of the cmo was needed, strengthening public intervention and market regulation instruments with a view to guaranteeing the sector's income, the stability of the markets, improving the marketing of fishery products and increasing their added value by raising the prices at first sale of fish. none of this was done. worse, the current cmos have been weakened further, dismantling some of the (few) remaining regulatory instruments. the aim is to achieve greater liberalization and market orientation. in the current context of the sector, this path could prove disastrous for numerous segments of the fleet, especially for small-scale fishing segments. the negotiations with the council have not produced any good results, and nothing has changed substantially. we therefore maintain our position against this reform.
in writing. − the objective of this proposal is to ensure sustainable fishing for deep-sea species, reduce unwanted by-catches, reduce the impact on fragile deep-sea habitats and increase the number of biological data on declining species. the text also provides for the phasing out of bottom trawls and gillnets used in directed fishing for deep-sea species. fishermen should be given sufficient time to adapt to the new requirements in order to minimise the negative consequences for the fleet involved in this fishing activity. vessels wishing to change gear should benefit from financial support from the european fisheries fund, provided that the new gear reduces the impact of fishing on non-commercial species and that the national operational programme allows for a contribution to such measures. that's why i'm in favour.

in writing. − stocks of deep-sea species normally evolve beyond continental shelves. they're usually associated with continental slopes or underwater mounds. the management of these fisheries requires special care, due to the great lack of detailed information on the resources and ecosystems (quite vulnerable) present. this shortfall must be addressed by providing more resources to public research institutions active in this field. this proposal for a regulation concerns deep-sea fisheries in the north-east atlantic. in this respect, the eu has been (and is) adopting in its legislation the guidelines issued by both international fisheries management organisations (in this case, the neafc - north-east atlantic fisheries commission, whose aim is to promote the conservation and rational use of fisheries resources in the north-east atlantic), and the united nations itself and its agencies. the proposal goes further, with regard to certain gear (notably trawling), by requiring the end of trawling gear. we have supported the commitment made in the committee on fisheries, which, supported by the scientific advice of national experts, introduces important measures for the conservation of these resources and makes clear the need to strengthen the scientific basis for decision-making. this is a matter which we will continue to monitor with attention and care.

in writing. the report by mrs elisabetta gardini deals with the proposal for a european parliament and council decision on a union civil protection mechanism. this proposal provides for the creation of a new union civil protection mechanism to support, coordinate and complement the actions of the member states in the field of civil protection, with a view to improving the effectiveness of systems for preventing, preparing for and responding to all types of natural or man-made disasters, within and outside the territory of the union. the number and severity of natural and man-made disasters have increased considerably in recent years, and climate change is expected to trigger even more severe disasters in the future. i therefore advocate an integrated approach to disaster management which seeks to achieve a high level of protection against disasters by preventing or reducing their effects and promoting a culture of prevention. i believe that this mechanism will improve the union's readiness to respond to disasters and promote the speed and effectiveness of emergency response interventions in major disaster situations.
in writing. − civil protection has as its main function the prevention of collective risks inherent in situations of major accidents or disasters, the mitigation of their effects and the protection and rescue of persons and property in danger. this is one of those areas where the benefits, and even the need, of establishing cooperation schemes between different countries, starting with those that share borders, are evident. but there are aspects of this report, as well as of the original proposal from the european commission, from which we are distanced and which give rise to many reservations. examples include the reference to military means, with the possibility of militarizing the mechanism, and the approach to interventions in third countries (at the request of organizations other than the un... which ones then?). on the other hand, as we said during the debate, the approach to disaster prevention - where everything should start - is very inadequate. many of the recommendations in our report on disaster prevention, which was approved by the european parliament in september 2010, have not been followed up. finally, we must not forget that countries like portugal need support to strengthen their own civil protection, which has been seriously weakened by the budgetary asphyxiation to which it has been subjected.

in writing. − the proposal for a european parliament and council decision on a union civil protection mechanism is based on article 196 tfeu, the legal basis introduced by the lisbon treaty for civil protection. this is the first time that a legislative proposal in the area of civil cooperation has been agreed under the ordinary legislative procedure. the proposal aims to contribute to the eu 2020 objectives and to improve the safety of eu citizens in the face of natural and man-made disasters. the purpose of this decision is to consolidate into a single text the aspects relating to the operation and financing of the mechanism, while simplifying the procedures for assistance. in view of the various aspects mentioned, i voted in favour of the document.

in writing. - mortgages are the most important long-term commitment made by households in the purchase of a home (about 70% in the eu), with a high economic importance in the eu (52.3% of gdp). despite their size, retail mortgage markets are fragmented. so legislating on this is crucial, considering that it was the crisis in the north american housing market, which spread to europe, that triggered the current crisis. the need to conclude responsible credit agreements and to eliminate bad practices is the point most emphasised by parliament. it is therefore necessary to achieve a sustainable internal market for mortgage credit by ensuring that the specificities of each market are respected and subsidiarity and proportionality are preserved. this requires fair and compatible practices, transparent relations between the parties, greater supervision, financial education, and adequate information and consumer protection (a subject on which parliament has been active, in particular by ensuring advice and strengthening the rights of customers). i voted in favour of this report because it will contribute to the strength of this market and will act in the best interests of consumers.

in writing. − this directive seeks to improve the rules on credit agreements for the purchase of residential immovable property in order to make them fairer and more transparent for the contracting parties, in particular for the debtors. in portugal, 82% of credit granted to private individuals is for the purchase of residential property and since 2008 there has been an increase in bad debt in this same sector. the european parliament has therefore introduced new rules aimed at giving private individuals greater protection in this type of contract, in particular the prohibition on making them dependent on the purchase of other insurance or financial products from the same bank, the possibility, by agreement, of the property being sufficient collateral for the payment of the loan and the termination of the contract, a period of at least 7 days for the debtor to accept the contract, among others. the market for credit for house purchase, given its importance for households, should be properly regulated and transparent, allowing for a truly informed choice that reflects households' ability to pay.
in writing. - mortgages are the most important long-term commitment made by households in the purchase of a home (about 70% in the eu), and are of great economic importance in the eu (52.3% of gdp). despite their size, retail mortgage markets are fragmented and legislation on this matter is crucial, given that it was the crisis in the us housing market, which spread to europe, that triggered the current crisis. the need to conclude responsible credit agreements, eliminating the bad practices that have been observed so far, is the point that parliament has stressed most in its opinion on this matter. much of the work on this dossier involves the sustainable establishment of an internal market in mortgage credit, ensuring that the specificities of each market are respected and subsidiarity and proportionality are preserved. this requires fair and compatible practices, transparent relations between the parties, greater supervision, financial education, and adequate information and consumer protection (a subject on which parliament has been active, in particular by ensuring advice and strengthening the rights of customers). i am voting in favour of this text, as it will strengthen this market and act in the best interests of consumers.
in writing. - by introducing some aspects of greater transparency into the process of granting housing credit, this directive may remove some additional obstacles to access to such credit. on the one hand, it provides for the obligation for guarantors to subscribe to financial products and to set up payment accounts, with capital accumulation to cover the credit granted. on the other hand, it maintains (and may even increase) the power of the banks in eviction proceedings, since it does not define rules for the protection of people who, in this context of severe crisis, face situations of unemployment, loss or decrease in income. nevertheless, it is positive that provision is made for clearer, more detailed and duly explained information and for an appropriate solvency check. but this report ends up keeping intact the mechanisms that allow banks to accumulate fabulous profits by extorting from individuals and families. the main responsibility for credit problems continues to lie with the borrower and not with the banks, which will continue to control the mechanisms of spreads and interest formation and to act with impunity. the power of national sovereign institutions to set adjusted credit policies, particularly in public banks, is also progressively eroded.
in writing. - the proposal aims to create an internal market in mortgage credit against the background of the financial crisis. the financial crisis has had a substantial impact on eu citizens. as borrowers found their loans increasingly unbearable, defaults and foreclosures increased. therefore, addressing the issue of irresponsible lending and borrowing is an important element in financial reform efforts. this proposal has two objectives: firstly, to create an efficient and competitive single market for consumers, lenders and credit intermediaries, with a high level of protection, promoting consumer confidence, customer mobility, cross-border activities of lenders and credit intermediaries; secondly, the proposal aims to promote financial stability by ensuring that mortgage credit markets operate in a responsible manner. that is why i am voting in favour.
in writing. - this report presents a number of measures on the problem of credit agreements for housing. i would like to stress the request to the commission to launch new initiatives on the responsible granting and taking of loans and the request to define contracts with special risks. such contracts should be defined and risks should be managed through additional measures, including consumer warnings and stricter prudential requirements, so that the parties exposed to the highest risks also bear the potential costs of assuming those risks. in agreeing with these and other measures, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − the creation of a stable, resilient, efficient and competitive internal mortgage credit market is vital for sustainable growth and for achieving the eu 2020 objectives. this document introduces new conditions for creditors and credit intermediaries, competent authorities and supervisory requirements. some of the key points in this report are responsible lending and borrowing; a definition of contracts with special risks, with those being managed through additional measures; the solvency check, which is essential for a sustainable market; the introduction of a cooling-off period, allowing consumers some time to compare the various offers; the right to early repayment, as it must be ensured that consumers are not penalised for exercising their rights; better property valuation for both lenders and consumers; and finally, giving greater power to local authorities, as each member state should have the power to set standards for property loans in its territory. we must regard national diversity as an asset, always preserving the principle of subsidiarity. i therefore voted in favour of adopting this report.
in writing. − by introducing some aspects of greater transparency into the process of granting loans for the purchase of housing, this directive will limit access to housing credit. on the one hand, it adds the obligation for guarantors to subscribe to financial products and to set up payment accounts, with capital accumulation to cover the credit granted; on the other hand, it maintains (and may even increase) the power of the banks in eviction proceedings, since it does not lay down rules for the protection of people who, in this context of severe crisis, face unemployment, loss of income or reduced incomes. nevertheless, it is positive that the provision of clearer, more detailed and properly explained information, an adequate solvency check is defined. however, this report ends up keeping intact the mechanisms that allow banks to accumulate fabulous profits by extorting individuals and families. in addition to the problems with credit agreements, there is also a desire to erode the power of the institutions of national sovereignty to define policies for the granting of credit, particularly in public banks, by centralising and harmonising these decisions, while also continuing the policies of replacing wages by credit. with these policies, the fundamental right to housing will be further away. we voted against it.
in writing. the resolution was intended to bring the provisions on imports of rice originating in bangladesh into line with the formal requirements of the lisbon treaty. the almost unanimous vote in committee shows that it is not contentious. i hope that rice imports from that country will respect food safety rules and that the product will be handled by workers whose labour rights and safety are respected. we are still too aware of the victims of the textile factory fires in bangladesh.
in writing. the aim of the commission proposal is to bring regulation (eec) no 3491/90 on imports of rice originating in bangladesh into line with the post-lisbon regime of implementing and delegated acts. the commission also proposes repealing regulation (eec) no 3491/90 and replacing it with a new regulation, which the rapporteur supports, as it considers that this regulation does not currently have any impact on the import arrangements of bangladesh to the eu. the rapporteur makes some amendments to the regulation to bring it into line with the general objectives of sustainable economic development, decent working conditions and poverty eradication in bangladesh. on export requirements, the rapporteur shall remove the references to the export tax to be charged by the exporting country from an amount corresponding to the reduction of import duties. this is because he believes that this decision should be taken by the political legislators of bangladesh and not by the institutions of the european union. we voted in favour.
in writing. − the aim of this proposal is to harmonise the regulation currently governing imports of rice from bangladesh into the eu, in line with the post-lisbon regime of implementing and delegated acts introduced by articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. however, i think it is essential that in this new regulation it should be in line both with the general provisions of article 208 tfeu and with the general objectives of sustainable economic development, decent working conditions and poverty eradication in bangladesh, and therefore a new recital and a new paragraph have been inserted in article 1 of the regulation. that's why i'm in favour.
in writing. − preferential access for products from the least developed countries (ldcs), including preferential import arrangements for rice, is a result of the uruguay round of gatt (general agreement on tariffs and trade, the predecessor to the wto), which was signed in its entirety in 1994. this report deals with the regulation on imports of rice originating in bangladesh and its updating to the post-lisbon regime. the request made by parliament to bring this regulation into line with both the general provisions of article 208 tfeu and the general objectives of sustainable economic development, decent working conditions and poverty eradication should be underlined, and a new recital and new paragraph have therefore been inserted in article 1 of the regulation. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this regulation.
in writing. - the aim of this report is to repeal council regulation (ec) no 3491/90 of 1990 on imports of rice from bangladesh in order to bring legal clarity, with the entry into force of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, as regards the implementing and delegated acts of the european commission. the new regulation will again take account of the preferential access of products from the least developed countries, in this particular case of rice imports from bangladesh with an annual quota, within the framework of everything but arms, which establishes a duty-free and quota-free market for all products from developing countries. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the aim of the commission proposal is to bring regulation (eec) no 3491/90 on imports of rice originating in bangladesh into line with the post-lisbon regime of implementing and delegated acts. the commission also proposes to repeal regulation (eec) no 3491/90 and replace it with a new regulation, which the rapporteur supports, as it considers that this regulation does not currently have any impact on the import arrangements of bangladesh to the eu. the rapporteur makes some amendments to the regulation to make it consistent with the overall objectives of sustainable economic development, decent working conditions and poverty eradication in bangladesh. the rapporteur also calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's external borders are not encroached upon by the countries of the region. we voted in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the establishment of criteria for determining when recovered paper ceases to be waste, because i was opposed to the commission's proposal, which in my view could have negative consequences for the environment, as it would introduce an increased risk to the recycling of waste paper in the european union by favouring its transfer to third countries.
in writing. the report by mr matthias groote deals with the timing of greenhouse gas emission allowance auctions. the excess of co2 allowances, due to the economic slowdown and the fact that supply has been higher than demand, has led to a decline in the carbon price to levels never expected when the eu emissions trading system (eu ets) was created. this reduction in the carbon price is insufficient to drive sufficiently sustainable scientific and technological innovation and has thus become a factor in reducing incentives to invest in low-carbon technologies. i agree with this proposal, in that it aims to allow the commission to freeze or postpone part of the auctions for co2 emission allowances in order to increase the price of these allowances and to encourage the development of technologies to reduce emissions in the fight against climate change. this proposed short-term measure should not be seen as a solution to the current imbalances, but rather as an option to ensure the stability of the eu ets until the necessary adoption of long-term structural measures.
in writing. - this report, while acknowledging the ineffectiveness (and implicitly the perversity) of the instrument, does not propose its abandonment, as was demanded and as we have insistently advocated. the issue of greenhouse gas emission allowances, the trading of pollution quotas only serves the big polluters, who have the capacity to buy the allowances. the amendment proposed is merely an amendment. they reduce or delay the issuance of allowances, as the supply is currently much higher than the demand, and the carbon price has decreased from around eur 30/t co2 to around eur 7/t co2. the promised incentives for the implementation of low-carbon technologies have disappeared. furthermore, this report advocates that such measures should only be adopted in exceptional circumstances and that the decision to adapt the auction calendar should be executed only once in the third trading period of the eu emission trading scheme (eu ets). it is not therefore a question of protecting the environment, but of protecting a market which is in decline because of lack of demand, as a result of the state of many industries, with thousands of factories closing. as we have said, this is the defence of yet another scheme for the generation of fictitious financial assets.
in writing. - the debate on emissions of polluting gases is becoming increasingly important, but we cannot continue to be hostages to our energy dependence on oil and its derivatives. we must therefore find energy alternatives that are more environmentally friendly and equally reliable. however, data from 2010 tells us that there was a 6% increase in carbon dioxide emissions into the atmosphere. however, as this report points out, europe is only responsible for 11% of global co2 emissions and our actions in isolation are not enough to stop the process of increasing co2 emissions. this has to be a joint effort by all the powers, particularly the brics, with increasing responsibilities in terms of co2 emissions. some short- and long-term measures are needed to rebalance the greenhouse gas emission allowance market, otherwise there will be no incentive to invest in renewable energy with the inherent adverse effects on our environment.
in writing. − the european union emission trading scheme (eu ets) is a key instrument for reducing eu industrial emissions in a cost-effective way. since the start of the second marketing year in 2008, emissions have been reduced by more than 10%. the original intention was to create a market-based measure that would stimulate the carbon price, thereby positively influencing investment in low-carbon technologies and renewable energy, which in turn would lead to a reduction in emissions. however, the reduction of emissions in the second marketing period contributed to a large extent to the economic crisis, which led to a reduction in economic activity and production, as stated in the commission report on the situation of the european carbon market in 2012. as there are currently serious imbalances in the system, i voted in favour of this report, which aims to clarify the legal provisions on the timing of auctions and to ensure that the stability and predictability of the eu ets is not undermined, as well as to ensure that an assessment is carried out to avoid any significant impact on sectors at risk of relocation.
in writing. − the european union emissions trading scheme (eu ets) was developed with the aim of creating a market-based measure to stimulate the carbon price, thereby encouraging investment in low-carbon technologies and renewable energy. the eu ets has indeed become a key instrument for reducing industrial emissions in the union, but it currently faces serious imbalances. the economic crisis we are facing today, combined with the influx of external credits from the clean development mechanism to reduce emissions, among other regulatory provisions, has resulted in the issuance of excess licences, which has resulted in a significant reduction in the carbon price: from €30/t co2 to around €7/t co2. therefore, and in order to correct the current imbalance, it is hereby proposed that greenhouse gas emission allowances that would have been auctioned in the period 2013-2020 be temporarily suspended.

in writing. - this proposal is based on the council's proposed regulation laying down certain criteria defining the quantities of non-paper elements in waste and the transformations undergone in order to determine whether they can be reintegrated into paper fibre processing or recycling processes and no longer be considered waste. the resolution considers that the proposed council regulation is not compatible with its own objective and exceeds the implementing powers conferred on the commission under the basic act, and that the impacts of the draft regulation on paper recycling and transfers of waste paper in the form of a product to third countries are not properly assessed, and is not able to provide the committee with a justification for changing the end point of the waste status. there is a market and demand for recovered paper by the paper industry and this regulation also aims to meet the standards and specifications of these industries without focusing too much on environmental criteria. the comments in the motion for a resolution are relevant and justified, and we have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. - there are more than 10 million roma in the european union, who are often victims of discrimination, racism and prejudice, which makes it difficult for them to be effectively integrated. in portugal, according to official estimates, there are between 50,000 and 100,000 roma. in 2011, the european union adopted a european framework for national roma integration strategies. the integration of roma is in the interest of the member states, as they represent a significant and growing part of the school-age population and the future workforce. the results of the implementation of the first strategies have shown the need for further progress, in particular in access to the labour market, education and health, the fight against discrimination and the fight against violence against women. the need for these strategies to be implemented with greater coordination and participation of ngos linked to the defence of roma and women's organisations is emphasised. for the reasons i have just given, i voted in favour of this report, which aims to improve the economic and social integration of roma in europe.
in writing. - there are some 10 to 12 million roma in europe, the largest minority in europe, who remain largely economically and socially marginalised, maintaining a vicious cycle of poverty that is passed on from generation to generation. determined action is needed, in active dialogue with roma communities, at national and eu level, to meet the challenge posed by the much needed integration of these communities. greater integration of roma into the labour market is urgently needed, which will have economic and financial consequences for roma populations and for the countries themselves. the other major priority is investment in education and training. the roma population is young, with some 35.7% under the age of 15, so it is essential to invest in their education and reduce the number of school leavers, so that these young people can more easily enter the labour market. national roma integration strategies should therefore be effective and meet the overall objectives set, with targeted actions and sufficient funding to meet them. a more effective use of eu funds should also be ensured, including through an effective monitoring system to ensure concrete results for these communities.
in writing. − although long-standing cultural reasons lead to different treatment of the genders within roma communities, the eu should strive in its roma integration policies to promote a greater balance in the treatment of men and women, especially in safeguarding the rights of the latter to physical integrity, education and freedom, promoting a true culture of respect for women and their essential role in the community.
