in writing. the european automotive industry represents 12 million direct and indirect jobs, 4% of european gdp, €90 billion in trade surpluses and a quarter of world production. this is why it is a highly relevant industry for the european economy and central to an employment and competitiveness strategy. that is why i welcome the presentation by the commission of the cars 2020 plan, the first sectoral approach developed by the commission, which is indicative of the commission's aim to make the automotive sector a priority by increasing the share of this sector in european gdp (from the current 16% to 20% in 2020).
in writing. - the automobile industry is in decline. statistics show that the number of vehicles sold fell by 6.85% for private use and by 10.87% for business use. the report endorses all the commission's initiatives and states that the solution for the sector lies in greater competitiveness, through the strengthening of the internal market and the guarantee of more competition. the recipe is not unknown, nor are the results that come from it: a race to the top in the exploitation of labour, a race to the bottom in wages and workers' rights. the report also stresses the need for restructuring of the automotive industry aimed at retraining workers and increasing labour flexibility, which are clearly leading to the destruction and precariousness of thousands of jobs in the sector in several member states. a well-known reality in portugal. it is regrettable that the proposals we put forward in committee have been rejected. these were proposals that sought to maintain existing production in countries such as portugal and to restructure the sector to requalify and modernise its micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, to defend skilled labour and the creation of work with rights.
in writing. the european automotive industry is an undeniable and strategic asset for the european union's economy and employment. the car industry is a pillar of our industrial economy, both in real terms and in symbolic terms. it is a sector which very clearly identifies the specificities of european industry and which therefore deserves priority and rapid political action. europe must urgently define a reform agenda and policy mechanisms, the result of genuine voluntarism to consolidate our automotive industrial policy at european level.
in writing. the european automotive industry is an undeniable and strategic asset for the european union's economy and employment. the automobile industry in europe is experiencing an unprecedented crisis. the european commission presented a cars 2020 action plan based on the consultation of all stakeholders in the sector (creation and reactivation of the cars 21 high level group) with the aim of developing a dynamic to put automotive industrial production back at the centre of economic development. a few years ago, europe had decided to put everything on services, but today's leaders recognise the economic and social interest in returning to a solid and lasting productive base. it is a courageous political choice which we must support in this and other areas. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which promotes a return to a productive base on the continent that makes us less dependent on our competitors.

in writing. − volunteering is an important pillar of our democratic and pluralist societies. it is an expression of commitment, support and active participation in society. the impact of volunteering is immediate, as it promotes solidarity between generations, contributes to active ageing and civic participation at all stages of life, and leads to effective social inclusion. the european year of volunteering 2011 has four main objectives: to create a favourable environment for volunteering activities, to improve activities by giving better tools to their organisers, to recognise volunteering activities, to raise public awareness of the importance of volunteering activities. a number of measures have been taken to achieve these objectives, including the creation of a european skills passport which provides a complete overview of volunteers' skills through official recognition, whether in a professional context or in terms of learning. to this end, the member states and the commission should provide for a single point of contact, as a permanent service, responsible for the voluntary policy and for coordination between the services and the different institutions. i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on volunteering and voluntary activities in europe, in favour of creating and promoting more opportunities for mobility and learning, especially for young people, through a common european approach to forms of volunteering, the adequacy of financial support and the protection of the health and safety of volunteers. volunteering activities in europe promote civic participation at all ages, thereby contributing to intergenerational solidarity and intercultural learning, which are important elements for the development of formal and non-formal skills and competences of european citizens.
in writing. − volunteering covers all forms of non-profit-making activities carried out on the basis of free will, choice and personal motivation. it is an expression of generosity that promotes the values of solidarity and mutual aid, contributing to social integration and the dissipation of feelings of discrimination. following the establishment of the european year of volunteering, several countries have implemented the international labour organisation's volunteering evaluation manual, encouraging others to do the same as it provides consistent data on volunteering in order to provide a clear framework for its important contribution. the report notes the positive results for the european year of volunteering in 2011, but this assessment may not be the same if we take into account that volunteering depends on the existence of free time for workers and is absolutely incompatible with exploitative situations, irregular or excessive working hours, low wages and job insecurity. improving the development of volunteering also involves promoting and supporting the activities of non-profit organisations, such as, among many others, the cooperative movement, local authorities and societies, residents' committees, sports, recreational, cultural, youth or child-oriented associations.
in writing. − volunteering is an expression of active citizenship in all aspects of social life and is a key activity for the development of democratic values, human dignity, equality and subsidiarity. it should therefore be supported by all member states. the figures reveal a body of 100 million european citizens engaged in various volunteering activities, capable of contributing to the production of 5% of european gdp, and these activities being considered by 80% of citizens as an important element of democratic life and a meaningful way for citizens to participate in society. volunteering is thus a precious european heritage.

in writing. − in a pluralistic and democratic society, the exercise of voluntary activity is of the utmost importance for the formation of an equal and just society. following the european year of volunteering in 2011 and the implementation by some member states of the international labour organisation's volunteering evaluation manual, it is imperative to continue to create an enabling environment for the development of volunteering activities. member states should encourage their citizens to recognise the importance of this activity through awareness campaigns and by increasing support for non-governmental organisations carrying out these activities. this report draws attention to the importance of creating a contact point to coordinate volunteering activities and to include it as an informal competence. i am voting in favour of this report.

madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, a word of congratulations to the rapporteur for her good work. the european globalisation adjustment fund has been an important instrument of solidarity in europe. the mass redundancies caused by globalisation and the economic crisis occur very frequently in regions where there are already many unemployed people and where the possibilities of reconversion or finding another job are very difficult. since its creation five years ago, the fund has helped more than 100 000 workers in 20 member states to find a new job and acquire new skills. the continuation of the egf is therefore very important, especially for countries in crisis. i therefore welcome the continuation of this fund until 2020, which was in danger of not happening, i welcome the 60% co-financing and i also welcome the fact that this fund is complementary to measures to combat youth unemployment, and can benefit young people who are in a more precarious situation, who cannot find a job or are not studying, and i welcome the extension of the scope of this fund to other categories of workers.

madam president, little is known about the social and employment situation of domestic workers, little or nothing is said about this occupational sector, and why? perhaps because most of these workers are certainly working in the informal sector. the statistical data are thus scarce and we think, too, uncertain. eurostat data estimate that there are 2.6 million domestic workers in the european union, 89% of whom are women and half of whom are migrants. it is clear that domestic work is one of the most unprotected and invisible jobs, given its isolated and individual character. it is therefore often difficult for domestic workers to obtain information about their rights, to organise themselves in associations and trade unions representing their interests and thus to be more protected in the defence of their labour and social rights. domestic work is characterized by precariousness, the absence of a work contract, late payment of wages, the demand for overtime without proper remuneration, disregard for the right to holidays and breaks, the non-payment of holidays and vacations, the absence of social security payments, among others. according to the ilo, in many cases domestic workers are victims of low wages, excessively long hours, lack of a weekly rest day and sometimes physical, mental or sexual abuse or restrictions on their freedom of movement. ilo research also shows that, globally, only 10% of all domestic workers are covered by general labour legislation to the same extent as other workers. the ilo convention referred to here expresses as its main objective the enhancement of domestic workers by providing, among other guarantees, the recognition of the importance of domestic workers to the economy, the adoption of measures by signatory states to respect, promote and implement the fundamental principles and rights of labour - freedom of association, freedom of association and effective recognition of the right to collective bargaining - the elimination of all forms of forced or compulsory labour, the effective abolition of child labour and the guarantee that domestic workers are informed of their working conditions in an appropriate and comprehensible manner and, where possible, by means of a written contract. we do, however, have some concerns. we know that there is trafficking in human beings, particularly trafficking in women, not only from third countries to the european union but also between countries of the european union. we therefore believe that states should pay particular attention to the monitoring of contracts concluded in their countries, particularly by private employment agencies which employ people from other countries to work as domestic workers. we are also particularly concerned about workers who work for different employers, which means that it will be more difficult to estimate for each employee what the wage will be given to him, taking into account the achievement of a minimum wage which is that which is designated by the convention we are talking about. the great challenge in raising the rights of domestic workers lies more in changing the practical reality than the legislation, so their organisation, strengthening and their capacity to demand are key. it is essential to bring this debate to the public, to value and dignify the important work of these workers, and we therefore agree that the council should authorise the member states to ratify this convention.
member of the commission. − madam president, the european commission works shoulder to shoulder with the international liberal organisations for decent work, improved working conditions and against poverty. this cooperation has been extended in recent years to new fora, such as the g20; in eu member states, on important issues like rebuilding the social dialogue, we work together with the ilo, especially in the so-called programme countries. in my view, implementing the ilo domestic workers’ convention well matches the core values and fundamental rights of the european union, as well as our social, gender equality and anti-discrimination policies. we also consider that the ratification of the convention contributes to our strategy towards the eradication of trafficking in human beings. the commission welcomes the draft recommendation submitted to this plenary. we will monitor the future of this convention within the member states and will certainly raise it in the future in our engagement with the member states, if necessary.

in writing. - i welcome this report because of the importance it attaches to a subject of the utmost importance, namely the counterfeiting of the euro. it is important to anticipate potentially damaging consequences for the european economy and the stability of the currency itself. the pericles programme has undoubtedly played an important role in this process. the commission proposal is not the most appropriate and this report is to guide it in maximising the money allocated to it.
in writing. - the euro remains a prime target for organised crime groups involved in counterfeiting currency, both inside and outside europe. the international dimension of the threat of counterfeiting the euro requires supranational coordination to deal effectively with it. the pericles programme is thus an action programme which responds to the need to continue the surveillance, exchange, training and technical assistance actions necessary for the protection of the euro against counterfeiting by providing a stable framework for the planning of member states' programmes. since its adoption in 2001, it has helped to maintain a high level of cooperation between member states and with third countries, leading to reduced levels of euro counterfeiting and the regular detection of illegal reprographies and printing workshops, with the consequent arrest of counterfeiters. the new programme will cover the period 2014-2020 and is expected to have an overall budget of more than eur 7 million. as with other programmes, in the context of the multiannual financial framework, the regulatory framework for this programme has been simplified, administrative burdens have been reduced, the preparation of applications by the competent national authorities has been facilitated, and their use in the relevant third countries has been facilitated.
in writing. − the pericles 2020 programme is to run for a period of seven years and aims to contribute to the protection and safeguarding of the euro against counterfeiting and associated fraud, in particular through the constant dissemination of the results of the activities supported by the programme. increasing transnational cooperation on counterfeiting protection is one of the measures envisaged for member states or countries with the highest euro counterfeiting rates, supporting and complementing the actions of member states which have adopted the euro as the single currency and assisting the competent national authorities. the programme provides co-financed financial support for measures to exchange and disseminate information through workshops, meetings, seminars, training, traineeships and exchanges of staff of the competent national authorities, in particular on methodologies for the control and analysis of the economic and financial impact of counterfeiting of currency, databases of early warning systems, research methods and scientific assistance. the recipients are competent services involved in detecting and combating counterfeiting, staff of information services, representatives of national banks, mints, commercial banks and other financial intermediaries, specialist lawyers and members of the judiciary connected with this field. we voted in favour.
in writing. - the counterfeiting of the euro is obviously a serious crime and its link to organised crime must be taken into account when assessing the economic and social impact of counterfeiting on the lives of citizens. large-scale counterfeiting has potentially damaging consequences for the european economy and the stability of the currency itself. however, the euro is not a currency that is subject to significant counterfeiting practices, largely due to its design and the existing structures at national and community level that control and combat counterfeiting. the pericles programme has played an important role in this process to date. this well-established programme has played a leading role in disseminating best practices in the fight against counterfeiting, thus contributing to the safeguarding of the financial interests of the union.
in writing. - the counterfeiting of the euro is obviously a serious crime and its link to organised crime must be taken into account when assessing the economic and social impact of counterfeiting on the lives of citizens. large-scale counterfeiting has potentially damaging consequences for the european economy and the stability of the currency itself. however, the euro is not a currency that is subject to significant counterfeiting practices, largely due to its design and the existing structures at national and community level that control and combat counterfeiting. the pericles programme has played an important role in this process to date. however, the current commission proposal for the new action programme on exchange, assistance and training for the protection of the euro against counterfeiting (the pericles 2020 programme) contains definitions that are too vague in certain areas. as such, this report aims to develop the proposal by guiding the programme towards maximising the use of the funds allocated to it. i agree with the solutions put forward and therefore vote in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − the pericles programme has been developing a framework of actions aimed at protecting the euro against counterfeiting. regardless of the success of its implementation, the legal basis on which it is based will expire at the end of 2013. the commission has therefore taken advantage of the expiry of the programme established by council decision 2001/924/ec to put forward a proposal to replace the pericles programme and to improve it in certain respects. i believe that the counterfeiting of the euro has very high economic and social repercussions and that all efforts to improve the protection of the euro against counterfeiting and associated fraud should be supported by parliament and the council. this report continues the action needed to protect the euro against counterfeiting, which is why i voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. − the pericles 2020 programme is to run for a period of seven years and has the express objective of contributing to the protection and safeguarding of the euro against counterfeiting and associated fraud, in particular through the constant dissemination of the results of the activities supported by the programme. increasing transnational cooperation on the protection of the euro inside and outside the union is one of the measures envisaged for member states or countries with the highest euro counterfeiting rates, supporting and complementing the actions of member states that have adopted the euro as the single currency. the programme provides co-financed financial support for measures to exchange and disseminate information through workshops, meetings, seminars, training, traineeships and exchanges of staff of the competent national authorities, in particular on methodologies for the control and analysis of the economic and financial impact of counterfeiting of currency, databases of early warning systems, research methods and scientific assistance. the recipients are the competent services involved in detecting and combating counterfeiting, staff of information services, representatives of national banks, mints, commercial banks and other financial intermediaries, lawyers and members of the judiciary. we voted yes.

in writing. − this report draws attention to a review of the legal framework for european statistics justified by the need to meet the challenges created by the latest developments in the global economy. the rapporteur says that the main objective of this update is to strengthen the management of the european statistical system in order to safeguard its credibility and to respond adequately to the need for more data in the framework of economic governance policy in the european union. while we agree that statistical data are important and should be in the service of a knowledge of reality, this report continues to reflect the intention of the european statistical programme to produce data which can be selected with political objectives associated with those who run the european institutions and the governments who defend them. we do not agree with the use of european statistics to define criteria for measuring the indicators set out in the so-called budgetary consolidation, legitimising and supporting policies which serve to punish member states and destroy public services and workers' rights.
in writing. - i approve this report which goes along with the draft council decision to ask the member states to ratify convention no 189 on domestic workers of the international labour organisation. it is important that after this process they take steps to ensure decent working conditions with social rights, preventing abuse, violence and child labour in domestic work.
in writing. - there are over 2.6 million domestic workers in the european union, the vast majority of whom are migrant women. the specific characteristics of domestic work make it vulnerable and unprotected, and these workers are often victims of discrimination. the international labour organisation's convention no 189 on domestic workers stipulates that states that ratify it must take measures to ensure decent working conditions with social rights to prevent abuses in domestic work. the european parliament, taking into account that some aspects of this convention fall within the competence of the european union, gave its favourable opinion to the member states for ratification of this convention as soon as possible. the international labour organisation convention calls in particular for the fixing of a minimum age for domestic workers, the guarantee of decent living and working conditions, the existence of a written employment contract transmitted to the worker before he goes to the country where he will work and the right to benefit from the minimum wage system if it exists in the host country. for the reasons i have given, i have supported this report.
in writing. − this recommendation for the ratification of the 2011 international labour organisation convention on decent work for domestic workers (convention no 189) is of the utmost importance. most of these workers work in the informal sector. eurostat data estimate that there are 2.6 million domestic workers in the eu, 89% of whom are women and half of whom are migrants. domestic work is one of the most unprotected and invisible jobs, given its isolated and individual character. it is therefore often difficult for domestic workers to obtain information about their rights, to organise themselves in associations and trade unions representing their interests and thus to be more protected in the defence of their labour and social rights. domestic work is generally characterized by precariousness, by the absence of a contract of employment. according to the ilo, in many cases domestic workers are victims of low wages, excessively long hours, lack of a weekly rest day and sometimes physical, mental and sexual abuse, or restrictions on their freedom of movement. ilo research also shows that worldwide only 10% of all domestic workers are covered by general labour legislation to the same extent as other workers.
in writing. - according to eurostat, there are estimated to be around 2.6 million domestic workers in the eu, 89% of whom are women and half are migrants. domestic work is one of the most unprotected and invisible jobs, so it is difficult for domestic workers to inform themselves about their rights, to organise themselves in associations and unions representing their interests and thus to protect themselves in defending their labour and social rights. the international labour organization's convention no. 189 on domestic workers, which was adopted in 2011 and entered into force on 5 september, states that states that ratify it must take measures to ensure decent working conditions with social rights, preventing abuse, violence and child labour in domestic work. the adoption of this report is the first step towards enabling member states to sign this convention and thus defend the labour rights of domestic workers.
in writing. − the international labour organisation's convention no 189 on domestic workers was adopted in 2011 and entered into force on 5 september. this convention states that states that ratify it must take measures to ensure decent working conditions with social rights, preventing abuse, violence and child labour in domestic work. the european commission presented on 21 march 2013 a proposal for a council decision authorising member states to ratify the convention (com (2013) 0152), which is necessary as the convention contains aspects falling within the competence of the eu. the report is intended to provide parliament's contribution to the progress of the process. i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the ratification of the convention by the member states.
in writing. − the 2011 international labour organisation convention on decent work for domestic workers (convention no 189) was adopted in 2011 and entered into force in september 2013. its main objective is to guarantee a set of principles and rights for domestic workers. ilo convention no 189 thus requires the protection of domestic workers who, being often women and migrant women, are in situations of great vulnerability and are often victims of discrimination and various types of abuse which constitute serious violations of human rights. for these reasons i have voted in favour of the document.
in writing. − the convention expresses as its main objective the enhancement of domestic workers, establishing, among other guarantees: the recognition of the importance of domestic workers to the economy, the adoption of measures by the signatory states, which respect, promote and apply the fundamental principles and rights of labour (freedom of association, freedom of trade union and effective recognition of the right to collective bargaining, elimination of all forms of forced or compulsory labour, effective abolition of child labour), the guarantee that domestic workers are informed about their working conditions in an appropriate and understandable manner and, where possible, by means of a written contract. we have some concerns: we know that there is trafficking in human beings, and in particular trafficking in women, not only from third countries to the eu but also between eu countries. we therefore believe that states should pay particular attention to the monitoring of contracts concluded in their countries, particularly by private employment agencies which employ people from other countries to work as domestic workers. it is essential to bring this debate into the public sphere, to make visible, to value and to dignify the important work of these workers. we have voted in favour of this report of our own, which is in line with the council's authorization of the member states to ratify the convention.

in writing. − the territorial collectivity of saint-barthélemy is an integral part of the french republic, but it ceased to be part of the european union on 1 january 2012, when it ceased to be an outermost region of the european union and became an overseas territory. in view of the change in status of this island and in order to continue to protect the interests of the union, in particular in the fight against cross-border tax fraud and tax evasion, it was considered necessary to ensure that the provisions of the european union legislation on administrative cooperation in the field of taxation and on the taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments continue to apply to the community of saint barthélemy. negotiations for an agreement between france and the eu were launched in 2012 to ensure the above. the european parliament now supports the terms of the same agreement, considering it essential and in the interest of european citizens that the terms of these directives be applied in this territory, as in the rest of french territory. i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. - the island of saint barthélemy ceased to be an outermost region when it gained the status of an overseas country and territory and ceased to be part of the european union. in order to safeguard the eu's interests in the face of this change, france has to conclude the necessary agreements on behalf of saint barthélemy with the european union, in particular for eu legislation on the taxation of savings and administrative cooperation in the field of taxation. to this end, account should be taken of legislative developments in these areas, so that the arrangements applicable to saint-barthélemy are identical to those applicable in mainland france. the agreement provides that the european commission has, with regard to the collectivity of saint-barthélemy, the same obligations as those laid down in directives 2011/16/eu and 2003/48/ec, as well as in other related legal instruments adopted by the council, which aim to facilitate administrative cooperation between the competent authorities of the member states, while the french republic and the other member states apply the directives and measures they have adopted to implement them. these are voluntary and sovereign decisions of the french republic which must be respected.
in writing. − by virtue of european council decision 2010/718/eu of 29 october 2010, the territorial collectivity of the island of são bartolomeu ceased to be an outermost region of the union, when it acquired the status of an overseas country and territory as from 1 january 2012. the decision states that france has undertaken to conclude the necessary agreements to ensure that the interests of the union are protected when the amendment is implemented. the authorisation is specifically aimed at an agreement between the french republic, acting on behalf of saint barthélemy, and the european union providing for the application to saint barthélemy of union legislation on taxation of savings and administrative cooperation in the field of taxation.

in writing. i am voting in favour of this proposal which accepts the terms on which the commission is presenting the new period of application of the authorization for spain to apply exemptions or reductions of the tax to certain products manufactured locally in the canary islands. the new regional aid guidelines for 2014-2020, adopted by the commission in 2013, will enter into force on 1 july 2014. in this regard, it is justified to extend the period of application of this decision, to which the report refers, by a period of six months, so that the expiry date coincides with the date of entry into force of the guidelines, and it is proposed that the decision be amended accordingly.
in writing. − the canary islands economy has been affected by the global economic crisis, with an impact on travel reduction, culminating in an increase in the unemployment rate from between 10.4% and 12% in the period 2001-2007 to over 26% in 2009. council decision 2002/546/ec, adopted on the basis of article 349 tfeu, authorises spain to apply, until the end of 2011, exemptions or reductions from the tax on certain locally produced products in the canary islands, measures designed to strengthen local industry. spain has requested an extension of the period of application to the european commission in view of the scale of the difficulties affecting the canary islands. given that there is an agreement on the renewal of these special rules for the period 2014-2020, which will enter into force on 1 july 2014, the commission considers that it is justified to extend the period of application of the decision for a period of six months, so that the expiry date coincides with the date of entry into force of the new guidelines. this will allow the economy to continue to develop and provide more stable employment in this outermost region. we voted in favour. we reiterate that the other outermost regions, in particular the azores and madeira, must not be discriminated against.
in writing. − the provisions of the treaty on the functioning of the european union which apply to the outermost regions of the eu, of which the canary islands are part, do not, in principle, allow any difference between the taxation of local products and the taxation of products from spain or other member states. article 349 tfeu does, however, provide for the possibility of introducing specific measures in favour of these regions, due to the existence of permanent handicaps which have an impact on the economic and social situation of the outermost regions. the 2009 global economic crisis, by its impact on the reduction of travel, had severe consequences for the canary islands' economy, with unemployment rising from a rate of between 10.4% and 12% in the period 2001-2007 to 26.2% in 2009, which is why i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council decision amending decision 2002/546/ec as regards its period of application.
in writing. − council decision 2002/546/ec of 20 june 2002, adopted on the basis of article 299 (2) of the ec treaty (now article 349 tfeu), authorises spain to apply, until 31 december 2011, exemptions or reductions from the tax on certain locally produced products in the canary islands, setting out the reasons for the adoption of the specific measures, designed to strengthen local industry by improving its competitiveness. the deadline was subsequently extended until 31 december 2013. the commission notes that the new guidelines on regional aid for 2014-2020, adopted by the commission in 2013, will enter into force on 1 july 2014, and that the commission considers it justified to extend the application period for a period of six months, so that the expiry date coincides with the date of entry into force of the new guidelines. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − council decision 2002/546/ec of 20 june 2002 adopted on the basis of article 299 (2) of the ec treaty (now article 349 tfeu) authorises spain to apply, until 31 december 2011, exemptions or reductions from the tax on certain locally produced products in the canary islands, stating the reasons for the adoption of the specific measures designed to strengthen local industry and improve its competitiveness. i am in favour of extending regional aid for a period of six months so that the expiry date coincides with the date of entry into force of the guidelines, and it is proposed that the decision be amended accordingly.
in writing. − the canary islands economy has been affected by the global economic crisis, with an impact on travel reduction, culminating in an increase in the unemployment rate from between 10.4% and 12% in the period 2001-2007 to over 26% in 2009. council decision 2002/546/ec, adopted on the basis of article 349 tfeu, authorises spain to apply, until the end of 2011, exemptions or reductions from the tax on certain locally produced products in the canary islands, measures designed to strengthen local industry. we voted in favour. we reiterate that the other outermost regions, in particular the azores and madeira, must not be discriminated against.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on eu donor coordination in the field of development aid, as it advocated the need for a new instrument for the coordination of development aid in the form of a regulation to make member states' contributions more effective and efficient.
in writing. - this is an own-initiative report with a legislative proposal. the report calls on the commission to submit a legislative proposal for a development aid donor coordination instrument to promote complementarity between the european union and its member states and to improve the effectiveness of eu donor coordination. the aim of the regulation should be to codify and strengthen mechanisms and practices that ensure better complementarity and effective coordination of development aid, and its scope should provide an appropriate response to the question of increasing the effectiveness and efficiency of eu development aid. the rapporteur believes that this is the appropriate way to ensure a balanced management of aid and to avoid geographical concentration (avoidance of aid concentration in the so-called favourite countries and aid orphans). the report also calls for the establishment of a european union-wide network of information centres for the protection of children and young people, and for the establishment of a european network of information centres for the protection of children and young people. we won't accept it.
in writing. − the cost of non-europe report shows that up to €800 million could be saved annually by cutting transaction costs if the eu and member states focused their aid efforts on fewer countries and activities, and that an additional €8.4 billion could be saved annually if country allocations were fully coordinated and poverty reduction made the main objective. more efficient implementation of development aid will result in more effective assistance on the ground. more effective eu and member state coordination through, inter alia, joint programming, including the allocation of tasks at national level, would also bring greater rationalisation in the use of the various support programmes that the eu makes available.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal which contains recommendations to the commission on the coordination of eu donors in the field of development aid. among the proposals, i highlight the call for more effective eu and member state coordination through, inter alia, joint programming, including the distribution of tasks at national level in order to avoid overlapping actions and high transaction costs, as well as the call for a careful analysis of the specific needs of each beneficiary country, while ensuring that the projects financed are incorporated into the local economy, benefiting those most in need.
in writing. − this report presents measures to strengthen the mechanisms and practices of coordination in development aid by the european union (eu). these need to be more effective and certain principles need to be respected, such as ownership the union and member states should respect the leadership of the partner country; harmonisation common modalities should be applied at national level; as well as predictability of funds and transparency and mutual cooperation. it also recognises that the effectiveness of such aid is being undermined by a lack of coordination between member states and the eu. the report also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's citizens are able to access the internet and to use it to make their own decisions. i am in favour of greater european coordination at all levels and therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the report calls on the commission to present a legislative proposal for a development aid donor coordination instrument to promote complementarity between the european union and its member states and to improve the effectiveness of eu donor coordination. the aim of the regulation should be to codify and strengthen mechanisms and practices that ensure better complementarity and effective coordination of development aid, and its scope should provide an appropriate response to the question of increasing the effectiveness and efficiency of eu development aid. they are relevant and seemingly justified objectives. if they are not mixed up with free market objectives, as the rapporteur does.

in writing. - i approve the report. the importance of external action means that we must establish rules of procedure for our external action, especially now that we have been operating the external action service for some time, with a view to improving our presence outside the union in defence of our values. in this respect, the report is positive in that it presents proposals aimed, for example, at a clearer financial framework, so that we can optimise the impact of our actions.
in writing. − by framing all the financial instruments for external action, the essential objective of this regulation is to deepen the eu's role as a global actor, i.e. to provide it with more means and concrete objectives for external intervention. this regulation aims to tie the action of the member states to a single policy and action which violates principles of international law and the un charter, as well as principles laid down in some national constitutions - in particular the constitution of the portuguese republic and its article 7, which establishes the principle of non-interference in the internal affairs of other states and cooperation with all other peoples for the emancipation and progress of humanity. the participation of third countries in the programmes financed is conditional on satisfactory progress towards the agreed objectives. this is when countries are called upon to participate in eu programmes, because in many cases what is being sought is the funding of the action of political actors (ngos, foundations, parties...) who are available to promote the interests of the eu's great powers. it is the eu's action that clearly denounces the hypocritical use of the promotion of the defence of human rights and democracy in the world.

in writing. − by framing all the financial instruments for external action, the essential objective of this regulation is to deepen the eu's role as a global actor, i.e. to provide it with more means and concrete objectives for external intervention. this regulation aims to tie the action of the member states to a single policy and action which violates principles of international law and the un charter, as well as principles laid down in some national constitutions - in particular the constitution of the portuguese republic and its article 7, which establishes the principle of non-interference in the internal affairs of other states and cooperation with all other peoples for the emancipation and progress of humanity. the participation of third countries in the programmes financed shall be conditional on satisfactory progress towards the achievement of the agreed objectives. this is when countries are called upon to participate in eu programmes, because in many cases what is at stake is the funding of the action of political actors who are willing to sell out sovereignty and the interests and aspirations of their people to further the interests of the eu's great powers and monopolies. it is the eu's action that clearly denounces the hypocritical use of the promotion of the defence of human rights and democracy.

in writing. − the objectives of the instrument for stability and peace converge with all other financial instruments for external policy and have in common that they are a mechanism for promoting external interference. this regulation states that its objective is to prevent conflict, consolidate peace and address global and transregional threats, to act in a specific context of crisis emergencies, to restore the conditions essential for the proper implementation of the eu's external policies and actions. what is the framework for conflict prevention or the possible emergence of conflicts? the existence of this regulation is already a violation of the principles laid down in international law and the charter of the united nations and the role of the un. the latter, like the other financial instruments, defines a set of political and financial mechanisms that demonstrate the eu's neo-colonial drift, when its objective is clearly to ensure the existence of political regimes that allow the eu to dominate its markets and natural resources or to use its geostrategic position. as with most other instruments, we voted against.
in writing. − this regulation establishes an instrument contributing to stability and peace which provides direct support to the union's external policy in 2014-2020 by increasing the effectiveness and coherence of the union's actions in the fields of conflict prevention, crisis preparedness, crisis response and peacebuilding, as well as in addressing global and transregional threats. i hope that the funds allocated to this instrument will be used effectively and that it will fulfil the objectives for which it was set up.

in writing. − the objectives of the instrument for stability and peace are convergent with all other financial instruments for external policy and it has in common that it too is a mechanism for promoting external interference. this regulation states that its objective is to prevent conflicts, consolidate peace and address global and transregional threats, to act in a specific context of crisis emergencies, to restore the conditions essential for the proper implementation of the eu's external policies and actions. in practice, what all this means is that if all the other instruments fail in their mission to ensure the denial of the free determination of peoples and when the economic interests of the eu monopolies are at stake, then this instrument will come into play. what is the framework for conflict prevention or the possible emergence of conflicts? the existence of this regulation is already a violation of the principles laid down in international law and the charter of the united nations and the role of the un. this, like the other financial instruments, defines a set of political and financial mechanisms that demonstrate the eu's neocolonial drift. we voted against it.

in writing. − what the european union wants from its neighbourhood is progressive integration into the eu's internal market, better access to its markets, including through comprehensive and deepened free trade areas, promoting the development of the private sector, ensuring the implementation of agreements that place neighbouring countries in a buffer role for the entry of immigrants, accentuating their strength. the alleged support defined through this instrument is subject to the fulfilment of the objectives set. in practice, compliance with the conditionality attached to this support places the countries involved in this partnership totally subordinate to the interests of the eu monopolies. the economies of the countries concerned are more fragile and in a context of opening up their markets and promoting free foreign investment in industry and agribusiness, the trend will be towards the destruction of their productive capacity, particularly of smes, small and mediumsized farmers, small fisheries - the dominant business structure in these countries - to the substitution of local production by imports, to the pressure on workers to lower wages and lose rights, which is the well-known factor of competitiveness. this is in addition to interference in the internal affairs of these countries with the aim of ensuring political stability for these economic interests.
in writing. − this regulation establishes the european neighbourhood instrument (eni) with a view to moving towards the creation of an area of shared prosperity and good neighbourliness encompassing the union and the countries and territories listed in the annex to this regulation (hereinafter referred to as the partner countries), through the development of privileged relations based on cooperation, peace and security, mutual accountability and the sharing of the universal values of democracy, the rule of law and respect for human rights in accordance with the treaty on european union. i hope that the funds allocated to this instrument will be used effectively and that it will fulfil the objectives for which it was set up.
in writing. − the union shall promote, develop and consolidate the values of liberty, democracy, the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms and respect for them, and the principles of equality and the rule of law, on which it shall build, through dialogue and cooperation with third countries, in compliance with the principles of international law. i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a european neighbourhood instrument and regulating the financing under this regulation which should be guided by these values and principles as well as by the commitments undertaken by the union under international law, taking into account the relevant policies and positions of the union.
in writing. − the european neighbourhood policy (enp), established in 2004, and the european neighbourhood instrument (enpi) aim to create a circle of good neighbourliness with prosperous and stable neighbouring countries through political association and deepened economic integration. the enp is composed of 16 partners: algeria, armenia, azerbaijan, belarus, egypt, georgia, israel, jordan, lebanon, libya, the republic of moldova, morocco, the occupied palestinian territories, syria, tunisia, ukraine and in some specific cases russia. this enp has been widely praised for the progress and success it has achieved in the partner countries. several projects have brought considerable development. the amendment aims to improve certain aspects, in particular the application of the more-for-more principle, more transparency in financial allocation and the programming process, results-oriented action programmes, and greater participation in cross-border programmes. i am voting in favour of this report because i consider it a key element of european foreign policy.
in writing. - with neighbours like the eu, one must be very careful... because what the eu wants from its neighbours is gradual integration into the eu's internal market, better access to its markets, including through comprehensive and deepened free trade areas, the development of the private sector, and the implementation of agreements that put neighbouring countries in a buffer role for immigrants, while forcing them to take measures to prevent their peoples from entering an eu that is increasingly emphasising its strength. the alleged support defined through this instrument is subject to the fulfilment of the objectives set. in practice, compliance with the conditionality attached to this support places the countries involved in this partnership totally subordinate to the interests of the eu monopolies. the economies of the countries concerned are more fragile and in a context of opening up their markets and promoting free foreign investment in industry and agribusiness, the trend will be towards the destruction of their productive capacity, particularly of smes, small and medium-sized farmers, small fisheries, towards the substitution of local production by imports, towards pressure on workers to lower wages and lose rights, which is the adjustment factor for competitiveness.

in writing. − as the title of the report itself indicates, this instrument aims at implementing economic and social policies so that the candidate countries are aligned with the eu's rules, standards, policies and practices. the policies and measures financed by this instrument include those which have contributed and continue to contribute to the destruction of the productive sectors of countries such as portugal. we are talking about their progressive alignment with the rules of the internal market, the stability pact, the europe 2020 strategy, the objectives of which are to continue to privatise even more companies, extending this process also to public services, and to liberalise strategic sectors of the economy. in other words, all the measures which have led to the destruction of labour and social rights, which have given the monopoly to profitable companies in key sectors - an example which is repeated in all the applicant countries - have destroyed and continue to destroy every year thousands of smes, small and mediumsized farms and small fisheries. and they are now forced to play the dirty role of implementing the eu's immigration policy, serving as buffer zones against the entry of immigrants, repressing them, criminalizing them and filtering them according to the interests of each moment in the eu.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa ii) which sets out the thematic priorities for assistance, of which i would highlight the respect of the principle of good administration and economic governance. interventions in this area should aim at: strengthening public administration, including the professionalisation and de-politicisation of the public service, the incorporation of meritocratic principles and the guarantee of adequate administrative procedures; strengthening the capacity to strengthen macroeconomic stability and support progress towards a viable market economy and a more competitive economy; supporting participation in the union's multilateral budgetary surveillance mechanism and systematic cooperation with international financial institutions on key economic policy objectives and strengthening public financial management.

in writing. − this instrument aims at implementing economic and social policies so that the candidate countries align themselves with eu rules, policies and practices. the policies and measures financed by this instrument include those which have contributed and continue to contribute to the destruction of the productive sectors of countries such as portugal. we are talking about its progressive alignment with the rules of the internal market, the stability pact and the europe 2020 strategy, the objectives of which are to continue privatising even more companies, extending this process also to public services, and liberalising sectors of the economy which are fundamental to the lives of workers and people. in other words, all the measures which have led to the destruction of labour and social rights, which have given the monopoly to profitable companies in sectors which are fundamental to ensuring the independence and sovereignty of the countries - an example which is repeated in all the applicant countries - have destroyed and continue to destroy every year thousands of smes, small and mediumsized farms and small fisheries. and they are now forced to play the dirty role of implementing the eu's immigration policy, serving as buffer zones against the entry of immigrants, filtering them according to the interests of each moment in the eu.

in writing. − this report is very clear in defining its objectives: to promote and serve the interests of the eu and mutual interests. and what are those interests? implement the international dimension of the europe 2020 strategy, improve access to third country markets and boost trade, investment and business opportunities for european companies, while removing barriers to market access and investment. and what are the target countries? countries that are playing an increasingly prominent role in world affairs, including foreign policy, the economy and world trade. the regulation also sets out the objective of promoting opportunities for european goods and services, especially in areas where the eu has a competitive advantage. this instrument is a concrete example of the use of public funds with the clear aim of promoting private interests, particularly the private profits of the large monopolies. the policies of destruction of social and labour rights and public services, of increased exploitation and the looting of national resources are inseparable from the objectives of this regulation, since it is evident here that the aim is to bring all means together in order to revive the eu's global competitiveness in this period of crisis, further accentuating the process of concentration and centralisation of capital.
in writing. − this regulation establishes a partnership instrument for cooperation with third countries to promote and serve the interests of the eu and mutual interests. the partnership instrument shall support measures that respond in an effective and flexible manner to objectives stemming from the union's bilateral, regional or multilateral relations with third countries and to challenges of global concern, or that ensure the proper follow-up of decisions taken at multilateral level. i hope that the funds allocated to this instrument will be used effectively and that it will fulfil the objectives for which it was set up.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a partnership instrument for cooperation with third countries, which constitutes a new and complementary instrument of direct support for the external policies of the european union, extending cooperation partnerships and political dialogue to areas and matters beyond development cooperation, following the experience gained with industrialized countries and high-income countries and territories. this new instrument, innovative in its scope and objectives, should create a positive climate for deepening relations between the european union and the relevant partner countries and promoting the vital interests of the union.
in writing. − this partnership instrument for cooperation with third countries replaces the financing instrument for cooperation with industrialised and other high-income countries and territories. however, the emergence of emerging economies such as brazil, india and mexico and the strategic agreements the union intends to sign show that there was a need for an instrument that would cover these countries, go beyond development cooperation and respond to global challenges such as climate change, cooperation programmes in innovation and technology. the evolution of the geopolitical chessboard and the status quo require that actors adapt. the union has done so and that is why i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. − this report is very clear in defining its objectives: to promote and serve the interests of the eu and mutual interests. and what are those interests? implement the international dimension of the europe 2020 strategy, improve access to third country markets and boost trade, investment and business opportunities for european companies, while removing barriers to market access and investment. and what are the target countries? countries that are playing an increasingly prominent role in world affairs, including foreign policy, the economy and world trade. the regulation goes even further when it sets out the objective of promoting opportunities for european goods and services, especially in areas where the eu has a competitive advantage. this instrument is a concrete example of the use of public funds with the clear aim of promoting private interests, particularly the private profits of the large monopolies. the policies of destruction of social and labour rights and public services which are imposed on countries like portugal, increasing the exploitation of workers and peoples are inseparable from the objectives of this regulation.
in writing. - the european union today is a factor of degradation and even a threat to democracy and to many of the human rights enshrined in its universal declaration - which is often read in a restrictive (not innocent) way. there is a great deal of hypocrisy in this proposal, but above all there is the intention to use universal values and achievements which reflect human progress to alter its liberating sense, instrumentalising them through processes of interference. it is a mechanism clearly designed to promote collaborative opposition - in the form of ngos, foundations, political parties and others - available to defend policies, regimes and reforms that defend the interests of eu monopolies. this instrument is also hypocritical because the eu will continue to support dictatorial regimes, as it did, for example, in egypt and tunisia, as long as they are useful to it, as long as they can continue to extract its resources and exploit its labour force. and he'll withdraw his support when the people rise up. in fact, what is often done is to prevent the right of peoples to self-determination and to prevent them from choosing the democratic path most consistent with their aspirations.
in writing. − this regulation establishes a european instrument for democracy and human rights, under which the union shall provide assistance for the development and consolidation of democracy and the rule of law, and for respect for all human rights and fundamental freedoms. i hope that the funds allocated to this instrument will be used effectively and that it will fulfil the objectives for which it was set up.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation establishing a financial instrument for the promotion of democracy and human rights worldwide. since the objectives of this regulation, namely the promotion of democracy and human rights worldwide, cannot be sufficiently achieved by the member states and can therefore, by reason of their scale and effects, be better achieved at union level, the union may adopt measures, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity as set out in article 5 of the treaty on european union. in accordance with the principle of proportionality, as set out in that article, this regulation does not go beyond what is necessary in order to achieve those objectives.
in writing. − this financial instrument contains the founding principle of the european union project, in which it is intended that internal actions be exported to the external context of the union's policy towards third countries. thus, as referred to in article 2 of the treaty on european union, the union is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. the principles of democracy and human rights govern the union's external action and must therefore be a sine qua non for relations with third countries. this instrument, which supports civil society and human rights organisations as well as election observation missions, is now intended to support ad hoc actions through direct grants and/or low value grants to support unforeseen events such as the arab spring.
in writing. - why should the eu create a financial instrument for the promotion of democracy and human rights in the world when it is itself increasingly an attack on democracy, political and democratic rights, labour and social rights, and the freedoms and guarantees of citizens? there is an intention to use universal values and achievements that translate human progress to alter its liberating sense, instrumentalizing them through processes of external interference. it is a mechanism clearly designed to intervene wherever there are countries and peoples who assert and defend their sovereignty, their interests and aspirations, by promoting collaborative opposition in the form of ngos, foundations, political parties and so-called human rights defenders. this instrument is also hypocritical because the eu will continue to support dictatorial regimes, as it did, for example, in egypt and tunisia, as long as they are useful to it, as long as they can continue to extract its resources and exploit its labour force. and he'll withdraw his support when the people rise up. the fundamental aim is to prevent the peoples' right to self-determination and to prevent them from exercising their human rights and choosing the democratic path most consistent with their aspirations.
in writing. - i vote in favour. development cooperation is an important action of the european union which justifies the creation of this new instrument. in this context, i would like to stress that the fight against poverty must remain the main objective of our development policy. at the same time, it should uphold democracy, the rule of law, the universality, indivisibility and respect of human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity, the principles of equality and solidarity and compliance with the principles of the united nations charter and international law.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the establishment of a financing instrument for development cooperation, the main objective of which is to combat poverty. i believe that the commitment made makes positive proposals, in particular with regard to ensuring a human rights-based approach and sustainable development, including measures to support climate change mitigation and adaptation.
in writing. − this regulation establishes the development cooperation financing instrument for the next multiannual financial framework, which is part of the eu's development cooperation policy and constitutes one of the instruments of support for the eu's external policies. this instrument aims to ensure just principles such as the development of basic social services such as health and education services, the promotion and protection of children's rights or the promotion of gender equality. however, some of our concerns about this instrument remain: the over-emphasis is still on a competitive local private sector and on a harmonious and progressive integration into the world economy, understood here as the opening up of these countries' markets, leaving them at the mercy of the great powers and their multinationals - in other words, subordinate, dependent, peripheral integration. we also believe that the objective of development policy should not be to defend the interests of the eu but rather the interests of the most vulnerable people on the planet. there must be coherence between the declared objectives of development cooperation policy and the various sectoral policies of the eu.
in writing. − this regulation is part of the union's development cooperation policy and constitutes one of the instruments in support of the european union's external policies. the fight against poverty remains the main objective of the european union's development policy. the union's action on the international scene should be guided by the principles which have inspired its own creation, development and enlargement and which the eu seeks to promote throughout the world: democracy, the rule of law, universality, indivisibility and respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity, the principles of equality and solidarity and observance of the principles of the united nations charter and international law. i hope that the funds allocated to this instrument will be used effectively and that it will fulfil the objectives for which it was set up.
in writing. − the union's development policies must take full advantage of the european union's added value, combining the weight of the member states and adding their joint political will to achieve the full influence that the union can achieve. this is more than just a question of the efficient use of financial resources. in fact, coordination and an intelligent division of labour between the member states and the commission will lead to better use of funds, which should be a priority. the present instrument is in line with this principle and i have voted in favour of this report, which welcomes the text of the proposal for a financing instrument for development cooperation, on greater complementarity and better harmonisation and alignment with partner countries, and coordination of procedures, both between the union and its member states and in relations with other donors and development actors, to avoid overlaps and omissions and to ensure cost-effective aid delivery.
in writing. − the development cooperation instrument (dci) supports developing countries with policies aimed at eradicating poverty and improving the quality of life of their people. it aims to implement the millennium development goals, which focus on poverty eradication, sustainable economic and social development, and the promotion of regional and global integration. icd assistance is based on geographical and thematic programmes. the scope of support for this instrument is extended by the creation of the pan-african programme, which aims to implement the objectives of the eu-africa strategy. this amendment to the icd also focuses on differentiated assistance, more adapted to the reality of each region/country, with a reinforcement of conditionality and mutual accountability, and the flexibility of geographical programmes. i shall vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − this regulation establishes the development cooperation financing instrument for the next multiannual financial framework, which is part of the eu's development cooperation policy and constitutes one of the instruments of support for the eu's external policies. the over-emphasis is still on a competitive local private sector and on a harmonious and progressive integration into the world economy, understood here as the opening up of these countries' markets, leaving them at the mercy of the great powers and their multinationals - in other words, subordinate, dependent, peripheral integration. we also believe that the objective of development policy should not be to defend the interests of the eu but the interests of the most vulnerable people on the planet.
in writing. - i approve this report because of the importance it has played so far in supporting workers who have been affected by one of the most serious consequences of the crisis, unemployment. it should be recalled that one of the three priorities of the europe 2020 strategy is precisely inclusive growth, which involves empowering people, investing in skills, fighting poverty and modernising labour markets and training and social protection systems, to help people anticipate and manage change, and build an inclusive, cohesive society. overcoming the harmful effects of globalisation also requires job creation within the union and a firm policy to support growth.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund was established in 2006 (with a planned duration of 2007 to 2013) with the aim of enabling the european union to show its solidarity with workers made redundant as a result of structural changes in international trade patterns due to globalisation and to support their rapid reintegration into the labour market. there is a certain cynicism on the part of those who are keenly pursuing the very structural changes which are at the root of the trail of redundancies and impoverishment. we voted against this operation to whitewash the relocations of multinationals, considering it unacceptable, stating that more than palliatives, what was needed was a change in the policies that sustain this capitalist globalisation, avoiding unemployment. it is now intended to extend this fund for the period 2014-2020. the commission has proposed extending the scope of the fund to farmers. a way of legitimising the potentially devastating consequences of the free trade agreements the eu is signing around the world - which have fortunately been rejected by the european parliament. however, the scope has been broadened and some other criteria have been changed. regardless of these amendments, the reasons which underpinned our vote against in 2006 are again entirely valid.
in writing. − the egf was set up to provide the eu with an instrument to show solidarity with, and support, workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade due to globalisation, and was subsequently extended to include workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. i think it will be important to keep this instrument active, because it can be important in combating unemployment, because it supports workers when they are unemployed, and helps them to increase/reconvert their skills or to seek independent activity.
in writing. − this fund was set up to provide the union with an instrument to show solidarity with and support workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade due to globalisation. it was subsequently extended to include workers made redundant as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. in this context, it is indeed regrettable that the crisis derogation has not been renewed because of a blocking minority in the council, despite strong support for its continuation from the commission and the european parliament. during 2009-2010, 82% of applications to the fund were based on the crisis derogation criteria and, in the same period, 10% of workers made redundant in the eu accessed the fund. the commission's proposal to include an unexpected crisis in the scope of the regulation should therefore be welcomed, as it allows the fund to respond to the real needs of workers made redundant. i voted in favour of this report, stressing that some of the innovations in this fund still meet the concerns and recommendations highlighted by parliament in the mid-term evaluation of the fund and should therefore add value to its operation.
in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) is an instrument of solidarity and support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade and as a result of the current economic and financial crisis. however, it needs to be simplified, making its use more accessible to the various member states. to this end, the report proposes that the commission and the national bodies be responsible for the management of the fund, ensuring that member states have the opportunity to access advice and guidance where justified. more flexibility should also be introduced in the amendment of the list of personalised services in order to improve the effectiveness of the fund by providing it with a greater and faster response capacity. this evaluation of the egf indicated that the various measures which were co-financed by the fund appeared to have helped to avoid a worsening of the current unemployment situation. on this basis, the egf can be a vital contributor to the eu's return to growth, which is why i voted in favour of adopting this report.
in writing. the result of the trilogue on this fund is clearly unsatisfactory. the 60% co-financing will prevent countries with the greatest economic difficulties from accessing the fund. the reduction from eur 500 million to eur 150 million per year, while increasing the scope of the fund (self-employed and young people), will severely limit the fund's intervention. it is also subject to macro-conditionality, which is an added injustice for countries like portugal. finally, as we have always said, we believe that the fund legitimizes the policy of redundancies, when what workers need is public support to keep them in their jobs.
in writing. - i vote in favour. tax fraud and tax evasion are among the most serious scourges afflicting the world and europe. institutions and leaders cannot ignore the need for action. any serious and firm progress in this area will have implications for the public accounts of the states, their financial capacity to implement measures of a social nature, to ease the tax burden and to revive the economy. only if the eu acts together, with courage, by exchanging information automatically for all forms of revenue, will it bring justice, recover money and hopefully engage the rest of the world in what is a global priority. what we really need is action, not more statements.
in writing. - tax fraud and evasion has recently been a subject of discussion and concern among european leaders, given the amount of money lost to the public purse each year and the inefficiencies and distortions that such diversions cause in the functioning of the real economy (it is estimated that each european citizen loses €2000 each year due to this problem). in this context, the commission has proposed to extend the automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation to other assets such as dividends, capital gains, other sources of income, etc. the automatic exchange of information is a sometimes controversial subject, but it is generally agreed that it improves the efficiency of tax collection. the eu's objective is thus to move towards a more comprehensive system of information exchange at the global level, and to make the system of information exchange between member states compatible with the rules of the facta information exchange system agreed with the us, as well as the g8/g20 and oecd initiatives. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - contrary to what is stated in the european commission proposal, which this report does not substantially change, the need to implement more effective administrative cooperation to combat fraud and tax evasion would not necessarily have to pass through the solutions proposed here, other solutions being possible to be found in a multilateral framework. there is a clear need for greater exchange of information, in particular on dividends, capital gains, other financial income and account balances paid, guaranteed or held by a financial institution for the direct or indirect benefit of a beneficial owner who is a natural person resident in another member state. this extension of the automatic exchange of data will, however, continue to prove ineffective in combating tax fraud and evasion, as long as the free movement of capital and tax havens are maintained. however, it is the power of each country's tax administrations that is being weakened and with it, and because of eu policies, the possibility of implementing systems that ensure the increasingly needed tax fairness.
