in writing. the report by mr kovács deals with the proposal for a council regulation establishing a community system for the registration of carriers of radioactive materials. the report aims to replace national declaration and authorisation procedures for carriers of radioactive materials with a single registration system. the application of the regulation should simplify procedures and reduce administrative burdens while maintaining a high level of radiation protection. i think that the criteria should be ensured so that the data models for the issuing of the registration certificate are identical and the registration process is harmonised. at the same time, online guidance should be made available and a dynamic help should be implemented explaining all the required fields. a simplified and transparent registration procedure is essential, while never losing sight of the highest security standards.
in writing. − the regulation relates to basic safety standards on the health protection of workers and the general public by replacing national declaration and authorisation procedures for carriers of radioactive materials with a single, online registration system with less red tape and administrative burden, while maintaining a high level of radiation protection. the proposal under discussion is intended to facilitate transport within the eu and to ensure better monitoring by the competent national authorities, by ensuring that the criteria and data templates for issuing the registration certificate are identical and that the registration process is harmonised. the necessary information, as well as a dynamic help explaining all the required fields and an electronic signature made online are the practical tools to avoid unjustified refusals. a mechanism for the exchange of information between the national authorities of the member states and the registry system will be established in order to facilitate cross-border information and transport. while we consider the overall objectives of this report to be positive, we believe that the registration system should provide the necessary security in terms of the protection of the data made available; be robust and fully operational.
in writing. − this proposal for a regulation aims to create a single european system for the registration of carriers of radioactive materials, replacing national systems, thus simplifying administrative procedures while maintaining adequate levels of protection.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation aims to replace national declaration and authorisation procedures for carriers of radioactive materials by a single registration system. the application of the regulation should simplify procedures and reduce administrative burdens while maintaining a high level of radiation protection. i voted in favour because the replacement of these national declaration and authorisation procedures by a single registration system for the transport practice will therefore help to simplify procedures, reduce the administrative burden, remove barriers to entry, while maintaining the high levels of radiation protection achieved.

in writing. - this report, like others on eu competition policy, is an apology for the single market, the deepening of liberalisation in key strategic sectors of the economy and free movement. the effects of this policy are felt on the skin by the people of the member states with the weakest economies. competition in the single market is inseparable from the destruction of the weakest production systems, from the colonization of national economies by the large foreign economic groups, from the growth of their dependence. we disagree with the internal energy market, the single transport market, the creation of the single european sky, the liberalization of the postal service, all of which are endorsed in this report, which considers that the public sector tends to be against opening up competition in many important economic sectors such as railways, airports, telecommunications and electricity. the rapporteur also ignores the main causes and consequences of the distortion of competition rules, namely: the increasing concentration of enterprises; the transformation of public enterprises into private monopolies with serious social implications, particularly in employment and the price of public services; the abuse of dominant positions by various monopoly groups with unacceptable practices in the social and environmental fields, leading to the dismissal of thousands of workers. we obviously voted against it.

i must say, mr president, that this report is very interesting, not so much because of the solutions it presents, but more so because it is a road map for the problems we have to solve in the framework of multilevel governance, not so much in the context, as is very well explained here, of the relationship with the national authorities, so it is not so much the division between the different european, regional and even national levels of the european union, but it is precisely the ability to have differentiated integration, which is how we should essentially deal with this issue. and here i think there is a very interesting road map, particularly with regard to economic issues, budgetary issues, fiscal issues and even, as has been said, social issues. there are aspects where even this logic can be very well integrated. we have spoken here this morning about the question of the common defence and security policy, because the idea of differentiated integration has great potential here and should also be applied there. so there's a common matrix here. two points i would like to draw attention to, however: the first is that i am somewhat disappointed with the idea of not making the eurogroup a truly formal council in the context of the european union. i think it was important to make this approximation now and then to give the appropriate translation in the european parliament, and there is another aspect, which is well underlined here, but which i think is very important to make clear, namely that for us the idea of governance with differentiated integration is not an objective, it is an instrument. the aim of the european union is that all the member states should be fully integrated at the same speed. the only reason for differentiated integration is that it does not exclude certain states, but that we must maintain the incentives for full integration into all the instruments of the union of 28 states and not simply accept the idea of integration at different speeds or differentiated integration. the risk of such a report, which is highly useful, is precisely that someone will realise the opposite, that we want differentiated integration, when what we want is differentiated integration as a path to full integration.
first of all, i would naturally like to congratulate mr alain lamassoure on this report, which i consider to be exemplary in many respects and which has therefore been one of the members with whom i have had the pleasure of working and with whom i have learned the most in this house and i do not want to leave it out of my mouth at this point. that said, what does it look like? it seems to me that we might have gained a little more, although this report is already a great step forward, a great improvement, in terms of the constitutional perspective and the separation of powers, of the european council's place. the european council is at present a hybrid body, with a dual nature, a mixed nature. on the one hand, it is a body which almost initiates legislation, or provides the council of ministers with a legislative impetus, and is therefore a kind of legislative super-chamber, and on the other hand, it is a body for political guidance which resembles a collegial head of state, so it has basically this dual nature. as a body of political direction or political address, to use the italian expression, i think it obviously has some accountability, it has to be accountable to parliament. as a body that is in the legislative process of the council, well, it is a kind of upper house or super upper house, and perhaps there should not be an accountability or accountability relationship, so i think this should be separated. i also have another question, namely whether there is any interest in the president of the european parliament attending council meetings. it reminds me of a sort of old english king-in-parliament solution, but in this case, on the contrary, it is parliament in king. it seems to me that this does not promote constitutional transparency in the european union system. perhaps it would be better to bring the president of the council here for the debates, but clearly to remove the council and parliament and to establish a separation of powers. one of the problems i think the european union has institutionally is that it pays little attention to the separation of powers and parliament tries to get into powers that are not its own, they are executive, they are political, they are international relations and the reverse also happens. and so the more we make the separation of powers clear, i think the more we gain institutionally and constitutionally.

the s&d group is calling for a 'finally'! finally, four years after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the omnibus i and omnibus ii legislative packages bring the union's external trade legislation into line with the new rules resulting from that treaty on commission implementing and delegated acts. it was this small revolution of the lisbon treaty that took four years to put into practice. it is good news for the union, but we must admit that it has been too long. the delay in the completion of this legislative process is something we should all take as a lesson to avoid similar cases in the future. the institutions, especially the council - the controls to ensure the effective implementation of the 27 international nuclear conventions by the gsp+ beneficiary countries, i.e. the enhanced trade preferences regime. the regulation does not provide for specific mechanisms for such control. the gsp+ scoreboards which the commission is now presenting will be an instrument for strengthening monitoring and dialogue with the beneficiary country. the scoreboards will be used in the light of new information, including from other sources such as the beneficiary states themselves or ngos. those will serve as a basis for the dialogue, the draft report to be submitted by the commission before 2016 and any reports on the exclusion of a country from the list of beneficiaries for breach of those conventions. the quality of these specific mechanisms. the key element is the result tables developed by the commission, which are a tool for more effective monitoring of the commitments made, a basis for dialogue with the beneficiary country and for the draft report to be drawn up by the commission. one of the problems with the evaluation of applications by the gsp+ is the absence of reports on these countries from the supervisory bodies of some of the conventions on the list. it does not seem reasonable that, in the absence of reports from these supervisory bodies, the conditions necessary for that purpose are met. without these reports, we cannot assess whether these countries are meeting the conditions associated with the gsp+, especially with regard to respect for human rights, and therefore we cannot know whether they are effectively implementing the conventions. we can only objectively assess the compliance of the beneficiary countries with the conventions if we set clear benchmarks. the union grants very favourable unilateral trade preferences and we should therefore expect real and measurable progress from the beneficiary countries. these benchmarks should be recorded and planned in the action plans of the respective gsp+ beneficiary countries. the last point is that the gsp scheme of the union, introduced in 1971, which is the most generous of all developed countries, is an instrument of development aid, which grants eligible countries access to the european market on privileged terms without any reciprocity. in one of its three forms, it is a special incentive scheme for sustainable development and good governance, which translates into additional concessions to countries that meet the necessary requirements, i.e. ratification and effective implementation of the 27 international conventions on human, labour and environmental rights. in the gsp regulation, the legislators delegated the power to the commission to adopt a delegated act to select gsp+ beneficiary countries. on 28 august the commission adopted a proposal for a delegated act to include a group of 10 countries in the list of beneficiaries. on 5 november the members of inta decided not to support a motion to object to this commission delegated act. this objection, which i share, is based on four reasons: the delegated act should not encompass the candidate countries as a package, since the granting of gsp+ status implies an individual assessment of each country on a case-by-case basis, and therefore it makes no sense to lump them into a single delegated act, preventing parliament from selecting from among the countries concerned those against which it may object. secondly, pakistan's application in particular is a matter of great concern, raising serious doubts as to whether it is fulfilling its obligations, given that the data provided by the commission itself reveal serious shortcomings in the implementation of some international conventions, particularly in the field of women's rights and children's rights. thirdly, the regulation makes it clear that it is not enough to ratify the 27 conventions, but that they must also be applied without serious flaws to any one of the conventions. fourthly, the granting of the gsp should be based on objective, impartial criteria and not on political favouritism, on grounds of political expediency, as may be the case. the green group and the gue have tabled the motion rejected in inta, which will be voted on tomorrow. needless to say, i'm going to vote for her.

the value of the benefits offered by nature is often overlooked. we continue to allow natural heritage to be degraded, which jeopardises long-term sustainability and increases vulnerability to environmental crises. green infrastructure offers a multitude of ecological, economic and social benefits through natural solutions. in fact, nature can sometimes offer cheaper and more sustainable solutions and contribute to job creation. in addition, investments in green infrastructure typically have a high return. green infrastructure solutions are very important in urban environments, where more than 60% of union citizens live, offering benefits to the individual and the community at physical, psychological, emotional and socio-economic levels. green infrastructure has positive effects on climate change mitigation: solutions such as green roofs and walls can help reduce greenhouse gas emissions, in addition to other benefits in terms of water retention, air purification and biodiversity promotion. green infrastructure initiatives, in particular in the agricultural and forestry sectors, also have a positive effect on carbon stocks and can contribute to the union's policies and its international obligations to combat climate change. such solutions further enhance disaster resilience and should therefore be integrated into the union and member states' policies on disaster risk management. green infrastructure solutions such as natural floodplains, riparian vegetation, mountain protection forests, beach barrier and coastal wetlands contribute to risk reduction and are attractive alternatives also in terms of cost-effectiveness. with increasing urbanisation of the territory and the consequent degradation of the soil, it is essential to integrate green infrastructure into the process of spatial planning and decision-making at all levels. as is well known, in many regions the soil has been irreversibly eroded, with low levels of organic matter or problems of contamination. green infrastructure must therefore be integrated into regional development and cohesion policies, climate change and environment policies and also disaster management, as i have said. i would like to conclude by saying that in recent years we have had good examples of green infrastructure projects, but it would be important to strengthen the consistency and coherence of these projects and the involvement of civil society would be very useful.
the development of so-called green infrastructure, understood as a continuum of ecological structure with functional relevance, can undoubtedly help to lay the foundations for a sustainable relationship between man and nature. green infrastructure solutions offer interesting possibilities to respond to the need to meet human needs in a framework of reduced resource consumption and increased resource efficiency. green infrastructure requires new infrastructure or adaptation of some existing infrastructure. public policies should devote efforts and investment to the development of these infrastructures. the budget of the european union could and should support these efforts, combining economic and social cohesion with environmental preservation. in this respect, the recent weakening of the european union budget and the questionable reorientation of its priorities cannot but be a cause for serious concern. we have long called for the creation of a specific instrument to finance the costs of managing the natura 2000 network, which has not been possible until now. it is also important that any budgetary resources that may be directed to this purpose, to green infrastructure and the creation of green infrastructure, should be directed within a framework of public ownership and management of infrastructure and the collective appropriation of its benefits, avoiding, for example, the channelling of public resources for private profit, of which the flourishing public-private partnerships are a prime example.

in writing. − for several years now, the number of cases decided by the general court has been lower than the number of new cases, so that the number of cases pending is constantly increasing. for this reason, it was decided to increase the number of judges. this report deals with the criteria for filling the posts in question. it therefore advocates that one judge be appointed per member state, in accordance with current practice, taking into account the need for geographical balance and taking due account of national legal systems. the 12 additional judges shall be selected, irrespective of their nationality, on the basis of their cv only. however, there may be no more than two judges per member state. the report also suggests that retired judges may nominate themselves to the committee provided for in article 255 tfeu. the committee shall attach its opinion on the suitability of the profile and experience of the candidates on the list, ranking them on the basis of merit. we believe that other criteria for filling the additional seats could have been defined, reinforcing rather than weakening the principle of equal representation of the different member states (e.g. a rotation criterion). moreover, this increase in the activity of the ecj cannot of course be dissociated from the deepening of federalism.

in writing. − since 2007, fees for keeping current accounts have increased by around 41% in portugal. in 1994, banks reported a bank commission revenue of eur 448 million, which by 2005 was already over eur 2,5 billion. banking commissions now account for about a quarter of banking output, compared with one tenth in 1994. it is clear that the profits from bank commissions have increased and that these commissions are a condition for access to and use of the bank account, at a time when these are now an almost obligatory service for receiving a salary, a pension or for making payments. the rules laid down by this directive do not guarantee that these practices of banks will be changed, maintaining for most accounts the charges associated with services. the right to access a payment account with basic features is created, intended for persons in a more vulnerable economic situation, who, as in the case of migrants or immigrants, will be required to provide proof of connection to the member state of residence, which should include a description of their economic and social profile. these basic accounts may create discriminatory situations and may be subject to a reasonable payment.

in writing. − this directive aims to improve the transparency and comparability of information on payment accounts, to facilitate switching of payment accounts, to eliminate discrimination on grounds of residence and to improve access to payment accounts with basic features within the european union. this directive shall apply to payment accounts held by consumers, so that accounts held by businesses are excluded from its scope. i have voted in favour of the document for the reasons stated.
in writing. − since 2007, current account fees have increased by around 41% on average in portugal. in 1994, banks reported a bank commission revenue of eur 448 million, which by 2005 was already over eur 2,5 billion. banking commissions now account for about a quarter of banking output, compared with one tenth of that in 1994. it is clear that these fees are a condition for access to and use of the bank account at a time when it is now an almost obligatory service to receive salary, pension or to make payments. the rules laid down by this directive do not change these practices of banks, maintaining for most accounts the charges associated with services. it will also set up a switching service, with a fee, for which customers will pay a reasonable price. and they create what they call the right of access to a payment account with basic features, vocationally for people in more vulnerable economic situations. these basic accounts may create discriminatory situations and may be subject to a reasonable payment. we are waiting for the outcome of the negotiations between the ep and the council.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on maritime spatial planning and integrated coastal management, as i believe that planning should follow an ecosystem-based approach, taking into account that maritime and coastal activities and uses, such as fishing, energy production and supply, tourism and transport, often take place in ecologically sensitive areas which should be safeguarded.
in writing. − this report deals with the framework for maritime spatial planning and integrated coastal management in the eu. the main objective is to promote the sustainable growth of maritime and coastal activities and the sustainable use of marine and coastal resources. to this end, member states should establish and implement maritime spatial planning plans in their waters and integrated coastal management strategies in their coastal zones, taking into account the specificities of regions and sub-regions, their sectoral activities, marine waters and coastal zones. all this is inseparable from the quest for the sea and its resources and from the growing competition between different uses, which often tends to neglect historical uses of obvious historical, cultural, social and economic importance, such as fishing. this is reflected in the intersection of energy supply, shipping, fisheries and aquaculture and the preservation and protection of the environment. notwithstanding that fair and relevant issues are addressed; the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the marine environment is a very important one, and i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work he has done.
in writing. − the european union has set itself the objective of becoming a smart, sustainable and inclusive economy by 2020. we can only achieve this by properly managing the marine environment and integrated coastal management, and we must not forget that coastal areas are responsible for a large part of the eu economy. however, the increasing use of coastal and marine areas and the effects of climate change, natural hazards and erosion are putting coastal and marine resources under pressure. in order to ensure sustainable growth and preserve coastal and marine ecosystems for future generations, integrated and coherent management is necessary. marine spatial planning is generally understood as a public process of analysing and planning the spatial and temporal distribution of human activities in marine areas with a view to achieving economic, environmental and social objectives. only then will we make the eu's coastal zones, which are so important for the necessary economic growth and the reduction of unemployment, more efficient and more prosperous.
in writing. − the blue economy is an essential pillar of the maritime dimension of the eu 2020 strategy. this importance is reflected in the figures: more than 200 million eu citizens live in coastal areas; the associated sectors, namely the maritime and marine sectors, employ 5.4 million workers and the gross value added represents eur 500 billion. it is therefore necessary to establish integrated coastal management plans in the member states, which make possible the sustainable development of these areas. on the other hand, the unknown of the deep sea is still enormous. there must therefore be a joint effort by the member states and the union to simultaneously map marine and maritime resources and identify potential and measures to safeguard and protect biodiversity. marine energy, mining, blue biotechnology and the pursuit of quality and sustainable tourism should be part of this approach, embracing the enormous potential of this area. i come from an island region and i cannot agree more with this report.

in writing. the report by mr matthias groote deals with the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending certain directives in the fields of the environment, agriculture, social policy and public health as a result of the change in mayotte's status with the union. according to decision 2012/419/eu, the new status of mayotte enters into force on 1 january 2014, which implies the full application of eu legislation, and it is no longer an overseas territory but an overseas department. since france cannot guarantee full implementation of union legislation from the outset, it will be necessary to define a number of transitional deadlines and provisions, in particular on waste water treatment, dimensions, water policy, bathing water quality management, sizes of cages for laying hens, among others. i therefore agree with the transitional arrangements proposed by the commission, but i believe that speed in the full implementation of union legislation is the best way forward, both for the environment and public health and for the welfare of the animals on the island.
in writing. - the change in the status of mayotte - which now becomes an outermost region - implies the full application of eu legislation. it is therefore necessary to define transitional periods and arrangements for this region, since it is impossible for france to ensure the full application of this legislation immediately. this report covers the application of specific legislation for waste water treatment, water policy, bathing water quality management, minimum health and safety requirements for workers' exposure to risks from physical agents and patients' rights in terms of cross-border health care, which should be routine. as in the case of other sectoral reports with the same objective, we voted in favour.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on support for european capitals of culture for the years 2020 and 2033, as it continues the european capitals of culture as a promoter of europe's cultural, linguistic and heritage wealth. european capitals of culture promote greater understanding between european citizens, reinforcing the feeling of belonging to a common cultural space, encouraging intercultural dialogue and promoting the common cultural and historical characteristics of cities.
in writing. − support for european capitals of culture has proved important in helping to promote the development of the target cities, both in terms of the cultural offer and its impact on local social and economic development. this report establishes an action entitled 'european capitals of culture for the years 2020-2033', the general objectives of which focus on safeguarding and promoting the diversity of cultures in europe and on the emergence of the common characteristics they share, as well as on strengthening citizens' sense of belonging to a common cultural space. despite the less correct formulations, which are steeped in the illusion of the existence of a so-called european cultural identity, the central issue of respect for the diversity and specific characteristics of the cultural heritage of each member state is emphasised, while at the same time enabling a greater dialogue between the various cultures, in particular through the promotion of culture for the long-term development of cities, in accordance with their respective strategies and priorities. these are positive aspects which deserve our support. such as enhancing the reach, diversity and european dimension of cultural offerings in cities, including through transnational cooperation. portugal is a potential candidate in the year 2027 for the period considered.
in writing. - the european capitals of culture can be considered one of the most successful eu initiatives in recent years. the current system governing the selection of european capitals of culture is due to expire in 2019. the new proposal lists the order in which countries will nominate cities for the title by 2033. the proposal proposes that, in addition to the two member states sharing the title each year, candidate or potential candidate countries may also nominate a european capital of culture every three years. the present proposal maintains the main features and structure of the current system. it proposes, in particular, that the title should continue to be awarded on a rotating basis to the member states. the selection criteria have been amended to provide more detailed guidance to potential capitals, which will also help to streamline the selection and monitoring processes of the cities involved. the commission proposal is the result of several evaluations of the current system and several public consultations. i think that this new regulation is well designed and will allow this initiative to continue to be a success.
in writing. − the european capitals of culture were set up in 1985 and have quickly become a european union action with wide recognition and interest throughout the european area. this report proposes the continuation of the european capitals of culture initiative after the end of the current system in 2019. however, some improvements to the evaluation system are highlighted, including new evaluation obligations for the cities themselves, and the opening up of this initiative to candidate and potential candidate countries. the involvement of local civil society in this initiative should be encouraged and the long-term sustainability of cultural projects should be improved. this is certainly an initiative that motivates european citizens, as can be seen from the high number of applications received annually, and in a time of economic crisis initiatives like this are to be safeguarded as they are meant to boost the competitiveness of the cultural and creative sectors in europe.

in writing. − countries seeking to join the union must demonstrate, at all stages of the accession process, their capacity to strengthen the practical implementation of the values on which the union is founded, and must establish and promote, from an early stage, the proper functioning of the institutions fundamental to democratic governance and the rule of law, from the national parliament to the government and the judiciary, including courts and prosecutors, as well as law enforcement agencies. the eu accession process should become a driving force for further reforms and the main factor in ensuring constructive and responsible cooperation between the country's political apparatus. the fact that the june 2013 elections were conducted in an orderly manner and that the transfer of power was peaceful has had a positive impact on the democratization process of the country and has improved its image internationally. albania, thanks to its reform efforts, and provided that the albanian people so wish, can move to the next stage of the accession process in 2013, i.e. to assume the status of a candidate country for accession, provided that it achieves the critical mass of concrete results in the main outstanding areas of the ongoing reforms.

in writing. - this report is moving forward with the most serious guidelines. a legal and institutional architecture is defined which not only seeks to consolidate eternal austerity by bringing the budgetary treaty into the legal order of the european union, but also creates additional conditions to enforce its application. it is even proposed that future amendments to the treaty may be brought into force even against the will of one fifth of the member states. the commission is proposing to extend the principle of reverse majority, adopted in the budgetary treaty, to automatic sanctions against countries found to be in breach of the rules, limiting their defence possibilities. it is agreed that the council, on the recommendation of the commission, should be supported in adopting binding economic policy guidelines for the euro area countries in the framework of the european semester. it calls for the council's voting procedures requiring unanimity to be replaced, with rare exceptions, by qualified majority voting, thus eliminating an important instrument for defending the vital interest of each state and one of the few guarantors of its equality. however, the word 'referendum' has been banned from the vocabulary of those who now approve this report. it is significant that the above proposals were voted in favour by the psd, cds, ps and also by the independent member of the green group.
in writing. − the treaties provide for a number of options and instruments for differentiated integration, including territorial scope limitations, safeguard clauses, derogations, enhanced cooperation, and specific provisions for member states whose currency is the euro. i agree with this report which makes a number of suggestions for improving the economic coordination of the european union, as well as strengthening the own resources and budgetary capacities, and the democratic role and responsibility of the european commission. i also stress the importance of a revision of the treaty to change the voting procedures in the council which require unanimity, qualified majority, a legal framework for european agencies with the capacity to carry out specific executive functions and the involvement of the social partners in the future revision.

in writing. - this report is mainly the result of the bad conscience of the european parliament, which, by railing against the (exaggerated and illegitimate, they say) power of the european council, by speaking out against what they call the intergovernmental method and by brazenly defending the role of parliament, co-decision and the community method, always, but always, ends up accepting and reproducing the positions of the european council, even those which it had previously criticised. it is parliament itself that is diminishing and losing credibility, as was clear throughout the process of approving the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework, in which parliament obediently acted on what it had previously said it would never accept. this is not surprising, since parliament reproduces the inequalities between states that exist in the council on the one hand and the majorities that exist in the governments of the member states on the other. only this repetitive and tedious farce was unnecessary. now, in the pre-electoral context and for the electorate to see, they are coming forward with a few more recommendations to strengthen the role of parliament. anyway, the usual proof of life. useless and inconsequential. in addition to all this, we obviously reject the whole federalist approach underlying this report. that is why we voted against it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the lamassoure report on relations between the european parliament and the institutions representing national governments, in particular the european council, which i regard as one of the most important documents of the ep's reflection on one of the most unexpected constitutional developments of the lisbon treaty, which was the taking over of power by the european council, composed of the heads of government of the member states and endowed with its own presidency. indeed, it is becoming clear that the european council is becoming a key element in the institutional architecture of the union, clearly exceeding the powers conferred on it by the treaties, even constraining the political-legislative powers of the council (of ministers) and parliament and the executive powers of the commission. the constitutional distortion is all the more worrying, since it is true that, by the very nature of things, the very power of political guidance conferred on the european council by the treaties is not binding on the european parliament. as the report points out, the decisive test will be how the european council will respect or not the indication of the vote of the european citizens in the next elections to the ep on the candidates for president of the commission.

in writing. the resolution welcomes the communication and welcomes the commission's recognition of the importance of preserving biodiversity in europe, protecting and restoring natural ecosystems by creating a green infrastructure that effectively protects natural capital, conserves natural habitats and species and maintains the good ecological status of water bodies. the establishment of technical standards and the development of a trans-european network of green infrastructure is advocated, taking this into account in planning and financing decisions. it is necessary to integrate green infrastructure into sectoral policies and ensure its adequate funding. in this respect, the recent weakening of the budget and the reorientation of its priorities cannot but be a cause for serious concern. it is also important that the budgetary resources that may be allocated for this purpose should be allocated within the framework of public ownership and management of the infrastructure concerned. the budget of the european union could and should support these efforts, combining economic and social cohesion with environmental preservation.
in writing. − green infrastructure should help nature to unlock the full potential of the ecosystem services it can provide to society. i am voting in favour of this report which aims to integrate green infrastructure into all the sectoral policies of the european union and the corresponding financing mechanisms, emphasises the positive effects on climate change mitigation and contributes to water filtration, the prevention of soil erosion and the preservation of the water table. finally, i believe it is essential that the private sector's participation in new green infrastructure investments be increased and that the european investment bank should create financing mechanisms that include the existence of green infrastructure investments.

in writing. the annual report of the european central bank (ecb) covers the development of the monetary policy pursued by the ecb during the year. this policy was essentially aimed at offsetting the negative effects of the european economic crisis and the sovereign debt crisis and was an essential instrument for stabilising the financial markets and the banking sector and for alleviating the financing conditions of member states in greater difficulty, as was the case in portugal. despite the ecb's active role, structural economic reforms and the consolidation of public accounts should be pursued vigorously in the member states. although the ecb's role is essentially to ensure price stability, i.e. to safeguard the value of the euro, its contributory role in resolving the crisis can and has been a guarantee and back-up of the impetus for european economic recovery. in this context, parliament considered it essential that the ecb should take all possible action within its mandate, ensuring that the transmission of monetary policy is effective and contributes to the recovery of the real economy, as well as being a confidence-building element in the recovery of the euro area. i welcome the recommendations mentioned.

in writing. the report recognises that europe's banking system remains fragile. nevertheless, it insists on the apology of the system, the policies and the guidelines that have brought us to the present situation. the main objective is to promote the concentration and centralisation of capital in the euro area and across the eu, through bank closures, mergers and acquisitions that will only benefit the giants of the eu banking sector. it was not for lack of a supervisory mechanism and lack of transparency that unemployment increased in the eurozone, that the average public debt rose to 92.7%. the contraction of markets and of consumer power was caused by the loss of purchasing power of wages and their replacement by credit. the burst was inevitable and when it did occur, governments tried to convert monumental private debts (of banks, for example) into public debt quickly. the rapporteur forgets the role played by the ecb in hindering the refinancing of large capital, promoting the dependence of the states on its financing vis-à-vis the large european financial economic groups and its responsibility in imposing bankruptcies, unemployment, the destruction of labour rights and public services (education, education, social security) in the countries under interference. we voted against it.

in writing. - tax fraud and evasion are a serious problem faced by eu member states. each year, €1 billion is lost due to these tax evasions. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european parliament, including the activities of the european parliament's committees and the european parliament's committees. i did not support the ecr resolution, as i do not explicitly support the approach of this resolution to the interest of efficient tax collection as more focused on the national interest. i supported, however, resolution b7-0552/2013 of the ppe, alde and s&d group, which stresses the need for greater harmonisation of member states' tax systems, the importance of collecting lost tax revenues (to be invested in strategies for growth, employment and balanced budgetary accounts) and the importance of credible fiscal systems in sustaining citizens' trust.

in writing. - tax fraud and evasion are a serious problem faced by eu member states. each year, about €1 billion (€2000 per citizen) is lost due to these tax evasions. it is urgent to combat this problem and make tax collection more efficient, since all the capital wasted annually could be used constructively in the fight against the economic crisis and in measures to promote growth and the well-being of our citizens. i support the resolution of the european people's party, which stresses the need for greater harmonisation of the tax systems of the member states, the importance of collecting lost tax revenues (which could be invested in growth and employment strategies and balanced budgetary accounts), and the importance of credible tax systems in supporting citizens' trust in their justice. i am voting in favour of this text, which calls for a reduction in the potential tax evasion, commends the actions taken so far by the european commission, but also calls for concrete measures such as the creation of indicators to measure tax evasion and its incorporation into the objectives of european economic governance.
in writing. - this resolution is vague, ambiguous and inconsistent in the necessary fight against tax evasion and avoidance. nothing is said about the effects of the free movement of capital; about the eu's complicity in the transfer of vast financial resources and public funds to the banking system by the states and the ecb; about tax havens and the immediate need to dismantle them to prevent the transfer to these centres of tax crime of billions of euros that do not pay taxes. nor is there any mention of the need to increase tax revenues from those who contribute little or nothing in the tax field but have considerable means and wealth. nor is there any reference to the so-called memoranda of understanding imposed on countries such as portugal and the profound impacts of the imposition of privatisation of public enterprises - some of them highly profitable and generating high tax revenues. nor is there any mention of the closure of thousands of businesses and the consequent destruction of many hundreds of thousands of jobs, with the consequent loss of tax revenue and the burden on social security. what they want is to reduce the tax payments of monopolies more and more and to increase their subsidies, tax exemptions and other types of support.
in writing. - it is widely accepted that tax fraud and evasion represent a significant loss of revenue for eu member state governments. this implies an increase in member states' deficit and debt levels as well as a reduction in the funds available to promote public investment, growth and employment. on the other hand, tax fraud and evasion undermine citizens' confidence in the fairness and legitimacy of tax collection. we must therefore make every effort to avoid the continuation of practices which harm everyone.
in writing. - i voted against this motion for a resolution because i consider that the commission and the council are well prepared to deal with the problem of potential tax evasion in the union, in particular by paying attention to the intensification of the fight against tax fraud and evasion and aggressive tax planning. i also regard the commission's proposals to extend the automatic exchange of information, to combat vat fraud and to amend the directive on parent companies and subsidiaries as very positive instruments to combat tax evasion and tax avoidance, objectives which should be taken into account in line with eu2020 and the european semester, as provided for in an alternative resolution which i supported.
